scenes.synopsis: the season opens — Monday morning; the estate books open; the restoration, declared.
scenes.prose:
> *(Monday comes in clear and early, the light lying flat across the Park the way it does when the day means business. Rose is at the morning-room desk before the house is properly awake, the estate books open in a row like soldiers on parade, the ink still wet on the first page of the new ledger. Hartwell Park has stood for two hundred years and been kept for most of them. Today she begins the keeping in earnest. The restoration — the deep one, the one the house has been waiting for — starts with a pen, a page, and a Monday.)*
> *(She writes the date at the top of the page and underlines it twice, which is the whole of the ceremony. No speeches. The house doesn't need speeches; it needs the books kept and the walls kept and the people in it kept. Outside, the Park waits — the walled garden, the cottages, the house itself — and somewhere in it a wall is leaning that she doesn't know about yet. The pen moves. The season, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: the archive's day face — dressing for the beginning; Letitia lays out the armor.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia lays out the Monday gown the way a quartermaster lays out kit: archive silk, deep grey, twenty years old and re-cut once, the skirt plain and the bodice severe — the grey doctrine's answer to a day of beginnings. "If the house is being restored," Letitia says, "the mistress can look it." The grandmother's pearls come out of their box, cool as river stones. The mended gloves, taken up again for the season.)*
> *(Letitia fastens the back with the brisk competence of a woman who has dressed this particular niece through four seasons of consequence. "The garden first, I suppose," she says to the buttons. "You always did start with the walls." Rose meets her aunt's eyes in the glass. "Somebody in this house has to notice the walls," she says, "and it clearly isn't the masons." Letitia's mouth twitches. The pearls, fastened. The gloves, pulled on. The woman, armored.)*

scenes.synopsis: the quartermaster's muster — the household assembled; the week's orders, given.
scenes.prose:
> *(The hall at eight, and Letitia has the household drawn up the way she draws up everything: in order, in silence, with the household book open on the stand. The servants stand in their rows — the indoor staff, the gardeners, the stable lads borrowed for the heavy work — and Rose stands on the second stair and tells them plainly what Monday begins. The restoration. The deep one. Every soul in the house will have a part in it, and the part will be in the book by supper.)*
> *("Questions?" Rose asks. There are none, which means Letitia has already answered them all in the kitchen at six. "Then the Park is ours to keep," Rose says, and the household disperses to its stations with the particular quiet of people who have been given a purpose before breakfast. Letitia closes the book. "Well," she says. "That's the easy part done." Rose looks at her. "That was the easy part?" "Oh, entirely," Letitia says. "The hard part has walls.")*

scenes.synopsis: Grandmama's terms — the dowager approves the restoration, with conditions.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta receives her in the blue drawing room at nine, enthroned by the fire with the air of a woman who has already decided everything and is merely waiting to be asked. "The restoration," the Dowager Marchioness of Ravencroft says. "Yes. It is time. The house has been shabby genteel for a decade and I am tired of genteel." She sets down her chocolate. "My terms, child. The old roses are not touched without my leave. The lake pavilion is not 'improved.' And whatever you do to the walled garden, you do not pull down anything older than I am without telling me first.")*
> *("Agreed," Rose says, "to the roses and the pavilion." Augusta's eyebrow rises. "And the third?" "The third," Rose says, "I will tell you first. I won't promise to obey you." The dowager regards her granddaughter for a long moment, and then — unexpectedly, entirely — laughs. "Good," she says. "Obedience would have been a disappointment. The terms stand as stated, minus the obedience. Go and restore, child. The Park has waited long enough for a Hartwell with a pen.")*

scenes.synopsis: the friend's counsel — Octavia maps the week's work; the clear-eyed order.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes at ten with the memorandum book and her pencil, and lays the week out the way she lays out everything: in order, with margins for the unexpected. "The survey of the garden today. The foreman's verdict by evening. The household's orders by supper. The village will know by Tuesday — Bell will see to that, and it will be the ordinary kind of knowing." She looks up. "One counsel, and it costs nothing: begin with the walls. Houses forgive slow curtains. Walls don't forgive slow anything.")*
> *("The garden, then," Rose says. "If the survey agrees." "The survey will agree," Octavia says, "because walls always agree with Octavia." She closes the book. "And Rose — the restoration is the right work, but it is also the visible work. Everything you do this week, the county will watch. Spend the watching well." The pencil, pocketed. The counsel, given. The friend, as always, precisely right and precisely on time.)*

scenes.synopsis: the atelier summoned — Élise and her girls; the archive of silks, opened.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise arrives at eleven with her workbasket and her girls, and the morning room becomes an atelier by noon. The stored silks come up from the cedar chests — her mother's, her grandmother's, folded in tissue and smelling faintly of lavender and years — and Élise spreads them on the long table with the reverence of a woman handling relics. "Oh," she breathes, touching a length of claret. "Oh, miss. The archive has been keeping secrets.")*
> *("Everything re-cut, nothing wasted," Rose says. "The season's gowns come from the archive." Élise is already pinning, already seeing: the claret for evenings, the blue damask for calls, the grey silk for the work itself. "The mended gloves stay," Élise says firmly, holding up the grey. "They are the season's emblem. Everything else we build around the mend." Rose laughs. "The atelier has spoken." "The atelier," Élise says, pinning, "is always right about gloves.")*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE RESTORATION'S ORDER: the walled garden first, the tenant cottages first, or the house first.
scenes.prose:
> *(Midday, and the question of order won't wait for the survey. The foreman's men are mustered, the household is tasked, and the restoration needs its sequence — the first thing, and then the next. Three orders offer themselves. The walled garden first: begin where the Park is most itself, where the walls are the oldest and the need is the plainest — the decisive claim, the work as statement. The tenant cottages first: the roofs before the roses, the people before the prospect — the mercy of a landlady who remembers who lives under her roofs. The house first: the county sees the house; the house is the family's face, and a face should be kept — the honest order, the visible work first.)*
> *(She stands at the morning-room window with the memorandum book open and thinks of Octavia's pencil: begin with the walls. But the walls are three places, not one, and the choosing among them is hers. The order, chosen, becomes the season's first fact.)*
> *(The restoration's order: garden, cottages, or house. She writes it in the memorandum book and underlines it once — one line, not two, because the order can be argued with and the date cannot. Letitia receives the instruction in the hall, and the household re-forms around it. The first fact, entered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the brother's part — Julian takes his share of the work; the tenants' side.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian finds her after luncheon in the estate office, turning the cottage rent-book over in his hands like a man reading weather. "Give me the tenants," he says, without preamble. "The cottages, the fences, the lane. You're going to be up to your elbows in garden walls, and somebody ought to be the brother who knocks on doors." Rose looks at him. "You'd knock on doors?" "I knock very well," Julian says. "It's the standing about afterward I'm bad at.")*
> *(She gives him the rent-book and the cottage keys, and he takes them with a gravity that surprises them both. "The thatch on number four," she says. "The well at the lane's end. And Julian — listen more than you promise." "I promise," he says, and then catches himself, and they both laugh, and the estate office feels — for a moment, on a Monday — like the beginning of something the family will be glad of. The brother, tasked. The tenants, his.)*

scenes.synopsis: the fitting — stored silks re-cut; the season's gowns, begun.
scenes.prose:
> *(The fitting at two, and Élise has the grey silk on the stand, pinned and chalked, the re-cut taking shape under her hands. "The archive gives us everything," Élise says, stepping back. "The claret for evenings — your mother's, re-cut to your shoulder. The blue damask for calls — the grandmother's, and it still holds its color like it was dyed yesterday. And this grey —" she pats the stand, "— this grey is the work itself. The restoration's own gown.")*
> *(Rose turns in the half-pinned bodice, and the glass shows a woman being built out of her family's past — the silks carrying their history in the weave. "The mended gloves with all of it," Élise says. "The mend is the season. Everything else is the setting." She pins the hem. "Stand still, miss. The archive is particular about hems." Rose stands still. The archive, honored. The gowns, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: the youngest — Henry walks the Park with Rose; the work through young eyes.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry attaches himself to her after the fitting with the persistence of a boy who has decided his sister is the most interesting thing in the county. They walk the Park together, and he asks the questions nobody else asks: why the garden has walls at all, whether the masons will find treasure, if he can have a trowel. "The walls keep the wind off the fruit," Rose says. "The treasure is unlikely. The trowel is possible, under supervision.")*
> *("Is the garden very old?" he asks at the gate. "Older than Grandmama," Rose says, "which is the oldest thing I know." He considers this. "Then it's practically ancient." "Practically," she agrees. They stand at the gate a moment, the boy and the mistress, looking at the walled garden the way you look at a relative you're about to operate on — with affection, and with the instruments ready. Henry swings the gate. The Park, entered. The youngest, enlisted.)*

scenes.synopsis: the survey — the walled garden walked; the oldest wall, found failing.
scenes.prose:
> *(The survey at three: the foreman walks the walled garden with Rose and Henry in tow, tapping the walls with his knuckles the way a doctor taps a chest — listening. The east wall is sound. The south wants repointing. And the north stretch — the oldest work, the stones green with a century of weather — he taps twice, frowns, and taps a third time. "This one's done, miss," he says. "The core's gone soft. She's standing on habit.")*
> *(Rose puts her palm flat to the stone. Cold, and under the cold a faint give, like a tooth loosening. Henry puts his palm up too, solemn as a surgeon. "How long?" Rose asks. "A winter, maybe. A hard frost, certainly." The foreman steps back, respectful. "She wants to come down, miss. The question is only whether you let her fall or lay her down." Above them the sky is the flat grey of a Monday that means business. The wall stands, on habit, and waits.)*

scenes.synopsis: the terms, honored — Rose tells Augusta first; the dowager's answer.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose goes straight to the blue drawing room, because a term is a term. Augusta listens to the foreman's verdict with her chocolate cooling and her eyebrow doing the work of a whole committee. "Older than I am," she says at last. "You told me first. The terms are honored." She sets down the cup. "And now, child — what will you do with a wall that's standing on habit?")*
> *("Take it down," Rose says. "The manner's still to choose." Augusta nods slowly. "Your grandfather kept that wall standing long past its honesty — he liked his walls the way he liked his secrets: upright and unexamined." A pause. "Yours comes down in the open. Think of it as opening a letter, child — the wall will talk, and you must be ready to hear it." She picks up her chocolate. "And Rose — when the wall comes down, the house will stand whatever follows. We've stood worse. We stood the Season.")*

scenes.synopsis: four o'clock — Laurent walks the Park; present, unknowing, and easy.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent is waiting at the garden gate at four, as promised — Laurent de Varenne, with his easy grace and his unguarded smile and his complete ignorance of everything the day has found. He takes in the chalk marks, the foreman's stakes, the survey's debris of string and pegs, and bows to all of it. "The restoration has a general," he says, "and the general has mud on her hem. Shall the civilian walk with her?")*
> *(They walk the Park's long loop, and he talks of London and the Season and nothing of consequence, and it is — Rose realizes with a small shock — the easiest hour of her day. He doesn't ask about the estimates. He doesn't ask about the order of the wounds. He asks whether the walled garden will have roses again, and when she says yes, he says, "Then it will be worth whatever the wall costs," with the absolute confidence of a man who has never had to price a secret. She doesn't correct him. The drive is empty, the light is going, and his hand is warm.)*

scenes.synopsis: the supper's dress — the household dines together on the restoration's first night.
scenes.prose:
> *(The household dines together tonight," Letitia says, laying out the evening's choices with quartermaster efficiency. "The dowager, the Frenchman, the clear-eyed friend, the brothers — the whole muster, at your table, on the restoration's first night. The archive provides." Three gowns on the bed: the claret silk, her mother's, re-cut to the shoulder — the archive's boldest color. The blue damask, the grandmother's — the estate's color, severe and splendid. The grey silk, the work's own gown — the day, carried into evening.)*
> *(Letitia holds up the claret. "The town will hear about this supper by Wednesday — Mrs. Pike's counter sees to that. Dress the rumor you want." Rose touches the blue damask — the estate's color, the color of whatever Monday chose. "The house is being restored," she says. "Let the house dress like it." The mended gloves go on last, the mend at the thumb, the grandmother's pearls at the throat. In the glass: the chatelaine of a building site, dressed for the muster.)*

scenes.synopsis: the village's parliament — Mrs. Pike's counter; the talk, and the dinners.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose walks down to the village before supper — the mistress showing herself on the first day of the work, the way Letitia insists is "quartermastering the rumor." Mrs. Pike's counter is the village's parliament, and Mrs. Pike presides with a pencil and opinions. "Miss Hartwell," she says. "The talk is the wall. My grandmother said that wall was old when she was a girl. What's in it, do they say?")*
> *("Stone, Mrs. Pike," Rose says. "Old stone, and older mortar." "Aye," Mrs. Pike says, unconvinced in the way of all parliaments. "Well. The village is glad of the work — the masons'll want their dinners, and dinners are my department." She wraps a parcel with brisk hands. "For the foreman's men, tomorrow. On the village — the wall comes down, the village feeds the men. That's the arrangement.")*

scenes.synopsis: the posting — Amos at the gatehouse; thirty years, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(Amos the porter is at his gatehouse when Rose walks down in the lamplight — Amos, who has opened the Park's gates for thirty years and closed them on everyone from bailiffs to brides. "Big week, miss," he says, touching his cap. "Masons at seven, dinners from the village, the wall coming down." He shakes his head at the garden's dark shape. "That wall's older than my service. Older than the dowager, some say, though I'd not say it where she hears.")*
> *("You'll keep the gate, Amos," Rose says, "whatever the week brings." "Aye, miss. That's the posting." He looks at her — the damask, the gloves, the general's uniform — and something like pride crosses the old face. "The Park's in good hands, miss. Has been since you took 'em." He opens the gate for her evening walk, and closes it behind her with the solid sound of thirty years' practice. The posting, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the verdict — two ways to take a wall down; the foreman's honest arithmetic.
scenes.prose:
> *(The foreman meets her at the wall at dusk with his estimate in his hand and his verdict in his mouth. "Two ways, miss," he says. "Stone by stone — we number every course, we lay her down gentle, we save what the wall can spare. Slow, dear, and honest. Or we pull her — ropes, tackle, a good team, and she's down by Thursday dinner. Fast, cheap, and the stone's fit for rubble." He looks at the wall the way men look at old horses. "She's earned the gentle way, if you've the purse for it.")*
> *(Rose does the arithmetic in her head — Octavia's tuition, priced by the course. Stone by stone means the wall gives up whatever it holds slowly, in order, numbered. Pulled down means Thursday dinner and rubble and no questions asked of the core. "And if there's —" she stops. "If there's what, miss?" the foreman asks. "Nothing," she says. "Old walls. Old stories." He nods like he hears old stories every week. "Aye. They all have 'em, miss. It's the mortar — it remembers.")*

scenes.synopsis: the manner debated — the quartermaster for the ropes; the watching, or the not-watching.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia, consulted at the dressing table, is firmly for the ropes. "Pull it down," the quartermaster says. "Thursday dinner and done. Stone by stone is a romance, miss — it costs by the course and it takes till Michaelmas, and meanwhile the garden's a building site and the men are underfoot." She pins up Rose's hair with decision in every pin. "The wall is a wall. It doesn't have feelings. It has mortar.")*
> *("The wall has a century," Rose says. "And the foreman says she's earned the gentle way." "The foreman," Letitia says, "is paid by the course, miss. Of course she's earned it — in his arithmetic." She steps back, considering. "But it's your wall, and your purse, and your —" she hesitates, "— whatever it is you're not saying about that wall. Stone by stone means you watch it come down. Ropes mean you don't have to." The pins, finished. "Choose the watching, or choose the not-watching. But choose.")*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE FAILING WALL: stone by stone, pulled down fast, or opened and looked at first.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the morning room at dusk, and the wall's fate is a line waiting to be written. Stone by stone: the gentle way, the numbered courses, the wall laid down like a patient — slow, dear, honest, and whatever the core holds comes out in order. Pull it down: ropes and tackle, down by Thursday, cheap and final — the rubble asks nothing. Or the third way, the one the foreman didn't offer because foremen don't offer it: open one course first, a single stone's width, and look — honestly look — before the choosing.)*
> *(Augusta's voice in her head: think of it as opening a letter. Letitia's: choose the watching, or choose the not-watching. Octavia's: begin with the walls. Rose picks up the pencil. The wall has stood a hundred years on habit; it can stand one more night while she decides how it falls.)*
> *(The pencil moves. The line is written — the wall's manner of falling, decided on a Monday evening. She sends word to the foreman's lodgings: tomorrow the wall comes down, and this is how.)*

scenes.synopsis: the blue dusk — the decision held; the wall's last night, granted.
scenes.prose:
> *(After the foreman's boy has run off with the order, Rose walks the garden alone in the blue dusk. The wall stands black against the sky, a hundred years of habit, one night left. She puts her palm to the stone once more — cold, the faint give beneath — and thinks of Augusta's figure — the letter, unopened. Tomorrow the masons come. Tomorrow the wall comes down, in whatever manner Monday chose.)*
> *(A blackbird sings once from the far wall and stops, as if it had thought better of it. Rose turns up the drive toward the lit windows — supper, the muster, the household. The wall keeps its shape in the dark, patient as a held breath — one more night of standing before the falling.)*

scenes.synopsis: the book, entered — Monday's decisions written fair; the house, tasked.
scenes.prose:
> *(Before supper, Letitia opens the household book at the kitchen table and writes Monday's decisions in her fairest hand — the restoration's order, the wall's manner, the week's muster. "The book remembers," she says, not looking up, "so the house doesn't have to." The pencil moves down the page: masons at seven, the wall's falling, the cottages' timber, the village's dinners. Every line a promise; every promise priced.)*
> *(Rose watches the quartermaster work and feels the day settle into order — the peculiar peace of being commanded by someone you trust. "There," Letitia says, blotting the page. "Monday, entered. The house knows what it's doing tomorrow." She closes the book with the gavel-thump. "And miss —" the pencil goes back behind the ear — "whatever that wall gives up, the house will stand it. We've stood worse." A flicker, almost a grin. "We stood the Season — the dowager's line, borrowed without leave.")*

scenes.synopsis: the violets — faithfulness at the wrist; the week's faces, proposed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes up while Rose dresses for supper with the week's posy — violets, deep purple, tied with a grey ribbon. "Faithfulness," she says, pinning one at Rose's wrist beside the mended glove. "The atelier's standing order, for the season: violets every Monday, for the wrist, for the work." The flowers are small and dark and exact. "The village will see them," Élise says. "Let the village read what it likes. Violets mean what they mean.")*
> *(Rose looks at the purple against the pearl-grey kid — the mend at the thumb, the flower at the wrist. "And if the week needs more than faithfulness?" she asks. Élise ties the ribbon with warm, certain hands. "Then the week will have it, and the violets will still be there. That's what standing orders are for." She steps back. "Now — the week's wearing. The atelier proposes three faces for the days ahead.")*

scenes.synopsis: supper — the muster in evening dress; the house, beginning again.
scenes.prose:
> *(Supper is the muster in evening dress: Augusta at the head of the table's conversation, Octavia precise over the soup, Letitia watching the service like a general reviewing troops, Julian quieter than at luncheon, Henry full of trowels, Laurent at Rose's right with the ease of a man who belongs there, Élise glowing at the far end among people who finally see her. The talk is of the week — the wall, the cottages, the party Saturday — and underneath the talk is the thing nobody says: the house is beginning again.)*
> *(Rose looks down the table — her household, her government, her people — and feels the day's decisions settle into something like peace. The order is chosen. The wall's manner is ordered. The violets are on her wrist and the mended gloves on her hands and the archive is open for the season. Letitia catches her eye and raises her glass a fraction — the quartermaster's salute. Rose raises hers, and drinks.)*

scenes.synopsis: the arithmetic — the fortune's shape; money, becoming something.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia stays late over the ledger, and the counsel comes with the figures attached — Octavia never gives one without the other. "The fortune covers the restoration," she says, "with margin, if the order holds. The wall is the dearest single item if you take it stone by stone — the foreman's honest, and honesty invoices." She turns a page. "The cottages are the cheapest and the most visible. The house is the dearest and the least urgent. There. That's the arithmetic. The affection is separate.")*
> *("And the affection?" Rose asks. Octavia looks up, and the precision softens by exactly one degree. "The affection is that you get to do this at all. A year ago the Park was a rumor and you were a scandal. Tonight you're choosing the order of the wounds with a pencil." She closes the ledger. "Spend it well, Rose. Money is only interesting when it's becoming something.")*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's verdict — Augusta judges the day; the gloves, recognized.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta holds court in the drawing room after supper with the particular authority of a woman who has outlived three sets of drawing-room fashions. She has watched the muster — the order, the wall's manner, the violets at Rose's wrist — and now she gives the verdict. "Well ordered," she says. "Letitia quartermasters, Octavia prices, Élise dresses, and you —" she looks at Rose over her tea, "— you choose. It's a better government than your grandfather ran. He chose, too, but he never let anyone watch.")*
> *(Her eyes drop to Rose's hands — the pearl-grey kid, the mend at the thumb — and stop. Something crosses the dowager's face: recognition, and then a smaller, rarer thing. "My gloves," Augusta says quietly. "I wondered where they'd gone." A beat. "Élise's mend is good. Wear them well, child." She picks up her tea. "Your grandfather kept his walls standing past their honesty. You're taking yours down in the open. That's the difference between you. Remember it when the wall talks.")*

scenes.synopsis: the evening walk — the romance before the devastation, tender and unpriced.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent walks her back up the drive in the dark, and the evening has the particular softness of a day well begun. He talks of the house party — Saturday, the half-restored Park as a stage, the ton coming to see what the fortune bought. "They'll come to judge," he says, "and stay to envy. It's the way of the world, and the world is welcome." His hand finds hers in the dark, easy as breathing. The mended glove, the warm hand. Neither of them mentions the wall.)*
> *(At the steps he stops, and for a moment the unknowing looks almost like wisdom — the man who loves the house without knowing its price. "Whatever this week costs you, Rose," he says quietly, "it won't cost you me." She looks at him in the lamplight — Laurent de Varenne, present and unknowing, the romance before the devastation — and holds his hand a moment longer than manners allow. "Monday's been kind," she says. It is the truest thing she can say, and the least true.)*

scenes.synopsis: Saturday, foreseen — the house party's dress, chosen while the atelier has the week.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise stays late with her sketchbook — the atelier thinks in weeks, and Saturday's house party is already on her page. "The Park's first stage," she says, "the half-restored house, the ton coming to look. The mistress must dress the rumor before the rumor dresses her." She turns the sketchbook: three faces for Saturday. The archive's full splendor — grandmother's lace, the rose silk, history worn like armor. The Hartwell blue, the household in the estate's color — the restoration, worn as a uniform. Or the atelier's newest work, shown on the mistress first — the present, dressed fresh.)*
> *(Rose studies the sketches — Élise's pencil, quick and sure, the gowns already half-real. "Saturday's five days away," she says. "Saturday," Élise says, "is four days of needlework away. Choose tonight, and the atelier begins tomorrow." The violets are still at Rose's wrist, the week still ahead. She touches the sketch she wants. The party, foreseen. The rumor, dressed in advance.)*

fashionChoices.detail: lace and rose silk; history, worn like armor.

fashionChoices.detail: the household in the estate's color; the restoration, uniformed.

fashionChoices.detail: Élise's work, shown first; the present, dressed fresh.

scenes.synopsis: the trowel, promised — the youngest gets his instrument; the garden, his.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry waylays her on the stairs with the persistence of a boy who has been saving up a question all evening. "The trowel," he says. "You said possible, under supervision. Was that a real possible or a grown-up possible?" Rose considers him — the youngest, enlisted at the garden gate at three, solemn as a surgeon with his palm on the failing wall. "A real possible," she says. "Under the foreman's supervision. The garden's yours to help, Henry — the wall comes down tomorrow, and somebody has to watch the small things.")*
> *("The small things," Henry repeats, trying the weight of it. "Like what?" "Like the string lines. Like the numbered stones, if we number them. Like —" she taps his nose, "— staying out from under." He grins, and the grin is the whole of Monday's reward. "I'll be the best under-stayer," he says, and races off to tell his pillow. The stairs, empty. The trowel, promised. The youngest, armed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the law, satisfied — the mason's contract signed; Monday's last instrument.
scenes.prose:
> *(Mr. Quill arrives at half past nine with the mason's contract in his bag and the law's patience in his manner — the solicitor who has papered every Hartwell decision since before Rose was born. "The restoration, in triplicate," he says, laying the contract on the morning-room desk. "The foreman's terms, the timetable, the penalties for haste." He taps the penalties. "I wrote those myself. Haste is the enemy of old stone.")*
> *(Rose signs where he points — the mistress's hand, three times, the ink still wet on Monday's last instrument. "The wall comes down tomorrow, Mr. Quill." "So the contract says," he says, sanding the signatures. "Signed, sealed, and —" he looks up, "— witnessed by whatever's inside it. Old walls, Miss Hartwell. They always have opinions." He bows himself out into the dark, the bag a little lighter, the law a little heavier.)*

scenes.synopsis: the beginning, dressed — the household dresses the Park's intent; the chapter's ritual.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the lamps — "begin as you mean to go on, miss. The house takes its tone from you.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the door — "the figures will keep. Tonight the intent keeps you.")*
> *(Story morsel: Augusta, at the stairs — "begin in the open, child. The house, too.")*
> *(Story morsel: Laurent, at the lamps — "whatever the wall costs — the house is worth it.")*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the door — "tomorrow's gloves get the extra stitch. For beginnings.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: Monday's work is chosen — the order set, the wall's manner ordered, the household assembled at one table. Tonight the house dresses its intent: what this restoration is for, worn on the body before a single stone moves. The great hall by lamplight, the whole household gathered, the Park's oldest wall standing its last night. Dress for the beginning: the archive's morning face carried into evening — deliberate, unafraid, honest about what the house is. Precise. Together. Begun. The house that begins together does not flinch apart.

scenes.synopsis: after the ritual — the intent, settled; the house, begun.
scenes.prose:
> *(The hall empties by lamplight, and Rose stands a moment in the direction she chose — the blue, the grey, the silk, worn — and feels the intent settle on her shoulders like a cloak that fits. The household has been dressed, fed, toasted, and steadied. The servants' hall is still humming. Somewhere, Letitia is turning down beds; somewhere, Octavia is copying figures by candlelight; somewhere, Augusta is — being Augusta, which needs no elaboration.)*
> *(Rose climbs the stairs slowly, the violets still at her wrist, the mended gloves in her hand. Monday is executed — the order, the wall, the muster. Tuesday will bring the masons at seven and the wall's falling, in whatever manner she ordered. She stops at the landing window and looks toward the garden's dark shape. One more night.)*

scenes.synopsis: the keeper, unnamed — who oversees the garden work; the week's last question.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia is waiting in the morning room with the week's last question — the quartermaster saves the hardest for last. "The garden work wants an overseer," she says. "The foreman knows stone, but the garden's yours, and someone must answer for it daily." She ticks the candidates on her fingers. "Me — the house runs itself by now, mostly. The foreman himself — the craft answers for the craft. Or you, miss — your eyes on it every day, the mistress in the mud.")*
> *(Rose considers the three. Letitia's discipline, the foreman's craft, her own daily walk — three kinds of keeping, three kinds of answer. "The wall comes down tomorrow," she says slowly. "Whatever it gives up —" she stops, and Letitia's pencil pauses above the book. "Whatever it gives up," Letitia repeats evenly, "someone should be there to see it. The book will want the name." The pencil waits. The keeper, unnamed.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE GARDEN'S KEEPER: Letitia, the foreman, or Rose herself.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone at midnight's edge, Rose does the last choosing of Monday. The garden's keeper: Letitia, and the quartermaster's discipline laid over the work like a plumb line — the house's answer. The foreman himself, and the craft's honor — the stone's answer, the gentle hands that know the wall's every course. Or herself, every day, her own eyes on the falling — the mistress's answer, the one who ordered it there to witness it.)*
> *(She thinks of the hollow she hasn't heard yet, the secret the wall keeps one more night, the letter Augusta says she's opening. Whoever keeps the garden will be the first to see what the wall gives up. The pencil is in her hand. The book is open. Letitia waits downstairs with the pencil ready. The name, written, is the week's last line.)*
> *(The name goes into the book in her own hand — the week's last line, the keeper appointed. Monday's choosing is done. Whatever Tuesday brings, it brings it to a garden that's watched.)*

options.label: Letitia oversees
options.detail: *Resolve+; the quartermaster's discipline.* The house's answer; the work, plumb-lined. *(Disciplined — and the household runs lean while she watches stone.)*

options.label: The foreman oversees
options.detail: *Mercy+; the craft's honor.* Trust the hands that know the wall; the gentle way, gently kept. *(Kind to the craft — and the wall's secrets come out in the mason's order, not hers.)*

options.label: Rose walks it daily herself
options.detail: *Candor+; the mistress's eyes.* Be there for whatever the wall gives up; face it first-hand. *(Honest — and the first sight of the secret will be hers alone, unsoftened.)*

scenes.synopsis: the tenants' report — Julian returns with the rent-book; the brother, proving.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian comes in late with the rent-book under his arm and mud on his boots — the brother who knocks on doors, returned from the knocking. "Number four's thatch wants doing before the rains," he reports. "The well at the lane's end wants a new windlass. The Millers want to know if the cottages are first or second, and I told them the book has the order and the book doesn't gossip." He sets the book down. "Did I do it right?")*
> *("You did it exactly right," Rose says, and means it. Something in his face eases — the standing-about afterward, managed, for once. "Tomorrow the wall comes down," she tells him. "Come and watch it, if the tenants can spare you." "The tenants," Julian says with dignity, "can spare me for a wall." He takes up the lamp. The rent-book, closed. The brother, proving.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Bell's Monday paragraph; ordinary restoration news, no scandal yet.
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting is the Gazette's Monday paragraph, read at the morning-room desk before bed — Bell's paper, noting the season's ordinary news.)*
> *(Rose reads it twice, the way she reads everything Bell writes, and finds no edge in it — no leader, no verdict, no favorite story. Just the facts, set in Bell's type: the muster, the survey, the wall. The paper covers the Season; the Season, this Monday, is stone and timber. She folds the Gazette and sets it by the memorandum book. Ordinary news. The last ordinary news, though she doesn't know it.)*
scenes.sting: the sting — Bell's Monday paragraph; ordinary restoration news, no scandal yet.

scenes.synopsis: the proprietor's note — Bell states her terms; the paper, unowned.
scenes.prose:
> *(Bell's note comes with the Gazette, in the proprietor's own blunt hand: "Miss Hartwell — The restoration is news, so we print it. When it's more than news, we'll print that too. The paper doesn't take sides on stonework. — N. Bell." Rose reads the note twice and laughs — once, shortly. It is the most honest thing anyone has sent her all day that wasn't a bill.)*
> *(She writes back three lines: the masons at seven, the village's dinners, the wall's manner — the facts, for the record. "The Gazette covers the Season," she says aloud to the empty room, sealing the note. "Let it." She gives the reply to the morning's post-boy with the Gazette. Bell will print what she prints. The verdict, whatever it becomes, can't be bought — but tonight, mercifully, there's no verdict to buy. Only stone.)*

scenes.synopsis: Tuesday's dawn, dressed — the mistress arms herself for the wall's falling.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia lays out the dawn's choices with the gravity of a woman arming a soldier: the green wool, pressed, the garden's color — the work, continued. The Hartwell blue, severe — the estate's color, the wall faced in state. The re-cut habit, the elbows reinforced — the archive, put to work. "The men muster at seven," Letitia says. "The mistress at half past, dressed for whatever the wall decides to be.")*
> *(Rose touches each in turn — the wool's hardiness, the damask's severity, the habit's history. Tomorrow the oldest wall comes down, in the manner Monday chose, under the keeper Monday named. "The wall gets its last night," she says. "I get the dawn." The mended gloves are laid beside the chosen gown, the violets' ribbon re-tied. In the glass, tomorrow's mistress, dressed ahead of time.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the archive at labor; the past, working.

scenes.synopsis: the day's close — the goodnight; the romance, intact for one more night.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent finds her at the landing window, looking toward the garden, and doesn't ask what she's looking at — the particular grace of him, tonight. "Monday's done," he says. "The house is mustered, the wall is condemned, the violets are deployed." He offers his arm. "Walk me to my door, General. The civilian is for bed.")*
> *(They walk the corridor in lamplight, unhurried, his hand over hers on his arm. At his door he stops — he stays the week, the guest wing, the unknowing guest. "Whatever the wall gives up," he says lightly, "it'll still be your wall." She smiles. "Good night, Laurent." "Good night, Rose." The door closes. The corridor is quiet. The day's close, tender and unpriced — the romance before the devastation, intact for one more night.)*

scenes.synopsis: the last round — the Park at night; the wall, unanswering.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose walks the Park once more before bed — the mistress's last round, the general's inspection. The house is dark behind her, the garden darker ahead, the wall a black line against the stars. Somewhere in the village a dog barks once. The air smells of cut grass and coming rain. Monday has been executed — every line written, every keeper named, every gown chosen.)*
> *(She stands at the garden gate and listens. Nothing moves. The wall keeps its shape in the dark, patient, habitual — one more night of standing before the falling. She thinks of the letter Augusta says she's opening, of Letitia's book, of Octavia's page now filled. "Tomorrow," she says aloud, to the wall, to the dark. The wall doesn't answer. Walls never do — until they do.)*

scenes.synopsis: the hollow — the wall comes down tomorrow, and the core sounds wrong.
scenes.prose: > *(The foreman comes up the drive at half past ten — too late for a social call, the right time for a mason's worry. He has been at the wall with a lamp, he says, making his marks for the morning. "Miss," he says, and his knuckles rap the air the way they rapped the stone, "there's a hollow in the core. North stretch, third course down. Stone shouldn't sound like that." He meets her eyes. "Thought you'd want to know before the men muster. The wall comes down at seven — and there's a hollow sound in the wall's core.")*

scenes.synopsis: the hollow, remembered — Tuesday dawn; the masons at seven; the night's report, carried into the morning.
scenes.prose:
> *(Tuesday comes in grey and early, the light flat on the Park the way it was Monday — a week, apparently, that means business. Rose is awake before the maid knocks, which is becoming a habit she does not care for. Half past ten last night: the foreman up the drive with his lamp still in his hand, his knuckles rapping the air. A hollow in the core, north stretch, third course down. She has heard the words all night, in the spaces between sleep.)*
> *(She dresses in the gown Letitia laid out — the dawn's armor, chosen ahead — and pulls on the mended gloves, Augusta's pearl-grey kid, the mend at the thumb. The garden is still dark beyond the window. The wall stands where it stood, on its habit, and somewhere inside a hundred years of stone there is a hollow where a hollow should not be. Seven o'clock. The men muster. She goes down.)*

scenes.synopsis: the morning's kit — the mistress arms herself for the falling; veil, shawl, or apron.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia is in the dressing room with the morning's kit laid out like instruments: the dust-veil, fine gauze on a wire frame, for the stone dust; the work shawl, grey wool, to throw over the morning's gown; the plain Holland apron, tied at the waist, undisguised labor. "The wall comes down today," Letitia says, "and the mistress goes to watch it. The dust will have opinions about the gown. Choose your defense, miss.")*
> *(Rose touches each — the veil's lightness, the shawl's warmth, the apron's honesty. Outside, the first carts are on the drive. "The wall gets the day," she says. "I get the kit." Letitia ties or pins or drapes, as ordered, and stands back. "There," she says. "The general, equipped. Try not to catch a falling stone, miss. The book has no column for it.")*

fashionChoices.label: The dust-veil
fashionChoices.detail: gauze against the stone dust; the mistress, veiled for labor.

fashionChoices.label: The work shawl
fashionChoices.detail: grey wool over the morning's gown; the gown, protected.

fashionChoices.detail: Holland, tied at the waist; the work, undisguised.

scenes.synopsis: the muster — seven o'clock at the wall; the hollow stretch, worked careful; Henry's trowel, employed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Seven o'clock at the north stretch, and the foreman's men are mustered with their tackle and their numbering chalk, and Henry is among them with his trowel held like a sceptre, under the foreman's eye as promised. The foreman walks Rose to the third course down and lays his palm where the hollow sounded. "We take this stretch the careful way, miss," he says. "Course by course, every stone numbered, whatever Monday's order said about the rest. A hollow's a hollow. The craft doesn't argue with it.")*
> *(Rose nods. The contract's penalties for haste sit in Quill's bag at the house; the foreman's own caution does the work better. "The numbered stones go where?" she asks. "Stacked by course on the south lawn, miss. Laid like patients," he says, and Henry — solemn, trowel aloft — repeats, "Like patients," and the men smile into their beards. The first stone comes free with a sound like a book closing. The wall begins to give up its century.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dinners — the village feeds the men; Mrs. Pike's department, delivered.
scenes.prose:
> *(Mrs. Pike arrives at eight with the first of the dinners in a cart — the village's department, as promised Monday. Pies, bread, a ham the size of a hassock, cheese, apples. "The men eat at noon and the wall eats nothing," Mrs. Pike says, directing the unloading like a field marshal. "My grandmother said that wall was old when she was a girl, Miss Hartwell, and she never once said what was in it. Villages notice walls. They notice what's in them, too.")*
> *("Stone, Mrs. Pike," Rose says. "Old stone." "Aye," Mrs. Pike says, in the tone of a woman filing the answer for later. She hands Rose a paper twist. "For the mistress's pocket — gingerbread. Watching walls is hungry work." The cart rattles off up the lane. The gingerbread goes in her pocket, and stays there all day.)*

scenes.synopsis: the day's counsel — Octavia on watching, money, and the village's eyes.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes at nine with the memorandum book and stands at the garden's edge watching the numbering go on — chalk, lift, stack. "The foreman's honest," she says. "Honesty invoices by the course, but it also keeps its eyes open. Counsel, and it costs nothing: whatever that hollow gives up today, the village must not be the first to know it. Mrs. Pike's dinners come with Mrs. Pike's ears.")*
> *("The dinners are the village's kindness," Rose says. "The ears are the village's nature," Octavia says. "Both can be true. Keep the men fed and the core unwatched — post Henry at the string lines, post the keeper at the gap, and let the village watch the stones come down. Stones are excellent theater. Cores are not." She makes a note. "And Rose — if the hollow pays out in anything but air, you tell me before supper. The figures and the facts travel together.")*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE FIND: the hollow opens mid-morning; the bundle in the core; draw it out, seal it till morning, or keep it household-quiet.
scenes.prose:
> *(Mid-morning, and the foreman's whistle comes three short blasts — the signal agreed for the hollow. Rose crosses the garden at a run she would not admit to, Henry at her heels with the trowel, and finds the men stood back from the third course in a ring, the foreman on his knees with his lamp. The hollow is open. In the core of the wall, where no hollow should be, there is a cavity the size of a bread oven — and in it a bundle, oilskin-wrapped, heavy with lead lining, the shape of papers within. Walled up a generation ago. Waiting.)*
> *(The garden goes very quiet. The men look at the foreman; the foreman looks at Rose. Three ways offer themselves. Draw it out now: lift the bundle into daylight, here, before witnesses — the honest handling of the cavity, the papers' seals left whole till Wednesday. Seal it back till morning: close the cavity, set a watch, let no hand touch it till the ordered opening — the patience of a house that can wait one more night. Or tell no one outside the household: the bundle lifted at dusk under cloth, the men kept from the gap, the village given the wall and nothing else — the keeping, quiet. She looks at the bundle in its hundred-year dark. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(The order goes to the foreman in a low voice, and the garden rearranges itself around it — the men to their stations, the cavity to its fate, the bundle to its keeping. Whatever Tuesday chose about the manner, one law holds the day entire: the bundle's seal is not broken. Not today. Tuesday may look, or wait, or hide — but Wednesday opens it. The foreman nods, once, and the work goes on around the hollow like water around a stone.)*

options.label: Draw it out and look
options.detail: *Candor+; the cavity, opened.* Lift the bundle into daylight before witnesses; the honest handling. *(Open — and the papers' seals stay whole till Wednesday; Tuesday looks, Wednesday reads.)*

options.label: Seal it back till morning
options.detail: *Resolve+; the patience, ordered.* Close the cavity, set the watch; no hand touches it till the opening. *(Patient — and the wall keeps its secret one more night, guarded.)*

options.label: Tell no one outside the household
options.detail: *Cunning+; the keeping, quiet.* The dusk lifting, household only; the village gets the wall, not the find. *(Quiet — and the men are kept from the gap, the talk kept from the lane.)*

scenes.synopsis: the small things — Henry at the string lines; the numbered courses, growing.
scenes.prose:
> *(By eleven the south lawn is growing a wall in reverse — the numbered courses stacked in order, chalk figures bright on old stone, Henry presiding over the string lines with his trowel and a gravity borrowed from the foreman. "Forty-one, forty-two," he counts, pointing with the trowel, and a mason twice his size moves the stone where pointed. Rose watches from the garden's edge and finds the sight doing something to her chest she did not order.)*
> *("Miss," Henry says, very low, coming over with dust on his nose, "the hollow one had a number. Forty-seven. I wrote it in my book." He shows her: a child's notebook, the figures wobbling. "Good," Rose says, and means it more than most things said today. "Forty-seven is the most important stone in the county, Henry. Guard your book." He nods, and goes back to his lines, and the wall keeps coming down in order around the place where the secret sits.)*

scenes.synopsis: the keeper's line — the garden's watch, ordered; Letitia's book, entered.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia meets her at the garden gate with the household book open and the keeper's line waiting — Monday's last decision, to be executed Tuesday. "The watch is set as the book orders," Letitia says. "The men work the south courses; the hollow stretch is the foreman's own hands only; the gap is never unwatched." She shuts the book. "And miss — whatever Monday's keeper decided about the manner of it, the garden is watched. The book has the name. The name has the garden.")*
> *("The village?" Rose asks. "The village," Letitia says, "is watching the stones come down, which is what villages are for. Mrs. Pike's dinners are excellent theater." She looks toward the north stretch. "And the —" she does not say bundle, "— the hollow's business is the household's business. The book says so." The pencil goes behind the ear, and Letitia goes back to the house, and the garden is watched.)*

scenes.synopsis: the tenants' brother — Julian from the cottages; the wall, witnessed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian comes up from the lane at noon with the rent-book under his arm and stops at the garden gate the way men stop at church doors — uncertain whether he's wanted. "The tenants can spare me," he says. "Number four's thatch is ordered. The well wants its windlass. I thought —" he looks at the stacked courses, "— I thought I'd watch a wall come down. I've never watched one.")*
> *("Stand by me, then," Rose says, "and watch it properly." They stand together while the courses come down in order, and Julian is quiet in the particular way of a man who is learning that watching is also a kind of work. "It's careful," he says at last. "I expected — ropes. Noise." "The wall earned the careful way," Rose says. "Everything here seems to earn things," he says. They stand together, and the wall comes down in order, and neither of them says anything else for a while.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dust, answered — Élise brings the midday change; the gown, or the sense.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at midday with dust on her own sleeves and a bundle over her arm — the atelier's answer to a morning among stones. "The morning's gown has done its duty, miss," she says, "and now the dust is winning. The atelier proposes the midday change." Three defenses on the bench: the linen kerchief for the hair, plain and defiant; the spare working gown, archive cotton, cut for labor; or nothing — the gown takes the dust, and the dust takes the gown.)*
> *(Rose looks down at herself — the morning's gown, the shawl, the stone dust already filming the hem. "The gown was laid out for a wall's falling," she says. Élise nods. "Which is why the atelier brought the cotton. Letitia," she says gently, "would rather her laying-out survived the wall." The kerchief, the gown, or the dust. Élise waits, warm and practical, the atelier's whole philosophy in her hands.)*

fashionChoices.label: The linen kerchief
fashionChoices.detail: plain and defiant; the dust, defied at the hair.

fashionChoices.label: The spare working gown
fashionChoices.detail: archive cotton, cut for labor; the morning's gown, spared.

fashionChoices.label: Nothing
fashionChoices.detail: the gown takes the dust; the archive, in the trenches.

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's inspection — Augusta comes to see the wall; the terms, remembered.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta comes at one o'clock in the barouche, because dowagers do not walk to building sites, and surveys the fallen courses from the garden gate with her lorgnette. "Older than I am," she says at last. "You told me first, and now I see it down. The terms are honored twice over." She lowers the lorgnette. "And the hollow your foreman found? The men are very careful around one particular stretch, child. Even I can see the choreography.")*
> *("The core was unsound," Rose says. Augusta regards her — the long, level look that has ended engagements. "Unsound," the dowager repeats. "Well. Your grandfather kept that wall standing past its honesty, and now it repays him by being interesting." She settles back. "You will tell me, Rose. Not today — today you have masons. But you will tell me." The barouche turns for the house. The lorgnette goes back in its case.)*

scenes.synopsis: the trowel's noon — Henry's report; the small things, counted.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry finds her at the stacked courses with his notebook and a face of tremendous importance. "The small things, miss — I mean, Rose," he corrects himself, and reports: forty-nine stones numbered, three string lines straight, one mason's dinner eaten (his own, at noon, with the men), and the hollow stone — forty-seven — watched all morning without blinking. "I blinked once," he admits. "At the pie.")*
> *(Rose inspects the notebook — the wobbling figures, the pie crumb. "A watch that blinks at pie is still a watch," she says gravely. "The foreman blinks at pie. Everyone blinks at Mrs. Pike's pie." Henry considers this absolution and pockets the book. "Tomorrow can I watch the —" he stops. "Tomorrow," Rose says, "there will be watching." He races off, trowel aloft, and the garden is louder for him.)*

scenes.synopsis: the cavity debated — the craft's counsel against the mistress's order; the stretch first, then dusk.
scenes.prose:
> *(The foreman asks for a word at two o'clock, man to mistress, with his cap in his hands. "Miss," he says, "the craft has a counsel, and you'll take it or leave it. That cavity's old work — older than the wall around it, I'd say, the lining lead, the wrapping oilskin. Whatever's in it has waited a generation. It can wait till the wall's down entire. My counsel: we finish the stretch, we lift the whole, we don't pick at the core till the courses are clear.")*
> *("And if I want it lifted at dusk?" Rose asks. The foreman turns the cap in his hands. "Then we lift it at dusk, miss, careful as christening. But the craft says: a wall gives up its secrets cleanest when it's all the way down. Picking at the core with the courses above it —" he shakes his head, "— that's how stones slip, and how men get curious." He meets her eyes. "Your wall, miss. Your order. The craft has spoken; the mistress decides.")*

scenes.synopsis: the unknowing, at midday — Laurent at the garden; the ease, and the abstraction.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent finds her at three by the stacked courses, and stops the way Julian stopped — only Laurent does not stop uncertainly. He stops the way a man stops at a painting. "The wall in reverse," he says. "You are numbering the century, Rose. It is the most you thing I have ever seen." He offers his arm. "Walk with the civilian. The general has been generaling since seven.")*
> *(They walk the south lawn, and he talks of the party Saturday — the half-restored Park as a stage, the ton coming to look — and she answers, and does not answer, her eyes going back to the north stretch the way a tongue goes to a loose tooth. "You are elsewhere," he says at last, not reproachfully. "I am counting stones," she says, which is true as far as it goes. "Count them beautifully, then," he says. "It is your best look." He squeezes her arm, and they walk on, and the north stretch keeps its counsel.)*

scenes.synopsis: the afternoon's face — the lane brings watchers; the mistress, faced for the village.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia waylays her at half past three with the afternoon's question. "The lane has had eleven souls past the gate since noon," the quartermaster reports. "Amos counts. The village is watching the theater, miss, and the theater should dress for it." Three faces on the bench: the Hartwell blue, severe — the estate's color, the wall faced in state; the morning's gown, kept — the day, unbroken into evening; or the labor worn openly — shawl, veil, and dust, the mistress undisguised.)*
> *("Dress the watching," Letitia says. "The village will describe you at supper, and the description should be the one you chose." Rose looks down at the morning's gown — the dust, the honest wreck of the hours. The blue waits, severe and splendid. The labor waits, honest and filmed. She chooses the afternoon's face.)*

scenes.synopsis: the gate, kept — Amos counts the watchers; the posting, Tuesday's.
scenes.prose:
> *(Amos is at his gatehouse at four with his tally stick — eleven notches, as reported. "Watchers, miss," he says, touching his cap. "Respectful ones. The Millers' boy, the blacksmith's wife, two from the Crown. Nobody past the gate but the dinners." He looks down the lane. "Thirty years I've kept this gate, miss, and never had to keep it against curiosity. Curiosity," he says, "is harder than bailiffs. Bailiffs knock.")*
> *("Keep it against the curious too, Amos," Rose says. "Aye, miss. That's the posting." He shows her the tally stick. "I'll keep the count, miss. The book likes a count." She smiles — Letitia's doctrine, everywhere. "The book does," she says. The gate stands open for the lane and closed for the garden, and Amos, between, keeps the difference.)*

scenes.synopsis: the afternoon's rhythm — the wall, mostly down; the gap, waiting.
scenes.prose:
> *(At five the north stretch is mostly down — the courses numbered and stacked, the gap in the garden's wall like a missing tooth, the cavity's stretch the foreman's own hands only, as ordered. Rose walks the line of the fallen wall alone, her hand trailing the stacked stones, each chalk number bright. Forty-seven sits apart, watched, its hollow dark behind the numbering.)*
> *(The garden feels larger with the wall down — the wind off the fields coming in where a century kept it out, the light changed, the prospect altered. She stands in the gap and looks out at the Park, and the Park looks back, and for a moment the mistress and the estate regard each other across the place where the secret sat. The wind moves her skirts, and the gap says nothing, and the garden keeps its counsel.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE MASONS: the men know; pay for silence, trust their loyalty, or send them home.
scenes.prose:
> *(Late afternoon, and the stretch is down, and the men are paid by the day and standing easy — and they know. They saw the hollow opened; they saw the ring stand back; they saw the choreography. Whatever Tuesday chose about the manner of the finding, the finding had witnesses. The foreman waits for the word on his men. Three ways.)*
> *(Pay for the silence: extra coin in every hand tonight, the foreman's distribution, the understanding plain — the wall's business is the house's business. Octavia will price it; the purse will feel it. Trust the loyalty: take the men's word as the county takes a man's word — they are Hartwell men, most of them, and loyalty is cheaper than coin and dearer to keep. Or send them home: the work pauses, the tools shouldered, the gap left to the household's watch — the wall waits, and the county notices the pause, and Wednesday begins quieter. She looks at the men, easy in the dusk. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(The word goes to the foreman, and he carries it to the men — the coin, the trust, or the dismissal, as Tuesday ordered. They take it as men take orders from a mistress who has watched a wall come down beside them all day: straight. The stretch stands empty. The tools are shouldered, the orders carried, and the gap belongs to the house.)*

options.label: Pay extra for silence
options.detail: *Cunning+; the quiet, bought.* Coin in every hand; the understanding, plain. *(Bought — and Octavia will price it, and the purse will feel it.)*

options.label: Trust their loyalty
options.detail: *Mercy+; the word, taken.* Hartwell men, the county's word; loyalty, kept. *(Kind — and the village will know something by supper, because villages do.)*

options.label: Send them home
options.detail: *Resolve+; the work, paused.* Tools shouldered; the gap, household-watched. *(Decided — and the wall waits a day, and the county marks the pause.)*

scenes.synopsis: the book, entered — Tuesday's watching and finding, written fair.
scenes.prose:
> *(Before supper, Letitia opens the household book at the kitchen table and writes Tuesday in her fairest hand — the wall's falling, the courses numbered, the dinners eaten, the watch set, the gap. The finding she writes as "the hollow's business," which is the book's way of knowing without saying. "The book remembers," she says, not looking up, "so the house doesn't have to gossip.")*
> *("And the men?" Rose asks. "The men," Letitia says, "are entered as Tuesday ordered — paid, trusted, or dismissed." She blots the page. "Whatever the order was, miss, the book holds it, and the house stands it." She closes the book with the gavel-thump. "And the bundle —" she does not look up, "— the bundle is the household's. The book says so." The pencil goes behind the ear. The book lies closed on the kitchen table, holding the day.)*

scenes.synopsis: the kept thing — the cavity at dusk's edge; the secret, unopened.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose walks to the gap alone before supper, while the light is still good. The cavity sits in the core's dark, the bundle in it — oilskin, lead-heavy, the papers' shape within — under the foreman's canvas and the keeper's watch. She does not touch it. Tuesday's law, by her own order: the seal unbroken. She stands a moment with her hands behind her back, like a visitor in a museum of her own family's making.)*
> *(A generation ago someone walled this up — hands she never knew, for reasons no one told. Elias's generation. The thought sits beside her, quiet, and she lets it sit; Wednesday is for longer thoughts. The canvas, the watch, the dark. Her hands stay behind her back.)*

scenes.synopsis: the brother's question — Julian asks what was in the hollow; the deflecting, kind.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian finds her at the supper table's edge before the others come down, and asks it straight, the way brothers do. "The men stood back in a ring at mid-morning," he says. "Henry says stone forty-seven is the most important stone in the county. Rose — what was in the hollow?" He looks at her with the rent-book still under his arm, the tenants' brother, the knocking brother, asking for the truth the way he asks for everything: plainly.)*
> *("Stone, Julian," Rose says. "Old stone, and older mortar." "That's Mrs. Pike's answer," he says. "It's everyone's answer," she says, "until Wednesday." He studies her — the sister who gave him the tenants and the keys — and nods slowly. "Wednesday, then," he says. "I'll knock on doors till Wednesday, and on Wednesday I'll knock on yours." He almost smiles. "Fair?" "Fair," she says. He takes up the rent-book, and the question goes back in his pocket with it.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's tea — Augusta suspects; the telling, scheduled.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta takes tea in the blue drawing room at six and sends for Rose, which means what it always means. "The barouche driver," the dowager says without preamble, "counts eleven souls at the gate. The cook counts forty-nine stones on the south lawn. The house counts one granddaughter who has been at the garden since seven with the look of a woman keeping something." She pours. "I have kept this house's secrets since before you were born, Rose. Do not keep this one from me longer than you must.")*
> *("Wednesday," Rose says. "The opening is Wednesday, Grandmama. You will be told —" she holds the dowager's eyes, "— before anyone outside this house." Augusta considers this — the terms, extended, honored in advance. "Wednesday," she says at last. "I shall be in the blue drawing room at ten, and you will come." She lifts her cup. "Your grandfather walled up more than garden walls, child. Remember it when the bundle talks." The chocolate is still warm. The interview is over.)*

scenes.synopsis: the supper dress — the day's end, dressed; the archive's evening face.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes up at half past six with the supper choices, and the atelier has been thinking. "The day's work is done, miss, and the evening wants its own face." Three on the bed: the claret silk, her mother's, re-cut to the shoulder — the evenings, claimed; the blue damask, the grandmother's — the estate's color, severe and splendid; the grey wool, the day's own — the work, carried to table.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret — the mother's silk, the archive's boldest. The day has been dust and canvas and kept things; the evening can be the archive, dressed. "The mended gloves with it," Élise says, laying them out, Augusta's pearl-grey kid, the mend at the thumb. "The emblem goes to supper too." In the glass: the mistress of the kept thing, dressed for the household.)*

scenes.synopsis: the abstraction, loved — the evening walk; the unknowing, held.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent walks her to the garden gate after supper, and the dusk is the color of the claret silk. He does not ask about the hollow, or the ring of men, or the canvas — the particular grace of him, again, or the particular blindness. "You have been counting stones all day," he says. "Have you finished?" "The wall is down," she says. "And the secret?" he asks lightly. "There is no secret," she says. "There is a wall, down." He laughs. "The general, debriefing.")*
> *(At the gate he stops, and the gap is behind them, dark, the canvas just visible. His hand finds hers. "Whatever Tuesday cost you, Rose," he says, "it hasn't cost you me." She looks at him — Laurent de Varenne, present and unknowing, the romance before the devastation — and the kept thing sits between them like a third person at the gate. She holds his hand. "Then let the evening be short," she says. He smiles. They walk on.)*

scenes.synopsis: the quartermaster's counsel — the night's order; Wednesday, arranged.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia comes to the morning room at eight with the night's order and the week's counsel together. "The watch," she says. "Two footmen at the gap till the lifting, the foreman's boy with the lamp, the household's eyes only. The dusk lifting: the foreman and two men, yourself, myself, and no one else at the garden. The bundle to the morning room, under cloth, till Wednesday." She ticks it off. "Counsel, miss, and it costs nothing: open it Wednesday with witnesses. Octavia for the figures, Quill for the law, Augusta —" she pauses, "— Augusta because she is Augusta.")*
> *("And Laurent?" Rose asks. Letitia's pencil stops. "The Frenchman," she says carefully, "is a guest in your house and —" she chooses the words the way she chooses gloves, "— the week's romance. Wednesday's opening is the family's business. The family, miss, is blood." She resumes ticking. "The bundle under cloth tonight. The witnesses Wednesday. The book has it all." The counsel, given. The night, ordered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening's figures — Octavia prices the day; the silence, costed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia stays late over the ledger, and the day's figures come with the counsel attached, as always. "The wall: the careful way, by the course, as ordered — the foreman's honest, and honesty invoices." She turns a page. "The dinners: the village's gift, priced at nothing and worth everything. The silence —" she looks up, "— if Tuesday bought it, it's entered here. If Tuesday trusted it, it's entered nowhere, which is also a price." The pencil taps. "Money is only interesting when it's becoming something, Rose. Today it became a quiet wall.")*
> *("And Wednesday?" Rose asks. "Wednesday," Octavia says, "is the opening, and the opening is priced in witnesses, not coin. Bring Quill. Bring the dowager. Bring me." She closes the ledger. The pencil goes in the pocket. The figures sleep till morning.)*

scenes.synopsis: the trowel's report — Henry's day, rendered; the boy, dismissed to bed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry waylays her on the stairs at half past eight with the day's final report, delivered standing at attention. "Forty-nine stones, miss — Rose. Three lines straight. The hollow's business watched till the foreman covered it. The trowel —" he holds it up, "— employed all day, under supervision, as promised." He salutes with it, nearly taking his own cap off.)*
> *("Dismissed to bed, guardsman," Rose says. "The wall will keep till morning." "The gap won't be unwatched?" he asks, suddenly small. "Two footmen, a lamp, and the foreman's boy," she says. "The most watched gap in England." He nods, satisfied, and races upstairs, and the stairs are empty, and the house exhales.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dusk wrap — the carrying, dressed; seen, or unseen.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia lays out the dusk's choices with the gravity of a woman dressing a mission: the grey cloak, hooded and plain — the carrying, unseen; the black silk shawl, respectable — the dusk, faced in state; the work shawl, the day's own — the labor, undisguised to the last. "The bundle comes up at dusk, miss," Letitia says. "The mistress walks with it. Dress the walking.")*
> *(Rose touches the grey cloak — the hood, the plainness, the vanishing. The black silk waits, severe. The work shawl smells of the day's dust. "The house carries its own," she says. Letitia drapes, or pins, or settles, as ordered. "There," she says. "The keeper, wrapped. Try not to look like a conspiracy, miss. The dusk has eyes.")*

scenes.synopsis: the foreman's word — the lifting, arranged; the craft's honor, given.
scenes.prose:
> *(The foreman meets her at the gap at dusk's edge with his two chosen men and the tackle for a careful lift. "Two men, miss, my steadiest. The canvas stays till the last. We lift it like christening, as promised." He looks at the cavity — the day's long labor around it. "Thirty years I've laid stone, miss, and never lifted a secret out of a wall. The craft," he says, "didn't train me for this. But the craft says: steady.")*
> *("Steady," Rose agrees. He nods, and the men take their stations, and the lamp is lit against the coming dark. "Whatever's in the wrapping, miss," the foreman says quietly, "it was put there by hands that wanted it kept. We'll hand it to hands that know how." He touches his cap. The word, given. The lifting, arranged.)*

scenes.synopsis: the keeping, dressed — the household dresses the secret's keeping; the chapter's ritual.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the gap — "keep as you mean to go on, miss. The house takes its tone from you.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the stones — "the figures will keep. Tonight the keeping keeps you.")*
> *(Story morsel: Augusta, at the gate — "keep in the open, child. The house, too.")*
> *(Story morsel: Laurent, at the lamps — "whatever the keeping costs — the house is worth it.")*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the door — "tomorrow's gloves get the extra stitch. For Wednesday.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: Tuesday's wall is down — course by course, the stones numbered and stacked, and the oldest work has given up what it held. The find sits in the core under canvas and watch, and at dusk it comes to the house. Before the lifting, the household gathers at the gap and dresses the keeping — what it means to hold a thing sealed. The garden at the day's end, the gap like a held breath, the men gone or paid or trusted, the stones in their rows. Dress for the keeping: dusk's colors, worn plain, eyes open. Precise. Together. Sealed. The house that keeps together does not flinch apart.

scenes.synopsis: after the ritual — the keeping, settled; the dusk, deepening.
scenes.prose:
> *(The household disperses from the gap by lamplight, and Rose stands a moment in the direction she chose — the grey, the blue, the silk, worn — and feels the keeping settle on her shoulders like the cloak she chose for the walking. The footmen take their posts. The foreman's boy trims the lamp. Somewhere, Letitia is locking the morning room; somewhere, Octavia is copying figures by candlelight; somewhere, Augusta is composing Wednesday's verdict.)*
> *(Rose looks once more at the canvas in the core's dark, the bundle's shape beneath it. An hour, maybe less, till the lifting. She turns up toward the house, where the lamps are lit and supper's remnants are being cleared. The dusk deepens around the gap, and the keeping holds its shape.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE GAP: rebuild the wall at once, leave it open, or stack the stones and wait.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone at the gap's edge, and the wall's future is a line waiting to be written. The north stretch is down, the courses numbered and stacked on the south lawn, the garden open to the fields where a century kept it shut. Three futures for the gap. Rebuild at once: the stones re-laid in their numbered order, the wall whole again by week's end — the order, restored, the hiding place erased, the garden as it was. Leave it open: the gap kept, the garden breathing through it, the wound shown — the honest prospect, and Saturday's party seeing exactly what the week cost.)*
> *(Or the third way: stack the stones and wait — no decision tonight, the courses kept in their rows, the masons' hands rested, the gap guarded till Wednesday's opening decides it. Augusta's voice: when the wall talks. Letitia's: the book will want the line. Octavia's: money is only interesting when it's becoming something. Rose looks at the gap, at the dark beyond it, at the house behind her. The pencil is in her hand. The line, waiting.)*
> *(The line goes into the memorandum book — the gap's future, decided at dusk. Letitia takes the book, and the pencil comes out from behind her ear.)*

options.label: Rebuild at once
options.detail: *Resolve+; the order, restored.* The numbered courses re-laid; the wall, whole again. *(Decided — and the hiding place erased, the garden as it was.)*

options.label: Leave it open
options.detail: *Candor+; the wound, shown.* The garden breathing through the gap; the prospect, honest. *(Honest — and Saturday's party will see exactly what the week cost.)*

options.label: Stack the stones and wait
options.detail: *Mercy+; the deciding, rested.* No night decision; Wednesday's opening settles it. *(Kind — and the gap stays guarded, the choosing kept for daylight.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Wednesday order — the opening, arranged; the bundle's night, assigned.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia receives the gap's order and folds it into the Wednesday plan without breaking stride. "The opening," she says, the pencil moving. "Wednesday, ten o'clock, the morning room. The witnesses as counseled — Octavia, Quill, the dowager. The bundle under cloth in the morning room tonight, the door locked, the key —" she looks up, "— in your pocket, miss, not the book's. Some things the book doesn't hold.")*
> *("And the men?" Rose asks. "The men are Tuesday's order, entered." Letitia blots the page. "Wednesday's order is the opening. Thursday's is the wall's future, as dusk decided." She closes the book. "The week, miss, is behaving like a ledger. Debits of stone, credits of —" she does not say secrets, "— of Wednesday." The pencil goes behind the ear. The opening, arranged.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's leave — Augusta's last word; the telling, promised.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends for her at half past eight — the blue drawing room, the chocolate, the eyebrow at full mast. "The household," the dowager says, "has been dressing the dusk like a wedding. I am too old to be kept from a wedding, Rose." She sets down the cup. "Wednesday, ten o'clock, the morning room. I shall be there." A pause. "It is a debt, child. Debts are paid in presence.")*
> *("It is a debt," Rose agrees. "The wall was older than you, Grandmama. The terms said tell you first." "The terms," Augusta says, "said nothing older than I am comes down without my leave. It came down. You told me." A pause. "The bundle, child —" she uses the word deliberately, "— is younger than I am. But you will open it in my presence, because I am your grandmother and because your grandfather was my husband." She picks up her chocolate. "That is all. Go and lift your secret, Rose.")*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Bell's Tuesday paragraph; ordinary restoration news, no scandal yet.
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting is the Gazette's Tuesday paragraph, come up with the evening post — Bell's paper, noting the day's ordinary news.)*
> *(Rose reads it twice, the way she reads everything Bell writes, and finds no edge in it — no leader, no verdict, no favorite story. Just the facts, set in Bell's type: the muster, the falling, the dinners. Nothing of the hollow. Nothing of the bundle. She folds the Gazette and sets it by the memorandum book. The paper smells of ink. The house smells of stone dust.)*
scenes.sting: the sting — Bell's Tuesday paragraph; ordinary restoration news, no scandal yet.

scenes.synopsis: Wednesday, foreseen — the opening's dress, chosen while the house has the night.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia lays out the dawn's choices with the gravity of a woman arming a soldier for the second day running: the green wool, pressed — the garden's color, the opening faced in green; the Hartwell blue, severe — the estate's color, the papers faced in state; the archive silk, the grandmother's — the past, worn to meet the past. "The bundle opens at ten, miss," Letitia says. "The mistress at half past nine, dressed for whatever a generation walled up.")*
> *(Rose touches each in turn — the wool's hardiness, the damask's severity, the silk's memory. Ten o'clock, the morning room, witnesses: the seal breaks on a generation's keeping. She chooses the morning's face. The mended gloves are laid beside the chosen gown, the mend at the thumb. In the glass: the opener, dressed ahead of the opening.)*
