scenes.synopsis: the day's close — the goodnight; the romance, unknowing.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent finds her at the landing window, looking toward the garden, and doesn't ask what she's looking at — the particular grace of him, tonight as Monday. "Tuesday's done," he says. "The wall is down, the stones are numbered, the dusk is —" he looks out, "— extremely well dressed." He offers his arm. "Walk me to my door, General. The civilian is for bed.")*
> *(They walk the corridor in lamplight, unhurried, his hand over hers on his arm. At his door he stops — the guest wing, the unknowing guest. "Whatever the wall gave up," he says lightly — and her heart stops, because he means the stones, the nothing he knows. "It'll still be your wall," he finishes. She smiles. "Good night, Laurent." "Good night, Rose." The door closes. The corridor is quiet, and his hand's warmth stays on hers a moment after.)*

scenes.synopsis: the memorandum — Wednesday's opening, witnessed; the list, closed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes to the morning room at nine with the memorandum book and the opening's list, and closes it the way she closes everything: in order. "Wednesday, ten o'clock. The witnesses: myself for the figures, Quill for the law, the dowager for the blood. Letitia for the book. Yourself for the house." She looks up. "The bundle under cloth till ten. The key in your pocket till ten. The village —" a pause, "— gets the wall's future, when dusk's line is entered.")*
> *("And if the papers name names?" Rose asks. Octavia's pencil stops. "Then Wednesday becomes interesting," she says, "and Thursday becomes arithmetic." She pockets the pencil. "Rose — whatever a generation walled up, it walled up for a reason. Reasons," she says, "are my department." The book, closed. The list, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the last round — the Park at night; the garden, the covered thing.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose walks the Park once more before the lifting — the mistress's last round. The house is lit behind her, the garden dark ahead, the gap a black notch in the wall's line, the lamp at the canvas burning steady. Somewhere in the village a dog barks once. The air smells of stone dust and coming rain. Tuesday has been executed — every course numbered, every watcher posted, every gown chosen.)*
> *(She stands at the garden gate a moment, the kept thing's keeper. The lamp burns. The canvas holds its shape. Behind her the house waits with its lit windows; ahead, the gap waits with its dark. She turns toward the foreman's lamp and raises her hand — the signal. The lifting, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: the lifting — at dusk the bundle comes out; the house, receiving.
scenes.prose: > *(At dusk the foreman gives the word, and the bundle is lifted out of the core — oilskin, lead-heavy, the papers' shape within, a generation in the dark — and carried up to the house under cloth, the foreman's two steadiest men fore and aft, Rose walking beside it with her hand near but not touching. The garden gate stands open. The house receives it.)*

scenes.synopsis: Wednesday's dawn — the morning room, the bundle under cloth; the key in the pocket.
scenes.prose:
> *(Wednesday comes in pale and punctual, and Rose is awake before the maid knocks for the third morning running, which has stopped being a habit and started being a schedule. She dresses standing at the window — the gown chosen last night, the mended gloves laid beside it, the key to the morning room already in her pocket where Letitia put it Tuesday night. "Some things the book doesn't hold." Some things the pocket does.)*
> *(Downstairs the house is quiet in the particular way of a house keeping an appointment. The morning room door is locked, as ordered. Behind it, under cloth, on the table where the tea things usually sit: a generation, waiting. She walks the corridor once, twice, the key knocking her thigh at every step. Ten o'clock. The house holds its breath.)*

scenes.synopsis: the opening's dressing — the gown chosen last night, styled for ten o'clock; Élise's hand.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise is in the dressing room with the chosen gown on the stand — the opening's dress, settled Tuesday night — and the question of how it is worn. "The gown is the gown, miss," she says. "The opening is the wearing." Three finishings on the tray: the grandmother's pearls at the throat — the past, worn to meet the past; the plain archive brooch at the shoulder — the estate's face, unadorned; or the mended gloves worn, not laid beside — Augusta's pearl-grey kid, the mend at the thumb, the emblem carried into the morning room.)*
> *(Rose touches the pearls — cool, heavy, her grandmother's weather in them. The brooch waits, severe. The gloves smell faintly of Tuesday's dust. "Ten o'clock," Élise says, "and witnesses. Dress the mistress the papers will meet." She chooses the morning's finishing. In the glass: the opener, dressed for the opening.)*

scenes.synopsis: breakfast, the knock — Julian's Wednesday; Henry's arithmetic of the morning.
scenes.prose:
> *(At breakfast Julian is at the table early, the rent-book under his elbow, and Henry is counting the morning's facts into his porridge: forty-nine stones, three lines straight, one bundle under cloth in the morning room, which he knows about the way children know about everything — by standing very still and listening. "Wednesday," Julian says, setting down his cup. "The knock I promised." He looks at her. "I knock on your door this morning, Rose. As agreed.")*
> *("Knock at a quarter to ten," Rose says, "and bring your brother's patience. The opening is the family's business before it's anyone's." "Quarter to ten," Julian says, and nods, and goes back to his letters, and the rent-book stays under his elbow like a dog that won't be shooed. Henry whispers to his porridge: "Ten o'clock." The house, informed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the law before the opening — what a grandfather's papers are to an heir; Quill's counsel.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill comes at nine to the study, as arranged, and states the law's position on grandfathers' papers with the briskness of a man clearing a table. "They are yours, Miss Hartwell. Sealed or unsealed, walled or unwalled — a man's papers pass with his estate, and yours is the estate. No living claimant, no trust, no caveat touches them. Open them in what company you choose; the choice is manners, not law.")*
> *("And if they name names?" Rose asks. Quill folds his hands. "Then the names are history's, and history is the one witness the law can't cross-examine. Counsel, and it costs nothing: read first, decide after. A paper read in haste is a paper misread, and misread papers make excellent kindling for other people's fires." He rises. "Ten o'clock. I shall be there — as counsel, or as witness, at your direction.")*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager arrives — Augusta's place, claimed; debts paid in presence.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta arrives at a quarter to ten in the barouche, because dowagers do not walk to openings either, and is shown to the morning room with the ceremony of a state visit. "The house," she says, surveying the cloth-covered table, the chairs set in their row, "has dressed the morning like a christening." She takes the chair nearest the table. "I am here, child. The debt is paid. Debts are paid in presence.")*
> *("You are here, Grandmama," Rose says. Augusta regards the cloth the way she regards everything — as a thing that will eventually be removed. "Your grandfather," she says, "walled up more than garden walls. I have waited a generation to be told what. I can wait another quarter of an hour." She folds her hands. "Open it in my presence, Rose. That was the whole of the terms." The clock ticks. The cloth waits.)*

scenes.synopsis: the room, readied — the morning room arranged; the household's last counsel.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia has readied the morning room like a quartermaster fitting out a campaign: the chairs in their row, the cloth on the table, the lamps lit though it is morning, the memorandum book open at Wednesday's page. "The witnesses as counseled," she says, the pencil moving. "Octavia for the figures, Quill for the law, the dowager for the blood. The question, miss —" she looks up, "— is whether the counsel is the order, or whether the morning gets a smaller room.")*
> *("The counsel was Tuesday's," Rose says. "The order is Wednesday's." Letitia blots the page. "Then Wednesday orders, and the book holds it." She shuts the pencil behind her ear. "One more counsel, and it costs nothing: whatever the morning gives you, miss, eat something first. Papers are hungry work." She goes to admit the witnesses. The room holds its arrangement.)*

scenes.synopsis: the gathering — Octavia and Quill arrive; the room, tenanted.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia arrives at ten precisely with the memorandum book under her arm and takes the chair for the figures without being shown. Quill follows, the law's bag in his hand, and stands a moment at the door the way men stand at christenings — uncertain of the liturgy. Julian is at the back, the rent-book left upstairs for once. The bundle sits on the table under its cloth, lead-heavy, patient.)*
> *(Rose looks at the room — the dowager, the figures, the law, the book, the brother — and at the cloth, and at the key in her own hand. The morning has gathered itself. What remains is the one decision Tuesday deferred to Wednesday: in whose presence the seal breaks. She sets the key on the table. The room looks at the key. The key says nothing.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE OPENING: who stands in the room when the seal breaks; the counseled witnesses, fewer, or the household entire.
scenes.prose:
> *(The key is on the table, and the room is waiting, and Augusta's place is not the question — the dowager has paid her debt in presence, and the debt is settled. The question is the rest of the room. Three ways offer themselves. The counseled witnesses: Octavia for the figures, Quill for the law, Letitia for the book, the dowager for the blood — the opening as Tuesday counseled it, witnessed proper, the household told first. Fewer: the room narrowed to Rose, Augusta, and Letitia — the blood, the house, the book — Quill and Octavia told after the first reading, the fewer the eyes the safer the keeping.)*
> *(Or the third way: the household entire — the footmen, Mrs. Pike called up from the kitchen — no one excluded from the house's business, the bundle the household's as the book says. Augusta's voice: keep in the open, child. Letitia's: the book will want the line. Quill's: manners, not law. Rose looks at the cloth-covered shape, at the witnesses waiting, at the dowager's level eyes. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(The order goes round the room in a low voice, and the morning rearranges itself around it — chairs added or chairs removed, the household admitted or dismissed, the witnesses as Wednesday ordered. Whatever the room became, one law holds it entire: the seal breaks at ten, in presence. The cloth is drawn back. The bundle lies on the table in its oilskin, lead-heavy, a generation in the dark. Augusta's hand finds Rose's wrist, once, and lets go.)*

options.label: The counseled witnesses
options.detail: *Candor+; the opening, witnessed.* Octavia, Quill, Letitia, the dowager; the morning, as Tuesday counseled. *(Open — and the household is told first, and the figures travel with the facts.)*

options.label: Narrow the room
options.detail: *Cunning+; the keeping, narrowed.* Rose, Augusta, Letitia only; Quill and Octavia told after. *(Quiet — and the fewer the eyes, the safer the keeping, the later the telling.)*

options.label: The household entire
options.detail: *Mercy+; the trust, shared.* Footmen, cook, Mrs. Pike called up; no one excluded. *(Shared — and the bundle is the house's business, and the house stands it.)*

scenes.synopsis: the seal, cut — Elias's seal; the opening, witnessed.
scenes.prose:
> *(The seal is Elias Hartwell's — the grandfather's device, pressed in wax gone the color of old tea, the Hartwell rose under a hand she never saw write it. Rose cuts it herself, the penknife steady, the wax parting with a sound like a small, dry cough. A generation's keeping, opened. The room does not breathe.)*
> *(Inside the oilskin, lead-lined against the damp of a hundred years: papers. A sheaf of them, tied with tape gone brittle, the top sheet in a bold clerk's hand she recognizes from the estate books — Elias's hand, the grandfather's, the same hand that signed the masons' contracts and the tenants' leases and, once, her mother's marriage lines. The room leans in. The papers lie on the table in the morning light, and the century exhales.)*

scenes.synopsis: the violets — pressed among the papers; faithfulness, from an untended garden.
scenes.prose:
> *(They are between the third and fourth sheets, and Rose's hand stops: violets, pressed flat, the purple gone to brown at the edges, the stems tied with a thread. Dried violets. Faithfulness — the lexicon's word, the garden's word. Someone pressed them into the bundle a generation ago, and they have kept their shape through the dark the way kept things do.)*
> *("Violets," Augusta says, and for once the dowager's voice does not carry its full mast. "Your grandfather," she says, and stops. "The garden had violets then," she says at last. "Before the wall went green. No one has tended that bed in years." She looks at the pressed flowers a long moment. "Faithfulness," she says. "He kept faith with something, your grandfather. The papers will say with what. Or they won't." She sits back. The violets lie on the table, brown-edged, faithful.)*

scenes.synopsis: the reading-day dress — the atelier dresses the long day; Élise's practical eye.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at half past ten with the reading day's question, and the atelier has been thinking about paper. "The morning's gown has done its duty, miss, and the day is a reading day. Paper wants its own dress." Three on the bench: the morning's gown, kept — the opening's dress, worn through the reading; the archive cotton, the spare working gown — dust and ink, the atelier's labor; the grey shawl, thrown over — the papers, read warm.)*
> *("Paper," Rose says, "is not stone. It does not film a hem." "Paper," Élise says, "is worse. It sits. It waits. It makes you forget to eat, and then you are cross with the century." She holds up the cotton. "The atelier votes the working gown. But the mistress," she says, "is the mistress." She waits, warm and practical, the day's whole philosophy in her hands.)*

scenes.synopsis: the reading begins — the war years; Elias's hand, unspooling.
scenes.prose:
> *(She begins with the top sheet and reads down, and the papers unspool in the grandfather's bold hand — the war years, when England was at war with France and the coast watched the water. Accounts first: rents, repairs, the estate's ordinary arithmetic. Then the other pages, the ones the tape held tightest — memoranda in a smaller hand, dates from the war's middle years, references to shipments, to passages, to names half-written and scratched through.)*
> *(The morning room is quiet around her. The witnesses have withdrawn to the window, the dowager to her chair, Letitia to the book. Rose reads on — the war years in Elias's hand, the estate's money moving in patterns she does not yet understand, the grandfather she never knew writing himself plain onto paper a generation before she was born. The pages keep coming. The century keeps its own counsel.)*

scenes.synopsis: the figures' counsel — Octavia on reading old accounts; what "creditor" meant then.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia takes the chair beside her at eleven with the ledger pages spread between them, and counsels the reading the way she counsels everything: on paper, in pencil. "Read the figures first and the words after," she says. "Old accounts lie in the words and tell the truth in the columns. And Rose — a creditor in the war years was not a creditor as we price them. Debts then were favors, and favors were politics, and politics —" she taps the page, "— were survival.")*
> *("These are estate papers," Rose says. "Rents and repairs." "These," Octavia says, "are estate papers the way the wall was a wall. The columns will tell you what the words won't. Read them twice." She makes a note in the memorandum book. "And when you find the column that doesn't balance —" she looks up, "— you bring it to me before supper. The figures and the facts travel together." The pencil goes in the pocket. The counsel, given.)*

scenes.synopsis: ledger names — de la Roche and de Brissac, glimpsed; the texture, unexpanded.
scenes.prose:
> *(The names surface in the ledger's middle pages, entered in Elias's hand among the war years' columns: de la Roche — £900, entered against a date in the war's third year; de Brissac — £1,400, two years later, the ink darker, the hand less steady. Creditor families, by the column's logic — money owed, or money paid, the figures don't yet say which. Octavia copies them into the memorandum book without comment.)*
> *("French names," Rose says. "Émigré names," Octavia says, "by the look of them. The war years were full of French names in English ledgers — passages paid, debts honored, favors priced." She blots the copy. "They are entries, Rose. Nothing more, till the reading says more." The names sit in the book in Octavia's fair hand: de la Roche, de Brissac — entries, nothing more, till the reading says more. The reading goes on.)*

scenes.synopsis: the unknowing, at noon — Laurent and the party Saturday; the ease, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent finds her at noon on the terrace, the papers put by for the dinner hour, and does not ask what the morning held — the particular grace of him, or the particular blindness. "The house," he says, "has the smell of an opening. Like a church after a wedding." He offers his arm. "Walk with the civilian. Tell me about Saturday — the party, the half-restored Park, the ton coming to look at your wall's honest wound.")*
> *(They walk, and he talks of Saturday — the guests, the music, the Park as a stage — and she answers, and does not answer, her mind still in the war years' columns. "You are elsewhere," he says at last, not reproachfully. "I am reading," she says, which is true as far as it goes. "Read beautifully, then," he says. "It is your second-best look." He squeezes her arm. The terrace, the noon, the unknowing — held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the midday refresh — the atelier's noon answer; the fichu, the bodice, or nothing.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at one with the midday's answer, and the atelier has been watching the reading. "The morning's dress has sat since seven, miss, and the afternoon is more paper. The atelier proposes the refresh." Three on the bench: the fresh fichu, linen at the throat — the afternoon, faced clean; the spare bodice, archive silk — the dress, renewed from the waist up; or nothing — the reading continues undisguised, the morning's dress carrying the day entire.)*
> *(Rose touches the fichu — clean linen, the atelier's small mercy. The spare bodice waits, the grandmother's silk. The morning's dress holds its shape, dustless, paper-creased at the skirt. "Paper," she says, "does not film a hem. It creases it." "Which," Élise says, "is why the atelier brought the linen." She waits, warm and practical. The afternoon, refreshed or not.)*

scenes.synopsis: the village's curiosity — Mrs. Pike's counter; the lane, watching.
scenes.prose:
> *(Mrs. Pike comes up at two with the dinners for the masons' half-day and a face full of the village's curiosity. "The lane," she says, unloading, "has had fourteen souls past the gate since morning. Amos counts. The village knows the wall's down and the papers are —" she looks toward the house, "— the village knows Wednesday is Wednesday, Miss Hartwell. Villages notice openings the way they notice walls.")*
> *("Wednesday is the restoration's business, Mrs. Pike," Rose says. "Aye," Mrs. Pike says, in the tone of a woman filing the answer for later. "The restoration's business. The cook says the morning room smells of old paper." She hands Rose the paper twist. "Gingerbread. Reading's hungry work." The cart rattles off. She pockets the twist; reading is hungry work, and the afternoon is long.)*

scenes.synopsis: the violets, asked after — Letitia's long memory; the bed, untended.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose finds Letitia in the stillroom at three with the pressed violets in a twist of paper, and asks the question the morning planted. "Whose were they, Letitia? The violets in the bundle." Letitia looks at the brown-edged flowers a long moment. "The garden had a violet bed," she says at last, "along the south wall. Your grandmother's bed — not the dowager. Your mother's mother. She pressed flowers into everything. Letters, books, once into a prayer book, which the parson found.")*
> *("And Elias kept them?" Rose asks. "Elias," Letitia says carefully, "kept what he kept. The bed's been untended twenty years, miss. Whatever faithfulness those violets were pressed for —" she folds the twist, "— it outlasted the gardener." She puts the violets by, and goes back to her jars, and the stillroom smells of lavender and kept things.)*

scenes.synopsis: the fragment — one half-torn letter; the second bundle, named.
scenes.prose:
> *(Late afternoon, and the reading has reached the bundle's middle — the memoranda thinnest here, the pages out of order, some half-torn where the tape held too tight. One fragment stops her: a letter in Elias's hand, dated in the war's late years, the bottom half gone. What remains is a closing line and a direction: "— the second bundle to London, kept till called for. The garden keeps the first. Tell no one the keeping's reason —" and there the tear takes it.)*
> *(She reads it three times. The second bundle to London. Kept till called for. The garden keeps the first — the one on the table, the one in her hands. She looks at the torn edge a long moment, then lays the fragment with the ledger pages, the violets beside it. The papers do not say where in London. The papers do not say who was to call for it. The tear keeps its counsel, and the afternoon goes on.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE READING: read alone first, read with Octavia, or read with Quill's counsel.
scenes.prose:
> *(The afternoon is thinning, and the papers are not — the sheaf goes deeper than the morning promised, the war years unspooling in Elias's hand, the columns and the memoranda and the torn fragment, and the day's law has become a question of company. Three ways to take the reading. Alone first: Rose reads the papers through alone before any other eyes — the first impression hers, the grandfather's hand met privately, the telling chosen after the knowing. With Octavia: the figures read together, the columns doubled — the arithmetic shared, the unbalanced column found sooner, the counsel immediate.)*
> *(Or with Quill's counsel: the lawyer reads with her, the law's eye on every page — copies made, the papers' standing secured, the reading guided by what the law can use. Quill's voice: read first, decide after. Octavia's: the figures and the facts travel together. Letitia's: the book will want the line. The papers lie on the table in the afternoon light, patient as stone. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(The order goes to the household in a low voice, and the reading rearranges itself around it — the room emptied or the chairs drawn up, the papers taken to the study or kept on the morning-room table, the company as Wednesday ordered. Whatever the reading became, one law holds it entire: the papers are read before they are told. The sheaf is gathered, the tape re-tied, the violets laid with the fragment. The afternoon gives way to the evening's work.)*

options.label: Read alone first
options.detail: *Candor+; the reading, private.* The papers through alone; the first impression, hers. *(Private — and the grandfather's hand met privately, the telling chosen after.)*

options.label: Read with Octavia
options.detail: *Resolve+; the figures, shared.* The columns read together; the arithmetic, doubled. *(Shared — and the unbalanced column found sooner, the counsel immediate.)*

options.label: With Quill's counsel
options.detail: *Cunning+; the law, advised.* The lawyer's eye on every page; copies, standing, use. *(Advised — and the reading guided by what the law can use.)*

scenes.synopsis: the reading's course — the evening's work, conditional on the decision.
scenes.prose:
> *(The evening's reading takes the shape Wednesday ordered. If she reads alone: the morning room empties, the lamps are lit, and Rose reads the war years through in the grandfather's hand — the memoranda, the columns, the torn fragment — with no eyes but her own, and the first impression settles the way sediment settles: slowly, and all the way down. If with Octavia: the chairs are drawn up, the ledger pages spread between them, and the columns are read twice — once for the figures, once for what the figures won't say — Octavia's pencil moving in the margins like a second hand on the papers.)*
> *(If with Quill's counsel: the study, the law's bag open, copies made in Quill's fair clerk's hand — the papers' standing secured, the reading guided, the torn fragment copied twice and the copies laid side by side. Whatever the company, the war years unspool the same: Elias's money moving in wartime patterns, the émigré names in the columns, the second bundle named and not found. The lamps burn. The reading goes on.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's knowing — Augusta on Elias's ways; the papers, and the man.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends for her at five — the blue drawing room, the chocolate, the eyebrow at half mast, which for the dowager is practically fond. "Well," she says. "The papers. The violets. Your grandfather's hand all over the morning." She pours. "Elias kept papers the way other men kept dogs — close, and for reasons he never explained. I was his wife forty years, Rose, and I never once asked what was in the packets he sealed. Wives then didn't. Wives now —" she looks at her granddaughter, "— open them at ten o'clock with witnesses.")*
> *("What was he, Grandmama? In the war years." Augusta considers the chocolate. "Careful," she says at last. "Your grandfather was careful the way deep water is careful. The estate prospered when other estates bled. I never asked how." She sets down the cup. "I am asking now, child — through you. Read them well." The chocolate is still warm. The interview is over.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, mapped — Octavia on Thursday; the missing bundle's three ways.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes at six with the memorandum book and maps the missing bundle the way she maps everything: on paper, in pencil. "The papers name a second bundle, sent to London, kept till called for. It is not here. Three ways, and counsel on each. Search the house: every cupboard, chest, and lumber room — the house ransacked by its own, the servants' talk priced in. Quill to London: quiet inquiries through his people — the ton unalerted, the inquiry deniable, the waiting longer.")*
> *("Or wait," Octavia says. "Let the trail surface. Counsel, and it costs nothing: the papers waited a generation; they can wait a week. But Rose —" she looks up, "— the fragment said kept till called for. Someone was meant to call. If no one has, the bundle is still wherever London keeps such things. If someone has —" she closes the book, "— Thursday becomes arithmetic." The map, drawn. The choosing, Wednesday's.)*

scenes.synopsis: the afternoon's face — Bell is coming; the mistress, faced for the press.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia waylays her at half past six with the afternoon's question. "Bell comes at seven," the quartermaster reports. "The Gazette's proprietor, calling on the restoration — which means calling on the papers, which means calling on you." Three faces on the bench: the Hartwell blue, severe — the estate's color, the press faced in state; the claret silk, the mother's — the archive's boldest, the papers faced in color; or the reading day's dress, kept — the morning's choice, unbroken into evening.)*
> *("Bell," Letitia says, "will describe you at breakfast, in print. The description should be the one you chose." Rose looks down at the reading day's dress — the paper creases, the honest wear of the hours. The blue waits, severe and splendid. The claret waits, bold. She chooses the evening's face.)*

scenes.synopsis: the proprietor calls — Bell wants the story; the story, withheld.
scenes.prose:
> *(Bell comes at seven, as reported, and does not waste the walk up the drive. "Miss Hartwell," she says, in the morning room, with the papers put by and the violets nowhere in sight. "The county knows the wall came down. The county knows Wednesday opened something. The Gazette prints facts, not smoke — so give me the fact, and I'll print it straight." She sets her notebook on her knee. "What was in the bundle?")*
> *("Estate papers," Rose says. "My grandfather's. The restoration's business." Bell writes it down — estate papers, the grandfather's — and looks up. "That's the fact?" "That's the fact." Bell closes the notebook. "Then that's what prints. The Gazette doesn't print smoke, Miss Hartwell — come back with fire." She stands. "One proprietor to another: when the papers say something worth the ink, I'll be at the gate. Till then —" she touches her cap, "— the wall's future, and the restoration, stone by stone." She goes.)*

scenes.synopsis: the law on the missing — Quill's avenues; what "lost papers" mean.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill stays after Bell, as arranged, and lays out the law on missing papers with the briskness of a man dealing cards. "Three avenues, Miss Hartwell. The house: yours to search, top to cellar, no warrant needed — your own lumber rooms can't sue you. London: my people can inquire, quietly — solicitors' clerks, carriers' books, the places where bundles go to wait. Or patience: the papers waited a generation; the law is in no hurry the papers aren't.")*
> *("And if the bundle is found — by another hand?" Rose asks. Quill folds his. "Then whoever holds it holds paper, not title. Your grandfather's papers are yours wherever they sit — the law follows the estate, not the cupboard." He rises. "Search, inquire, or wait. The avenues are open. The choosing —" he bows, "— is manners, not law." The bag closes. The counsel, given.)*

scenes.synopsis: the search, planned — the house's cupboards; the book records its readiness.
scenes.prose:
> *(Before supper, Letitia opens the household book at the kitchen table and starts a fresh page — the missing bundle's hunting, entered fair, the hunting not yet ordered. "The lumber rooms first," she says, the pencil moving, "if the searching falls to us — then the library's high shelves, the attics, the old nursery. The house searched by its own, top to cellar, as the law allows." She looks up. "The servants will talk, miss. The book will record where we looked, so the house doesn't have to gossip about what we found — when we look.")*
> *("Have it ready," Rose says. Letitia blots the page. "The footmen at first light, if the order's the search. I take the library myself — I know where this house hides things, miss, having hidden some of them." The pencil goes behind the ear. "And whatever Thursday's order is about the London inquiry —" she closes the book with the gavel-thump, "— the house will have done its part, or be ready to." The search, planned. The book, holding the hunt's readiness.)*

scenes.synopsis: the quartermaster's unease — Letitia's long memory; Elias's generation, named.
scenes.prose:
> *(After the book is closed, Letitia does not go — she stands at the kitchen table with her hands flat on it, the quartermaster's composure thin at the edges. "Miss," she says at last. "There are things I hoped never to see in his hand." She does not say which things. "Elias's generation kept its own counsel, and the counsel was —" she stops, starts again, "— the war years were not like other years. Money moved then the way water moves in the dark.")*
> *("You knew him," Rose says. It is not a question. "I was a girl in this house when he was an old man," Letitia says. "I carried his letters to the post. Sealed letters, miss. I never asked." She lifts her hands from the table. "I am asking now — through you. Read them well." She goes upstairs, and the kitchen is quiet, and the unease stays behind like a coat left on a chair.)*

scenes.synopsis: the supper dress — the day's end, dressed; the archive's evening face.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes up at half past seven with the supper choices, and the atelier has been thinking about paper all day. "The reading is done for the day, miss, and the evening wants its own face." Three on the bed: the claret silk, her mother's, re-cut to the shoulder — the evenings, claimed; the grey wool, the day's own — the work, carried to table; the blue damask, the grandmother's — the estate's color, severe and splendid.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret — the mother's silk, the archive's boldest. The day has been seals and columns and kept things; the evening can be the archive, dressed. "The mended gloves with it," Élise says, laying them out, Augusta's pearl-grey kid, the mend at the thumb. "The emblem goes to supper too." In the glass: the mistress of the papers, dressed for the household.)*

scenes.synopsis: the reading, dressed — the household dresses the week of reading ahead; the chapter's ritual.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the table — "read as you mean to go on, miss. The house takes its tone from you.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the papers — "the columns will keep. Tonight the reading reads you.")*
> *(Story morsel: Augusta, at the door — "read in the open, child. The house, too.")*
> *(Story morsel: Laurent, at the lamps — "whatever the reading costs — the house is worth it.")*
> *(Story morsel: Élise, at the door — "tomorrow's gloves get the extra stitch. For Thursday.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: Wednesday broke the seal — the bundle opened, the papers in Elias's hand, the violets pressed between the sheets. The reading will take days: the war years, the columns, the torn fragment, the second bundle named and not found. Before the week of reading, the household gathers in the morning room and dresses it — what it means to read a generation's keeping. The papers on the table, the lamps lit, the house quiet around its own past. Dress for the reading: the archive's colors, worn with intent, eyes open. Precise. Together. Attentive. The house that reads together does not flinch apart.

scenes.synopsis: after the ritual — the papers, boxed; the house, settling.
scenes.prose:
> *(The household disperses from the morning room by lamplight, and Rose stands a moment in the direction she chose — the silk, the wool, the damask, worn — and feels the reading settle on her shoulders like the wrap she chose for the evening. The papers are gathered, the tape re-tied, the violets laid with the fragment in their twist of paper. Letitia locks the morning room. The key goes back in the pocket.)*
> *(Rose looks once more at the table where the century lay open all day — the lamps still burning, the chairs in their row, the cloth folded now. Somewhere, Octavia is copying columns by candlelight; somewhere, Augusta is composing Thursday's verdict; somewhere, the house is deciding what it thinks of grandfathers. The evening deepens around the papers, and the keeping holds its shape.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening walk — the romance, unknowing; Saturday, and the papers between.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent walks her to the garden gate after supper, and the dusk is the color of old paper. He does not ask about the seal, or the violets, or the torn fragment — the particular grace of him, again, or the particular blindness. "Wednesday's done," he says. "The papers are opened, the columns are read, the dusk is —" he looks out, "— extremely well dressed." He offers his arm. "Walk me to my door, General. The civilian is for bed.")*
> *(They walk the terrace in lamplight, unhurried, his hand over hers on his arm. At his door he stops — the guest wing, the unknowing guest. "Whatever the papers said," he says lightly — and her heart stops, because he means the estate, the nothing he knows. "It'll still be your house," he finishes. She smiles. "Good night, Laurent." "Good night, Rose." The door closes. The corridor is quiet, and the papers sit between them like a third person at the gate.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE MISSING BUNDLE: search the house, send Quill to London, or wait.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the study, and the missing bundle is a line waiting to be written. The fragment's direction: the second bundle to London, kept till called for. It is not in the house — or it is, and the house hasn't been properly asked. Three ways. Search the house: the footmen at first light, the lumber rooms, the library's high shelves, Letitia's own hands — the house ransacked by its own, the servants' talk priced in, the finding soonest if the finding is here.)*
> *(Quill to London: quiet inquiries through his people — solicitors' clerks, carriers' books, the places where bundles wait — the ton unalerted, the inquiry deniable, the answer slower. Or wait: let the trail surface on its own — the papers waited a generation, the house can wait a week, the patience of a house that knows how. Octavia's voice: Thursday becomes arithmetic. Quill's: the law follows the estate. Letitia's: the book will want the line. Rose looks at the fragment in its twist of paper, at the torn edge, at the dark beyond the window. The pencil is in her hand. The line, waiting.)*
> *(The line goes into the memorandum book — the missing bundle's fate, decided at night. Letitia takes the book, and the pencil comes out from behind her ear.)*

options.label: Quill to London
options.detail: *Cunning+; the inquiry, placed.* Quiet inquiries through his people; the ton, unalerted. *(Placed — and the answer slower, the asking deniable.)*

options.detail: *Mercy+; the patience, kept.* Let the trail surface; the house, that knows how to wait. *(Kept — and the papers waited a generation; the week can wait.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night's order — the missing bundle's fate, executed; Thursday, arranged.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia receives the night's order and folds it into Thursday's plan without breaking stride. "The search," she says, the pencil moving — or the inquiry, or the waiting, as the book orders. "The footmen at first light, or Quill's letter by the morning post, or the house's patience — entered fair, whichever Wednesday chose." She blots the page. "Thursday's order is the bundle's fate. Friday's is the reading's second day." She closes the book.)*
> *("And the papers?" Rose asks. "The papers," Letitia says, "are boxed in the morning room, the key in your pocket, the violets with the fragment. The book has it all." The pencil goes behind the ear. "The week, miss, is behaving like a ledger. Debits of paper, credits of —" she does not say answers, "— of Thursday." The night, ordered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Bell's Wednesday paragraph; ordinary restoration news, no scandal yet.
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting is the Gazette's Wednesday paragraph, come up with the evening post — Bell's paper, noting the day's ordinary news.)*
> *(Rose reads it twice, the way she reads everything Bell writes, and finds no edge in it — no leader, no verdict, no favorite story. Just the facts, set in Bell's type: the opening, the witnesses, the wall's future. Nothing of the hollow. Nothing of the violets. Nothing of London. She folds the Gazette and sets it by the memorandum book. The paper smells of ink. The house smells of old paper.)*
scenes.sting: the sting — Bell's Wednesday paragraph; ordinary restoration news, no scandal yet.

scenes.synopsis: the book, entered — Wednesday's opening and reading, written fair.
scenes.prose:
> *(Before the dusk round, Letitia opens the household book at the kitchen table and writes Wednesday in her fairest hand — the seal cut at ten, the papers in Elias's hand, the violets pressed between the sheets, the ledger names copied, the fragment's direction, the missing bundle's fate as the night ordered. The bundle's business she writes as "the papers' business," which is the book's way of knowing without saying.)*
> *("The book remembers," she says, not looking up, "so the house doesn't have to gossip." "And the search?" Rose asks. "The search," Letitia says, "is entered as Wednesday ordered — begun, placed, or borne." She blots the page. "Whatever the order was, miss, the book holds it, and the house stands it." She closes the book with the gavel-thump. The pencil goes behind the ear. The book lies closed on the kitchen table, holding the day.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dusk wrap — the garden round, dressed; seen, or unseen.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia lays out the dusk's choices the way she lays out everything: like orders of the day — the grey cloak, hooded and plain — the round, unseen; the black silk shawl, respectable — the dusk, faced in state; the reading day's shawl, the grey — the papers, carried to the garden. "The mistress walks the round at dusk, miss," Letitia says. "The gap, the gate, the garden's edge. Dress the walking.")*
> *(Rose takes the grey cloak — hood up, plain, the night's own color. The black silk hangs back, severe. The reading shawl smells of the day's lamps. "The house walks its own," she says. Letitia drapes, or pins, or settles, as ordered. "There," she says. "The reader, wrapped. Walk like the mistress, miss, not like a secret. The dusk has eyes.")*

scenes.synopsis: the dusk round — the garden, the gap; the keeper's last walk.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose walks the dusk round alone — the mistress's last walk of the day. The garden lies quiet under the evening, the gap in the wall a dark notch where the secret sat, the stacked courses numbered on the south lawn, the lamp at the canvas burning steady though the canvas is empty now. The air smells of cut grass and coming rain. Wednesday has been executed — the seal cut, the papers read, the orders given.)*
> *(She stands at the gap a moment, the keeper of the papers now. Behind her the house waits with its lit windows; ahead, the lane runs down to the gate, and beyond the gate the road to the village, and beyond the village — London, where a second bundle waits to be called for. She turns toward the garden gate, and the dusk deepens, and the round goes on.)*

scenes.synopsis: the gate, kept — Amos's evening tally; the lane, quiet.
scenes.prose:
> *(Amos is at his gatehouse at dusk with his tally stick — fourteen notches, as reported. "Watchers, miss," he says, touching his cap. "Respectful ones, all day. The lane's gone quiet now — the dinners are done, the wall's men are home." He looks down the road toward the village. "Thirty years I've kept this gate, miss. Quiet evenings are the ones I like. Quiet," he says, "means nothing's coming.")*
> *("Mind the lane keeps it respectful, Amos." "Aye, miss. That's the posting." He tucks the tally stick away. "Fourteen today. The book'll want the number." She nods — Letitia's doctrine, everywhere. "The book shall have it." The gate, the lane, the garden: Amos between them, keeping the difference.)*

scenes.synopsis: the watcher — at dusk's last light, a scarred gentleman at the garden gate, watching the house.
scenes.prose: > *(At dusk's last light, turning back from the gatehouse, Rose sees him: a gentleman at the garden gate — past it, on the lane's edge — standing very still in the failing light, watching the house. Scarred — the cheek catches the light wrong, an old scar, white in the dusk. He does not move. He does not knock. He watches the lit windows the way a man watches a place he once knew, and then the light goes, and the lane is empty.)*

scenes.synopsis: Thursday's dawn — the watcher's face, carried overnight; the morning room, the key.
scenes.prose:
> *(Thursday comes in pale and early, and Rose has been awake an hour before it — the watcher's face went with her to bed and stayed there, the way unwelcome guests do. The scarred gentleman at the garden gate. Watching the house. She dresses at the window with the mended gloves laid out beside the gown, and the morning-room key goes in the pocket where it has lived since Tuesday. Some things the book doesn't hold. The pocket holds the rest.)*
> *(Downstairs the house is stirring — the kitchen's early noises, the footmen's boots, the ordinary Thursday of a house mid-restoration. The garden bundle lies boxed in the morning room, the violets with the fragment, the ledger pages copied fair. Rose walks the corridor once, the key knocking her thigh. Whoever stood at the gate at dusk has had the night to decide whether to knock. She has had the night to decide how to answer. Ten o'clock is hours off. The house, meanwhile, is awake.)*

scenes.synopsis: the caller's dressing — Thursday may bring a knock; Élise's eye.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise is in the dressing room with the Thursday question laid out before it's asked. "The watcher may knock, miss, or he may not. The atelier dresses for the knock." Three on the stand: the archive grey silk, the day's own — the papers' color, the mistress faced for business; the Hartwell blue, severe — the estate's face, the caller faced in state; or the plain morning dress with the mended gloves worn — the house's own, the emblem carried to whatever comes.)*
> *(Rose touches the grey silk — the reading's color, honest wear at the cuffs. The blue waits, splendid and severe. The gloves lie beside the plain dress, Augusta's pearl-grey kid, the mend at the thumb. "If he knocks," Élise says, pinning, "he meets the mistress, not the morning." She chooses Thursday's face. In the glass: the keeper, dressed for the keeping.)*

scenes.synopsis: the gatehouse report — Amos's morning news; a name, left at the gate.
scenes.prose:
> *(Amos comes to the kitchen door at eight with his tally stick and a face that has been saving something. "Miss," he says, touching his cap. "The watcher come back." Letitia's pencil stops. "After dark, miss — stood at the garden gate again, an hour, watching. Then this morning, first light, he knocked at the gatehouse." Amos straightens. "Gave his name, miss. James Harrow. A gentleman, scarred as you saw. Carries a bundle, wrapped in oilskin. Asks to see Miss Hartwell — at the door, at eleven, if the house will have him.")*
> *("Did he say what the bundle is?" Rose asks. "No, miss. Said it was kept for the house, and the keeping's done." Amos touches the tally stick. "Thirty years I've kept this gate, miss. I know a man with business from a man with none. This one —" he looks for the word, "— this one's got the weight of it. In his shoulders." He goes back to his gate. The name sits in the kitchen like a third person at the table: James Harrow.)*

scenes.synopsis: the law before the caller — Quill's counsel on receiving a stranger with papers.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill comes at nine to the study, as arranged, and hears the name without surprise, which is the lawyer's whole expression. "James Harrow," he says. "The law has no Harrow on its books — no suits, no debts, no claims. Which tells you nothing, Miss Hartwell. The war years are thin in the law's books, and men who carried things in the war years carried them outside the law's sight.")*
> *("Counsel, and it costs nothing," Quill says, folding his hands. "Hear him in the morning room or the study, never the library — the library is where the papers live, and a stranger needn't see the shelves. Ask what he wants before you offer what he might have. And whatever the bundle holds —" he rises, "— remember Wednesday's doctrine: read first, decide after. The choosing is manners, not law." The bag closes. Eleven o'clock is two hours off.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE RECEIVING: receive him as guest, as prospective employee, or at arm's length.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the study, and eleven o'clock is an hour off, and the question is the room. James Harrow comes to the door with a bundle kept for the house, and the house must decide what door it opens. Three ways offer themselves. As a guest: the morning room, tea, the house's hospitality — the stranger received as the Park receives, the bundle's business heard in comfort, the keeping honored by the welcome. As a prospective employee: the study, the terms heard as terms — he seeks work, let him name it, the house weighing a man the way it weighs a mason.)*
> *(Or at arm's length: the hall, formal, the bundle's business and nothing more — the door kept ajar in the figurative sense, the stranger's measure taken before the house commits a chair. Augusta's voice: look at his hands, child. Letitia's: the book will want the line. Quill's: ask what he wants before you offer what he might have. Rose looks at the key in her pocket, at the morning room beyond the corridor, at the clock moving toward eleven. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(The order goes to the household in a low voice, and the house rearranges itself around it — the morning room readied or the study cleared or the hall kept formal, the tea ordered or not, the chairs as Thursday commanded. Whatever the receiving became, one law holds it entire: he is met at eleven, at the door, by the mistress of the house. Letitia takes the order. The clock moves.)*

scenes.synopsis: the receiving, arranged — the household prepares; the book takes the line.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia receives the order and folds it into the morning without breaking stride. "The morning room," she says, the pencil moving — or the study, or the hall, as the book orders. "Tea if he's a guest, the ledger if he's a workman, nothing if he's at arm's length. The footmen briefed. Mrs. Pike warned off the corridor." She blots the page. "And the name, miss — James Harrow — entered fair. The book likes a name before a face.")*
> *("What does the book say about him?" Rose asks. "The book," Letitia says, "says a gentleman called at eleven with a bundle kept for the house. The book does not speculate." The pencil goes behind the ear. "Though between the book and the ceiling, miss —" she looks up, "— a man who watches a house at dusk and knocks at eleven is either honest or rehearsed. The morning will tell which." She goes to arrange it. The house, readying.)*

scenes.synopsis: the door, eleven o'clock — James Harrow, personified; the scar, the bow, the bundle.
scenes.prose:
> *(At eleven precisely the footman announces him, and Rose goes to the door herself — the receiving as Thursday ordered it. He stands in the hall with his hat in his hand: a gentleman of sixty-one, spare and upright, his coat shabby at the cuffs in the way of good clothes long kept. The scar runs down his left cheek, old and white, catching the hall light. He bows — the bow of a man who learned it young and kept it. "Miss Hartwell," he says. "I am James Harrow. I have kept something of your grandfather's, and the keeping is done.")*
> *(In his hands: a bundle, wrapped in oilskin, tied with tape — the twin of the garden's bundle, smaller, the tape gone brittle at the edges. He holds it the way a man holds a thing he has carried a long time — not possessively. Carefully. The way one holds a sleeping animal, or a debt. "May I come in?" he asks. The house, which has been holding its breath since dusk, breathes. "Mr. Harrow," Rose says, "come in.")*

scenes.synopsis: his terms — work, sought; the bundle, kept till called for.
scenes.prose:
> *(In the morning room — or the study, or the hall, as Thursday ordered — he sets the bundle on the table and does not let go of it at once. His hands are a clerk's hands, ink at the knuckles, the nails trimmed square. "I will be plain, Miss Hartwell," he says. "I kept your grandfather's second bundle. 'To London, kept till called for' — I was the keeping. Twenty years I have carried it. I am sixty-one, and I am tired of carrying. I seek work — the ordering of papers, the keeping of archives, honest work for honest pay.")*
> *("The bundle," Rose says. "It is the second bundle. The London bundle." "It is," he says. "Your grandfather's hand, like the first. I have never opened it. That was the keeping — to keep, not to read." He looks at her levelly. "I kept faith with a dead man for twenty years, Miss Hartwell. I would like, before I am done, to keep faith with a living house." The bundle sits on the table between them, patient as stone. The terms, stated.)*

scenes.synopsis: the midday refresh — the long talk ahead; the atelier's answer.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at half past twelve with the midday's question, and the atelier has been watching the caller. "The morning's dress has met the gentleman, miss, and the afternoon is the longer talk. The atelier proposes the refresh." Three on the bench: the fresh fichu, linen at the throat — the afternoon, faced clean; the archive shawl, grey wool — the papers' color, the talk kept warm; or nothing — the morning's dress, unbroken, the mistress undisguised before the stranger.)*
> *(Rose touches the fichu — clean linen, the atelier's small mercy. The shawl waits, grey and honest. The morning's dress holds its shape, the grey silk uncreased. "He has carried a bundle twenty years," she says. "The least the house can do is change its linen." "Which," Élise says, "is why the atelier brought it." She waits, warm and practical, the afternoon's whole philosophy in her hands.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's measure — Augusta on the name Harrow; the hands, advised.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends for her at one — the blue drawing room, the chocolate, the eyebrow at full mast, which for the dowager is an inquisition. "Harrow," she says. "James Harrow. Sixty-one, scarred, carrying your grandfather's papers like a christening." She pours. "I do not know him, Rose. The war years had a hundred such men — clerks, carriers, keepers of other men's secrets — and Elias collected them the way other men collected snuffboxes.")*
> *("What do I look for, Grandmama?" "His hands," Augusta says promptly. "Elias's men were filed by their hands. A clerk's hands tell the truth about twenty years — ink doesn't lie, and neither does the way a man sets down a bundle." She sets down the cup. "And child —" the eyebrow lowers a fraction, "— whatever he asks for, give him the dignity of the asking. Old men who have carried things are proud the way wounded animals are proud. Handle accordingly." The chocolate is still warm. The counsel, given.)*

scenes.synopsis: the scar, asked after once — answered once, and closed.
scenes.prose:
> *(After the chocolate she asks it — once, directly, the way Augusta taught her to ask things. "Mr. Harrow. The scar." He touches his left cheek with two fingers, the gesture of a man checking a thing he long ago stopped feeling. "The war years," he says. "A French port, an English errand, a disagreement about which of us was carrying what." He lowers his hand. "Twenty years a useful face, Miss Hartwell. Men remember the scar and forget the errand, which suited your grandfather's purposes and, later, mine. Ask me anything else.")*
> *("I am sorry," she says. "Don't be," he says. "It has been a long time a face." He folds his hands — the clerk's hands, ink at the knuckles. "The errand is over. The face remains. It is not the interesting part of me, Miss Hartwell, whatever the dusk suggested." She nods, and the scar is never mentioned again — it sits in the room the way furniture sits, present and unremarked. The asking, done. The closing, mutual.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, figured — Octavia on a man with a bundle; the arithmetic of trust.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes at two with the memorandum book and does the arithmetic of the caller the way she does everything: on paper, in pencil. "A man of sixty-one, carrying your grandfather's papers for twenty years, asking for work. The figures, Rose: twenty years of keeping is either the longest honesty in the county or the longest patience. Counsel, and it costs nothing — pay him for the keeping he has done, whether or not you employ him for the keeping to come. A debt acknowledged is a man disarmed.")*
> *("And the bundle?" Rose asks. "The bundle," Octavia says, "is an unbalanced column till Friday. Keep it sealed, keep it witnessed, keep it where the house can see it. And Rose —" she looks up, "— whatever Thursday decides about his hands, the bundle's arithmetic is simple: it is yours. The law follows the estate, and the estate is you." She makes a note. "Pay the keeper. Keep the bundle. The counsel, given.")*

scenes.synopsis: the afternoon's face — the house dresses for the stranger within.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia waylays her at half past two with the afternoon's question, the quartermaster's eye on the caller within. "The gentleman is in the house, miss, and the house should look like it meant to have him." Three faces on the bench: the blue damask, severe and splendid — the caller, faced in state; the grey wool, the day's own — the work, carried through the afternoon; or the claret ribbon at the throat, the archive's boldest touch — the papers, faced in color.)*
> *(Rose touches the damask — the grandmother's color, splendid. The grey wool waits, honest. The claret ribbon lies coiled like a question. "He has seen the morning's dress," she says. "Let him see the afternoon's." Letitia pins, or drapes, or ties, as ordered. "There," she says. "The mistress, for the afternoon.")*

scenes.synopsis: the work, named — what he can do; the archives, offered honest labor.
scenes.prose:
> *(In the afternoon he names it — the work, plainly, the way he does everything. "I kept papers for your grandfather," he says. "I can keep them for the house. The estate's archives want ordering — I know how a house's shelves go to seed, Miss Hartwell, and they want a clerk's hand. Copying, cataloguing, the mending of bindings. I read the old hands. I know the war years' shorthand." He sets his hands on the table, the ink at the knuckles. "Name the wage. I will earn it.")*
> *("You were a schoolmaster," Rose says — Amos's report, the village's knowledge. "I am a schoolmaster," he corrects gently. "The schoolhouse cottage, the copybooks, the Crown on Fridays. The papers were the night work." He looks at the bundle on the table. "Twenty years of night work, Miss Hartwell. I would like the day work now. In the open." The offer sits between them, precise as a ledger line. The wage, unnamed. The wanting, plain.)*

scenes.synopsis: the civilian meets the archivist — Laurent's ease; the romance, unthreatened.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent finds them at three on the terrace — the papers put by, the talk paused for air — and takes in the stranger with the particular grace of him. "Mr. Harrow," he says, offering his hand like a man who has never met a scar he needed to stare at. "The house's guest, I hope. Or the house's new clerk — Rose collects strays with ledgers, it's her particular vice." Harrow takes the hand, and something in his shoulders eases a fraction. "The clerk, perhaps. The jury is out.")*
> *("The jury," Laurent says, "is Rose, and she is merciless. Walk with us, Mr. Harrow. Tell me about the schoolhouse — I have always wondered what copybooks look like from the other side of the desk." They walk, and Laurent talks of Saturday — the party, the music, the Park as a stage — and Harrow listens with the attention of a man storing details, and Rose walks between them with her hand on Laurent's arm. The civilian, the archivist, the mistress. The terrace, the afternoon, the ease — held entire, and undivided.)*

scenes.synopsis: the law on the bundle — what a kept bundle is, in law; the keeping's terms.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill comes at four, as arranged, and looks at the oilskin bundle on the table the way a man looks at a deed. "It is yours, Miss Hartwell," he says. "Kept in London or kept in the village, in his hands or on your table — your grandfather's papers are yours wherever they sit. The law follows the estate, not the cupboard. What Thursday decides is not ownership. It is custody.")*
> *("And if I pay him for the keeping?" Rose asks. "Then pay him," Quill says, "and enter it in the book — wages for the keeping done, wages for the keeping to come, the terms plain. A paid keeper is a keeper the law understands. An unpaid keeper is a volunteer, and volunteers —" he folds his hands, "— are the law's mystery." He rises. "Custody, Miss Hartwell. Manners, not law. The choosing is yours." The bag closes. The counsel, given.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE BUNDLE: the house's keeping, his hands, or Friday's joint reading.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the study, and the afternoon is thinning, and the bundle sits on the morning-room table where he set it — the oilskin, the tape, the twenty years. Three keepings offer themselves. Into the house's keeping: the bundle laid on the table tonight, sealed, under the morning room's lock — the house's trust taken, his receipt entered fair in the book, the keeping done as he asked. In his hands: the keeping honored — he carries the weight still, the house honoring the carrier, the bundle returning with him and coming back Friday.)*
> *(Or Friday's joint reading: both bundles sealed till Friday, the two halves read together at ten — the garden's and London's, side by side at last, the week's whole question answered in company. Octavia's voice: keep it sealed, keep it witnessed. Quill's: custody, not ownership. Letitia's: the book will want the line. Harrow's: to keep, not to read. Rose looks at the bundle through the study door, at the tape gone brittle, at the twenty years. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(The order goes to the household in a low voice, and the keeping rearranges itself around it — the morning room locked or the bundle entrusted back to his hands or the two bundles set side by side for Friday, the book entering the line as Thursday ordered. Whatever the keeping became, one law holds it entire: the bundle stays sealed till Friday. The tape is not cut tonight. The reading waits.)*

scenes.synopsis: the keeping, told — his answer to the order; pride, and relief.
scenes.prose:
> *(She tells him at five, in the morning room, the bundle between them — the order as Thursday gave it. If the house keeps it: he looks at the bundle a long moment, then nods once, the precise nod of a man signing a ledger. "Twenty years," he says. "It is a strange thing to set down." If his hands: his shoulders drop a fraction — relief, undisguised. "Thank you," he says simply. "For not taking what I carried.")*
> *(If Friday's reading: he touches the tape with one finger, the brittle edge. "Side by side," he says. "The garden's and London's. Your grandfather would have —" he stops. "No. I don't know what he would have. That is the honest answer, and I find I prefer it." Whatever the keeping, he meets her eyes when it is told — level, clerk-precise, grateful in the way proud men are grateful: without saying so. The order, given. The answer, taken.)*

scenes.synopsis: the violets, doubled — his bundle carries them too; faithfulness, kept two ways.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone with the bundle at half past five — the morning room quiet, the tape's brittle edge catching the light — Rose sees what the morning missed: tied to the tape with a thread, a sprig of dried violets. Brown-edged, flat-pressed, the purple gone the way of all kept purples. The same keeping as the garden bundle's. Faithfulness — the lexicon's word — pressed into the London bundle by whatever hand tied the tape.)*
> *(She does not touch them. Some things are not for touching on the first day. But she understands, standing there, what twenty years of carrying means: it means the violets were tied on by someone, and kept by someone, and the someone is sixty-one and downstairs drinking the house's tea. Two bundles, two sprigs, one word. The keeping, flowered. The afternoon goes on.)*

scenes.synopsis: the village's curiosity — the caller's name, already traveling.
scenes.prose:
> *(Mrs. Pike comes up at six with the suppers for the wall's men and a face full of the village's arithmetic. "The lane," she says, unloading, "has had nine souls past the gate since dinner. Amos counts. And the name's out, Miss Hartwell — Harrow. James Harrow. The village knows him, of course — the schoolmaster, the copybooks, the Crown on Fridays — but the village didn't know he had business at the Park, and now it's doing the sums.")*
> *("The sums being?" Rose asks. "The sums being," Mrs. Pike says, in the tone of a woman filing the answer for later, "that a man carries a bundle to the great house at eleven and stays till six, and whatever's in the bundle, it's the restoration's business." She hands Rose the paper twist. "Gingerbread. Callers are hungry work — his, I mean. Yours too, likely." The cart rattles off. The village, informed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the quartermaster's memory — Letitia carried a letter for a Harrow, once.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose finds Letitia in the stillroom at half past six with the question the afternoon planted. "Letitia. The name Harrow — did you know it? In Elias's day." Letitia looks at her jars a long moment. "I carried his letters to the post," she says at last. "Sealed letters, miss. I never asked. But once —" she stops, starts again, "— once there was a letter for a Mr. Harrow. London direction. Sealed, like all his. I took it to the carrier myself.")*
> *("And?" Rose asks. "And nothing," Letitia says. "The carrier took it. London took it. Whatever was in it went wherever London keeps such things." She folds her hands. "But miss — a man your grandfather wrote to in the war years, and a man who watched the house at dusk —" she does not finish. "The book," she says instead, "will want that letter's line. If the carrier's book still exists —" She goes back to her jars. The memory, entered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the supper dress — the stranger at table; the atelier's evening face.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes up at seven with the supper choices, and the atelier has been thinking about the caller all day. "The gentleman sups with the house, miss — or he doesn't, as Thursday ordered — and the evening wants its own face." Three on the bed: the claret silk, her mother's, re-cut to the shoulder — the evenings, claimed; the grey wool, the day's own — the work, carried to table; the blue damask, the grandmother's — the estate's color, severe and splendid.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret — the mother's silk, the archive's boldest. The day has been doors and bundles and kept things; the evening can be the archive, dressed. "The mended gloves with it," Élise says, laying them out, Augusta's pearl-grey kid, the mend at the thumb. "The emblem goes to supper too." In the glass: the mistress of the keeping, dressed for the household.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, dowagered — Augusta on keeping the past in the house.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends for her before supper — the blue drawing room, no chocolate this time, the eyebrow at half mast, which for the dowager is practically tender. "Well," she says. "The caller. The bundle. The keeping, whatever Thursday ordered." She regards her granddaughter. "Counsel, child, and it costs nothing: a house that takes in the past must give it a chair and a wage. Guests of the past, kept as guests, curdle. Give him work — real work, the archives, the copying — and he is a clerk. Keep him as a curiosity, and he is a ghost. Houses are haunted by unpaid keepers.")*
> *("And the bundle?" Rose asks. "The bundle," Augusta says, "is paper, and paper waits." She rises, which is the dismissal. "Your grandfather found such men and kept them, and then he died and left the keeping to you. Curate it, Rose. That is what heirs are for." The door closes. The counsel, given.)*

scenes.synopsis: the boy's arithmetic — Henry counts the caller; the child's eye.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry finds her on the stairs before supper with the day's count, the way children bring tribute. "Nine," he says. "Mrs. Pike's nine, I counted too. And he's sixty-one, and the scar's on the left, and the bundle's got violets like ours." He looks up. "Is he going to live here? Julian says the house collects people the way the garden collects walls.")*
> *("The house," Rose says carefully, "is considering it. What do you think of him?" Henry considers — the full weight of eight years brought to bear. "He walks like the wall's men," he says at last. "Heavy, but on purpose. And he didn't stare at the scar." A pause. "I like him." He runs off to wash for supper. The tribute, delivered. The verdict, eight years old and entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: the afternoon's hour — he speaks of Elias, sparingly; the archival air.
scenes.prose:
> *(After supper — or after the talk, as Thursday ordered — he speaks of Elias, and does it sparingly, the way a man handles a thing that might break. "Your grandfather," he says, "was careful the way deep water is careful. He gave me the bundle in the war's late years and said: keep it till called for. He did not say who would call. He did not say when. I kept it." He looks at his hands. "I have sometimes thought the calling would never come. I am glad —" he stops, starts again, "— I am glad it was the house that called. And not the other kind of calling.")*
> *(Rose feels it then, plain and uncomplicated: responsibility. The weight of a man who kept faith with the dead and is asking, politely, to keep faith with the living. Curiosity, too — the war years, the French port, the errand — but the curiosity can wait. What can't wait is the answer to the asking. She looks at him: the spare shoulders, the white scar, the clerk's hands folded. "The house," she says, "is glad you knocked." He bows his head. The hour, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dusk wrap — the garden round, dressed; the caller within.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia lays out the dusk's choices with the gravity of a woman dressing a mission: the grey cloak, hooded and plain — the round, unseen; the black silk shawl, respectable — the dusk, faced in state; the archive shawl, the grey wool — the papers, carried to the garden. "The mistress walks the round at dusk, miss," Letitia says. "The gap, the gate, the garden's edge. The gentleman is within. Dress the walking.")*
> *(Rose touches the grey cloak — the hood, the plainness, the vanishing. The black silk waits, severe. The archive shawl smells of the day's lamps. "The house walks its own," she says. Letitia drapes, or pins, or settles, as ordered. "There," she says. "The keeper, wrapped. Try not to look like a conspiracy, miss. The dusk has eyes.")*

scenes.synopsis: the dusk round — the walled garden, the violet bed; faithfulness, untended.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose walks the dusk round alone — the mistress's last walk of the day. The garden lies quiet under the evening, the gap in the wall a dark notch, the stacked courses numbered on the south lawn. Along the south wall she stops at the violet bed — her grandmother's bed, untended twenty years, the leaves low and wild. No flowers now; the season for violets is past. But the bed is there, and the keeping is there, and two sprigs of the same lie pressed in two bundles in the house.)*
> *(She stands a moment with the dusk coming on, the keeper of the papers now — both papers, or the papers' promise. Behind her the house waits with its lit windows, and in it a man of sixty-one who carried faithfulness in oilskin for twenty years. She turns toward the garden gate, and the dusk deepens, and the round goes on.)*

scenes.synopsis: the brother's plain talk — Julian on the stranger; the steadying.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian walks her back from the garden gate, the rent-book under his elbow though it is dusk, and talks plainly, the way brothers do when the house has taken in something large. "A man comes to the door with your grandfather's papers," he says. "The house gives him tea and a wage, or the house gives him the road. Which is it?" "The house," Rose says, "is still deciding. What does the rent-book say?")*
> *("The rent-book," Julian says, "says a clerk's wage is cheaper than a mystery, and a mystery in the house is dearer than either." He looks at her. "He's honest, Rose. I watched him at supper —" or at the talk, as Thursday ordered, "— men who carry things for twenty years don't learn new carryings at sixty-one." He squeezes her arm. "Decide, and I'll stand it. That's the brother's whole doctrine." The dusk, the brother, the plain talk — held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night's lodging — where he sleeps; the terms, honored.
scenes.prose:
> *(At nine Letitia takes the order for the night's lodging, the quartermaster's pencil ready. If Thursday received him as a guest: the spare room in the guest wing, made up, the fire lit — the house's hospitality, entire. If as a prospective employee: the room over the study, the clerk's room, plain and clean — the wage's lodging, honest. If at arm's length: he bows and takes his bundle and his hat, and the lane takes him back to the schoolhouse cottage — the keeping his, till Friday.)*
> *(Whatever the lodging, he accepts it the way he accepts everything: precisely, with thanks. "I will earn the room," he says — if it is the house's room. "Work," Rose says, and he almost smiles. "Work," he agrees. Letitia shows him up, or shows him out, as Thursday ordered. The pencil goes behind the ear. The night, lodged.)*

scenes.synopsis: the archive's Thursday face — the household dresses the house for the stranger's keeping; the chapter's ritual.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the table — "keep as you mean to go on, miss. The house takes its tone from you.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the bundles — "the columns will keep. Tonight the keeping keeps you.")*
> *(Story morsel: Augusta, at the door — "curate it, child. The house, too.")*
> *(Story morsel: Harrow, at the back — come from the village, the keeping new on him.)*
> *(Story morsel: Élise, at the door — "tomorrow's gloves get the extra stitch. For Friday.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: Thursday brought the watcher to the door — James Harrow, sixty-one, scarred, carrying the London bundle kept twenty years. The house has received him, the bundle's keeping is ordered, and Friday will read the two halves together. Before the week of reading's second day, the household gathers in the morning room and dresses the house for the keeping — what it means to take the past in and give it a chair. The bundles on the table, the lamps lit, the house quiet around its own keeping. Dress for the archive: the keeper's colors, worn with intent, eyes open. Precise. Together. Attentive. The house that keeps together does not flinch apart.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — HIS STORY: press him tonight, let it come in its own time, or set the terms for Saturday.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the study, and the night is thinning toward ten, and Harrow's story sits in the house like a third bundle — unopened. He has given the terms, the work, the scar's one telling. The rest — the war years, the French port, the twenty years of night work — is his. Three ways. Press him tonight: ask it plain, the whole of it, before the lamps are out — the story taken while the taking is easy, the week's question answered before Friday's reading. Let it come in its own time: the waiting kept — he tells it when the telling is ready, the house patient as the papers.)*
> *(Or set the terms: his story before Saturday's party — the Park filling with guests, the ton coming to look at the wall's honest wound, and no unanswered questions walking the terrace. Augusta's voice: old men who have carried things are proud. Letitia's: the book will want the line. Harrow's: to keep, not to read — but the keeping is done, and the reading is Friday. Rose looks at the lamp, at the dark beyond the window, at the closed door. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(The order goes out in a low voice — to Harrow's door, or to no door at all, as Thursday commanded — and the night rearranges itself around it: the talk taken up or the talk deferred, the story tonight or the story in its season. Whatever the telling became, one law holds it entire: it is his to tell. The asking is hers; the telling is his. Letitia takes the order. The lamps burn.)*
