scenes.synopsis: the telling, as ordered — the story's shape, conditional on the decision.
scenes.prose:
> *(What she chose, she enacts. If she pressed him: he comes to the study at ten, and tells it plain — the war's late years, the French port, the errand, the bundle given into his hands with the direction. He tells it the way he does everything: precisely, without performance, the scar unmentioned. If she let it come: she does not knock. The house is quiet, and the story keeps its own counsel, and somewhere a man of sixty-one sleeps the first easy sleep of twenty years.)*
> *(If she set the terms: she tells him at the study door — before Saturday, Mr. Harrow, when the Park fills. He nods, the precise nod. "Saturday," he says. "The story will be ready. Twenty years a story keeps; it can keep two days more." Whatever the telling, he meets her eyes when it is done — level, clerk-precise. The night, ordered. The story, placed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night's order — his keeping entered; Friday, arranged.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia receives the night's order and folds it into Friday's plan without breaking stride. "The keeping," she says, the pencil moving — the house's, his, or Friday's, as the book orders. "The story — tonight, in its time, or before Saturday — entered fair, whichever Thursday chose." She blots the page. "Friday's order is the joint reading: the two bundles, the morning room, ten o'clock. The witnesses as Wednesday counseled — or as Friday orders.")*
> *("And Mr. Harrow?" Rose asks. "Mr. Harrow," Letitia says, "is lodged as Thursday ordered, and the book has his wage's line waiting for Friday's figure." The pencil goes behind the ear. "The week, miss, is behaving like a ledger. Debits of paper, credits of —" she does not say answers "— of Friday." She closes the book with the gavel-thump. The night, ordered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the proprietor at dusk — Bell wants the caller; the fact, withheld.
scenes.prose:
> *(Bell comes at dusk, as threatened, and does not waste the walk up the drive. "Miss Hartwell," she says, in the hall, with the bundles put by and the violets nowhere in sight. "The village says a gentleman called at eleven with a bundle and stayed till supper. The Gazette prints facts, not smoke — so give me the fact, and I'll print it straight." She sets her notebook on her knee. "Who is he?")*
> *("A gentleman of the county, on the restoration's business," Rose says. Bell writes it down — a gentleman, the restoration's business — and looks up. "That's the fact?" "That's the fact." Bell closes the notebook. "Then that's what prints. The Gazette doesn't print smoke, Miss Hartwell — come back with fire." She stands. "One proprietor to another: when the bundle says something worth the ink, I'll be at the gate. Till then —" she touches her cap, "— the wall's third course, and the restoration, stone by stone." She goes.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Bell's Thursday paragraph; ordinary restoration news, no scandal yet.
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting is the Gazette's Thursday paragraph, come up with the evening post — Bell's paper, noting the day's ordinary news.)*
> *(Rose reads it twice, the way she reads everything Bell writes, and finds no edge in it — no leader, no verdict, no favorite story. Just the facts, set in Bell's type: the caller, unnamed; the wall's third course; the reading, proceeding. Nothing of the bundle. Nothing of Harrow. Nothing of London. She folds the Gazette and sets it by the memorandum book. The paper smells of ink. The house smells of old paper.)*
scenes.sting: the sting — Bell's Thursday paragraph; ordinary restoration news, no scandal yet.

scenes.synopsis: the last talk — a line of the war years, offered; the weariness, plain.
scenes.prose:
> *(He finds her in the hall at half past nine — if he is within; if the lane took him back, she finds the note he left with Amos, and the note says the same. "Miss Hartwell," he says. "One line, and then I am done for the night. Your grandfather, in the war's late years, moved money the way other men moved troops — quietly, and to purpose. I carried the papers. I never asked the purpose." He looks at her. "I am telling you this so that Friday's reading does not surprise you into thinking me surprised. Whatever the papers say —" he stops. "I kept them. That is the whole of my part.")*
> *("Thank you, Mr. Harrow," she says. "For the line." "For the line," he agrees, and bows — the bow of a man who learned it young — and goes to his room, or to the lane, as Thursday ordered. She stands in the hall with the lamps burning and thinks: sixty-one, and tired, and precise, and the house is the better for him. The weariness, plain. The night, nearly done.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's last word — on faithfulness, and the living.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends for her at ten — the blue drawing room, the chocolate going cold, the eyebrow at rest, which for the dowager is the end of the day. "Well," she says. "The caller is kept, the bundle is ordered, the story is placed. You have done Thursday well, child." She regards her granddaughter over the cup. "Your grandfather pressed violets into his papers. Faithfulness." She sets down the cup. "Keep faith with the living, Rose. The clerk upstairs —" or the schoolmaster in the village, as Thursday ordered, "— the household, the brother with his rent-book. The dead have had their turn.")*
> *(She rises, which is the dismissal. "Go to bed, child. Friday reads the papers, and Friday will need you rested." The lamps are low. The interview is over.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night's undressing — the day unmade; the atelier's last word.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at half past ten with the night's question, and the atelier has been thinking about Thursday all day. "The caller is kept, miss, the bundle is ordered, and the day wants unmaking." Three on the bed: the grandmother's lace robe, ivory — the night, faced in heirloom; the plain flannel, warm — the sleep, faced honestly; or the archive shawl, kept on — the papers, carried to bed.)*
> *(Rose touches the lace — the grandmother's, ivory, the night's heirloom. The flannel waits, honest and warm. The shawl smells of the day's lamps. "The house kept its Thursday," she says. Élise unpins, or folds, or settles, as ordered. "There," she says. "The keeper, unmade. Sleep, miss. Friday reads." The lamp is turned low. The day, undone.)*

scenes.synopsis: the book, entered — Thursday's caller and keeping, written fair; Friday, arranged.
scenes.prose:
> *(Before the night round, Letitia opens the household book at the kitchen table and writes Thursday in her fairest hand — the caller at eleven, James Harrow, sixty-one, the London bundle kept twenty years, the keeping as Thursday ordered, the story tonight or in its time or before Saturday, the wage's line waiting for Friday's figure. The bundle's business she writes as "the papers' business," which is the book's way of knowing without saying.)*
> *("The book remembers," she says, not looking up, "so the house doesn't have to gossip." "And Friday?" Rose asks. "Friday," Letitia says, "is the joint reading — the two bundles, the morning room, ten o'clock, the witnesses as Friday orders. The book has it all." She closes the book with the gavel-thump. The pencil goes behind the ear. The book lies closed on the kitchen table, holding the day.)*

scenes.synopsis: the other half — at night, he lays his bundle on the table beside the garden's.
scenes.prose: > *(At eleven, with the house quiet, there is a knock at the morning-room door — soft, the way the household knocks when the news is kept. Harrow stands there with his bundle in his hands. If the house keeps it: he lays it on the table beside the garden's bundle and steps back — the entrusting, done. If he keeps it: he lays it on the table for the night's showing, the seal unbroken beside the garden's seal, and takes it up again — the keeping his, till Friday. If Friday's reading: he lays it beside the garden's and ties nothing, cuts nothing — the two halves, side by side, waiting for ten o'clock. Whatever Thursday ordered, the showing is the same: the other half, on the table, the tape brittle, the violets tied with thread. "Kept till called for," he says. "Called for, at last." He bows, and goes. The two bundles lie on the table in the lamplight, seals unbroken, waiting for Friday.)*

scenes.synopsis: Friday's dawn — the bundles on the table; ten o'clock, hours off.
scenes.prose:
> *(Friday arrives the way the week has trained it to: early, grey, and with business. Rose wakes before the maid — the fifth morning running — and lies a moment listening to the house. Downstairs, in the morning room, the two bundles wait on the table where the night left them: the garden's and London's, the tape brittle, the violets tied with thread. Seals unbroken. Ten o'clock is hours off, and already the day feels arranged around it, the way furniture arranges itself around a fire.)*
> *(She dresses at the window — the mended gloves laid out, the morning-room key in the pocket where it has lived since Tuesday. The book will want Friday's lines, Letitia will want Friday's order, and between now and ten there is the household to brief and the room to set. But first she stands at the window and watches the drive. Whatever the bundles say at ten, they will say it in Elias's hand. She has been dreading and wanting that in equal measure. The drive stays empty.)*

scenes.synopsis: the reading's dressing — the archive's Friday face; Élise's eye.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise is in the dressing room with Friday's question already laid out — the atelier has been waiting all week for this one. "The reading, miss. Ten o'clock, the two halves, the house's eyes on you. The atelier proposes the Friday face." Three on the stand: the archive grey silk — the papers' color, the mistress faced for business, the honest wear at the cuffs; the Hartwell blue, severe — the estate's face, the reading faced in state; or the plain morning dress, the violet sprig pinned at the throat — the house's own, faithfulness worn where the papers can see it.)*
> *(Rose touches the sprig — dried, brown-edged, the lexicon's word made wearable. The grey silk waits, the day's own. The blue, splendid and severe. "Ten o'clock," she says, "wants the mistress, not the morning." "Which," Élise says, pinning, "is why the atelier is here." She chooses Friday's face. In the glass: the reader, dressed for the reading.)*

scenes.synopsis: the morning room, readied — the witnesses arranged; the watched table.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia is in the morning room at half past eight with the order already half executed, which is the quartermaster's whole philosophy. "Ten o'clock," she says, the pencil moving. "The table cleared, the lamps trimmed for daylight's failure, the chairs —" she counts, "— for you, the dowager, Miss Octavia, Mr. Harrow. Mr. Quill at nine, if you'll have him, for the law's blessing on the breaking.")*
> *("And the bundles?" Rose asks. "Where the night left them," Letitia says. "Under my eye and the housemaid's, in rotation, since seven. The book calls it 'the watched table,' miss." She blots the page. "The seals are whole. I checked them the way other women check soup — frequently, and with suspicion." The room stands ready. The ten, arranged.)*

scenes.synopsis: the law on the reading — breaking seals, witnessed; counsel.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill comes at nine to the study, as arranged, and hears the plan without surprise, which is the lawyer's whole expression. "The breaking of seals," he says. "In law, Miss Hartwell, a seal broken by the owner in the presence of witnesses is a reading witnessed, and the law asks nothing more. Break them at ten, in the morning room, with the house's people round the table. Let every hand that touches a page be a hand the book can name.")*
> *("And after?" Rose asks. "After," Quill says, "the keeping is custody, as Thursday counseled. Read them where the house can see them. Copy what matters. And whatever the papers say —" he rises, "— remember they are your grandfather's papers, and you are his heir, and the law has no opinion about grandfathers." The bag closes. Ten o'clock is an hour off.)*

scenes.synopsis: his last morning as the carrier — the bundle, regarded; the witness, becoming.
scenes.prose:
> *(He comes at half past nine — from the village or from the spare room, as Thursday ordered — and stands in the morning room looking at the table the way a man looks at a thing he is about to stop carrying. The bundle lies where he laid it at eleven last night, beside the garden's: the oilskin, the tape, the violet sprig tied with thread. "It looks smaller," he says, "than twenty years.")*
> *("Does it feel smaller?" Rose asks. "No," he says. "It feels finished." He touches the tape with one finger, the brittle edge. "Twenty years I have been the keeping, Miss Hartwell. Today I am —" he looks for the word, "— the witness. It is a promotion I did not apply for." She almost smiles. The carrier, at the table's edge, becoming the witness.)*

scenes.synopsis: ten o'clock — the company, gathered; the seals, broken in company.
scenes.prose:
> *(At ten the morning room holds its company: Augusta in the chair by the fire, the eyebrow at full mast; Octavia with the memorandum book, pencil sharp; Letitia at the table's corner, the household book open; Quill by the window, the law's witness; and Harrow at the table's far side, his hands folded, clerk-precise. The two bundles lie in the middle of the table, side by side, seals whole, violets tied.)*
> *(Rose stands at the table's head and looks at the company her Thursday assembled. "The seals," she says, "broken at ten, in company, by the owner's hand." She cuts the garden bundle's tape first — the brittle edges parting — then the London bundle's, Harrow watching with his hands folded and his face giving nothing away, which is a clerk's whole repertoire. The oilskin folds back. The papers lie bare. The reading, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — HIS PLACE: the schoolhouse cottage, a room in the house, or village lodgings.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the study, and the reading is underway, and the question of the man runs alongside the question of the papers. James Harrow, sixty-one, carrier twenty years, schoolmaster by courtesy. Three keepings offer themselves. The schoolhouse cottage: the Park's patronage, the schoolmaster's chair made his in deed as in courtesy — the copybooks, the cottage, the village's children, the archives kept alongside. A room in the house: the clerk's room over the study, plain and clean — the house's shelter entire, the archivist under the Park's roof.)*
> *(Or village lodgings: a room at the Crown, the house paying the reckoning — the man his own master, the archives his day's work, the lane between him and the Park kept walkable. Augusta's voice: give him work and a wage, not a ghost's chair. Letitia's: the book will want the line. Harrow's: the day work, in the open. Rose looks at the key in her pocket, at the reading room beyond the door. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(The order goes to Letitia in a low voice, and the keeping rearranges itself around it — the cottage readied or the clerk's room aired or the Crown's reckoning opened, the book entering the line as Friday ordered. Whatever the place became, one law holds it entire: it is his, and it is earned, and the house will call it the schoolmaster's keeping. The reading waits. The choosing is done.)*

options.detail: *Resolve+; the keeping, given.* The Park's patronage; the schoolmaster's chair, his in deed. *(Given — and the copybooks, the cottage, the village's children.)*

options.label: A room in the house
options.detail: *Mercy+; the shelter, taken.* The clerk's room over the study; the archivist, under the roof. *(Taken — and the house's shelter, entire.)*

options.label: Village lodgings
options.detail: *Candor+; the distance, kept.* A room at the Crown; his own master, the lane walkable. *(Kept — and the man his own, the work his day's.)*

scenes.synopsis: the place, told — his answer to the order; the keeping, begun.
scenes.prose:
> *(She tells him at half past ten, in the study, away from the table — the order as Friday gave it. If the cottage: he is silent a long moment, and his hands — the clerk's hands, ink at the knuckles — open and close once. "The schoolmaster's chair," he says, "in deed." If the house's room: he bows his head. "Under the Park's roof," he says. "It is more than the carrying deserved." If the Crown's room: he almost smiles. "My own master," he says, "with the lane to walk. You have read me correctly, Miss Hartwell.")*
> *(Whatever the keeping, he meets her eyes when it is told — level, clerk-precise. "I will earn the room," he says. "Work," Rose says, and he nods, the precise nod. The telling, done. The man's place, placed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the reading begins — the halves, side by side; the papers, talking.
scenes.prose:
> *(The reading begins the way all true readings begin: slowly, and with the wrong end first. The garden bundle holds memoranda — Elias's hand, the late years, the ink gone brown: lists of ventures, ports, names half-remembered by the ton. The London bundle holds the keeping's other half: copies, cross-references, dates in a clerk's fair hand — twenty years of "kept till called for" written out in order.)*
> *(Harrow reads over Octavia's shoulder when she asks him to, and his finger finds the cross-references unerringly — the clerk's memory, twenty years deep. "This one," he says, touching a line, "answers that one." The two halves, side by side, begin to speak to each other across the table. Rose watches her grandfather's hand meet her grandfather's keeping. The halves, talking.)*

scenes.synopsis: the midday refresh — paper dust and ink; the atelier's answer.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at noon with the midday's question, and the atelier has been watching the reading. "Paper dust, miss, and ink, and the morning's dress has done its duty. The atelier proposes the refresh." Three on the bench: the reading apron, grey linen, the archive's own — the papers, faced in work clothes; the fresh fichu, clean at the throat — the afternoon, faced clean; or nothing — the morning's dress, unbroken, the reader undisguised before the papers.)*
> *(Rose touches the apron — grey linen, honest, the archive's livery. The fichu waits, clean. The morning's dress holds its shape. "The papers don't mind dust," she says. "But the atelier does." "Which," Élise says, "is why the atelier is here." She waits, warm and practical, the afternoon's whole philosophy in her hands.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the morning's dress; the reader, undisguised.

scenes.synopsis: the garden bundle's first pages — Elias's hand, the ventures, the reckoning.
scenes.prose:
> *(After the refresh the reading settles to its work, and the garden bundle gives up its first pages: Elias's memoranda, the war's late years, the hand unmistakable — the tall E, the impatient crossings. "The Nantes venture," Octavia reads aloud, "advanced, the spring sailing." A list follows: sums, ports, names. "The Lisbon account." "The Cadiz drafts." The ink is brown with age, the paper thin at the folds, and every page carries the violet's ghost — pressed flowers leave their shadow long after the flower is gone.)*
> *(Rose holds a page to the light and sees her grandfather's mind at work — a reckoning. Money moved quietly, to purpose, the way Harrow said at half past nine on Thursday. She sets the page down carefully. "He kept everything," she says. "Everything," Harrow says, from the table's far side, "except the reason." The pages, Elias's. The reason, missing.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, figured — Octavia on the two halves' columns; the total, uncomputed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia does the arithmetic of the two halves the way she does everything: on paper, in pencil, with the memorandum book open to a clean page. "The garden's bundle lists the advances," she says. "The London bundle lists what came back — or didn't." Her pencil moves down the columns. "Rose. The ventures paid little. The advances went out like tides and came back like —" she stops. "They didn't come back.")*
> *("Don't sum it," Rose says quietly. Octavia looks up. "I wasn't going to. Not yet." She taps the pencil. "Counsel, and it costs nothing: whatever the columns say when they're finished, they say it in your grandfather's hand, and a column is not a verdict. Read on." She makes a note, and does not write a total. The columns, open. The total, uncomputed.)*

scenes.synopsis: his story, in his own time (1) — his family, destroyed by the fall; the receipt, a man's life.
scenes.prose:
> *(It is Harrow who breaks the afternoon's rhythm, and he does it the way he does everything: precisely, without performance. A page comes up — the Nantes venture, the spring sailing — and his finger stops on a line. "My father's firm advanced on that sailing," he says. "When the venture failed, the firm failed. I was nineteen. My father died within the year.")*
> *("The same fall," Rose says. "The papers describe it, and you lived in the rubble of it." "I went to London with a clerk's hand and a ruined name," he says, "and your grandfather found uses for ruined names. The keeping was one of them." He looks at his hands — the ink at the knuckles. "The papers are the receipt, Miss Hartwell. I am the change." The story, begun. The telling, his.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, dowagered — Augusta on the unnamed sin; the ton's favorite story.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta keeps her chair through the afternoon's reading, the chocolate sent for at three, the eyebrow doing the work of commentary. "Well," she says, when Rose brings her the Nantes page. "Your grandfather moved money, and money moved men, and men broke. This is not news, child. Every fortune in this county has a page like this one. What matters is what the page doesn't say yet.")*
> *("What must it not say?" Rose asks. "It must not say it in the Gazette," Augusta says promptly. "Bell prints facts, and the ton loves nothing like an old scandal, and your grandfather's speculation is the paper's favorite kind of story. Read it all. Name it to no one — not yet. A sin unnamed is a paper unread, and a paper unread is a week you still own." She sets down the cup. "The ton can't buy the verdict, child. Neither can you. Read on." The counsel, given.)*

scenes.synopsis: the afternoon's dress — the reading goes long; the house dresses for the duration.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia waylays her at half past three with the afternoon's question, the quartermaster's eye on the long table. "The reading goes long, miss, and the house should look like it meant to stay." Three on the bench: the claret ribbon at the throat, the archive's boldest touch — the papers, faced in color; the grey wool, the day's own — the work, carried through the afternoon; or the blue damask, severe and splendid — the estate, faced in full.)*
> *(Rose touches the ribbon — claret, coiled like a question. The grey wool waits, honest. The damask, splendid. "The papers have had the morning's dress," she says. "Let them have the afternoon's." Letitia pins, or drapes, or ties, as ordered. "There," she says, stepping back. "The reader, readied." The pencil goes behind the ear. The afternoon, dressed.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the day's work; the labor, carried through.

scenes.synopsis: the London bundle — the keeping's entries; "kept till called for," documented.
scenes.prose:
> *(The London bundle, opened after the garden's, is the keeping made visible: twenty years of "kept till called for" written out in a clerk's fair hand — dates, crossings, the oilskin's journeys, the seals checked and re-tied. The record of the keeping itself: where the bundle slept, when it moved, the nights it traveled. On the last page, in Elias's own hand, the direction: "To London, kept till called for." Harrow's finger rests beside it.)*
> *("You never opened it," Rose says. "I never opened it," Harrow says. "That was the keeping — to keep, not to read." He looks at the direction in Elias's hand. "Though I will confess, Miss Hartwell, that in twenty years I memorized the weight of it. Some pages are heavier than others. The keeping teaches what the reading confirms." The bundle, kept. The keeping, ended.)*

scenes.synopsis: the creditors' names — de la Roche, de Brissac; the fall's parish.
scenes.prose:
> *(Late in the afternoon the reading reaches the creditors' pages, and the names come up like stones in a field: de la Roche — nine hundred — advanced on the Nantes venture, unreturned. De Brissac — fourteen hundred — on the Lisbon account, unreturned. Octavia copies them fair, the pencil steady. Harrow, at the table's far side, says nothing at all — which, from him, is a kind of speech.)*
> *("They are entries," Octavia says, reading Rose's look. "The papers needed names. The names are not the story." But Harrow's silence sits at the table like a fifth bundle, and Rose understands what the pencil doesn't: to him they were people. The fall had a parish. The entries, copied. The parish, unspoken.)*

scenes.synopsis: his story (2) — the French port; where the bodies are; the shape, withheld.
scenes.prose:
> *(It is nearly four when he speaks of the port, and he does it because a page requires it — a draft on a French house, dishonored. "The war's late years," he says. "Your grandfather's errand took me to a French port with papers like these, and there was a disagreement about which of us was carrying what." He touches his left cheek with two fingers. "The scar is the disagreement's signature. Men remember the scar and forget the errand.")*
> *("What was the errand?" Rose asks. "Money," he says, "moved the way your grandfather moved it — quietly, and to purpose. I carried the papers. I never asked the purpose." He looks at the creditors' page. "I can show you where the bodies are, Miss Hartwell — this entry, that sailing, the firms that broke. But the shape of the sin —" he stops. "The shape is not in the papers yet. When it comes, you will know it." The knowledge, shown. The shape, withheld.)*

scenes.synopsis: the boy at the door — Henry's question; the copybook, held out.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry appears at the morning-room door at half past four with a copybook under his arm and the day's question. "Is Mr. Harrow going to be the schoolmaster?" he asks. "Properly, I mean. With the cottage and the copybooks and everything." Harrow looks up from the table, and something in his face — the spare, scarred, clerk-precise face — does a thing Rose has not seen it do. It softens.)*
> *("The house is deciding," Rose says. "What would you have it decide?" Henry considers with the full weight of eight years. "The cottage," he says. "A schoolmaster should have a cottage. It's in the —" he looks for the word, "— the arrangement of things." He holds out the copybook. "For when he starts." The tribute, delivered. The arrangement, eight years old and entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, civilian — Laurent on the terrace; the romance, unthreatened.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent finds her on the terrace at five, the reading paused for air, and takes in the day's weight with the particular grace of him. "You look," he says, "like a woman who has been reading her grandfather's mail. Tell me the papers are dull, Rose. Tell me Elias was a boring old man with boring old ventures." "Elias," she says, "was never boring." "I know," he says. "It was worth asking.")*
> *(They walk, and he asks what she will do with what's read, and she says she doesn't know yet — the sin has no shape, the keeping has no home, the schoolmaster has no cottage, or has one, as Friday ordered. "You are collecting strays with ledgers again," he says. "It's my particular vice," she says. "I know," he says. "It's why I'm walking here." His hand finds hers. The terrace, the evening, the ease — held entire, and undivided.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE KEEPING: the house's library under seal, Quill's strongbox, or divided again.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the study, and the afternoon's reading is done, and the papers lie on the morning-room table waiting for their keeping. Three keepings offer themselves. The house's library, under seal: the papers shelved where the house's papers live, Rose's seal on the box, the keeping the Park's own — consulted at Hartwell thereafter, the archive's heart beating in the library. Quill's strongbox: the law's keeping — the papers in the solicitor's iron, inventoried, witnessed, the custody formal and fireproof.)*
> *(Or divided again: the garden's bundle to the library, the London bundle to Harrow's keeping — the halves honored as halves, the carrier carrying still, the papers' two homes the week's two truths. Quill's voice: custody, not ownership. Octavia's: the columns will want consulting. Harrow's: to keep, not to read — but the keeping is done. Rose looks at the key in her pocket, at the library beyond the corridor. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(The order goes to the household in a low voice, and the keeping rearranges itself around it — the library's shelf cleared or the strongbox's inventory begun or the bundles parted once more, the book entering the line as Friday ordered. Whatever the keeping became, one law holds it entire: the papers stay the house's, wherever they sleep. The seals are re-tied. The reading waits on nothing.)*

options.label: Divided again
options.detail: *Mercy+; the halves, honored.* The garden's to the library, London's to Harrow's keeping; two homes, two truths. *(Honored — and the carrier, carrying still.)*

scenes.synopsis: the keeping, ordered — the seals re-tied; the book, entered.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia receives the order and folds it into the evening without breaking stride. "The keeping," she says, the pencil moving — the library's shelf, the strongbox's inventory, or the parting, as the book orders. If the library: the box is brought, the papers laid in, Rose's seal pressed in the wax — the house's mark on the house's papers. If the strongbox: Quill's clerk is sent for, the inventory begun in duplicate. If divided: the garden's bundle to the library's shelf, the London bundle to Harrow's hands, the carrier carrying still.)*
> *("The book," Letitia says, blotting the page, "has the keeping's line. Whatever Friday ordered, the papers are the house's, and the house knows where they sleep." She closes the book with the gavel-thump. The seals, re-tied. The keeping, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the reading resumes — the hands matched; the week of the fall, dated.
scenes.prose:
> *(The reading resumes after the keeping's order, and the evening's work is the matching: Elias's hand in the garden's bundle against Elias's hand in the London bundle — the memoranda against the keeping's copies, the ventures dated, the fall given its week. "The same hand," Octavia says, holding two pages to the lamp. "Twenty years apart, and the E still tall." Harrow nods from the table's far side. "He wrote the direction himself," he says. "To London, kept till called for. I watched him write it.")*
> *(Rose looks at the two pages — the young man's E and the old man's E, the venture and the keeping — and feels the week close around the papers like a hand around a wrist. Not the sin's shape. Not yet. But the papers are one thing now, not two, and the house holds them. The halves, matched. The week, dated.)*

scenes.synopsis: the supper dress — the evening after paper; the atelier's answer.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at seven with the supper question, and the atelier has been thinking about paper dust all day. "The reading is done, miss, the keeping is ordered, and the evening wants the mistress back." Three on the bed: the deep green silk, remade from the stores — the archive's answer to a week of grey; the claret, her mother's, re-cut — the evenings, claimed in color; or the grey wool, the day's own — the work, carried to table unadorned.)*
> *(Rose touches the green — stored silk, remade, the archive giving back. The claret waits, bold. The grey wool, honest. "The papers had the day," she says. "The evening is the house's." Élise pins, or drapes, or settles, as ordered. "There," she says. "The mistress, returned." In the glass: the keeper, dressed for her own table.)*

scenes.synopsis: supper — the household entire; the schoolmaster, taking shape at table.
scenes.prose:
> *(Supper is the household entire — Augusta at the table's head in spirit if not in chair, Julian with the rent-book put by for once, Octavia, Letitia, Laurent, and Harrow, seated where Friday ordered him: among them, not apart. Mrs. Pike's kitchen sends up the Friday joint, and the talk is of Saturday's party — the guests, the music, the Park as a stage — and not of papers, by unspoken agreement.)*
> *(Harrow eats quietly and answers when spoken to, and Henry — permitted the table for the pudding — asks him about copybooks, and Harrow answers at length, and the table listens. Rose watches the schoolmaster take his shape at her table: the spare shoulders eased, the clerk's hands at rest. Whatever Friday ordered, the man is kept. The supper, shared. The household, entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: the law on the wages — the keeping done, a debt; the figure, Friday's to name.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill comes after supper, as arranged, with the wage's figure and the law's plain arithmetic. "The keeping done," he says, "is a debt, Miss Hartwell — twenty years of it, and the law understands a paid keeper better than a grateful one. Name the figure. Enter it in the book. Wages for the keeping done, wages for the keeping to come, the terms plain.")*
> *("The figure," Rose says, "is Friday's to name." "Then name it Friday," Quill says, "and name it fairly — the keeping was long, and the man is proud, and pride prices itself. A paid keeper is a keeper the law understands. An unpaid keeper —" he folds his hands, "— is the law's mystery, and you have mysteries enough." He rises. The bag closes. The counsel, given.)*

scenes.synopsis: the village's Friday arithmetic — the lane's sums; the school, wanting a master.
scenes.prose:
> *(Mrs. Pike comes up at half past eight with the supper things and the lane's whole account. "The village," she says, stacking, "has done its sums, Miss Hartwell, and the sums say the schoolmaster's to have the cottage. Or the clerk's room. Or the Crown's best chamber — the lane can't agree, which means the lane's interested." She hands Rose the paper twist. "Gingerbread. Decisions are hungry work.")*
> *("And the school?" Rose asks. "The school," Mrs. Pike says, "has had no master to speak of since the old one went to Bath with his lungs, and the children have had the copybooks but no corrector. The village would take Mr. Harrow in a minute." She hoists the tray. "The lane's words, miss, not mine — though mine agree." The cart rattles off. The village, consulted.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dusk wrap — the garden round; the reading's dust, walked off.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia meets her at the stair with the dusk's question and the quartermaster's eye on the weather. "The round, miss — the garden wants its mistress before the light goes, and the reading's dust wants walking off." Three on the peg: the grey cloak, hooded — the dusk, walked unseen; the green wool shawl, the garden's color — the round, faced in green; or the black silk, respectable — the evening, faced in state.)*
> *(Rose touches the green wool — the garden's color, the threshold's shade. The grey cloak waits, plain. The black silk, severe. "The papers are kept," she says. "The garden kept me first." Letitia drapes, or pins, or settles, as ordered. "There," she says. "The keeper, wrapped." The dusk, dressed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dusk round — the violet bed; the deciding, settled like dust.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose walks the dusk round alone — the mistress's last walk of the reading day. The garden lies quiet, the gap in the wall a dark notch, the violet bed along the south wall low and wild, flowerless. She stops there, as Thursday, and thinks of the two sprigs pressed in two bundles: faithfulness, kept two ways, now unsealed and read.)*
> *(Behind her the house waits with its lit windows, and in it a man of sixty-one whose place is ordered and whose wage waits for naming. She stands a moment with the dusk coming on, and the deciding settles the way dust settles: the place, the keeping, the figure. The house has taken the past in and given it a chair. Tomorrow the Park fills for the party. Tonight the garden holds the mistress. The round, walked.)*

scenes.synopsis: Friday's keeping ritual — the household dresses the house for the keeping of papers.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the box — "keep as you mean to go on, miss. The house takes its tone from you.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the papers — "the columns are open, Rose. Tonight the keeping keeps you.")*
> *(Story morsel: Augusta, at the door — "curate it, child. The house, too.")*
> *(Story morsel: Harrow, at the back — the schoolmaster, the keeping new on him.)*
> *(Story morsel: Élise, at the door — "tomorrow's party gets the extra stitch. For Saturday.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: Friday read the two halves together — the garden's bundle and London's, side by side at ten, the seals broken in company. The papers are kept now, the keeping ordered, the schoolmaster placed. Before the week of the reading's last night, the household gathers in the morning room and dresses the house for the keeping of papers — what it means to hold the past and give it a chair. The box on the table, the lamps lit, the house quiet around its own archive. Dress for the keeping: the papers' colors, worn with intent, eyes open. Precise. Together. Attentive. The house that keeps together does not flinch apart.

scenes.synopsis: the brother's plain talk — the rent-book's blessing on the keeping.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian walks her back from the garden gate, the rent-book under his elbow though it is dusk, and talks plainly, the way brothers do when the house has taken in something large. "His place," he says. "The schoolmaster's chair. The archives by day, the copybooks by calling. The rent-book says the school wants a master, and one man answering it is economy.")*
> *("And the wage?" Rose asks. "The wage," Julian says, "is Friday's to name, and Friday is nearly done. Name it fairly — the keeping was long, and the man is proud, and the rent-book has a line for honest wages." He looks at her. "He's honest, Rose. I watched him at the table — men who carry things for twenty years carry them straight." He squeezes her arm. "Whatever Friday names, the rent-book stands it." The dusk, the brother, the plain talk — held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening's talk — the thanking, done properly; paternal, the night.
scenes.prose:
> *(He finds her in the hall at half past nine — the schoolmaster, the keeping new on him — and speaks plainly, the way the evening has taught them both. "Miss Hartwell," he says. "Twenty years I kept your grandfather's papers, and tonight I am a man with a cottage, or a room, as Friday ordered, and work in the open. I have been thanked. I would like, before the day ends, to do the thanking.")*
> *(She stands in the hall with the lamps burning and watches him — the spare shoulders, the white scar, the clerk's hands at his sides. Responsibility, plain and uncomplicated, the way Thursday named it. Curiosity, too — the sin has no shape yet, and he knows where the bodies are. But tonight is the keeping's night, and the keeping is done. The lamps burn. The hall, quiet.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's last word — on the sin unnamed; the ton's favorite story.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends for her at ten — the blue drawing room, the chocolate going cold, the eyebrow at rest, which for the dowager is the end of the day. "Well," she says. "The papers are read, the man is kept, the keeping is ordered. You have done Friday well, child." She regards her granddaughter over the cup. "The sin has no shape yet. Let it wait for its shape. Your grandfather's speculation is the ton's favorite kind of story, and Saturday's party will be full of ears.")*
> *(She rises, which is the dismissal. "And Rose — the house did well by the clerk this week. See it does as well by the mistress. Go to bed, child. Friday will need you rested — and so will Saturday." The lamps are low. The interview is over.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE WAGES: pay him now, settle quarterly, or let his pride refuse.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the study, and the night is thinning toward eleven, and the wage's line waits in the book for Friday's figure. Three namings offer themselves. Pay him now: the keeping done, priced fair — the twenty years, acknowledged in the book, the debt entered fair and paid, the keeper paid as Octavia counseled and Quill advised. Settle quarterly: the schoolmaster's wage and the archivist's, entered as terms — the keeping to come, priced by the quarter, the house's books carrying him the way they carry the masons.)*
> *(Or let his pride refuse: name the figure, and let him decline it — his place and the work his wage, the dignity of the refusing honored, the book entering "declined with thanks" in Letitia's fairest hand. Augusta's voice: give him the dignity of the asking. Harrow's: I will earn the room. Quill's: a paid keeper is a keeper the law understands. Rose looks at the book, at the waiting line, at the lamp burning low. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(The order goes to Letitia in a low voice, and the wage's line is filled as Friday commanded — the figure entered, the quarters set, or the declining honored, the book holding whichever Friday chose. Whatever the naming became, one law holds it entire: the man is the house's, and the house pays its debts, in coin or in honor. The pencil goes behind the ear. The night, ordered.)*

options.label: Pay him now
options.detail: *Resolve+; the debt, acknowledged.* The keeping done, priced fair; entered fair, paid. *(Acknowledged — and the twenty years, priced in the book.)*

options.label: Settle quarterly
options.detail: *Candor+; the terms, plain.* The schoolmaster's and archivist's wage, by the quarter. *(Plain — and the keeping to come, carried like the masons'.)*

options.label: Let his pride refuse
options.detail: *Mercy+; the dignity, kept.* Name it; let him decline; the cottage and the work his wage. *(Kept — and "declined with thanks," in the fairest hand.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Bell's Friday paragraph; ordinary reading news, no scandal yet.
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting is the Gazette's Friday paragraph, come up with the evening post — Bell's paper, noting the day's ordinary news.)*
> *(Rose reads it twice, the way she reads everything Bell writes, and finds no edge in it — no leader, no verdict, no favorite story. Just the facts, set in Bell's type: the reading, the keeping, the wall's fourth course, the schoolmaster, unnamed. Nothing of the bundles' halves. Nothing of Elias. Nothing of London. She folds the Gazette and sets it by the memorandum book. The paper smells of ink. The house smells of old paper.)*
scenes.sting: the sting — Bell's Friday paragraph; ordinary reading news, no scandal yet.

scenes.synopsis: the night's closing — the seals re-tied under Rose's seal; the room, locked.
scenes.prose:
> *(At eleven Letitia brings the keeping's last order to the morning room, and the night's closing is done as Friday commanded. If the library: the box is sealed with Rose's seal, shelved where the house's papers live, the key in the pocket where it has lived since Tuesday. If the strongbox: Quill's inventory is signed in duplicate, the iron locked. If divided: the garden's bundle sealed in the library, the London bundle in Harrow's hands — the carrier carrying still, till the house calls.)*
> *(Whatever the keeping, Letitia closes the household book with the gavel-thump, and the morning room is locked, and the house is quiet. "The papers sleep, miss," she says. "The house knows where." The pencil goes behind the ear. The night, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night's undressing — the day unmade; the atelier's last word.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at half past eleven with the night's question, the atelier's last word on a week of paper. "Done, miss — the reading, the keeping, the placing. The day wants unmaking, and the atelier has opinions." Three on the bed: the grandmother's lace robe, ivory — the night, faced in heirloom; the plain flannel, warm and honest — the sleep, faced without dressing; or the green silk, kept on a little longer — the evening, unwilling to end.)*
> *(Rose touches the lace — ivory, the grandmother's, the week's reward. The flannel waits, warm. The green silk holds the evening's shape. "The house kept its Friday," she says, "and Friday was long." Élise unpins, or folds, or settles, as ordered. "There," she says. "The keeper, unmade. Sleep, miss. The party can wait till morning." The lamp is turned low. The day, undone.)*

scenes.synopsis: the book, entered — Friday's lines, written fair; Saturday's business.
scenes.prose:
> *(Before the night round, Letitia opens the household book at the kitchen table and writes Friday in her fairest hand — the joint reading at ten, the seals broken in company, the creditors' names copied, Harrow's story begun, his place ordered as Friday commanded, the keeping as Friday commanded, the wage's line filled with Friday's figure. The bundle's business she writes as "the papers' business," which is the book's way of knowing without saying.)*
> *("The carrier's book," Rose says. "The letter for Mr. Harrow you carried to the post — did you trace it?" "The carrier's book still exists," Letitia says, "and the tracing is Saturday's business. Tonight the book holds Friday." She closes the book with the gavel-thump. "And Saturday, miss — the party. The Park fills at four. The house will want its mistress rested." The pencil goes behind the ear. The book lies closed on the kitchen table, holding the day.)*

scenes.synopsis: the house at night — the round; the sin, unnamed; the weight, carried.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose walks the night round alone — the mistress's last walk of the reading week. The morning room is locked, the box sealed, the key in her pocket. The house is quiet the way houses are quiet when they have done a hard thing well. In the village, or in the clerk's room, as Friday ordered, a man of sixty-one sleeps the second easy sleep of his keeping's ending.)*
> *(She stops at the stair window and looks out at the dark garden, the wall's fourth course a pale line in the moonlight. The papers are read and kept. The sin has no shape yet — the shape is not in the papers, Harrow said, and when it comes she will know it. Curiosity, and the responsibility that outranks it. She turns toward her room, and the night goes on.)*

scenes.synopsis: the last sheet — the first full ledger page, in Elias's own hand; the speculation entries.
scenes.prose: > *(Near midnight — the lamps low, the book closed — Harrow's knock comes at the study door, soft, the way the household knocks when the news is kept. In his hands: a single sheet, from the London bundle's bottom, saved for last. "This is the page the keeping was for," he says. "The first full page. Your grandfather's hand, and no one else's." He lays it on the desk and goes. Rose holds it to the lamp: the ledger page, ruled, dated — the war's late years. The Nantes venture — advanced — nine hundred. The Lisbon account — fourteen hundred. The Cadiz drafts — returned nothing. Line after line, Elias's speculation entries in Elias's own hand, the tall E, the impatient crossings. She reads to the page's foot, and the lamp gutters, and the last line waits to be read.)*

scenes.synopsis: Saturday's dawn — the ledger page on the study desk; the last line, still unread; the house wakes first.
scenes.prose:
> *(Saturday wakes her before the maid, the way the week has trained it to — but this dawn is bluer, earlier, the hour when the house is all held breath. Rose lies a moment and sees the study desk in her mind's eye, though she is in her own bed: the ledger page lying where she left it at midnight, Elias's hand running to the page's foot, the last line folded under the lamplight, unread.)*
> *(She meant to read it at dawn. The house has other plans — the stair already creaks, Letitia's pencil already moves somewhere below, Saturday already arranging itself around the party the way furniture arranges itself around a fire. The last line waits. The Park fills at four. She dresses in the blue dark, and the page keeps its counsel.)*

scenes.synopsis: the day's order — the quartermaster's Saturday; the book's lines; the tracing, reported.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia is in the morning room with the day's order already half executed, Saturday's whole philosophy. "Four o'clock," she says, the pencil moving. "The carriages, the receiving, the Park's first stage. Six — the garden walk, the route as the book orders. Eight — supper. After — the dancing, and the musicians want the hall by seven." She blots the page. "The house," she says, "is a machine with one setting today.")*
> *("And the letter?" Rose asks — Harrow's letter, carried to the post in Elias's day, the carrier's book holding it. "Traced," Letitia says. "The carrier's book gives it up clean — the Tuesday coach to London, thirty years gone, the London direction. The book keeps the sending, miss, not the answering. Whatever Elias wrote Mr. Harrow then, it went." She closes the book with the gavel-thump. "Saturday's business, done before breakfast. The book likes that.")*

scenes.synopsis: the party dress — Saturday's foreseen choice; the atelier's three faces, come to the day.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise has been waiting all week for this one — the sketchbook's Saturday page, come to life on the stand. "The foreseen, miss," she says. "Chosen in the sketchbook, cut in the week, finished last night by lamplight. Three faces, as promised. The archive's full splendor — grandmother's lace over the rose silk, history worn like armor. The Hartwell blue — the household in the estate's color, the restoration worn as a uniform. Or the atelier's newest work — the present, dressed fresh, the mistress first in it.")*
> *(Rose touches the lace — the grandmother's, ivory over rose, the week's reward. The blue waits, severe. The newest work, bright. "Saturday," she says, "wants the rumor dressed before the rumor dresses me." "Which," Élise says, pinning, "is why the atelier began Tuesday." She chooses Saturday's face. In the glass: the mistress, staged.)*

scenes.synopsis: the archive on display — heirloom lace, grandmother's jewels, remade stored silks; the house dressing its people.
scenes.prose:
> *(The atelier has dressed the whole household, and Élise shows her the muster the way a general shows troops: Letitia in remade stored silk, the quartermaster splendid; Octavia in dove grey with the second-best lace at the throat; the maids in the house's livery, brushed and pressed; even Mrs. Pike's kitchen whites gone solemn for the day. The stored silks, remade, walk the corridors.)*
> *("The archive," Élise says, "gives back what it was given. Twenty years in the stores, and Saturday wears it." Rose looks at the house's people in the house's old clothes, and the restoration stops being stone and courses for a moment and becomes something else. The silk, the lace, the remade. The house, wearing its history.)*

scenes.synopsis: the guest list — county families and London guests; the household's own; Amos at the door.
scenes.prose:
> *(The guest list lies on the morning-room table in Letitia's fairest hand, and Rose reads it the way she reads everything now: twice. The county families — the squire's wife and the squire, the rectory, the families whose names are on the cottages. The London guests — the Season's names, come down to see what the fortune bought. And the household's own: Augusta, Julian, Octavia, Laurent, Henry in his party clothes, the atelier, the kitchen.)*
> *("Amos at the door," Letitia says. "The porter's whole philosophy is doors, and Saturday is his day." She sets the list square. "The book," she says, "calls it 'the Park's first stage.' The book," Rose says, "has been reading the atelier's sketchbook." "The book," Letitia says, "reads everything." The list, squared. The stage, set.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE GUESTS: county first, London first, or the household's own.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the study, and the list is squared, and the question of the order runs alongside the question of the dress. The county first: the squire's wife, the rectory, the names on the cottages — the Park's own ground, honored before the ton's. The London guests first: the Season's names, the judgment that matters in print — the ton, courted, the verdict managed before it is written. Or the household's own first: Augusta and Julian and Octavia and Laurent and Henry, the house's people — the party built from the middle out, the mistress receiving her own before she receives the world.)*
> *(Augusta's voice: the ton respects nothing it wasn't made to wait for. Letitia's: the book will want the order. Laurent's, unknowing: receive them all at once, and let the house be the house. Rose looks at the list, at the four o'clock drawing nearer, at the key in her pocket. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(The order goes to Letitia in a low voice, and the receiving rearranges itself around it — Amos briefed at the door, the hall's order re-set, the book entering the line as Saturday ordered. Whatever the order became, one law holds it entire: the mistress receives, and the house stands behind her receiving. The carriages are on the road. The choosing is done.)*

scenes.synopsis: the ordering, done — Amos briefed; the hall re-set; the book's line.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia takes the order and folds it into the afternoon without breaking stride. If the county: Amos is told the squire's carriage first, the hall's order re-set, the neighbors' names at the top of the receiving line. If London: the Season's names first, the ton's carriages given the door, the county's to follow. If the household's: Augusta's chair placed, Julian at the stair, Octavia with the book, Laurent and Henry — the house's own, received before the world.)*
> *("The book," Letitia says, blotting the page, "has the receiving's line. Whatever Saturday ordered, the door knows its order." She closes the book with the gavel-thump. Amos takes his post, the porter's shoulders squared for the day's philosophy. The hall stands ready. The road, watched.)*

scenes.synopsis: the walled garden, readied — the gap, the numbered stones; the walk's route, planned.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia walks the garden's route with her at noon, the memorandum book open, the walk planned the way Octavia plans everything: on paper. "The south wall first," she says, "the violet bed, the old espaliers. Then the north stretch — the gap." The gap stands open to the fields, the oldest wall down, the courses numbered and stacked on the south lawn, the masons' yard beyond. The fourth course of the new work runs pale along the east.)*
> *("Six o'clock," Octavia says, "the light does the wall's work for it." She makes a note. "Rose. Whatever the walk shows, the garden is the week's honest page. Let it be read." The gap waits, open to the fields, a dark notch in the old stone. The route, planned. The garden, readied.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, dowagered — Augusta on the party; the ton's ears; the London names.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta receives her in the blue drawing room at two, the chocolate sent for, the party's hour approaching. "Well," she says. "The Park's first stage. The county will come to be pleased, and the London names will come to judge, and both will leave having done neither quite as they planned — if you manage it." She regards her granddaughter over the cup. "The London guests have ears, child. Your grandfather's speculation is the ton's favorite kind of story. Give them the restoration to look at, and keep the papers' business where the papers are.")*
> *("In the library," Rose says. "Under seal." "Under seal," Augusta says, "and under your eye. Enjoy the party, child — the house has earned an evening. But remember: a hostess hears everything and repeats nothing. It is the whole of the office." She rises, which is the dismissal. The eyebrow, at full mast. The counsel, given.)*

scenes.synopsis: four o'clock — the first carriages; the Park, filling; the stage, lit.
scenes.prose:
> *(At four the drive fills the way a tide fills — first one carriage, then three, then the gravel loud with them. Amos at the door, the porter's philosophy in full force; Letitia in the hall, the receiving's order in her head; Augusta in her chair, the eyebrow deployed; Julian at the stair, the rent-book put by; Octavia with the memorandum book; Laurent at Rose's side, easy; Henry in his party clothes, very straight.)*
> *(Rose stands at the hall's head in Saturday's face — the dress as the sketchbook ordered — and receives. The county first, or the London names, or the household's own, as Saturday commanded. The Park fills. The half-restored house shows what the restoration has made: the stone, the silk, the remade. The stage, lit. The party, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: the jewels — dressed to receive; the grandmother's jewels, the heirloom lace, the silver rose pin.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at half past four with the receiving's last question, the atelier's eye on the hall's light. "The dress is Saturday's face, miss. The jewels are its voice." Three on the tray: the grandmother's jewels — the heirlooms, worn as worn, the house's old brilliance; the heirloom lace doubled at the throat and wrist — the archive, layered, lace answering lace; or the silver rose pin, plain — the house's mark, worn quiet, the mistress undisguised.)*
> *(Rose touches the jewels — the grandmother's, heavy with the wearing of women she never met. The lace waits, ivory. The pin, plain silver. "The hall's light," she says, "wants something that catches it." "The hall's light," Élise says, pinning, "wants you." She chooses the receiving's voice. In the glass: the hostess, jeweled.)*

scenes.synopsis: Laurent unknowing and attentive — the terrace's edge; the dramatic irony, held.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent finds her between receivings, at the terrace's edge, and looks at the Park the way he looks at everything she has made: as if it were inevitable. "Your grandfather," he says, "would have enjoyed this — the house full, the county come to look. Old Elias, holding court among the stones." He says it warmly, easily, the way a man speaks of a legend he never had to live with.)*
> *(Rose feels the ledger page on the study desk like a weight in another room — the speculation entries, the last line unread — and smiles, and takes his arm. "He would have enjoyed the judging," she says. "He enjoyed most things that involved an audience." Laurent laughs, unknowing, attentive, his hand over hers. The irony sits between them, invisible, patient. The terrace, the afternoon, the ease — held entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: the old émigré names — a London guest, over the punch; Nantes, named; the cup, pausing.
scenes.prose:
> *(It is over the punch, in the hall's bright middle, that a London guest — one of the Season's names, all ease and observation — says it. They are talking of the restoration, of the French stone, and he laughs. "Nantes," he says. "Takes me back — those old émigré names, de la Roche, de Brissac, the war's leavings, scratched into every carrier's book from Bath to Lisbon.")*
> *(Rose's cup pauses — half an inch, no more. De la Roche. De Brissac. The ledger's entries, spoken aloud in her own hall by a man with punch on his breath. "The ports," she says evenly, "are full of many things." He laughs again, and the talk moves on, and nobody marks the pause but her. The names, spoken. The hall, bright.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, brothered — Julian on the Park's showing; the rent-book, at rest.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian finds her at the stair's turn, the rent-book put by for once — actually put by, not carried — and talks plainly. "The Park's showing well," he says. "The county's pleased, the London names are looking, and the looking is the kind that spends money." He glances at the hall. "Counsel, and it costs nothing: let them look. The house has nothing to hide that the stone doesn't already say.")*
> *("The stone says the wall's fourth course," Rose says. "The stone," Julian says, "says the Hartwells build. Let the London names write that in their letters. It's the only sentence Saturday needs." He squeezes her arm, brotherly, and goes back to the stair. The counsel, given. The rent-book, resting.)*

scenes.synopsis: Henry in his party clothes — the boy, very straight; the schoolmaster, asked after.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry finds her by the morning-room door, very straight in his party clothes, the copybook nowhere in evidence — a concession to Saturday. "Is Mr. Harrow coming to the party?" he asks. It is the day's question, asked with the full weight of eight years. "He practiced his letters," Henry adds, in case the question needs ballast. "For when he starts.")*
> *(Rose looks at the boy — the straight back, the party clothes, the copybook's invisible weight — and chooses her words the way she chooses everything today: carefully. "The schoolmaster keeps his own hours, Henry. Saturday is deciding the rest." Henry considers this with the gravity of a judge. "Tell him I asked," he says. The tribute, delivered twice over. The boy, dispatched to the cake.)*

scenes.synopsis: the garden-walk wrap — six o'clock coming; the atelier's answer to the dusk.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise meets her at the stair at half past five with the walk's question, the atelier's eye on the sky. "Six o'clock, miss, the garden, the gap — and the dusk has opinions about silk." Three on the peg: the green wool shawl, the garden's color — the walk, faced in green; the grey silk mantle, fine — the dusk, faced fine; or the grandmother's paisley, the archive's warmth — the evening, faced in heirloom.)*
> *(Rose touches the green wool — the garden's color, the threshold's shade. The grey mantle waits, fine. The paisley, warm with the wearing of women she never met. "The garden kept me first," she says. "Let it see me in its color." Élise drapes, or pins, or settles, as ordered. "There," she says. "The walker, wrapped." The walk, dressed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the party at full — the Park showing; the rooms, lit; the music, tuning.
scenes.prose:
> *(By half past five the party is at full — the hall bright, the drawing rooms open, the corridors carrying talk the way gutters carry rain. The county families admire the stone; the London guests admire the scale; everybody admires the remade silks, which is the atelier's whole reward. The musicians tune in the hall, the strings finding each other.)*
> *(Rose moves through it the way Saturday taught her: receiving, turning, listening, repeating nothing. The half-restored Park shows what the restoration has made — and the showing is the thing itself, the house's old brilliance worn in daylight. The rooms, lit. The music, tuning. The party, entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: the library, slipped away — the ledger page, held to the lamp; the last line, nearly read.
scenes.prose:
> *(It is Octavia who makes it possible — Octavia, precise, who sees Rose's eyes go to the corridor and says, "Three minutes. The walk is at six; the company will survive your absence." The library is cool and dim, the box sealed under Rose's seal on the shelf, the ledger page where she left it on the study desk. Rose holds it to the lamp: Elias's hand, the ventures, the sums — Nantes, Lisbon, Cadiz — de la Roche's nine hundred, de Brissac's fourteen hundred, entered fair. Line after line, to the page's foot.)*
> *(Her eyes reach the last line — the ink, the tall E, the impatient crossings — and Octavia is at the door, the memorandum book in her hand. "Rose. They're asking for the walk." The page goes down. The lamp gutters. The last line waits, the way it has waited since midnight, patient as stone. The library, left. The secret, trembling.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE GARDEN: shown with the gap open, shown with the gap curtained, or kept from the walk.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone for a moment at the garden door, and the walk is at six, and the question of the gap runs alongside the question of the ledger's last line. Shown open: the walk goes by the north stretch, the gap confronted — the numbered stones, the masons' yard, the wall's honest wound, Saturday's guests seeing exactly what the week cost. Shown curtained: canvas hung along the north stretch, the work veiled — the garden's beauty uninterrupted, the gap a rumor behind sailcloth. Or kept from the walk: the route turned to the south lawn, the violet bed, the espaliers — the garden spared the showing, the gap unwitnessed.)*
> *(Octavia's voice: the garden is the week's honest page. Augusta's: give them the restoration to look at. The mason's: the courses are numbered, the work is clean. Rose looks at the north stretch, at the six o'clock light doing the wall's work for it, at the company gathering. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(The order goes to the gardeners in a low voice, and the walk rearranges itself around it — the route's flags moved, or the canvas hung, or the south lawn's path swept, the book entering the line as Saturday ordered. Whatever the walk became, one law holds it entire: the garden is the week's honest page, and Saturday reads it as Saturday chose. The company gathers. The choosing is done.)*

scenes.synopsis: the walk, led — the garden at six; the gap, confronted as Saturday chose.
scenes.prose:
> *(At six she leads the walk herself — the mistress's office — the company following through the south wall's gate: the county families, the London guests, the household. The violet bed along the south wall, low and wild; the old espaliers; the light doing the wall's work. And the north stretch — if open: the gap confronted, the numbered stones stacked, the masons' yard beyond, the guests quiet before the wound. If curtained: the canvas hung clean, the sailcloth hiding the work, the beauty uninterrupted. If turned: the south lawn instead, the gap unwitnessed, the garden entire.)*
> *(She walks it the way Saturday taught her: steadily, answering the questions the stone can answer, leaving the rest to the light. A London guest asks about the wall's age; the squire's wife asks about the courses. The garden gives up its beauty and keeps its counsel. The walk, led. The six, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, figured — Octavia on the London guest's names; the reading, deferred to Sunday.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia finds her after the walk, the memorandum book in her hand, the pencil doing the thinking. "De la Roche," she says. "De Brissac. The ledger's entries, spoken in your hall by a man with punch on his breath." She taps the pencil. "Counsel, and it costs nothing: the names are entries, not people — not yet. The papers needed names. Whatever the London guest knew, he knew the ports, not the page.")*
> *("And Sunday?" Rose asks. "Sunday," Octavia says, "the last line gets read, and the columns get summed, and the shape — if there is a shape — gets its first look. Tonight is the party's. The papers can wait till the house is quiet." She makes a note, and does not write a total. The counsel, given. The Sunday, set.)*

scenes.synopsis: the county's verdict — the squire's wife on the restoration; the Park, coming back.
scenes.prose:
> *(The squire's wife finds her by the espaliers, county-direct, and says what the county has been saying all afternoon in lower voices. "It's coming back, Miss Hartwell. The Park." She looks at the wall, the garden, the house beyond. "We watched it go down, and we're watching it come up, and there's not a family in the county that isn't glad to see it." She pats Rose's arm, country-kind. "Your grandfather would be pleased.")*
> *(Rose feels the ledger page again — the speculation entries, the last line — and the county's kindness lands the way kindness does when it names the wrong man pleased. "The Park," she says, "thanks the county." The squire's wife nods, satisfied, and moves on to the roses. The verdict, county-given. The arm, patted.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening refresh — the walk's dust; the atelier's answer to the dance's approach.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at seven with the evening's question, the atelier having watched the walk. "Garden dust, miss, and the walk's green on the hem, and the dance approaching. The atelier proposes the refresh." Three on the bench: the hair re-dressed, pinned higher — the evening's second face; the mended gloves, kept for the dancing — the mend, worn where the company can see it; or the shawl for the terrace air — the night, faced warm.)*
> *(Rose touches the hair — the walk's pins loosened, the dusk in it. The gloves wait, fresh. The shawl, warm. "The garden had the afternoon," she says. "The evening is the house's." Élise pins, or changes, or drapes, as ordered. "There," she says. "The dancer, refreshed." In the glass: the evening, faced.)*

scenes.synopsis: supper ordered — the quartermaster's evening; the table, set; the musicians, placed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia waylays her at half past seven with the evening's order, the quartermaster's eye on the dining room. "Eight o'clock," she says, the pencil moving. "Supper — the long table, the county and the London names mixed as the book orders. The musicians in the hall by seven, the punch iced, the terrace doors open to the night." She blots the page. "The house," she says, "is running like a watch.")*
> *("And after?" Rose asks. "After," Letitia says, "the dancing, and the dance cards want filling, and the mistress wants to be seen enjoying her own party — the book is firm on that line." She closes the book with the gavel-thump. "Eight o'clock, miss. The table will want its mistress hungry." The pencil goes behind the ear. The supper, ordered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, brothered — Julian at supper's edge; the evening, judged.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian catches her at the dining-room door, between the ordering and the sitting, and talks plainly. "The evening's going well," he says. "The county's fed and flattered, the London names are writing their letters in their heads, and the Park's the hero of every one." He looks at her — brother's eyes, seeing more than the party. "Counsel, and it costs nothing: eat something. You've received a county on an empty stomach.")*
> *("The book says the mistress must be seen enjoying," Rose says. "The book," Julian says, "is right, and the rent-book seconds it. Enjoyment takes fuel." He steers her toward the table, brotherly, and the evening's weight eases a fraction. The counsel, given. The supper, imminent.)*

scenes.synopsis: supper served — the long table; the county and the London names, mixed; the toasts.
scenes.prose:
> *(Supper is the long table at eight — the county and the London names mixed as the book ordered, Augusta at the table's head in state, Julian with the rent-book put by, Octavia, Laurent at Rose's right, Henry permitted the table for the pudding, the atelier and the kitchen in their Saturday best. Mrs. Pike's kitchen sends up the Saturday joint, and the talk is of the Park — the wall, the garden, the stone — and the papers, by unspoken agreement, are left to sleep in the library.)*
> *(The toasts: the Park, the restoration, the county. Rose drinks them standing, Saturday's face on, the jewels catching the candlelight. A London guest toasts the hostess; the squire's wife toasts the wall. The table is loud and kind and full. The supper, served. The evening, at full.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dance dressing — the atelier's last word before the first set; the dancer, faced.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at nine with the dance's question, the atelier's last word on Saturday. "Supper's done, miss, the table's cleared, and the first set wants the dancer." Three on the bed: the dancing slippers, soled for the floor — the evening, faced light; the sash retied, the bow at the back — the waist, faced for the turning; or the grandmother's fan, ivory — the hand, faced with something to do between sets.)*
> *(Rose touches the slippers — satin, the floor's whole promise. The sash waits, bright. The fan, ivory, cool. "The party," she says, "has been the house's all day. The dance is mine." Élise ties, or reties, or places, as ordered. "There," she says. "The dancer, faced." In the glass: the evening's second self.)*

scenes.synopsis: the terrace before the dance — Laurent's hand; the unknowing, held close.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent finds her on the terrace before the first set, the night come down, the hall's light behind them. "Dance the first with me," he says. "The Park's mistress should open her own floor." His hand is warm, his ease entire, and he looks at her the way he looked at the Park at four — as if it were inevitable, as if nothing in the house's past could touch the evening.)*
> *(She takes his hand — the mended glove, the warm hand — and the ledger page sits on the study desk two corridors away, the last line unread, the sin without a shape. He knows nothing. He holds her hand like a man holding something certain. "The first," she says, "is yours." The terrace, the night, the ease — held entire, and undivided.)*

scenes.synopsis: the boy, sleepy — taken up; the copybook's report; the day, ended for the eight-year-old.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry is found at half past nine on the stair's third step, very straight no longer — the party clothes rumpled, the eyelids at half mast, the day's weight finally telling. "I practiced," he tells her, rallying. "The letters. For Mr. Harrow. Tell him I asked." It is the day's question, asked a third time, and this time it is a message.)*
> *(Rose sits beside him on the step — the mistress, the dancer, the sister — and the house's noise comes up the stair, kind and distant. "I'll tell him," she says. "Up you go." He goes, the copybook's invisible weight carried upstairs, and Saturday ends for the eight-year-old on the third step. The stair, quieted. The boy, delivered.)*

scenes.synopsis: Saturday's dance ritual — the household dresses the house for the dance.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the candles — "light as you mean to go on, miss. The house takes its tone from you.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the cards — "the sets are numbered, Rose. Tonight the counting dances.")*
> *(Story morsel: Augusta, at the door — "dance it, child. The house, too.")*
> *(Story morsel: Élise, at the hem — "the extra stitch held, miss. All week, for Saturday.")*
> *(Story morsel: Julian, at the stair — "the floor's clear, Rose. The Park's ready when you are.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: Saturday filled the Park at four — county families and London guests, the house showing what the restoration has made. The garden is walked, the table is cleared, and the evening turns toward the dance. Before the first set, the household gathers in the hall and dresses the house for the dancing — what it means to open the Park's doors and let the county see the work. The candles lit, the floor cleared, the music tuned. Dress for the dance: the evening's colors, worn with intent, eyes open. Precise. Together. Attentive. The house that dances together does not stumble apart.

scenes.synopsis: the dance begins — the first set; the Park as stage; the floor, opened.
scenes.prose:
> *(The dance begins at ten — the hall cleared, the candles lit every branch, the musicians tuned and placed. Rose opens the floor with Laurent, the first set, Saturday's face on, the slippers finding the floor the way the atelier promised. The company follows: the county families, the London guests, the household — the Park dancing in its own hall for the first time in twenty years.)*
> *(She dances it the way Saturday taught her: turning, smiling, repeating nothing. The half-restored house holds the music the way it held the talk — entire. Augusta watches from her chair, the eyebrow at rest. Julian dances with the squire's wife. The floor, opened. The ten, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — HARROW: presented as the schoolmaster, kept from the party, or introduced quietly to a few.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone for a moment at the hall's edge, between the sets, and the question of the man runs alongside the question of the evening. Presented: brought into the hall before the company and named — James Harrow, the Park's schoolmaster, his place ordered — the keeping honored in the open, the scarred face faced. Kept from the party: the schoolmaster's evening his own, his door quiet — the papers' keeper unseen, the party unshadowed, the man spared the ton's looking. Or introduced quietly: no presentation, no announcement — walked to the squire's wife and two neighbors, the schoolmaster named in conversation, eased in the way a book is shelved.)*
> *(Augusta's voice: the ton respects what it is told to respect. Letitia's: the book will want the line. Harrow's: I will earn the room. Rose looks at the dancing floor, at the door, at the night beyond it. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(The order goes out in a low voice, and the evening rearranges itself around it. If presented: she brings him to the hall's head between the sets, and names him — James Harrow, the Park's schoolmaster — and the company turns, and turns back to the dancing, and the scarred face is faced. If kept: she slips to his keeping herself with the evening's word — the party is the house's, his evening his own — and he bows, clerk-precise, and the night keeps him. If introduced quietly: she walks him to the squire's wife and two neighbors, and the naming is done in conversation, and nobody marks it but the book. Whatever the evening became, one law holds it entire: the man is the house's, and the house stands behind its naming. The choosing is done.)*
