scenes.synopsis: the telling — his answer to the evening's order; the schoolmaster, placed.
scenes.prose:
> *(She tells him as Saturday ordered — in the hall's bright middle, or at his door, or among the neighbors, as the evening commanded. If presented: he bows to the company, clerk-precise, the scarred face steady, and takes the naming the way he took his place — as a keeping. If kept: at his door he hears the evening's word, and bows, and says, "The house is generous, Miss Hartwell. The evening is yours." If introduced quietly: he shakes the squire's wife's hand, and answers her questions about copybooks at length, and the neighbors nod.)*
> *(Whatever the telling, he meets her eyes when it is done — level, unadorned. "I will earn the evening," he says, "as I earned the room." "Work," Rose says, and he nods, the precise nod. The telling, done. The schoolmaster, placed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dance, continued — the second set; Laurent's warmth; the irony, danced.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent claims the second set, and the third, the way a man claims what the evening offered him. They dance, and he talks between the figures — of the Park, of the evening, of the house's future, all certainty. "Whatever the past held," he says, turning her, "the future's dancing in your hall." He says it lightly, fondly, unknowing — and the past is on the study desk two corridors away, holding its last line.)*
> *(Rose turns in his arms, Saturday's face on, the fan — or the sash, or the slippers — doing its office. He knows nothing. The music knows nothing. The hall is bright and the floor is full and the irony dances between them, invisible, patient, keeping time. The set, danced. The night, at full.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Bell's Saturday paragraph; the party, printed; no scandal yet.
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting is the Gazette's Saturday paragraph, come up with the evening post — Bell's paper, noting the party's opening hours, the proprietor's eye on the Season.)*
> *(Rose reads it between the sets, the way she reads everything Bell writes, and finds no edge in it — no leader, no verdict, no favorite story. Just the facts, set in Bell's type: the four, the six, the ten. Nothing of the ledger. Nothing of Elias. Nothing of the last line. She folds the Gazette and gives it to Octavia for the memorandum book. The paper smells of ink. The hall smells of candles.)*
scenes.sting: the sting — Bell's Saturday paragraph; the party, printed; no scandal yet.

scenes.synopsis: the party's closing — the last carriages; the house, settling; the night, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(The party ends the way parties end: gradually, then all at once. The last set at midnight, the last carriage at half past, Amos at the door till the gravel is quiet, the candles guttering branch by branch. The county families carry the evening home; the London guests carry their letters-in-their-heads. The household gathers in the hall's aftermath — Augusta's eyebrow at rest, Julian's rent-book still put by, Octavia's pencil down, Letitia's book open for the night's lines.)*
> *(Rose stands in the hall's middle in Saturday's face, the dance's dust on the slippers, and the house settles around her the way it settled Friday — having done a hard thing well. "The book," Letitia says, blotting the page, "calls it 'the Park's first stage, played.'" The pencil goes behind the ear. The night, kept. The party, ended.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, dowagered — Augusta's verdict on the evening; the ton, managed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends for her at half past twelve — the blue drawing room, the chocolate going cold, the eyebrow at rest, which for the dowager is the end of the evening. "Well," she says. "The Park's first stage, played. The county is pleased, the London names are writing, and nobody heard anything the house didn't mean them to hear." She regards her granddaughter over the cup. "You did Saturday well, child.")*
> *(She rises, which is the dismissal. "Sleep, Rose. The papers will keep till the house is quiet — and the house," she says, looking at the dark windows, "is nearly quiet." The lamps are low. The interview is over. The verdict, dowager-given.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night's undressing — the day unmade; the atelier's last word on Saturday.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at one with the night's question, the atelier's last word on a day of faces. "Done, miss — the party, the walk, the dance. The day wants unmaking, and the atelier has opinions." Three on the bed: the grandmother's lace robe, ivory — the night, faced in heirloom; the plain flannel, warm and honest — the sleep, faced without dressing; or the rose silk, kept on a little longer — the evening, unwilling to end.)*
> *(Rose touches the lace — ivory, the grandmother's, the day's reward. The flannel waits, warm. The rose silk holds the dance's shape. "The house played its Saturday," she says, "and Saturday was long." Élise unpins, or folds, or settles, as ordered. "There," she says. "The dancer, unmade. Sleep, miss. The papers can wait till morning." The lamp is turned low. The day, undone.)*

scenes.synopsis: the house at night — the round; the last line, still waiting; Sunday, coming.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose walks the night round alone — the mistress's last walk of the party day. The hall is dark, the morning room locked, the library sealed, the box on its shelf under her seal. In the study the ledger page lies where she left it at midnight Friday — Elias's hand, the ventures, the sums, the last line folded under the lamplight, still unread. She stands over it a moment, and does not turn it. Sunday will want the reading; Saturday has earned its ending.)*
> *(She stops at the stair window and looks out at the dark garden, the gap in the wall a dark notch in the moonlight. The party is ended, the Park is quiet, the papers are kept. The sin has no shape yet — and the shape, Harrow said, will come when it comes. She turns toward her room, and the night goes on. The round, walked.)*

scenes.synopsis: the garden's figure — late, Harrow found alone in the walled garden among the fallen stones.
scenes.prose: > *(It is past one — the lamp low, the round nearly done — when she sees him from the stair window: a figure in the walled garden, among the fallen stones of the north stretch, standing where the gap opens to the fields. Harrow. Alone. The moonlight lays the numbered courses in pale rows, and he stands among them the way a man stands among headstones — still, his scarred face turned to the gap, his clerk's hands at his sides. He does not move. The garden holds him. The stones, fallen.)*

scenes.synopsis: Sunday's dawn — the house at rest; the ledger page on the study desk; the reading, today's.
scenes.prose:
> *(Sunday wakes her the way the week has trained it to — early, bluer, before the maid — and for a moment she lies listening to the house not moving. No stair creaking. No pencil below. The party's aftermath is a held breath, the whole Park exhaling at once. She dresses in the blue dark, and her feet take the corridor toward the study without consulting her.)*
> *(The ledger page lies where she left it Friday at midnight — Elias's hand running to the page's foot, the last line folded under the lamplight, still unread. She stands over it a moment and does not turn it yet. Sunday is the day for it. The house is quiet, the guests are sleeping, and the page has waited two nights. One more hour will not spoil it. She leaves the study and goes down to breakfast, and the page keeps its counsel.)*

scenes.synopsis: Sunday's morning face — the archive's Sabbath answer; the atelier's quiet choice.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes with the morning's question, the atelier's eye on the Sabbath. "Sunday, miss, and the house at rest — the atelier proposes the quiet face." Three on the stand: the archive grey silk, sober — the Sabbath, dressed sober; the claret, quiet — the week's color, worn low; or the Hartwell blue — the estate's color, Sunday uniformed.)*
> *(Rose touches the grey — the week's workhorse, the reading's dress. The claret waits, deep. The blue, severe. "Sunday," she says, "wants the woman, not the mistress." "Sunday," Élise says, buttoning, "wants you rested, miss, which is the atelier's whole doctrine." She chooses the morning's face. In the glass: the reader, dressed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the quartermaster's Sunday — the day's order, gentle; the book's one line.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia is in the morning room with the day's order already executed — Sunday's whole philosophy. "Nine o'clock," she says, the pencil at rest. "Church. The household walks — the guests as they please, which for the London names means not. Dinner at two, the Sabbath's dinner, Mrs. Pike's whole religion. Evening — supper at seven, and the house quiet after." She looks up. "The book," she says, "has one line for Sunday.")*
> *("And the line?" Rose asks. "Rest," Letitia says. She blots nothing, because there is nothing to blot. "The book says the house earned it. The book," she adds, "does not know about the study." Rose laughs, surprised. The pencil goes behind the ear. The Sunday, ordered — gently.)*

scenes.synopsis: the last line — read; the covering, stated in Elias's hand.
scenes.prose:
> *(She goes to the study after breakfast, because Sunday's order has a hole in it shaped exactly like a page. The house is at church — the household walked, the bells gone quiet, the London names sleeping it out — and the study is hers. She takes the ledger page to the lamp, the way she has twice before, and reads Elias's hand down the ventures and the sums: Nantes, Lisbon, Cadiz, the entries fair, the crossings impatient.)*
> *(And then the last line — the tall E, the impatient crossings, the ink gone brown with the years. "The Hartwell interest is made whole. The rest must look to better times." She reads it three times. Made whole. The rest. Better times. The words sit on the page like stones. She sets the page down, and the lamplight gutters, and Sunday's quiet comes back into the room. The line, read. The shape, beginning.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, figured — Octavia on the last line; what "made whole" costs.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes from church with the memorandum book already open, the pencil doing the thinking. Rose shows her the last line. Octavia reads it twice, the way Rose reads everything now. "Made whole," she says. "A curious phrase for a ledger. Ledgers don't make things whole — they balance them." She taps the pencil. "Counsel, and it costs nothing: the line tells you the order. Hartwell first. The rest —" she looks at the page, "— the rest, whenever.")*
> *("And the rest never came," Rose says. "The rest," Octavia says, "is what Sunday is for. Read the columns, Rose — the entries will tell you who 'the rest' was. But read them all before you decide what they mean. A page's foot is a conclusion. The columns are the evidence." She makes a note, and does not write a total. The counsel, given. The evidence, assigned.)*

scenes.synopsis: the shape — a generation ago; the funds, played; the house, saved first.
scenes.prose:
> *(She reads the columns the way Octavia ordered — all of them, before the meaning — and the shape comes up out of the page the way a stone comes up out of a field. A generation ago, the war years: the funds, the speculation, Elias playing them with money that wasn't all his. Émigré money, entrusted — the French families, the ports, the war's leavings, given into a respectable English hand for safekeeping. He played it. The funds collapsed.)*
> *(And then the line explains itself: the Hartwell interest is made whole. He covered the house first — the estate, the name, the interest — and the rest, the entrusted rest, was left to look to better times. Better times did not come. The entries are fair, the hand is steady, and the sin is the quiet kind: no knives, no enemies, no malice — ledgers, and daylight, and a steady hand. The shape, formed. The surprise, that it is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the names — ledgered; Laurent's family among the ruined.
scenes.prose:
> *(The entries name them, fair and steady, in Elias's hand. De Varenne — the name stops her cold, the ink going strange under her eyes. Laurent's family. The de Varennes, ruined in the collapse, the money gone with the funds. She reads on, because the page does not stop: de Valcourt — the banking branch, Augusta's own distant French kin, the branch fallen in the war years. De la Roche — nine hundred pounds, entered fair. De Brissac — fourteen hundred, entered fair.)*
> *(She sits back, and the study is very quiet, and the names sit on the page like guests at a table. De Varenne. Her guest is upstairs — Laurent, unknowing, at her house, eating her dinners, dancing in her hall — and his family is in her grandfather's ledger as one of the ruined. The page does not apologize. Elias's hand never apologizes. The names, named. The table, set.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE KNOWLEDGE: told, kept, or given to Augusta first.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the study, and the names are named, and the question of the knowing runs alongside the question of the day. Tell Laurent now: find him this Sunday, and tell him the branch fell — the shape of it, his ruin sitting in her grandfather's hand — let him hear it from her before he hears it from anyone — the candor of it, and the cost of it, and the guest's face when he learns what the page holds. Tell no one yet: read the rest first, choose the hour, keep the papers silent — the household's Sabbath unbroken, the knowledge hers alone till she decides what it is. Or tell Augusta first: Grandmama before the guest, the blood before the stranger — the dowager's counsel on what the family owes, before the family owes it aloud.)*
> *(Octavia's voice: read them all before you decide what they mean. Laurent's, unknowing: whatever the past held. Augusta's: the ton respects what it is told to respect. Rose looks at the page, at the Sunday quiet beyond the study door, at the names sitting like guests. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(The knowledge goes where she sends it — to the guest, or nowhere, or to Grandmama first. If Laurent: she finds him after supper, when the table has cleared, and tells him the fall — the branch, the ruin, the shape of it, no more — and the Sunday's calm is spent. If no one: the page goes back under her seal, the study door shut, the Sabbath kept, the knowing carried alone. If Augusta: late, the blue drawing room, the chocolate gone cold — and the dowager hears the branch named, and her counsel asked, and nothing of the going of it — the fall confessed as the ledger's own, the hand behind it not. Whatever Sunday became, one law holds it entire: the knowing is hers, and she chose its hour. The choosing is done.)*

options.detail: *Cunning+; the knowledge, kept.* Read the rest first; choose the hour; the papers, silent. *(Kept — and the Sunday, still calm.)*

options.detail: *Mercy+; the dowager, warned.* Grandmama before the guest; the family's counsel, before the stranger's claim. *(Warned — and the blood, put first.)*

scenes.synopsis: his family's story — told in his own time; the fall, as he lived it.
scenes.prose:
> *(She finds him at the schoolmaster's keeping at noon — the cottage, the clerk's room, or the Crown's reckoning, as Friday ordered — the schoolmaster's day of rest, the door open, the copybooks stacked. He hears what she has to ask before she asks it, the way he does. "Miss Hartwell," he says. "You've read the last line." It is not a question. She tells him the shape as she has it — the funds, the entrusted money, the covering — and he listens the way a man listens to his own story told back to him.)*
> *("My family was among the rest," he says, when she is done. "Not the great names — the Harrows were clerks and schoolmasters, the small entrusting. My father put what he had into Elias's hands, and the funds took it, and the better times never came." He looks at his clerk's hands. "I was a boy. I remember the fall as weather — the house smaller, the table thinner, my mother counting. I don't blame the ledger, Miss Hartwell. I keep it." He meets her eyes, level, paternal. "Someone should keep the papers honestly. It may as well be the boy who watched." The story, told. The witness, named.)*

scenes.synopsis: the midday face — the reading's dress; the atelier's answer to the page.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at half past twelve with the midday's question, the atelier having watched the morning. "The reading's dress, miss — the grey has done its office, and the afternoon wants a face." Three on the peg: the grey silk, kept — the page's color, the reading continued; the archive ivory — the Sabbath, dressed bright; or the blue wool, plain — the estate's color, the day uniformed.)*
> *(Rose touches the ivory — bright, the grandmother's, the Sabbath's own. The grey waits, sober. The blue wool, severe. "The page," she says, "has had the morning. The afternoon is the household's." "The afternoon," Élise says, fastening, "is yours, miss — the atelier only dresses it." She chooses the midday's face. In the glass: the woman, refaced.)*

scenes.synopsis: the walled garden — Sunday; the stones; the gap, regarded.
scenes.prose:
> *(She walks the garden at one, because the study has had her all morning and the air wants her back. Sunday's garden is a held thing — the violet bed along the south wall, the old espaliers, the light doing the wall's work. The north stretch: the gap, open to the fields, the numbered courses stacked pale on the south lawn, the masons' yard quiet for the Sabbath.)*
> *(She stands where Harrow stood last night among the fallen stones — the moonlight's place, now daylight — and thinks of the figure she saw from the stair window, still, among the courses. The garden keeps its counsel the way the page keeps hers. The stones are fallen, the wall is down, and underneath both is the oldest thing at Hartwell: the shape of what was covered. The gap, regarded. The walk, walked.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Sabbath, kept — the bells, the walk, the household at church; the guests, as they please.
scenes.prose:
> *(The household walked at nine — Augusta's carriage for the dowager, the rest on foot, Henry very straight between Julian and Octavia — and the bells went with them, and came back without them. The London names took the Sabbath in bed, as the London names do. Letitia's book has the dinner at two, the evening at seven, and nothing between but the day's own business.)*
> *(Rose walks the drive a little, because the church's quiet followed her home. The Park is at rest — the masons gone, the gardeners' Sabbath, the fields beyond the gap doing nothing at all. A house party's Sunday is a strange, suspended thing: the guests are hers, the house is hers, and the day belongs to no one. The bells, rung. The rest, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the guest, unknowing — the walk after dinner's approach; the irony, held.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent finds her on the terrace at half past one, easy, the guest's whole philosophy in his shoulders. "A quiet house," he says. "I like it quiet. The Park on a Sunday — it has the look of a place that has decided what it is." He walks with her to the garden's edge, unknowing, attentive, the way he looked at the Park at four yesterday: as if it were inevitable.)*
> *(She walks beside him, and the ledger page sits in the study with his family's name in it, and he talks of the espaliers. "The de Varennes," he says, laughing, "were never gardeners. Bankers, my grandfather — or so the family says. The money went in the war years." He says it lightly, the way a man speaks of weather he never stood in. She smiles, and takes his arm, and the irony walks between them, invisible, patient. The terrace, the afternoon, the ease — held entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: the afternoon dress — the reading resumed; the atelier's second face.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at two with the afternoon's question, the atelier's eye on the dinner. "The Sabbath's dinner, miss, and the reading after — the atelier proposes the second face." Three on the bed: the grey, again — the page's color, the reading resumed; the claret silk — the blood, worn at the desk; or the atelier's newest work — the present, dressed fresh, the mistress first in it.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret — deep, the week's color, the blood's own. The grey waits, sober. The newest work, bright. "The desk," she says, "wants the woman who isn't afraid of it." "The desk," Élise says, fastening, "has met its match, miss." She chooses the afternoon's face. In the glass: the reader, returned.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, dowagered — Augusta on Sunday; the de Valcourt branch, mentioned lightly; she does not learn.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends for her at three — the blue drawing room, the chocolate, the Sabbath's own hour. "Well," she says. "The house kept its Sunday. The county approves of rest — it is the one thing the county does better than the ton." She regards her granddaughter over the cup. "You look," she says, "like a woman who has been reading. The papers' business, I collect — under your eye, as ordered.")*
> *("Under my eye," Rose says. Augusta nods. "Your grandfather's French cousins — the de Valcourt bank — went in the war years, you know. The branch fell. Respectable people, gone respectable. It happens to the best families, child — the money fails, and the name carries on without it." She says it lightly, the way she says everything that matters. Rose hears the branch's fall named as weather, and holds Elias's hand behind her teeth, and says nothing of the covering. The chocolate, drunk. The branch, weathered. The dowager, unknowing — kept so.)*

scenes.synopsis: the reading, deepened — more pages; Elias's hand through the afternoon.
scenes.prose:
> *(She gives the afternoon to the pages, because Octavia's counsel was to read them all. The box yields its sheets one by one — the ventures, the sums, the crossings, the tall E — and the hand is the same throughout: steady, unhurried, a man writing down what he did the way a man writes down the weather. No hesitation in the ink. No second thoughts in the margins.)*
> *(That is the worst of it, worse than the sums: the steadiness. He did not agonize. He covered the house, he left the rest to better times, and he wrote it down fair, as if fairness in the recording could stand in for fairness in the doing. She reads till the light goes, and the pages accumulate, and the shape gets its edges. The hand, steady. The afternoon, spent. The evidence, entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: where the bodies are — Harrow names what Elias did; the covering, witnessed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Harrow comes at five, because the schoolmaster's day of rest ends at the study door. She lays her pages beside his half on the desk — the keeping, joined for the hour — and he reads her columns with the pencil, clerk-steady. "There," he says at last, tapping a line. "The Hartwell accounts, settled first. And there — the de Varenne entries, left. The de Valcourt, left. Your grandfather paid the house out of the entrusted money, Miss Hartwell, and wrote the rest down as waiting.")*
> *("Waiting," Rose says. "Waiting," Harrow says. "The better times were the story he told the page. The page believed him — pages do." He looks at her, level, the scarred face quiet. "I kept my half because someone should know where the bodies are. Not buried — filed. That is the family's way, I think. Nothing hidden. Everything written down, and nothing done." The pencil, laid by. The bodies, filed.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE PAPERS: locked, read, or shown to Harrow entire.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the study at six, and the pages are spread, and the question of the papers runs alongside the question of the evening. Lock them away: the box shut, her seal on it, the reading done till she chooses otherwise — the house guarded, the papers silent, Sunday's calm kept entire. Keep reading: the rest of the pages, the whole of the evening, whatever they hold — the shape finished, the knowing complete, the lamp burning late. Or show Harrow everything: her pages to his keeping, the two halves joined — the witness trusted, the man honored, the papers whole for the first time in a generation.)*
> *(Harrow's voice: someone should keep the papers honestly. Octavia's: read them all before you decide what they mean. Letitia's: the book will want the line. Rose looks at the spread pages, at the seal, at the dusk beyond the study windows. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(The papers go where she sends them — into the box, or through the evening, or into Harrow's hands. If locked: the seal pressed, Letitia witnessing, the box to the shelf, the study dark. If reading: the lamp trimmed, the chair drawn close, the evening given to the pages, whatever they hold. If Harrow: she carries her pages to his keeping herself, and lays them beside his half, and the keeping is joined — his clerk's hands, her seal, the whole at last. Whatever the evening became, one law holds it entire: the papers are hers, and she chose their keeping. The choosing is done.)*

options.detail: *Mercy+; the witness, trusted.* Her pages to his keeping; the halves, joined. *(Trusted — and the man, honored.)*

scenes.synopsis: the keeping, ordered — Letitia executes the papers' fate; the book's line.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia comes at the study door with the evening's order half executed — Sunday's philosophy, even at six. If the papers are locked: she witnesses the seal, the quartermaster's eyes on the wax, and carries the box to the shelf herself. "The book," she says, "calls it 'the papers, sealed.' The book approves of seals." If the reading continues: she trims the lamp, brings the tea, and posts herself at the corridor's end. "The book," she says, "calls it 'the mistress, reading.' The book approves of lamps.")*
> *(If Harrow has them: Letitia walks the pages to his keeping herself, the quartermaster's hands on the family's oldest secret, and comes back quiet. "The book," she says, "has no line for that. The book," Rose says, "will think of one." "The book," Letitia says, "is thinking." The pencil goes behind the ear. The keeping, ordered. The book, entered — or thinking.)*

scenes.synopsis: Henry's Sunday — the letters, reported; the schoolmaster's greeting, delivered.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry finds her at half past six on the stair's second step, the copybook in evidence — a concession to Sunday, which allows study. "Did you tell him?" he asks. It is the week's question, asked a fourth time, and this time it is a reckoning. "I told him," Rose says. "Mr. Harrow says the letters are coming along, and a schoolmaster rests on Sunday, and you'll show him the copybook Monday.")*
> *(Henry considers this with the gravity of a judge. "Tell him I rested too," he says. "Mostly." Rose laughs — the day's first real laugh, startled out of her. "I'll tell him mostly," she says. He goes up the stair, the copybook's weight carried light, and Sunday ends for the eight-year-old on the second step. The stair, quieted. The boy, delivered — mostly rested.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, brothered — Julian on Sunday's quiet; the rent-book's Sabbath.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian finds her in the hall at seven, the rent-book put by for the whole Sabbath — actually put by, not carried — and talks plainly. "A quiet house," he says. "The county's gone home, the London names are dressing for supper, and nobody's asked me for anything since dinner. It's unnerving." He glances at her. "Counsel, and it costs nothing: whatever the papers said today, Sunday's done its office. The house is rested. Let the evening be the evening.")*
> *("The rent-book kept the Sabbath too," Rose says. "The rent-book," Julian says, "is holier than I am. It never once asked about the ledger." He squeezes her arm, brotherly, and goes to dress. The counsel, given. The brother, plain.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening refresh — the day's dust; the atelier's answer to the supper's approach.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at half past six with the evening's question, the atelier having watched the day. "Reading dust, miss, and the claret's afternoon on the skirt, and supper at seven. The atelier proposes the refresh." Three on the bench: the claret, evening — the blood, dressed for the night; the ivory, layered — the Sabbath, kept bright; or the blue, quiet — the estate, worn to supper.)*
> *(Rose touches the ivory — layered, the Sabbath's own, bright to the end. The claret waits, deep. The blue, severe. "The day," she says, "has been the page's. The evening is the house's." "The evening," Élise says, pinning, "is yours, miss — the atelier only faces it." She chooses the evening's refresh. In the glass: the mistress, refaced.)*

scenes.synopsis: the columns, summed — Octavia's pencil; the entries, fair; no total.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes at the study door with the memorandum book and the pencil doing the thinking. "The columns," she says. "Show me." They go through them together — the ventures, the sums, the entries fair: de la Roche's nine hundred, de Brissac's fourteen hundred, the de Varenne entries, the de Valcourt, the Hartwell interest made whole first and the rest left waiting. Octavia's pencil moves down the page, checking, and stops — deliberately — short of a sum.)*
> *("No total?" Rose asks. "No total," Octavia says. "Not yet. The total is a conclusion, and conclusions want all the pages." She closes the memorandum book. "What the columns say, Rose, is the order: first, and the rest. Everything else is arithmetic. The shape is the thing — and the shape," she says, looking at the page, "is that your grandfather paid his own house with other people's money and called the remainder patience." The pencil, down. The shape, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the irony, continued — the guest's ease before supper; she holds the knowing.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent is in the hall before supper, the guest at his ease, watching the house gather. "Your Sunday," he says, "is a well-kept thing. The de Varennes never managed Sundays — we were always counting something." He laughs, and the laugh is the unknowing made audible, and Rose hears the ledger's entries in it the way she hears the page's foot.)*
> *(She stands beside him, and the hall fills around them — Augusta's chair, Julian's stair, Octavia's book, Henry's pudding hopes — and he is kind, and certain, and entirely the guest, and his family's ruin is in her study in her grandfather's hand. "The house," she says, "keeps its Sundays." "The house," Laurent says, "keeps everything." The irony sits between them, invisible, patient, keeping time. The hall, the evening, the ease — held entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, quartermastered — Letitia on the household; the weight, noticed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia waylays her at the stair with the supper's last order and the quartermaster's eye. "Seven o'clock," she says. "Supper — the Sabbath's table, the household and the guests, Mrs. Pike's whole religion on it. The book has the seating." She looks at Rose, and the look is the aunt's, not the book's. "And you," she says. "You've been at the page all day. The book doesn't ask what the page said. I ask how the reader is.")*
> *("The reader," Rose says, "is — reading." "The reader," Letitia says, "is carrying something, and the carrying shows in the shoulders. Eat, miss. The page will keep." She blots the page — there is nothing to blot, but the gesture is the whole of Letitia. "Whatever Sunday said, Monday will want you fed." The pencil goes behind the ear. The counsel, given. The shoulders, noticed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the surprise, landed — respectability, not malice; the family's own quiet sin; she is its heir.
scenes.prose:
> *(She stands a moment alone before supper — the mistress's minute, the house gathering without her — and lets the day's reading settle into its final shape. It is not what S1 was. S1 was malice engineered from outside, for money: an enemy's engine, knives in the dark. This is quieter, and worse. No enemy. No knives. A respectable man, a steady hand, a ledger — and the ruin done with columns instead of blades.)*
> *(And that is the shock of it, the one she has been reading toward all week: the sin is the family's own. Elias did not steal in the night — he balanced in the daylight, and the daylight was the crime. Respectable ruin. And she — the heir of the interest made whole, the reader of the hand — stands in the house the covering built, wearing the archive's silk, about to sit down to supper with the victim's kin. Her hand finds the page's edge in her mind, and the ink is brown, and the E is tall. The shape, landed. The heir, named.)*

scenes.synopsis: the kitchen's Sunday — the Sabbath's table; Mrs. Pike's whole religion.
scenes.prose:
> *(Mrs. Pike waylays her at the kitchen stair with the supper's report, the cook's whole philosophy in her apron. "Seven o'clock, miss — the Sabbath's joint, the pudding, the table for the household and the guests. The kitchen," she says, "has done its Sunday." The smells come up the stair, kind and certain, and Rose stands in them a moment.)*
> *("The house thanks the kitchen," Rose says. "The kitchen," Mrs. Pike says, "thanks the house for eating." She shoos her up the stair, the way she has shooed three generations. The table, set. The Sunday, fed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the study at dusk — the papers, kept as she chose; the sin, faced.
scenes.prose:
> *(She stops at the study before supper, because the day's last office is the papers. If they are locked: the box on the shelf under her seal, the wax holding, the study dark and quiet. If the reading continues: the pages stacked fair, the lamp trimmed for the night, the chair waiting. If Harrow has them: the desk empty, the shelf bare, the halves joined where he keeps them.)*
> *(Whatever the keeping, the sin has its shape now, and the shape is hers to carry: the funds, the entrusted money, the covering, the names. She stands in the dusk a moment, and the study holds her the way it held Elias — the desk, the lamp, the hand. Then she turns toward the stairs, and supper, and the guest. The dusk, faced. The day, carried.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening dress — supper's approach; the atelier's last word on Sunday.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at a quarter to seven with the supper's question, the atelier's last word on the day. "Supper, miss, and the household gathering — the evening wants its face." Three on the bed: the claret silk — the evening, faced in color; the grey silk, grave — the day, worn to the table; or the blue, state — the mistress, Sunday-finished.)*
> *(Rose touches the grey — grave, the day's own, the page's color. The claret waits, deep. The blue, severe. "The day," she says, "was the page's. Let the table see it." "The table," Élise says, fastening, "will see you, miss — the atelier's whole doctrine." She chooses the evening's dress. In the glass: Sunday, faced.)*

scenes.synopsis: Sunday's reading ritual — the household dresses Sunday for the Sabbath's keeping.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the lamps — "light as you mean to go on, miss. The house takes its tone from you.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the chairs — "the seats are numbered, Rose. Tonight the reading sits.")*
> *(Story morsel: Augusta, at the door — "keep it, child. The house, too.")*
> *(Story morsel: Élise, at the hem — "the extra stitch held, miss. All day, for Sunday.")*
> *(Story morsel: Julian, at the stair — "the chairs are set, Rose. The house is ready when you are.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: Sunday — the quiet after Saturday's party; the house at rest, the reading resumed, the sin taking its shape. Before supper, the household gathers in the library and dresses Sunday for the reading — what it means to keep the Sabbath's calm while the papers work underneath. The lamps lit, the books closed, the voices low. Dress for the reading: Sunday's colors, worn with intent, eyes open. Precise. Together. Attentive. The house that reads together does not stumble apart.

scenes.synopsis: after the ritual — the house at rest; the lamps; the dispersing.
scenes.prose:
> *(The ritual ends the way rituals end: the household dispersing, the library's lamps low, the dressed Sunday settling over the house like a shawl. Augusta to her chair, Julian to the stair, Octavia with the memorandum book, Letitia's book closed for the hour, Laurent to the terrace's edge, Henry to the pudding's promise. The house is at rest — dressed, faced, kept.)*
> *(Rose stands in the library's middle a moment, the direction chosen, the pins placed, the evening taken. The papers are where she put them — sealed, or stacked, or at his keeping — and the Sabbath holds. The lamps, low. The house, rested.)*

scenes.synopsis: the last reading before supper — the shape, entire; what Sunday knows.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia finds her at the library door with the memorandum book shut and the pencil behind her ear — the day's work, done. "Sunday knows the shape," she says. "The funds, the entrusting, the covering, the names. What Sunday doesn't know —" she looks at Rose, "— is what Monday does with it. The papers are kept as you chose. The knowledge goes at the hour you chose. The rest is the week's business.")*
> *("And Laurent?" Rose asks. "Laurent," Octavia says, "is a guest at supper, and supper is at seven, and the Sabbath is kept. The branch, if you must — the bare fact — may go to him Sunday. The shape, the full of it, waits for a weekday." She squeezes Rose's hand once, precise as everything she does. "Eat, Rose. The shape will keep." The book, shut. The shape, entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — SUNDAY'S FACE: kept, worked, or doubled.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone for a moment before supper, and the week is coming, and the question of Sunday's face runs alongside the question of the table. Keep the Sabbath calm: the household's Sunday unbroken, the papers silent, supper the Sabbath's own — the mercy of rest, the house undisturbed, the knowing carried quiet. Continue the work: the pages read to the end, the shape entire, the lamp burning late — the resolve of it, the knowing complete, Sunday spent at the desk. Or rest openly while the papers work in private: the household sees the Sabbath, the study sees the lamp — both true, neither whole, the day doubled.)*
> *(Letitia's voice: the book has one line for Sunday. Octavia's: the shape will keep. Augusta's: the house has earned an evening. Rose looks at the table beyond the door, at the study behind her, at the Sunday nearly done. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(Sunday's face goes to the household in a low voice, and the evening rearranges itself around it. If kept: the study dark, the papers silent, the Sabbath entire — supper the day's whole business. If worked: the lamp trimmed, the pages waiting, the evening given to the reading — supper brief, the desk the night's. If doubled: the Sabbath's face at the table, the lamp's face after — the household rested, the papers advancing, neither the wiser. Whatever the evening became, one law holds it entire: the day is hers, and she chose its face. The choosing is done.)*

options.label: Continue the work
options.detail: *Resolve+; the reading, finished.* The pages read to the end; the shape, entire; the lamp, late. *(Finished — and the knowing, complete.)*

options.label: Rest openly, work in private
options.detail: *Cunning+; the face, kept; the work, hidden.* The household sees the Sabbath; the study sees the lamp; both, true. *(Hidden — and the day, doubled.)*

scenes.synopsis: before supper — the irony, held entire; the guest, easy.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent is waiting at the stair when she comes down — the guest, easy, the evening's whole philosophy in his shoulders. "A fine Sunday," he says. "Your house keeps them well. The de Varennes," he laughs, "kept nothing so well — except, my grandfather always said, our name." He offers his arm, unknowing, fond, and she takes it, because the Sabbath's face is the face she chose.)*
> *(They walk to the dining room together, and his family's ruin walks with them, invisible, patient, keeping time — the ledger's entries, the war years, the better times that never came. He knows nothing. He holds her arm like a man holding something certain. "The name," she says, "is well kept." "The name," Laurent says, "is everything." The stair, the evening, the ease — held entire, and undivided.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Bell's Sunday paragraph; the Sabbath, printed; no scandal yet.
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting is the Gazette's Sunday paragraph, come up with the evening post — Bell's paper, noting the Sabbath's keeping, the proprietor's eye on the Season.)*
> *(Rose reads it before supper, the way she reads everything Bell writes, and finds no edge in it — no leader, no verdict, no favorite story. Just the facts, set in Bell's type: the church, the gates, the seven. Nothing of the ledger. Nothing of Elias. Nothing of the last line. She folds the Gazette and gives it to Octavia for the memorandum book. The paper smells of ink. The hall smells of supper.)*
scenes.sting: the sting — Bell's Sunday paragraph; the Sabbath, printed; no scandal yet.

scenes.synopsis: the supper's voice — the table's approach; the atelier's finishing.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at a quarter to seven with the supper's last question, the atelier's eye on the dining room's light. "The dress is Sunday's face, miss. The voice is the table's." Three on the tray: the grandmother's fan, ivory — the hand, occupied; the violets, dried — faithfulness, kept past their season, worn; or the silver rose pin, plain — the house's mark, worn quiet.)*
> *(Rose touches the violets — dried, Élise's keeping, faithfulness brown-edged and flat. The fan waits, ivory. The pin, plain silver. "The table," she says, "wants something honest." "The table," Élise says, pinning, "wants you." She chooses the supper's voice. In the glass: the hostess, voiced.)*

scenes.synopsis: the supper's order — the table set; the Sabbath kept; the house, gathered.
scenes.prose:
> *(Supper is the dining room at seven — the household and the guests, the Sabbath's table: Augusta at the table's head in state, Julian with the rent-book put by, Octavia, Laurent at Rose's right, Henry permitted the table for the pudding, Letitia's book closed for the hour, the atelier and the kitchen in their Sunday best. Mrs. Pike's kitchen sends up the Sabbath's joint, and the talk is of the Sunday — the church, the rest, the quiet — and the papers keep the Sabbath too, silent in the library.)*
> *(Rose sits at the table's head in Sunday's face — the dress as the day ordered, the violets — or the fan, or the pin — doing their office. The house gathers. The Sabbath, kept. The table, entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, dowagered — Augusta's Sunday word at the table's head.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta holds her a moment before the sitting — the dowager's minute, the blue drawing room's echo in the dining room's doorway. "A well-kept Sunday, child," she says. "The house rested, the table set, the guests easy. Whatever the week brings —" the eyebrow lifts, just, "— it finds a house that kept its Sabbath." She regards her granddaughter, and the regard is the whole of the counsel: steady, unsurprised, entirely Augusta.)*
> *("Grandmama," Rose says — and stops, because the de Valcourt branch is on her tongue, and the covering with it, and the dowager must not hear it. Not tonight. Not from this table. "The house," she says instead, "thanks its dowager." Augusta's mouth does something it rarely does. "The dowager," she says, "is thanked." She takes her chair, which is the dismissal and the blessing both. The word, given. The branch, unspoken.)*

scenes.synopsis: supper served — the talk; the old families; Laurent, laughing.
scenes.prose:
> *(Supper is served at seven — the Sabbath's joint, the pudding, the talk turning the way supper talk turns: to the county, to the old families, to the names on the cottages. The London guests ask after the Park's history; the household answers with the restoration. Laurent is at his ease, the guest among guests, laughing at the squire's wife's story about the rectory's roof.)*
> *(Rose eats, and listens, and repeats nothing — the hostess's office, Sunday-kept. The talk is kind, and the table is full, and the irony sits at her right hand in a guest's chair, invisible, patient, keeping time. The supper, served. The talk, turning.)*

scenes.synopsis: the honor, named — at supper Laurent, laughing, speaks of family honor; Rose cannot meet his eyes.
scenes.prose: > *(The talk turns to the old families — the county's favorite subject — and Laurent laughs, the guest's laugh, easy. "The de Varennes were bankers, you know — respectable ruin, when the war took the money. But the honor survived. Your grandfather saw to that, Rose — old Elias kept the family's honor when the money failed." He raises his glass to her, fond, certain, unknowing. And Rose — the heir of the covering, the reader of the page — cannot meet his eyes. The glass, raised. The honor, named. The eyes, lowered.)*

scenes.synopsis: Monday's dawn — the morning after supper; Laurent's line, still in her ears; the choices, carried.
scenes.prose:
> *(Monday wakes her the way the week has trained it to — early, bluer than Sunday, before the maid — and the first thing in her head is not the ledger but Laurent's voice at supper, easy, certain: "old Elias kept the family's honor when the money failed." The glass, raised to her. Her eyes, lowered to the table. She lies a moment in the blue dark and lets the line sit where it sat all night, beside her like a guest who won't leave.)*
> *(Sunday's choices come with her into the week. The knowledge went where she sent it — to the guest, the fall and nothing of the going, or nowhere, or to Grandmama first, the branch named and her counsel asked — and the papers are kept as she chose: sealed, or stacked for the reading, or joined at the cottage. If the Sabbath was kept, the study stood dark all evening; if the work went on, the lamp burned late; if both, neither the wiser. Monday inherits it all. She dresses in the blue dark, and the house begins.)*

scenes.synopsis: Monday's morning face — the archive's weekday answer; the atelier's first word.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes with Monday's question, the atelier's eye on the week. "Monday, miss, and the week to face — the archive proposes the weekday face." Three on the stand: the grey silk, sober — the reader's dress, the page's color, Monday uniformed; the claret, steady — the week's color, worn to work; or the Hartwell blue — the mistress's Monday, the house's color, dressed for the drive.)*
> *(Rose touches the grey — the week's workhorse, the reading's dress. The claret waits, deep. The blue, severe. "Monday," she says, "wants the woman who can carry it." "Monday," Élise says, buttoning, "wants you dressed, miss, which is the atelier's whole doctrine." She chooses the morning's face. In the glass: the mistress, Monday-faced. The mended gloves, taken up again.)*

scenes.synopsis: breakfast — the aunt's comedy, kept; the first unfinished sentence.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia is at breakfast ahead of her, the household book open, the pencil doing the morning's arithmetic. "Monday," she says, "and the week in full cry. The masons at seven, the plasterers at eight, the London names departing after luncheon — the book has them all, and the book," she adds, "has forgiven Sunday." It is the usual comedy, dealt at the usual pace, and Rose smiles at the usual places. But the smile comes a beat late on Letitia's side, and the pencil taps twice where it never taps, and the whole performance has the kept quality of a dress folded for a journey.)*
> *(Then, over the toast: "Rose — when your grandfather—" She stops. The pencil stops. A full breath passes, the toast cooling between them, and Letitia says, too brightly, "—would have wanted his eggs, I was going to say. The kitchen does them too soft." She butters the toast with great attention. Rose watches the butter, and the hands, and says nothing about grandfathers. The sentence, unfinished. The eggs, too soft.)*

scenes.synopsis: Monday's order — the week resumed; the household feels the tension without naming it.
scenes.prose:
> *(The book's order for Monday is read at nine, Letitia brisk, the quartermaster's whole philosophy in the pencil: the masons at seven, the plasterers at eight, the schoolroom at ten, the London names' carriages after luncheon, dinner at half past six, the evening as the evening decides. The household takes its orders. Amos is slower on the stair than usual. The maids are quieter. Nobody names anything; everybody has noticed something. The tension sits in the house like a guest nobody introduced.)*
> *(Rose walks the corridor after, and the Park is at the week's work — the carts, the courses, the mortar's smell — and the house behind her holds its quiet the way a hand holds a cup too full to set down. Monday, ordered. The week, resumed. The quiet, carried by all of them, unnamed.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE APPROACH: ask her directly, watch and wait, or ask Octavia what she sees.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the morning room after the order is read, and the aunt's quiet has its shape now — the kept comedy, the unfinished sentence, the hands — and the question of the approach runs alongside the question of the day. Ask her directly: find Letitia before noon, put the question plain — what is she carrying, what did she know — the candor of it, and the risk that the asking shuts what the watching might open. Watch and wait: say nothing, keep the routine, let the day's signs accumulate — the discipline of it, the patience, the aunt coming in her own time or not at all. Or ask Octavia what she sees: the friend's eye is the county's sharpest, and two watchers see more than one — the indirection of it, and the counsel, precise.)*
> *(Letitia's voice from breakfast: your grandfather would have wanted his eggs. Octavia's: read them all before you decide what they mean. Rose looks at the morning room's window, at the masons' yard beyond, at the Monday getting on without her. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(The approach goes where she sends it — to the aunt's door, or into the day's patience, or to Octavia's memorandum book. If direct: she finds Letitia in the morning room before the schoolroom hour, and puts the question plain, and the comedy meets it like a wall, kindly built. If waiting: she says nothing all morning, and watches, and the signs come — the avoided corridor, the early laugh, the jam counted. If Octavia: the note goes by Amos before ten, and Octavia's word comes back at eleven — she'll watch her today, and tell Rose at noon what she sees — the friend's eye, lent for the day. Whatever Monday became, one law holds it entire: the approach is hers, and she chose its manner. The choosing is done.)*

scenes.synopsis: the approach, executed — the aunt met three ways; the wall, kindly built.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she asked directly: she finds Letitia in the morning room at half past ten, and puts it plain — "Aunt, what are you carrying?" — and the comedy comes up like a shutter: the book, the plasterers, the pudding, Henry's bun, all of it dealt at double pace, and underneath the pace the stillness. "Carrying?" Letitia says, bright as a new coin. "The household, my dear. Somebody must." If she watches: she says nothing, and the morning gives her the signs — Letitia takes the long way round to avoid the study corridor, laughs at Julian's joke before the joke is done, counts the jam with Mrs. Pike though she never counts the jam.)*
> *(If she asked Octavia: the note goes by Amos, and Octavia's word comes back at eleven — "I'll watch her today. Noon, the morning room, and I'll tell you what I see." So Rose watches too, because two watchers were the point, and the morning's signs are hers as well: the long way round, the early laugh, the jam. Whatever the manner, the aunt is met — and the wall, kindly built, holds. The approach, executed. The quiet, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the week's work — the walled garden; the gap; the masons' Monday.
scenes.prose:
> *(She walks the garden at eleven, because the morning room has had her long enough and the air wants her back. Monday's garden is a working thing — the masons at the north stretch, the numbered courses rising pale against the old wall, the mortar's smell, the foreman's chalk. The gap is narrower than Friday. Course by course, the wall comes back, and the oldest thing at Hartwell gets covered again in new stone.)*
> *(She stands where the moonlight stood in the figure's place — Harrow's place, the night he watched — and thinks of stones, and of coverings, and of grandfathers who wrote things down fair. The wall rises. The garden keeps its counsel. The foreman touches his cap, and she nods, and the week gets on. The gap, narrowing. The walk, walked.)*

scenes.synopsis: the study at noon — the papers, kept as she chose; the sin's shape, and the aunt's beside it.
scenes.prose:
> *(She stops at the study at noon, because the day's middle wants the papers' accounting. If they are locked: the box on the shelf under her seal, the wax holding, the study cool and dark. If the reading continues: the pages stacked fair where the evening left them, the lamp trimmed, the columns waiting — de la Roche's nine hundred, de Brissac's fourteen hundred, entered fair. If Harrow has them: the desk bare, the shelf empty, the keeping joined at the cottage — his clerk's hands, her seal, the whole at last.)*
> *(Whatever the keeping, the two shapes stand side by side in the noon quiet: the grandfather's covering, written down fair in brown ink — and the aunt's quiet, walking the corridors with the household book. One she has read. The other she is reading now, in hands and laughs and sentences that stop. She shuts the study door and goes back to the day. The noon, faced. The shapes, paired.)*

scenes.synopsis: the midday face — the watching's dress; the atelier's answer to noon.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at half past twelve with the midday's question, the atelier having watched the morning. "The morning's dress has done its office, miss — the afternoon wants a face for the watching." Three on the peg: the grey silk, kept — the page's color, the reading continued; the archive ivory — bright, the grandmother's, the week dressed light; or the blue wool, plain — the estate's color, the mistress uniformed for the afternoon.)*
> *(Rose touches the ivory — bright, the week's own. The grey waits, sober. The blue wool, severe. "The afternoon," she says, "is the household's." "The afternoon," Élise says, fastening, "is yours, miss — the atelier only dresses it." She chooses the midday's face. In the glass: the watcher, refaced.)*

scenes.synopsis: the kept comedy — Letitia at full tilt; the phrase, surfaced; the second unfinished sentence.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia finds her at one with the household's midday business, and the comedy is at full tilt — the plasterers' estimate ("highwaymen with trowels"), the linen inventory, Henry's bun (earned, she insists, by the copybook) — dealt at the double pace, over-bright, and every laugh landing a beat early, the way a nervous rider takes a fence too soon. Rose laughs in the right places. The wrongness sits between them like a third person at the table.)*
> *(Then, of the mason's bill: "—and they'll want it by Friday, and better times, they'll say, when they see the state of—" She stops. The pencil stops. "Better times." The phrase hangs between them — her grandfather's phrase, Elias's brown ink: the rest must look to better times. Letitia's mouth does something complicated. "Rose, there was a time when—" The pencil snaps — actually snaps in her fingers — and she looks at the two halves, surprised, and says, brightly, "—when I kept spare pencils. I'll fetch one." She goes, brisk, gone. The pencil's halves stay on the table where she left them.)*

scenes.synopsis: Octavia's reading — the friend's eye, lent or given; what the day shows.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia finds her in the morning room at noon — or Rose finds Octavia; the memorandum book is out either way, the pencil doing the thinking. If Rose asked: "Well," Octavia says, "I watched her. She takes the long way round the study corridor. She laughed before Julian's joke was done. She counted Mrs. Pike's jam, and Letitia never counts the jam." The pencil taps. "She knows the shape of something, Rose. She has the walk of a woman carrying a kept thing.")*
> *(If Rose didn't ask: Octavia closes the memorandum book and says it anyway — "Your aunt is carrying something. I don't know what. I know the walk." — because that is what friends are for. Either way the counsel is the same, precise as everything she does: "Don't corner her, Rose. A kept thing, cornered, goes deeper. Let the day do the asking." She squeezes Rose's hand once. The reading, given. The walking, named.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, dowagered — Augusta on the aunt; the branch, conditional.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends for her at two — the blue drawing room, the chocolate, Monday's own hour. "Your aunt," she says without preamble, "is performing the household instead of keeping it. I have watched Letitia perform before — she performed at my wedding, she performed at her come-out — and this is not performance, child. This is a woman holding a door shut with her back." She regards her granddaughter over the cup. "Doors," she says, "open in their own time, or not at all.")*
> *(If Augusta was told Sunday: "The branch," she says, quieter, "has been on my mind since yesterday. The de Valcourts, gone respectable — and the ledger naming what the county only guessed. If Letitia knows something of it, she learned it young, when the house still talked." If not: the de Valcourt branch stays unspoken between them, weather still, and Augusta says only, "Whatever the door is, it is hers to open. You may stand near it, child. You may not push." The chocolate, drunk. The counsel, dowagered. The door, shut — for now.)*

scenes.synopsis: the kitchen's Monday — Mrs. Pike's report; the jam, counted.
scenes.prose:
> *(Mrs. Pike waylays her at the kitchen stair at half past two with the week's report, the cook's whole philosophy in her apron. "The household's fed, miss, and the London names' baskets packed for the road. And Miss Letitia," she says, lowering her voice the way the kitchen lowers it for family business, "was in my kitchen at six this morning counting the jam. She never counts the jam, miss. Thirty years, and never once." The smells come up the stair, kind and certain.)*
> *("The house thanks the kitchen," Rose says, "and the kitchen will not mention the jam." "The kitchen," Mrs. Pike says, "mentions nothing. The kitchen notices." She shoos her up the stair, the way she has shooed three generations. The jam, counted. The noticing, general.)*

scenes.synopsis: the guest — Laurent at Monday's middle; told or untold, the ease altered.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she told him Sunday: Laurent is in the hall at three, courteous, the guest's manners intact and the guest's ease gone. He asked after the morning room this morning and did not go in. "Miss Hartwell," he says, and the name is formal where it was fond. "The Park is —" he looks for the word, "— very kind." He walks the terrace alone after, and the fall walks with him, patient. The telling, told. The cost, carried.)*
> *(If she did not: he finds her at the garden's edge at three, easy, unknowing, the whole philosophy in his shoulders. "The de Varennes," he laughs, "were never farmers — bankers, my grandfather, or so the family says. The money went in the war years." He says it lightly, the way a man speaks of weather he never stood in. "The name," he says, "is everything." She takes his arm, and the irony walks between them, invisible, patient, keeping time. The ease, held. The knowing, hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the corridor — Letitia and the study door; the footsteps, stopped.
scenes.prose:
> *(She comes down the corridor at half past three and hears them — Letitia's footsteps, the quartermaster's brisk ones, coming toward the study. She steps back into the stair's shadow without deciding to, and watches: Letitia reaches the study door, her hand half-raised to the handle — and stops. A breath. Two. The hand lowers. She turns and goes back the way she came, brisk, the book under her arm, and does not look at the door again.)*
> *(Rose stands in the stair's shadow till the footsteps fade, and thinks of the pencil's halves on the morning-room table, and the phrase in the air, and the hand half-raised. Whatever the aunt knows, it lives behind that door — or she believes it does. The corridor, empty. The door, unopened. The watching, done.)*

> *(Élise comes at four with the afternoon's question, the atelier's eye on the evening. "The London names are gone, miss — the house is the household's again." Three on the bed: the grey, again — the page's color, the watching continued; the claret silk — deep, the week's color, the blood's own; or the atelier's newest work — the present, dressed fresh, the mistress first in it.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret — deep, steady, the week's own. The grey waits, sober. The newest work, bright. "The leave-taking," she says, "wants the house, not the reader." "The house," Élise says, fastening, "is what you are, miss — the atelier only says so." She chooses the afternoon's face. In the glass: the mistress, deepened.)*

scenes.synopsis: Henry's Monday — the copybook; the extra bun; the schoolmaster's report.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry finds her at half past four on the stair's third step, the copybook in evidence — Monday allows no concessions. "Mr. Harrow says the letters are coming along," he reports, "and Aunt Letitia gave me an extra bun at nuncheon." He considers this with the gravity of a judge. "She never gives extra buns. I asked why and she said the copybook deserved it, which is not an answer." Rose laughs — the day's first easy laugh, startled out of her.)*
> *("The copybook," she says, "is a demanding master." "The copybook," Henry says darkly, "is why the bun." He goes up the stair, the copybook's weight carried light, and the afternoon steadies around him. The stair, quieted. The boy, bun-fed — and the aunt's love, noted.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, brothered — Julian on the aunt; the early laugh, priced.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian finds her in the hall at five, the rent-book under his arm — actually carried, the Sabbath being over — and talks plainly. "Your aunt," he says, "laughed at my joke about the plasterers before I'd finished it. She's never early to a laugh, Rose — she's the one who waits for the end and then decides whether it deserved her." He glances at her. "Counsel, and it costs nothing: whatever she's carrying, she's carrying it at speed. Don't chase. Let her set it down.")*
> *("The rent-book's counsel," Rose says. "The rent-book," Julian says, "has seen three generations of Hartwells carrying things. It knows the walk." He squeezes her arm, brotherly, and goes to the estate books. The counsel, given. The brother, plain.)*

scenes.synopsis: the leave-taking — the London names go; the house exhales; Laurent stays.
scenes.prose:
> *(The London names go in the afternoon — the carriages, the baskets, the road — and the house exhales the way a held breath exhales: all at once, and with relief. Letitia oversees the leave-taking with the quartermaster's crispness almost restored — the rugs, the hampers, the coachman's fee — and for an hour she is herself again, or the nearest thing to it, and the household watches her the way the household watches weather clearing.)*
> *(Laurent stays — "a few days more, at the house's pleasure," courteous, the guest's whole philosophy — and the drive empties, and the Park settles to its own. If he was told: he stands apart at the leave-taking, the distance kept kindly. If not: he waves the carriages off, easy, unknowing, at her side. Either way the house is the household's again. The road, taken. The week, narrowed.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE HOUSEHOLD: keep the routine steady, give her space, or keep her close and busy.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone at five, and the day's signs are all in — the unfinished sentences, the phrase, the avoided corridor, the early laugh, the jam — and the question of the household runs alongside the question of the evening. Keep the routine steady: the book's order unchanged, the aunt at her post, the household seeing no difference — the resolve of it, the discipline, the quartermaster held to her quartermastering. Give Letitia space: take the book for the afternoon yourself, send her to the garden, the village, her room — the mercy of it, the hands emptied, the carrying given air. Or keep her close and keep her busy: invent the errands, the linen, the village calls — motion disguises the mind, and a busy aunt is a held aunt — the indirection of it, and the kindness inside the cunning.)*
> *(Augusta's voice: you may stand near it, child. You may not push. Julian's: don't chase. Octavia's: let the day do the asking. Rose looks at the hall beyond the door, at the evening coming on, at the household waiting for its face. The choosing is hers.)*
> *(The household's face goes to the evening in a low voice, and the house rearranges itself around it. If steady: the book's order stands, Letitia executes it with the old crispness almost, and nobody sees a difference — which is the point. If space: Rose takes the book herself at six, and Letitia's hands are empty, and the garden gets her for an hour, or her room does. If busy: the errands multiply — the linen, the village, the stillroom — and the aunt is kept in motion, kindly, entirely. Whatever the evening became, one law holds it entire: the household is hers, and she chose its face. The choosing is done.)*

options.label: Keep her close, keep her busy
options.detail: *Cunning+; the motion, prescribed.* Errands, linen, village calls; a busy aunt, held. *(Held — and the mind, disguised.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening's face, executed — the aunt met three ways; the reaction, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(If the routine stood: Letitia executes the evening's order with the old crispness almost — dinner at half past six, the seating, the book's lines — and the almost is the whole story. If she was given space: Rose takes the book at six, and Letitia stands a moment with empty hands, surprised by the lightness, and goes to the garden as told — and comes back with her hair loosened by the wind, looking younger, looking worse. If she was kept busy: the errands do their office — the linen counted, the village called on, the stillroom inventoried — and she comes to dinner flushed with motion, the comedy shelved for the hour, quieter underneath.)*
> *(Whatever the face, the aunt takes it with the quartermaster's nod and the kept smile — and behind the smile, the something Monday has not named. At six she finds Rose in the hall and says, "The evening's order stands," or "The garden was kind," or "The linen's done" — whichever the day gave her — and the pencil goes behind the ear, and the evening is hers to run. The face, executed. The running, hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the signs, set down — the day's accumulation, listed the way Octavia lists columns.
scenes.prose:
> *(She takes the library at half past five, because the watching wants a desk and the memorandum book is Octavia's, not hers — so she makes her own list, in her head, the way she learned the ledger: two unfinished sentences, breakfast and midday. The phrase, surfaced — better times, in her aunt's mouth. The study corridor, avoided; the door, unopened. The laugh, early. The jam, counted. The pencil, snapped.)*
> *(She sets them down in order, fair and steady, the way Elias set down his ventures — and the shape comes up the way a stone comes up out of a field. Her aunt knew that shape when she was young, and has been carrying it since, and Monday is the day the carrying started to show. The list, listed. The stone, surfaced.)*

> *(Élise comes at six with the evening's question, the atelier having watched the day. "The afternoon's dust, miss, and the claret's color on the skirt, and dinner at half past. The atelier proposes the refresh." Three on the bench: the claret, evening — deep, dressed for the night; the ivory, layered — bright, the week kept light; or the blue, quiet — the estate, worn to the table.)*
> *(Rose touches the ivory — layered, bright, the week's own. The claret waits, deep. The blue, severe. "The day," she says, "has been the household's. The evening is the table's." "The table," Élise says, pinning, "wants you, miss — the atelier's whole doctrine." She chooses the evening's refresh. In the glass: the hostess, refaced.)*

scenes.synopsis: Monday's dinner — the table set; the household and the guest; the tension, unnamed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Dinner is the dining room at half past six — the household and the remaining guest, Monday's table: Augusta in state, Julian with the rent-book put by at last, Octavia, Laurent at Rose's right (or a careful chair down, if Sunday told him), Henry permitted the table for the pudding, Letitia's book closed for the hour, Mrs. Pike's joint doing its office. The talk is of the week — the masons, the garden, the village — and not of papers, and not of aunts, by unspoken agreement.)*
> *(Rose sits at the table's head in the afternoon's face — the claret, or the grey, or the newest work — and the house gathers. The tension sits at the table like a guest nobody introduced, and everybody passes it the salt. The dinner, served. The table, entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dinner talk — Letitia's comedy at the table; the kept quality, priced by all.
scenes.prose:
> *(The talk turns the way dinner talk turns: to the village, to the masons' foreman's new tooth, to Henry's copybook (exhibited, admired, returned). Letitia deals the comedy at the table's pace — the plasterers, highwaymen still; the jam, unmentioned — and twice the table laughs and she doesn't quite, the smile arriving after the laugh like a guest after the carriages. Augusta's eyebrow lifts, just. Octavia's pencil is still. Laurent is courteous, whichever Sunday made him.)*
> *(Rose eats, and listens, and repeats nothing — the hostess's office, Monday-kept. The pudding comes; Henry is vindicated. The talk is kind, and the table is full, and the aunt's quiet sits at its corner in a hostess's chair, invisible, patient, keeping time. The dinner, talked. The table, turning.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening's pause — the library after dinner; the question of tomorrow, set down.
scenes.prose:
> *(She takes the library after dinner, because the drawing room has the household and she wants the hour alone. The day's signs are all in, the list is listed, the stone is surfaced — and the question underneath is tomorrow's: the quiet confrontation, waiting one more night. She could ask tonight. The corridor is quiet. The aunt's door is shut. But Augusta's voice is in her ears — doors open in their own time — and Octavia's — let the day do the asking — and the day is not done asking yet.)*
> *(She stands at the library's window and watches the Park go dark, the garden's gap a paler dark against the wall, the masons' yard still. Monday has done its office: the aunt's quiet has a shape now, and the shape is load-bearing, and tomorrow she will put her hand to it — gently, or not. The window, darkened. The tomorrow, set.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening's voice — the drawing room's approach; the atelier's finishing.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at eight with the evening's last question, the atelier's eye on the drawing room's light. "The dress is the evening's face, miss. The voice is the drawing room's." Three on the tray: the grandmother's fan, ivory — the hand, occupied; the violets, dried — faithfulness, kept past their season, worn; or the silver rose pin, plain — the house's mark, worn quiet.)*
> *(Rose touches the violets — dried, Élise's keeping, faithfulness brown-edged and flat. The fan waits, ivory. The pin, plain silver. "The drawing room," she says, "wants something honest." "The drawing room," Élise says, pinning, "wants you." She chooses the evening's voice. In the glass: the mistress, voiced.)*
