scenes.synopsis: the counsel, brothered — Julian on the money moving; the estate's eye.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian finds her at the drawing-room door after dinner with the rent-book under his arm — carried, the evening being the evening. "London buying Hartwell paper," he says without preamble. "Quill's note. I've been thinking about it the way I think about rents — small paper bought quiet means somebody's building a holding. You don't buy debts to forgive them, Rose.")*
> *("Counsel, and it costs nothing," he says. "Don't sell them anything — not a note, not a denial, not the time of day. A man building a holding needs the other side to move. Stand still, and he overpays for air." He squeezes her arm, brotherly, and goes to the estate books. The counsel, given. The brother, plain.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, continued — Octavia's evening reading; watch the watchers.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia finds her at the stair at nine with the memorandum book open to the day's page — the inn, the lane, Slade, the sheet, the London paper, all dated, all sourced. "The day's whole account," she says. "And my evening's reading of it: the hunters are professionals, Rose. Paid questions, a field man, a sheet primed, debts bought quiet. This is a shaped operation. Somebody's, and somebody's money.")*
> *("Watch the watchers," Octavia says. "Bell's men see everything in this county. Whatever the Gazette is alert to, we want to be alert to first — or at least second." She shuts the book. Something in her face says she has a name for the somebody and is not saying it. Rose does not ask. The book, shut. The counsel, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the study at night — the papers under their new keeping; the seal, the wax.
scenes.prose:
> *(She stops at the study before the ritual, because the night's last office is the papers. If they were moved: the shelf stands honest and empty, the box in Harrow's keeping under his hand and her seal. If they were guarded: the new bolt on the study door, the wax holding on the box, Amos's rotations on the stair. If they were split: the box sealed on the shelf, the packet gone in Octavia's reticule to a keeping nobody names.)*
> *(Whatever the keeping, the thought that comes with the dark is Julian's: stand still, and he overpays for air. She looks at the ledger — de la Roche's nine hundred, de Brissac's fourteen hundred, entered fair — and thinks of London buying paper it cannot read. Let them buy, she thinks. The columns are here. She shuts the study door and goes to dress the evening. The night, faced. The columns, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night's face — the atelier's last word on Wednesday; the bedchamber's keeping.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes with the night's question, the atelier's eye on the bedchamber. "The day is done, miss — the night wants its face." Three on the rail: the ivory nightdress — the week's white, the sleep's own; the grey wrapper — the reader's, the page's color, worn to the window; or the claret shawl — deep, the week's color, kept for the cold.)*
> *(Rose touches the grey — the reader's wrapper, the page's color, the day's own. The ivory waits, white. The claret shawl, deep. "The night," she says, "wants the woman, not the watcher." "The night," Élise says, low, "wants you rested, miss." She chooses the night's face. In the glass: Wednesday, undressed.)*

scenes.synopsis: Wednesday's watch ritual — the household dresses Wednesday for watchfulness; the signs, answered with steadiness.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the book — "Wednesday's line is written, miss. The book thanks the mistress for the watch.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the window — "the lane is quiet, Rose. Tonight the signs sleep.")*
> *(Story morsel: Augusta, at the door — "unruffled, child. The moths can wait.")*
> *(Story morsel: Élise, at the hem — "the extra stitch held, miss. All day, for Wednesday.")*
> *(Story morsel: Julian, at the stair — "the bolt's on, Rose. The house is ready when you are.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: Wednesday — the day the outside world leaned in; the house dresses for watchfulness — every window a witness, every door a decision, the table unruffled underneath it all. Dress for the watch: Wednesday's colors, worn with intent, eyes open. Attentive. Unruffled. Together. The house that watches together is not taken by surprise.

scenes.synopsis: Bell's warning — the proprietor's hand; someone is buying eyes.
scenes.prose:
> *(Bell's note comes with the evening post, and it is not the Gazette — it is the proprietor's own hand, two paragraphs, no masthead. "Miss Hartwell," it reads. "Someone is buying eyes in this county. Questions paid for in the village, on the lane, and now — my man tells me — after old paper in London. I write as one proprietor to another: the Gazette is alert, and you should be.")*
> *(She reads it twice in the hall, the way she reads everything Bell writes. It is not an offer and not a threat — it is a weather report from a woman who sells weather for a living. Buying eyes. The phrase sits in her like the stone in the shoe. She folds the note and puts it with the log. The post, read. The warning, received.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — BELL'S WARNING: heed it and prepare, dismiss it, or use the Gazette's alertness.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the hall with Bell's note in her hand, and the question of the warning runs alongside the question of the night. Someone is buying eyes. The Gazette is alert. The paper will cover the old scandal when it breaks — Bell has said as much before, in her way — and the verdict is not for sale. The question is what Rose does with a warned house.)*
> *(Heed it and prepare: put the house on its guard — every question reported, every stranger logged, the lane watched, the servants told what to say and what not to — the resolve of it, the household armed, the risk of a house that jumps at shadows. Dismiss it: weigh the warning and set it down — gossip, wind, the county's old habit of looking at the Park — the house keeps its order and gives the paper nothing to print — the candor of it, the calm kept, the risk of the unready. Or use the Gazette's alertness: let Bell's men watch — feed the paper what it needs, take its warnings as they come, the hunters watched by the watchers — the cunning of it, the alliance unspoken, the risk of the debt.)*
> *(The warning goes where she sends it — into the guard, into the wind, or into the paper. If heeded: the orders go out before ten — the lane, the inn, the servants' stair — and the house sleeps with one eye open. If dismissed: the note goes in the log and the house goes to bed, and Wednesday ends unruffled. If used: a line goes back to Bell by the morning post — "the Gazette's eyes are the county's best; the Park thanks the paper for its alertness" — and nothing more is said, because nothing more needs saying. Whatever the night became, one law holds it entire: the warning was hers, and she chose its answer. The choosing is done.)*

options.label: Heed it and prepare
options.detail: *Resolve+; the warning, heeded.* The house on its guard; every question reported, every stranger logged. *(Heeded — and the shadows, jumped at.)*

options.label: Dismiss it
options.detail: *Candor+; the warning, weighed.* Gossip and wind; the house keeps its order, the paper gets nothing. *(Weighed — and the calm, kept.)*

options.label: Use the Gazette's alertness
options.detail: *Cunning+; the paper, borrowed.* Bell's men watch; the hunters, watched by the watchers. *(Borrowed — and the debt, unspoken.)*

scenes.synopsis: the answer, executed — the house takes its orders for the night.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she heeded: the orders go out before ten — Amos's rotations on the stair, the gardeners to report every stranger on the lane, the servants told what to say and what not to — and the house takes them the way it takes everything, entire. If she dismissed: nothing goes out but the routine — the book's order stands, the evening as the evening decides — and the house sleeps unruffled. If she used: the line goes to Bell by the morning post, and Octavia's log gains a column headed "the Gazette," and nobody speaks of it.)*
> *(In every night the same law: the household is hers, and it moves as she moves. She walks the corridor once, and the doors are shut, and the lamps are low, and the house holds its Wednesday the way a hand holds a kept thing — firmly, and without squeezing. The corridor, walked. The answer, given.)*

scenes.synopsis: the goodnight — the aunt's door; Wednesday's end, held.
scenes.prose:
> *(She stops at Letitia's door on her way to bed, because the day deserves its ending where so many days have ended. The door is shut — the ordinary shut, the household's shut, nothing in it of Tuesday's altered wood. "Good night, Aunt," she says through it, quietly. A breath. "Good night, my dear," comes back, steady — and underneath the steadiness, the loosening, kept.)*
> *(She stands a moment with her hand off the door's frame — not on it, tonight; the door is the aunt's — and thinks of the morning room's lamplight, and the shape, and the thirty years, and takes herself to bed. The door stays shut. The loosening, kept between them. The goodnight, given.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Bell's Wednesday paragraph; the terms, printed; the verdict, not for sale.
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting is the Gazette's Wednesday paragraph, come up with the late post — Bell's paper, the proprietor's eye on the week's weather.)*
> *(Rose reads it in the hall, the way she reads everything Bell writes, and finds the edge in it this time — the leader's edge, the proprietor's terms set in type. Someone is buying eyes, and Bell has told the county — and Rose — exactly what her paper is: alert, independent, and unbought. She folds the Gazette and gives it to Octavia for the memorandum book. The paper smells of ink. The hall smells of night.)*
scenes.sting: the sting — Bell's Wednesday paragraph; the terms, printed; the verdict, not for sale.

scenes.synopsis: the bedchamber — Wednesday accumulated; the mended gloves, put by.
scenes.prose:
> *(She goes up at ten, because the day has had her entire and the bedchamber is the last room. The day accumulates behind her as she climbs: the inn, the lane, Slade's name, the Lash's paragraph, the London paper, Bell's warning in her own hand. She undresses slowly, and Élise's hands are gentle, and the mended gloves go back in the drawer.)*
> *(She stands at the window in her nightdress and watches the Park's dark — the garden's gap, the wall's new courses pale in the moonlight, the north lane a paler line beyond it. The house is quiet. The papers are kept as she chose. Wednesday is done, and the hunters have shown their signs, and the signs are all logged. The window, watched. The night, entered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the corridor — the morning-room door, dark; the letter, left alone.
scenes.prose:
> *(She cannot sleep, and the corridor is the only room left, and she goes — the grey wrapper over the nightdress, the house dark around her. At the corridor's end the morning-room door stands shut, and no lamplight lies across the boards. No footsteps. No shadow at the desk. Tuesday's long thin shape is gone, and the dark is only the dark.)*
> *(She stands a moment where the light ended last night, and thinks of the letter behind the household book's false back — the seal unbroken, the thirty years, the direction in the hand she must not see yet — and leaves it there, untouched, unopened, unasked-for. Some doors are not hers to open, and some letters are not hers to hurry. She goes back the way she came, soft, unheard. The corridor, walked. The letter, left.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night's voice — the late hour's finishing; the atelier's last word.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at eleven with the night's last question, the atelier's eye on the late hour. "The day has been looked at, miss — the night wants its voice." Three on the tray: the grandmother's fan, ivory — the hand, occupied; the violets, dried — faithfulness, the week's flower, worn against the signs; or the silver rose pin, plain — the house's mark, worn quiet.)*
> *(Rose touches the pin — plain silver, the house's mark, the watching's own. The fan waits, ivory. The violets, dried. "The late hour," she says, "wants the house on it." "The house," Élise says, pinning, "is on you, miss — the atelier only says so." She chooses the night's voice. In the glass: the mistress, marked.)*

scenes.synopsis: the lamp — the hour before sleep; the hunters, counted.
scenes.prose:
> *(She lies in the dark and listens to the house settle — the stair's last creak, the servants' door, the wind at the garden's gap. Wednesday's account runs itself once more, unbidden: the inn, the lane, Slade, the sheet, the London paper, the warning in Bell's own hand, the verdict not for sale. The hunters have shown their signs, and the signs are logged, and the log is shut.)*
> *(She thinks of coin changing hands for the shape of her house — in the village, on the lane, in London — and of the columns, entered fair, holding their own against whatever the money buys. The lamp is cold. The house holds its breath, and then lets it out. She is nearly asleep when the knock comes — the maid's knock, soft, the last post come late. The dark, breathed out. The knock, come.)*

scenes.synopsis: the last post — Bell's final line; Pounce's man, paying; the sheet, bought.
scenes.prose: > *(The knock is the last post, and it is Bell's hand again — one line, no masthead: "My man saw Pounce's man in a London coffeehouse tonight, paying for something. The sheet is bought, Miss Hartwell." Rose stands in the hall in her nightdress with the note in her hand, the house asleep around her, and the hunters' money has found its direction — toward the Lash, toward print, toward morning.)*

scenes.synopsis: Thursday's dawn — Bell's midnight line still in her hand; the sheet bought; the house wakes.
scenes.prose:
> *(She wakes before the maid — the grey dark, the habit holding from the week — and the first thing in her hand is the midnight line: "The sheet is bought, Miss Hartwell." She read it standing in the hall in her nightdress; she reads it now sitting up in bed, as if the words might have changed in the night. They have not. Pounce's man, paid in a London coffeehouse. The Lash's Thursday number, bought and paid for, printing now.)*
> *(The house is already awake below — the masons at the wall by seven, the book read at nine, Thursday's whole order in her hand before the maid knocks. Wednesday's signs are all logged: the inn, the lane, Slade, the sheet, the London paper, Bell's warning. Thursday, she thinks, will have a face to it. The hunters paid for the shape of her house; today one of them comes to measure the door. She rises. The day, booked.)*

scenes.synopsis: the morning face — the atelier dresses Thursday for a day of callers; the archive's Thursday.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes with Thursday's question, the atelier's eye on a day with a caller in it. "The week has a color for strangers at the door, miss — the house is looked at, and ought to look back unmoved." Three on the stand: the claret morning — the week's own, deep, the mistress's Thursday, worn to the door; the archive blue — the estate's, severe, the wall's color, worn to the walls; or the grey silk — the reader's, the ledger's color, worn to the study's business.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret — deep, steady, the week's own color. The blue waits, severe. The grey, sober. "Thursday," she says, "wants the house at the door." "At the door," Élise says, fastening, "and unmoved, miss — the atelier's whole doctrine." She chooses the morning's face. In the glass: the mistress, Thursday-eyed. The mended gloves, kept ready.)*

scenes.synopsis: Thursday's order — the book read at nine; the quartermaster, steady.
scenes.prose:
> *(The book's order for Thursday is read at nine, Letitia's voice back at its full quartermaster pitch — the masons at seven, already at the wall; the household accounts at ten; the stillroom at eleven; the village at three; dinner at half past six; the evening as the evening decides. Her pencil is behind her ear. The comedy is not attempted, and the room does not miss it.)*
> *(Rose takes the orders with the household and watches her aunt's hands — steady, the thirty years sitting where they sit, neither hidden nor displayed. Whatever the book's false back holds, the morning holds the book, and the book holds the house. The order, read. The Thursday, booked.)*

scenes.synopsis: the porter's word — Slade settles his account at the inn; asks the way to the Park.
scenes.prose:
> *(Amos finds her on the stair after the reading, the porter's news kept for the mistress's ear. "The man from the inn, miss — Slade. He settled his account this morning, and paid it fair." He looks at his boots. "And he asked the boy the way to the Park, miss. The house, not the garden. Said he had business with the mistress.")*
> *("A card, then," Rose says. "Like as not, miss," Amos says. "He had the manner of a man who sends a card." Paid fair. Asked the way. Wednesday's signs have put on a coat and are coming to the door. "Thank you, Amos," she says. "The door will be ready." The stair, climbed. The caller, coming.)*

scenes.synopsis: the memorandum book — Octavia's reading of the caller; the species, described.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia hears it in the morning room with the memorandum book open — "the inn, settled; the way, asked; the manner, of a card" — the pencil moving as Rose speaks. "A solicitor's man will have the manners," she says, "and a client he cannot name, and questions he is paid to ask politely. That is the whole of the species.")*
> *("What do I do with him?" Rose asks. "Exactly what you do with the Lash," Octavia says. "Read the reader. Note what he asks after — the order of the asking tells you the order of the wanting. And give him nothing that isn't already his to know — which is the house, the garden, and the weather." She underlines. The book, open. The counsel, logged.)*

scenes.synopsis: the card — Slade's hand, unknown; the client, unnamed; the hour, hers to give.
scenes.prose:
> *(The card comes at half past ten, on the silver tray, in a hand Rose does not know: "Mr. Slade, on behalf of a client — solicits the honor of an hour of Miss Hartwell's time, at her convenience, on a matter of old family business." Old family business. The phrase sits in the hall like a hat left on a chair — belonging to someone, claiming nothing.)*
> *(She turns the card over. Nothing on the back — no firm, no direction, no client's name. A solicitor's man with no solicitor named. She thinks of Bell's midnight line, and of the coin paid in a London coffeehouse, and of the lane, and the wall. "At her convenience," she says to the empty hall, and the empty hall agrees that her convenience is the entire question. The card, turned. The hour, hers to give.)*

scenes.synopsis: Harrow's place — where he stands when the caller comes; the manner, conditional.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she warned him: Harrow is at his keeping, warned and watching, the scarred gentleman with his eyes open and his papers under his hand. If she watches him: Harrow is on the lane at his work, unwatched-seeming, the log's unnamed column taking in his lane twice a day. If she housed him: Harrow is under the roof, in the blue room, the household having learned by breakfast that the scarred gentleman breakfasts in the house.)*
> *(Wherever he is, the question of Slade runs alongside the question of Harrow — because Slade will ask after him, polite and deniable, and the house must know where its answer stands before the question is put. A man who asks gardeners has finished asking the county; a man who sends a card has come to the door. She takes Harrow's measure the way she takes everything now: as a column, entered fair. The measure, taken. The placing, next.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — SLADE: receive him civilly, keep him waiting, or see him and say nothing.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the study with Slade's card on the desk — the hand she does not know, the client he cannot name — and the question of the hour runs alongside the question of the house. A solicitor's man, polite, patient, deniable, at her door. The hunters have put on a coat and sent a card. The house must answer the card.)*
> *(Receive him civilly: give him the hour, the morning room, the mistress's courtesy — the candor of it, the house unflustered, the risk that courtesy is read as welcome. Keep him waiting: let the card cool on the tray till afternoon — the cunning of it, the man kept guessing, the risk of the insult delivered before a word is spoken. Or see him and say nothing: receive him, and meet his questions with the house's silence — the resolve of it, deniability answered with deniability, the risk that silence is printed as guilt.)*
> *(The card goes where she sends it — into the morning room, onto the cooled tray, or into the drawing room's silence. If received: Amos shows him up at eleven, and the morning room is aired, and the mistress is courteous. If kept: the card waits on the tray till three, and Slade waits in the village, and the house goes about its business. If silenced: he is shown to the drawing room at noon, and offered tea, and met with the house entire and unanswering. Whatever the hour became, one law holds it entire: the door was hers, and she chose its opening. The choosing is done.)*

scenes.synopsis: the execution — the hour, given three ways; the caller, placed.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she received: the morning room at eleven — aired, the chairs set, Slade shown up by Amos with the porter's whole ceremony, the mistress rising to meet him. If she kept him waiting: three o'clock — the card cooled, the man cooled with it, shown up when the house has finished its business. If she silenced: the drawing room at noon — the tea poured, the household about its business around them, the mistress courteous and entire and unanswering.)*
> *(In every hour the same law: Slade is polite. He bows like a man who has bowed in better rooms. He sits when asked, or stands if not asked, and his patience is the professional kind — the kind that has waited out louder houses than this. The hour, given. The caller, placed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's counsel — how to receive a solicitor's man; the notebook, emptied in advance.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends for her before the hour — the blue drawing room, the chocolate, Thursday's own counsel. "A solicitor's man," she says. "I have received a hundred. They want three things, child: to see the house, to hear the voice, and to carry something home in their notebook. Give them the first two. The notebook goes home empty.")*
> *("And if he asks after Harrow?" Rose asks. "He will," Augusta says. "Deniable men ask after deniable things. You tell him Mr. Harrow is a gentleman employed about the Park, and you tell it the way you tell the weather — true, dull, and final." She drinks. "And the papers?" "The mistress reads what she likes," Augusta says. "That is the whole of the law on papers." The chocolate, drunk. The doctrine, dowagered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the receiving face — the atelier arms the mistress for the caller; the house, dressed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes with the receiving's question, the atelier's eye on the caller in the house. "The morning's dress has stood its watch, miss — the receiving wants the house's armor." Three on the peg: the claret, kept — deep, the week's color, the mistress unmoved at the door; the archive ivory — bright, the grandmother's, the house unruffled; or the blue wool, severe — the estate's, uniformed for the stranger.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret — kept, deep, the week's own. The ivory waits, bright. The blue wool, severe. "The receiving," she says, "wants the house." "The house," Élise says, fastening, "is on you, miss — the atelier only says so." She chooses the receiving's face. In the glass: the mistress, armored.)*

scenes.synopsis: the receiving — Slade's face at last; the client, unnamed; the business, old.
scenes.prose:
> *(Slade is as the lane described him and better dressed for it — a plain dark coat, a civil bow, a voice with London ironed into it. "Miss Hartwell," he says. "I am much obliged. My client —" the pause is professional — "prefers not to be named at this stage. A private gentleman, with an interest in old family business. I make inquiries on his behalf.")*
> *(Old family business. The phrase again, this time with a face to it. "My family," Rose says, "is in the household book, Mr. Slade, and the book is not private." He smiles — the patient smile, the deniable smile. "Then we shall get on," he says, "for I ask after nothing that isn't." The bow, taken. The business, named and unnamed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the conversation, opened — the garden asked after, then the county; the order of the asking.
scenes.prose:
> *(He asks after the garden first — the wall, the restoration, what the county's oldest walls may yet give up. She tells him the wall is a wall, and the restoration is the masons' business, and the garden will be a garden again. He writes nothing down, which she notes the way Octavia taught her: the order of the asking is the order of the wanting.)*
> *(He asks after the county next — who comes to the Park, who is in residence, how the household stands. She tells him the household stands entire, and the guests are the mistress's own affair. He smiles the deniable smile and asks nothing twice. The politeness, professional. The patience, entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: Harrow, asked after — the scarred gentleman, three ways placed; the answer, one way given.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she warned him: Slade asks after the scarred gentleman at his keeping — what brings a man to England to live quietly, what he does about the Park. If she watches him: Slade asks after the man seen on the lane — the scarred gentleman, the wall's counsel. If she housed him: Slade asks after the gentleman under the roof — the blue room's occupant, the household's new face.)*
> *(In every asking the same answer: "Mr. Harrow is a gentleman employed about the Park." True, dull, and final. Slade nods, patient, and does not ask twice — but the not-asking-twice is itself an entry in Octavia's book, for a man who lets a thing lie is a man with another way of lifting it. The lie, let. The lifting, noted.)*

scenes.synopsis: the papers, asked after — the goods, reached for last; nothing shown, nothing named.
scenes.prose:
> *(He asks after the papers last — whether the mistress keeps old family paper at the house, whether the walled garden gave up anything besides stone. The order of the asking, Octavia said, is the order of the wanting — and the papers are last because the papers are the goods, and a professional does not reach for the goods first.)*
> *(Rose looks at him across the hour — the morning room, or the drawing room's silence, as the choosing decided — and says, "The mistress reads what she likes, Mr. Slade." He bows to it, entire. "A complete answer," he says, "to an incomplete question." Nothing shown. Nothing named. The keeping — moved, guarded, or divided, as the week chose — sits undisturbed behind the hour. The papers, unasked into his hands.)*

scenes.synopsis: the midday face — the atelier answers the receiving; the woman, not the door.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at half past twelve with the midday's question, the atelier having heard the house's news through the servants' stair. "The receiving has had its hour, miss — the afternoon wants the woman, not the door." Three on the bed: the grey silk — the reader's, the ledger's color, the logging continued; the ivory, layered — bright, the house unruffled; or the claret, again — deep, the week's color, kept for the afternoon.)*
> *(Rose touches the grey — the reader's, the page's color, the afternoon's own. The ivory waits, layered. The claret, deep. "The afternoon," she says, "is the household's." "The household's," Élise says, fastening, "and unruffled, miss — the atelier only says so." She chooses the midday's face. In the glass: the mistress, continued.)*

scenes.synopsis: the leaving — no door forced, no threat spoken; the deniability, intact.
scenes.prose:
> *(Slade takes his leave at one — or at four, as the hour chose — with the same civil bow he came in with, and thanks the mistress for her courtesy, and says his client will be gratified by her frankness. No door is forced. No threat is spoken. The deniability goes out the way it came in: entire, polite, and empty-handed.)*
> *(Rose watches him go down the drive from the morning-room window — the plain dark coat, the unhurried step, a man who has waited out louder houses. Amos shuts the door behind him with the porter's whole ceremony. The house exhales. The test, taken. The house, holding.)*

scenes.synopsis: the reader, read — Octavia takes Slade's hour apart; the test, assessed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes to the study with the memorandum book, and takes Slade's hour apart the way a cook takes a joint apart — the garden first, the county second, Harrow third, the papers last. "The order of the asking," she says, underlining. "The papers are the goods. Harrow is the way in. The garden is the advertisement. And the county —" the pencil taps — "is the measuring of the house.")*
> *("What did he learn?" Rose asks. "That the house is courteous, the mistress is dull on the subjects that matter, and the notebook goes home empty," Octavia says. "What did he signal? That the asking is professional, the money behind it is patient, and they will not force a door." She shuts the book. "A test of the defenses, Rose. And the house held." The book, shut. The reader, read.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — HARROW: hide him, stand him openly, or send him to London.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone at half past one, and the question of Harrow runs alongside the question of the afternoon. Slade has asked after him — polite, deniable, patient — and Slade will ask again, or another face will. The scarred gentleman is the way in, Octavia said. The house must decide what the way in becomes.)*
> *(Hide him: keep him out of the strangers' sight — his door shut to callers, the blue room's occupant unseen, the lane unwalked — the cunning of it, the way in closed, the risk that a hidden man looks like a kept secret. Stand him openly: let Harrow be seen — the Park's man, the wall's counsel, nothing to hide — the candor of it, the house unflustered, the risk that the open is read as the offered. Or send him to London: put him under Quill's roof, out of the county, where the strangers' eyes are dearer — the resolve of it, the way in removed, the risk of the road and the talk it makes.)*
> *(Harrow's afternoon goes where she sends it — hidden, opened, or roaded. If hidden: the word goes to his keeping — no callers, the lane unwalked — and the blue room's occupant, if housed, keeps to the house. If opened: Harrow walks the wall at three with the foreman, in sight of the lane, the Park's man entire. If roaded: the chaise is ordered for the morning, and Quill has the word by the evening post, and Harrow takes the London road with her seal on his keeping. Whatever the afternoon became, one law holds it entire: Harrow is hers to consider, and she chose the manner. The choosing is done.)*

options.detail: *Candor+; the standing, plain.* The Park's man, the wall's counsel; nothing to hide. *(Plain — and the offering, risked.)*

options.label: Send him to London
options.detail: *Resolve+; the journey, made.* Under Quill's roof, out of the county; the way in, removed. *(Made — and the talk, weathered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the telling — Harrow meets the new placing standing; the man, placed.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she hid him: she tells him at his door — or the blue room's door, as the housing chose — plain: no callers, the lane unwalked, till the strangers' eyes move on. If she opened him: she tells him at the wall at three — walk it, be seen, the Park's man. If she roaded him: she tells him in the study — the chaise at morning, Quill's roof, her seal on his keeping.)*
> *(In every telling the same law: Harrow meets it standing. "I have been placed before, Miss Hartwell," he says — dry, the scarred face still — "and I like the placing done plain." If hidden: he nods, and his door shuts. If opened: he walks the wall at three. If roaded: he packs the trunk by nine. The telling, done. The man, placed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, brothered — Julian on the solicitor's man; stand stiller.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian finds her at the study door with the rent-book under his arm — carried, the afternoon being the afternoon. "A solicitor's man," he says. "Quill's note said London's buying Hartwell paper. Now the buying has a face and manners. You didn't sell him anything?" "Not the time of day," Rose says.)*
> *("Good," Julian says. "Counsel, and it costs nothing: a man building a holding needs the other side to move. You stood still. Stand stiller." He squeezes her arm, brotherly. "And if he comes again —" "He won't force a door," she says. "No," Julian says. "He'll wait for you to open one. Don't." The counsel, given. The brother, plain.)*

scenes.synopsis: the guest's ease — Laurent courteous; the luncheon, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent finds her in the hall before luncheon, the guest's whole philosophy in his shoulders — come down early, he says, the afternoon being fine. "Your caller, Miss Hartwell," he says. "A London man? The Park looks well for it — a house with business is a house alive.")*
> *(She thinks of the log — the garden, Harrow, the papers, the order of the asking — and says only, "Business, Monsieur, of the dullest kind." He bows, the guest's bow, entire, and offers his arm to luncheon. Some kindnesses hold a house up, she thinks — the kind that do it by simply standing in it. The arm, taken. The ease, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the afternoon face — the atelier's deeper word for the stranger's day.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at three with the afternoon's question, the atelier's eye on the day the stranger came. "The caller has gone, miss — the afternoon wants the mistress, not the door." Three on the bench: the claret silk — deep, the week's color, the day's own, worn to the watching of it; the atelier's newest work — the present, dressed fresh, the mistress first in it; or the grey, again — the reader's, the page's color, the logging continued.)*
> *(Rose touches the newest work — fresh, the present, the atelier's whole argument. The claret waits, deep. The grey, sober. "The afternoon," she says, "wants the house steady." "Steady," Élise says, fastening, "is the week's whole color, miss — the atelier only says so." She chooses the afternoon's face. In the glass: the mistress, steadied.)*

scenes.synopsis: the garden at three — the wall, the gap, the waiter's patience; the waiting, his.
scenes.prose:
> *(She walks the garden at three, because the study has had her and the air is owed its hour. The masons are at the north stretch, the courses rising pale and numbered, the foreman's chalk white on the stone. The gap is a hand's breadth narrower than Wednesday. Course by course the wall comes back over the oldest thing at Hartwell — and this morning a polite man asked what it covers, and went away empty.)*
> *(She stands where the papers were found — the giving-up place, the soil turned and turned again — and thinks of Slade's patience, the professional kind, the kind that has waited out louder houses. Let him wait, she thinks. The wall is rising anyway. The foreman touches his cap. She nods. The waiting, his. The wall, hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the quartermaster's afternoon — Letitia at the stillroom; the letter, sealed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia is at the stillroom accounts at half past three, the household book open, the pencil at its old pace — the quartermaster's afternoon, resumed. She looks up when Rose comes in, and the look is the aunt's, and it has the whole week in it. "The caller," she says. "Gone?" "Gone," Rose says. "And empty-handed.")*
> *(Letitia nods, and goes back to the columns, and the steadiness passes between them the way it has all week — unspoken, entire. Behind the book's false back the letter sits sealed, untouched, unasked-for. Some doors are not Rose's to open. She leaves her aunt to the stillroom and the columns. The book, kept. The letter, left.)*

scenes.synopsis: the verdict, dowagered — the house's defenses tested; the test, passed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends for her at four — the blue drawing room, the chocolate, Thursday's own hour. "Well," she says. "The solicitor's man came, and the solicitor's man went, and the notebook went home empty. I have seen this weather before, child — deniable men, patient money, the old sin sniffed at from a distance.")*
> *("Did the house hold?" Rose asks. "The house," Augusta says, "was courteous, dull, and final — the three virtues of a house under examination. Hunters want a chase, my dear. You gave them a house going quietly about its business, and the man went home to tell his client exactly that." She drinks. "The test, passed. The defenses, held." The chocolate, drunk. The verdict, dowagered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the boy's hour — the copybook's Thursday page; the household's ballast.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry is permitted the drawing room at five for the copybook's Thursday page — the boy's hour, the household's ballast. He exhibits the page with both hands, the way he has all week: the letters even, the lines straight, the Thursday done fair. "Very good," Rose says, and means it the way she means everything on Thursdays now — entirely.)*
> *(He tells her about the masons' chalk — white, on the stone, the courses numbered — with the gravity of a small surveyor. She listens the way Augusta taught her: entire. Somewhere beyond the north lane the strangers are counting their money, and here is a boy counting chalk marks, and the house holds them both. The page, exhibited. The ballast, kept.)*

scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at six with the evening's question, the atelier having watched the day to its edge. "The stranger has had his day, miss — the evening wants the table's face." Three on the rail: the claret, evening — deep, the week's color, dressed for the night and the table; the ivory, layered — bright, the house unruffled; or the blue, quiet — the estate, worn to the table, the mistress uniformed.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret — evening, deep, the week's own color. The ivory waits, layered. The blue, severe. "The evening," she says, "is the table's, and the table is unruffled." "The table," Élise says, pinning, "wants you, miss — the atelier's whole doctrine." She chooses the evening's face. In the glass: the hostess, refaced.)*

scenes.synopsis: Thursday's dinner — the table; the stranger's day, worn quiet.
scenes.prose:
> *(Dinner is the dining room at half past six — the household, Thursday's table: Augusta in state, Julian with the rent-book put by, Octavia with the memorandum book shut for the hour, Laurent at Rose's right, Henry permitted the table for the pudding, Letitia's book closed, Mrs. Pike's joint doing its office. The talk is of the week — the masons, the garden, the wall — and not of callers, and not of solicitors' men, by unspoken agreement.)*
> *(Rose sits at the table's head in the evening's face and the house gathers. The day sits at the table like a guest nobody introduced — the card, the hour, the asking, the leaving — and everybody passes it the salt, and it passes the salt back. The dinner, served. The table, entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: Thursday's holding ritual — the household dresses Thursday for the holding; the stranger's day, answered with steadiness.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the book — "Thursday's line is written, miss. The book thanks the mistress for the holding.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the window — "the lane is quiet, Rose. Tonight the doors hold.")*
> *(Story morsel: Augusta, at the door — "courteous, child. Dull. Final.")*
> *(Story morsel: Élise, at the hem — "the extra stitch held, miss. All day, for Thursday.")*
> *(Story morsel: Julian, at the stair — "the bolt's on, Rose. The house is ready when you are.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: Thursday — the day the stranger came to the door; the house holds its line — every threshold a decision, every answer measured, nothing theatrical and nothing forced. Dress for the holding: Thursday's colors, worn with patience. Courteous. Watchful. Entire. The house that holds together is not pried open.

scenes.synopsis: the evening post — Quill's line; the field man and the paper-buying, two hands.
scenes.prose:
> *(The evening post brings Quill's line — the solicitor's hand, all business: a London solicitor's man, client unnamed, has had inquiries this week after old Hartwell paper. Small notes, old debts, the kind of paper that changes hands quietly. Quill names no firm and no client. "The interest," he writes, "is professional, and the patience is expensive.")*
> *(She holds the note a long moment. Slade at the door by day; Slade's trade in London by night — the field man and the paper-buying, two hands of one operation. The patience is expensive. She enters it in the log: London, the debts, the patience — dated, sourced. The draft, felt again. The door, still unfound.)*

scenes.synopsis: the study at night — the keeping, visited; the columns, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(She stops at the study after the ritual, because the night's last office is the papers. If they were moved: the shelf stands honest and empty, the box in Harrow's keeping — wherever the afternoon left him — under her seal and his hand. If they were guarded: the bolt on the study door, the wax holding on the box, Amos's rotations on the stair. If they were split: the box sealed on the shelf, the packet gone in Octavia's reticule to a keeping nobody names.)*
> *(Whatever the keeping, the thought that comes with the dark is Julian's: stand still, and he overpays for air. She looks at the ledger — de la Roche's nine hundred, de Brissac's fourteen hundred, entered fair — and thinks of Slade's empty notebook going home to his client. Let them pay, she thinks. The columns are here. She shuts the study door. The night, faced. The columns, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE HOUSEHOLD: tell them nothing, tell them enough, or keep the staff close and quiet.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone at nine, and the question of the household runs alongside the question of the night. Slade came to the door; another face may come. The house held today — but a house holds better when it knows what it is holding against, or when it knows nothing at all. The question is what the household is told.)*
> *(Tell them nothing: the servants keep the order, the kitchen keeps its philosophy, and nobody is told there is anything to know — the cunning of it, the calm unbroken, the risk of the unready. Tell them enough: the household told plain — a stranger came asking, strangers may come again, every question reported — the candor of it, the house armed, the risk of a house that jumps at shadows. Or keep the staff close and quiet: no speeches, no warnings — the household drawn in, the doors watched, the talk kept low — the resolve of it, the holding entire, the risk of the silence curdling.)*
> *(The household goes where she sends it — into silence, into knowledge, or into the close quiet. If nothing: the routine stands, and the house sleeps unruffled, and nobody is told. If enough: the word goes out before ten — every question reported, every stranger logged — and the house takes it entire. If close: no word goes out, but Amos's rotations tighten, the doors are watched, and the talk stays low by unspoken agreement. Whatever the night became, one law holds it entire: the household is hers, and she chose its keeping. The choosing is done.)*

scenes.synopsis: the answer, executed — the house takes its orders for the night.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she told nothing: the corridor at ten — the doors shut, the lamps low, the house asleep unruffled, and nobody the wiser. If she told enough: the orders go out before ten, and the servants take them the way they take everything, entire. If she kept them close: nothing said, and everything watched — the stair, the lane, the doors.)*
> *(In every night the same law: she walks the corridor once, and the house holds its Thursday the way a hand holds a kept thing — firmly, and without squeezing. The corridor, walked. The answer, given.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — the Lash's Thursday squib; sharp, not the scandal; Bell's Gazette stays clean.
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting is the Lash's Thursday paragraph, come up with the late post — Pounce's sheet, the gutter's eye on the week's weather.)*
> *(Rose reads it in the hall, the way she reads everything the gutter prints, and finds the edge in it — the advertising edge, the sheet telling its buyers what it intends to sell them. It names no sums, no names — only the shape, sniffed at. And Bell's Gazette carries no paragraph Thursday — the proprietor's paper clean, alert, unbought. She folds the Lash and gives it to Octavia for the memorandum book. The paper smells of ink. The hall smells of night.)*
scenes.sting: the sting — the Lash's Thursday squib; sharp, not the scandal; Bell's Gazette stays clean.

scenes.synopsis: the bedchamber — Thursday accumulated; the mended gloves, put by.
scenes.prose:
> *(She goes up at ten, because the day has had her entire and the bedchamber is the last room. The day accumulates behind her as she climbs: the card, the hour, the garden asked after, Harrow asked after, the papers asked after, the leaving, the squib. She undresses slowly, and Élise's hands are gentle, and the mended gloves go back in the drawer.)*
> *(She stands at the window in her nightdress and watches the Park's dark — the garden's gap, the wall's new courses pale in the moonlight, the drive a paler line beyond it. The house is quiet. The papers are kept as she chose. Thursday is done, and the stranger has come and gone, and the house held. The window, watched. The night, entered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night's voice — the late hour's finishing; faithfulness, worn against the asking.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at eleven with the night's last question, the atelier's eye on the late hour. "The stranger has had his day, miss — the night wants its voice." Three on the tray: the grandmother's fan, ivory — the hand, occupied; the violets, dried — faithfulness, the week's flower, worn against the asking; or the silver rose pin, plain — the house's mark, worn quiet.)*
> *(Rose touches the violets — dried, faithfulness, the week's flower. The fan waits, ivory. The pin, plain. "The late hour," she says, "wants the house on it." "The house," Élise says, pinning, "is on you, miss — the atelier only says so." She chooses the night's voice. In the glass: the mistress, marked.)*

scenes.synopsis: the corridor — the morning-room door, dark; the letter, left alone.
scenes.prose:
> *(She cannot sleep, and the corridor is the only room left, and she goes — the grey wrapper over the nightdress, the house dark around her. At the corridor's end the morning-room door stands shut, and no lamplight lies across the boards. No footsteps. No shadow at the desk. The week's long thin shape is gone, and the dark is only the dark.)*
> *(She stands a moment where the light ended, and thinks of the letter behind the household book's false back — the seal unbroken, the thirty years, the direction in the hand she must not see yet — and leaves it there, untouched, unopened, unasked-for. Some doors are not hers to open, and some letters are not hers to hurry. She goes back the way she came, soft, unheard. The corridor, walked. The letter, left.)*

scenes.synopsis: the lamp — the hour before sleep; Thursday, counted; the house, holding.
scenes.prose:
> *(She lies in the dark and listens to the house settle — the stair's last creak, the servants' door, the wind at the garden's gap. Thursday's account runs itself once more, unbidden: the card, the hour, the asking, the leaving, Harrow placed, the household told as she chose, the squib. The stranger came to the door, and the door held, and the house is logged and shut.)*
> *(She thinks of Slade's patience — the professional kind — and of the columns, entered fair, holding their own against whatever the money buys. The lamp is cold. The house holds its breath, and then lets it out. She is nearly asleep when the knock comes — the maid's knock, soft. Not the post. Amos's word, come late. The dark, breathed out. The knock, come.)*

scenes.synopsis: the second face — Amos's late word; another man at the inn; the operation, more than one.
scenes.prose: > *(The knock is Amos's word, come late up the servants' stair: a second man took a room at the village inn tonight — London coat, London questions, asking after the Park. Slade is gone down the drive, and the inn has another face in his place. The operation, Rose understands in the dark, has more than one face — and the house, having held the first, must hold the second.)*

scenes.synopsis: Friday's dawn — Amos's overnight word; the second man goes to London; the house follows.
scenes.prose:
> *(She wakes to Amos's word brought up with the tea — the porter kept the inn watched through the night, as the keeping ordered. The second man breakfasted early, walked the lane to look at the wall, and took the morning coach toward London. Slade went down the drive Thursday; his second goes up the road Friday. The operation has more than one face, and one of them is going to the ball.)*
> *(She stands at the window and watches the lane empty itself of the second man. If she hid him: his door is shut behind Harrow, the lane unwalked, the way in closed. If she opened him: Harrow is on the wall by seven, in sight of the lane, the Park's man entire. If she roaded him: Harrow took the chaise Thursday morning, and Quill has him under his roof in London. Wherever he stands, the town house must stand ready by nightfall — the carriages at eight, the rooms aired, the ball by ten.)*

scenes.synopsis: the morning face — the atelier dresses Friday for the road; the London house, answered.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes with Friday's question, the atelier's eye on the road. "London by night, miss — the morning wants the traveler, not the hostess." Three on the stand: the claret, roaded — deep, the week's color, worn to the coach; the archive blue — the estate's, severe, worn to the town house; or the grey silk — the reader's, the ledger's color, worn to the journey's business.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret — roaded, deep, the week's own. The blue waits, severe. The grey, sober. "The road," she says, "wants the mistress packed and calm." "Packed," Élise says, fastening, "and calm, miss — the atelier's whole doctrine." She chooses the morning's face. In the glass: the traveler, mistressed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the keeping, visited — the papers sit as the week chose; the road, taken.
scenes.prose:
> *(She stops at the study before the carriages, because the night's first office is the papers, and London is a day away. If they were moved: the shelf stands honest and empty, the box in Harrow's keeping — wherever the week left him — under her seal and his hand. If they were guarded: the bolt on the study door, the wax holding on the box, Amos's rotations on the stair. If they were split: the box sealed on the shelf, the packet in Octavia's reticule, going up to London in better company than the mail.)*
> *(Whatever the keeping, the house stands entire behind her as she shuts the door — the masons at the wall, the garden at its gap, the Park kept. The papers go where the week sent them, and she goes where Friday sends her. The London road, taken. The keeping, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the book's Friday order — the quartermaster reads the road; the letter, sealed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia reads the book's Friday order on the step, pencil behind her ear, the quartermaster's road voice on: the London house opened by noon, the staff's order, the ball's hour, the carriages at eight. The household takes it entire. The comedy is not attempted, and the road does not miss it.)*
> *(Behind the book's false back the letter sits sealed, untouched, unasked-for — going up to London in the book, because the book goes everywhere. Letitia's hand rests a moment on the cover, and Rose sees it, and says nothing. Some doors are not Rose's to open, and Friday is not the day for doors. The book, shut. The road, booked.)*

scenes.synopsis: the road's arithmetic — Octavia reads the ton's weather; the columns, entered fair.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia rides with the memorandum book on her knee, and reads the ton's weather the way she reads everything — aloud, underlined. "The Lash has primed the room all week," she says. "The ton loves nothing like an old scandal, and Pounce has been serving it the shape of one without the substance. Tonight the room will want the substance. It will not get it.")*
> *("And the second man?" Rose asks. "London coat, London questions," Octavia says. "He will be in the room, or his employer will. Either way —" the pencil taps — "the arithmetic is the same. We are not buying the verdict, Rose. We are outlasting the asking." She looks at the ledger — de la Roche's nine hundred, de Brissac's fourteen hundred, entered fair — and shuts the book. "The columns are here. Let them pay for air.")*

scenes.synopsis: the town house — arrival; the evening, mapped; the staff's order.
scenes.prose:
> *(The town house opens at noon — the shutters back, the covers off, the staff's Friday order taken entire. The ball's hour is mapped in the hall: the gown's bones laid, the jewels fetched, the carriages at eight, the doors of the ball at ten. London is smaller than the Park and louder, and the house takes it the way it takes everything — entire.)*
> *(Rose walks the rooms once, and the rooms are the town's — high, narrow, polished — and the evening sits in them like a guest already arrived. If she told the household nothing: the order stands, and nobody is told there is anything to know. If she told them enough: every stranger logged, every question reported. If she kept them close: nothing said, and everything watched. Whatever the keeping, the house is ready. The mapping, done.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE ROOM: meet the whispers openly, cut them with a scene, or withdraw with dignity.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the London drawing room with the ball three hours off — the candles laid, the gown's bones on the stand — and the question of the room runs alongside the question of the night. The Lash has primed the ton; the second man has a London coat; the whispers will come whether she is ready or not. The house must decide how the mistress meets them.)*
> *(Meet them openly: walk the room as if the whispers were weather — heard, unhurried, unanswered — the candor of it, the house unflustered, the risk that the open is read as the unbothered, and the unbothered as the guilty. Cut them with a scene: answer one whisper with a moment the room cannot misread — a laugh, a toast of her own, a turn of the floor — the resolve of it, the gossip given a better story, the risk that the scene is printed as the performance. Or withdraw with dignity: take the supper room's corner, the dowager's wing, the quiet end of the evening — the mercy of it, the house entire, the risk that the quiet is read as the hiding.)*
> *(The night goes where she sends it — into the open, into the scene, or into the quiet. If open: she takes the floor early, and the room sees her unbothered, and the whispers must keep up with her. If staged: she holds one moment for the room's eye — the laugh, the toast, the turn — and the gossip has a better story to carry home. If quiet: she takes Augusta's wing, and the supper room, and the evening's dignity, and the whispers find no purchase. Whatever the night became, one law holds it entire: the room was hers to meet, and she chose the manner. The choosing is done.)*

scenes.synopsis: the execution — the night planned three ways; the manner, set.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she chose the open: the evening is planned for the floor — early arrival, the first dances taken, the room walked as if the whispers were weather. If she chose the scene: one moment is held for the room's eye — the laugh placed, the toast ready, the turn rehearsed in the glass. If she chose the quiet: the supper room's corner is claimed in advance, the dowager's wing arranged, the evening's dignity mapped like a campaign.)*
> *(In every night the same law: the manner is chosen before the doors open, because a manner chosen in the room is a manner the room chose. She stands at the window and watches London darken. The planning, done. The night, hers to meet.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Friday number — Pounce's priming squib; the room, advertised.
scenes.prose:
> *(The Lash's Friday number comes up with the afternoon post — Pounce's sheet, the gutter's eye on the night ahead. Octavia reads it aloud in the drawing room, pencil ready.)*
> *(Rose listens, and finds the shape in it — the advertising shape, the sheet telling its buyers what it intends to sell them. It names no sums, no names — only the promise, sniffed at. "The priming," Octavia says, underlining, "before the pour." She folds the Lash for the memorandum book. The paper smells of ink. The room smells of candles.)*

scenes.synopsis: the gown's bones — the atelier lays the ball's foundation; the night, structured.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at four with the ball's question, the atelier having ridden up in the second carriage with its whole London box. "The bones first, miss — the night is built on them." Three on the stand: the claret, full dress — deep, the week's color, the mistress in state; the archive blue — the estate's, severe, the wall's color worn to the town; or the ivory, layered — bright, the grandmother's, the house unruffled.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret — full dress, deep, the week's own color. The blue waits, severe. The ivory, bright. "The foundation," she says, "wants the house under it." "The house," Élise says, pinning, "is under everything, miss — the atelier only says so." She chooses the bones. In the glass: the structure, mistressed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's counsel — Grandmama on the ton; the branch fell, and no more.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends for her at five — the London drawing room, the chocolate, Friday's own counsel. "The ton," she says, "loves nothing like an old scandal, child, because a new one might be theirs. An old one is safe to savor. Tonight they will savor you. Let them. A savored thing is not a ruined thing.")*
> *("And the branch?" Rose asks — the de Valcourt branch, fallen, the old name. "Fell," Augusta says, final as weather. "Long before your time, and nothing to do with tonight's whispers. A fallen branch is a fact, child, not a confession." She drinks. "Wear what you like. The room wants a story; give it a gown instead." The chocolate, drunk. The doctrine, dowagered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel, brothered — the verdict cannot be bought; stand stiller.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian finds her at the stair with his gloves in his hand — the brother, Fridayed, the evening's arithmetic already done in his head. "The room wants the scandal," he says. "It can't have it. And before you ask — no, you can't buy the verdict. Not with money, not with charm, not with the best gown Élise ever pinned. The ton's judgment isn't for sale, and trying to buy it is how you lose it.")*
> *("Then what do I do?" Rose asks. "What you've done all week," Julian says. "Stand still. The hunters paid for the shape of the house; tonight they want the shape of the woman. Don't give them either." He squeezes her arm. "And Rose — enjoy one dance. The house can spare you one." The counsel, given. The brother, plain.)*

scenes.synopsis: the boy stays home — Henry keeps the house; the ballast, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry is found in the library with his copybook, permitted the town house but not the ball — the boy's Friday, the household's ballast. He exhibits the week's pages with both hands: the letters even, the lines straight, the Friday done fair. "Very good," Rose says, and means it entirely.)*
> *(He asks whether the ball has masons, and she tells him it has musicians, which satisfies him the way chalk satisfies him. She leaves him to the library and the copybook. Somewhere across town a room is filling with the ton's arithmetic, and here is a boy counting letters, and the house holds them both. The pages, exhibited. The ballast, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the guest's promise — Laurent in London; the first dance, his; devotion, entire.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent finds her in the hall at half past six, the guest's whole philosophy in his shoulders — come down early, the evening being fine. "London," he says, "and a ball. I have been practicing my English small talk all afternoon. It is terrible." She laughs, and the laugh is the week's first unguarded one.)*
> *("The first dance is mine," he says. "I have asked no one else's permission, because I am a guest and guests may be presumptuous." "It is yours," she says. He bows, devoted and entire — the still point the whole evening turns around. The arm, promised. The unknowing, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening's hand — Letitia dresses the ball's face; the heirloom, chosen.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia comes at seven with the evening's question, the aunt's hands on the ball's face. "The bones are Élise's, miss — the face is the family's." Three on the tray: the heirloom lace — the grandmother's, at the throat, the house's oldest voice; the pearls, the grandmother's — the branch's own, worn open; or the silver rose pin, plain — the house's mark, worn quiet.)*
> *(Rose touches the lace — old, the grandmother's, the throat's own. The pearls wait. The pin, plain. "The evening," she says, "wants the family on it." "The family," Letitia says, pinning, "is on you, miss — the quartermaster only says so." She chooses the evening's hand. In the glass: the mistress, familied.)*

scenes.synopsis: the footmen's orders — the London staff takes the night's keeping; conditional.
scenes.prose:
> *(At half past seven the London staff takes the night's orders in the hall — the footmen, the coachman, the hall boy, the keeping entire. If she told them nothing: the routine stands, the doors are the doors, and nobody is told there is anything to know. If she told them enough: every question reported, every stranger logged, the second man's description passed hand to hand. If she kept them close: no word, but the doors are watched, the talk kept low, the night held close and quiet.)*
> *(In every keeping the same law: the staff takes the orders the way it takes everything — entire, unruffled, London-polished. The hall, ordered. The night, staffed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the proprietor's word — Bell calls before the ball; the Gazette prints nothing.
scenes.prose:
> *(Mrs. Nance Bell calls at eight — no card sent ahead, the proprietor's privilege — and is shown to the drawing room with the ink still on her cuffs. "I don't stay," she says. "I came to say it to your face: my paper carries no paragraph tonight. Not of the scandal, not of the ball, not a line. The Lash can print its provocations; the Gazette prints what it can stand behind.")*
> *("Thank you," Rose says. "Don't," Bell says, blunt. "It's not kindness. It's the paper. A proprietor who prints what she can't prove is a pamphleteer, and I am not Pounce." She is gone by five past, the ink and the bluntness with her. The word, given. The sheet, clean.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE COLORS: wear the de Valcourt colors openly, wear only Hartwell, or wear mourning-white and say nothing.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone at half past eight with the ball an hour off — the gown's bones pinned, the jewels laid, the night's whole arithmetic in her hand — and the question of the colors runs alongside the question of the answer. The Lash has primed the room; the whispers will name the branch. She can wear the de Valcourt colors and meet the naming, wear only Hartwell and let the house answer, or wear mourning-white and say nothing at all. The house must decide what the mistress wears to the reckoning.)*
> *(Wear the de Valcourt colors openly: the branch's blue and silver, worn where the room can see them — the resolve of it, the naming answered with the wearing, the risk that the open is read as the defiant, and the defiant as the guilty. Wear only Hartwell: the archive claret, the estate's own — the cunning of it, the house entire and unprovocative, the risk that the unprovocative is read as the evasive. Or wear mourning-white and say nothing: the grandmother's white, silence worn — the mercy of it, the dignity entire, the risk that the silence is printed as the hiding.)*
> *(The colors go where she sends them — onto the branch, onto the house, or onto the silence. If the branch: the blue and silver are laid out, and the room will see the de Valcourt colors and know she is not hiding them. If the house: the claret goes on, deep, the week's own, and the estate answers for the mistress. If the white: the grandmother's silk, quiet, and the night gets no answer but the wearing. Whatever the colors became, one law holds it entire: the answer was hers to wear, and she chose the wearing. The choosing is done.)*

scenes.synopsis: the execution — the colors worn three ways; the answer, dressed.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she chose the branch: the de Valcourt blue and silver go on — the sash, the ribbon at the wrist, the branch's colors worn where the candles find them. If she chose the house: the archive claret, deep — the week's color, the estate's answer, the mistress housed in Hartwell. If she chose the white: the grandmother's silk, quiet — mourning-white, nothing said, the dignity entire.)*
> *(In every wearing the same law: the colors are chosen before the doors open, because colors chosen in the room are colors the room chose. She stands in the glass a moment. The answering, dressed. The wearing, hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the last entries — the memorandum book closes before the ball; the counsel, final.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes at nine with the memorandum book, and makes the last entries before the ball — the second man's description, the Lash's Friday number filed, Bell's word logged: no paragraph. The pencil moves the way it has all week: preemptive, entire.)*
> *("One counsel for the room," Octavia says, shutting the book. "The whispers are weather. You have met weather before. And Rose —" the precision softens, once — "whatever the room says about the branch, the branch is not you. The house is not the sin. Remember which one of you is going to the ball." She gives her the book's shut cover to touch, for luck. The entries, made. The counsel, final.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sealed letter — the book's false back stays shut; the aunt, steady.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia is at the household book at half past nine, the pencil at its old pace — the quartermaster's evening, resumed. The book goes to the ball in the reticule, because the book goes everywhere, and behind its false back the letter sits sealed, untouched, unasked-for.)*
> *(Rose watches her aunt's hands — steady, the thirty years sitting where they sit — and thinks of the whispers waiting across town, and of the branch's name on the ton's tongue. "The letter stays," Letitia says, not looking up. "Tonight is not the night for doors." She shuts the book. The steadiness, entire. The letter, left.)*

scenes.synopsis: the final detail — the pin, the gloves, the fan; faithfulness, worn.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone at ten with the ball's hour on her — the gown's bones set, the colors chosen, the jewels laid — and the last question is the atelier's smallest one. Three on the tray: the grandmother's fan, ivory — the hand, occupied; the violets, dried — faithfulness, the week's flower, worn against the whispers; or the silver rose pin, plain — the house's mark, worn quiet.)*
> *(She touches the violets — dried, faithfulness, the week's flower. The fan waits, ivory. The pin, plain. "The hour," she says to the empty room, "wants the house on it." The empty room agrees. She chooses the final detail. In the glass: the mistress, finished.)*

scenes.synopsis: the hour — the carriages; the town house empties; the night, boarded.
scenes.prose:
> *(The carriages are called at half past ten — the household's Friday night, boarded like a campaign. Augusta in the first carriage, the dowager's state entire; Rose in the second with Letitia and the book; Julian and Octavia in the third; Laurent riding with the party, the guest's privilege. The town house empties behind them, the lamps left burning.)*
> *(Rose takes her seat, and the colors she chose settle around her — the branch's, the house's, or the white's — and the night's whole arithmetic rides with her. The wheels turn. London opens. The hour, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the streets — London at night; the room ahead; the arithmetic, carried.
scenes.prose:
> *(The carriage moves through London at night — the lamps, the wet streets, the town's whole Friday shining. She carries the night's arithmetic the way she carries everything now: as a column, entered fair. The whispers are weather. The verdict is not for sale. The colors are chosen. The house holds.)*
> *(She thinks of the second man in his London coat, somewhere ahead of her in the shining streets, and of Slade's patience, the professional kind. Let them be in the room, she thinks. The room is hers to meet. The streets, shining. The arithmetic, carried.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's last word — in the carriage; the wing, offered.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta rides in the first carriage and sends her word back by the footman — the dowager's economy, entire. "Grandmama says," the footman says, "that the mistress is to take the dowager's wing when she enters, whatever the night's manner. The wing is held. The corner is hers.")*
> *(Rose smiles in the dark of the carriage — the wing, offered; the corner, held. If she chose the quiet: the wing is the plan entire. If she chose the open or the scene: the wing is the fallback, the dowager's insurance. Whatever the manner, the house has her flank. The word, sent. The wing, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the doors — arrival; the names announced; the chorus, unnamed.
scenes.prose:
> *(The doors open at ten — the ball's whole Friday shining inside them. The names are announced on the stair: the dowager, the brother, the aunt, the guest — and "Miss Hartwell," and the room turns the way rooms turn, all at once and all together. The ton is a chorus tonight, unnamed and entire, and every face in it has read the Lash.)*
> *(She stands at the stair's head a moment, and the colors she chose catch the candles — the branch's blue and silver, the house's claret, or the grandmother's white — and the room sees her before she moves. The announcement, made. The entering, hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the retiring room — the last repair before the floor; the aunt's hands.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia draws her into the retiring room before the floor — the aunt's privilege, the last repair. "The candles are cruel, miss — the room wants one mending." Three on the tray: the violets, reset — faithfulness, the week's flower, pinned dried against the whispers; the mended gloves, changed — the week's pair, the mend honored; or the heirloom lace, eased — the grandmother's, the throat graced again.)*
> *(Rose touches the violets — reset, dried, faithfulness. The gloves wait, mended. The lace, eased. "The floor," she says, "wants the mistress entire." "Entire," Letitia says, pinning, "is the week's whole word, miss — the quartermaster only says so." She chooses the repair. In the glass: the mistress, mended.)*

scenes.synopsis: the entry — the manner executed; the room, met three ways.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she chose the open: she takes the floor early — the room walked as if the whispers were weather, heard, unhurried, unanswered, the mistress unbothered. If she chose the scene: she holds one moment for the room's eye — the laugh, placed; the turn, taken; the gossip given its better story. If she chose the quiet: she takes the dowager's wing — the supper room's corner, the evening's dignity, the whispers finding no purchase.)*
> *(In every entry the same law: she does not flinch. The room watches for the flinch the way the ton watches for everything — entire, unblinking — and she gives it nothing to watch. The entry, made. The manner, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the whispers — overheard; the branch's name, nearly said; the threat, gathering.
scenes.prose:
> *(She hears it in the card room's doorway — a voice, unnamed, the chorus at its work: "de Valcourt — wasn't that the name? The branch that fell?" And another voice, lower: "Hush — she'll hear." But she has heard, and the hearing is the whole of the threat: the old name, on the ton's tongue, the scandal's shape sniffed at in the open.)*
> *(She does not turn. She does not hurry. The whispers are weather, Octavia said, and she walks through them the way she walks through weather — unhurried, unanswering, the colors she chose catching the candles. Behind her the voices lower, and the room leans in, and the night tilts toward the breaking. The hearing, done. The threat, gathered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the answering ritual — mid-ball, the mistress re-dresses for the night's second half; the threat, answered.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, in the retiring room — "the book's with me, miss. The night's line is written when you say.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the retiring-room door — "the room is still turning, Rose. Turn it back.")*
> *(Story morsel: Augusta, from the wing — "unhurried, child. The room watches for the hurry.")*
> *(Story morsel: Élise's word, sent with the gown — "the extra stitch held, miss. All night, for Friday.")*
> *(Story morsel: Julian, from the supper room — "one dance, Rose. The house can spare you one.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: Friday night — the ball's second half; the room has whispered, and the mistress answers. Nothing theatrical and nothing forced. Re-dress for the answering: the night's colors, worn with patience. Heard. Unhurried. Entire. The woman who does not flinch is not pried open.

scenes.synopsis: the return — the answering dress re-enters the room; the line, held.
scenes.prose:
> *(She comes back through the retiring-room door, and the room turns again — the answering dress, the night's colors, the mistress entire. The whispers find the same woman they left: heard, unhurried, unanswered. Whatever the direction — the branch's blue and silver, the house's claret, the grandmother's white — it is worn the way a house is worn: entire.)*
> *(She takes the floor's edge, and the candles find her, and the room does the arithmetic it does on every woman who refuses to flinch. Let it. The returning, owned. The line, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dance — the quadrille; Laurent devoted; the romantic center, holding.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent claims the first dance as promised — the quadrille, the floor's whole Friday turning around them. He dances the way he does everything: entire, devoted — the guest's philosophy in his shoulders, the evening's center holding. "You are enjoying yourself," she says, surprised to find it nearly true. "I am with you," he says, "which is the same thing.")*
> *(They turn through the figures, and the room watches, and the whispers must wait for the music to end. For the length of the dance the night is simple: a man who asks nothing and loves her anyway, a woman who knows everything and dances anyway. The figures, turned. The center, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the toast, cut short — the scandal threatens to break; she does not flinch.
scenes.prose:
> *(It happens at supper — a voice, unnamed, the chorus at its boldest, a glass raised high: "To old families — and the paper they keep!" The room turns. The name is on every tongue and not yet said — the de Valcourt name, the branch, the old sin's shape hanging in the candlelight. The scandal leans toward the breaking.)*
> *(She does not flinch. She raises her own glass — to the room, to the night, to nothing in particular — and drinks, unhurried, and the moment passes the way weather passes: the voice falters, the toast dissolves into the general clinking, the name goes unsaid. The household holds its line around her — Augusta's wing, Julian's shoulder, Octavia's eye — and the room, denied its breaking, turns back to its supper. The threatening, weathered. The breaking, declined.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE NIGHT'S END: leave at the height, stay till the last dance, or leave early with the household.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the supper room's corner with the night past midnight — the toast weathered, the scandal unbroken, the room turning back to its pleasures — and the question of the ending runs alongside the question of the night. The household has held the line; Laurent is waiting for the last dances; the Lash's Saturday number is already being set in type. The house must decide how the mistress ends the ball.)*
> *(Leave at the height: go now, the night's triumph entire, the room left wanting — the resolve of it, the leaving as the last word, the risk that the early going is read as the retreat. Stay till the last dance: dance it with Laurent, close the ball the way she opened it — the candor of it, the night entire, the risk that the late hours bring the whispers back. Or leave early with the household: gather them all — the dowager, the brother, the aunt, the guest — and go home together, the house entire — the mercy of it, the holding closed as one, the risk that the leaving looks like the hiding.)*
> *(The night ends where she sends it — at the height, at the last dance, or in the gathering. If at the height: she takes her leave with the room watching, and the triumph goes home with her. If at the last dance: she dances it with Laurent, and the ball closes the way it opened — entire. If gathered: the household is collected — the dowager, the brother, the aunt, the guest — and they go home together, the house entire. Whatever the ending became, one law holds it entire: the night was hers to end, and she chose the ending. The choosing is done.)*
