scenes.synopsis: the sting — the Lash's Friday-night provocation; the scandal threatens; Bell's Gazette prints nothing.
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting is the Lash's Friday-night sheet, brought to the supper room by a runner — Pounce's late edition, the gutter's eye on the ball.)*
> *(Rose reads it in the cloak room, and finds the provocation in it — the threat, printed. It names no sums, no names — only the shape, sniffed at, and the promise of Saturday. And Bell's Gazette carries no paragraph Friday night — the proprietor's paper clean, alert, unbought. She folds the Lash and gives it to Octavia for the memorandum book. The paper smells of ink. The night smells of rain.)*
scenes.sting: the sting — the Lash's Friday-night provocation; the scandal threatens; Bell's Gazette prints nothing.

scenes.synopsis: the night's wrap — the cloak room; the ball, unpinned; the aunt's hands.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia meets her in the cloak room with the night's last question, the aunt's hands on the unpinning. "The ball has had its hours, miss — the wrap wants the woman." Three on the peg: the evening cloak, claret-lined — deep, the week's color, worn home; the ivory shawl — the grandmother's, quiet, the dignity kept; or the grey mantle — the reader's, the ledger's color, the night logged and closed.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret-lined — deep, the week's own, worn home. The shawl waits, quiet. The mantle, sober. "The wrap," she says, "wants the house." "The house," Letitia says, fastening, "is going home, miss — the quartermaster only says so." She chooses the night's wrap. In the glass: the mistress, unwound.)*

scenes.synopsis: the execution — the leaving, three ways; the night, ended.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she left at the height: she takes her leave with the room watching — the curtsey, the dowager's nod, the triumph going home with her. If she stayed till the last dance: she dances it with Laurent, and the ball closes the way it opened — entire, the floor's last turning hers. If she gathered the household: they are collected — Augusta, Julian, Octavia, Letitia, Laurent — and they go out together, the house entire.)*
> *(In every leaving the same law: the night was hers to end, and she ends it. The carriages are called. The doors close behind them. The ending, executed. The ball, done.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dispersing — London empties; the carriages; the night, spent.
scenes.prose:
> *(London empties around the carriages — the ton dispersing into its coaches, the ball's whole Friday dissolving into the wet streets. The household boards in the order it came: Augusta in the first, Rose in the second with Letitia and the book, the rest behind. The lamps are lit. The horses steam.)*
> *(She looks back once at the doors — shut now, the candles still burning inside for nobody — and the night sits behind her like a guest she has seen out. The dispersing, watched. The night, spent.)*

scenes.synopsis: the ride home — Laurent beside her; devotion, to the last.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent rides in the second carriage — the guest's privilege, the night's own logic — and sits beside her in the lamplight, devoted to the last. "A triumph," he says. "You were magnificent, and the room knew it. I am very proud to have danced the first with you.")*
> *(She thanks him, and the thanks are true, and the lamplight is kind, and for a stretch of the wet streets the night is only a night — a ball, a dance, a man who loves her and knows nothing. She holds the silence the way she held the room: entire. The riding, shared. The devotion, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the question — late, in the carriage, Laurent asks what she cannot answer.
scenes.prose: > *(The carriage is late and dark, the town house near — and Laurent turns to her in the lamplight, the night's kindness still on him, and asks the question the whole evening was circling: "Rose — what did they mean tonight? The whispers — your family — the name they would not say. Tell me, and I will carry it with you, whatever it is." She looks at him, and the answer is in her and cannot come out, and the carriage lamps light her silence.)*

scenes.synopsis: Saturday's dawn — the carriage question, carried overnight; the day's one office: the answer.
scenes.prose:
> *(She wakes before the maid, the way the week has trained her, and the first thing in the room is last night's question, sitting where the carriage lamps left it. "Tell me," he said, "and I will carry it with you, whatever it is." She lay awake after with the words for company, and they were poor company, and honest.)*
> *(Saturday has one office written across it in her own hand, and it is not the household's, and it is not the papers'. The answer. She dresses in the blue dark, takes up the mended gloves, and goes down to a house that does not yet know what the day will cost it. The morning, entered. The answering, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: the morning's face — dressing for the telling; the archive's Saturday answer.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia comes with Saturday's question, the aunt's eye on the day's office. "The telling wants the mistress dressed for it, miss — not the ball's, not the road's. The Saturday face." Three on the stand: the archive claret — the house's color, the week's own, worn to the answering; the grey silk — the reader's, the ledger's color, worn to the business of it; or the ivory, plain — the grandmother's, quiet, worn to the mercy of it.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret — the house's, the week's own color. The grey waits, sober. The ivory, quiet. "The telling," she says, "wants the house under it." "The house," Letitia says, fastening, "is under everything, miss — the quartermaster only says so." She chooses the morning's face. In the glass: the mistress, answered.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the house's color; the week's own, worn to the answering.

fashionChoices.detail: the reader's; the ledger's color, worn to the business.

fashionChoices.detail: the grandmother's; quiet, worn to the mercy.

scenes.synopsis: the keeping, visited — the papers sit as the week chose; Saturday, London.
scenes.prose:
> *(She stops at the town house study before the day begins, because the day's first office is the papers, and the telling will want them to hand. If they were moved: the box sits in Harrow's keeping under her seal and Harrow's hand, the Park keeping its own — the telling goes without the pages, and the pages keep. If they were guarded: the bolt on the Park study door, the wax holding, Amos's rotations on the stair — the telling goes on her word alone, and her word is the ledger's. If they were split: the box sealed on the Park shelf, the packet in Octavia's reticule, here in London — the telling has its proof in the house, and the proof stays shut unless she opens it.)*
> *(Whatever the keeping, the law holds: the papers are where the week sent them, and the telling is hers to shape. She shuts the study door. The keeping, kept. The day, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: the book's Saturday order — the quartermaster reads the day; the letter, sealed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia reads the book's Saturday order at breakfast, pencil behind her ear, the quartermaster's Saturday voice on: the town house quiet, no callers before noon, the staff's order, the evening plain. The household takes it entire. The comedy is not attempted, and Saturday does not miss it.)*
> *(Behind the book's false back the letter sits sealed, untouched, unasked-for — the thirty years in it, undisturbed. Letitia's hand rests a moment on the cover, and Rose sees it, and says nothing. Some doors are not Rose's to open, and Saturday is not the day for doors. The book, shut. The letter, left.)*

scenes.synopsis: the ledger's texture — the entries, sparse; no total written.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia brings the memorandum book to the morning room, and the ledger's texture comes with it — the entries copied fair, the sums sparse, the columns honest. De la Roche: nine hundred pounds, entered in Elias's hand. De Brissac: fourteen hundred, the ink darker. The de Varenne entry, the sum entered fair beside the name — and no total anywhere on the page, because Octavia has not written one.)*
> *("The shape is enough for Saturday," Octavia says, shutting the book. "A man can hear the shape. The sums can wait for the week. Tell him what was done, Rose. Leave the arithmetic its own hour." The counsel, precise. The texture, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the town house Saturday — breakfast; the household entire; Friday, carried.
scenes.prose:
> *(The town house breakfasts late on Saturday — the household entire, the night's arithmetic carried in daylight. Henry exhibits the copybook's Saturday page with both hands, the letters even, the lines straight, permitted the town house and the table. "Very good," Rose says, and means it entirely.)*
> *(If she met the room openly: the staff moves easy, the night's weather walked through. If she cut it with a scene: the laugh is remembered in the kitchen, retold. If she withdrew: the dowager's wing is spoken of with approval. If she told the household nothing: the staff knows only the order, and the order is enough. If she told them enough: the footmen watch the street without being told why. If she kept them close: the house moves quiet, and nobody asks. And however the night ended — at the height, at the last dance, or gathered — the house carries it the same way: entire. The breakfast, taken. The Friday, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel on telling — candor's cost; what the telling does to a man.
scenes.prose:
> *("Say it plainly," Octavia says, "because he asked for plainly, and because anything else is a second sin laid on the first. But Rose —" the precision pauses, which is rare — "plainly is not gently, and you should know which you are choosing before you open your mouth. He will hear his grandfather's ruin in your grandfather's hand. That is not information. That is an inheritance.")*
> *("And if it breaks him?" Rose asks. "Then he breaks," Octavia says, "and you will know it was the truth that did it, not the telling. The telling is the only part that is yours." She opens the memorandum book, and shuts it again, and does not write. The counsel, given. The part, assigned.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's Saturday word — the branch fell, and no more; the telling is not hers.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends for her at ten — the London drawing room, the chocolate, Saturday's own counsel. "You have the look," she says, "of a woman with a letter to write. Write it, or don't — but do not bring it to me, child. The branch fell. I have had thirty years to make my peace with the falling, and I will not have it unburied for the ton's amusement.")*
> *("It is not for the ton," Rose says. "Then it is for the guest," Augusta says, "and that is your business, not mine. A dowager's counsel, free: tell him the shape, keep the sums, and do not apologize for the blood. The blood is not yours to apologize for." She drinks. The chocolate, drunk. The door, closed on the branch.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE TELLING: all at once, gently in pieces, or written down.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the morning room with Saturday's whole weight on the table — the ledger's texture, the carriage's question, the guest waiting somewhere in the house — and the question of the telling runs alongside the question of the day. The truth is entire and it is hers to give; the only question is the manner of the giving. The house must decide how the mistress tells it.)*
> *(All at once: say it entire, in the morning room, the ledger's shape whole — the candor of it, the shock unbuffered, the risk that the plain arrives as the brutal. Gently, in pieces: give it in portions, let him set the pace, stop when he needs — the mercy of it, the easing, the risk that the gentle is read as the evasive. Or written down: the account fair-copied, given into his hands, read at his own hour — the cunning of it, the distance, the risk that the handing is read as the hiding.)*
> *(The telling goes where she sends it — into the plain, into the pieces, or into the hand. If plain: the morning room, the whole shape, the shock unbuffered and the honesty entire. If eased: the portions, his pace, the stopping and starting, the mercy of the slowness. If handed: the fair copy, the sealed packet, his own hour to read it. Whatever the telling became, one law holds it entire: the truth was hers to give, and she chose the giving. The choosing is done.)*

options.label: All at once
options.detail: *Candor+; the telling, plain.* Say it entire, in the morning room; the ledger's shape, whole. *(Plain — and the brutal, risked.)*

options.label: Gently, in pieces
options.detail: *Mercy+; the telling, eased.* Portions, at his pace; stop when he needs. *(Eased — and the evasion, suggested.)*

options.label: Written down
options.detail: *Cunning+; the telling, handed.* The account fair-copied; his own hour, his own reading. *(Handed — and the hiding, risked.)*

scenes.synopsis: the execution — the telling prepared three ways; the answer, readied.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she chose the plain: she goes over the shape once, entire — the funds, the collapse, the covering — and sets it in order in her head the way she sets a column. If she chose the pieces: she divides it — the mechanism first, the names after, the line last — and marks where she will stop if he needs. If she chose the hand: she fair-copies the account, seals the packet, and writes his name on it in her own hand.)*
> *(In every telling the same law: the truth is prepared before he enters the room, because a truth prepared in the room is a truth the room prepared. She stands at the window and watches the square. The preparation, done. The answering, readied.)*

scenes.synopsis: the telling dress — what she wears to the answer; Friday's colors, carried.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at eleven with the telling's question, the atelier's eye on the day's office. "The telling wants its dress, miss — not the morning's, the answer's." Three on the stand, and Friday's colors run through them: the de Valcourt blue, worn open — the branch's colors, the naming answered with the wearing; the archive claret, steady — the house's, the estate entire; or the ivory, quiet — the grandmother's, nothing insisted.)*
> *(Rose touches the blue — open, the branch's, worn where he can see it. The claret waits, steady. The ivory, quiet. "The answer," she says, "wants no hiding in it." "No hiding," Élise says, fastening, "is the atelier's whole doctrine, miss — the house only says so." She chooses the telling's dress. In the glass: the mistress, unhidden.)*

scenes.synopsis: the asking — she asks him to the morning room; the question, met.
scenes.prose:
> *(She finds him in the library at half past eleven, the guest's Saturday at its ease — a book open, the morning's whole philosophy in his shoulders. "Laurent," she says, and the name costs her something, and he hears it. If she told him Sunday: "Sunday I gave you the shape. Today I will give you the weight — all of it, plainly, the why with the what. Come to the morning room with me." If she did not: "Last night you asked me what the whispers meant. Come to the morning room with me. I will tell you — all of it, plainly, as you asked.")*
> *(If she told him Sunday: the shape he has carried all week takes its full weight — Friday's whispers gave it a name, and today gives it the why. If she did not: the shape arrives entire, first-heard, and the library's ease goes out of his shoulders like a lamp going out. He rises. He comes. The asking, made. The answering, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: the telling, first — the mechanism; the funds, the collapse, Hartwell first.
scenes.prose:
> *("A generation ago," she says, "in the war years, French families put their money into my grandfather's hands. Émigré money — for safekeeping, while the war ran its course. Your family among them." She says it plainly, because he asked for plainly, and the plain is the only mercy she has. "He did not keep it safe. He played the funds with it — Nantes, Lisbon, Cadiz, the ventures in his ledger — and the funds collapsed.")*
> *(Laurent is very still. "And then?" he says. "Then," she says, "he made Hartwell whole first. The estate, the name, the interest — covered, entire. And the rest — the entrusted money, your family's among it — was left to look to better times." She stops, because the plain has a limit, and the limit is his face. "Better times," he says, "did not come." "No," she says. "They did not." The mechanism, told. The stillness, entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: the line — Elias's hand, spoken aloud; the de Varenne entry; the names.
scenes.prose:
> *(She speaks the line then, because the telling wants the grandfather's own words in it — the tall E, the impatient crossings, the brown ink. "The Hartwell interest is made whole. The rest must look to better times." It sits in the morning room like a stone. "That is his hand," she says. "That is the covering, written down fair.")*
> *(And the names, because the plain wants them: de Varenne — his family's entry, the sum entered fair beside the name, the ruin ledgered. De Valcourt — the banking branch, fallen. De la Roche, nine hundred pounds. De Brissac, fourteen hundred. She does not total them; the shape is Saturday's business, and the arithmetic keeps its own hour. The line, spoken. The names, named.)*

scenes.synopsis: the devastation — grief and fury in one body; not cruelty toward her.
scenes.prose:
> *(He stands, and goes to the window, and stands there a long time with his back to her — and what comes off him in the morning room's quiet is not one thing but two, held in the same body: grief, for the grandfather whose ruin was never respectable war-loss but a man's covering, the family honor spent to make another house whole; and fury, at Elias — at the waste, at the years, at the better times that never came. He does not turn the fury on her. Not once. His hands on the sill are white, and his voice, when it comes, is level.)*
> *("My grandfather," he says, "believed he had been ruined by history. He was ruined by a man." He turns then, and his face is devastated — the word is the only one — and entire. "I am not leaving, Rose. I said I would carry it, and I am still saying it. But do not ask me to be kind about him. Not today." The devastation, held. The staying, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: the walk's provision — the telling wants air; the pelisse, the gloves.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise finds her in the hall after, the atelier's eye on the devastation's aftermath. "The telling wants air, miss — the square's garden, the walk. The provision." Three on the peg: the claret pelisse — the house's color, the staying's own, worn against the wind; the grey walking dress — the reader's, the ledger's color, worn to the reckoning; or the ivory shawl — the grandmother's, quiet, the mercy kept close.)*
> *(Rose touches the pelisse — claret, the house's, the wind's answer. The grey waits. The shawl, quiet. "The walk," she says, "wants the house on it." "The house," Élise says, fastening, "is walking, miss — the atelier only says so." She chooses the provision. In the glass: the mistress, aired.)*

scenes.synopsis: the walk — the square's garden; his fury at Elias, held and spoken.
scenes.prose:
> *(The square's garden is Saturday-quiet, the gravel loud underfoot, the town held off by the railings. He walks fast at first, the fury walking with him, and speaks of Elias the way a man speaks of a thief he cannot prosecute — the covering, the better times, the thirty years of the house standing on it. "He wrote it down," Laurent says, "fair. As if the fairness of the hand excused the hand." The fury is held — white-knuckled, level-voiced — and it is all for the dead man. None of it touches her.)*
> *(She walks beside him, and does not defend the grandfather — there is no defense, and she will not invent one — and does not apologize for the blood, as Augusta counseled. The gravel, loud. The fury, walked. The dead man, unexcused.)*

scenes.synopsis: the grief — the de Varenne name; the grandfather; what was lost.
scenes.prose:
> *(The fury burns down to the grief as they turn the garden's second circuit — the way fires do, to the truer thing. He speaks of his grandfather then: the banker, the name, the ruin borne as history's verdict all his life, the family honor carried through the loss like a banner through rain. "He never knew," Laurent says. "He died believing the war took it. I have to decide what to do with knowing, and he never had to." His voice breaks once, and mends.)*
> *(She does not touch him — the grief has its own perimeter, and she will not cross it uninvited — but she slows, and walks the slower pace with him, and the garden holds them both. The banner, rained on. The knowing, his to carry now.)*

scenes.synopsis: the interval — the walk's end; the staying's cost, counted.
scenes.prose:
> *(They come back to the town house at one, and he goes up to his room without another word, emptied out and quiet — and she stands in the hall and counts the cost of the staying. He is devastated, and he stays, and the staying is not a triumph. It is a man holding grief and fury in one body and refusing to set either down at her door. That is what she asked him to carry. She does not un-ask it.)*
> *(Letitia passes with the household book, and sees her face, and does not ask — the quartermaster's mercy, entire. The hall, quiet. The cost, counted. The staying, his.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — HIS ANSWER: stay and fight, stay and grieve, or time that is not leaving.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the morning room at two, the devastation's morning behind her and the afternoon ahead — and the question of his answer runs alongside the question of the day. He stays; that is his. But what she asks of the staying is hers: whether she asks him to fight beside her, or holds the grief with him untimed, or grants him the hour he needs to reckon. The house must decide what the mistress asks of the man who stayed.)*
> *(Stay and fight: ask him to stand beside her against the hunters — the sin faced together, the house and the guest lined as one — the resolve of it, the burden shared, the risk that the fighting asks too much of a devastated man. Stay and grieve: hold the grief with him, no demands, no timetable — the mercy of it, the devastation given its hour, the risk that the grieving becomes the dwelling. Or time that is not leaving: grant him his own time to reckon — apart, not gone, the door held open — the candor of it, the honesty of the needing, the risk that the time is read as the distance.)*
> *(The answer goes where she sends it — into the fighting, into the grieving, or into the granted hour. If fighting: she asks it of him plainly, and the house lines beside the guest. If grieving: she holds the hour with him, and asks nothing, and the devastation has its room. If granted: she gives him the time, and holds the door, and waits without hovering. Whatever the answer became, one law holds it entire: the staying was his, and what she asked of it was hers. The choosing is done.)*

scenes.synopsis: the brother's reading — the staying, witnessed; counsel, plain.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian finds her at three on the stair, his gloves in his hand, the brother's Saturday at its plainest. "He's upstairs," he says. "Not packing, before you ask. I checked the way brothers check — the valet's face." He almost smiles. "Whatever you told him, Rose, he's still here. That counts for more than you think.")*
> *("It cost him," she says. "Everything costs," Julian says. "The question is what it buys. You bought the truth told by the right person at the right hour. That's the most expensive thing in this house, and you paid it yourself." He squeezes her arm. "Let him come down when he comes down." The counsel, given. The brother, plain.)*

scenes.synopsis: the witness, placed — Harrow's Saturday, three ways.
scenes.prose:
> *(At four the day's thoughts turn to the witness, because the telling touched his half of the sin. If she hid him: his door shut at the Park, the lane unwalked, Harrow keeping his quiet behind it — the telling done without him, and the quiet kept for him. If she opened him: Harrow on the wall at the Park, the mason's courses rising past him, the schoolmaster entire in the Saturday light — the telling done in his sight-line, and the sight-line held. If she roaded him: Harrow under Quill's roof in London, the chaise's Thursday business done — and she writes him a note by the four o'clock post, telling him the guest has been told, and the keeping stands.)*
> *(In every keeping the same law: the witness is kept, and the telling does not spend him. She seals the thought, or the note, and goes back to the day. The witness, placed. The keeping, unbroken.)*

scenes.synopsis: the ledger, un-totaled — the sums keep their hour; the week, not the day.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes at five with the memorandum book, and the ledger's page is as Saturday left it — the entries fair, the sums sparse, no total written. "The week will want the arithmetic," Octavia says, "and the week shall have it. But not today. Today the shape did the work, and the shape was enough. A total is a weapon, Rose. Don't forge it till you need it.")*
> *("And the hunters?" Rose asks. "The hunters," Octavia says, "are counting something else — Pounce's Saturday number, Slade's second man, the money moving in London. Watch the spending, not the silence." She shuts the book. The pencil, capped. The total, unforged.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening's dress — re-dressing for dinner; the house, held.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at six with the evening's question, the atelier's eye on the devastation's aftermath. "The evening wants the mistress dressed for it, miss — not the telling's, the holding's." Three on the stand: the claret, evening — deep, the house's color, the staying worn to dinner; the archive blue — the estate's, severe, the wall's color worn to the table; or the ivory, layered — bright, the grandmother's, the house unruffled.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret — evening, deep, the house's own. The blue waits, severe. The ivory, bright. "The holding," she says, "wants the house under it." "The house," Élise says, pinning, "is under everything, miss — the atelier only says so." She chooses the evening's dress. In the glass: the mistress, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: dinner — the household entire; the unspoken, carried.
scenes.prose:
> *(Dinner is at seven, the household entire — Augusta at the head, Julian, Octavia, Letitia with the book beside her plate, Henry permitted the table for the Saturday, Laurent in his place, quieter than his custom and present entire. The unspoken sits at the table like a guest no one introduced, and the household carries it the way it carries everything: with good manners and better silence.)*
> *(The courses come and go. Nobody mentions the morning room. Nobody mentions the better times. Henry asks for more bread, and is given it, and the ordinary saves the evening the way the ordinary always does. The dinner, taken. The unspoken, carried.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager at dinner — the branch, fallen, and no more; the silence, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta holds the table the way she holds everything — entire, unhurried, the dowager's Saturday at its ease. Once, when the talk turns to old families, her eye finds Rose's across the candles — the branch, fallen, acknowledged between them and no further. She does not ask what the morning room heard. She does not need to. The branch fell, and that is the whole of what she carries, and she carries it the way she carries everything: upright.)*
> *(After the sweet, she touches Rose's hand in passing — one touch, the dowager's whole vocabulary in it. The candles, low. The silence, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: after dinner — the quiet; the staying, begun to cost; his steadiness.
scenes.prose:
> *(After dinner he comes to the drawing room, because the staying means being in the rooms, not only in the house — and sits, and takes the coffee, and is quiet in the particular way of a man holding two things at once. When Henry shows him the copybook's Saturday page, he looks at it properly, both hands, the way Rose does. "Very good," he says, and means it. The devastation has not unmade his manners. It has only made them cost more.)*
> *(She watches him across the room, and the watching is its own ache — the man she loves, grieving in her house, for a ruin her house made. He catches her eye, and does not look away. The quiet, shared. The cost, showing.)*

scenes.synopsis: the ledger line again — what she owes; Sunday ahead.
scenes.prose:
> *(She steps out to the hall between the drawing room's hours, and the ledger's line comes back to her uninvited — the tall E, the brown ink. The Hartwell interest is made whole. She thinks of what the week has cost to learn it, and what the learning obliges: the sums un-totaled, the hunters circling, the man downstairs carrying her grandfather's sin like a stone in his shoe. Sunday is ahead, and the week after, and the reckoning the week has been walking toward.)*
> *(But tonight is Saturday, and the house is holding, and the staying is the whole of the business. She goes back in. The line, remembered. The owing, hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night's hand — the retiring room's repair; the letter, still sealed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia draws her into the retiring room at nine — the aunt's privilege, the night's repair before the ritual. "The evening has had its hours, miss — the hand wants the woman." Three on the tray: the mended gloves, changed — the week's pair, the mend honored, worn to the staying; the silver rose pin, plain — the house's mark, worn quiet; or the violets, reset — faithfulness, pinned dried against the night.)*
> *(Rose touches the gloves — mended, the week's own, the mend honored. The pin waits, plain. The violets, dried. "The night," she says, "wants the house on it." "The house," Letitia says, pinning, "is on you, miss — the quartermaster only says so." Behind the book's false back, the letter sits sealed, untouched, unasked-for. She chooses the night's hand. In the glass: the mistress, mended.)*

scenes.synopsis: the staying ritual — Saturday night, the mistress re-dresses for the holding; the devastation, weathered.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, in the retiring room — "the book's with me, miss. The night's line is written when you say.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the retiring-room door — "the house is holding, Rose. Hold it back.")*
> *(Story morsel: Augusta, from the wing — "steady, child. The night watches for the tremble.")*
> *(Story morsel: Élise's word, sent with the gown — "the extra stitch held, miss. All night, for Saturday.")*
> *(Story morsel: Julian, from the supper room — "one evening, Rose. The house can spare you one.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: Saturday night — the answer given, the devastation weathered; the house dresses for the staying. Nothing brave and nothing brittle. Dress for the holding: the night's patience, worn plain. Heard. Steady. Entire. The woman who told the truth is not unraveled by it.

scenes.synopsis: the return — the ritual dress re-enters the night; the holding, worn.
scenes.prose:
> *(She comes back through the retiring-room door, and the night takes her the way it took her at the ball — the ritual dress, the staying's colors, the mistress entire. Whatever the direction — the watch's claret, the ledger's grey, the grandmother's ivory — it is worn the way a house is worn: entire. The devastation has had its day; the holding has its night.)*
> *(She takes the drawing room's edge, and the lamplight finds her, and the house does the arithmetic it does on every woman who told the truth and did not flinch from the telling. Let it. The returning, owned. The holding, worn.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE OFFERING: the papers, her word, or her silence and patience.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone at ten with the night's holding on her — the staying asked, the devastation weathered, the guest somewhere in the house with his grief — and the question of the offering runs alongside the question of the night. He stays; she has asked what she asks of it. Now: what she gives him for the carrying. The house must decide what the mistress offers the man who stayed.)*
> *(The papers: Elias's pages, the entries fair-copied, the whole truth in his hands to read at his own hour — the candor of it, the evidence given, the risk that the giving is read as the discharging. Her word: her promise that the house will answer for the sin — a vow, not evidence, spoken plain — the resolve of it, the binding, the risk that the vow outruns what she can yet do. Or her silence and patience: no demands on his answer, patience entire, the house quiet around him — the mercy of it, the waiting kept, the risk that the patience is read as the retreat.)*
> *(The offering goes where she sends it — into the papers, into the vow, or into the waiting. If the papers: the fair copy goes into his hands, and the reading is his, at his own hour. If the vow: she speaks it plain, and the house hears her, and the promise stands. If the waiting: she asks nothing, and the house keeps its quiet, and patience does the work. Whatever the offering became, one law holds it entire: the staying was his, and what she gave for it was hers. The choosing is done.)*

options.label: Her word
options.detail: *Resolve+; the vow, spoken.* The house will answer for the sin; a vow, not evidence. *(Spoken — and the outrunning, risked.)*

options.label: Her silence and patience
options.detail: *Mercy+; the waiting, kept.* No demands; patience, entire; the house, quiet. *(Kept — and the retreat, suggested.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening conversation — the offering, given; his receiving.
scenes.prose:
> *(She finds him in the morning room at half past ten — the room where the telling happened, the lamps low — and gives him what the night chose. If the papers: the fair copy, into his hands, and he takes it the way a man takes a weight he has already agreed to carry. If the vow: she speaks it — the house will answer for the sin — and he hears it all the way through before he answers. If the waiting: she tells him she asks nothing of him tonight, and the quiet does the offering's work.)*
> *("You told me," he says, "because I asked, and because it was yours to tell. In thirty years, nobody else's family told mine anything." He looks at the offering — the pages, or the vow, or the quiet — and nods once, slowly. "I am still here, Rose. That is the whole of my answer tonight." The offering, given. The receiving, entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: the execution — the offering, three ways; the night, settled.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she gave the papers: he keeps the fair copy, and the reading will be his, at his own hour — tonight, or tomorrow, or never entire. If she gave the vow: the promise stands in the morning room like a third person, and the house will have to keep it. If she gave the waiting: the night asks nothing of him, and he sits a while in the lamplight, and the quiet holds them both.)*
> *(In every offering the same law: what she gave was hers to give, and the staying remains his. They sit till the lamps burn low. The execution, done. The night, settled.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — the Lash's Saturday sheet; the shadow lengthens; Bell's Gazette prints nothing.
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting is the Lash's Saturday sheet, brought up with the evening post — Pounce's number, the gutter's eye on the town house.)*
> *(Rose reads it in the drawing room, and finds the threat in it — the lengthening, printed. It names no sums, no names — only the shape, sniffed at, and the promise of more. And Bell's Gazette carries no paragraph Saturday — the proprietor's paper clean, alert, unbought. She folds the Lash and gives it to Octavia for the memorandum book. The paper smells of ink. The night smells of rain.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night's wrap — the cloak room; the Saturday, unpinned; the aunt's hands.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia meets her in the cloak room at eleven with the night's last question, the aunt's hands on the unpinning. "The Saturday has had its hours, miss — the wrap wants the woman." Three on the peg: the evening cloak, claret-lined — deep, the week's color, the staying worn to the night; the ivory shawl — the grandmother's, quiet, the dignity kept; or the grey mantle — the reader's, the ledger's color, the day logged and closed.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret-lined — deep, the week's own, the staying's. The shawl waits, quiet. The mantle, sober. "The wrap," she says, "wants the house." "The house," Letitia says, fastening, "is abed soon, miss — the quartermaster only says so." She chooses the night's wrap. In the glass: the mistress, unwound.)*

scenes.synopsis: the house, quiet — the day, accounted; the telling, the staying, the offering.
scenes.prose:
> *(The town house settles at midnight — the staff's Saturday done, the lamps turned low, the book shut in Letitia's room with the letter still sealed behind its false back. She walks the hall once, the way she walked it Friday before the ball, and accounts the day: the telling, told; the devastation, weathered; the staying, his; the offering, given. The columns are hers, and they balance.)*
> *(She thinks of the Lash's Saturday number, folded in Octavia's book, and of Bell's clean sheet, and of the hunters' money moving somewhere in London's dark. Tomorrow is Sunday. Tonight was Saturday, and Saturday held. The hall, walked. The day, accounted.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dispersing — the house to bed; the lamps, lit; the night, spent.
scenes.prose:
> *(The household disperses to bed — Augusta's door shut, Julian's lamp still burning, Octavia's pencil capped at last, Letitia's book closed, Henry long abed with the copybook on the chair. The town house keeps its Saturday the way it keeps everything: entire, unruffled, London-quiet.)*
> *(She stands at the stair's foot a moment, and the house is the house — the staying in it, the devastation weathered in it, the night spent honest. The lamps, lit. The dispersing, watched.)*

scenes.synopsis: the late hour — the stair's foot; the dark; the hand, reaching.
scenes.prose:
> *(He comes down at half past twelve — not to leave, the hour being far past leaving, but to the stair's foot, where she stands with the night's last of the lamplight. The house is dark around them, the devastation's day behind them, and for a moment neither speaks — the quiet they have earned, or been given, or taken.)*
> *("Rose," he says — just the name, the way Letitia says it when the book is too full — and in the dark his hand finds hers. The reaching, made. The dark, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the hand — found, and not let go; the staying, sealed.
scenes.prose: > *(Late, and the house dark, and the lamps low — and Laurent's hand finds Rose's in the dark at the stair's foot, and does not let go. The devastation's day is behind them. The staying is ahead, unpriced and entire. His hand holds hers, and the dark keeps its counsel.)*

scenes.synopsis: Sunday's dawn — the hand, relinquished with the morning; the day's one office: the arithmetic.
scenes.prose:
> *(Sunday wakes her the way Saturday left her — before the maid, the room grey, his hand no longer in hers. She let it go at dawn, when the house began to stir; the staying stands without it. The dark kept its counsel, as promised, and the morning keeps its own: the arithmetic, the library, Octavia's pencils laid in a row like a muster.)*
> *(Sunday has one office written across it in her own hand, and it is not the household's, though the household will keep the Sabbath entire. The reckoning. The papers are waiting in the library where Saturday left them, and the sums are sparse, and the columns are honest, and somewhere in them — Octavia says — a total is hiding, the way a splinter hides in a thumb. She dresses in the blue dark, takes up the mended gloves, and goes down. The morning, entered. The counting, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: the morning's face — dressing for the reckoning; the archive's Sunday answer.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia comes with Sunday's question, the aunt's eye on the day's office. "The reckoning wants the mistress dressed for it, miss — not the ball's, not the road's. The Sabbath face." Three on the stand: the archive grey — the reader's, the ledger's color, the counting's own; the claret — the house's, Sabbath-dressed, the reckoning faced in full; or the ivory, plain — the grandmother's, quiet, worn to the patience of it.)*
> *(Rose touches the grey — sober, the ledger's, the day's own color. The claret waits. The ivory, quiet. "The counting," she says, "wants no ceremony in it." "No ceremony," Letitia says, fastening, "is the aunt's whole doctrine, miss — the quartermaster only says so." She chooses the Sabbath's face. In the glass: the mistress, numbered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the town house Sunday — breakfast; the Sabbath order; the household to church.
scenes.prose:
> *(The town house breakfasts at nine on Sunday — the household entire, the Sabbath's own order in Letitia's book: church at eleven, no callers, the staff's Sunday, the kitchen's cold collation at two. Augusta takes the head of the table in her Sunday black, Julian with the week's paper folded small, Henry permitted the table with the copybook's Sunday page exhibited and praised.)*
> *(Rose announces it over the toast — she will keep the house; the books want their Sunday in the library, and Octavia with them. Augusta lifts one eyebrow, which is the dowager's whole sermon on the subject, and Julian says "The Sabbath was made for ledgers," which is the brother's. The household takes it entire. Church at eleven. The reckoning at noon.)*

scenes.synopsis: the library, arranged — the papers, the memorandum book, the pencils; the day's terms.
scenes.prose:
> *(The library at noon is Sunday-quiet — the household gone to church, the staff's order done, the house holding its breath the way it does when the mistress has announced an office. Octavia has laid it out the way a surgeon lays instruments: the papers in their order, the memorandum book open, the pencils in a row, the ink fresh.)*
> *("The whole of the day," Octavia says, "and no interruptions. Church till one, collation at two, dinner at seven. The arithmetic has its hours, and the hours are fenced." She caps the pencil she isn't using. "Rose — before we begin. The reckoning will have an audience, or it won't. You should decide that first." The question, placed. The instruments, waiting.)*

scenes.synopsis: Octavia's question — the reckoning's audience; the three ways of carrying it.
scenes.prose:
> *("The household entire," Octavia says, "means Augusta hears a sum, and Julian, and Letitia, and the staff hears it by supper. The number will be the house's by nightfall — which is honest, and which is a leak you cannot close." She turns the memorandum book toward Rose, the page still blank of totals.)*
> *("Or the three of us," Octavia says. "You, me, and Laurent — the heir, the accountant, and the man whose family was ruined. He has a right to the arithmetic that the household doesn't. Or —" and the precision pauses — "you alone. The number lives in one head till the week wants it." The audiences, three. The choosing, hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE AUDIENCE: publish the reckoning, keep it to Rose, or keep it between the three of them.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the library with Sunday's whole weight on the table — the papers in their order, the pencils in a row, the blank page where the total will go — and the question of the audience runs alongside the question of the day. The reckoning will be computed; the only question is who carries it when it's done. The house must decide how the mistress bounds it.)*
> *(Publish it: the household entire hears the sum — Augusta, Julian, Letitia, the staff by supper — the candor of it, the house carrying the weight together, the risk that the telling spreads beyond the walls. Keep it to herself: the number lives in one head — the cunning of it, the reckoning weaponed, the risk that the holding alone becomes the hiding. Or the three of them: Rose, Octavia, Laurent — the heir, the accountant, the wronged — the mercy of it, his right honored, the risk that the rest of the house is shut out of its own reckoning.)*
> *(The audience goes where she sends it — into the house, into the one head, or into the three. If the house: the sum is spoken at dinner, and the staff hears it by supper, and the number belongs to everyone. If the one: the page stays shut, and the total lives behind her eyes, and no one knows. If the three: Laurent is sent for at two, and the library's door closes on the reckoning's own. Whatever the audience became, one law holds it entire: the counting was hers to bound, and she chose the bounding. The choosing is done.)*

options.detail: *Candor+; the reckoning, spoken.* Augusta, Julian, Letitia — the house entire; the sum, carried together. *(Spoken — and the spreading, risked.)*

options.label: Keep it to Rose
options.detail: *Cunning+; the number, held.* One head; the reckoning, hers alone till the week wants it. *(Held — and the hiding, suggested.)*

options.label: Keep it between the three of them
options.detail: *Mercy+; the reckoning, shared.* Rose, Octavia, Laurent — the heir, the accountant, the wronged. *(Shared — and the shutting-out, risked.)*

scenes.synopsis: the entries, begun — de la Roche, nine hundred pounds; the day's first arithmetic.
scenes.prose:
> *(If the three: Laurent is sent for at two, and comes, and the library's door shuts on the reckoning's own. If the house: the counting goes on with the dinner's telling ahead of it. If the one: the page is hers, and the pencils hers, and Octavia works beside her knowing she will not see the total till Rose writes it.)*
> *(In every audience the same law: the entries come first, fair and sparse, before any total. De la Roche: nine hundred pounds, in Elias's hand, the tall E on the entry like a signature on a theft. Octavia copies it into the memorandum book, and the pencil's sound is the day's first arithmetic. The entry, booked. The counting, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel — what a total is for; the weapon, forged in daylight.
scenes.prose:
> *("A total is a weapon," Octavia says, "and yesterday I told you not to forge it till you needed it. Today you need it — the week will want the arithmetic, and the week shall have it. But know what you're forging, Rose. A total doesn't pay anyone. It only tells you the size of the owing, so the owing can be faced plainly instead of only felt.")*
> *("And if the size breaks us?" Rose asks. "Then it breaks us honestly," Octavia says, "which is the only kind of breaking this house has left." She turns the page. The counsel, given. The forging, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: the de Valcourt promise — £2,800, already promised; the entry, read.
scenes.prose:
> *(The de Valcourt entry comes at half past two — the banking branch, fallen, and beside the name a sum already promised: two thousand eight hundred pounds, entered in Octavia's fair hand from the week's own papers. "Already promised," Octavia says. "Before the counting. It stands outside the arithmetic — a debt acknowledged, not a sum to find.")*
> *(Laurent reads the entry over her shoulder — if he is of the audience; if he is not, the entry waits in the book for his hour — and is quiet a long moment. "Two thousand eight hundred," he says at last. "My family knew nothing of it." "They will," Rose says. The promise, booked. The branch, entered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the walk's provision — the counting wants air; the Sabbath's walk.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at three with the walk's question, the atelier's eye on the library's hours. "The counting wants air, miss — the square's garden, the Sabbath's walk. The provision." Three on the peg: the grey walking dress — the reader's, the ledger's color, the reckoning walked; the claret pelisse — the house's, the Sabbath's own, worn against the wind; or the ivory shawl — the grandmother's, quiet, the patience kept close.)*
> *(Rose touches the grey — the ledger's, the day's own color, the counting's. The pelisse waits. The shawl, quiet. "The walk," she says, "wants the reckoning on it." "The reckoning," Élise says, fastening, "is walking, miss — the atelier only says so." She chooses the provision. In the glass: the mistress, aired.)*

scenes.synopsis: the walk — the square's garden, Sunday; the de Valcourt name, carried.
scenes.prose:
> *(The square's garden is Sunday-quiet, the gravel loud underfoot, the Sabbath holding the town off behind the railings. He walks slower than yesterday — the fury walked out of him, the grief settled into the pace. "De Valcourt," he says. "The banking branch. My grandfather's correspondents — the name was in his letters. Two thousand eight hundred pounds, promised." He stops at the garden's turn. "To whom, Rose? The branch fell. Who is left to pay?")*
> *("The promise stands to the name," she says, "and Octavia will find who holds it. That is the accountant's office, and she does not lose things." She walks beside him, and does not hurry him past the question. The gravel, loud. The name, carried.)*

scenes.synopsis: the entries, continued — de Brissac, £1,400; the canal's ten years, reckoned.
scenes.prose:
> *(Back in the library at four, the entries continue — de Brissac: fourteen hundred pounds, the ink darker, the hand hurried. "He was in a hurry that year," Octavia says, "or past caring about the fairness of the hand." The entry goes into the memorandum book beside de la Roche's nine hundred, and the columns begin to look like what they are: a list of the ruined, priced.)*
> *(And then the canal — the revenue, the steady one, the Hartwell interest's own artery. "Three thousand a year," Octavia says, "for ten years. Thirty thousand pounds, if the canal runs as it runs." She writes the figures in the margin, and the margin holds them. The years, counted. The artery, priced.)*

scenes.synopsis: the brother's reading — the ten years; what the reckoning forbids.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian finds her at half past four in the hall, his Sunday at its plainest. If the reckoning is the household's: "Thirty thousand pounds of canal," he says, naming the sum like a man naming a price at market. If it is not: "The canal's years," he says, naming the shape — the walls have ears, and the shape was always going to travel.)*
> *("Ten years, Rose," he says. "That's the Park's improvements, the garden's wall, the tenants' roofs — ten years of the estate standing still while the canal pays for the past." "The estate can stand still," she says. "Can it?" Julian says. "Still is a direction too, sister — make sure it's the one you're choosing." He squeezes her arm. The reading, given. The brother, plain.)*

scenes.synopsis: the afternoon's change — the house's afternoon; the reckoning, faced.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at five with the afternoon's question, the atelier's eye on the reckoning's hours. "The afternoon wants the mistress changed for it, miss — not the walk's, the house's." Three on the stand: the claret — the house's color, Sabbath-dressed, the reckoning faced in full; the archive blue — severe, the estate's, the wall's color worn to the counting; or the ivory, bright — the grandmother's, the patience kept plain.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret — the house's, the Sabbath's own. The blue waits, severe. The ivory, bright. "The afternoon," she says, "wants the house under it." "The house," Élise says, fastening, "is under the day, miss — the atelier only says so." She chooses the afternoon's face. In the glass: the mistress, entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: the surplus — £8,800, immediate; the sum that can be touched.
scenes.prose:
> *(The surplus comes at half past five — the fortune's own, the year's spare, counted fair. "Eight thousand eight hundred," Octavia says, "immediately. From the surplus, not the estate's running. It is there, Rose. It can be moved on Sunday, or Monday, or never — but it is there, and the reckoning knows it.")*
> *(Rose looks at the figure, and the figure looks back — the most immediate of the sums, the one that can be touched. "And if it's moved," she says, "the house runs tighter." "The house," Octavia says, "has run tighter." The surplus, counted. The touching, priced.)*

scenes.synopsis: the total — £41,600; the number lands for the first time.
scenes.prose:
> *(At six Octavia does the adding — the pencil moving down the memorandum book's Sunday page, the columns closing one by one. The de Valcourt promise: two thousand eight hundred, standing outside the finding. The surplus: eight thousand eight hundred, immediate. The canal's ten years: three thousand a year, thirty thousand. She writes the figures in the margin, draws the line, and adds.)*
> *(The pencil stops. Octavia looks at the sum a long moment before she says it aloud, the way a woman looks at a door before she opens it. "Forty-one thousand six hundred pounds." The number sits in the library like an uninvited creditor. The reckoning, summed. The sin, priced.)*

scenes.synopsis: the absorbing — the number, carried to him; his family's share, priced.
scenes.prose:
> *(She finds him in the morning room at half past six — if he is of the audience, the number is already his, and they sit with what it means. If the household heard it at dinner, the sum sits between them unspoken, and the unspoken is enough. If she chose the one head, she keeps the number behind her eyes — and tells him only that the counting is done, the owing has a size, and the size has an hour coming.)*
> *(He is quiet a long time. If he knows it: "Ten years of canal," he says at last. "And the surplus. And the de Valcourts' promise." He turns it over the way a man turns a stone. "It is honest, Rose. That is the worst of it — there is nothing in it to argue with." If he does not: "The shape I have," he says. "The size can wait its hour. It is yours to carry, Rose — and I am still beside you." The reckoning, absorbed. The arguing, declined.)*

scenes.synopsis: the family's arithmetic — his answer to the number; what he will and will not take.
scenes.prose:
> *(If he knows the number: "It is my family's money in those columns," he says. "De Varenne — the sum entered fair beside the name. I have spent a day hearing how my grandfather was ruined by a man, and now I am told the price of the un-ruining." He looks at her straight. "I will not take a penny of it for myself, Rose. The de Valcourt promise, the canal years — let them go to the names in the book. My family's share can stand last in the line.")*
> *(If he does not: "It is my family's money in those columns," he says, "and I have spent a day hearing how my grandfather was ruined by a man. When the week wants the number, I will hear it — from you, at your hour. I will not take a penny of what is owed my family for myself, Rose. Let it go to the names in the book.")*
> *("It won't stand last," she says. "The book doesn't line them that way." "Then the book," he says, "is more honest than I am." He almost smiles, and the almost is the whole of Sunday's mercy. The arithmetic, answered. The family, priced.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE £8,800: set it aside now, wait, or let Octavia arrange it.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the library at seven, the total written and the evening ahead — forty-one thousand six hundred on the memorandum book's Sunday page, the house dressing for dinner around her — and the question of the surplus runs alongside the question of the night. Eight thousand eight hundred pounds, immediate, from the surplus. It can be moved, or held, or handed. The house must decide what the mistress does with the money that can be touched.)*
> *(Set it aside now: move the £8,800 on Sunday into the reckoning's keeping — the resolve of it, the owing begun in fact, the risk that the house runs tighter than comfort. Wait: hold the surplus liquid till the week's shape is known — the cunning of it, the timing kept, the risk that the waiting reads as the wavering. Or let Octavia arrange it: the accountant's hands, the instruments her own — the mercy of it, the burden laid on willing shoulders, the risk that the trusting is read as the delegating.)*
> *(The surplus goes where she sends it — into the keeping, into the waiting, or into Octavia's hands. If moved: the £8,800 leaves the surplus on Sunday night, and the reckoning has its first fact. If waited: the money stays liquid, and the week will decide its hour. If handed: Octavia takes the instruments, and the arranging is hers. Whatever the surplus became, one law holds it entire: the money was hers to move, and she chose the moving. The choosing is done.)*

options.label: Set it aside now
options.detail: *Resolve+; the surplus, moved.* Sunday: the £8,800 into the reckoning's keeping. *(Moved — and the tightening, entire.)*

options.label: Wait
options.detail: *Cunning+; the holding, timed.* The surplus liquid till the week's shape is known. *(Timed — and the wavering, suggested.)*

options.label: Let Octavia arrange it
options.detail: *Mercy+; the burden, handed.* The accountant's hands; the instruments, her own. *(Handed — and the delegating, risked.)*

scenes.synopsis: the execution — the £8,800's keeping, three ways; the Sunday page, written.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she moved it: Octavia writes the order on Sunday night, and the £8,800 leaves the surplus into the reckoning's keeping — the reckoning's first fact, entered fair. If she waited: the surplus stays liquid, and Octavia marks the page with the sum and the word "held," and the week will decide. If she handed it: Octavia takes the instruments with a nod, and the arranging becomes the accountant's own office.)*
> *(In every holding the same law: the memorandum book's Sunday page carries the total entire — forty-one thousand six hundred, written fair — and the £8,800's line beside it, marked as the house chose. She shuts the book. The execution, done. The Sunday, entered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's Sunday — the branch, fallen; the number's meaning, withheld.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends for her at half past seven — the London drawing room, the chocolate, Sunday's own counsel. "You kept the house today," she says. "The Sabbath, the books. Your grandfather kept his Sundays with the canal's accounts, and look where that led." The dryness is entire, and so is the warning under it.)*
> *("The branch fell," Rose says. "I know what you carry, Grandmama." "And I know what you are counting," Augusta says. "Do not bring me the sum, child. The branch fell. I have had thirty years to make my peace with the falling, and I will not have it unburied for the arithmetic's amusement." She drinks. The chocolate, drunk. The door, closed on the number.)*

scenes.synopsis: Sunday dinner — the Sabbath table; the household entire; the number, unspoken.
scenes.prose:
> *(Dinner is at eight, the household entire — Augusta at the head, Julian, Octavia with the memorandum book nowhere in sight, Letitia with the household book beside her plate, Henry permitted the table for the Sabbath, Laurent in his place, quieter than his custom and present entire. If the reckoning is the household's: the sum sits at the table like a guest everyone has agreed not to introduce. If it is not: the unspoken sits there instead, and the house carries it the way it carries everything.)*
> *(The courses come and go. Nobody mentions the memorandum book. Nobody mentions the canal. Henry asks for more bread, and is given it, and the ordinary saves the evening the way the ordinary always does. The dinner, taken. The Sabbath, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening's dress — Sunday night's face; the reckoning, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia comes at nine with the evening's question, the aunt's eye on the reckoning's aftermath. "The evening wants the mistress dressed for it, miss — not the counting's, the keeping's." Three on the stand: the claret, evening — deep, the house's color, the reckoning worn to the night; the grey — the reader's, the ledger's color, the sum logged and closed; or the ivory, layered — bright, the grandmother's, the Sabbath unruffled.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret — evening, deep, the house's own. The grey waits. The ivory, bright. "The keeping," she says, "wants the house under it." "The house," Letitia says, pinning, "is under the night, miss — the quartermaster only says so." She chooses the evening's dress. In the glass: the mistress, kept.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the reader's; the ledger's color, the sum logged and closed.

scenes.synopsis: the household book's Sunday page — the order, kept; the letter, sealed.
scenes.prose:
> *(In the retiring room Letitia reads the household book's Sunday page — the Sabbath's order, kept entire: church, the collation, dinner, the staff's Sunday, all accounted. The pencil is even. The hand is steady. The quartermaster's Sunday, entire.)*
> *(Behind the book's false back the letter sits sealed, untouched, unasked-for — the thirty years in it, undisturbed by the day's arithmetic. Letitia's hand rests a moment on the cover, and Rose sees it, and says nothing. Some doors are not Rose's to open, and the reckoning's Sunday is not the day for doors. The book, shut. The letter, left.)*

scenes.synopsis: the copybook's Sunday page — the child, the forbidding; the wall, waited.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry finds her in the hall at half past nine with the copybook's Sunday page, exhibited with both hands — the letters even, the lines straight, the Sabbath's own. "Very good," Rose says, and means it entirely, and he beams the way only a child permitted the Sunday table can beam.)*
> *("Will the garden's wall be finished by Christmas?" he asks — the Park's wall, the mason's courses, the week's own building. "The wall," she says carefully, "is waiting its turn, like everything." He accepts this the way children accept the mysteries of grown money. The page, praised. The wall, waited.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel — what the number forbids; the ten years' discipline.
scenes.prose:
> *("Forty-one thousand six hundred," Octavia says, "is not only a sum. It is ten years of the canal, which is ten years of the estate standing still — the Park's improvements, the garden's wall, the tenants' roofs, all waiting their turn. The reckoning forbids the spending, Rose. That is the discipline of it, and the discipline is the point.")*
> *("And if the house chafes?" Rose asks. "Then the house," Octavia says, "will learn what the émigrés learned — what it is to wait for better times, and mean it." She caps the pencil. The counsel, given. The forbidding, priced.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening — the window seat; the sum, present; the staying's price, counted.
scenes.prose:
> *(He comes to the drawing room after dinner, because the staying means the rooms, not only the house — and takes the window seat, and watches the square's lamps come on one by one. When the talk turns to the week's business, he listens the way a man listens to weather he has agreed to stand out in. The devastation has not unmade him. The arithmetic has only given it a figure.)*
> *(She sits near enough that their sleeves nearly touch, and not so near as to presume — the grief's perimeter, redrawn for the evening. He does not speak of the number. He does not need to. It is in the room like the lamps are in the room: lit, and not to be looked at directly. The quiet, shared. The sum, present.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night's hand — the retiring room's repair; the keeping, worn.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise finds her in the retiring room at ten — the atelier's privilege, the night's repair before the ritual. "The evening has had its hours, miss — the hand wants the woman." Three on the tray: the mended gloves, kept — the week's pair, the mend honored, worn to the reckoning's keeping; the silver rose pin, plain — the house's mark, worn quiet; or the violets, reset — faithfulness, pinned dried against the night.)*
> *(Rose touches the gloves — mended, the week's own, the mend honored. The pin waits, plain. The violets, dried. "The night," she says, "wants the keeping on it." "The keeping," Élise says, pinning, "is on you, miss — the atelier only says so." She chooses the night's hand. In the glass: the mistress, kept.)*

fashionChoices.detail: plain; the house's mark, worn quiet.

fashionChoices.detail: faithfulness; pinned dried against the night.

scenes.synopsis: the dispersing — the house to bed; the hunters' money, unreckoned.
scenes.prose:
> *(The household disperses at half past ten — Augusta's door shut, Julian's lamp still burning, Octavia's pencil capped at last, Letitia's book closed, Henry long abed with the copybook on the chair. The town house keeps its Sunday the way it keeps everything: entire, unruffled, London-quiet.)*
> *(She stands at the stair's foot a moment with Octavia's last word of the day in her ear — "the hunters are counting something else; watch the spending, not the silence" — and thinks of the money moving somewhere in London's dark. The lamps, lit. The Sunday, spent.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Sabbath's reckoning — Sunday night, the mistress re-dresses for the keeping; the number, worn.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, in the retiring room — "the book's with me, miss. The night's line is written when you say.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the retiring-room door — "the number is written, Rose. Wear it the way you wrote it.")*
> *(Story morsel: Augusta, from the wing — "steady, child. The night watches for the tremble.")*
> *(Story morsel: Élise's word, sent with the gown — "the extra stitch held, miss. All night, for Sunday.")*
> *(Story morsel: Julian, from the supper room — "one evening, Rose. The house can spare you one.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: Sunday night — the arithmetic done, the total written; the house dresses for the reckoning's keeping. Nothing showy and nothing solemn-for-show. Dress for the Sabbath's end: the quiet's own patience, worn plain. Heard. Steady. Entire. The woman who counted the sin is not unraveled by the sum.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE SABBATH'S END: carry the number into the week, set it down till Monday, or tell Augusta tonight.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone at eleven with the night's keeping on her — the total written, the surplus decided, the house abed around her — and the question of the Sabbath's end runs alongside the question of the night. The number is computed; the reckoning has its sum. Now: whether she carries it into the week, or sets it down till Monday, or tells the dowager tonight. The house must decide how the mistress ends the Sabbath.)*
> *(Carry it: take the number into the week entire — Monday's business, priced — the resolve of it, the reckoning begun, the risk that the week never rests. Set it down: the Sabbath kept whole, the number locked in the book till Monday — the mercy of it, the rest entire, the risk that the pausing reads as the flinching. Or tell Augusta tonight: the dowager hears the reckoning exists — and refuses the sums, as she refused the branch's unburying — the candor of it, the telling done, the risk that the refusing is the whole of her answer.)*
> *(The Sabbath ends where she sends it — into the week, into the keeping, or into the dowager's refusing. If borne: the number goes into Monday entire, and the week is priced from its first hour. If kept: the book locks on the sum, and the night is uncounted, and the Sabbath holds. If told: Augusta hears that the reckoning has a sum, and declines the arithmetic — the branch fell, and that is enough, and the door closes on the number. Whatever the ending became, one law holds it entire: the Sabbath was hers to end, and she chose the ending. The choosing is done.)*

options.label: Carry the number into the week
options.detail: *Resolve+; the reckoning, borne.* Monday takes the sum; the week, priced entire. *(Borne — and the resting, foregone.)*

options.label: Set it down till Monday
options.detail: *Mercy+; the Sabbath, kept.* The number locked in the book; tonight, uncounted. *(Kept — and the flinching, suggested.)*

options.label: Tell Augusta tonight
options.detail: *Candor+; the dowager, told.* She hears the reckoning exists — and refuses the sums. *(Told — and the refusing, entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: the execution — the number's keeping, three ways; the Sabbath, ended.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she bore it: the memorandum book goes into the Monday folio, and the week is priced from its first hour. If she kept it: Octavia locks the book on the sum, and the Sabbath holds uncounted. If she told: the dowager's refusing is entered in the household's memory — the reckoning exists, the sums declined, the branch enough.)*
> *(In every ending the same law: the number is kept where the house chose — borne, locked, or told-and-refused — and the keeping is entire. Octavia caps the pencil. The execution, done. The Sabbath, ended.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's night — the branch, fallen; the peace, kept or refused.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she told: Augusta heard it in the drawing room at half past eleven — the reckoning exists, the sum computed — and declined it entire. "The branch fell," she said. "I will not have it unburied, child — not for the ton, not for the arithmetic." The door closed on the number, and the dowager's peace held.)*
> *(If she did not: Augusta's door is shut, the wing quiet, the dowager's Sabbath entire — the branch fallen, the peace unburied, the number never brought to her. Rose passes the door on her way up, and does not knock. Some doors are not hers to open, and the number's meaning is not hers to give unasked. The door, shut. The peace, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the late hour — the stair's foot; the week, priced; the staying's rhythm.
scenes.prose:
> *(He comes down at midnight — not to leave, the hour being far past leaving, but to the stair's foot, where the library's door stands open on the memorandum book's shut cover. The house is dark around them, the reckoning's day behind them, and for a moment neither speaks.)*
> *("Monday," he says. "The week, priced." "The week," she says, "is ours to price." His hand finds hers in the dark — briefly, the staying's rhythm, found and let go with the night — and the dark keeps its counsel. The late hour, held. The week, ahead.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Bell's Sabbath paragraph; the Gazette clean; the scandal, unbroken.
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting is Bell's Sabbath paragraph, brought up with the Sunday post — the proprietor's own, the Gazette clean on the Sabbath.)*
> *(Rose reads it in the drawing room, and finds the cleanliness in it — no sums, no names beyond the ton's own, the proprietor's paragraph entire. Bell's Gazette carries no reckoning Sunday — the paper clean, alert, unbought. She folds the paragraph and gives it to Octavia for the memorandum book. The paper smells of ink. The Sabbath smells of candles.)*
scenes.sting: the sting — Bell's Sabbath paragraph; the Gazette clean; the scandal, unbroken.

scenes.synopsis: the sting, read — Bell's clean sheet; the hunters' silence, watched.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia files Bell's paragraph in the memorandum book beside the Lash's Saturday number — the clean beside the unclean, the Sabbath's whole press. "Bell prints nothing," Octavia says, "which is the proprietor telling you the reckoning is still yours to make. The scandal is unbroken. The watching continues — hers, and Pounce's.")*
> *("And Pounce's arithmetic?" Rose asks. "Pounce," Octavia says, "is counting something else — the money moving in London, Slade's second man, the spending. Watch it, not the silence." She shuts the book. The paragraph, filed. The silence, watched.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night's wrap — the cloak room; the Sunday, unpinned; the aunt's hands.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia meets her in the cloak room at half past eleven with the night's last question, the aunt's hands on the unpinning. "The Sunday has had its hours, miss — the wrap wants the woman." Three on the peg: the evening cloak, claret-lined — deep, the week's color, the reckoning worn to the night; the ivory shawl — the grandmother's, quiet, the dignity kept; or the grey mantle — the reader's, the ledger's color, the sum logged and closed.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret-lined — deep, the week's own, the reckoning's. The shawl waits, quiet. The mantle, sober. "The wrap," she says, "wants the keeping." "The keeping," Letitia says, fastening, "is abed soon, miss — the quartermaster only says so." She chooses the night's wrap. In the glass: the mistress, unwound.)*

fashionChoices.label: The ivory shawl
fashionChoices.detail: the grandmother's; quiet, the dignity kept.

fashionChoices.label: The grey mantle
fashionChoices.detail: the reader's; the ledger's color, the sum logged and closed.

scenes.synopsis: the house, quiet — the day, accounted; the telling, the total, the keeping.
scenes.prose:
> *(The town house settles at midnight — the staff's Sunday done, the lamps turned low, the memorandum book shut in the library with the total written fair inside it. She walks the hall once, the way she walked it Saturday, and accounts the day: the entries, booked; the total, landed; the surplus, decided; the audience, chosen; the Sabbath, ended. The columns are hers, and they balance.)*
> *(She thinks of Bell's clean paragraph, folded in Octavia's book, and of the hunters' money moving somewhere in London's dark. Tomorrow is Monday, and the week is priced. Tonight was Sunday, and Sunday held. The hall, walked. The day, accounted.)*

scenes.synopsis: the late hour — the library door; the total, kept; the week, priced.
scenes.prose:
> *(She steps out to the hall past midnight, and the library's door stands open on the memorandum book's shut cover — forty-one thousand six hundred, written fair, locked in the dark. She thinks of what the week will cost to pay it, and what the paying obliges: the canal's ten years, the surplus moved, the de Valcourts' promise standing outside the finding like a sentry.)*
> *(But tonight is Sunday, and the house is holding, and the number is the whole of the business. She shuts the library door. The total, kept. The week, priced.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sheet — Sunday night, the Lash prints a sum; the hunters' own arithmetic.
scenes.prose: > *(Late, and the house dark, and the lamps low — and the Lash's Sunday-night sheet comes up with the last post, Pounce's number, the gutter's eye on the town house. It names no names. It prints a sum — forty thousand pounds, more or less, "the Hartwell reckoning, by our counting" — and the sum is too close to be a guess. The hunters have their own arithmetic.)*

scenes.synopsis: Monday's breakfast — the Sunday sheet on the table; the hunters' arithmetic, mirrored; the week, priced.
scenes.prose:
> *(Monday's breakfast has an uninvited guest. Pounce's Sunday sheet sits folded beside Octavia's plate, the way a bad card sits beside a good hand: forty thousand pounds, more or less, "the Hartwell reckoning, by our counting." Rose reads it over the toast and sets it down without haste, which costs her more than the reading.)*
> *("Sixteen hundred short of mine," Octavia says, "which is either mercy or the part they haven't found." She butters the toast left-handed, the pencil hand, which tells Rose the arithmetic is still running under the Sabbath's quiet. "They have a reckoning, Rose. It isn't mine. It's close enough to spend." The sheet, folded. The week, priced.)*

scenes.synopsis: Monday's face — dressing for the doors; the archive's answer.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia comes with Monday's question before the toast is cold. "The doors are open today, miss, all three, and the house wants to know which one you're walking toward. The gown can say it, or not say it." Three on the stand: the archive grey, the reader's, the ledger's color, the counting walked into the week; the claret, the house's, Monday-dressed, the doors faced in full; or the ivory, plain, the grandmother's, quiet, the patience of the unchosen.)*
> *(Rose touches the grey, sober, the ledger's, the week's own color. The claret waits. The ivory, quiet. "The doors," she says, "want no ceremony either." "No ceremony," Letitia says, fastening, "is becoming the house doctrine, miss. The quartermaster only says so." She chooses Monday's face. In the glass: the mistress, undecided and dressed.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the reader's; the ledger's color, the counting walked into the week.

fashionChoices.label: The claret
fashionChoices.detail: the house's; Monday-dressed, the doors faced in full.
