fashionChoices.detail: the grandmother's; quiet, the patience of the unchosen.

scenes.synopsis: Harrow's testimony — the library; the shadow's halves; the thirty years, laid out.
scenes.prose:
> *(Harrow comes to the library at eleven, as summoned, and brings his testimony the way a clerk brings a ledger: his papers' halves in a canvas satchel, the copies he made in the war years in a hand younger than the one that carries them now. He lays them out without ceremony. "I kept Mr. Elias's shadow," he says. "The entries he hurried, I copied fair. The names he priced, I kept.")*
> *(Rose turns the pages: de la Roche's nine hundred, the tall E standing like a signature; de Brissac's fourteen hundred, the ink darker, the hand hurried; the canal's figures, year on year, patient as weather. "You could have sold these," she says. "I could have," he says. "I kept them instead. That is the difference between a witness and a thief, though the ton would not see it." He meets her eye. "Ask what you need, Miss Hartwell. The thirty years are yours to read." The satchel, emptied. The shadow, laid out.)*

scenes.synopsis: Harrow's door — expose; the witness asks to be named; the price, stated.
scenes.prose:
> *("There is a door you haven't opened," Harrow says, "because it has my name on it. Open it." He stands at the library table with his copies between them, and the plainness of him is the whole argument. "Print me. Print the copies, the names, the sums. Let Bell set them in her clean type and let the town read what your grandfather's money did.")*
> *("The town," Rose says, "will read your name too." "My name," he says, "has been buried thirty years, and the burial hasn't agreed with it." A pause. "It will cost your grandmother her peace, and the Comte his family's quiet, and you the luxury of being the only one who knows. I know the price, Miss Hartwell. I am asking to pay my share of it." The door, named. The price, stated.)*

scenes.synopsis: the proprietor's terms — expose's press; the Gazette prints what's true.
scenes.prose:
> *(Bell comes at noon with ink on her cuffs and no patience for thresholds. "I hear you're choosing doors," she says. "Here's mine, if you want it. If it's true, I'll print it: the sums, the names, Harrow's copies with his leave. Not for you. The Gazette doesn't print favors, Miss Hartwell. It prints facts, and a wartime ledger is a fact with a long shadow.")*
> *("And if the fact ruins the living?" Rose asks. "The living," Bell says, "are already living it. The printing only tells them the shape of the room they're in." She takes her tea standing. "One proprietor to another: my press is yours the day you have the truth entire. Not before. The Gazette doesn't print halves, and it doesn't print maybes." The terms, stated. The press, offered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's door — bury; the branch fell; the papers, locked.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends for her at two, and the London drawing room has the air of a courtroom that has already decided. "You are choosing doors, I hear," the dowager says. "Then hear mine. Lock the papers. Harrow's halves with them. Let the Lash print its forty thousand. They have no proof, and proof is the only thing that matters in this town.")*
> *("The proof exists," Rose says. "It exists in my library, in two satchels, in Octavia's book." "Then it exists nowhere," Augusta says, "until you publish it. The branch fell, child. I have had thirty years to make my peace with the falling, and I will not have it unburied for the arithmetic's amusement, or the town's." She drinks her chocolate. "Bury it. Pay what must be paid, quietly, and let the sin lie with the dead. The living have earned their quiet." The door, shut. The burying, counseled.)*

scenes.synopsis: the brother's door — atone; the honorable arithmetic; pay it in the open.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian finds her at three in the hall, and his counsel has the plainness she remembers from the nursery. "Pay it," he says. "Not all at once, the house couldn't, but in the open, year by year, the way Octavia's book has it. The canal's ten years. The surplus. The de Valcourts' promise." He leans on the newel post. "It's the only door that doesn't ask anyone to lie, Rose. Expose tells everything and calls it honesty. Bury tells nothing and calls it peace. Atone just pays.")*
> *("Ten years of the estate standing still," she says. "Ten years," he agrees, "of the estate standing for something. There's a difference, and the tenants will know it even if the ton doesn't." He squeezes her arm, the brother's whole argument in the grip. "We owe it, sister. Owing is simple. It's the paying that's the work." The door, plain. The brother, heard.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE DOOR: walk closest to expose, bury, or atone; the leaning, chosen.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the library at four, the three doors standing open in her mind the way they stood in the day's counsel: Harrow's, asking to be named; Augusta's, shut on the branch's falling; Julian's and Octavia's, the long arithmetic of the paying. The choosing is Thursday's, or the week's, or never's, but the leaning is today's, and the house must know which door the mistress walks nearest.)*
> *(Walk closest to expose: Harrow named, Bell's press, the sin aired entire, the candor of it, the living named aloud, the risk that the airing ruins more than it cleans. Walk closest to bury: the papers locked, Harrow's halves with them, the silence kept, the cunning of it, the proof nowhere till published, the risk that the hunters' arithmetic fills the quiet. Walk closest to atone: the £41,600 over the years, the canal's ten, the surplus moved, the resolve of it, the owing paid in the open, the risk that ten years standing still breaks the house.)*
> *(The leaning goes where she sends it: toward the airing, the locking, or the paying. If opened: Harrow is told his name may be printed, and Bell is told the truth is coming entire. If shut: the satchels go into the library's locked press, and the house learns the discipline of the unflinching. If entered: Octavia is told to ready the instruments, and the ten years begin their quiet march. Whatever the leaning became, one law holds it entire: the choosing waits, but the walking has begun. The leaning is chosen.)*

options.detail: *Cunning+; the door, shut.* The papers locked; the silence, kept. *(Shut — and the filling, risked.)*

options.label: Walk closest to atone
options.detail: *Resolve+; the door, entered.* The £41,600 over the years; the price, begun. *(Entered — and the breaking, risked.)*

scenes.synopsis: the doors, costed — the accountant's reading; each price, stated plain.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes at five with the memorandum book and no opinions, which is her way of having all of them. "You want the doors costed," she says. "Expose: the ton reads the sin by Friday, the living are named, Harrow is a hero or a scandal, and the town decides which, not you. Bury: the papers sleep, the hunters print their shape, and you spend the year proving a negative. Atone: forty-one thousand six hundred, ten years of canal, the surplus moved, the house running tighter than comfort.")*
> *("And your counsel?" Rose asks. "My counsel," Octavia says, capping the pencil, "is that doors are not chosen by their prices. They're chosen by what you can live behind." She looks at her friend. "Price them all, Rose. Then live behind the one you can stand." The costing, done. The living, named.)*

scenes.synopsis: the afternoon's air — the square's garden; the doors, walked.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at half past five with the walk's question, the atelier's eye on the day's counsel. "The doors want walking, miss, the square's garden, the air. The provision." Three on the peg: the archive blue walking dress, severe, the estate's, the wall's color worn to the thinking; the grey redingote, the reader's, the ledger's, the reckoning walked; or the claret shawl, the house's, warm, the doors faced in the family's color.)*
> *(Rose touches the blue, severe, the estate's own. The redingote waits. The shawl, warm. "The walk," she says, "wants the thinking on it." "The thinking," Élise says, fastening, "is walking, miss. The atelier only says so." She chooses the afternoon's air. In the glass: the mistress, aired.)*

scenes.synopsis: the mason's letter — the garden half-restored; the courses, waiting.
scenes.prose:
> *(The mason's letter comes with the evening post, and Rose reads it in the library with Harrow's satchels still on the table, the country's business beside the town's. Two courses laid on the walled garden's breach, the mortar setting fair; the third course by Saturday, weather holding. The men have found the old footing sound. The wall, the mason writes, remembers how to stand.)*
> *(She folds the letter and thinks of the garden half-restored: the beds turned, the paths re-laid, the wall rising course by course around a choosing not yet made. The garden is waiting its turn, like everything. The letter, kept. The wall, waited.)*

scenes.synopsis: the household book's Monday page — the order, kept; the letter, sealed.
scenes.prose:
> *(In the retiring room Letitia reads the household book's Monday page: the doors' day, kept entire, the library at eleven, the proprietor at noon, the dowager at two, the brother at three, all accounted. The pencil is even. The hand is steady. The quartermaster's Monday, entire.)*
> *(Behind the book's false back the letter sits sealed, untouched, unasked-for, the thirty years in it undisturbed by the day's three doors. Letitia's hand rests a moment on the cover, and Rose sees it, and says nothing. Some doors are not Rose's to open, and the eve of the choosing is not the day for doors. The book, shut. The letter, left.)*

scenes.synopsis: the eve of Tuesday — his family's name; the staying; the uncounseled door.
scenes.prose:
> *(He finds her at nine in the morning room, and the day's three doors are in the room with them, unmentioned and entire. "My family's name is in Octavia's columns," he says. "And the de Valcourt promise — two thousand eight hundred pounds, standing like a sentry. I have spent the day hearing which door you walk nearest, and I have come to tell you I will not counsel it.")*
> *("You won't tell me which?" she asks. "I will tell you this," he says. "The number — if I carry it — is my family's too; if I do not, it will be when the hour comes. Whatever door you open, I am on the far side of it: not advising, not permitting, only staying." He takes her hand briefly, the staying's rhythm, found and let go. "Choose, Rose. I will be there when you have." The door, uncounseled. The staying, entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: Tuesday's morning — the town house; the post; the ordinary, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(Tuesday wakes the town house to its ordinary: the breakfast at nine, the post at ten, the household's week running under the doors' weight the way a river runs under ice. Augusta takes the head of the table in her Tuesday black. Julian has the paper folded small. Henry is permitted the table with the copybook's Tuesday page half done and wholly praised.)*
> *(Rose announces nothing, and the house asks nothing; the leaning was yesterday's, and yesterday is priced. The post comes at ten: the mason's nothing new, Bell's nothing further, and a letter from the village in a carrier's hand, franked hastily, that Letitia sets apart from the rest. The ordinary, kept. The Tuesday, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: the first word — the village note; a man asking after Harrow; the lodgings, asked.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia brings the village note to the morning room at half past ten, and her face has the quartermaster's particular stillness. "From Mrs. Pike," she says. "By the carrier. There's a man in the village asking after Mr. Harrow." Rose looks up. "Asking what?" "Where he lodges, to begin with. His keeping; the lane, the cottage, the Crown — the village knows where he keeps, so everyone told him. He came down Monday evening, the carrier says, and he's been asking since this morning. From London. Ordinary coat. Ordinary hat." A pause. "The kind you'd forget.")*
> *(The note is short, Mrs. Pike's hand hurried, the news entire in four lines. Rose reads it twice. A man, asking. The lodgings, asked. The week, acquiring a reader.)*

scenes.synopsis: Tuesday's face — dressing with a reader in the village; the archive's answer.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia comes with Tuesday's question, and the village note is in the room with them, unmentioned. "The day wants the mistress dressed for it, miss, not the doors', the week's." Three on the stand: the dove grey, the reader's, quiet, the watching worn soft; the claret morning gown, the house's, Tuesday-dressed, the asking faced in full; or the ivory muslin, the grandmother's, plain, the patience kept close.)*
> *(Rose touches the dove, quiet, the watching's color. The claret waits. The muslin, plain. "The week," she says, "wants no alarm in it." "No alarm," Letitia says, fastening, "is the whole of the quartermaster's doctrine, miss. The aunt only says so." She chooses Tuesday's face. In the glass: the mistress, unalarmed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the second word — Élise's village; the habits, the friends, the letters; the notebook.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at noon with the second word, and hers is the fuller telling, the flower-seller's network, the village entire. "He's asking his habits now," she says. "When Mr. Harrow walks, whether he's church Sundays, who his friends are." She hesitates. "And whether he writes letters. Whether his keeping holds him, or something else does.")*
> *("Who told him?" "Everyone," Élise says. "The village is beginning to enjoy itself. The Crown's boy told him Mr. Harrow's friends are his books, and the carrier said his keeping gets more post than a schoolmaster should." She looks at Rose. "He writes it down, miss. Everything. In a little book." The habits, asked. The letters, asked. The notebook, filling.)*

scenes.synopsis: the counsel — the questions of a man pricing a witness; the spending, watched.
scenes.prose:
> *("Those are the questions of a man pricing a witness," Octavia says, when Rose lays the two words before her. "Lodgings, habits, friends, letters. He is learning what Harrow is worth, and to whom. A man doesn't ask whether a schoolmaster writes letters unless he's wondering who reads them.")*
> *("The hunters," Rose says. "The hunters," Octavia agrees, "are counting something else: the money moving in London, the spending. Watch it, not the silence." She caps the pencil. "A stranger with a notebook is a symptom, Rose. The money behind him is the disease. Find the money, or watch the man, but don't mistake one for the other." The counsel, given. The pricing, priced.)*

scenes.synopsis: the thinking — who pointed them at Harrow; the circle; the unresolving.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone at two, Rose turns the two words over the way she turned Harrow's copies: for what they say and what they withhold. What they say: a man from London, ordinary, asking. What they withhold: who sent him, and what the notebook is for. She thinks of the spring, the breach, the papers carried in daylight, the village that watched it all happen.)*
> *(She does not finish the thought. Some arithmetic wants Octavia's pencil, not hers, and some readers are better left unread till Thursday. She stands at the window and lets the unresolving stand. The thinking, done. The week, still poised.)*

scenes.synopsis: the schoolmaster, ordinary — breakfast's Latin; the man being priced, unaware.
scenes.prose:
> *(Harrow is at breakfast on Tuesday, entirely the schoolmaster; the week's business has brought him to town, and the town house has absorbed him the way it absorbs stray cats and second cousins. He talks to Henry about Latin verbs with the particular joy of a man who has found his audience. "Amo, amas," Henry recites. "Amat." "Very good," Harrow says, "and the passive will come when you're older, which is true of most things.")*
> *(Rose watches him butter his toast: the scarred gentleman, the witness, the man with a stranger's notebook filling in the village, his name at the top of the page. He does not know. The toast, buttered. The Latin, recited. The pricing, underway.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE STRANGER: watch him, warn Harrow, or do nothing yet; the pricing, answered.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the morning room at three, the two words from the village on the table, the lodgings asked, the habits, the friends, the letters, the little book filling, and the question of the stranger runs alongside the question of the afternoon. A man is pricing her witness. The house must decide how the mistress answers the pricing.)*
> *(Watch him: set Élise's village to watching, the Crown's boy, the carrier, Mrs. Pike's girl, eyes on his questions, his notebook, his letters' direction. The cunning of it, the inquiry inventoried, the risk that the watching is seen. Warn Harrow: tell him he is being priced, the mercy of it, the witness armed, the risk that the warning frightens the schoolmaster out of his ordinary. Or do nothing yet: no eyes, no warning, the week unruffled, the resolve of it, the discipline kept, the risk that the waiting reads as the blindness.)*
> *(The stranger goes where she sends him: into the watching, into the warning, or into the week's unruffled air. If watched: Élise's word goes down to the village by the evening post, and the Crown's boy takes up his post. If warned: Harrow hears it in the library at four, and the schoolmaster's ordinary acquires a shadow. If neither: the week goes on as the week was, and the notebook fills unwatched. Whatever the stranger became, one law holds it entire: the pricing was hers to answer, and she chose the answering. The answering is done.)*

options.label: Watch him
options.detail: *Cunning+; the eyes, set.* Élise's village; the questions, inventoried from a distance. *(Set — and the seeing, risked.)*

options.label: Warn Harrow
options.detail: *Mercy+; the warning, given.* He is told he is being priced; the fear, his to carry. *(Given — and the frightening, risked.)*

options.label: Do nothing yet
options.detail: *Resolve+; the discipline, kept.* No eyes, no warning; the week, unruffled. *(Kept — and the blindness, suggested.)*

scenes.synopsis: the execution — the stranger, three ways; the village, tasked or untasked.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she watched: Élise's word goes down to the village by the evening post, the Crown's boy to note his hours, the carrier his letters' direction, Mrs. Pike's girl his questions. "Not close," Rose says. "I don't want him knowing he's watched." If she warned: Harrow hears it in the library at four, and takes it the way he takes everything, plainly, without flinching, the schoolmaster acquiring a shadow he refuses to wear. If she did neither: the evening post carries nothing, and Élise's village goes unwarned, and the week holds its unruffled air.)*
> *(In every answering the same law: the stranger keeps asking, and the village keeps answering, and the notebook keeps filling, watched, warned-against, or neither. She stands at the window as the post goes. The execution, done. The Tuesday, priced.)*

scenes.synopsis: the man of business — what watching buys; eyes cheap, hands expensive.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill comes at five with his leather case and the week's accounts, and Rose lays the stranger before him like another entry. He listens the way he listens to figures: completely, without surprise. "Eyes are cheap, Miss Hartwell," he says. "The Crown's boy costs you nothing and tells you everything the village knows. Hands are expensive. The day you lay a hand on that man, warn him off, buy his notebook, have him followed to London, the day becomes a story.")*
> *("And stories?" "Travel," Quill says, "faster than strangers. A watched man tells his master he's watched, and the master changes the man." He snaps the case shut. "Watch, if you must. But count the shillings too. A stranger with a notebook is some man's money at work, and money leaves a smell." The counsel, given. The money, named.)*

scenes.synopsis: Tuesday dinner — the town house table; the doors, unchosen; the stranger, unmentioned.
scenes.prose:
> *(Dinner is at eight, the household entire: Augusta at the head, Julian, Octavia with the memorandum book nowhere in sight, Letitia with the household book beside her plate, Harrow in his place, quieter than his custom and present entire. Nobody mentions the village. Nobody mentions the notebook. The doors stand open in the house the way they stand open in her mind: unchosen, entire, waiting.)*
> *(The courses come and go. Harrow asks Henry for his verbs, and Henry recites, and the table applauds, and the ordinary saves the evening the way the ordinary always does. The dinner, taken. The Tuesday, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening's dress — Tuesday night's face; the watching, worn.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia comes at nine with the evening's question, the aunt's eye on the day's two words. "The evening wants the mistress dressed for it, miss, not the watching's, the keeping's." Three on the stand: the claret evening silk, deep, the house's color, the asking worn to the night; the grey, lamplit, the reader's, the ledger's, the notebook answered in kind; or the ivory, layered, the grandmother's, quiet, the patience unruffled.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret, evening, deep, the house's own. The grey waits, lamplit. The ivory, quiet. "The keeping," she says, "wants the house under it." "The house," Letitia says, pinning, "is under the night, miss. The quartermaster only says so." She chooses the evening's dress. In the glass: the mistress, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: Tuesday night — the doors in her mind; the stranger's notebook, imagined; the week, poised.
scenes.prose:
> *(She stands at the window at eleven with Tuesday behind her, the doors in her mind like rooms off a corridor, each lit, each entered in thought and left unchosen. Expose: Harrow's name in Bell's type. Bury: the satchels in the locked press. Atone: the ten years, marching. She walks the corridor and opens nothing. The choosing waits.)*
> *(And at the corridor's end, a smaller door: a man with a notebook, writing down a schoolmaster's hours. She imagines the page, lodgings, habits, friends, letters, and wonders what the next page holds, and whose hand turns it. The window, faced. The week, poised.)*

scenes.synopsis: Wednesday's morning — the household returns to Hartwell; the carriages; the packing, done.
scenes.prose:
> *(Wednesday wakes the town house to the packing: the household returns to Hartwell, the carriages at ten, the week moving to the country for whatever Thursday brings. Letitia's book rules the morning, the trunks, the servants, the memorandum book in its oilskin, Harrow's satchels in the second carriage. Amos the porter stands at the door with the way-bill, and the house empties in good order.)*
> *(Rose walks the hall once before she goes, the way she walked it Sunday: the town house keeping its counsel, London-quiet, the doors folded into the carriages with the rest of the luggage. The hall, walked. The country, called.)*

scenes.synopsis: the road — London to the Park; the arrival; the half-restored, seen.
scenes.prose:
> *(The road runs London to the Park in four hours, and Rose rides it with the memorandum book on her knee and the week's three days behind her like milestones. The country comes up green and unsurprised: the hedges, the tenants' roofs, the Park's gates standing open the way they have stood open all her life, as if the house had never doubted her return.)*
> *(And there it is at two: Hartwell, half-restored, the scaffolding on the garden wall, the courses rising, the beds turned, the whole estate waiting its turn with the patience of old stone. She steps down at the door, and the house takes her the way it takes everything: entire, unruffled, home. The road, run. The Park, entered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the country's face — arriving dress; the Park's answer.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise meets her at the Park with the arrival's question, the atelier's eye on the country hours. "The Park wants the mistress dressed for it, miss, not the road's, the house's." Three on the stand: the country grey, the reader's, the stone's color, the wall's own; the claret traveling dress, the house's, worn through the road, the arriving faced in full; or the ivory pelisse, the grandmother's, quiet, the patience brought home.)*
> *(Rose touches the grey, the stone's, the wall's own. The claret waits, road-dusted. The pelisse, quiet. "The house," she says, "wants the country under it." "The country," Élise says, fastening, "is under you, miss. The atelier only says so." She chooses the country's face. In the glass: the mistress, arrived.)*

scenes.synopsis: the eve's dressing — Wednesday night, the mistress re-dresses for the choosing's edge; the patience, worn.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, in the retiring room — "the book's with me, miss. The eve's line is written when you say.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the retiring-room door — "the doors are priced, Rose. Wear the one you can live behind.")*
> *(Story morsel: Augusta, from the wing — "steady, child. The eve watches for the tremble.")*
> *(Story morsel: Élise's word, sent with the gown — "the extra stitch held, miss. All evening, for the eve.")*
> *(Story morsel: Laurent, from the garden's edge — "the number is carried, Rose. Carry it well.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: Wednesday night — the household home at the Park, the garden waiting, Thursday coming; the mistress dresses for the eve of the choosing. Nothing bridal and nothing funereal. Dress for the threshold: the archive's patience, worn plain. Heard. Steady. Entire. The woman who would choose has not chosen yet — and the not-choosing is its own posture.

scenes.synopsis: the walled garden — half-restored; the courses, rising; the waiting, entire.
scenes.prose:
> *(She walks to the walled garden at four, alone, and stands at the breach where the spring put the papers into her hands. Two courses laid, the mortar setting fair, the mason's men gone for the day; the third course by Saturday, weather holding. The beds are turned, the paths re-laid, the old wall remembering how to stand around a garden that has waited thirty years to be chosen for.)*
> *(She puts her hand on the new course, cool, rough, honest, and thinks of the three doors, folded into the carriages, unpacked into the house. The garden does not hurry her. The garden has waited this long. The course, touched. The waiting, entire.)*

scenes.synopsis: the eve's counsel — the quartermaster; the sealed letter; doors that open from inside.
scenes.prose:
> *("The eve," Letitia says in the retiring room, "is the quartermaster's hardest hour, miss. The house is fed, the books are shut, the garden's waiting, and there's nothing left to order." She lays out the night's things with hands entirely steady. "So I'll say what the book can't. Whatever door you open, miss, open it in the morning, not the night. Night doors only lead back into the house.")*
> *(Behind the household book's false back the letter sits sealed, untouched, the thirty years in it undisturbed by the week's three doors. "And that one?" Rose asks, nodding at the book. "That one," Letitia says, "opens from the inside, or not at all. It isn't the week's door, miss. It never was." The counsel, given. The letter, left.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE EVE: keep the house together, send everyone to their own counsel, or sit with Laurent; the night, disposed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone at seven with the Park around her, the house fed, the books shut, the garden waiting, Thursday coming, and the question of the eve runs alongside the question of the night. The choosing waits for its hour. Tonight is only the disposing: how the mistress holds the house on the last night before the choosing.)*
> *(Keep the house together: one roof, one table, the household entire, Augusta, Julian, Octavia, Harrow, Letitia, the eve shared, the doors unmentioned. The resolve of it, the holding entire, the risk that togetherness becomes the watching. Send everyone to their own counsel: Augusta to her wing, Octavia to her sums, Julian to his road, the night honest, each with their own door. The candor of it, the dispersing, the risk that apart becomes alone. Or sit with Laurent: the garden's edge, the evening, the number his family's too, the mercy of it, the staying shared, the risk that the sharing becomes the leaning.)*
> *(The eve goes where she sends it: into the holding, the dispersing, or the sharing. If held: the household dines entire, and the doors go unmentioned, and the togetherness is the evening's whole argument. If dispersed: Augusta takes her wing, Octavia her sums, Julian the road to the village, and the house is quiet by nine. If shared: she walks to the garden's edge with Laurent, and they sit with the number between them, present and unmentioned, and say very little. Whatever the eve became, one law holds it entire: the night was hers to dispose, and she chose the disposing. The disposing is done.)*

scenes.synopsis: the execution — the eve, three ways; the night, disposed.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she held: the household dines entire at eight, and the doors go unmentioned, and the togetherness carries the evening. If she dispersed: the house is quiet by nine, Augusta's wing shut, Octavia's pencil capped, Julian's lamp burning in the village-bound room. If she shared: the garden's edge holds two figures till the light goes, and the reckoning — the number if it is his, the shape of it if it is not — sits between them, present and unmentioned.)*
> *(In every disposing the same law: the choosing waits for its hour, and the eve is only the holding, of the house, the counsel, or the evening. She walks the hall once, the way she walked it Sunday and the way she walked it this morning, and accounts the day: the road, run; the Park, entered; the garden, touched. The execution, done. The Wednesday, entered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Wednesday night, the Lash's compositor's room; Thursday's item, in type.
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting is not Rose's to read, not yet. It is Wednesday night in the Lash's compositor's room, the lamps lit, the Thursday edition going into the stick. Pounce stands over the proof and reads the four lines once, then again, his thumb on the tail of them. He nods. The boy locks the forme. Thursday, set.)*
> *(Rose, at Hartwell, knows none of this. The night is hers; the type is his. The item, poised. Thursday, coming.)*
scenes.sting: the sting — Wednesday night, the Lash's compositor's room; Thursday's item, in type.

scenes.synopsis: Wednesday dinner — the Park's table; the eve, shared or dispersed; Thursday, poised.
scenes.prose:
> *(Dinner is at eight at the Park, the household as the eve disposed it: entire, dispersed, or two figures at the garden's edge come in hungry. The courses come and go. Nobody mentions Thursday. Nobody needs to. The Lash is in type somewhere in London, the stranger is in the village with his notebook, the doors stand open in the house, and the evening holds them all the way the garden holds the wall: entire, unhurried, waiting.)*
> *(After, in the drawing room, Augusta takes up her embroidery, Julian the paper, Octavia a book she does not read. The ordinary, kept. The Thursday, poised.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night's dress — Wednesday night's face; the eve, worn.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia comes at ten with the night's question, the aunt's eye on the eve's disposing. "The night wants the mistress dressed for it, miss, not the eve's, the choosing's edge." Three on the stand: the claret, night, deep, the house's color, the eve worn to its end; the grey, moonlit, the reader's, the ledger's, the doors answered in silver; or the ivory wrap, the grandmother's, quiet, the patience kept to the last.)*
> *(Rose touches the claret, night, deep, the house's own. The grey waits, moonlit. The wrap, quiet. "The edge," she says, "wants the house under it." "The house," Letitia says, pinning, "is under the choosing, miss. The quartermaster only says so." She chooses the night's dress. In the glass: the mistress, edged.)*

scenes.synopsis: the book's Wednesday page — the order, kept; the letter, still sealed.
scenes.prose:
> *(In the retiring room Letitia reads the household book's Wednesday page: the country's order, kept entire, the carriages at ten, the arrival at two, dinner at eight, the staff's Wednesday, all accounted. The pencil is even. The hand is steady. The quartermaster's Wednesday, entire.)*
> *(Behind the book's false back the letter sits sealed, untouched, unasked-for, the thirty years in it undisturbed by the week's three doors and the eve's disposing. It has traveled to the country and back, London to the Park, and never been opened. Letitia shuts the book. The page, read. The letter, left.)*

scenes.synopsis: the garden's edge — the staying; the number, his family's; the unchosen, shared.
scenes.prose:
> *(He walks with her to the garden's edge at half past ten. If the eve was shared, they have been there since the light went; if it was not, he finds her there, because the staying means knowing where she goes. The moon is on the new courses, the mortar pale, the breach half-mended. They do not speak of the doors.)*
> *(If the number is his: "Forty-one thousand six hundred," he says at last, not looking at her. "I have carried it three days, and it has not gotten lighter." "It won't," she says. If it is not: "The size has its hour coming," he says at last, not looking at her, "and I will be there when it arrives." "It will be heavy when it comes," she says. "No," he agrees. "But it is honest, and honesty has a weight a man can learn to carry." He turns from the wall toward the house, and she turns with him, the choosing unchosen, the staying entire. The edge, walked. The night, shared.)*

scenes.synopsis: the cliffhanger — Wednesday night, the walled garden; the moon on the fallen courses; the three doors, unopened; Thursday, coming.
scenes.prose:
> *(Wednesday night, and she goes alone to the walled garden, past the new courses, past the mason's idle tools, to the breach where the spring put the papers into her hands. The moon is on the fallen courses, the old stone and the new, and the three doors stand open in her mind, expose, bury, atone, each lit, each waiting, each unopened. She stands among them the way she stood among the papers in April: the mistress of the sin, the chooser not yet choosing.)*
> *(Then she turns from the wall toward the house, the lamps lit, the household abed, Thursday coming up the road with its blind item and its stranger and its card not yet arrived. The choosing waits for morning. The night, hers. The doors, unopened.)*

scenes.synopsis: the blind item arrives — Thursday's Lash, sent up from London by a friend; the first sighting of the hunters.
scenes.prose:
> *(The Lash comes inside a friend's letter. That is the first thing. Not bought at a stall, not left at the door — forwarded, with a short note in a hand Rose knows: "My dear, I thought you should see what the town is reading. — C." The sheet itself is the usual filth, prizefights and kept women and a parson caught at cards, and Rose is turning past it, already done, when the blind item catches her eye at the foot of the third page. Four lines. No names. She reads them standing at the morning room window, and reads them again sitting down.)*
> *(This is what they print: "We hear that a certain great house in the shires keeps, behind a fallen wall, a ledger of the war years — and that the names entered in it are not English names. The town will recall what became of French money in English hands, in the years when England bled. More anon." Four lines. Behind them, a wall she knows. A ledger she has held. Names she has read by candlelight until they stopped being names and started being debts. She folds the sheet once, precisely, and lays it on the table like an unexploded shell. The hunters have surfaced. They have printed four lines to see if she flinches.)*

scenes.synopsis: dressing for a siege — archive grey silk, fashionable; the grandmother's mended gloves; the motif taken up.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia takes one look at the folded Lash and goes to the cedar wardrobe without being asked. "Archive grey," she says. "If the town is reading about us, the town can read grey." The gown she lays out belonged to Rose's grandmother — dove grey silk, twenty years old, the bodice re-cut last spring in the current fashion, the skirt's embroidery still fine enough to catch lamplight. With it, from the glove drawer, a pair of kid gloves, pearl grey, with a mend along the left thumb so fine it can only be found by touch. "She wore these the winter your grandfather died," Letitia says. "Mended them herself. Said a glove could be mended but a reputation had to be earned back stitch by stitch.")*
> *(Rose puts them on. The mend sits against her thumb like a small scar, deliberate and unhidden. In the glass she looks like what she is: a woman dressed by her grandmother's doctrine, in a gown that has outlasted two scandals and a war, cut to the current mode and better for it. "If they want the archive," she says, flexing the mended thumb, "they can have the archive. All of it. The mends included." Letitia nods once, the quartermaster approving the uniform. The mend, worn outward, becomes the season's answer before the season has asked its question.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the scar, kept; private armor.

fashionChoices.label: Letitia's choice
fashionChoices.detail: the quartermaster dresses the day.

scenes.synopsis: Octavia reads the four lines — the friend's counsel; what a blind item is for.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia arrives before noon, summoned by a note carried at a gallop, and reads the blind item standing in the hall with her bonnet still on. "Four lines," she says. "No names. 'More anon.'" She looks up. "It's a probe, Rose. They print the shape of the thing and watch who flinches. The flinch is the confirmation." She takes off the bonnet. "The question is not what they know. The question is what they want you to do about it." They go into the morning room, and Octavia reads the item a third time, aloud, the way you'd test a floorboard.)*
> *("A fallen wall," she says. "A ledger of the war years. Names not English. French money in English hands." She sets the sheet down. "It's your wall. It's your ledger. It's your names. They know enough to aim and not enough to hit. Yet." A pause. "Who else has read this?" "Half of London by dinner," Rose says. "And Harrow?" Octavia asks quietly. "Does he know he's about to be interesting?" Rose looks at the folded sheet, the unexploded shell. If she warned him Tuesday: "He knows he's being priced — I told him Tuesday. What he doesn't know is the four lines." If she did not: "Not yet," she says. "He will be, by tonight." The counsel, taken. The probe, understood.)*

scenes.synopsis: the quartermaster's reading — Letitia on probes, flinches, and household discipline.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia's reading of the blind item is practical. "They want a flinch," she says, laying out the luncheon with unnecessary precision. "So we don't flinch. The household goes about its business. Nobody asks questions in the village. Nobody writes to London. Nobody" — she points a spoon at Rose — "rides to the wall to stare at it." Rose, who had been considering exactly that, puts down her own spoon. "The wall," Letitia continues, "is being rebuilt. That's the story. Third course by Saturday. Anyone asks, that's the answer.")*
> *("And if the village is already talking?" "The village," Letitia says, "is talking about the blacksmith's new apprentice and whether the rain will hold. The village does not read the Lash." A beat. "Élise reads the Lash," Rose says. "Élise," Letitia concedes, "reads everything. That's why she's useful." She sets down the spoon. "Discipline, miss. The house that flinches at four lines will not survive forty." The quartermaster's doctrine, stated. The household, braced.)*

scenes.synopsis: the four lines, parsed — what they know, what they're guessing, what they're missing.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone after luncheon, Rose parses the four lines the way her grandmother taught her to parse letters: for what they say, what they withhold, and what they want. What they say: a great house, a fallen wall, a wartime ledger, French names, French money. What they withhold: every name, every sum, every date. What they want: the flinch. The "more anon" is the hook; the blind item is never the story, it's the advertisement for the story. Someone has paid for the advertisement. Someone wants her to know it's coming.)*
> *(What they're missing: Harrow's name. The émigré sums, exact. The de Varennes, the de Valcourts. The papers' halves. If they had the papers, they'd print the papers; a gutter sheet with proof doesn't deal in blind items. So they have a reader, not the ledger. Someone who saw, or heard, or was told the shape. She thinks of the spring: the breach, the papers, the people who knew. The circle was small. The circle has a leak. She folds the Lash again, precisely, and puts it in the drawer. The parsing, done. The leak, somewhere.)*

scenes.synopsis: Élise's first report — a stranger in the village, asking after Harrow.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at three with the violets and the news, and the news is the kind she delivers the way other people deliver weather. "There's a man asking after Mr. Harrow," she says, arranging the posy. "In the village. Since Tuesday." Rose goes still. "Asking what?" "His lodgings. His habits. His friends." Élise looks up. "Whether he goes to London. Whether he writes letters. Whether he's —" she hesitates, "— well off, for a schoolmaster." The questions of a man pricing a witness.)*
> *("What does he look like?" "Ordinary," Élise says. "That's the thing. Ordinary coat, ordinary hat, ordinary face. The kind you'd forget." She sets the violets down. "The Crown's boy says he's from London. The carrier says he asked about parcels. Mrs. Pike's girl says he tried to buy her a ribbon and asked about French poetry." A beat. "Mrs. Pike's girl," Élise adds, "told him her grandmother was French and taught her a verse. There is no French grandmother. The girl's family is from Derby." Rose laughs despite everything. "The village is lying to him." "The village," Élise says, "is enjoying itself.")*

scenes.synopsis: the debrief — what the stranger wants; Élise's network, tasked.
scenes.prose:
> *("Tell me exactly," Rose says. "Every question, every answer the village gave." Élise counts on her fingers. "He asked where Harrow lodges. His keeping; the village knows it, and told him. He asked his habits: walks, church, the Crown on Fridays. He asked his friends —" she stops. "What did they say?" "They said Mr. Harrow's friends are his books." A pause. "And?" "And the blacksmith said his keeping is haunted." Rose stares. "Haunted?" "The blacksmith," Élise says solemnly, "has decided his keeping is haunted, and has told the stranger so at length. The stranger wrote it down." They look at each other, and the laughter comes, helpless, the first of the day.)*
> *(When it passes, Rose is brisk. "Élise. I need eyes on him. Not close — I don't want him knowing he's watched. The Crown's boy, the carrier, Mrs. Pike's girl. What he asks, what he writes down, where his letters go." Élise nods, the flower-seller's face settling into something older. "And if he approaches Harrow?" "He won't," Rose says. "Not yet. He's still pricing." She touches the violets. "But if he does —" "You'll know before he knocks," Élise says. The network, tasked. The stranger, watched by a village that's enjoying itself.)*

scenes.synopsis: Julian's anger — the suitor hears of the blind item; the old fury, leashed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian arrives at four, having ridden over at speed, and he has the look he wore at Brighton the year he nearly killed a man over a card game. "Show me," he says. Rose shows him the four lines. He reads them once, and the Brighton look deepens. "I'll —" he starts. "You'll what?" Rose says. "Ride to London? Find Pounce? The man prints filth for a living, Julian. You can't duel a printing press." "I can buy it," he says. "The paper. I've the money." She looks at him: the eagerness, the fury, the complete misunderstanding of the weapon.)*
> *("Sit down," she says. He sits, which surprises them both. "The blind item is a probe. If you buy the paper, or threaten the printer, or do anything at all dramatic, that's the flinch. That's the confirmation." He looks at her, the fury visibly leashing itself. "So we do nothing." "We do nothing," Rose agrees, "that they can see." A beat. Then, grudging: "The grey suits you." "It's the archive," Rose says. "Dressed for a siege." He nods slowly. "Next to you," he says. "Not in front." "Next to," she agrees. The suitor, steadied. The fury, banked.)*

scenes.synopsis: the law — what a blind item can and can't do; the solicitor's counsel, dry.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill comes at five, summoned by the same galloping note, and reads the four lines with a solicitor's face, which is to say no face at all. "It's nothing," he says at last. "Legally. No names, no sums, no actionable statement. 'We hear' is the whole defense." He folds the sheet. "What it is, practically, is a beginning. They'll follow it. Next week, or the week after, with more." He looks at Rose. "The question for you is whether you want to be ahead of it or behind it.")*
> *("Ahead," Rose says. "Then you need to know what they have," Quill says. "A blind item means they lack proof. Proof, in this case, means the papers. So the papers are the ground. Hold the ground." He stands. "One more thing. If anyone offers to sell you the story — to suppress it, to manage it, to tell it kindly — that's a transaction. Transactions leave records. Records are evidence." He takes his hat. "Don't buy anything, Rose. Don't sell anything. Hold the ground." The law, stated. The ground, named.)*

scenes.synopsis: the mend, examined — the glove's history; fashion as doctrine, restated.
scenes.prose:
> *(Before dinner she stands at the glass and examines the mend properly for the first time in years: the tiny stitches, even as print, her grandmother's hand along her grandfather's — no, along her own thumb now. The gloves were the grandmother's; the wearing is Rose's. That's the doctrine of heirlooms: they don't stay in drawers. They're worn, mended, worn again, until the wearing is the inheritance. The dove grey silk, re-cut this spring, moves the way silk moves when it's been kept well: like water, like memory, like money.)*
> *(She thinks about what the hunters are buying: eyes, ears, a gutter sheet. What they're buying against: this. A house that dresses its wounds fashionably. A woman who wears the scar outward. Let them read the grey. Let them read the mend. Let them try to price what isn't for sale. She turns from the glass, the silk settling, the glove's mend catching the light one last time. She will show them the grey, the mend, the house in its archive dress — and nothing else, nothing they haven't earned. That is the other doctrine, and it is hers.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the scar, the season's answer; worn outward, always.

fashionChoices.label: Mend as private
fashionChoices.detail: the scar, kept for herself; the world gets the silk.

fashionChoices.label: Letitia's finishing touch
fashionChoices.detail: the quartermaster's eye.

scenes.synopsis: Bell's counsel — four lines is the fitting; the Gazette's proprietor, unmoved.
scenes.prose:
> *(Bell comes at six, uninvited and unsurprised, with ink on her cuffs and the week's Gazette already put to bed. She reads the blind item once, snorts, and hands it back. "Four lines," she says. "That's the fitting. Pounce prints the shape, watches who flinches, then prints the flinch." She helps herself to tea. "It's bought ink, Miss Hartwell. Someone's paying for the advertisement. The question is whether you're the customer or the goods." Rose, despite everything, smiles. "Charming." "I deal in print," Bell says. "Charm costs extra.")*
> *("What do I do?" Rose asks. "Nothing Pounce can see," Bell says. "That's the whole of it. You don't answer blind items. Answering is the flinch." She sets down the cup. "But you prepare. Because the next one won't be blind. The next one will have a name in it, or a sum, and then the probe becomes a story." She looks at Rose levelly. "When it's a story, Miss Hartwell, you come to me. Not because I'm your friend — though I am — but because my press is the only one in England that prints what's true." She goes. The counsel remains, the fitting named, the press offered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the money, traced — a London factor's draft; the account name: Vane.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill arrives at seven with his leather case and the face of a man carrying a number. "The advertisement," he says, without preamble, "was paid for. Pounce's books are not as private as Pounce thinks." He lays a paper on the desk: a factor's draft, London, drawn on an account in the name of Vane. "One hundred pounds," Quill says. "For 'advertising services.' That's the blind item, bought and paid for." Rose looks at the name. Vane. "Who is Mrs. Vane?" "Nobody knows," Quill says. "Which is itself information. Money that clean, that quiet, with a name nobody knows — that's managed money. Someone's managing it.")*
> *("Can you trace it further?" "I can try," Quill says. "Factors' drafts leave paper. But managed money is managed precisely so the paper stops somewhere boring." He taps the draft. "This stops at a London factor's desk. Beyond that —" he shrugs, the solicitor's shrug, "— beyond that is fog, and fog is expensive to walk in." Rose studies the name. Vane. Four letters, no face. "Walk in it anyway," she says. "Carefully." Quill nods, and puts the draft in his case. The money, traced one step. The name, obtained. The fog, beyond.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE BLIND ITEM: answer it, starve it, or feed it; the probe, handled.
scenes.prose:
> *(Night. The blind item sits in the drawer, folded precisely, and the question of what to do with it won't wait for morning. Three handlings offer themselves. Answer it: write to the Lash, or to Bell, or to London generally — deny, correct, explain. The honest impulse. But the solicitor's rule holds: answering is the flinch, and a denial confirms the shape. Starve it: say nothing, do nothing, let the four lines die of inattention. The discipline of the unflinching. But starvation takes time, and Pounce's next item is already being set. Feed it: give the village's misinformation a push — the haunted keeping, the French grandmother from Derby, the poetry. Let the stranger's notebook fill with nonsense. The weaponization of the probe. But feeding is a kind of answering, and lies have a way of surfacing.)*
> *(She stands at the drawer and thinks of Bell: four lines is the fitting. Of Octavia: the flinch is the confirmation. Of Letitia: the house that flinches at four lines will not survive forty. The handling, chosen, becomes the week's doctrine.)*
> *(Her answer to the probe: a letter, silence, or ghosts. The drawer closed on the folded sheet. Whatever Pounce printed next, it would not be her flinch.)*

options.label: Answer it
options.detail: *Candor+; the denial, issued.* Write the correction; deny the shape; explain the wall. *(Honest, and the honesty confirms the aim; Pounce prints the flinch.)*

options.label: Starve it
options.detail: *Composure+; the silence, kept.* Nothing said, nothing done; let four lines die unattended. *(Disciplined, and slow; the next item is already in type.)*

options.label: Feed it
options.detail: *Cunning+; the nonsense, encouraged.* Push the village's lies; fill the stranger's notebook with ghosts. *(Delicious, and risky; lies surface, and surface near truth.)*

scenes.synopsis: the readers, named — who reads blind items; Octavia on being read by strangers.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia stays for dinner, and over the soup she talks about readers. "Blind items are read by everyone and believed by no one," she says. "That's their nature. The town reads them the way it reads the weather: interested, uncommitted." She lays down her spoon. "But the people who paid for it — they're not reading the item. They're reading you. Your silence, your household, your village. You're being read, Rose, by readers you've never met." She looks at her friend: the grey silk, the mended glove, the woman being read like a book.)*
> *("Then let them read something worth reading," Rose says. "That's the spirit," Octavia says. "But know this: being read changes the reader's subject. You will start performing the unflinching, instead of being it. Watch for that." She takes up her spoon. "The performance is fine — it's armor. Just don't mistake it for the thing underneath." Rose considers the soup, the counsel, and the distinction. "What's underneath?" "A woman," Octavia says, "who is furious and frightened and doing it anyway." The readers, named. The subject, warned.)*

scenes.synopsis: the shape of the leak — who knew the papers' shape; the circle, narrowed.
scenes.prose:
> *(After dinner, the two friends narrow the circle. "Who knew the shape?" Octavia asks. "Not the papers, the shape. The wall, the ledger, the French names." Rose counts. "Letitia. You. Laurent — since the spring. Harrow, obviously. Augusta — the shape, not the sums. Henry, the shape." She stops. "Bell knows I have papers. Quill knows the shape." Octavia nods slowly. "That's eight. Eight people who could describe the shape to a stranger." "None of them would," Rose says. "Would they?" The question hangs.)*
> *("It's not one of the eight," Octavia says. "A blind item bought for a hundred pounds doesn't need a traitor. It needs a reader — someone who saw the breach in the spring, or heard the village talk, or put two and two together from the wall being rebuilt." She ticks the village: the masons, the carrier, the Crown's boy. "The circle was never eight, Rose. The circle was everyone who walked past the walled garden in April." Rose thinks of the gap in the wall, the spring, the papers carried in daylight. "So the leak is the spring itself." "The leak," Octavia says, "is that it happened where people live." The circle, widened. The leak, unfindable.)*

scenes.synopsis: Harrow, warned — Rose rides to the village at dusk; the witness hears he's interesting, or reads the four lines if Tuesday already warned him.
scenes.prose:
> *(She rides to the village at dusk, because some warnings shouldn't wait for morning. Harrow is at his keeping, marking copybooks, and he looks up with the mild surprise of a man whose door is rarely knocked at dusk. "Miss Hartwell." She doesn't waste time. If she warned him Tuesday: "The four lines," she says, and lays the Lash's blind item on the copybooks. "It's in print now — the wall, the ledger, the French money. You're about to be interesting, and I wanted you to read it before the village does." He reads it standing, the pen still in his hand. If she did not: "There's a man asking after you. In the village. Since Tuesday. Your lodgings, your habits, your friends." Harrow sets down the pen. "What kind of man?" "Ordinary," Rose says. "The forgettable kind. Élise's network is watching him." She tells him about the blind item, the four lines, the fallen wall.)*
> *(He listens without moving, and then he does the thing she will come to count on: he steadies. "The papers," he says. "He's after the papers." "He's after you," Rose corrects. "The papers are the ground. You're the way in." Harrow nods slowly. "Sixty-one years old," he says, "and I'm the way in." The dryness, intact. "What do you want me to do?" "Live your life," Rose says. "Walk, church, the Crown on Fridays. Be uninteresting. The village is telling him his keeping is haunted — let them." He almost smiles. "Haunted." "The blacksmith's idea." "The blacksmith," Harrow says, "has always been wasted on iron." The warning, delivered. The witness, steady.)*

scenes.synopsis: the papers, discussed — Harrow's half; the ground, held jointly.
scenes.prose:
> *("Show me your half is safe," Rose says. Harrow lifts the cloth on the table: the papers, his half, the grandfather's hand. "They don't leave this room," he says. "They haven't in three years." She looks at the papers, the other half of her inheritance, and feels the ground the solicitor named: the papers are the ground, and the ground is in two places. "If he knocks," she says, "you don't answer." "If he knocks," Harrow says, "I'll offer him tea and talk about the haunting. The blacksmith gave me the details." Despite everything, she laughs.)*
> *("Mr. Harrow." "Miss Hartwell." "Whatever happens, whatever they print, whatever he asks, the papers stay." "The papers stay," he agrees. "They've stayed this long." He covers them again, the cloth settling. "You know," he says, "for twenty years I thought these were my shame. Carrying them, hiding them. Now there's a man from London asking after my habits, and I find I'm —" he looks for the word, "— I'm rather proud of the habits." She looks at him: the schoolmaster, the witness, the keeper of the other half, steady as the wall being rebuilt. "The habits," she says, "are excellent." The ground, held. Jointly.)*

scenes.synopsis: the ride home — habit, horse, dusk; the fashionable equestrienne, unbowed.
scenes.prose:
> *(She rides home in the dusk in her riding habit, and the habit is worth noting: dark grey wool, cut by the best tailor in the county, the skirt's fullness managed with the kind of skill that makes riding look like dancing. The beaver hat, the veil, the gloves — the mended pair, because the doctrine doesn't stop at the stable door. On the grey mare, in the grey habit, with the park wall rising ahead, she looks like the answer to the blind item: a woman with nothing to hide and no intention of explaining herself.)*
> *(The mare's hooves beat the lane's rhythm, and Rose thinks about Harrow's steadiness, the blacksmith's haunting, Mrs. Pike's girl's French grandmother from Derby. The village is lying to the stranger, and the lies are working, and somewhere in London a woman named Vane is paying for eyes and ears. Let her pay. The eyes will see a haunted keeping. The ears will hear French poetry from Derby. The gutter sheet will print four lines, and the four lines will starve, or be answered, or be fed ghosts. She touches the mare's neck, the veil lifting. The ride, the habit, the dusk: unbowed.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the park, the wall, the evening; the ground, surveyed.

fashionChoices.detail: the household, waiting; the night, begun.

fashionChoices.detail: the wall, seen; the gap, measured.

scenes.synopsis: the stranger tries the keeping — the knock, unanswered; the haunting, deployed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise's evening report comes with the night's violets: the stranger walked to Harrow's keeping at dusk, stood off it for ten minutes, and came away without knocking. "He's still pricing," Élise says. "The Crown's boy heard him ask the carrier about parcels again. He's waiting for something. Or someone." Rose turns the violet in her fingers. "Or instructions," she says. "A man like that doesn't knock until he's told to." Élise nods. "Mrs. Pike's girl tried to sell him another ribbon. He bought it." They share the look: the village's counter-intelligence, funded by ribbon sales.)*
> *("And Harrow?" "Harrow," Élise says, "had tea, marked copybooks, and went to bed at ten. The most uninteresting evening in the history of evenings." Rose smiles. "Good. That's the doctrine." She sets the violet in water. "Double the watch," she says. "If he knocks, I want to know before the echo fades." Élise is already moving. No knock yet. The haunting waits in the wings, and Harrow is gloriously, deliberately dull.)*

scenes.synopsis: the French grandmother from Derby — the village's star liar, honored.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose walks to the village herself the next morning, on the pretext of ordering ribbon, and finds Mrs. Pike's girl behind the counter: sixteen, sharp-eyed, the heroine of the hour. "Tell me about the French poetry," Rose says. The girl recites, in atrocious French, a verse about a nightingale that is clearly about a Derby milkmaid. "My grandmother taught me," she says solemnly. "Your grandmother," Rose says, "is from Derby." "My grandmother," the girl says, "is very well-traveled." They look at each other, and the conspiracy is complete.)*
> *("He wrote it down," the girl says. "Every word. He asked if I knew other verses. I told him my grandmother knew dozens, but she only sang them when the moon was right." Rose buys three ribbons she doesn't need. "You're a credit to the village," she says. "The village," the girl says, "is a credit to itself." Walking home, Rose thinks about misinformation: the blacksmith's haunted keeping, the French grandmother, the poetry. The stranger's notebook is filling with Derby. Somewhere in London, Mrs. Vane is paying for this. The thought sustains her all the way home.)*

scenes.synopsis: Laurent learns of the probe — the émigré's son; the fury, first seen.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent comes at noon, having heard from Élise, and the black coat is on, and the fury is already in the room before he speaks. "They printed it," he says. "Four lines. About —" he can't finish. "About the wall," Rose says. "About the ledger. About French names." She shows him the item. He reads it, and the fury does what fury does in the young: it looks for a target. "Who?" "We don't know. A woman named Vane pays the money. A man from London asks the questions. Pounce prints the lines." Laurent's hands close. "I'll —" "You'll do nothing," Rose says, "that they can see.")*
> *("It's my family they're pricing," he says. "The de Varennes. My mother's name, in a gutter sheet." "It's my family too," Rose says quietly. "The sin was my grandfather's. The papers are in my drawer. The stranger is asking after my witness." She looks at him: the émigré's son, the fury, the youth. "I know what it costs to read those four lines. I read them standing up, and then I sat down. But if you do anything — anything — that's the flinch, and the flinch is the confirmation." He breathes, once, hard. "The coat," he says at last. "Your grandmother's doctrine. Stitch by stitch." "Stitch by stitch," she agrees. The fury, leashed. For now.)*

scenes.synopsis: the task — Laurent set to watch the wall's masons; the fury, given work.
scenes.prose:
> *(She gives him the masons. "The wall," she says. "Third course by Saturday. I need eyes on everyone who comes near it — not the workers, the watchers. Anyone sketching, anyone asking, anyone who doesn't belong." Laurent nods, the fury finding its work. "And if I find one?" "You tell Élise," Rose says. "You don't touch him, you don't threaten him, you tell Élise, and Élise tells me." He looks at her. "That's all?" "That's everything," she says. "The wall is the ground, Laurent. The papers are the ground. We hold the ground by watching it, not by bleeding on it.")*
> *(He goes, the black coat disappearing down the drive, and Rose watches him with the complicated feeling of someone who has just handed a young man a leash for his own anger. Octavia, in the doorway, says: "Well done." "Was it?" "He needed work, not comfort. You gave him work." They stand together, watching the drive. "He'll hold," Octavia says. "He's his mother's son." "His mother," Rose says, "is a paragraph in a gutter sheet." "Not yet," Octavia says. "Not ever, if we hold the ground." The task, given. The fury, employed.)*

scenes.synopsis: Augusta, consulted — the dowager's reading; the de Valcourt name, kept out of it.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta comes at two, unannounced, which for Augusta is announcement enough. She reads the blind item once, through her lorgnette, and sets it down. "Four lines," she says. "No names." "No names," Rose agrees. "The de Valcourt name," Augusta says. It isn't a question. "Stays out," Rose says. "Whatever comes. My word on it." Augusta studies her: the grey silk, the mended glove, the woman holding the ground. "Your grandfather," she says at last, "was a fool about money and a gentleman about debts. Remember the second part." She rises. The audience, over.)*
> *(At the door she turns. "The woman. Vane." "We know the name. Nothing else." Augusta nods once. "Money with no face is usually a face with no courage," she says. "Find the face." She goes, leaving the counsel like a calling card. Rose stands with the lorgnette's ghost on the table and thinks about the dowager's two sentences: the gentleman about debts, the face with no courage. The kinship, light as ever. The boundary, firm as ever. The de Valcourt name, out of it.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's velvet — fashion as armor, at Augusta's age; the archive, modeled.
scenes.prose:
> *(What Augusta wears to a crisis is worth recording: dark blue velvet, twenty years old, cut when waists were waists and skirts meant it, the silver embroidery at the cuffs still bright. She wears it the way she wears everything: as if fashion were a form of government. "You stare," she says, catching Rose's eye. "I admire," Rose says. "At my age," Augusta says, "admiration is the only tribute that matters." They take tea in the morning room, two women in archive dress, twenty years apart in fashion and not at all apart in doctrine.)*
> *("The grey becomes you," Augusta says. "It became my grandmother first," Rose says. "Then it becomes you second. That's how archives work." Augusta inclines her head, conceding the point. "Dress the siege, Rose. The town reads clothes before it reads sheets. Let them read that the house is not —" she looks for the word, "— not diminished." Rose looks at the velvet, the silver, the government of fashion. "Not diminished," she agrees. The lesson, taken. The archive, modeled at the highest level.)*

fashionChoices.label: Velvet's lesson
fashionChoices.detail: dress every siege as if the town is watching — it is.

fashionChoices.label: Grey's answer
fashionChoices.detail: the grandmother's doctrine; the archive, worn.

fashionChoices.label: Augusta's eye
fashionChoices.detail: let the dowager dress the next occasion.

scenes.synopsis: the haunting — the blacksmith's masterpiece; misinformation, at scale.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose walks to the forge at four, on the pretext of a loose shoe, and the blacksmith tells her about the haunting at length: the lights, the French voices, the cold spot by the hearth. He has, in two days, invented a complete supernatural history for Harrow's keeping. "And the stranger?" Rose asks. "Wrote it all down," the blacksmith says, with the satisfaction of an artist. "Asked if the voices spoke French. I told him they spoke the French of the old country, very pure." "The old country being?" "Derby," the blacksmith says solemnly. Rose laughs until the forge rings.)*
> *(Walking home, she thinks about what's been built: a haunted keeping, a French grandmother, poetry from Derby, ribbons as counter-intelligence funding. The village has, without being asked, constructed a complete false countryside for the stranger to report. She carries it up the drive, past the wall's third course, into the house — the whole false countryside, bought and paid for by Mrs. Vane's money, built by the village out of spite and poetry.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — HARROW'S KEEPING: bring him inside, leave him in the village, or arm him with knowledge; the witness, placed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Evening. The stranger is still pricing, still watching his keeping, and the question of Harrow won't wait: the witness is the way in, and the way in must be guarded. Three keepings offer themselves. Bring him inside: Hartwell's gates, Hartwell's roof, the household's guard. Safe behind stone. But a schoolmaster moved into the great house is a visible move, and visible moves are flinches the village will read. Leave him in the village: his keeping, the habits, the uninteresting evenings. The cover of the ordinary. But the ordinary is where the stranger is watching, and Saturday's pressure will fall on Harrow first. Arm him with knowledge: tell him everything, the full shape of the papers, the Vane money, the Saturday timetable. Make him a partner, not a protected thing. Knowledge is armor. But armor is heavy, and Harrow is sixty-one.)*
> *(She rides to his keeping at dusk and puts it to him plainly. He listens, the lamp lit, the copybooks stacked, and then he says the thing that decides it: "Miss Hartwell, I've kept half the sin for twenty years without knowing the whole of it. If knowing the whole would help me keep it better —" he stops. "Tell me what I need," he says. "No more, no less." She looks at him, the steady hands, the schoolmaster's face, and chooses his keeping.)*
> *(She placed the witness the way she'd placed everything that week: deliberately, and where he could stand it. Harrow nodded at the placing, the lamp lit, the copybooks stacked. Whatever the stranger did next, the keeping would hold.)*

options.label: Bring him inside
options.detail: *Resolve+; the gates, opened.* Hartwell's roof, the household's guard; safety behind stone. *(Visible, and the village reads visible; the flinch, communal.)*

options.label: Leave him in the village
options.detail: *Composure+; the ordinary, defended.* His keeping, the habits, the uninteresting evenings. *(The stranger watches the ordinary; Saturday's pressure falls on Harrow first.)*

options.label: Arm him with knowledge
options.detail: *Trust+; the partner, made.* Tell him the whole shape; make him a partner, not a protected thing. *(Knowledge is armor; armor is heavy, and he is sixty-one.)*

scenes.synopsis: the keeping, enacted — whatever was chosen, the witness is settled; the night watch, arranged.
scenes.prose:
> *(What she chose, she enacts. If Hartwell: the spare room made up, the gates' routine explained, Harrow's books carried up in a hamper. If the village: the watch doubled, Élise's boy on the lane, the blacksmith's haunting on standby. If knowledge: the whole shape, told plainly over tea: the Vane money, the Saturday timetable, the three doors not yet named. Whichever keeping, Harrow takes it the way he takes everything: steadily. "Thank you," he says. "For not —" he looks for the word, "— for not managing me." "You're sixty-one," Rose says. "You've earned unmanagement.")*
> *(Riding home in the dark, she thinks about the witness: the schoolmaster who carried half the sin for twenty years and is now, by choice or by placement, in the middle of the siege. The stranger wants him. The village guards him. The household — forty pairs of mending hands and counting — holds him. She touches the mended glove, the thumb's scar. The keeping, enacted. The witness, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the siege mood — the servants' hall; the household, braced and mending.
scenes.prose:
> *(The servants' hall at nine is the household's parliament, and the mood is siege: the good silver counted, the gates' routine reviewed, the watch roster pinned up. Letitia presides, the quartermaster in her element. "Nobody," she says, "talks to strangers about the family. Nobody answers questions about the wall, the papers, or Mr. Harrow. Anyone asks, the answer is: the wall's third course by Saturday." A beat. "And his keeping?" someone asks. "Haunted," Letitia says firmly. "The blacksmith has the details." The hall laughs, the siege-laugh, short and warm.)*
> *(Rose stands in the doorway, unannounced, and the hall quiets. She doesn't make a speech. She says: "Thank you." Two words. The hall hears the whole of it: the trust, the siege, the forty pairs of hands. Then she says: "Saturday's gloves get an extra stitch. For luck." The hall laughs again, longer this time, and the mending baskets come out, and the evening's work begins. The mood, braced. The household, mending.)*

scenes.synopsis: the porter's report — Amos sees everyone; the stranger's letters, counted.
scenes.prose:
> *(Amos the porter has held the gates for thirty years, and he sees everyone. "The stranger," he reports at ten, "has written four letters. The carrier takes them. London direction." He counts on his fingers. "Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, today. Four letters in four days." Rose considers. "And received?" "Two," Amos says. "Wednesday and today. The today's came by the afternoon post. He read it in the Crown's yard." A pause. "He didn't like it, miss. Whatever it said." The porter's reading of faces, thirty years honed.)*
> *("Four letters out, two in," Rose says. "He's reporting, and being instructed." She thinks of the Vane money, the managed funds, the face with no courage. "Amos. I need the carrier's direction — where in London the letters go. Can you ask?" Amos looks offended. "Miss, I can ask the carrier anything. He owes me for the foaling." The porter's network, older than Élise's and nearly as good. "Ask him," Rose says. "Carefully." Amos touches his hat. The letters, counted. The direction, sought.)*

scenes.synopsis: the mending ritual — the household mends together; forty pairs; the chapter's ritual.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the baskets — "forty pairs, miss. The household's uniform.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, threading a needle — "I haven't mended since I was twelve. It comes back like riding.")*
> *(Story morsel: Harrow, at the door — come from the village, the spare glove in his pocket.)*
> *(Story morsel: Rose, at the lamp — "stitch by stitch. That's the whole doctrine, and it's enough.")*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the door — "Saturday's gloves get the extra stitch. For luck.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: The probe has been answered with discipline, the witness is placed, and the stranger is still pricing. Tonight the household does what it does best: it mends. Forty pairs of gloves, forty pairs of hands, the servants' hall by lamplight. Dress for the work: the archive's finest, fashionable and deliberate — mending is not plain work, and the house does not under-dress its doctrine. Precise. Together. Unafraid. The house that mends together does not flinch apart.

scenes.synopsis: the violet's meaning — faithfulness, restated; the household's emblem, worn.
scenes.prose:
> *(After the ritual she keeps one violet back, and holds it to the lamp in the empty hall. Faithfulness. The season's flower. Forty wrists wore it tonight; forty-one, counting Harrow's spare glove in his pocket. She thinks about what the flower means, applied to the week: not loyalty to the grandfather, who doesn't deserve it. Not loyalty to the secret, which is a burden, not a virtue. Loyalty to the people the secret touched. The witness. The village. The household. The friends.)*
> *(She pins the violet inside her bodice, where it won't be seen, which is where faithfulness belongs: not displayed, but carried. The hall is empty, the baskets stacked, the lamps low. The stranger is at the Crown, writing his fourth letter. Mrs. Vane's money is buying eyes and ears. And here, in the servants' hall, forty pairs of mended gloves lie folded like a small army's uniforms. She blows out the last lamp. The emblem, worn. The army, uniformed.)*

scenes.synopsis: evening — archive dress for dinner; the grey, worn like a verdict.
scenes.prose:
> *(She dresses for dinner in the grey silk's full statement: the re-cut bodice, the embroidered hem, the grandmother's pearls at the throat, the mended gloves. In the glass, the siege's fashionable face. Letitia, fastening the pearls, says: "The town can read grey." "The town," Rose says, "is reading." They go down together, the mistress and the quartermaster, and the dining room rises — Julian, Octavia, Henry, Augusta — and the evening begins the way evenings begin when the house is holding its breath: with excellent soup.)*
> *(The talk is ordinary, deliberately: the wall's third course, the canal's levels, the blacksmith's apprentice. But underneath runs the week's current: the four lines, the stranger, the Vane money, the Saturday timetable nobody's named yet. Rose looks down the table at her people — the grey silk bright among them, the mended glove lifting the glass — and feels the thing she felt in the servants' hall: not strategy, but the thing underneath. Her household. Her forty. Whatever the hunters print, it prints about people who mend gloves together. That is not nothing. That is nearly everything.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — VANE'S MONEY: chase it, watch its spending, or bluff the investigation; the hunters' funds, handled.
scenes.prose:
> *(Night. The name sits in Quill's case, in the draft for a hundred pounds' worth of advertising services: Vane. Money with no face, managed by someone, buying eyes, ears, and a gutter sheet. Three handlings offer themselves. Chase it: fund Quill's walk through the fog — the factor's books, the drafts, the London desks. Find the face. Expensive, slow, and the fog is managed precisely to defeat walking. Watch its spending: don't chase the source, watch the mouth — the stranger's letters, Pounce's books, the next purchase. Follow the money forward, not back. Patient, and the spending will declare itself. Bluff the investigation: let it be known, in the village and in London, that the money is being traced. The hunters, told they're hunted, may hurry, and hurried hunters make mistakes. But bluffs can be called, and a called bluff is a flinch.)*
> *(She stands at the window with Quill's draft copied in her memorandum book, and thinks of Augusta: money with no face is usually a face with no courage. Find the face. The handling, chosen, becomes the week's second doctrine.)*
> *(The money, handled her way: chased, watched, or bluffed. The memorandum book closed on the copied draft. Whatever Mrs. Vane bought next, it would be bought under observation.)*

options.label: Chase it
options.detail: *Resolve+; the fog, walked.* Fund Quill's tracing: factors' books, drafts, London desks. *(Find the face; the fog is managed to defeat walking, and walking is slow.)*

options.label: Watch its spending
