scenes.synopsis: the order, received — Octavia receives the order decision; the affection, again.
scenes.prose:
> *(She shows Octavia the chosen order, and Octavia receives it precisely. "Harrow first," she says, reading the choice. Or: "The émigrés first." Or: "All together." Whichever Rose chose, Octavia nods. "Defensible," she says. Or: "Honest." Or: "Brave." She adjusts the figures, the neat hand moving. "You know what I like about this?" she says. "You didn't take the easy order. Most people, given three sequences, take the one that flatters them and call it judgment." She looks up. "You chose like someone who intends to pay.")*
> *("I do intend to pay," Rose says. "I know," Octavia says. "That's the affection, by the way. Not the numbers. The intending." She closes the ledger. "Whatever door you take, Rose —" she stops. "Whatever door. The order was worth choosing. A woman should know the price of things, even the things she doesn't buy." The order, received. The intending, noted.)*

scenes.synopsis: Laurent, told of the creditors — the de Varennes, named as creditors; the son, steadied.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent comes at four, and Rose tells him the de Varenne figure: twelve hundred, over ten years, from the canal. He is quiet a long time. Then: "Creditors." "Creditors," Rose confirms. "Not victims. Your cousins in London, paid like any creditors." He looks at her: the grey silk, the pearls, the woman pricing his family's ruin like a bill. "My mother," he says slowly, "would have liked the word. Creditors." A pause. "She never liked charity." "It's not charity," Rose says. "It's debt. That's the difference." He nods, once. "Then I —" he stops. "Thank you. For the counting.")*
> *(They stand a moment in the hall, the émigré's son and the sinner's granddaughter, and the fury of the week has gone somewhere quieter: into the figures. "Ten years," Laurent says. "I'll be —" he calculates, "— thirty-two." "You'll be a creditor's cousin," Rose says, "which is a respectable thing." He almost smiles. "The coat," he says. "Stitch by stitch." "Stitch by stitch," she agrees. The son, steadied. The creditors, named.)*

scenes.synopsis: the son's question — what restitution means for the émigré name; the answer, careful.
scenes.prose:
> *("Miss Hartwell," Laurent says, and the formality means the question is real. "If you pay — when you pay — what does it make us? The de Varennes." Rose considers. "It makes you creditors," she says. "Paid creditors. Which is what you were, before the fall: people owed money, not people pitied." He nods slowly. "And my grandfather? The one who entrusted?" "A man who trusted," Rose says carefully, "and was betrayed by the trustee. The ledger says so. The trust's founding paper will say so." She looks at him. "The shame was never yours, Laurent. The ledger proves it.")*
> *("The ledger proves it," he repeats. He stands straighter, the black coat settling. "Twenty years my family has carried this like a shame. And it's —" he looks for the word, "— it's an account." "It's an account," Rose agrees. "And accounts get settled." He looks at her a long moment. "Stitch by stitch," he says, and goes. The question, answered. The name, restored to creditor.)*

scenes.synopsis: the black coat, noted — the émigré's son, dressed for the accounting; fashion, filial.
scenes.prose:
> *(What Laurent wears to the accounting is worth noting: his father's black coat, brushed and mended, the cuffs turned back to show the lining's repair. He wears it the way his father wore it: as a uniform. "The coat," Rose says. "Your father's." "My father's," he agrees. "He wore it to count the losses, in the bad year. I wear it to count the repayment." The filial fashion, stated. The coat has outlasted the ruin and will outlast the restitution.)*
> *(Rose looks at him: the young man in the old coat, standing straighter. Fashion, at its best, is inheritance worn deliberately. The black coat, the grey silk, the mended gloves: the accounting has its uniform, and the uniform is the archive. "It becomes you," she says. "It became my father first," he says. "Then it becomes me second. That's how coats work." The echo of Augusta's lesson, returned. The son, dressed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Gazette and the restitution — what Bell prints about a paid debt.
scenes.prose:
> *(Bell comes at five, summoned by a note, and hears the price: forty-one thousand six hundred, ten years, the trust. She listens without interrupting, which for Bell is respect. "A paid debt," she says at last. "That's a story." She ticks the angles on her fingers. "One: the heiress pays her grandfather's debts. Two: the émigré creditors, made whole. Three: the trust, founded, public, clean." She looks at Rose. "It's the only story Pounce can't print first, because it's yours to tell. He can print the sin. He can't print the payment. The payment hasn't happened yet.")*
> *("And if I choose another door?" "Then it's a shorter story," Bell says. "Expose: the sin, told truly. Bury: no story at all." She stands. "But the restitution story —" she pauses, "— the restitution story is the one where the Gazette gets to print the word 'creditors' instead of 'victims.' I like that word." She goes, leaving the angles. The story, previewed. The word, liked.)*

scenes.synopsis: the trust's founding — Quill on the public act; the paper, prepared.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill dines with them, and over the soup he talks about the trust's founding as a public act. "The paper will be read," he says. "In London. By the very people who are paying Pounce." He lays down his spoon. "That's not a drawback. That's the weapon. A trust founded to pay émigré debts is a fact. Facts are harder to print around than silences." He looks at Rose. "Pounce's Saturday issue prints the sin. Your trust's founding prints the payment. The town will compare the two, and the town can count.")*
> *("The town can count," Rose repeats. "The town," Quill says, "counts money better than it counts morals. Give it money to count." Octavia, down the table, lifts her glass. "To the town's arithmetic," she says. They drink. The founding, framed. The weapon, identified: a fact.)*

scenes.synopsis: Augusta, told of the acknowledgment — the de Valcourt sum, received lightly.
scenes.prose: > *(Augusta is told after dinner, privately, in the hall. "Twenty-eight hundred," Rose says. "Folded into the trust. Acknowledged by name. Paid over the ten years." Augusta nods, once. "Light," she says. "As agreed." A pause. "The founding paper. What does it say, exactly?" "That the de Valcourts are creditors of the trust," Rose says. "No more." Augusta studies her. "No narrative." "No narrative." "Good." She turns to go, then turns back. "Your grandmother," she says, "once settled a debt of your grandfather's without telling him. He found out at Christmas. She said, 'The ledger needed it.'" A pause. "The ledger needed it," Rose repeats. "The ledger," Augusta says, "always needs it." She goes. The acknowledgment, received. Lightly.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Park's stones — the entail, walked; what can't be sold, seen.
scenes.prose:
> *(After dinner she walks the Park's boundary in the dusk, the grey silk dark against the hedges. The stones: the wall, the gate piers, the ha-ha, the bridge. The entail holds them all; they can't be sold, and Octavia's price doesn't ask them to be. Eight thousand from the surplus, three thousand a year from the canal. The Park stands outside the arithmetic, untouched. She touches the gate pier, cool and solid. "Not you," she says to the stone. "Never you." The stone, obliging, says nothing.)*
> *(She thinks about what the boundary means: the restitution is paid from the fortune's surplus and the canal's income — from what the estate earns and what it holds above its needs. Not from the Park's stones. Not from the roofs. The house pays its debts without diminishing itself. That is the difference between atonement and ruin: atonement leaves the house standing. She walks home in the dusk, the stones behind her, untouched. The boundary, walked. The line, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the village's view — Élise on the price; what forty-one thousand six hundred means downhill.
scenes.prose: > *(Élise comes with the night's dried violets and stays for the news. "Forty-one thousand six hundred," Rose says. Élise whistles, low. "That's —" she calculates, "— that's four hundred cottages." "It's ten years," Rose says. "And it's owed." Élise nods slowly. "The village will like it," she says. "The village likes a debt paid. We don't like debts." She sets the dried violets down. "Will they know? The village." "The trust's founding is public," Rose says. "They'll know." "Good," Élise says. "The village should know the big house pays." The downhill view, taken. The paying, approved.)*

scenes.synopsis: the affection, restated — why Octavia counted; the friend's stake.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes to the study at nine, without the ledger, and the conversation is the affection without the precision. "You asked me once," she says, "why I count things. It was after my father died, and the Harrington accounts were a mess, and I was twenty-two." She looks at the fire. "Counting was how I loved him. Doing the sums right, because he'd taught me. That's all." She looks up. "I counted your price the same way. Precisely, because I love you. The affection isn't separate from the precision. It is the precision.")*
> *("Octavia." "I know," she says. "Too much?" "Not enough," Rose says. They sit a moment in the firelight, the friends, the price between them like a third person they've both agreed to love. "Whatever door," Octavia says. "Whatever door," Rose agrees. The affection, restated. The counting, loved.)*

scenes.synopsis: evening — the grey, worn like a verdict; the price, dressed.
scenes.prose:
> *(She keeps the grey for the evening, and the grey has changed meaning through the day: morning, it was the accounting dress; now it is the verdict's color. The price, heard and held. The dove silk, the pearls, the mended glove: the woman who knows what things cost. Letitia, dressing her for dinner, says: "You look like the ledger." "Is that good?" "The ledger," Letitia says, "is the most honest thing in the house." They go down, and the dining room receives the verdict's color with the respect it deserves.)*
> *(The talk at dinner is the price, discussed openly for the first time: the hundred and fifty, the twelve hundred, the twenty-eight hundred, the ten years. The household hears the sums and nods. The sums are large, and the household is not frightened of large sums. The household is frightened of unpaid ones. "To the clean ledger," Julian says, lifting his glass. "In ten years," Octavia says. "To ten years," the table says. The price, worn. The verdict, dressed.)*

fashionChoices.label: Grey, verdict
fashionChoices.detail: the color, worn as the answer.

fashionChoices.label: Pearls, bright
fashionChoices.detail: the heirloom, through the toasts.

fashionChoices.label: Letitia's eye
fashionChoices.detail: the quartermaster judges the table.

scenes.synopsis: the three doors, laid out — with the price known, each door's cost is clear.
scenes.prose:
> *(After dinner, the two friends lay out the three doors with the price in hand. "Expose," Octavia says. "Cost: the telling. The Gazette prints the true account. Harrow is 'the accomplice' for a week. The de Varennes are a story. The price," she taps the ledger, "is unpaid, because exposure isn't payment." "Bury," Rose says. "Cost: the conscience. The papers burn. The agents lose their proof. Harrow keeps his roof, the de Varennes keep their ruin, and I," she stops. "And you live with it," Octavia finishes. "The price uncounted, because there's nothing to count.")*
> *("Atone," Octavia says. "Cost: forty-one thousand six hundred, ten years, the canal's income. Harrow paid, the de Varennes creditors, the de Valcourts acknowledged. The price" — she rests her hand on the ledger — "the price is the point. It's the only door where the sin is paid for." They sit with the three doors, priced and unpriced. "The choosing," Rose says, "is Sunday." "The choosing," Octavia agrees, "is Sunday. Saturday is Pounce's." The doors, laid out. The costs, clear.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE DISCLOSURE: how the paying is announced — all at once, in stages, or not yet; the schedule, presented.
scenes.prose:
> *(Night. The price is known, the order is chosen, and the structure is fixed (eight thousand eight hundred now, three thousand a year for ten years, thirty-eight thousand eight hundred to pay), but how the paying is announced is Rose's to decide. Three disclosures offer themselves. All at once: publish the trust's founding with the full schedule, the creditors named, the ten years laid open. The bold stroke: Pounce can't print a secret that's already public. But boldness invites scrutiny, and scrutiny invites the question of why it took forty years. In stages: announce Harrow's hundred and fifty now, his keeping deeded (the living debt, settled), and let the émigré trust's founding follow quietly, creditor by creditor. The controlled release. But staged news looks like managed news, and Pounce manages news for a living. Not yet: sign nothing public, announce nothing; let the trust work privately and let Saturday's Pounce print his lie unanswered. The silent door. But silence is what the wall was, and the wall is what she's unchoosing.)*
> *(She stands at the ledger with Quill's draft trust beside it, and thinks of Harrow: "Then choose it." Of Laurent: "Creditors." Of Octavia: the shape of the next ten years. The disclosure, chosen, becomes the announcement.)*
> *(The disclosure was hers: boldly, carefully, or not at all. The trust's paper waited for her word. Whatever Saturday printed, the paying would have its own voice — hers.)*

options.label: All at once
options.detail: *Resolve+; the bold stroke.* The full schedule published, the creditors named; no secret to print. *(Boldness invites scrutiny; forty years will be asked about.)*

options.label: In stages
options.detail: *Prudence+; the controlled release.* Harrow now, the émigrés quietly after; the news, managed. *(Staged news looks managed; Pounce manages news for a living.)*

options.label: Not yet
options.detail: *Patience+; the silent door.* The trust works privately; Saturday's lie goes unanswered. *(Silence was the wall; the wall is what she's unchoosing.)*

scenes.synopsis: the schedule, drafted — Quill writes the trust to the chosen shape; the paper, prepared.
scenes.prose:
> *(She sends for Quill at dawn, and the chosen disclosure becomes the draft. He writes it in the solicitor's hand: the émigré trust, founded with the eight thousand eight hundred, fed by the canal's three thousand a year for ten years — and the announcement shaped to her choosing: published whole, released in stages, or held silent until Sunday. The founding paper names the creditors: the de Varennes, by name; the de la Roches; the de Brissacs; the de Valcourts, already promised and acknowledged. Harrow's deed, separate. He reads it back, and the legal language does what legal language does: it makes the intention real.)*
> *("Sign?" he asks. "Not yet," Rose says. "The choosing is Sunday. The paper waits for the door." Quill nods, and puts the unsigned draft in his case. "It'll keep," he says. "Paper is patient." She watches him down the drive. The schedule, drafted. The paper, waiting for the door.)*

scenes.synopsis: the servants' view — the household hears the price; the mending table, consulted.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia reports the servants' hall's view at noon: the household has heard the price — forty-one thousand six hundred, ten years — and the hall's verdict is unanimous. "The house pays," Letitia says. "That's the view. The Harringtons paid for ten years, and nobody thought the worse of them." She pauses. "The mending table has a question." "Ask it." "Will the paying change the household? Fewer hands, plainer table?" Rose shakes her head. "The bread is not in it. The canal pays. The surplus pays. The household stands as it is." Letitia nods. "Then the table's answer is: ten years is nothing. We've mended longer.")*
> *(Rose looks at her quartermaster: the household, consulted and consenting. "Tell the table," she says, "that Saturday's gloves get the extra stitch. For luck." "Already ordered," Letitia says. The view, taken. The consent, given.)*

scenes.synopsis: night — the ledger by lamplight; the wrapper, the dried violet, the figures.
scenes.prose:
> *(The bedroom, late. She wears the grey silk's wrapper over her nightdress, the pearls still at her throat — she forgot to take them off, or chose not to — and reads Octavia's ledger by lamplight. The figures, in the neat hand: £150. £1,200. £2,800. £41,600. They are beautiful, the way things exactly faced are beautiful. Élise's dried violet lies on the ledger's open page, faithfulness on the figures. She touches the dried violet, the paper, the pearls: the three textures of the day.)*
> *(She closes the ledger and sets the dried violet on its cover. Tomorrow is Saturday. Pounce's issue. The stranger's next move. The price, known and held. She unpins her hair, the pearls finally coiled, the wrapper exchanged for the nightdress. The lamp lowered. The figures, kept. She sleeps.)*

fashionChoices.label: Dream in figures
fashionChoices.detail: the sums, kept in sleep; the ledger, balanced.

fashionChoices.label: Dream in grey
fashionChoices.detail: the verdict's color; tomorrow, uncolored.

fashionChoices.label: No choosing
fashionChoices.detail: sleep takes what it takes.

scenes.synopsis: the ledger ritual — the household accounts, reckoned; the price, witnessed; the chapter's ritual.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the ledger — "forty-one thousand six hundred. Say it aloud. It's less frightening spoken.")*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, with the household accounts — "the bread is not in it. I checked twice.")*
> *(Story morsel: Harrow, at the door — come from the village, the deed not yet signed, the hope already.)*
> *(Story morsel: Rose, at the slate — "ten years. The house stands it. I stand it.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the door — "the precision was the easy part. The rest is Sunday.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: The price is known: forty-one thousand six hundred pounds, ten years, the canal and the surplus. Tonight the reckoning is witnessed: the household's accounts laid open, the creditors named, the trust's shape drawn. Dress for the counting: the archive's finest, fashionable and deliberate — precision is not plain, and the house does not under-dress its debts. Exact. Affectionate. Unafraid. The house that faces its ledger does not flinch from it.

scenes.synopsis: the dried violet on the ledger — faithfulness, laid on the figures; the quiet, after the witnessing.
scenes.prose:
> *(After the ritual she sits a moment in the morning room, the ledger closed, the lamp low. Élise's dried violet lies on the cover where she left it, and Rose holds it to the light. Faithfulness. The season's flower. The figures beneath it: £150, £1,200, £2,800, £41,600. She thinks about what faithfulness means, applied to the price: not loyalty to the sums, which are just sums. Loyalty to the people the sums name. Harrow. The de Varennes. The de Valcourts, lightly. The household, whose bread is not in it. Faithfulness is not keeping the secret. It's keeping the people. It's paying the debts.)*
> *(She lays the violet back on the ledger and blows out the lamp. Tomorrow is Saturday. The price, known. The doors, laid out. The choosing, Sunday. She goes up to bed, the grey silk exchanged for the nightdress, the pearls coiled, the mended glove set out for morning. The house is quiet. The ledger is closed. The woman who knows the price sleeps the sleep of the informed, which is not the same as the decided, but nearer than it was.)*

scenes.synopsis: the quartermaster's arithmetic — Letitia on ten years; the household's view, final.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia comes at dawn with the household's final arithmetic. "Ten years," she says. "The Harringtons paid for ten years. The house stood it." She looks around the morning room. "This house will stand it better." She sets down the breakfast tray with unusual ceremony. "The servants' hall has done its own counting. Three thousand a year from the canal. That's —" she calculates, "— that's the canal's business, not ours. Our business is the mending, and the mending goes on." She pours the tea. "Ten years of mending. We've done longer.")*
> *("Tell the hall," Rose says, "that the choosing is Sunday. Whatever door, the paying is the same." Letitia nods. "The hall knows. The hall's answer is: the house pays." She goes, leaving the tea, the arithmetic, and the consent. The quartermaster's view, final. The household, standing.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE DOORS, WEIGHED: with the price known, which door leans — expose, bury, or atone.
scenes.prose:
> *(Dawn. The price is known, the schedule is drafted, and Saturday is hours away. Before the choosing — Sunday — the weighing. Three leanings offer themselves. Toward expose: the price unpaid, the truth told. The Gazette prints the true account, whole and untrimmed. The town reads it. The hunters' version dies of irrelevance. But Harrow is "the accomplice" for a week, the de Varennes are a story, and the thirty-eight thousand eight hundred stays in the canal's future, unspent. Toward bury: the papers burn, the wall rebuilds, the agents lose their proof. Nothing paid, nothing told. The household keeps its secret, and Rose keeps the cost: living with the unatoned sin. Toward atone: the price paid, the trust founded, the creditors named. Forty-one thousand six hundred, ten years, the clean ledger. The only door where the innocent get something. But ten years of paying, and Saturday's Pounce prints the sin before the payment begins.)*
> *(She stands at the window with the ledger closed on the table, and thinks of Octavia: the precision was the easy part. The weighing, done honestly, becomes Sunday's choosing.)*
> *(She weighed the doors the way she'd weighed everything that week: honestly, and with the price in hand. The ledger stayed closed. The leaning, whatever it was, would become Sunday's choosing — or Sunday would surprise her. Weighing is not choosing. That was the week's last lesson.)*

options.label: Toward expose
options.detail: *Candor+; the telling, leaned to.* The truth, printed first; the hunters' version, dead. *(Harrow is "the accomplice" for a week; the price stays unspent.)*

options.label: Toward bury
options.detail: *Resolve+; the wall, leaned to.* The papers burn; the agents starve; nothing told. *(Nothing paid; the conscience carries the sin.)*

options.label: Toward atone
options.detail: *Mercy+; the paying, leaned to.* Forty-one thousand six hundred, ten years; the innocent get something. *(Ten years of paying; Saturday prints the sin first.)*

scenes.synopsis: the leaning, shared or kept — the friends, before Saturday; the price, carried together.
scenes.prose:
> *(She tells Octavia the leaning — or keeps it, whichever she chose — and Octavia hears her out — precisely, and with affection. "Good," she says. Or: "Good." Whichever the leaning, the answer is the same, because the weighing was honest. "You know," Octavia says, "my father used to say that a weighing honestly done is half the choosing. The other half is courage." She takes Rose's hand. "You have the courage. I've watched you all week. The teal, the grey, the refused clock, the counted price." She smiles. "Whatever door, Rose. I've priced them all. I can afford any of them. Can you?")*
> *("I can," Rose says. And finds, saying it, that it's true. The friends, before Saturday. The price, carried together.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Bell's draft: "THE LEDGER — On Forty-One Thousand Six Hundred Pounds."
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting arrives with the morning post, in Bell's own hand, marked for Rose's eyes: the proprietor's new draft, and the headline set in type: "THE LEDGER — On Forty-One Thousand Six Hundred Pounds." Three paragraphs, cool and exact. They describe, without naming, a house that has counted its grandfather's debts; a sum, stated precisely; a trust, to be founded; creditors, not victims. The last line is the aim: "The Gazette notes that some houses inherit money. This house has inherited an account. The account will be paid. Saturday's readers may consider the difference." Bell's rule holds: no names. But the warning is unmistakable: the payment is coming, and it will be public.)*
> *(Rose reads it twice and understands the weapon's shape: Bell has drafted the answer to Pounce's Saturday issue in advance, and the draft waits its turn. "The account will be paid." The promise, extended to the whole town. The hunters, told without being told: the debt is acknowledged, and acknowledged debts can't be blackmailed. She files the draft with the Lash and the trust's unsigned paper: the drawer fills: an archive of the reckoning. The blade, aimed. Saturday, hours away.)*
scenes.sting: THE LEDGER — On Forty-One Thousand Six Hundred Pounds.

scenes.synopsis: the promise, written — Rose writes to Harrow; the hundred and fifty, pledged in ink.
scenes.prose:
> *(She writes to Harrow at noon: the promise, in writing. "A hundred and fifty pounds, your wages — paid if the door is atone. His keeping, deeded. It's in Octavia's ledger. It's owed." She signs it, seals it with the plain band, and sends it by Élise's boy. A promise in ink is a debt acknowledged, and acknowledged debts are the ones that get paid. She keeps a copy, filed with the trust's unsigned draft. The drawer: the Lash, Bell's drafts, the trust paper, the promise. The archive of the reckoning, complete.)*
> *(She stands at the desk a moment after the boy goes. The promise is written. The price is known. The doors are weighed. All that remains is Saturday — Pounce's issue, the stranger's next move — and Sunday, the choosing. She touches the mended glove. "Stitch by stitch," she says to the empty study. The study, full of paper, seems to agree. The promise, written. The ink, drying.)*

scenes.synopsis: undressing — the grey, hung; the ledger's day, unpinned; the woman, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(The bedroom, late. The grey silk comes off and is hung with care; it has been the accounting dress, the verdict's color, the witnessing gown, and it has earned its rest. The pearls are coiled, the rope wound. The mended gloves come last. She holds them to the lamp: the grandmother's stitches, even as print, holding through the day of the price. Forty-one thousand six hundred pounds. Ten years. The clean ledger. The stitches held. They will hold through Saturday. They will hold through Sunday.)*
> *(She lays the gloves beside tomorrow's dried violet and unpins her hair. The day unpins with it: the ledger, the columns, the trust's shape, the promise to Harrow, the three doors weighed. Each pin down. Each figure kept. She is tired the way a woman is tired after facing every number she owes. The lamp lowered. The grey, hung. The figures, kept. Enough for today.)*

scenes.synopsis: the friends' talk — the night before Saturday; precision and affection, at rest.
scenes.prose:
> *(At eleven there's a knock, and Octavia with two cups of chocolate, in her dressing gown. "Debrief," she says. "The unofficial one." They sit by the fire. "How does it feel," Octavia asks, "to know the price?" Rose considers. "Like being told the length of a journey. It's long. But it's measured." Octavia nods. "Ten years." "Ten years," Rose agrees. "And at the end, a clean ledger." "And at the end," Octavia says, "you'll be forty. And magnificent." They drink the chocolate. The friends' talk, at rest.)*
> *("Octavia." "Yes?" "Thank you. For the counting. For the affection." "The affection," Octavia says, "was the easy part. The precision took all week." They look at each other, and the laughter comes, tired and warm. "Sunday," Octavia says. "Sunday," Rose agrees. "Whatever door." "Whatever door." The price, carried together. The choosing, coming.)*

scenes.synopsis: dawn — the ledger, closed; Saturday, arrived; the price, carried into the day.
scenes.prose:
> *(Dawn. Saturday. She wakes to the rain on the glass and the knowledge that Pounce's issue is on a carrier's cart somewhere, rolling toward the village. The ledger is closed on the morning room table. The trust's draft is unsigned in Quill's case. Harrow's promise is in ink. The price is known: forty-one thousand six hundred, ten years, the canal and the surplus. She dresses in the grey silk — the verdict's color, the accounting dress — and goes down. The house is already awake, the siege routine running. Letitia meets her in the hall. "Saturday," the quartermaster says. "Saturday," Rose agrees.)*
> *(She touches the mended glove, the dried violet at her wrist, and goes into the morning room to wait for the post — the price carried into the day, the ledger closed, the choosing tomorrow.)*

scenes.synopsis: the cliffhanger — Saturday morning; the knock at Harrow's door; the screw, turning.
scenes.prose: > *(The schoolhouse cottage, Saturday morning. The knock comes at eight, sharp, three raps. Harrow, who has been awake since six with Rose's promise in his pocket, goes to the door. The stranger stands on the step: ordinary coat, ordinary hat, ordinary face. "Mr. Harrow," he says. "My name is Slade. I act for interested parties." He holds out a letter. "I think you should read this." Harrow looks at the letter, the hand, the face. He does not take it. "What is it?" "An offer," Slade says. "Concerning your papers." The letter hangs in the air between them. The knock, knocked. The screw, turning.)*

scenes.synopsis: Saturday morning — the Lash arrives; Pounce's issue, in her hands.
scenes.prose:
> *(Saturday comes up bright and hard, and the Lash comes with the morning post. Rose reads it standing in the hall, Letitia beside her, Octavia on the stairs. Pounce has kept his promise. The blind item is back, louder. The name is in it now: de Varenne. The sum is in it: twelve hundred pounds. "A great house in the shires." "A fallen wall." "French money in English hands." And the lies, mixed in like sand in sugar: a duel, a midnight burial, a priest. She reads it once, folds it, and hands it to Letitia. "File it," she says. "With the others.")*
> *(The household reads it after breakfast, in the servants' hall, aloud. Nobody flinches. The discipline holds. But Rose sees what Pounce has done: he's printed enough truth to make the lies stick. The name, the sum, the wall: true. The duel, the burial, the priest: sand. The town will read it over breakfast and remember the sand. She goes up to dress for battle. The issue, read. The screw, turning.)*

scenes.synopsis: dressing for battle — Hartwell blue, fashionable; the mended gloves as gauntlets.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia lays out the Hartwell blue: damask, severe and splendid, the estate's color. "Blue," she says. "Today is blue. Grey was for the siege. Blue is for the battle." The gown is ten years old, cut in the current fashion, the silver embroidery at the cuffs bright. With it, the silver rose pin, and the mended gloves. "Gauntlets," Letitia says, holding them up. "Today they're gauntlets." Rose puts them on. The mend at the thumb, the scar, the doctrine: worn like armor.)*
> *(In the glass, the battle's face. Hartwell blue, silver, the rose pin. Fashionable, deliberate, unafraid. "The town reads clothes before it reads sheets," Augusta said. Let the town read blue. Let Pounce read it. Let Slade read it. She turns from the glass, the damask settling. The dressing, done. The battle, joined.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the estate's color; the battle, dressed.

fashionChoices.label: Blue, softened
fashionChoices.detail: the rose pin, prominent; iron, in velvet.

fashionChoices.label: Letitia's call
fashionChoices.detail: the quartermaster arms the day.

scenes.synopsis: the issue, assessed — Octavia on what Pounce printed and what it means.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia assesses the issue over breakfast, brisk. "The name: true. The sum: true. The wall: true. The duel, the burial, the priest: sand." She sets the sheet down. "It's the shape we expected. Enough truth to carry the lies." She looks at Rose. "What it means: they've spent real money. This isn't a probe anymore. This is the story, or the first half of it." A pause. "The second half needs Harrow. Or the papers. That's why Slade knocked.")*
> *("Then today is about Harrow," Rose says. "Today," Octavia agrees, "is about the witness." She takes Rose's hand. "Whatever Slade offered him —" "We don't know yet." "Whatever he offered," Octavia says, "Harrow's had Rose's promise in his pocket since yesterday. Ink holds." The assessment, done. The day, defined.)*

scenes.synopsis: the quartermaster's orders — Saturday's discipline; the household, braced.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia's Saturday orders are short. "Nobody talks to strangers. Nobody answers questions. Anyone asks about the Lash, the answer is: we don't read it." She looks around the servants' hall. "The watch stays doubled. The gates stay locked. Mr. Harrow's cottage gets the extra eye." A beat. "And if anyone offers money for gossip," she pauses, "anyone, for anything: you tell me. Before you answer. Before you think about answering. Me. First." The hall nods. The orders, given.)*
> *(Rose, in the doorway, hears the last of it. Letitia sees her and doesn't break stride. "The blue," the quartermaster says. "Good. The house should see it." Rose nods, and goes. The discipline, ordered. The household, braced.)*

scenes.synopsis: Harrow's report — Slade's letter, its terms; the offer to the witness.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise's boy runs in at nine with Harrow's note, and Rose reads it in the hall. Slade's letter, copied in Harrow's neat hand: five hundred pounds for his half of the papers. His silence, purchased. His departure — a schoolmastership in the north, arranged, "where the air is healthier." And the lever, stated politely: "A story is about to be printed. Men named in such stories are rarely safe. London remembers." Rose reads it twice. The money: insulting. The schoolmastership: exile, gift-wrapped. The lever: his safety.)*
> *("He didn't take it," Élise says. "He's waiting for you." "Of course he's waiting," Rose says. She is already moving. "Tell Letitia: the blue goes to the village.")*

scenes.synopsis: the cottage — Slade's letter, the original; Harrow's steadiness under pressure.
scenes.prose:
> *(The cottage at ten. Harrow is at his table, the cloth over the papers, Slade's letter beside it, unanswered. He looks up, and the relief in his face is the day's first honest thing. "Miss Hartwell." She sits. "Tell me." "He knocked at eight," Harrow says. "Three raps. He gave me the letter. He said" — Harrow's voice is steady — "he said men named in such stories are rarely safe. He said it kindly." Rose picks up the letter. The paper is good. The hand is a clerk's. The terms are exactly as copied: five hundred, silence, the north.)*
> *("What did you say?" "I said I would consider it," Harrow says. "I thought considering it would keep him from knocking again." A pause. "Was that wrong?" "It was perfect," Rose says. "Considering is not answering. Considering is the clock, refused politely." She looks at him: the schoolmaster, the witness, the man who was offered exile gift-wrapped and chose to wait for her. "Mr. Harrow. You're not going north." "I know," he says. "I like the air here." The steadiness, under pressure. The witness, unmoved.)*

scenes.synopsis: the safety lever — Rose answers Slade's threat; the witness, protected.
scenes.prose:
> *("Now," Rose says. "The safety. Are you afraid?" Harrow considers. It's the consideration of a brave man, which is to say honest. "A little," he says. "Men named in stories —" "Are rarely safe," Rose finishes. "Yes. But Harrow: the story's already printed. Your name isn't in it. If they name you now, it's retaliation, and retaliation is actionable." She leans forward. "And more: you're not alone. The village watches. The household watches. I watch." She takes his hand, the single mended glove on hers. "No one touches the witness. That's the doctrine.")*
> *("The doctrine," Harrow repeats. He looks at the glove on her hand, the mate to the one in his pocket. "Forty pairs," he says. "Forty," Rose agrees. "And the cottage?" "The cottage stands. The watch doubles. And if he knocks again —" "I offer him tea," Harrow says, "and talk about the haunting." "And the haunting," Rose agrees. The lever, answered. The witness, protected.)*

scenes.synopsis: the law — Slade's letter as evidence; witness-tampering, named.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill reads Slade's letter at noon, in the village, with the cottage behind them. "It's witness-tampering," he says. "Dressed as an offer. Five hundred for papers, silence, and departure: that's three crimes in a clerk's hand." He folds the letter. "Keep it. If this goes to law, it's evidence." He looks at Rose. "And the safety lever — 'men named are rarely safe' — that's a threat. Also evidence." He puts the letter in his case. "Slade's been careful. But careful isn't innocent.")*
> *("What do we do with him?" "Nothing," Quill says. "Today. He's done nothing actionable yet — offered, threatened politely, knocked. The law needs more." He looks at the cottage. "But Harrow's safe. The watch, the village, the letter in my case. If Slade moves, we move." The law, stated. The evidence, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the ride — the blue habit; the equestrienne, at speed.
scenes.prose:
> *(She rides between the cottage and the house at noon, and the blue habit is worth noting: Hartwell blue wool, cut by the best tailor in the county, the skirt managed at speed. The beaver hat, the veil, the gauntlet gloves. On the grey mare, in the blue habit, riding hard down the lane, she looks like what she is: a woman who will not be hurried, hurrying. The contradiction doesn't trouble her. Some days the doctrine is stillness. Today the doctrine is speed.)*
> *(The mare's hooves beat the lane's rhythm, and Rose thinks about Slade's letter, the five hundred, the north. They tried to buy the witness. They tried to frighten him. He chose to wait for her. That is the day's first victory, and it belongs to Harrow. She touches the mare's neck, the veil lifting. The ride, the blue, the speed: unhurried at heart.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the mare, spared; the day, measured.

fashionChoices.detail: the wall, seen; the gap, closing.

scenes.synopsis: Laurent reads the issue — the fury, barely leashed; the de Varenne name, in print.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent is in the hall at one, the Lash in his hand, and the fury is barely leashed. "They printed it," he says. "My mother's name. In Pounce's sheet." Rose takes the paper from him, gently. "Read the sand," she says. "The duel. The burial. The priest. None of it happened." "The name happened," Laurent says. "The sum happened." "The name and the sum," Rose agrees, "are the truth they're using to carry the lies." She looks at him: the black coat, the young face, the fury. "And the truth," she says, "is about to have a trust fund. Creditors, not victims. Remember?")*
> *(He breathes, once, hard. "The trust." "The trust," Rose confirms. "Twelve hundred. Your cousins, creditors." The fury settles, marginally. "Sunday," he says. "You choose Sunday." "I choose Sunday," Rose agrees. "And until Sunday?" "Until Sunday," Rose says, "you watch the masons, and you don't touch Slade." He nods, slowly. "The coat," he says. "Stitch by stitch." "Stitch by stitch." The fury, leashed. Barely.)*

scenes.synopsis: the approach — a servant is offered money; the quartermaster's report.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia finds Rose at two, in the morning room, and the report is short. "Alice. The second housemaid. A man stopped her on the lane — not Slade, another one, younger — and offered her ten pounds for anything she knows about the ledger." Letitia's voice is flat. "She told him she knows nothing about any ledger. He offered twenty. She told him to ask the mistress herself, and came straight to me." A pause. "Twenty pounds, Rose. That's a year's wages. She refused it.")*
> *("Where is she?" "In the kitchen, crying. Not from fear. From anger." Rose stands. "Tell her she's to have the afternoon off, and the blue ribbon from the notion box. And Letitia —" "I know," the quartermaster says. "Me. First. The hall knows." The approach, reported. The refusal, honored.)*

scenes.synopsis: the housemaid — Alice's refusal; the household's loyalty, in person.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alice is in the kitchen, red-eyed, furious. Rose sits beside her. "Tell me." "He was young," Alice says. "Polite. He said he was writing a book about great houses, and he wanted anything about the ledger. I said there's no ledger." A pause. "There is a ledger. Octavia's. But it's not his." She looks at Rose. "Twenty pounds, ma'am. I could have —" "You didn't," Rose says. "I know." She takes the girl's hand. "Alice. The house knows what loyalty costs. The house pays its debts, and it pays its people. Your twenty pounds is noted.")*
> *("Ma'am." "The blue ribbon's yours, and the afternoon. And Alice — if he comes back, or another one, you tell Letitia. Me, first." "Yes, ma'am." The girl's tears stop. The anger stays, which is better. Loyalty, in person. The household, holding.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE WITNESS'S GUARD: Harrow's safety, arranged; how the house protects its own.
scenes.prose:
> *(Afternoon. Slade's letter, Alice's twenty pounds, and the safety lever. Harrow is the screw's target, and the guard is Rose's to arrange. Three arrangements offer themselves. Bring him to Hartwell: the schoolmaster in the guest room, under the household's roof, the watch indoors. The safest. But Harrow's cottage is his dignity; removing him looks like hiding. Post the guard at the cottage: the village men, the gamekeeper, the watch doubled around his door. He stays home, protected visibly. But a visible guard is a public statement, and Slade will read it. Send him to Octavia's: the Harrington house, twenty miles, the friend's roof. Safe, distant, discreet. But twenty miles is twenty miles from Rose's eye, and the stranger's network is wider than the village.)*
> *(She stands in the morning room with the blue damask settling around her, and thinks of Harrow: "I like the air here." The guard, chosen, becomes the night's arrangement.)*
> *(She arranged the guard the way she'd arranged everything that week: deliberately, and with Harrow's dignity in hand. The night's watch settled into place. Whatever Slade tried next, the witness would not be alone.)*

options.label: Bring him to Hartwell
options.detail: *Resolve+; the guest room.* Under the household's roof, the watch indoors. *(The safest; his cottage, left empty.)*

options.label: Guard the cottage
options.detail: *Doctrine+; the village men.* He stays home, the watch doubled, visible. *(A public statement; Slade reads it.)*

options.detail: *Patience+; twenty miles.* Safe, distant, discreet, the friend's house. *(Twenty miles from Rose's eye; the network is wide.)*

scenes.synopsis: the guard, enacted — Harrow's answer; the witness, settled.
scenes.prose:
> *(She tells him herself, at the cottage, at four. Whatever arrangement she chose, she carries it herself, because the witness deserves the mistress's own voice. Harrow listens, and nods. "It's sensible," he says. "Though I'll miss the haunting." "The haunting," Rose says, "can visit." He smiles, tired. "Miss Hartwell." "Mr. Harrow." "Whatever you decided — thank you. For the letter. For the guard. For the air here." He looks around the cottage. "It's a good cottage. I'll be glad to —" he stops. "Whichever. I'm glad.")*
> *(The guard takes its posts as the light goes. The witness, settled. The night's arrangement, made. Rose rides home in the blue habit, the veil down, and thinks: they tried money, they tried fear, they tried the servants. All three failed. The screw is turning on nothing. Tomorrow, Slade will have to try something else. Or nothing. The guard, enacted. The witness, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the flower-seller's network — what the village saw; Slade's man, traced.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise reports at five, with the evening's dried violets. "The young one — the book-writer — he's been in the village three days. Asking questions. He asked my boy about the ledger." She sets the dried violets down. "My boy told him the mistress reads books, not ledgers. The boy got a penny for his trouble and gave it to the church." She looks at Rose. "They're mapping us. The lanes, the servants, the habits. Slade's the face. The young one's the feet." A pause. "Want me to have him followed?")*
> *("Gently," Rose says. "No touching. Just eyes." Élise nods. "Eyes we have." The network, mobilized. The feet, watched. The village, which likes a debt paid, does not like strangers mapping its lanes. The dried violets, laid. Faithfulness, on the table.)*

scenes.synopsis: the village's view — Mrs. Pike on the Lash; the downhill verdict.
scenes.prose:
> *(Mrs. Pike comes up to the house herself, which she never does, and asks for Rose. "I've read it," she says, without preamble. "Pounce's sheet. The name, the sum, the wall." She looks at Rose, the blue damask, the battle's face. "The village has read it too." "And?" "And the village," Mrs. Pike says, "doesn't believe the duel." A pause. "The village believes the sum. The village always believes sums. But the duel —" she shakes her head. "Nobody duels over money anymore. It's old-fashioned." Rose almost laughs. "The sand," she says. "Doesn't stick." "The sand," Mrs. Pike agrees, "doesn't stick.")*
> *("Tell the village," Rose says, "that the choosing is Sunday. The house will have its answer." Mrs. Pike nods. "The village will like that. The village likes answers." She goes, and Rose thinks: the sand doesn't stick. Pounce spent real money on sand. The verdict, downhill. The truth, believed. The lies, old-fashioned.)*

scenes.synopsis: the fitting runs — Bell's "THE FITTING — On Bought Ink and Borrowed Outrage," in print.
scenes.prose:
> *(The evening Gazette arrives, and the fitting is in it: "THE FITTING — On Bought Ink and Borrowed Outrage." Bell has done what Bell does. The column names no names, but it describes, precisely, a sheet that prints blind items on commission; a sum paid for a story; a stranger asking after schoolmasters. The last line is the blade: "The Gazette notes that some papers sell their columns. This paper sells nothing but the truth, and the truth is not for sale." The household reads it in the servants' hall, and the hall's verdict is unanimous: that's telling them.)*
> *(Rose reads it twice. It's the answer to Pounce's Saturday issue, printed the same day, and it does what answers do best: it exists. "Bought ink and borrowed outrage." The town will read both sheets over Sunday breakfast and compare. Bell's rule held — no names — but everyone will know. The fitting, run. The blade, in print.)*

scenes.synopsis: dinner — the blue, worn at the table; the household, unbowed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Dinner, Saturday. She keeps the blue, and the blue has earned its keep: the cottage, the village, the guard, the fitting. At the table, the talk is the day: Slade's letter, Alice's twenty pounds, the fitting in print. The household hears it all and nods. Nobody is frightened. The household is not frightened of screws. The household is frightened of unpaid debts, and the debts are being paid. Octavia, in her grey, raises her glass. "To Alice," she says. "To twenty pounds refused." "To Alice," the table says. The blue, worn. The household, unbowed.)*
> *(After, in the drawing room, Rose catches her reflection: Hartwell blue, the silver rose pin, the mended gloves laid on the table beside her. The battle's face, a little tired. "You look," Octavia says, "like the house." "Is that good?" "It's the best thing I can say." The fashion beat, quiet. The unbowed, dressed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the last lever — Slade's final move; the safety, pressed once more.
scenes.prose:
> *(Slade's last move comes at eight, by letter, delivered to the house. Rose reads it in the study, Octavia beside her. It's short. The offer is doubled: a thousand pounds for Harrow's papers. The schoolmastership is upgraded: a living, not a mastership. And the lever, pressed once more, harder: "Men who stand near stories that are about to be printed have been known to suffer accidents. London is a large city, but its memory is long." Rose reads it, folds it, and hands it to Henry, who has come up for the evening. "Evidence," he says. "More of it.")*
> *("He's desperate," Octavia says. "Doubled the money. Upgraded the exile. It's the last lever, pressed twice." "Or," Rose says, "it's not the last." She looks at the letter. "But it doesn't matter. Harrow's guarded. Alice is ribboned. The village is watching. The screw is turning on nothing." She puts the letter with Slade's first. The lever, pressed. The evidence, filed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the price, still good — the friends, before the choosing; Sunday, confirmed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes to the study at nine, with the ledger, and the conversation is the price, confirmed. "Forty-one thousand six hundred," she says. "Ten years. Whatever Pounce prints, whatever Slade offers, the price doesn't change." She looks at Rose. "The choosing is tomorrow. The doors are weighed. Are you ready?" Rose considers. It's the consideration of a woman who has been pressed all day and has not moved. "I'm ready," she says. "The price is known. The witness is safe. The household holds. Tomorrow I choose.")*
> *("Good," Octavia says. "Then tonight we rest." She closes the ledger. "The precision is done. Tomorrow is the courage." They sit a moment in the firelight, the blue and the grey, the friends, the price between them like a third person they've both agreed to love. "Whatever door," Octavia says. "Whatever door," Rose agrees. The price, still good. The choosing, confirmed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the answer, considered — Rose weighs Slade's doubled offer; the screw's shape, seen.
scenes.prose:
> *(Night. The study. Slade's two letters lie on the desk beside Pounce's issue and Bell's fitting. Rose looks at them the way she looked at the ledger: as figures to be faced. The offer: a thousand pounds, a living, safety implied. The cost of accepting: Harrow's papers, Harrow's silence, Harrow's departure. The sin, sold to the people who would use it. She thinks about what the doubled offer means: they're afraid. The fitting stung. The village didn't believe the duel. Harrow didn't take the five hundred. So they doubled it. Desperation, priced at a thousand.)*
> *(She folds the letters and puts them with Henry's evidence file. The answer will come, but not tonight. Tonight is the watch. Tonight the household guards its own. She touches the mended glove. "Stitch by stitch," she says to the empty study. The study, full of paper, seems to agree. The screw's shape, seen. The answer, pending.)*

scenes.synopsis: the watch, ordered — Saturday night's guard; the quartermaster's disposition.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia's night orders are precise. "Harrow's cottage: two men, the gamekeeper's dog. The gates: locked, the lodge awake. The wall's gap: watched. The servants' stairs: the footmen take turns." She looks at Rose. "And you." "And me?" "You sleep," Letitia says. "That's an order. The blue comes off, the nightdress goes on, and you sleep. The choosing is tomorrow. The house needs you rested." Rose looks at her quartermaster: the flat voice, the tired eyes, the woman who has run the siege all week. "And you?" "I sleep," Letitia says, "when you do.")*
> *("Together, then," Rose says. The watch, ordered. The quartermaster, obeyed — barely. The disposition, made. The night, guarded.)*

scenes.synopsis: the friends' undressing — the blue, unpinned; the day, laid down.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia helps her out of the blue in the bedroom, the way she did the grey, and the ritual is becoming a friendship: the gown, the pins, the day. "Slade doubled it," Rose says. "A thousand." "Desperation," Octavia says, unpinning. "The fitting stung. The village laughed at the duel. Harrow stayed." She lays the damask down. "They have nothing left but the lever. And the lever's guarded." She looks at Rose in her nightdress, the pearls coiled, the mended gloves on the table. "Tomorrow you choose. Tonight you sleep. Doctor's orders. Quartermaster's orders. Friend's orders.")*
> *("Three orders," Rose says. "I obey." The undressing, done. The day, laid down. The choosing, tomorrow.)*

scenes.synopsis: night — the blue wrapper; the dried violet, the letters, the figures.
scenes.prose:
> *(The bedroom, late. She wears the blue damask's wrapper over her nightdress, the silver rose pin still at the throat — she forgot to take it off, or chose not to — and reads nothing. The night is for rest, by three orders. Élise's dried violet lies on the table beside the bed, faithfulness in the lamplight. She touches it, the petals, the stem: the day's textures. The blue, the damask, the doubled offer, Alice's twenty pounds refused, the fitting in print. Each texture, kept. Each figure, filed.)*
> *(She sets the dried violet on Slade's letters, filed on the table: faithfulness on the threats. The lamp lowered. The wrapper exchanged for the nightdress, the pin finally unpinned. The choosing, tomorrow. The woman, resting. The screw, endured.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the battle's color; Sunday, uncolored.

fashionChoices.label: Dream in violets
fashionChoices.detail: faithfulness; the people, kept.

fashionChoices.label: No choosing
fashionChoices.detail: sleep takes what it takes.

scenes.synopsis: the summons, written — Rose sets Sunday's choosing; the shape, set on Saturday night.
scenes.prose:
> *(Saturday evening. The screw's answer is still unsent, Slade's letters are in the drawer, and the decision is made: the choosing will be announced — not the choice, the choosing. Tomorrow. The morning room. The three doors, laid out, and Rose will choose, and the house will witness. No more being hurried. No more Slade's clock. She writes the summons herself, in the blue wrapper, by lamplight: "Tomorrow. The morning room. The choosing." She seals them with the plain band. The shape, set.)*
> *(She stacks the summons on the table. The house will hear it first. The town will hear it after. Slade will hear it last. That is the order of things. The choosing, announced. Sunday, hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE SCREW'S ANSWER: Slade's doubled offer, answered; what the house says to the hunters.
scenes.prose:
> *(Saturday evening. The summons are written, the choosing is announced, and Slade's answer is Rose's to give. Three answers offer themselves. Answer him directly: a letter, in her own hand. "The papers are not for sale. The witness is not for sale. The house is not afraid." The hunters, told plainly. But a letter is engagement, and engagement is what they want. Ignore him: no letter, no word, the doubled offer unanswered. Silence, as doctrine. The screw turns on nothing, again. But silence can be read as fear, and Slade reads everything. Use Bell: give the fitting's author the doubled offer, the threats, the whole file. Let the Gazette print "THE SCREW." The town reads the hunters' methods over breakfast. But using Bell is using the press, and Rose has sworn the press is not hers to use.)*
> *(She stands at the window with Slade's letters in her hand, and thinks of Quill: evidence. Of Octavia: desperation. Of Harrow: "I like the air here." The answer, chosen, becomes the house's voice.)*
> *(She answered Slade the way she'd answered everything that week: deliberately, and with the house's dignity in hand. The letters went where she sent them — or nowhere, if she chose nowhere. The hunters would read the answer, or the silence, and know: the house is not for sale.)*

options.label: Answer him directly
options.detail: *Resolve+; her own hand.* "Not for sale. Not afraid." The hunters, told. *(A letter is engagement; engagement is what they want.)*

options.label: Ignore him
options.detail: *Doctrine+; silence.* The doubled offer, unanswered. The screw, on nothing. *(Silence reads as fear; Slade reads everything.)*

options.label: Use Bell
options.detail: *Candor+; the file, given.* "THE SCREW," in print. The town reads the methods. *(Using Bell is using the press; she swore it isn't hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the answer, shared — the friends, on Saturday evening; the choosing, a day away.
scenes.prose:
> *(She tells Octavia that evening, in the morning room, the summons stacked on the table. Whatever answer she chose, Octavia receives it precisely. "Good," she says. Or: "Good." The weighing was honest; the answer is the house's. "You know," Octavia says, "my father used to say that an answer honestly given is half the battle. The other half is the choosing." She takes the summons and reads the top one. "The morning room. The choosing." She looks up. "It's a good room for it. The light's honest.")*
> *("The light's honest," Rose agrees. They sit with the lamps lit, the blue and the grey, the friends, the choosing a day away. The answer, shared. The eve, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the room, readied — Letitia prepares the morning room; Sunday's choosing, staged.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia takes the summons Saturday night, and prepares the morning room for Sunday: the chairs in a semicircle, the ledger on the table, the three doors — not yet; the doors come with the choosing — the dried violets in a bowl. Not yet the household; the household comes Sunday. Letitia inspects the arrangement with the quartermaster's eye. "The light's honest," she says, echoing Octavia. "Good. Choosing should be done in honest light.")*
> *(Rose watches from the doorway, in the blue wrapper, not yet dressed for the choosing. The room, readied. The choosing, staged. The screw, answered. All that remains is the night, the dressing, the doors, the choice.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dressing, for the choosing — what does a woman wear to choose?
scenes.prose:
> *(The bedroom, Saturday evening. The question is the dressing: what does a woman wear to choose? Not the teal; the teal was for the hunt. Not the grey; the grey was for the siege. Not the blue; the blue was for the battle. The choosing needs its own color. She goes to the archive with Letitia, and they look: the deep rose silk, twenty years old, fashionable still. The color of the name. Hartwell rose. "This," Letitia says. "The choosing is the house's. The house's color." Rose touches the silk. Twenty years old. Worn by her mother, perhaps. The archive, giving up its finest.)*
> *(She holds the rose silk to the light. Tomorrow she will stand in the morning room, in honest light, and choose. The gown is the choosing's. The woman is the house's. The dressing, prepared.)*

scenes.synopsis: the watch ritual — Saturday night's guard, dressed; the household's vigil, witnessed; the chapter's ritual.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the door — "the watch is posted. The house is held. Sleep, all.")*
> *(Story morsel: Alice, with the blue ribbon — "twenty pounds. I said no. I'd say it again.")*
> *(Story morsel: Harrow, at the cottage — the guard at his door, the promise in his pocket, the waiting.)*
> *(Story morsel: Rose, at the window — "the screw turned all week. The house held. Stitch by stitch.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the door — "sleep. The choosing needs you rested. The price needs you brave.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: The screw has turned all week, and the household has held. Tonight the watch is witnessed: the guard's posts named, the servants' loyalty honored, the choosing's eve kept. Dress for the vigil: the archive's finest, fashionable and deliberate — the house does not under-dress its guardians. Alice's twenty pounds refused, Harrow's steadiness, the village's eyes: honored, all. Exact. Grateful. Unafraid. The house that guards its own does not flinch.

scenes.synopsis: the vigil, kept — Saturday night's watch; the house, held; the woman, unhurried.
scenes.prose:
> *(The house settles into Saturday night, and Rose keeps the vigil with it — not dressed for choosing, not yet. The blue wrapper, the mended gloves, the pearls put away. She walks the posts with Letitia and Octavia: the gates, the wall's gap, the servants' stairs, Harrow's cottage with the guard at the door and the lamp lit. Everything held. "The screw turned all week," she says to the night. "The house held. Stitch by stitch." Letitia nods. "Sleep, all," the quartermaster says at the door. "The choosing needs you rested. The price needs you brave." The vigil, kept. The night, tended.)*
> *("Brave," Octavia echoes, "is a strong word for ten o'clock." "Ten o'clock," Rose says, "is when brave starts." They laugh, tired and warm, and go in.)*

scenes.synopsis: the rose, laid out — Sunday's gown, prepared; fashion as doctrine.
scenes.prose:
> *(The rose silk is laid out on the bed, not yet worn: deep rose, twenty years old, the weave still fine, the color still true. The archive's keeping is the house's keeping: things last, here. The long rope of pearls beside it, the grandmother's, doubled. The silver rose pin. The mended gloves, the mend at the thumb like a signature. Letitia has brushed the silk; Octavia will do the pearls. In the lamplight Rose studies the gown the way a general studies a map: tomorrow she stands in the morning room, in honest light, and chooses. The gown is the choosing's. The woman is the house's.)*
> *(Fashion as doctrine: the choosing is not under-dressed, even in advance. The house does not flinch from its own color. The rose, laid out. The lamp, low. The woman, preparing.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE WITNESSING: how Sunday's choice will be witnessed — the household, the village, or the town at once; the choosing's audience, set.
scenes.prose:
> *(Saturday night. The rose silk is laid out, the summons are written, the room is readied, and one thing remains: how Sunday's choice will be witnessed: not the choice, the witnessing. The trust stays unsigned; the doors keep their hour. Three witnessings offer themselves. The household only: the choosing in the morning room, witnessed by the house (the servants' hall, the village men, Harrow, Quill, the friends), and the town told after, by letter. The house's choice, the house's witness. But a private choosing can be called a secret one, and secrets are what she's unchoosing. The village too: open the morning room's doors and let the village men and Élise's network stand witness. The choosing, made the parish's. But witnesses become audiences, and audiences become Pounce's readers. The town, at once: riders standing ready with the choice the hour it's made (the trust's founding, the account, the burning, whichever door), so the town hears it from the house before the Gazette or the gutter sheet. The bold stroke. But the bold stroke is also the hasty one, and the doors deserve their hour.)*
> *(She stands in the lamplight with the rose silk laid out, and thinks of Octavia: the precision was the easy part. The witnessing, chosen, becomes the summons' last line.)*
> *(The witnessing was chosen, and the summons would carry the last line — who was called to witness. Sunday would do the rest. The trust stayed unsigned. The doors kept their hour.)*

options.label: The household only
options.detail: *Doctrine+; the house's witness.* The choosing, witnessed by the house; the town, told after. *(Private choosing can be called secret; secrets are what she's unchoosing.)*

options.label: The village too
options.detail: *Candor+; the parish's.* The doors opened, the village standing witness. *(Witnesses become audiences; audiences become Pounce's readers.)*

options.label: The town, at once
options.detail: *Resolve+; the bold stroke.* Riders with the choice, the hour it's made. *(Bold is hasty; the doors deserve their hour.)*

scenes.synopsis: the eve, enacted — the summons go out; the house, readied.
scenes.prose:
> *(Whatever witnessing she chose, she enacts it Saturday night, in the blue wrapper, by lamplight. The summons go out in Letitia's own hand: the household for the morning room; the village men too, if she chose them; the riders' orders, if she chose the town at once. The morning room stands ready: the semicircle, the ledger, the dried violets. Rose stands in the doorway a moment. "Thank you," she says to the empty room, "for the week. For the holding. Whatever door —" she stops. "Whatever door," the room seems to say back. The eve, enacted. The house, readied.)*
> *(She looks at the room once more: the chairs, the loyalty, the twenty pounds refused, the steadiness, the eyes that will be here Sunday. All that remains is the night, the dressing, the doors, the choice. She trims the lamp. "Stitch by stitch," she says. The eve, enacted. The choosing, a day away.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Bell's draft: "THE SCREW — On Bought Testimony."
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting arrives Saturday evening, in Bell's own hand, marked for Rose's eyes: the proprietor's new draft, and the headline set in type: "THE SCREW — On Bought Testimony." Three paragraphs, set cool. They describe, without naming, a stranger who offered a schoolmaster money for papers; a doubled offer; a threat, politely worded. The last line is the blade: "The Gazette notes that testimony, like ink, can be bought. This paper buys neither. Sunday's readers may consider the difference." Bell's rule holds: no names. But Slade will read it, and know he's read.)*
> *(Rose reads it twice and understands the weapon's shape: Bell has drafted the answer to the screw in advance, and the draft bides its time. "This paper buys neither." The hunters, told without being told: the witness can't be bought. She files the draft with the Lash and the trust's paper: the drawer's archive of the reckoning, thicker. The blade, aimed. The choosing, tomorrow.)*
scenes.sting: THE SCREW — On Bought Testimony.

scenes.synopsis: the letters, written — Harrow, Quill, the household; the eve's paper, prepared.
scenes.prose:
> *(She writes Saturday night: the eve's paper. To Harrow: "Come to the morning room, Sunday. Bring nothing. The guard walks with you." To Quill: "Bring the draft. Unsigned, still. The choosing decides." To the household: "Thank you. Whatever door." She signs them, seals them with the plain band, and sends them. The paper, prepared. The choosing's machinery, oiled.)*
> *(She sits a moment after the letters go. The rose silk, laid out on the bed. The ledger on the table, the dried violets in the bowl. All that remains is the night, the dressing, the choosing's hour — the three doors, laid out — and the choice. She touches the mended glove. "Stitch by stitch," she says to the bedroom. The bedroom, full of lamplight, seems to agree. The letters, written. The ink, drying.)*

scenes.synopsis: the choosing's eve, dressed — the blue wrapper, the rose laid out; the woman, before the doors.
scenes.prose:
> *(She keeps the blue wrapper for the evening, and the rose silk lies on the bed, laid out. The gown has changed meaning through the day: this morning it was the archive's finest; now it is the choosing's armor, waiting. The witnessing, chosen. The summons, sent. The letters, written. The sting, filed. She stands in the bedroom, in lamplight, and looks at the woman in the glass: the wrapper, the mended gloves, the dried violet at her wrist. The choosing's eve, kept. The woman who will choose, preparing.)*
> *(She touches the dried violet at her wrist — Élise's, faithfulness — and thinks of the three doors, waiting in the wings. Expose. Bury. Atone. The price, known. The witness, safe. The household, holding. All that remains is the night, the dressing, the hour, and the courage. The wrapper, kept on. The woman, ready.)*

scenes.synopsis: the friends' talk — the choosing's eve; precision and affection, at rest.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes to the bedroom at ten, in her grey wrapper, with two cups of chocolate. "Debrief," she says. "The unofficial one." They sit by the fire. "How does it feel," Octavia asks, "to be about to choose?" Rose considers. "Like standing at the top of the stairs. The stairs are measured. The stepping is mine." Octavia nods. "The price." "The price," Rose agrees. "Forty-one thousand six hundred. Ten years. The doors, weighed." "And the witnessing?" "Chosen," Rose says. "Slade's clock stopped. Mine started." They drink the chocolate. The friends' talk, at rest.)*
> *("Octavia." "Yes?" "Thank you. For the counting. For the affection." "The counting," Octavia says, "was the easy part. The precision took all week." They look at each other, and the laughter comes, tired and warm. "The choosing," Octavia says. "The choosing," Rose agrees. "Whatever door." "Whatever door." The eve, kept. The courage, coming.)*

scenes.synopsis: the hour, coming — the morning room, prepared; the three doors, waiting.
scenes.prose:
> *(Evening. She goes down to the morning room alone, in the blue wrapper, and looks at the choosing's stage. The chairs in a semicircle. The ledger on the table. The dried violets in a bowl. The lamplight, low and warm. The three doors — not yet; the doors come in the hour — wait in the wings. She touches the ledger's cover, the violet on it, the mended glove. "Stitch by stitch," she says to the empty room. The room, full of lamplight, seems to agree.)*
> *(She stands a moment in the lamplight, the wrapper, the choosing's eve, and thinks of the week: the blind item, the offer, the price, the screw. Each day, faced. Each figure, kept. Each door, weighed. All that remains is the night, the dressing, the hour, and the courage. The hour, coming. The woman, ready.)*

scenes.synopsis: the cliffhanger — the witness comes himself, with his half of the papers; the choosing's eve, broken open.
scenes.prose: > *(The knock comes at nine, soft, two raps. Rose is in the morning room, in the blue wrapper, and Letitia brings him in: Harrow, in his best coat, with a parcel wrapped in oilcloth. "Miss Hartwell," he says. "I've decided the cottage isn't safe. Not the cottage — the papers." He unwraps the oilcloth. His half: the schoolmaster's pages, the neat hand, the other side of the torn sheet. "I thought," he says, "that the choosing should have both halves." He holds them out. The two halves, in the honest light. The choosing's eve, broken open.)*

scenes.synopsis: Sunday morning — the choosing's hour; the house, awake.
scenes.prose:
> *(Sunday comes up gold, and the house is awake before her. She hears it through the bedroom door: the servants' stairs, the kitchen, the gates, the village. The choosing's machinery, running quietly. She lies a moment in the dawn light, in the rose silk's wrapper, and thinks of the week: the blind item, the offer, the price, the screw — each day faced, each figure kept, each door weighed. Today, the choosing.)*
> *(She rises, and the day rises with her. The choosing's hour is ten. The household will gather. The three doors will be laid out. And she will choose. She touches the dried violet at the table — Élise's, faithfulness — and begins to dress.)*

scenes.synopsis: the choosing's dress — the rose silk, the archive's finest; the woman, in her name's color.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia dresses her in silence, and the silence is the dressing's honor. The rose silk: deep rose, twenty years old, fashionable still. The long rope of pearls, doubled. The silver rose pin. The mended gloves, last. In the glass, the choosing's face: calm, pale, resolved. "The house's color," Letitia says. "The house's," Rose agrees. She turns, the silk settling. The choosing's dress, worn. The woman, in her name's color.)*
> *(Down the stairs, through the hall, into the morning room's honest light. The household is gathering. The choosing's hour is striking. The rose, worn. The choosing, dressed.)*
