scenes.synopsis: the gathering — the morning room, in honest light; the witnesses, assembled.
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning room at ten, in honest light. The chairs in a semicircle. The ledger on the table. The dried violets in a bowl. And the people: Octavia, with the ledger's authority. Harrow, with his half of the papers. Laurent, with the de Varenne name. Letitia, with the household's loyalty. Quill, with the unsigned draft. Henry, with the family's loyalty. The friends, the village men, the servants' hall's representatives. The choosing's witnesses, assembled.)*
> *(Rose stands before them in the rose silk, and the room quiets. "Thank you," she says. "For the week. For the holding." She looks around: the faces, the loyalty, the twenty pounds refused, the steadiness. "Today the house chooses. Three doors. One choosing." The gathering, done. The choosing, opened.)*

scenes.synopsis: the true price, stated — Octavia's accounting, precise and affectionate, before the choosing.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia rises, and the room turns to her. She opens the ledger, and her voice is the week's voice: precise, and underneath it, affectionate. "The true price," she says. "Stated exactly, because Rose deserves exactly." She reads: "To Mr. James Harrow: one hundred and fifty pounds. His wages. His keeping, deeded. To the creditors of the de Varenne family: twelve hundred pounds. Their ruin, acknowledged as debt. To the de la Roche family: nine hundred pounds. To the de Brissac family: fourteen hundred pounds. To the de Valcourt family: twenty-eight hundred pounds — signed and promised in the spring, and acknowledged here.")*
> *(She looks up. "The total: forty-one thousand six hundred pounds. Twenty-eight hundred promised; thirty-eight thousand eight hundred to pay: eight thousand eight hundred now from the surplus (a hundred and fifty to Harrow, the rest to found the trust), three thousand a year for ten years from the canal's revenue. The Park's stones untouched. The roofs untouched. The household's bread untouched." A pause. "That is the price. It is large. It is exact. And it is" — her voice softens — "the price of a clean ledger, which is the only inheritance worth having." The price, stated. Precisely. Affectionately.)*

scenes.synopsis: the friend's stake — why Octavia counted; the affection, before the doors.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia closes the ledger, and the conversation is the affection without the figures. "You asked me once," she says to the room, "why I count things. It was after my father died, and I was twenty-two, and counting was how I loved him." She looks at Rose. "I counted your price the same way. Precisely, because I love you." The room is very quiet. "Whatever door you choose," she says, "I've priced them all. I can afford any of them. The question" — she smiles — "is which one you can afford to live with.")*
> *("Thank you," Rose says. "For the counting. For the affection." "The affection," Octavia says, "was the easy part — the precision took all week, and Sunday takes the rest." The room laughs, softly, and the tension breaks, and reforms around something warmer. The stake, stated. The friend, before the doors.)*

scenes.synopsis: the witness, present — Harrow's half, laid beside Rose's; the papers, joined.
scenes.prose:
> *(Harrow rises, and the room turns to him. He lays his half on the table beside Rose's: the schoolmaster's pages, the neat hand. The two halves, together, make the torn sheet whole. "I kept them," he says, simply. "Twenty years, I kept them. Not for money. For the truth." He looks at Rose. "Whatever door, Miss Hartwell. The keeping is done. The papers are yours." He sits. The witness, present. The papers, joined.)*
> *(Rose looks at the whole sheet: her grandfather's hand, Harrow's neat pages, the tear mended by their meeting. Twenty years apart. One morning room. The keeping, done. The choosing, coming.)*

scenes.synopsis: the promise, kept — Rose answers the witness; his safety, pledged before all; the paying, reserved for atone.
scenes.prose:
> *("Mr. Harrow," Rose says, and the room listens. "Whatever door, you are safe. The guard stays. No one touches you, no one buys you, no one prints you. That is unconditional." She looks at him: the schoolmaster, the witness, the man who kept the truth for twenty years. "The hundred and fifty — your wages, your keeping, deeded — belongs to the third door. If I choose atone, it is paid. It's in Octavia's ledger. It's owed." Harrow bows his head. "Miss Hartwell." "The promise," Rose says, "is that no door makes you pay for my choosing.")*
> *(The room hears it: the witness, protected regardless. The paying, reserved for atonement. The choosing, unburdened by debt to the living. The promise, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the first door — EXPOSE, laid out; the telling's full moral weight.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose rises, and lays out the first door. "Expose," she says. "The complete truthful account — the émigré money, the gambling, the Hartwell losses covered first, the de Varennes and de Valcourts allowed to fall — given to the Gazette, whole and untrimmed. Mrs. Bell prints it because it is true and newsworthy." She looks around the room. "The town reads it. The hunters' version dies of irrelevance. The sin is named, publicly, by the house that committed it.")*
> *(She lets the door stand, and speaks its cost honestly. "The cost: Harrow is 'the accomplice' for a week. The de Varennes are a story. Laurent's mother's name is in every sheet in England. And the thirty-eight thousand eight hundred —" she touches the ledger — "stays in the canal's future, unspent. Exposure is not payment. The truth is told, and the debts remain." The first door, laid out. Its weight, carried.)*

scenes.synopsis: the second door — BURY, laid out; the wall's full moral weight.
scenes.prose:
> *(She lays out the second door. "Bury," she says. "The papers burn — both halves, in this room, witnessed. The wall rebuilds. The agents lose their proof. Pounce has yesterday's issue and nothing more." She looks at the joined sheet on the table. "The household keeps its secret. Harrow keeps his cottage. The de Varennes keep their ruin, unacknowledged. And I —" she stops. "And I live with it," she finishes. "The unatoned sin. The clean ledger, unopened.")*
> *(She lets the door stand, and speaks its cost honestly. "The cost: nothing is paid. The hundred and fifty stays in the surplus. The twelve hundred stays a ruin. The twenty-eight hundred stays a silence. The proof disappears, and the moral cost remains — mine, to carry, for the rest of my life. The wall is rebuilt, and I live behind it." The second door, laid out. Its weight, carried.)*

scenes.synopsis: midday — the rose, in honest light; the choosing's gown, between the doors.
scenes.prose:
> *(Between the doors, the room breathes, and the honest light does what honest light does: it shows the rose silk truly. Deep rose, twenty years old, the weave still fine. The long rope of pearls, doubled. The silver rose pin. The mended gloves, laid on the table beside the joined papers. She stands between the first door and the second, and the gown is the choosing's: fashionable, deliberate, unafraid. The archive's finest, between the doors.)*
> *(She touches the dried violet at her wrist — faithfulness — and lays out the third door. The rose, worn. The light, honest. The choosing, continuing.)*

scenes.synopsis: the third door — ATONE, laid out; the paying's full moral weight.
scenes.prose:
> *(She lays out the third door. "Atone," she says. "The forty-one thousand six hundred, paid. Eight thousand eight hundred now — a hundred and fifty to Harrow, the rest to found the trust. Three thousand a year, for ten years, from the canal. The de Varennes are creditors, not victims. The de Valcourts are acknowledged, lightly. The trust is public. The ledger is clean.")*
> *(She lets the door stand, and speaks its cost honestly. "The cost: ten years of paying. The canal's income, committed. The surplus, spent. And Saturday's truth" — she looks at Pounce's issue, filed on the table — "is that the town will read the sin before the payment begins. The atonement is slow, and the shame is fast. But it is" — she looks at Octavia — "the only door where the innocent get something. The only door where the price is paid." The third door, laid out. Its weight, carried.)*

scenes.synopsis: the de Varenne voice — Laurent speaks for his mother's name; the creditors, heard.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent rises, and the room turns to him. He is young, and the black coat is severe, and his voice, when it comes, is steady. "My mother's name was in Pounce's sheet yesterday," he says. "A story. Sand." He looks at Rose. "I don't want the name in Bell's sheet tomorrow. Not as a story." A pause. "But I want the twelve hundred. Not as charity. As debt." He looks around the room. "My cousins are creditors. Say it." The room is quiet. "Creditors," Octavia says. "Not victims.")*
> *("Thank you," Laurent says. He sits. The de Varenne voice, heard. The creditors, named.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE HEARING: before the doors, one voice; whose testimony shapes the choosing.
scenes.prose:
> *(Midday. The three doors stand open, and before the choosing, one voice will speak. Three voices offer themselves. Laurent again, the de Varenne heir, the creditors' voice, the young man who asked for debt, not charity. Let him speak the cost of ruin: what twelve hundred meant, in a French town, for twenty-five years. But he has spoken, and repetition dulls. Harrow the witness, twenty years of keeping, the schoolmaster's steadiness, the man who was offered a thousand pounds and chose the air here. Let him speak the cost of silence: what keeping meant. But the choosing is Rose's, and the witness has given enough. Letitia the quartermaster, the household's voice, the servants' hall, the twenty pounds refused, the mending table's ten years. Let her speak the cost of loyalty: what the house pays, and why. But Letitia speaks with orders, not testimony.)*
> *(She stands in the rose silk with the three doors open around her, and thinks: the choosing is mine, but the hearing is the room's. The voice, chosen, shapes the hour.)*
> *(The voice, chosen deliberately, the room's dignity in hand. The testimony was given, and the choosing's hour deepened around it.)*

scenes.synopsis: the testimony — the hearing, given; the choosing, deepened.
scenes.prose:
> *(The chosen voice rises — Laurent, Harrow, or Letitia, whichever Rose called — and speaks. The testimony is short, because the week has been long and the room knows the facts. What the voice gives is not information but weight: the cost, carried in a human voice, in the morning room's honest light. The room listens. Rose listens. The three doors stand open, and the testimony settles around them like dust in light.)*
> *(When it ends, the room is quieter than before. "Thank you," Rose says. The voice sits. The hearing, given. The choosing, deepened.)*

scenes.synopsis: the quartermaster's view — the household's testimony; the mending table's ten years.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia rises, uncalled but not unwelcome, and the room turns to her. "The servants' hall," she says, "has a view." She looks around: the flat voice, the tired eyes, the woman who ran the siege. "The view is: the house pays. Ten years, the Harringtons paid, and nobody thought the worse of them. Ten years, we'll pay, and nobody will think the worse of us." She looks at Rose. "The mending table's answer is: ten years is nothing. We've mended longer." She sits. The quartermaster's view, given.)*
> *(The room hears it: the household, consenting. The paying, precedented. The loyalty, priced at nothing and worth everything.)*

scenes.synopsis: the draft, ready — Quill's trust paper, unsigned; the atonement, prepared.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill rises, and lays the draft on the table: the émigré trust, founded with the eight thousand eight hundred, fed by the canal's three thousand, the creditors named — the de Varennes, by name; the de Valcourts, lightly. Harrow's deed, separate. "It's ready," he says. "The shape you chose. Unsigned." He looks at Rose. "The paper waits for the door." The room looks at the paper: the legal language, the intention made real. The draft, ready. The atonement, prepared.)*
> *(Rose touches the draft's edge. "Thank you, Mr. Quill." "Paper is patient," he says. The room almost smiles. The paper, waiting. The door, coming.)*

scenes.synopsis: the choosing's gown, witnessed — the room sees the rose; fashion as courage.
scenes.prose:
> *(The room sees the rose, and the seeing is part of the choosing. Deep rose, twenty years old, fashionable still. The long rope of pearls, doubled. The silver rose pin. The mended gloves, on the table beside the papers. She stands in the honest light, between the doors, and the gown is the choosing's: the archive's finest, the color of the name. The witnesses see it, and the seeing steadies them. Fashion as courage: the house does not under-dress its choosing.)*
> *(She meets Octavia's eye, and her friend nods: the rose, right. The gown, witnessed. The courage, dressed.)*

scenes.synopsis: expose, weighed — the town's right to know; Harrow's week in the papers.
scenes.prose:
> *(She weighs the first door, aloud, for the room. "Expose," she says. "The town's right to know: the sin was committed against the town's neighbors — the émigré families, the creditors, the village that read Pounce's sheet. The truth, told by the house, is the only telling that isn't theft." She looks at Harrow. "The cost: Mr. Harrow is 'the accomplice' for a week. The papers will say it. The town will repeat it." Harrow meets her eye, steady. "And the forty-one thousand six hundred," she says, "stays unspent. The telling is not the paying.")*
> *(The room weighs it with her: the candor, the cost, the unpaid price. The first door, weighed.)*

scenes.synopsis: bury, weighed — the wall rebuilt; the conscience, carried.
scenes.prose:
> *(She weighs the second door. "Bury," she says. "The papers burn, the wall rebuilds, the agents starve. The household keeps its peace. Harrow keeps his quiet. Nobody is 'the accomplice.' Nobody is a story." She looks at the joined sheet. "The cost: the proof disappears, and the moral cost remains. Mine. For the rest of my life." She looks around the room. "The wall is rebuilt, and I live behind it. The ledger stays closed. The thirty-eight thousand eight hundred stays in the canal's future, unowed and unpaid.")*
> *(The room weighs it: the peace, the cost, the carried sin. The second door, weighed.)*

scenes.synopsis: atone, weighed — the ten years; the slow shame and the clean ledger.
scenes.prose: > *(She weighs the third door. "Atone," she says. "The forty-one thousand six hundred, paid — the trust public, the creditors named, the ledger clean." She looks at Octavia. "The cost: ten years. The canal's income, committed. The surplus, spent. The town reads the sin on Saturday and the payment begins on Sunday — the shame is fast, the atonement is slow." She looks at Laurent. "But the innocent get something. The de Varennes are creditors. Harrow is paid. The de Valcourts are acknowledged." A pause. "It is the only door where the price is paid.")*

scenes.synopsis: the friends, before the doors — precision and affection, at the choosing's edge.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes to her in the pause, and the room gives them the moment. "The precision," Octavia says, quietly, "is done. The price is stated. The doors are weighed." She takes Rose's hand. "Whatever door, Rose. I've priced them all. I can afford any of them." A pause. "Can you afford to live with yours?" Rose looks at her friend: the precise hand, the bright eyes, the affection that does arithmetic. "I'm about to find out," she says.)*
> *("Then," Octavia says, "choose." The friends, before the doors. The affection, at the edge.)*

scenes.synopsis: the silence — the room waits; the choosing's weight, held.
scenes.prose:
> *(She stands before the three doors, in the rose silk, in the honest light, and the room waits. The silence is the choosing's: not empty, but full. The ledger, closed. The papers, joined. The draft, unsigned. The dried violets, in the bowl. The witnesses, watching. She thinks of the week: the blind item, the offer, the price, the screw. Each day, faced. Each figure, kept. Each door, weighed. Now, the choosing.)*
> *(She breathes, once. The silence holds. The doors stand open. The woman, choosing.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Dowager's word — Augusta, present; the old wisdom, lightly.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta rises, slowly, the ebony cane, and the room turns to its oldest witness. "I have lived," she says, "through three choosings of this kind. My own, my son's, and now yours." She looks at Rose, the sapphire velvet, the pearls. "The advice is always the same, and always useless: choose the door you can walk through every day for the rest of your life." A pause. "The doors don't close behind you, my dear. You live in the one you choose." She sits. The Dowager's word, given.)*
> *(The room hears it: the doors, inhabited. The choosing, daily. The old wisdom, lightly.)*

scenes.synopsis: the papers, in her hands — both halves; the sin, held.
scenes.prose:
> *(She takes up the joined sheet, both halves, and holds it. Her grandfather's hand. Harrow's neat pages. The tear, mended by their meeting. The émigré money, the gambling, the Hartwell losses covered first, the de Varennes and de Valcourts allowed to fall. The sin, in her hands. The proof, whole. She looks at it a long moment, and the room watches her look.)*
> *(One entry holds her longer than the rest: the de Valcourt banking branch, entered fair and ruined entire — the sums, the dates, Elias's hand unhurried over the worst of it, the Hartwell covering written in the same script as everything else. She knows that name from four seasons of other ledgers. Lucien de Valcourt. The Network's London face. The man who spent four seasons pricing her house had been priced himself, a generation earlier, by the hand she is holding. He never said so.)*
> *(She sets it down, gently, on the table between the doors. The papers, held. The choosing, coming.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE LEANING: before the choosing, the honest lean; which door pulls.
scenes.prose:
> *(Afternoon. The doors are laid out, weighed, inhabited by Augusta's wisdom, and before the choosing, the lean. Three leanings offer themselves, honestly. Toward expose: the candor pulls. The town's right to know, the hunters' version dying, the sin named by the house. The telling, clean and public. But Harrow is "the accomplice" for a week, and the thirty-eight thousand eight hundred stays unspent. Toward bury: the peace pulls. The papers burn, the wall rebuilds, nobody is a story. The household's quiet, kept. But the proof disappears, and the moral cost is hers, for life. Toward atone: the paying pulls. The forty-one thousand six hundred, the ten years, the innocent getting something. The only door where the price is paid. But ten years is long, and the shame is fast.)*
> *(She stands in the rose silk with the joined sheet on the table, and thinks of Octavia: which one can you afford to live with. The leaning, honestly felt, becomes the choosing's ground.)*
> *(She leaned the way she'd leaned all week: honestly, and with the price in hand. The leaning settled, and the choosing's hour deepened around it. Leaning is not choosing. But it is the ground the choosing stands on.)*

options.label: Toward atone

scenes.synopsis: the leaning, shared or kept — the friends, at the choosing's edge.
scenes.prose:
> *(She shares the leaning with Octavia — or keeps it, whichever she chose — and Octavia receives it precisely. "Good," she says. Or: "Good." The weighing was honest; the leaning is the ground. "You know," Octavia says, "my father used to say that a leaning honestly felt is half the choosing. The other half is courage." She takes Rose's hand. "You have the courage. I've watched you all week." She smiles. "Whatever door, Rose. The price is stated. The affection is stated. Choose.")*
> *("I will," Rose says. And finds, saying it, that it's true. The leaning, shared or kept. The choosing, coming.)*

scenes.synopsis: afternoon — the rose, the light changing; the choosing's gown, at the hour.
scenes.prose:
> *(Afternoon, and the honest light is going golden. The rose silk in gold light: deeper, warmer, the twenty-year-old weave glowing. The long rope of pearls, doubled, catching the light. The silver rose pin. The mended gloves, on the table. She stands in the changing light, between the doors, and the gown is the choosing's: the archive's finest, the color of the name, at the hour. The witnesses watch the light change on the silk, and the changing steadies them.)*
> *(She touches the dried violet at her wrist — faithfulness, in gold light — and turns to the doors. The rose, at the hour. The woman, choosing.)*

scenes.synopsis: the last temptation — the hunters' final offer; the choosing, tested.
scenes.prose:
> *(The last temptation comes at four, by letter, delivered to the house. Letitia brings it in, and Rose reads it before the room. It's short. The offer is tripled: three thousand pounds for the papers, the story, the exclusive. The threat is gone — no more safety lever, just money, plain. "My principal," Slade writes, "will not wait past Sunday." Rose reads it, folds it, and sets it on the table between the doors. "The hunters' final offer," she says. "Three thousand. Plain money, no threats." She looks around the room. "It's the most honest thing they've sent all week.")*
> *(The room is quiet. Three thousand pounds: a fortune, for papers. The temptation, laid beside the doors. The choosing, tested.)*

scenes.synopsis: the temptation, refused — the sin is not for sale; the choosing, unhurried.
scenes.prose:
> *(She looks at Slade's letter, lying between the doors, and the refusal is the week's refusal, stated one last time. "The sin," she says, "is not for sale. Not for two thousand. Not for three." She picks up the letter and hands it to Henry. "Evidence." She looks around the room. "Their clock said hurry. My clock says Sunday. It's Sunday." The temptation, refused. The choosing, unhurried.)*
> *(She stands in the rose silk, in the gold light, with the three doors open and the hunters' money filed as evidence, and the room knows: the choosing is hers. The refusal, final. The hour, come.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Three Doors ritual — the choosing's ceremony; the doors, entered in fashion; the chapter's ritual.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: the first door — EXPOSE. She enters it in the mind: the Gazette's press, the complete account, the town reading. Harrow, "the accomplice," for a week. The de Varennes, a story. The truth, told — and the forty-one thousand six hundred, unspent. She walks through the telling, fully, and comes back. The door stands open.)*
> *(Story morsel: the second door — BURY. She enters it in the mind: the papers burning, the wall rebuilding, the agents starving. The household's peace. Nobody, a story. The proof, gone — and the moral cost, hers, for life. She walks through the keeping, fully, and comes back. The door stands open.)*
> *(Story morsel: the third door — ATONE. She enters it in the mind: the forty-one thousand six hundred, the ten years, the trust's founding. The de Varennes, creditors. Harrow, paid. The de Valcourts, acknowledged. The shame, fast; the paying, slow. The only door where the innocent get something. She walks through the paying, fully, and comes back. The door stands open.)*
> *(Story morsel: the three doors, standing open. She has walked each one, fully, and come back. The rose silk, the gold light, the witnesses. The choosing's hour is now.)*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the ledger — "the precision is done. Choose.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: The choosing is come. Three doors stand open: expose, bury, atone. Tonight the choosing is witnessed in fashion: the household's finest, deliberate and unafraid — the house does not under-dress its choosing. Walk the three doors in the ritual's order. Enter each one in the mind, fully, and come back. Then choose. Exact. Courageous. Unhurried. The house that chooses does not flinch from its doors.

scenes.synopsis: the hour strikes — the ritual done; the choosing, now.
scenes.prose:
> *(The ritual ends, and the room is gold. She has walked the three doors, fully, and come back. The rose silk, the gold light, the witnesses. Octavia at the ledger: "The precision is done. Choose." The room holds its breath. The choosing's hour is now.)*
> *(She stands, in the rose silk, between the doors. The joined sheet on the table. The draft, unsigned. The dried violets, in the bowl. The leaning, felt. The courage, summoned. Now.)*

scenes.synopsis: the choosing's gown, at the choosing — the rose, in gold light; the woman, at the door.
scenes.prose:
> *(The gold light on the rose silk: the choosing's gown, at the choosing. Deep rose, twenty years old, the weave glowing. The long rope of pearls, doubled. The silver rose pin. The mended gloves, in her hands now, the mend at the thumb like a signature. She stands at the doors, in the gold light, in the archive's finest, and the gown is the choosing's: fashionable, deliberate, unafraid. The woman, at the door.)*
> *(She touches the dried violet at her wrist — faithfulness, in gold light — and chooses. The rose, worn. The choosing, done.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the door, entered; the gown, armor.

fashionChoices.label: Rose, softened
fashionChoices.detail: the pearls, bright; the threshold, held.

fashionChoices.detail: the gown decides.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE CHOICE: expose, bury, or atone; the sin, faced; the door, entered.
scenes.prose:
> *(Now. The three doors stand open, the ritual is walked, the price is stated, the leaning is felt. Three doors, each with its full weight. Expose: the complete truthful account, the émigré money entrusted and gambled, the Hartwell losses covered first, the de Varennes and de Valcourts allowed to fall, given to the Gazette whole and untrimmed, for Mrs. Bell to print because it is true and newsworthy. The town reads the sin, told by the house. The hunters' version dies. The cost, honestly held: Harrow is "the accomplice" for a week; the de Varennes are a story; Laurent's mother's name is in every sheet; and the thirty-eight thousand eight hundred stays unspent, because exposure is not payment. The truth is told, and the debts remain — for the town to know, and the house to still owe.)*
> *(Bury: the papers burn — both halves, in this room, witnessed. The wall rebuilds. The agents lose their proof. Pounce has yesterday's issue and nothing more. The household keeps its peace; Harrow keeps his quiet; nobody is "the accomplice," nobody is a story. The cost, honestly held: nothing is paid. The hundred and fifty stays in the surplus. The twelve hundred stays a ruin. The twenty-eight hundred stays a silence. The proof disappears, and the moral cost remains — hers, to carry, for the rest of her life. The wall is rebuilt, and she lives behind it, and the ledger stays closed.)*
> *(Atone: the forty-one thousand six hundred, paid. Eight thousand eight hundred now — a hundred and fifty to Harrow, his wages, his keeping deeded; the rest to found the émigré trust. Three thousand a year, for ten years, from the canal's revenue. The de Varennes are creditors, not victims, named by name. The de Valcourts are acknowledged, lightly. The trust is public. The ledger is clean. The cost, honestly held: ten years of paying. The canal's income, committed. The surplus, spent. The town reads the sin on Saturday and the payment begins on Sunday — the shame is fast, the atonement is slow. But it is the only door where the innocent get something. The only door where the price is paid.)*
> *(She stands in the rose silk, in the gold light, with the three doors open and the room waiting, and thinks of Octavia: the precision was the easy part. Of Augusta: you live in the one you choose. Of Elias: the choice he made in the bad years. Of Harrow: "I like the air here." And of herself: the unchoosing. The choice, made, becomes the life.)*
> *(The choice was made the way the week had been lived: deliberately, honestly, with the price in hand. The door, entered, became the life. Whatever she chose, she had weighed it fully, and the choosing was clean.)*

options.label: Expose
options.detail: *Candor+; the telling.* The complete truthful account to the Gazette; Bell prints because it is true. *(Harrow is "the accomplice" for a week; the thirty-eight thousand eight hundred stays unspent — exposure is not payment.)*

options.label: Bury
options.detail: *Resolve+; the wall.* The papers burn, witnessed; the agents lose their proof; the household keeps its peace. *(Nothing is paid; the moral cost is hers, for life — the ledger stays closed.)*

options.label: Atone
options.detail: *Mercy+; the paying.* Forty-one thousand six hundred, ten years; the trust founded, the creditors named, the ledger clean. *(Ten years of paying; the shame is fast, the atonement slow — but the innocent get something.)*

scenes.synopsis: the choice, spoken — the room hears; the door, named.
scenes.prose:
> *(She speaks the choice aloud, in the rose silk, in the gold light, before the witnesses. Whatever door she chose, expose, bury, or atone, she names it plainly, and the room hears it. "Expose." Or: "Bury." Or: "Atone." The word lands in the honest light, and the room receives it precisely, and with loyalty. Octavia closes the ledger — or opens it. Harrow bows his head. Laurent breathes. Letitia nods, once. The choice, spoken. The door, named.)*
> *(She looks around the room: the faces, the loyalty, the week. "Thank you," she says. "For the holding. Whatever door —" she stops, and smiles. "This door." The choosing, spoken. The life, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Bell's draft: "THE CHOICE — On Sunday's Door."
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting arrives at six, in Bell's own hand, delivered to the house: the proprietor has drafted all three versions, and the frame she shows Rose is the headline set in type: "THE CHOICE — On Sunday's Door." Three paragraphs, cool and unhurried. They describe, without naming, a house that weighed three doors and walked through one; a choosing, witnessed; a consequence, beginning. The last line is the blade: "The Gazette notes that some houses inherit money. This house has inherited a choice. Tomorrow's readers will know which door." Bell's rule holds: no names. But the town will read it, and know.)*
> *(Rose reads it twice and understands the weapon's shape: Bell has drafted the choosing's announcement in advance, and the draft waits — for the first step, which is Rose's to take. She files the draft with the Lash and the trust's paper: the drawer, the archive of the reckoning, complete. The blade, aimed. The step, coming.)*
scenes.sting: THE CHOICE — On Sunday's Door.

scenes.synopsis: the first step — the choice, enacted; the door, walked through.
scenes.prose:
> *(Evening. The choice is spoken, and the first step is Rose's. If she chose expose: she seals the complete truthful account, written in her own hand, whole and untrimmed: the émigré money, the gambling, the Hartwell losses, the de Varennes and de Valcourts, and sends it by Letitia's boy to the Gazette office, marked for the proprietor's eyes only. No meeting, no handshake, no favor asked; Bell will print it because it is true and newsworthy, or not at all. If she chose bury: she takes the joined sheet, both halves, and lays it on the morning room fire, witnessed by the household. The papers catch, the proof burns, and she begins rebuilding the wall: the order given to the masons before the ashes cool. If she chose atone: she takes Quill's pen and signs the trust's founding draft (the eight thousand eight hundred, the canal's three thousand a year, the creditors named), and the hundred and fifty is ordered to Harrow, his keeping deeded, the payment begun.)*
> *(Whatever door, the first step is taken. The choice, enacted. The life, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: evening — the rose, kept on; the choosing's gown, after the choice.
scenes.prose:
> *(She keeps the rose silk for the evening, and the rose has changed meaning through the day: morning, it was the choosing's gown; now it is the chosen's. The choice, spoken. The first step, taken. The door, entered. She stands in the bedroom, in lamplight, and looks at the woman in the glass: the rose, the pearls, the pin, the mended gloves. The archive's finest, on the choosing's night. The woman who chose, dressed.)*
> *(She touches the dried violet at her wrist — Élise's, faithfulness — and thinks of the door she's living in now. Expose, bury, or atone: whichever, it's hers. The rose, kept on. The woman, chosen.)*

fashionChoices.label: Rose, severe
fashionChoices.detail: the chosen's gown; the door, inhabited.

fashionChoices.label: Rose, softened
fashionChoices.detail: the pearls, bright; the evening, met.

fashionChoices.label: No choosing
fashionChoices.detail: the gown decides.

scenes.synopsis: the household's answer — the room receives the choice; the loyalty, returned.
scenes.prose:
> *(The household gathers in the evening, in the morning room, in lamplight, and the room receives the choice. Whatever the door, expose, bury, or atone, the answer is the same, because the choosing was honest. Letitia speaks for the hall: "The house," she says, "stands with the choosing." The servants' hall, the village men, the friends: the loyalty, returned. Harrow, paid or burning or told, whichever it is, bows his head. "Miss Hartwell." Laurent, creditor or story or silence, whichever it is, nods. "Stitch by stitch.")*
> *("Stitch by stitch," the room says back. The household's answer, given. The choosing, upheld.)*

scenes.synopsis: the friends' talk — the choosing's night; the price, faced.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes up at eleven, in her dressing gown, two cups of chocolate in hand. "Debrief," she says. "The unofficial one." They sit by the fire. "How does it feel," Octavia asks, "to have chosen?" Rose considers. "Like being told the length of a journey, and starting to walk it." Octavia nods. "The price." "The price," Rose agrees. "Stated. Faced. Paid, or told, or carried." "And the affection?" "Stated," Rose says. "Faced. Kept." They drink the chocolate. The friends' talk, at rest.)*
> *("Octavia." "Yes?" "Thank you. For the counting. For the affection." "Don't thank me for the affection," Octavia says. "That's the part that cost nothing." They look at each other, and the laughter comes, tired and warm. "The door," Octavia says. "The door," Rose agrees. "Whatever it is." "It's yours," Octavia says. The price, faced. The choosing, done.)*

scenes.synopsis: the cliffhanger — London; the agent reports, and a letter in a woman's hand arrives, signed "Vane"; the consequence, beginning.
scenes.prose: > *(London, Sunday night. Slade writes the report by lamplight, in the plain hand: the choosing happened; the door, whichever it was; Pounce's sheet with yesterday's issue and nothing more. The money bought eyes, ears, and the gutter sheet, and the eyes have reported. He seals it for the morning post. And with the evening delivery comes the answer — a letter in a woman's hand, signed "Vane." He reads it once, and his face gives nothing away. The principal has read the evening post. The principal has decided. Slade folds the letter and looks at the fire. "So," he says, to the empty room. "She chose. And now — we answer." The agent, instructed. The consequence, beginning.)*

scenes.synopsis: lamplight — the house after the choosing; dinner's aftermath, absorbed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Sunday evening, and the long table is cleared. The lamps are lit against a sky going blue at the windows, and the house makes its ordinary sounds: the kitchen settling, the stairs, the gates' far creak, the village dogs. She stands in the hall a moment and listens to the choosing settle into the walls. It sounds like nothing. That is the strange part. A day that weighed forty-one thousand six hundred pounds lands as quietly as a folded cloth.)*
> *(She touches the dried violet at her wrist — faithfulness — and goes in to the evening. The house, after the choosing. The vigil, beginning.)*

scenes.synopsis: the vigil's dress — the choosing's rose set aside; the archive's night face.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia helps her out of the rose silk, and the choosing's gown goes over the chair like a shed skin. In its place the archive's answer to the night: slate silk, the color of lamplight on old silver, twenty-five years old and re-cut once, the skirt plain, the bodice severe. The long rope of pearls, doubled. The silver rose pin. The mended gloves, last. In the glass the vigil's face: paler than the choosing's, and steadier for it.)*
> *("The house," Letitia says, "does not keep vigils in its best rose." "The house," Rose says, "keeps them in silver." The slate, worn. The night, dressed.)*

fashionChoices.label: Rose, watchful
fashionChoices.detail: the slate, severe; the night, met.

fashionChoices.label: Rose, gentle
fashionChoices.detail: the pearls, kept; the house, held.

fashionChoices.label: Letitia's eye
fashionChoices.detail: the quartermaster dresses the vigil.

scenes.synopsis: the hall's answer — the loyalty, settling into the night's work.
scenes.prose:
> *(Below stairs the evening goes on the way good houses go on: into the work. Alice banks the kitchen fire and sets the lamps for the night's second sitting. The hall has absorbed the choosing the way it absorbs everything — a death, a wedding, a Sunday of three doors — by folding it into the orders. Upstairs the choosing was a doctrine. Downstairs it is a roster: who sits where, who carries what, who minds the gates.)*
> *(Amos takes the lantern for the gates' first hour. "The house," he says to nobody in particular, pulling on his coat, "has chosen." The hall hears it the way the hall hears everything: as an order it had already given itself. The loyalty, settled. The night's work, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: the first ripples — the boy, the mason, the deed; the choice, going outward.
scenes.prose:
> *(The choice does not stay in the morning room. If she chose expose: Letitia's boy rode at six with the sealed account — the complete truthful account in Rose's own hand, whole and untrimmed, Harrow's half cited with his leave — for the Gazette office, marked for the proprietor's eyes only. The road to town is dark now, and the boy is on it. If she chose bury: the mason's order went out before the ashes cooled, and the cart of stone stands at the gate by lamplight. The wall rebuilds course by course; the third course by seven in the morning. If she chose atone: Quill's seal is on the founding draft since noon, the £150, three years' wages, is ordered to Harrow, the keeping's deed copying fair in the study, and the trust is public before the ink is dry.)*
> *(Three different evenings, one house. The ripples, going outward. The choosing, at work in the world.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening's talk — the choosing, absorbed into ordinary conversation.
scenes.prose:
> *(At table's end the talk is ordinary, and the ordinariness is the point. The village men discuss the mason's rates. Someone's cousin's boy is apprenticed. The choosing sits among them like a guest who has been introduced and requires no further ceremony. When the talk brushes it — the wall, the paper, the trust — it brushes it the way one brushes a new scar: carefully, and with ownership.)*
> *("Stitch by stitch," someone says, and the room takes it up without quite meaning to, the way a hall takes up a hymn. The doctrine, passed hand to hand. The evening, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the witness, kept — the cottage, the guard, the telling; per door.
scenes.prose:
> *(Harrow is told, and kept, and the telling is shaped to the door. If she chose expose: she tells him what the account says of him — that the town will call him "the accomplice" for a week — and he takes it the way he has taken everything: steadily, the schoolmaster's back straight. "The truth," he says, "was never going to flatter me, Miss Hartwell. I kept it anyway." If she chose bury: he watched the papers burn, both halves, and keeps his cottage and his quiet. Nothing is paid; the keeping is its own wage. If she chose atone: the £150, three years' wages, is ordered, his keeping deeded outright, and he bows his head over the news the way a man bows over grace.)*
> *(Whatever the door, the rest is unconditional, and she says it again so the night hears it: the guard stays. No one touches him, no one buys him, no one prints him. "Miss Hartwell," he says. The witness, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the heir, spare — the garden, the empty chair; the card, not yet written.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent takes no dinner. His chair at table stands empty through the evening, and once, from the hall window, Rose sees him walking the walled garden's path alone — the black coat, the hands in the pockets, the young man's back to the house. He does not look up. The card he will write in the morning's post is not yet written; whatever it will say, tonight he is only the heir of a ruin, walking.)*
> *(She does not call to him. Some griefs want company and some want the garden, and she has learned, this week, to tell the difference. The empty chair. The dark path. The heir, spare.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE VIGIL'S POSTURE: how Rose meets the household's eyes tonight.
scenes.prose:
> *(Evening, and the house is watching her — not anxiously, but the way a household watches its mistress on the choosing's night: to learn the posture. Three postures offer themselves. Hold the room: sit with them through the evening in the slate silk, the choosing's face kept on, the talk ordinary around her. The vigil, kept in company. Walk the house: make the vigil's circuit — the gates, the garden wall, the cottage — seen by all, the choosing's walk made visible. The posture, in motion. Work the night: spare the house the performance and do the night's business quietly — the memorandum, the letters, the morning's orders. The vigil, kept at the desk.)*
> *(She stands in the hall with the lamps lit and the house listening, and thinks: the choosing was the door. Tonight is how she lives in it, the first night.)*
> *(She chose the posture the way she had chosen the door: deliberately, and with the house in hand. Whatever it was, the household read it as the choosing's continuation, and settled around it. The vigil's posture, taken.)*

options.label: Hold the room
options.detail: *Resolve+; the evening's face.* Sit with them through the evening, the choosing's face kept on. *(The night is long; the face, held.)*

options.label: Walk the house
options.detail: *Candor+; the circuit.* The gates, the garden wall, the cottage — the choosing's walk, made visible. *(The walking is the answer.)*

options.label: Work the night
options.detail: *Mercy+; the desk.* Spare the house the performance; do the night's business quietly. *(The work, done; the room, spared.)*

scenes.synopsis: the debrief's second hour — the night's arithmetic, per door; the memorandum book.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia finds her after the posture is taken, with the memorandum book and the night's arithmetic. If expose: "The account is on the road," Octavia says. "Bell prints because it is true. The week of 'the accomplice' — we prepare Harrow for it, and the house for the town's reading." If bury: "The proof is ash," she says. "The wall's courses: count them. Third by seven. The agents hold Saturday's issue and nothing more — the arithmetic of starvation." If atone: "The trust is founded," she says. "The first payment is entered. Ten years, three thousand a year, the canal's revenue — the figures, kept where the town can see them.")*
> *(She writes as she talks, the pencil moving, the friend's courage wearing its favorite disguise: sums. "Whatever the door," Octavia says, not looking up, "the night's arithmetic is the same. We chose first. The rest is bookkeeping." The debrief's second hour. The sums, loved.)*

scenes.synopsis: the post, sealed — Henry's evidence drawer; the watch on the agents.
scenes.prose:
> *(In the study Henry files the week's evidence with a clerk's neatness: Slade's final offer — three thousand, refused — laid beside the two thousand, both dead now, both kept. The morning post's letters are sealed for London: the ordinary ones, the estate's business, nothing the agents could use. And the agents themselves — Cecilia's people, their lodgings, their bought eyes — are watched quietly, the way one watches a dog that has stopped barking.)*
> *("Too quiet," Henry says. "Agreed," Rose says. A hunter who misses does not go home. He reloads. The post, sealed. The watch, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the flower, kept — Élise's night dried violets; faithfulness, for the evening.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes up with the night's dried violets, warm as ever, unruffled by a week that would have flattened a lesser woman. "For the morning room," she says, arranging the posy where the choosing's bowl stood. "The town may read what it likes tomorrow. Tonight the house smells of faithfulness." She steps back, tilts her head. "The slate becomes you, Miss Hartwell. The choosing wore rose. The vigil wears silver. Somebody should tell the Gazette's fashion column." Rose laughs, surprised out of the evening's gravity. "Somebody," Élise says, "will not be me.")*
> *(She pins a dried violet at Rose's wrist, where the choosing's had wilted. Faithfulness: not to the grandfather, who does not deserve it. To the people the week touches. The flower, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the slate, in lamplight — the vigil's dress, re-seen; fashion as steadiness.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone in the bedroom she looks at the vigil's dress in lamplight, and the lamplight does what honest light does: it shows the slate silk truly. The color of lamplight on old silver. The long rope of pearls, doubled, catching it. The silver rose pin. The mended gloves, laid on the dressing table, the mend at the thumb like a signature. The dried violet at the wrist. She stands in the archive's night face, and the gown is the vigil's: severe, deliberate, unafraid. Fashion as steadiness: the house does not under-dress its night.)*
> *(She turns from the glass. The slate, worn. The vigil, dressed.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the modiste judges the vigil.

scenes.synopsis: the night's work — the per-door second moves; stone, road, or pen.
scenes.prose:
> *(The evening's work goes on past the lamps' lighting. If she chose bury: the mason's cart is unloaded at the gate by lantern light, and the first stones go up in the dark — the wall's first courses, the mortar's clean smell, the trowel's tap carrying across the garden. Rose stands at the morning-room window and watches a stone set true. If she chose expose: the road to town is dark and Bell's boy is not yet returned; the Gazette office's lamp burns in her imagination, the sealed account waiting on the proprietor's desk. The waiting is the work. If she chose atone: Quill's clerk copies the deed fair in the study, the pen scratching past nine, the seal's red wax warming by the candle. The £150 order, three years' wages, is already on its way to Harrow.)*
> *(Three different labors, one night. The stone, the road, the pen. The choosing, worked.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening's ordinary — the drawing room, the fire, the choosing absorbed.
scenes.prose:
> *(In the drawing room the fire is built up and the talk refuses, nobly, to be solemn. The Harringtons' eldest tells a story about a runaway gig. Somebody's aunt is quoted. The choosing sits in the corner like a dog that has been walked and fed: present, content, requiring nothing. When the talk does touch it — the wall, the paper, the ten years — it is with the ease of people who have decided, and are done deciding.)*
> *(Rose sits among them in the slate silk and lets the ordinary do its work. The evening, held. The house, at ease in its door.)*

scenes.synopsis: the creditors, remembered — the names, carried; per door.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone for a minute in the hall, she runs the creditors through her mind the way Octavia ran them at noon: the de Varennes, twelve hundred, creditors not victims, named by name. The de Valcourts, twenty-eight hundred, promised in the spring on their own paper, acknowledged lightly. The de la Roche, nine hundred. The de Brissac, fourteen hundred. And the others — the trust's paper names them all, or the account does, or no one ever will.)*
> *(If she chose expose: their names will be in every sheet in England by Monday, told true. If she chose bury: their names go with the smoke, unacknowledged, and the carrying is hers alone. If she chose atone: their names are on the trust's founding, and the paying has begun. Three fates for the same list. She carries it into the drawing room like a weight she has chosen to lift. The names, remembered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the quartermaster's night — Letitia, dressed for the vigil; the tremor, planted.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia dresses for the vigil in the quartermaster's blacks — bombazine, twenty years old, the collar's lace her one concession — and the dressing is an order of battle: everything in its place, everything accounted for. She fastens her cuff, and her fingers pause on the button. Not a fumble. A hesitation, the length of a breath, before the button goes through. She does the other cuff without pause, as if to prove the first one nothing. In the glass her face is the household's face: composed, tired, intact.)*
> *(Rose, watching from the door, says nothing. The pause, noted. The naming, withheld. The quartermaster, dressed.)*

fashionChoices.label: Letitia, composed
fashionChoices.detail: the night, managed; the quartermaster, intact.

fashionChoices.label: Letitia, gentle
fashionChoices.detail: the lace, showing; the aunt, softened.

fashionChoices.label: Rose's eye
fashionChoices.detail: the niece judges the vigil.

scenes.synopsis: the debrief closes — the night, divided; the friends, at ease.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia closes the memorandum book with a snap that is almost cheerful. "The debrief," she says, "is adjourned. The night is divided thus: Amos has the gates till midnight, the second man after. The clerk has the deed till it's fair. You" — she looks at Rose — "have the choosing's night, which is yours to spend as the posture dictates." She rises, and at the door turns. "Rose." "Yes?" "Whatever Monday costs — the reading, the courses, the payments — it costs less than Saturday's timetable. You chose Monday's." She is gone before Rose can answer, which is Octavia's favorite way to have the last word.)*
> *(The night, divided. The friends, at ease. The last word, had.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE NIGHT'S ORDER: what the house does with the night.
scenes.prose:
> *(Nine o'clock, and the house waits for the night's order. Three orders offer themselves. Set the watch: the house awake in shifts, the lamps lit, the drive held, the cottage guarded, nobody sleeping unguarded — the choosing's night staffed like a siege, because the hunters are quiet and quiet is information. Keep it gentle: the house to bed, only the necessary lamps, the vigil kept by two — Amos and the second man — the choosing's night rested, because the week was long and the household has earned its sleep. Work it through: the night's business done before morning — the memorandum finished, the letters written, the post ready, the deed fair — the choosing's night worked, because Monday will be full.)*
> *(She stands in the hall with the order in her mouth, and thinks of the posture she took at eight: the evening's face, the circuit, the desk. The night's order follows the vigil's posture — or corrects it.)*
> *(She gave the order the way she had given the morning's: plainly, and once. Whatever it was — the watch, the gentleness, the work — the household took it up without a murmur, the way the hall takes up everything: as an order it had already given itself. The night's order, set.)*

options.label: Set the watch
options.detail: *Resolve+; the gates, the lamps.* The house awake in shifts; the drive held; nobody sleeps unguarded. *(The night, staffed.)*

options.label: Keep it gentle
options.detail: *Mercy+; the choosing's night, rested.* The house to bed; only the necessary lamps; the vigil kept by two. *(The house, spared.)*

options.label: Work it through
options.detail: *Candor+; the letters, the ledger.* The night's business done before morning; the memorandum finished; the post ready. *(The work, finished.)*

scenes.synopsis: the aunt, quiet — the cracking begins; the sentences, stopped.
scenes.prose:
> *(After the order, Letitia moves through the evening with the quartermaster's efficiency — and twice, she stops. Once at the morning-room door: her hand on the frame, a breath taken, nothing said. Once at the stairs: a sentence started — "Rose, I —" — and not finished. "Nothing," she says, when Rose looks up. "The week." She goes up with the household book under her arm, and her footsteps on the stairs are not the quartermaster's footsteps. They are a woman's, going somewhere she does not want to go.)*
> *(Rose does not follow. Some silences are load-bearing, and this one is holding up the whole house. The aunt, quiet. The cracking, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night's labor — the mason's stones, the boy's road, the clerk's pen; per door.
scenes.prose:
> *(The night's labor shows itself by lamplight. If she chose bury: the mason's men are at the wall, and the first courses go up in the lantern light — stone on stone, the mortar's clean smell, the wall rising where the gap was. Rose watches from the garden door as the third stone of the second course is tapped true. It is not yet ten, and the wall is already less of a wound. If she chose expose: the road to town stays dark, and Bell's boy is still out. Somewhere between the Park and the Gazette office, the sealed account rides in a boy's coat pocket — the complete truthful account, in her own hand, whole and untrimmed. The night holds its breath around it. If she chose atone: the clerk's pen scratches on in the study, copying the deed fair — the keeping, the trust, the creditors named — and the seal's red wax waits by the candle like a small patient sun.)*
> *(Stone, road, pen. The labor, shown. The choosing, worked by other hands.)*

scenes.synopsis: the gates, held — Amos, the night's porter; the drive, empty.
scenes.prose:
> *(Amos walks the gates' first hour with the lantern, and the drive is empty all the way to the village. He has held these gates through four lines and a stranger and an offer of three thousand pounds, and he holds them tonight the way he holds everything: as if the holding were the job and the job were the honor. Rose walks down with him as far as the lodge, and they stand a minute in the dark, two Hartwell people, saying nothing that needs saying.)*
> *("All quiet, Miss Hartwell." "All quiet, Amos." The lantern swings. The gates, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Dowager, at ease — sapphire velvet in lamplight; the age, dry.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta holds the drawing room's best chair in sapphire velvet, the silver embroidery catching the lamplight, the pearls loose at her throat, the ebony cane across her knees. She has the air of a woman for whom every evening since 1790 has been a kind of vigil, and who long ago learned to dress for it. "At my age, my dear," she says, "every night is a vigil. One simply sees that the velvet is brushed." She knows only that the de Valcourt banking branch fell, all those years ago — a thing one mentions the way one mentions weather — and she mentions it tonight only to say: "The past, Rose, is a tiresome guest. Feed it once, and it stays for the week.")*
> *(She rises, slowly, splendidly, and goes up. The velvet, brushed. The Dowager, at ease.)*

fashionChoices.label: Augusta, exact
fashionChoices.detail: the velvet, severe; the age, honored.

fashionChoices.label: Augusta, at ease
fashionChoices.detail: the pearls, loose; the evening, enjoyed.

fashionChoices.label: Rose's eye
fashionChoices.detail: the niece judges the Dowager.

scenes.synopsis: the room, after — the morning room, what the choosing left; per door.
scenes.prose:
> *(She goes back to the morning room once, alone, to see what the choosing left. If she chose expose: the desk holds the account's fair copy, the sealed original gone to town — her own hand, whole and untrimmed, waiting in duplicate for the morning's reading. If she chose bury: the fireplace is cold, the ash swept, and through the window the wall's gap shows the lantern light where the mason's men work. The proof is gone; the room keeps the shape of it anyway. If she chose atone: Quill's draft lies on the desk with the seal still warm, the trust's founding signed and public, the £150 order, three years' wages, gone to Harrow.)*
> *(She stands a moment in the room where she chose, and the room gives her nothing back but lamplight. That is enough. The room, after. The choosing, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the hall, at rest — Alice, the kitchen fire, the night's second hour.
scenes.prose:
> *(The servants' hall settles toward its rest. Alice banks the kitchen fire and lays the morning's kindling; the second sitting's dishes are washed and put away; the talk is low and contented, the talk of people whose orders are clear. Somewhere upstairs a door closes softly. The house exhales.)*
> *(In the hall's book, in Alice's neat hand, tomorrow's first orders are already entered: the mason's kitchen door at seven, the Gazette boy's expected return, the deed's fair copy to be collected. The choosing's night, administered. The hall, at rest.)*

scenes.synopsis: the flower's errand — rosemary, remembrance; the night's last kindness.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes once more, at half past nine, with a sprig of rosemary cut from the garden in the dark. "For the morning room," she says. "Remembrance. The night's flower, after the day's." She lays it beside the dried violets — faithfulness and remembrance, the season's two truths, in one bowl. "The garden," she adds, "is very dark and very ordinary tonight, Miss Hartwell. I checked. Nothing in it but rosemary and the mason's lantern.")*
> *(She curtsies, warm as ever, and is gone down the stairs. The rosemary stays, smelling of the dark garden. The errand, done.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE LAST ACT: Rose's last act before ten o'clock.
scenes.prose:
> *(Half past nine, and the house is nearly settled. One act remains before ten o'clock — hers, the last of the choosing's day. Three acts offer themselves. The memorandum: sit at the desk and write the evening into Octavia's book — the figures, the watch's order, the morning's plan — the night entered, the record kept. The garden: walk the walled garden alone in the dark, where the papers were found and the wall is rising or standing — look at it once, in the night, and come back. The past, faced where it lives. The candle: leave the morning room's candle burning for whoever cannot sleep — Letitia, with her load-bearing silence; Laurent, with his garden; Harrow, with his week ahead — the vigil's light, kept for the house.)*
> *(She stands in the hall with the lamps turned low, and thinks: the choosing was the door, the posture was the evening, the order was the night. This is the last act. Then ten o'clock, and the night's deep hour, and Monday.)*
> *(She did the last act the way she had done the first step: deliberately, and with her own hands. Whatever it was — the book, the garden, the candle — the house would find it in the morning and know the vigil had been kept. The last act, done.)*

options.label: The memorandum
options.detail: *Resolve+; the night, entered.* Write the evening into the book — the figures, the watch, the morning's plan. *(The record, kept.)*

options.label: The garden
options.detail: *Candor+; the dark, walked.* The walled garden, alone, where the papers were found. *(The past, faced where it lives.)*

options.label: The candle
options.detail: *Mercy+; the light, left.* The morning room's candle burning, for whoever cannot sleep. *(The house, kept company.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Dowager's word, at night — light, dry; the going up.
scenes.prose: > *(Augusta goes up before ten, the ebony cane, the sapphire velvet, the pearls. At the stairs she turns. "You may keep your vigil, my dear," she says. "I shall keep my bed, which is the older wisdom. The de Valcourts" — the banking branch, fallen all those years ago, a thing one mentions the way one mentions weather — "would have approved of the velvet, if not the hour." She smiles, dry as dust, and climbs. The Dowager's word, given. The house, settling.)*

scenes.synopsis: the watch, posted — the night's order, executed; Amos, the cottage guard.
scenes.prose:
> *(The night's order is executed as given. If she set the watch: the house wakes in shifts — Amos at the gates till midnight and the second man after, the cottage guard doubled, the lamps lit on every landing, the drive held like a held breath. If she kept it gentle: the house goes to bed, and only the necessary lamps burn — Amos and the second man keep the vigil between them, the gates, the cottage, the quiet. If she worked it through: the study lamp burns toward ten, the memorandum finished, the letters written, the post ready, the deed fair — and then, the lamps out, the house to bed.)*
> *(Whatever the order, the executing is the household's gift: done without murmur, the way the hall does everything. The watch, posted. The night, ordered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the vigil, kept — Rose, the evening's settling; logistics and one image.
scenes.prose:
> *(She sits in the bedroom with the dried violet at her wrist and does the logistics of morning: the mason's third course at seven, or the Gazette's reading by eleven, or the trust's first accounting — the figures, the post, the watch's changing, each item placed where Monday can find it. The ledger of the night, balanced. And underneath the logistics, unsaid, the image she would never speak aloud: the walled garden in the dark, the gap in the wall like a mouth closed around a secret, or opening to tell it.)*
> *(She sets the dried violet in water. The logistics, done. The image, kept. The vigil, nearly kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Vigil ritual — the choosing's night, dressed and ordered; the chapter's ritual.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: the dressing — per door. Expose: the account sealed and gone to town; the house dresses for a week of being read. Bury: the wall's first stones rising in the dark; the house dresses around a secret it will carry. Atone: the trust signed and public; the house dresses for ten years of paying. Whatever the door, the vigil's face is the same: severe, deliberate, unafraid.)*
> *(Story morsel: the posting — the watch posted per the night's order. Amos at the gates with the lantern; the second man at the lodge till midnight's change; the cottage guard doubled; the lamps lit on every landing, or only the necessary ones, as ordered. The house that chose does not sleep carelessly.)*
> *(Story morsel: the keeping — the house settling around the choice. The drawing room's fire built up; the servants' hall at rest; Letitia's candle still burning under her door; Laurent's chair empty at table, his path in the garden dark. The night holds them all, and asks nothing.)*
> *(Story morsel: the evening's labor — per door. Expose: the road to town dark, the sealed account riding in a boy's coat pocket, the Gazette office's lamp imagined. Bury: the mason's lantern at the wall, stone on stone, the wound closing course by course. Atone: the clerk's pen in the study, the deed copying fair, the seal's red wax like a small patient sun. Three labors, one evening.)*
> *(Story morsel: the evening's close — the house settling toward ten, the watch awake. The memorandum closed, or the garden walked, or the candle burning in the morning room, as she chose. The vigil is kept to ten o'clock. Monday waits past the dark, punctual as ever.)*

ritual.occasionBrief: The choosing is done; the night is the household's to keep. The vigil is dressed and ordered: the house in its night face, the watch posted, the lamps lit against the dark. Walk the night in the ritual's order — the dressing, the posting, the keeping. Exact. Quiet. Unhurried. The house that chose does not sleep carelessly.

scenes.synopsis: the evening settles — the house toward rest, the watch awake.
scenes.prose:
> *(The clock nearing ten, and the house settling toward its rest around the watch. The lamps are turned down on the landings. The ordinary sounds of an evening closing: a stair's tread, the kitchen cat, the wind at a shutter. From the village, nothing at all — the night holding itself quiet, the way it holds everything, till morning. The choosing's evening, drawn close around the house.)*
> *(On the drive the lantern holds its ground — Amos at the gates, the round not yet begun. The evening, closing. The watch, awake.)*

scenes.synopsis: the wrapper — the evening's private hour; the vigil, eased.
scenes.prose:
> *(Before ten she takes the vigil's private hour — the wrapper, dove grey silk, white stitching, the night's own color — and the vigil eases toward its closing. The mended gloves are set down on the dressing table, the mend at the thumb catching the candlelight. The dried violet stays at her wrist. In the glass the woman of the choosing's evening: grey, quiet, unadorned, and — she is surprised to find — at rest. The archive has a face for every hour, and this is the evening's deepening.)*
> *(She puts the slate back on before the clock strikes — the house will have its mistress dressed for ten. The wrapper, folded. The vigil, eased and resumed.)*
