fashionChoices.detail: the mistress judges the brother.

scenes.synopsis: the hand's cost, totalled — what the weighing costs each of them; the seal, uncut.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone, past one, she totals the night the way she totals everything: in columns that don't balance. What the woman's hand costs Octavia: the sums, loved and left, the arithmetic done, the weighing that is not arithmetic. What it costs Henry: the law's limit, the books shut till nine, the name Monday's. What it costs Rose: the mirror, looked at in water, the pen held steady, the question of what she becomes to hold it.)*
> *(The signature is unknown. The contents are unknown. The intent is priced. She takes the seal from the purse shelf and holds it uncut, the wax beside it, and does not write. Not yet. The seal, in her hand. The night, weighed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Dowager, asleep — the longest game, at rest; what she knows, and doesn't.
scenes.prose:
> *(She passes Augusta's door at half past one, and the Dowager is asleep the way she does everything: completely, and on her own terms. The candle is out. The ebony cane stands by the chair. The sapphire velvet lies over the chairback, the pearls coiled beside it. She knows that the de Valcourt banking branch fell, a generation ago. She does not know whose hand finished it.)*
> *(Rose stands a moment in the dark hall. The longest game in the house is sleeping, and the house is better for it. She does not knock. The cane, standing. The game, at rest.)*

scenes.synopsis: the garden, at half past one — the past, quiet; the wall, per door.
scenes.prose:
> *(From the bedroom window the walled garden lies at half past one, and the past, no new face, only the old sin, lies quiet in it still. If she chose bury: the second course stands complete in the dark, the gap less of a wound, stone on stone, and the third course waits for seven. If she chose expose or atone: the gap stands open to the night, the wall down where the papers came out, and the dark sits in it patiently, the way it has sat since Sunday.)*
> *(Rosemary grows black against the wall, remembrance, and the reload does not reach the garden; the garden is older than the hunters, and will be here when their money is gone. She watches it a moment, and the watching steadies her. The garden, at half past one. The past, quiet.)*

scenes.synopsis: the blacks, at one — the quartermaster's night dress, re-seen; the wrapper, the woman.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia at one o'clock is two women in one dressing. The quartermaster's blacks hang in the wardrobe, the bombazine, the collar's lace, the cuffs fastened, the brooch straight, the uniform waiting for morning. The woman wears the wrapper, the grey wool, the night plait, the loosened lace of a concession twenty years unpermitted. In the morning room's glass the two of them stand side by side: the office, and the woman the office was built to house.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the town will read the shape she kept silent, and the wrapper is worn against the reading. If she chose bury: the silence is kept, and the wrapper is worn against the keeping. If she chose atone: the shape is paid for, and the wrapper is worn against the price. Whatever the door, the dressing is the same: the quartermaster, at one, coming undone one woman at a time. The lace, loosened. The aunt, showing.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the wrapper, worn; the woman, showing.

fashionChoices.detail: the niece judges the uniform.

scenes.synopsis: the plan, set — half past one; the working night, nearly done; the money, moving.
scenes.prose:
> *(Half past one in London, and Slade's working night is nearly done. His second man's instructions are changed and in his head. The boy is paid and gone. The lodgings' rent is a month in advance, the roof kept, the watching over, the working staffed. He sits with the purse lighter by the night's spending and counts what remains the way a man counts ammunition: carefully, and with respect for what it will do.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the remaining money is the Monday special's paper and ink, the lie set before the truth. If she chose bury: the remaining money is the search's week, the stones, the letters, the memory, priced by the day. If she chose atone: the remaining money is the smear's run, the forty-one thousand six hundred dressed as hush money, the ledger dirtied in print. In every door the counting is the same: the purchase failed, the purchaser is buying again, and the principal's patience is spent. The plan, set. The money, moving.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Letter's Answering ritual — the house answers the woman's hand in fashion; the chapter's ritual.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: the answering — per door. Expose: the account riding to Bell; the house dresses for the week of being read, and being read first by the gutter. Bury: the wall rising in the dark; the house dresses around the secret it carries, and the search for it. Atone: the trust paying; the house dresses for the smear, and outlasts it. Whatever the door, the answering's face is the same: exact, quiet, unafraid.)*
> *(Story morsel: the weighing — the three weigh the hand, the purse, the changed orders. The signature unknown, the contents unknown, the intent priced. The memorandum closed, the draft folded, the seal in her hand, uncut. The night holds them all, and asks nothing.)*
> *(Story morsel: the keeping — the house settling around the weighing, against the reload. The watch on the drive; Harrow's guard doubled, or the household at rest, or Henry's ride readied, as ordered at ten. The drawing room's fire banked; the servants' hall asleep. The night holds them all, and asks nothing.)*
> *(Story morsel: the night's third hour — per door. Expose: the road to town dark, the boy still out, the gutter's Monday special setting in type. Bury: the wall's second course standing, the search's money moving in London. Atone: the deed half fair-copied, the smear's first line being written. Three labors, one reload, one weighing.)*
> *(Story morsel: two o'clock's approach — the house nearly asleep except the watch. The memorandum closed, or the garden walked, or the candle burning, as she chose at midnight. The answering is done. Two o'clock waits past the dark, punctual as ever.)*

ritual.occasionBrief: The letter has been weighed — the hand, the purse, the changed orders, the principal's intent priced three ways. The house answers the only way it knows: it dresses for the night it is in. The small hours are answered and ordered: the watch kept, the sums held, the hand met, unnamed, unanswered or answered in kind. Walk the night in the ritual's order — the answering, the weighing, the keeping. Exact. Quiet. Deliberate. The house that weighed does not meet the dawn unarmed.

scenes.synopsis: half past one — the house, asleep except the watch; the reload, answered.
scenes.prose:
> *(Half past one, and the house is asleep except the watch. The lamps burn low on the landings. The morning room's fire is banked. The study's lamp is out, the draft folded away for morning, Henry's bag packed by the door. Somewhere the kitchen cat; somewhere a shutter; somewhere in the village a dog barks once at the lodgings' bright windows, then doesn't.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the road to town is dark, and the boy is still out with the sealed account. If she chose bury: the wall stands in the dark, and the third course waits for seven. If she chose atone: the deed waits half fair-copied, and the trust's first letters wait for the post. Whatever the door, the third hour is the same: the house asleep, the reload staffed, and the house knowing it. The night, deepened. The watch, awake.)*

scenes.synopsis: the hall, asleep — Alice, the bread baked; the kitchen, at rest.
scenes.prose:
> *(Below stairs the night is done the way weather is done: quietly, and without asking. Alice set the night's bread to rise at eleven, and by half past one it is baked, the loaves cooling on the rack, the kitchen's work finished. The second sitting's voices are gone. The hall is dark except the banked range, and the house's people sleep the sleep of people whose orders were clear.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the hall sleeps knowing the boy is on the road, and Monday's reading. If she chose bury: the hall sleeps knowing the wall rises, and the third course at seven. If she chose atone: the hall sleeps knowing the trust pays, and ten years. Whatever the door, the hall's answer is the same: the orders were clear, the night was staffed, and the house is already loaded for Monday, stitch by stitch, the way it does everything. The bread, baked. The hall, asleep.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE UNWRITTEN: whether Rose writes her own letter to the unknown hand.
scenes.prose:
> *(Half past one, and the weighing is done, and one question remains: the hand wrote to Slade, and Slade's orders changed. Does Rose write back? Three answers offer themselves. Write it: her own formed hand, the house's answer, sealed and held for morning, resolve against the principal, because a woman who writes is answered in writing. Hold it: wait for the morning's evidence, the factor's books, the name the money wears, candor to the unknown, because the letter written blind is the letter regretted. Refuse it: no correspondence with the hunters' money, the hand unanswered, mercy to the night, because some letters dignify their senders by being ignored.)*
> *(She stands in the morning room with the seal in her hand and the wax beside it, and thinks: the choosing was the door, the hand was the reckoning, the aunt was the family, the weighing was the night. This is the letter, written or not.)*
> *(She decided for the letter the way she had decided for the night: deliberately, and once. Whatever it was, the writing, the holding, the refusing, the seal went back to the purse shelf, or the wax was cut, or the pen stayed dry, and the small hours took it up without a murmur. The letter, decided.)*

options.detail: *Candor+; the evidence, awaited.* The factor's books; the name, first. *(The blind letter, unwritten.)*

options.detail: *Mercy+; the correspondence, declined.* The hand, unanswered; the night, kept. *(Some letters dignify by being ignored.)*

scenes.synopsis: the drive, at quarter to two — the lantern; the empty road; the night, guarded.
scenes.prose:
> *(At quarter to two the second man walks the drive with the lantern, and the drive is empty all the way to the village. Nothing has come up it all night but the mason's cart. Nothing will till morning. He walks it steady, unhurried, and the lantern swings its small circle of Hartwell light down the drive and back, the way it has swung since midnight, the way it will swing till the watch changes at two.)*
> *(Rose watches from the bedroom window. Whatever the door, the account riding, the wall rising, the trust paying, the watch is the same: the night guarded into its last quarter-hour, the house asleep behind it. The lantern, swinging. The drive, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — the reload, at the gates; the note, refused; the night's last arrival.
scenes.prose: > *(The sting comes at quarter to two, and it is the reload trying the gates. A boy at the lodge with a note for Harrow's keeping, in a clerk's hurried hand, the seal plain. If she chose expose: the note is the accomplice's summons, Harrow called to the lodgings before the Monday special prints. If she chose bury: the note is the search's bribe, the grandfather's letters, the schoolmaster's memory, priced. If she chose atone: the note is the smear's first purchase, a creditor's name bought for the ledger's dirtying. Whatever the door, the guard refuses it: no one touches him, no one buys him, no one prints him. The boy goes back down the drive empty-handed. The note, refused. The reload, turned away.)*
scenes.sting: the sting — the reload, at the gates; the note, refused; the night's last arrival.

scenes.synopsis: the refusal, reported — the boy, the note; the lodgings, quieting.
scenes.prose:
> *(The second man brings the report at quarter to two, standing, the way he stands for things that are finished. The boy at the lodge, the note for the keeping, the seal plain, the clerk's hurried hand. "Refused him, Miss Hartwell. He went back down the drive." In the agents' lodgings, he adds, the lamps are going out, one by one: the working night finished, the plan set, the hunters' money done buying for tonight.)*
> *(Rose nods. The reload tried the gates and found them held, the way the week found them held, through four lines and a stranger and an offer of £2,000. The report, made. The night, guarded.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night's last dressing — the wrapper, at two; the dried violet; the woman, weighed.
scenes.prose:
> *(At two she looks once more at the night's face in the glass, and the glass gives it back plainly: the wrapper, the plait, the dried violet at her wrist, the woman who weighed a hand at midnight and answered it at half past one. The mended gloves lie on the dressing table, the mend at the thumb catching the candlelight. She sets the dried violet on the sill, faithfulness, keeping its color in the dark, and turns down the lamp.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the face the town will read on Monday is weighed and ready. If she chose bury: the face that keeps the secret is weighed and ready. If she chose atone: the face that will pay for ten years is weighed and ready. Whatever the door, the dressing is done: exact, deliberate, her own. The lamp, turned down. The weighing, kept.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the night, faced; the glass, armor.

fashionChoices.detail: the dried violet, bright; the hour, held.

fashionChoices.detail: the small hours judge the weighing.

scenes.synopsis: the aunt, at quarter to two — the candle, out; the drawer, one last time; the crack, at its widest, unconfessed.
scenes.prose:
> *(She passes Letitia's door at quarter to two, and the candle is out. Then, in the dark, the smallest sounds: the drawer opened, the folded letter taken out, the folded letter held a moment, the folded letter put back. A breath. Then, so quiet it is almost not a voice: "Rose—" The name hangs in the dark hall. Nothing follows it. The drawer closes, softly this time, the way a woman closes something she has decided to carry a while longer.)*
> *(Rose stands with her hand half-raised to the door, and does not knock. The confession, whatever it is, is not tonight's, the shape she knew pressing at the silence, and the silence holding. Not yet. She goes on to her room. The aunt, awake. The crack, at its widest, unconfessed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the weighing, closed — the three part for the night; the hand, weighed and unnamed.
scenes.prose:
> *(At two the three of them part in the morning room, and the parting is the weighing's last rite. Octavia takes the memorandum book under her arm, the third arithmetic entered, the sums loved and left. Henry takes the study's lamp down, the draft folded, the bag packed, the morning's ride readied. Rose takes the seal from the purse shelf and sets it back, the wax uncut, the letter written or held or refused, as she chose.)*
> *(They do not say goodnight the way people say goodnight. Octavia nods once, the way she nods at sums that balance. Henry bows, the way he bows to things that aren't finished. Rose watches them go, and the house takes them up, lamp by lamp, into the dark. The signature unknown. The contents unknown. The intent priced. The night, weighed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the cliffhanger — two o'clock; the lodgings' lamps, going out; the plan, set.
scenes.prose: > *(Two o'clock. In the agents' lodgings, the rooms the village pretends not to know, the three lamps go out one by one, the working night finished, the plan set, the reload's money done buying for tonight. The dark takes the street back. And in the last light before the lamps go, a shape at the window, watching the house: the reload, finished, and already looking at morning.)*

scenes.synopsis: two o'clock, held — the night's labor at its fourth hour; the choosing, worked.
scenes.prose:
> *(Two o'clock, and the house holds it the way it held midnight: without announcement. The landings' lamps burn at their lowest. The morning room's fire is banked to embers. She stands at the hall window and reads the dark the way she read it at ten, at twelve, at one: the drive empty, the lodgings dark since two, the village shut. The night's labor has gone into its fourth hour.)*
> *(If she chose bury: the wall's second course stands complete in the dark, and the third course waits for seven, the mason's order out, the men's breakfast readied. If she chose expose: the road to town lies dark, and the boy is still out, the sealed account riding somewhere between the Park and the proprietor's desk, whole and untrimmed, in her own hand. If she chose atone: the deed waits fair-copied, the trust's first notices addressed in the clerk's best hand, and the seal's wax waits by the candle for the morning's first letter. Three labors, one small hour. She stands at the window a moment longer, listening. The house sounds ready.)*

scenes.synopsis: the change, at two — the lantern, passed; the night, guarded by different hands.
scenes.prose:
> *(At two the watch changes, the way it has changed all week: quietly, and on the hour. The second man brings the lantern up the drive for the last round of his watch, and at the lodge the relief takes it, the same man who walked Harrow's guard's round at one, come up in his turn. The light passes hand to hand. Nothing else moves. The drive stays empty, the village stays dark, and the night goes on being guarded, only by different hands.)*
> *(Rose watches from the hall window till the first round is walked. Whatever the door, the account riding, the wall rising, the trust paying, the changing is the same: the house does not leave its dark unwatched for a minute. The lantern, swinging. The drive, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the vigil's fourth dressing — the wrapper, at two; the night, unpinned and unafraid.
scenes.prose:
> *(At two the vigil gets its fourth dressing, and the fourth is the plainest yet: the wrapper, kept on, the dove grey silk gone soft at the elbows from a week of nights, the white stitching, the night's own color. The plait is down and loose. The dried violet is at her wrist, faithfulness, the one ornament the small hours permit. The mended gloves lie on the dressing table, the mend at the thumb catching the candlelight.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the grey will be read on Monday, and the dressing reads steady. If she chose bury: the grey keeps the secret, and the dressing keeps it. If she chose atone: the grey will attend ten years, and the dressing will last. Whatever the door, the glass shows the same woman: the mistress, at two, dressed for the groundwork. The wrapper, worn. The hour, met.)*

fashionChoices.label: Rose, loosed
fashionChoices.detail: the plait, down; the hour, allowed.

fashionChoices.label: The lamp's eye
fashionChoices.detail: the light judges the vigil.

scenes.synopsis: the aunt, past two — the mending basket, out; the speaking, nearly.
scenes.prose:
> *(She finds Letitia in the morning room past two, and the mending basket is out. The quartermaster's blacks are hung for the night, and Letitia wears the wrapper, the grey wool, the hair in its night plait, and a pair of the household's gloves in her lap, the thumb gone at the seam. She sews the way she does everything: exactly, and too fast. "The mason's men," she says without looking up. "Seven. The kitchen door. I told the cook.")*
> *(Rose sits. The needle goes in and out. Then Letitia says, "Rose, I—" and stops. The needle stops with her. A moment. Then: "Never mind. The thread's too short. I meant to say the thread's too short." She rethreads the needle, and the rethreading is very deliberate, and the sentence is gone. The mending, going on. The speaking, not.)*

scenes.synopsis: the gloves — the household's mends; the penance, stitched.
scenes.prose:
> *(The gloves in Letitia's lap are the household's, not the mended pair from the drawer: the kitchen maid's, the thumb gone; the stable boy's, the cuff frayed. She does them one after another, the needle flashing in the lamplight, and each mend is the same small mercy: the seam closed, the thread knotted, the glove laid aside. Forty pairs she mended in the spring, and the forty-first was Harrow's spare. These are the forty-second and third, and she sews them like penance.)*
> *(Rose watches the mends accumulate. Whatever the door, the account riding, the wall rising, the trust paying, the mending is the same: the aunt's hands doing what the aunt's hands have always done, making the household whole one seam at a time, while the thing she cannot mend sits in the drawer upstairs. The needle, flashing. The gloves, whole.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dark, at two — the reload's lamps, out; the plan, waiting.
scenes.prose:
> *(Past two the lodgings are dark, the first dark they have shown all week. The three lamps are out. The street is empty. Somewhere behind the shutters Slade sleeps, or doesn't. The plan was set at half past one, the money counted like ammunition, his second man's instructions in his head and on no paper. The reload has done its buying for tonight. What it bought, only morning will show.)*
> *(If she chose expose: what it bought is the gutter's Monday special, set before the truth. If she chose bury: the search's first prices, the stones, the letters, the memory. If she chose atone: the smear's first line, the paying dressed as buying. Whatever the door, the dark is the same: the plan, waiting. Rose stands at the hall window and regards it the way one regards weather. It will come, and the house will meet it, and there is nothing at two o'clock but to note the sky. The lodgings, dark. The plan, waiting.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE SMALL HOURS: what the house does with the dark it has left.
scenes.prose:
> *(Past two, and the house is at the small hours' question: what does a house do with the dark it has left? The watch is changed, the relief on the drive. The mending goes on in the morning room. The gown waits to be laid. Three answers offer themselves. Keep the watch doubled: every lamp lit, the relief and the second man both walking, Harrow's guard tripled, the house armed to the teeth till dawn, resolve to the night, because the reload is only sleeping and a house that has held all week holds to the end. Let the house sleep: the labor is done, the night's orders are set, the household has earned its rest, mercy to the house, because the groundwork is laid and the dawn will ask enough. Brief the household: wake the keys at three with Monday's orders plain, the mason's men, the post, the kitchen door, candor to the house, because a household that knows its morning meets it standing.)*
> *(She stands in the hall with the house asleep around her and the dark holding outside it, and thinks: the choosing was the door, the weighing was the night, the eve is the groundwork. This is the small hours, answered.)*
> *(She chose for the small hours the way she had chosen for the night: deliberately, and once. Whatever it was, the doubling, the sleeping, the briefing, the house took it up the way it takes up everything, as an order, or a mercy, or a warning, and the eve went on. The small hours, answered.)*

options.label: Keep the watch doubled
options.detail: *Resolve+; the house, armed.* Every lamp lit; both men walking; the guard tripled. *(The reload sleeps; the house, wakeful.)*

options.label: Let the house sleep
options.detail: *Mercy+; the rest, given.* The labor done; the orders set; the dawn, enough. *(The groundwork, laid; the night, released.)*

options.label: Brief the household
options.detail: *Candor+; the morning, named.* Wake the keys at three; Monday's orders, plain. *(A household that knows, standing.)*

scenes.synopsis: the bag, at half past two — the trace, packed; the name, Monday's.
scenes.prose:
> *(In the study at half past two Henry's bag stands packed by the door, the way it has stood since one: the factor's direction copied fair in the breast pocket, the draft folded away in the evidence drawer, the three hands on its back initials and flourishes, no names, the last endorsement Friday's. The books open at nine. The coach goes in the morning. The name is still Monday's, not tonight's.)*
> *(Rose stands in the doorway and does not wake him. He sleeps in the chair, the brother undressed by halves, the cravat still tied. If she chose expose: the morning will name whose money bought the gutter's ink. If she chose bury: the morning will name whose money buys the search. If she chose atone: the morning will name whose money buys the smear. Whatever the door, the sleeping is the same: the trace, at rest before its hardest working day. The bag, packed. The brother, half-undressed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the friend, at half past two — the book, closed; the sums, loved and left.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia is in her room at half past two, and the memorandum book is closed on the night table, the third arithmetic entered, the pencil laid across it like a seal. She is not asleep. She sits by the window with the shawl pulled close, looking at the dark where the lodgings were lit, and when Rose looks in she says, "The sums are done being counted," the way she said it at midnight. "The rest of the eve is for the groundwork, and the groundwork is not arithmetic.")*
> *(Rose leans in the doorway. "Sleep, Octavia." "In a minute," Octavia says, and does not move, and the two of them smile at the echo of it: Letitia's line, borrowed. Whatever the door, the account riding, the wall rising, the trust paying, the friend is the same: the courage to name the cost, and the grace to sit with the dark. The book, closed. The friend, awake.)*

scenes.synopsis: the garden, at quarter to three — the past, quiet; the wall, per door.
scenes.prose:
> *(From the bedroom window the walled garden lies at quarter to three, and the past lies quiet in it still. If she chose bury: the second course stands complete in the dark, the gap less of a wound, stone on stone, and the third course waits for seven. If she chose expose or atone: the gap stands open to the night, the wall down where the papers came out, and the dark sits in it the way it has sat since Sunday.)*
> *(Rosemary grows black against the wall, remembrance, and the garden is empty of the heir. Laurent's walking is done for the night. The path is his no longer, or his again at dawn. She watches it a moment. The garden is older than the hunters and older than the sin, and it will be here when both are gone. The garden, at quarter to three. The past, quiet.)*

scenes.synopsis: the mender, at half past two — the wrapper; the spectacles; the woman, showing.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia at half past two is the mender, and the mending has its own dress: the wrapper, the grey wool, the night plait, a pair of spectacles she does not wear by day perched on her nose, the gloves in her lap. The quartermaster's blacks hang in the wardrobe behind her, the bombazine, the collar's lace, the cuffs fastened, the brooch straight, the uniform waiting for morning, and the woman out of it for the night's small remainder.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the town will read the shape she kept silent, and the stitches go in against the reading. If she chose bury: the silence is kept, and the stitches go in against the keeping. If she chose atone: the shape is paid for, and the stitches go in against the price. Whatever the door, the dressing is the same: the aunt, at half past two, mending what can be mended. The spectacles, perched. The aunt, showing.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the blacks, waiting; the morning, faced.

fashionChoices.label: Letitia, mending
fashionChoices.detail: the gloves, in hand; the night, sewn.

fashionChoices.detail: the niece judges the mender.

scenes.synopsis: the hall, turning — Alice; Monday's page, begun; the orders, written.
scenes.prose:
> *(Below stairs the night has turned its face toward morning. Alice is up before the range with the night's loaves cooling on the rack and the morning's bread already set, and the household book lies open on the dresser with Monday's page begun: the mason's men at seven, the kitchen door, the men's breakfast; the post bag to be tied; the morning room's fire to be laid. The second sitting's voices are long gone. The hall is dark except the banked range, and the orders are written in Letitia's hand from an hour ago, steady then.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the hall will wake to the town reading, and the breakfast is ordered large, the way it is ordered for days that take strength. If she chose bury: the hall will wake to the wall's third course, and the mason's men get the kitchen door and hot breakfast. If she chose atone: the hall will wake to the trust's first letters, and the clerk gets the study's fire and strong tea. Whatever the door, the book is the same: Monday, begun in ink. The orders, written.)*

scenes.synopsis: the working mouth — the latch, oiled; the mason's breakfast, ordered; the course, per door.
scenes.prose:
> *(At three the kitchen door stands ready the way it stands for every working morning: the latch oiled, the step swept, the men's breakfast ordered, bread, cheese, small beer, the way the mason's men take it. If she chose bury: the third course goes up at seven, stone on stone, and the men will want the door at half past six, the mortar mixed, the stones sorted, the mason's order out, the course promised to the dark.)*
> *(Rose checks the latch herself, the way she checked it at the choosing's hour. Whatever the door, the account riding, the trust paying, the kitchen door is the same: the house's working mouth, open to the morning's labor. If the wall rises, it rises through this door. If the letters go, they go past it. The latch, oiled. The door, ready.)*

scenes.synopsis: the witness, at three — the lamp, the guard; the keeping, unbroken.
scenes.prose:
> *(She walks as far as the garden gate at three and looks down the path, the way she has looked all week. Harrow's lamp still burns, the schoolmaster awake, or reading, or sitting with the papers that are his half of the sin, or, on the bury door, with the memory that is all that is left of them. The guard's fire is lit in the lean-to, the relief walking his round. The note was refused at quarter to two. Nothing has tried the keeping since.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the town will call him the accomplice for a week, and the guard is the house's answer. If she chose bury: the quiet is kept, and the guard is the quiet's price. If she chose atone: the £150 order, three years' wages, is written, his deed fair-copied, and the guard is the deed's honor. Whatever the door, the light is the same: the witness, kept. She turns back. The path, dark. The keeping, lit.)*

scenes.synopsis: the schoolmaster, at three — the dressing gown; the scar, lit; the witness, awake.
scenes.prose:
> *(Harrow at three wears the keeping's own undress: the dressing gown, twenty years old, the cuffs mended, the slippers worn thin, the lamp's light on the scar. Sixty-one, and the scar shows in lamplight the way it does not by day, the receipt of the fall. The keeping is spare and ordered: the books, the cloth-covered box, the kettle on the hob. He reads, or sits, the schoolmaster awake in the small hours with the half of the sin that is his, or, on the bury door, the memory of it.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the week will name him, and the gown is worn against the naming. If she chose bury: the quiet is kept, and the gown is worn against the keeping. If she chose atone: the deed is his, and the gown is worn against the owning, sixty-one and learning to be kept by a house. Whatever the door, the dressing is the same: the witness, at three, awake. The lamp, lit. The schoolmaster, kept.)*

fashionChoices.label: Harrow, steady
fashionChoices.detail: the gown, worn; the night, borne.

fashionChoices.label: Harrow, wakeful
fashionChoices.detail: the book, open; the hour, read.

fashionChoices.label: Rose's eye
fashionChoices.detail: the mistress judges the witness.

scenes.synopsis: the laying out — the claret archive silk; Monday, dressed before Monday.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise is in the dressing room at three, and the Monday gown is out. The archive silk, deep claret, twenty-five years old and re-cut twice, lies across the chaise, the skirt's embroidery a shade darker than the stuff, catching the candlelight. She brushes it with the soft brush, long strokes, the way she brushes everything the archive gives up. "Old silk takes the brush well," she says, "when it's been kept. Your grandmother kept everything.")*
> *(The mended gloves lie beside it. The grandmother's pearls are coiled in their case. Rose stands in the doorway in the wrapper and looks at Monday, laid out. "There," Élise says, stepping back. "The archive's answer." The gown, laid. The morning, dressed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the re-cut — the stitch-holes; the silk, holding.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose runs a hand along the gown's side seam, and the re-cutting shows under her fingers: the old stitch-holes, the let-out waist, the second taking-in, the silk altered twice and holding. Twenty-five years old, and it takes the brush, takes the candlelight, takes her. "The embroidery's a shade darker than the stuff," Élise says. "She chose it so. She said claret should argue with itself.")*
> *(Rose laughs, the first laugh of the small hours. The silk is warm from the brushing. The gown has waited twenty-five years in the archive for a Monday, and Monday is coming. The seam, felt. The silk, holding.)*

scenes.synopsis: the heir, elsewhere — the garden, empty; the card, unwritten.
scenes.prose:
> *(At three the garden is empty of him. The path where he walked a dozen times at half past twelve holds only his absence, and the gap where the papers came out stands open to the night, or closed by the second course, per the door. His window is dark. The card he may write in the morning's post is not written. Tonight he is not deciding, only sleeping, or lying awake the way the house is awake.)*
> *(If she chose expose: his mother's name will be in Monday's Gazette, told true. If she chose bury: his mother's name stays out of the papers, and the keeping has its price. If she chose atone: the twelve hundred is debt, named and paying, and he is learning to be a creditor. Whatever the door, the dark window is the same: the heir, spare. She does not knock. The garden, empty. The heir, elsewhere.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE AUNT'S MENDING: what Rose does with Letitia's widening crack at three.
scenes.prose:
> *(Past three, and Letitia's mending goes on, and the crack goes on with it. She has nearly spoken once, "Rose, I—" and the thread's too short, and the shape she knew presses at the silence the way the needle presses at the seam. Three answers offer themselves. Sit and hear her: take the chair beside her, say the sentence for her, and hear whatever comes, candor to the woman who kept the house, because the crack is at its widest and a crack met is a crack mended. Send her to bed: the night holds it, the confession keeps till its own hour, mercy to the aunt, because the mending is penance enough and the small hours are no hour for twenty years. Set her to the orders: Monday's page, the quartermaster's duty, the household needing its head, resolve to the house, because Letitia has never once failed an order and the work will hold her till the hour comes.)*
> *(She stands in the morning room's doorway with the mending basket between them and the candle burning low, and thinks: the choosing was the door, the small hours were the groundwork, the aunt is the family. This is the mending, met or left.)*
> *(She chose for the aunt's mending the way she had chosen for the small hours: deliberately, and with love in hand. Whatever it was, the hearing, the bed, the orders, Letitia would receive it the way she receives everything, as a question, or a mercy, or an order, and answer in kind. The mending, answered.)*

options.label: Sit and hear her
options.detail: *Candor+; the question, asked.* Take the chair; say the sentence; hear it. *(The crack, met before it breaks.)*

options.label: Send her to bed
options.detail: *Mercy+; the rest, given.* The night holds it; the hour, hers. *(The small hours, no hour for twenty years.)*

options.label: Set her to the orders
options.detail: *Resolve+; the quartermaster, kept.* Monday's page; duty as the splint. *(She has never failed an order.)*

scenes.synopsis: the plan, sleeping — the reload, like weather; the money, moving.
scenes.prose:
> *(At three in London Slade sleeps the sleep of a man whose orders are in other men's heads: his second man's instructions, the boy's packet money spent, the lodgings' rent a month in advance, the purse lighter by the night's spending and the morning's prices already set. The plan is the reload's weather now. It will come, and the house will meet it, and there is nothing at three o'clock but to note the sky.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the weather is the gutter's Monday special, the lie set before the truth, the compositor's overtime bought. If she chose bury: the weather is the search, the stones, the letters, the memory, priced by the day. If she chose atone: the weather is the smear, the forty-one thousand six hundred dressed as hush money, the ledger dirtied in print. In every door the sleeping is the same: the purchase failed, the purchaser is buying again, and the principal's patience is spent. The plan, set. The money, moving.)*

scenes.synopsis: the village, asleep — the quiet, deepest; the counsel, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(At three the village sleeps the sleep of a place that has decided to sleep through something. The Crown's windows are shuttered. Mrs. Pike's blind is down, the headache she never had unmentioned again. The blacksmith's forge is cold. The lodgings are dark. And the not-talking has settled into its deepest shape: the village keeps its counsel the way it keeps its churchyard, completely, and without being asked.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the village will wake to the Gazette's Monday truth, and the talk will start again. If she chose bury: the village will wake to the wall's third course, and the talk will stay buried with the stones. If she chose atone: the village will wake to the trust's first letters, and the talk will be of paying. Whatever the door, the sleeping is the same: the quiet, kept. The village, dark. The counsel, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the drawer, shut — the week's paper, filed; the truth, kept for morning.
scenes.prose:
> *(In the study at three the evidence drawer is shut, and the week's paper lies inside it in order: Slade's first letter, the two thousand, offered Thursday, refused in writing by nightfall; the refusal, in Rose's hand; the draft from the factor on top, its back read twice, its last coat hanging in a counting-house that opens at nine.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the drawer holds the account's fair copy, delivered, the boy's errand done or doing. If she chose bury: the drawer holds the ash's record, the burning witnessed, the wall's order. If she chose atone: the drawer holds the trust's founding, sealed, the eighty-eight hundred moved, the first payment entered. Whatever the door, the drawer is the same: the week's truth, filed. The evidence, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the modiste's night — the black silk; the lilies, cut for Monday.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise at three wears the night's own working dress: the modiste's black silk, twenty years old and cut like a uniform, the white apron, the sleeves turned back for the brushing. The basket stands by the chaise, dried violets and rosemary, faithfulness and remembrance, and a new posy for the morning: white lilies, purity of intent, cut at dusk from the garden's own bed. "For Monday," she says. "Whatever Monday is, it should have lilies.")*
> *(If she chose expose: the lilies are for the house that will be read, dressed steady. If she chose bury: the lilies are for the house that keeps its secret, dressed quiet. If she chose atone: the lilies are for the house that pays, dressed to last. Whatever the door, the modiste is the same: warm, exact, unbuyable. The posy, cut. The morning, flowered.)*

fashionChoices.label: Élise, composed
fashionChoices.detail: the black silk; the night, managed.

fashionChoices.label: Élise, conspiratorial
fashionChoices.detail: the basket, set down; the news, shared.

fashionChoices.label: Rose's eye
fashionChoices.detail: the mistress judges the modiste.

scenes.synopsis: the morning's posy — dried violets, rosemary, lilies; the house's language.
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning's flowers stand in the dressing room: the dried violets, faithfulness, the season's flower, laid beside the water; the rosemary, remembrance, cut long, and the white lilies, purity of intent, for whatever Monday is, standing in their water. Élise arranges them the way she arranges everything: exactly, and as if the arrangement were a sentence. "Dried violets for the wrist," she says. "Rosemary for the garden. Lilies for the morning room, where the town will look first.")*
> *(Rose touches a lily's petal. Purity of intent: the flower the season has been waiting to earn. If she chose expose: the intent is the telling, whole and true. If she chose bury: the intent is the keeping, witnessed and borne. If she chose atone: the intent is the paying, ten years, named. Whatever the door, the flowers are the same: the language the house speaks when it has no words left. The posy, set. The morning, flowered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the eve, totalled — half past three; the choosing, carried by other hands.
scenes.prose:
> *(Half past three, and she totals the eve the way she totals everything: in columns that almost balance. The watch changed. The mending going. The gown laid. The drawer shut. The lodgings dark. The garden quiet. The choosing, carried into its fourth hour by other hands, and her hands, for once, empty.)*
> *(If she chose expose: her hands are empty because the account is the town's now, riding or arrived. If she chose bury: her hands are empty because the papers are ash and the wall is the mason's. If she chose atone: her hands are empty because the trust is the clerk's and the paying is the fortune's. Whatever the door, the emptiness is the same: the choosing, done, and the doing belonging to the morning. She stands at the window with empty hands. The eve, nearly spent.)*

scenes.synopsis: the garden, at half past three — the dark, thinning; the breath, held.
scenes.prose:
> *(From the hall window the walled garden lies at half past three, and the dark in it is thinning at the edges, the way dark thins before it thinks about light. If she chose bury: the second course stands in the first grey, stone on stone, and the third course waits for seven, promised. If she chose expose or atone: the gap stands open, and the grey finds it first, the wall down where the papers came out, the dark sitting in it patiently.)*
> *(The rosemary is black against the wall still, remembrance, and will be green by morning. The garden does not hurry. It has been here since before the sin and will be here after the paying, and the eve is a small thing to it, a held breath between days. She watches till the grey steadies. The garden, at half past three. The breath, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE DAWN: how she crosses into Monday.
scenes.prose:
> *(Half past three, and the dark is thinning, and one question remains for the eve: how does she cross into Monday? The choosing was Sunday's. The weighing was the night's. The groundwork is the eve's. Three answers offer themselves. Hold the door: keep the choosing's labor the house's own till morning, the wall, the deed, the account unspoken to the town, resolve to the choosing, because Monday will ask its questions soon enough and the eve owes it nothing early. Let it come: no rehearsal, no dread, the dawn arriving and she meeting it as it arrives, mercy to herself, because the night has been weighed and the morning can carry its own weight. Name it: say aloud, alone, what she did on Sunday, the choosing named, the door owned, the cost stated plainly to the empty room, candor to herself, because a woman who cannot name it to the dark cannot hold it in the daylight.)*
> *(She stands at the hall window with the grey coming up over the garden wall, and thinks: the choosing was the door, the small hours were the groundwork, the dawn is the crossing. This is Monday, met at its edge.)*
> *(She decided for the dawn the way she had decided for the night: deliberately, and once. Whatever it was, the holding, the letting, the naming, the small hours took it up without a murmur, and the grey went on coming up over the wall. The dawn, decided.)*

options.label: Hold the door
options.detail: *Resolve+; the choosing, kept.* The labor, the house's own; Monday, unowed. *(The dawn, unrehearsed by the night.)*

options.label: Let it come
options.detail: *Mercy+; the morning, unmet halfway.* No dread; the dawn, arriving. *(The night, weighed; the morning, its own.)*

options.label: Name it
options.detail: *Candor+; the choosing, spoken.* Aloud, alone; the cost, stated. *(Named to the dark; held in the daylight.)*

scenes.synopsis: the aunt, at half past three — the sentence, begun; the breaking, timed.
scenes.prose:
> *(She goes back to the morning room at half past three, and the mending is nearly done: the last glove in Letitia's lap, the needle going slower now, the basket empty beside her. Letitia looks up, and the look is the crack at its widest yet, the shape she knew, twenty years, pressing at the silence that kept the family's peace. "Rose," she says. "I kept it. All of it. I—")*
> *(The shutter bangs below stairs, the kitchen's, loose in the first wind of morning, and the sound breaks the sentence like a thread snapping. Letitia looks down. "The gown," she says, too quickly. "Élise has the hem. Tell her the hem wants another quarter inch." The needle goes in. The sentence is gone. The crack, at its widest, unconfessed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the last stitch — the basket, empty; the drawer, shut; the aunt, held.
scenes.prose:
> *(The last stitch goes in at quarter to four. Letitia knots the thread, bites it off, the quartermaster's habit, twenty years unbroken, and lays the glove with the others: the household's gloves, whole, the seams closed. The basket is empty. The morning room is quiet. She sits a moment with her hands in her lap, looking at nothing, and then she opens the drawer, looks at the folded letter with its three lines crossed out, and closes the drawer.)*
> *(Rose, from the door, says nothing. The letter stays. The confession stays. Whatever the door, the account riding, the wall rising, the trust paying, the aunt's night ends the same: the mending done, the silence kept, the crack carried upstairs like the basket. Letitia rises, and goes up. The candle, out. The aunt, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Eve's Dressing ritual — the house dresses Monday before Monday wakes; the chapter's ritual.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: the laying — per door. Expose: the account delivered, the Gazette's Monday truth set in type before dawn. Bury: the wall's second course standing, the third course promised to seven. Atone: the deed fair-copied, the trust's first notices addressed. Whatever the door, the laying's face is the same: the groundwork, done; the morning, readied.)*
> *(Story morsel: the confirming — the orders for Monday, entered in the household book. The mason's men at seven, the kitchen door. The post bag tied. Bell at nine. Whatever the door, the confirming's face is the same: Monday, begun in ink.)*
> *(Story morsel: the keeping — the house settling around the eve, against the reload. The watch on the drive; Harrow's guard doubled; the lodgings dark; the drawer shut. The small hours hold them all, and ask nothing.)*
> *(Story morsel: the eve's last hour — per door. Expose: the road to town dark, the boy's errand done or doing, the Gazette's press at work. Bury: the wall's second course standing, the search's money moving in London. Atone: the deed fair-copied, the smear's first line being written. Three labors, one reload, one eve.)*
> *(Story morsel: four o'clock's approach — the kitchen fire lit, the post bag tied, the claret waiting. The house nearly awake. The eve done. Four o'clock waits past the dark, punctual as ever.)*

ritual.occasionBrief: Two o'clock has struck and the house is at its groundwork: the claret gown laid for morning, the kitchen door ordered for the mason's men, the trust's notices addressed, the Gazette's printing awaited. The night staff and the small hours dress Monday before Monday wakes. Walk the eve in the ritual's order — the laying, the confirming, the keeping. Exact. Quiet. Deliberate. The house that chose does not meet the dawn undressed.

scenes.synopsis: the friend, before four — the precision, at rest; the eve, claimed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia before four is the precision at rest, and the rest is the point: the shawl pulled close, the memorandum book closed on the night table, the pencil laid across it. She has given up the window and taken the chair by the morning room's banked fire, and she looks, for the first time all week, like a woman who has finished something. "The eve," she says, "is the only part of the week that belongs to the house. Monday belongs to everyone.")*
> *(If she chose expose: the house's eve ends with the town's reading coming. If she chose bury: the house's eve ends with the wall's third course coming. If she chose atone: the house's eve ends with the trust's first letters going. Whatever the door, the friend is the same: the courage to name the cost, and the grace to sit by a banked fire. The shawl, close. The friend, unpinned.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the book, closed; the eve, exact.

fashionChoices.label: Octavia, softened
fashionChoices.detail: the shawl, close; the fire, banked.

fashionChoices.label: Rose's eye
fashionChoices.detail: the mistress judges the friend.

scenes.synopsis: the yard, per door — the stones, waiting; the course, or not.
scenes.prose:
> *(At quarter to four the mason's yard keeps its own counsel, an hour before its hour. If she chose bury: a lantern moves among the stones, the day's courses being sorted by feel in the dark, the mortar's sand heaped, the trowels lined on the bench, the yard loading for the third course — the stones counted, the mason's order out, the wall's promise kept to the dark. If she chose expose or atone: the yard sleeps, the wall down where the papers came out, the stones waiting for whatever Monday decides they are.)*
> *(Rose watches from the garden door. Whatever the door, the account riding, the trust paying, the yard is the same: the Park's own labor, older than the week, its stones sorted and waiting on Monday.)*

scenes.synopsis: the bag, tied — Monday's words, ready before Monday's mouth.
scenes.prose:
> *(At quarter to four the post bag waits by the hall door, tied and addressed, the night's last piece of groundwork. The London letters. The county letters. If she chose atone: the trust's first notices, addressed in the clerk's best hand, the seal's wax on the founders' copies, the paying begun on paper. If she chose expose: the road to town holds only its dark now, the sealed account the town's, the boy's errand done or doing. If she chose bury: the bag holds nothing of the week's truth, and that is the truth it holds.)*
> *(Rose touches the bag's string. Whatever the door, the bag is the same: Monday's words, ready before Monday's mouth is open. The string, tied. The post, prepared.)*

scenes.synopsis: the drive, at quarter to four — the lantern; the empty road; the night, guarded.
scenes.prose:
> *(At quarter to four the relief walks the drive with the lantern, and the drive is empty all the way to the village. Nothing has come up it all night but the mason's cart. Nothing will till morning: the mason's men at seven, the post's cart, the coach, whichever Monday brings. He walks it steady, unhurried, and the lantern swings its small circle of Hartwell light down the drive and back.)*
> *(Rose watches from the hall window. Whatever the door, the account riding, the wall rising, the trust paying, the watch is the same: the night guarded into its last quarter-hour, the house asleep behind it. The lantern, swinging. The drive, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Monday, spending before the house has woken; the dark, thinning.
scenes.prose: > *(The sting comes at quarter to four, and it is the morning's first purchase. If she chose expose: the London road carries its first cart, and behind it the Gazette's Monday paper is already in type, the account set before dawn, the truth on the press before the lie can buy its ink. If she chose bury: the mason's yard has its lantern lit an hour early, the third course's stones being sorted by feel in the dark. If she chose atone: the post-horse is being saddled in the dark yard, the trust's first notices addressed and waiting for the bag. Whatever the door, the sting is the same: Monday has started spending before the house has woken. The dark, thinning. The morning, buying.)*
scenes.sting: the sting — Monday, spending before the house has woken; the dark, thinning.

scenes.synopsis: the claret, at four — the gown, seen; the woman, nearly.
scenes.prose:
> *(At four she stands before the claret in the dressing room, and the gown gives it back plainly: the deep claret archive silk, twenty-five years old, re-cut twice, the embroidery a shade darker than the stuff. In the wrapper she is the night's woman. The gown on the chaise is Monday's. The mended gloves lie beside it, the mend at the thumb catching the candlelight. The grandmother's pearls are coiled in their case. She does not put it on yet. The eve is not done.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the claret will be read by a town that knows. If she chose bury: the claret will keep what the town doesn't. If she chose atone: the claret will attend ten years of paying. Whatever the door, the gown is the same: the archive's answer, laid out. The silk, waiting. The woman, nearly.)*

fashionChoices.label: Rose, armored
fashionChoices.detail: the claret, faced; the morning, met.

fashionChoices.label: Rose, unhurried
fashionChoices.detail: the silk, warm; the hour, held.

fashionChoices.label: The candle's eye
fashionChoices.detail: the small hours judge the gown.

scenes.synopsis: the aunt, at four — the blacks, restored; the speaking, not; the sleep, allowed.
scenes.prose:
> *(At four Letitia is abed at last, and the quartermaster's blacks hang in the wardrobe, the bombazine, the collar's lace done up again, the cuffs fastened, the brooch straight, the uniform waiting for morning, and the woman in it for what remains of the night. The mending basket stands empty by the chair. The drawer is shut, the folded letter inside it, the three lines crossed out. The candle is out.)*
> *(Rose passes the door and does not knock. The crack is at its widest, and the silence is holding it. Whatever the door, the account riding, the wall rising, the trust paying, the aunt's night ends the same: the mending done, the speaking not, the confession keeping till its own hour. The door, unknocked. The aunt, asleep.)*

scenes.synopsis: four o'clock — the reload, like weather; the eve, spent.
scenes.prose:
> *(Four o'clock, and the house is at the eve's edge. The kitchen's shutter bangs once in the first wind and is still. The landings' lamps are out. The morning room's fire is banked to grey. She stands at the hall window and regards the reload the way one regards weather: the lodgings dark since two, the plan set at half past one, the money moving somewhere she cannot see, the morning's first purchase already made. It will come. The house will meet it. There is nothing at four o'clock but to note the sky.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the sky holds the Gazette's Monday truth, set in type. If she chose bury: the sky holds the wall's third course, promised to seven. If she chose atone: the sky holds the trust's first letters, addressed. Whatever the door, the regarding is the same: the choosing, done; the doing, the morning's. She turns from the window. The eve, spent.)*

scenes.synopsis: the waking — the kitchen fire, lit; the groundwork, finished.
scenes.prose:
> *(Before dawn the house wakes the way it always wakes: from below. The kitchen fire is lit, the range coming up, Alice at the bread with the morning's batch, the mason's men's breakfast on the board. The morning room's fire is laid. The post bag waits by the hall door. The claret gown waits in the dressing room. The household book lies open on the dresser, Monday's page begun in Letitia's steady hand from an hour ago.)*
> *(Rose stands in the hall and listens to the house come up around her, lamp by lamp, the way she listened to it go down. Whatever the door, the account riding, the wall rising, the trust paying, the waking is the same: the groundwork, done. The eve kept its promise. Monday can come. The fire, lit. The house, awake.)*

scenes.synopsis: the cliffhanger — the lodgings, relit; the reload, awake before the house.
scenes.prose: > *(Four o'clock. The dark thins over the village, and in the agents' lodgings, dark since two, one lamp is lit. The reload, awake before the house. The plan, set at half past one, is already spending: the morning's first purchase, made before the birds. The house wakes at four. The hunters woke first.)*

scenes.synopsis: four o'clock, held — one lamp in the lodgings; the reload, awake before the house.
scenes.prose:
> *(Four o'clock, and the dark over the village has one lamp in it where two o'clock had none. The agents' lodgings, dark since two, show a single lit window: the reload, awake before the house. The plan, set at half past one, is already spending — the morning's first purchase, made before the birds. She stands at the hall window in the wrapper and watches the one lamp the way she has watched the whole night: as weather. It will come. The house will meet it.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the lamp is the gutter's Monday special being set ahead of the truth, the compositor's overtime bought. If she chose bury: the lamp is the search's first prices — the stones, the letters, the memory, priced by the day. If she chose atone: the lamp is the smear's first line, the forty-one thousand six hundred dressed as hush money. Whatever the door, the watching is the same: the one lamp, the dark, the morning priced before it arrives. The lamp, lit. The house, wakeful.)*

scenes.synopsis: the four o'clock round — the night watch's last circuit; the drive, empty.
scenes.prose:
> *(At four the relief walks the drive with the lantern, the last full round of the night's watch. The stones are cold underfoot, and the air has the thin edge it gets before a frost without quite committing to one. He walks it steady, unhurried, and the lantern swings its small circle of Hartwell light down the drive and back. At the lodge Amos has the door ajar and the day's first word ready: all quiet — the keeping, the garden gate, the village road.)*
> *(Rose watches from the hall window till the round is walked. Whatever the door, the account riding, the wall rising, the trust paying, the watch is the same: the night guarded into its last hour, the house asleep behind it, the dark held off hand to hand all week. The lantern, swinging. The drive, empty.)*

scenes.synopsis: the kitchen, waking — Alice at the bread; the range, roaring.
scenes.prose:
> *(Below stairs the kitchen is awake all the way now. Alice has the morning's loaves out on the rack, the crusts singing as they cool, and the mason's men's breakfast on the board — bread, cheese, small beer, the way the mason's men take it. The range roars. The second sitting's crockery is washed and racked. On the dresser the household book lies open, Monday's page begun in Letitia's steady hand from an hour ago: the mason's men at seven, the kitchen door, the post bag tied.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the kitchen will wake to the town reading, and the breakfast is ordered large, the way it is ordered for days that take strength. If she chose bury: the kitchen will wake to the wall's third course, and the men will want the door at half past six. If she chose atone: the kitchen will wake to the trust's first letters, and the clerk gets the study's fire and strong tea. Whatever the door, the waking is the same: the house's working mouth, open. The range, roaring. The bread, cooling.)*

scenes.synopsis: the vigil's fifth dressing — the wrapper, at four; the night, nearly done.
scenes.prose:
> *(The fifth dressing of the vigil is the wrapper again, the dove grey silk gone soft at the elbows from a week of nights, the white stitching, the night's own color. The plait is down and loose. The dried violet is at her wrist, fading now, the small hours' one ornament, faithfulness going pale at the edges. The mended gloves lie on the dressing table, the mend at the thumb catching the candlelight.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the grey will be read by a town that knows, and the dressing reads steady. If she chose bury: the grey keeps the secret, and the dressing keeps it. If she chose atone: the grey will attend ten years, and the dressing will last. Whatever the door, the glass shows the same woman: the mistress, at four, the night nearly done on her face — grey under the eyes, steady in them. The wrapper, worn. The hour, nearly met.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the grey, kept; the night, outlasted.

fashionChoices.label: Rose, steady
fashionChoices.detail: the eyes, clear; the morning, faced.

fashionChoices.label: The glass's eye
fashionChoices.detail: the candlelight judges the vigil.

scenes.synopsis: the witness, at four — the lamp, still burning; the keeping, unbroken.
scenes.prose:
> *(She walks as far as the garden gate at four and looks down the path, the way she has looked all week. Harrow's lamp still burns — the schoolmaster awake, or reading, or sitting with the papers that are his half of the sin, or, on the bury door, with the memory that is all that is left of them. The guard's fire is lit in the lean-to, the relief walking his round. The note was refused at quarter to two. Nothing has tried the keeping since.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the town will call him the accomplice for a week, and the guard is the house's answer. If she chose bury: the quiet is kept, and the guard is the quiet's price. If she chose atone: the £150 order, three years' wages, is written, his deed fair-copied, and the guard is the deed's honor. Whatever the door, the light is the same: the witness, kept. She turns back. The path, dark. The keeping, lit.)*

scenes.synopsis: the garden, at four — the dark, holding; the heir, elsewhere.
scenes.prose:
> *(From the garden gate the walled garden lies at four, and the dark holds in it still. If she chose bury: the second course stands complete in the dark, the gap less of a wound, stone on stone, and the third course waits for seven, promised. If she chose expose or atone: the gap stands open to the night, the wall down where the papers came out, and the dark sits in it the way it has sat since Sunday.)*
> *(Rosemary grows black against the wall, remembrance, and the garden is empty of the heir. His window is dark. The path where he walked at half past twelve holds only his absence. She watches it a moment. The garden is older than the hunters and older than the sin, and it will be here when both are gone. The garden, at four. The past, quiet.)*

scenes.synopsis: the one lamp, watched — the reload, spending; the street, empty.
scenes.prose:
> *(The lodgings keep their one lamp past four, and the street below it is empty all the way to the Crown. Somewhere behind the shutters Slade is awake with the plan, the money counted like ammunition at half past one, his second man's instructions in his head and on no paper. The purchase failed. The purchaser is buying again. The morning's first purchase was made before the birds; the second is being priced now, in lamplight.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the pricing is the gutter's Monday special, the lie set ahead of the truth. If she chose bury: the pricing is the search — the stones, the letters, the memory, priced by the day. If she chose atone: the pricing is the smear, the paying dressed as buying. Whatever the door, the lamplight is the same: the reload, spending; the house, watching. The lamp, lit. The street, empty.)*

scenes.synopsis: the yard, per door — the stones, waiting; the third course, or not.
scenes.prose:
> *(At half past four the mason's yard keeps its own counsel, two and a half hours before its hour. If she chose bury: a lantern moves among the stones, the day's courses being sorted by feel in the dark, the mortar's sand heaped, the trowels lined on the bench, the apprentice at work with his coat buttoned wrong, half asleep and wholly exact, the way the Park's own labor always is. If she chose expose or atone: the yard sleeps, the wall down where the papers came out, the stones waiting for whatever Monday decides they are.)*
> *(If she chose bury: the third course goes up at seven, stone on stone — the stones counted, the mason's order out, the wall's promise kept to the dark. If she chose expose or atone: the wall stays down where the papers came out, and the stones wait. Whatever the door, the labor is the same: the Park's own, older than the sin, its stones sorted and waiting on Monday.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE WAKING: what the house does with its sleeping keys.
scenes.prose:
> *(Half past four, and the question of the waking will not wait. The kitchen is up. The keys are not. Three answers offer themselves. Wake the keys at five: the orders read aloud in the servants' hall, Monday's page, every key at her post before the bell, resolve to the house, because Monday is loaded and the household should carry it standing. Let the bell do it: no hand laid on a sleeping house, the keys waked by the six o'clock bell and not before, mercy to the household, because the night's labor was the staff's too and rest is the only wage the small hours pay. Tell the keys the truth first: the week's shape spoken plain in the servants' hall before the orders are given, candor to the house, because a household that knows what Monday carries meets it with its eyes open.)*
> *(She stands in the hall with the kitchen's noise coming up below and the dark holding outside, and thinks: the choosing was the door, the night was the weighing, the waking is the groundwork's first order. This is the household, answered.)*
> *(She chose for the waking the way she had chosen all week: deliberately, and once. Whatever it was, the rousing, the sparing, the telling, the house took it up the way it takes up everything, as an order, or a mercy, or a warning, and the small hours went on toward the bell. The waking, answered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the bag, away — the early sorting; Monday's words, riding.
scenes.prose:
> *(At five the post bag goes to the stable yard on the boy's shoulder, tied and addressed — the London letters, the county letters, the night's last piece of groundwork sorted and sealed. The string is knotted the way the night porter knots everything: twice, and tight. The post horse stamps in the dark yard. The mail cart goes at six.)*
> *(If she chose atone: the trust's first notices ride among them, addressed in the clerk's best hand, the founders' copies sealed with the wax by the candle, the paying begun on paper. If she chose expose: the bag holds no more of the week's truth — the account went Sunday night in her own hand, and the road to town holds only its dark. If she chose bury: the bag holds nothing of the week's truth, and that is the truth it holds. Whatever the door, the bag is the same: Monday's words, ready before Monday's mouth is open. The string, tied. The post, away.)*

scenes.synopsis: the village, waking — the counsel, kept; the paper, unread.
scenes.prose:
> *(At five the village wakes the way it always wakes: the Crown's boy up with the shutters, Mrs. Pike's blind going up, the blacksmith's forge lit, the first smoke from the chimneys lying flat in the still air. The lodgings' street is empty, the one lamp still burning behind its shutter. The taproom's talk has not begun — Monday's paper is not yet read — and the not-talking holds its deepest shape a while longer.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the village will wake to the Gazette's Monday truth, and the talk will start again by eleven. If she chose bury: the village will wake to the wall's third course, and the talk will stay buried with the stones. If she chose atone: the village will wake to the trust's first letters, and the talk will be of paying. Whatever the door, the waking is the same: the quiet, kept. The village, dark. The counsel, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the kitchen's dress — the apron; the flour; the girl, at work.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alice at five wears the kitchen's own uniform: the plain stuff gown, the apron starched yesterday and softened by the night's baking, the sleeves rolled to the elbow, flour to the wrist and in the hair, the cap pinned straight. She moves between the range and the rack with the loaves, and the night's labor sits on her the way the heat sits in the kitchen: completely, and without complaint. "The men's breakfast is on the board," she says. "The bread's the night's. It kept.")*
> *(If she chose expose: the kitchen will feed a house the town is reading, and the girl feeds it steady. If she chose bury: the kitchen will feed the mason's men at half past six, and the girl feeds them hot. If she chose atone: the kitchen will feed the clerk with his letters, and the girl feeds him strong tea. Whatever the door, the dressing is the same: the kitchen, at five, at work. The apron, softened. The girl, unbowed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the room, laid — Monday's page, carried; the orders, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(At five the breakfast room is laid for the house's waking: the cloth straight, the silver out, the toast rack ready, the chocolate pot coming up. The household book lies open on the dresser, Monday's page in Letitia's steady hand from an hour ago, and the keys take it up the way they take up everything: as the quartermaster's orders, which is what they are. The mason's men at seven. The kitchen door. The post bag tied. The morning room's fire laid.)*
> *(Rose checks the page herself, the way she checked the latch at the choosing's hour. Whatever the door, the account riding, the wall rising, the trust paying, the page is the same: Monday, begun in ink, the groundwork written down. The orders, carried. The room, laid.)*

scenes.synopsis: the friend's arithmetic, at five — the lamp, priced; the spending, watched.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia is up at five with the memorandum book open on the morning room table, the night's sums reviewed, the pencil laid across like a seal. She has given up the window and taken the chair by the banked fire, and she watches the lodgings' one lamp through the glass the way she watches everything: exactly. "One lamp," she says. "He is buying the morning while we are watching him buy it. The watching is over, Rose. The wages are doubled, the packet is sent. No more waiting — she has bought the hands to prove it.")*
> *(If she chose expose: the hands are setting the gutter's Monday special ahead of the truth. If she chose bury: the hands are pricing the search — the stones, the letters, the memory. If she chose atone: the hands are writing the smear, the paying dressed as buying. In every door the column is the same: the purse is fresh, the patience is spent. The book, entered. The intent, priced.)*

scenes.synopsis: the brother, at five — the bag; the draft; the coach, readied.
scenes.prose:
> *(In the study at five Henry's bag stands packed by the door, the way it has stood since one: the factor's direction copied fair in the breast pocket, the draft folded away in the evidence drawer, the three hands on its back initials and flourishes, no names, the last endorsement Friday's. The books open at nine. The coach goes in the morning. He drinks his tea standing, the brother dressed whole again, the cravat tied, the trace at rest no longer.)*
> *(Rose stands in the doorway and does not keep him. If she chose expose: the morning will name whose money bought the gutter's ink. If she chose bury: the morning will name whose money buys the search. If she chose atone: the morning will name whose money buys the smear. Whatever the door, the standing is the same: the trace, dressed and going. The bag, packed. The brother, ready.)*

scenes.synopsis: the gown, brushed — Élise's last pass; the hem, pinned.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise is in the dressing room before five with the soft brush, going over the claret once more, long strokes, the way she brushes everything the archive gives up. The archive silk, deep claret, twenty-five years old and re-cut twice, takes the brush, takes the candlelight, takes the coming grey. Then she kneels at the hem with the pins: another quarter inch, per the midnight instruction, the one Letitia gave instead of the sentence. She pins it exactly.)*
> *(The mended gloves lie beside the gown. The grandmother's pearls are coiled in their case. Rose stands in the doorway in the wrapper and looks at Monday, laid out and brushed and hemmed. "There," Élise says, stepping back. "The archive's answer, answered twice." The gown, kept. The hem, pinned.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE LAMP'S GOING OUT: what Rose does when the witness sleeps.
scenes.prose:
> *(At half past five Harrow's lamp goes out — she watches it happen from the garden gate, the small square of light closing like an eye. Sixty-one years, the week's weight, the keeping. The schoolmaster asleep at last, or sitting in the dark with the half of the sin that is his. Three answers offer themselves. Go down herself: the path in the grey, the door not knocked, the word left with the guard that the keeping holds, candor to the witness, because the keeping has been the week's spine and the spine should hear the morning is coming. Let him sleep: no word, no knock, the guard as ordered and the dawn his own, mercy to the old man, because the night asked enough and the morning will ask its own. Double the keeping: Amos down with the day's orders, Harrow's guard doubled till the post is away and the coach gone, resolve to the witness, because the reload is awake and the sleeping are the ones the morning hunts.)*
> *(She stands at the garden gate with the grey coming up over the wall, and thinks: the choosing was the door, the lamp was the keeping, the witness is the living. This is the small hours' last kindness, or its last order.)*
> *(She chose for the lamp's going out the way she had chosen for everything: deliberately, and once. Whatever it was, the going, the leaving, the doubling, the keeping took it up in its sleep, and the grey went on coming up over the wall. The lamp, answered.)*

options.label: Let him sleep
options.detail: *Mercy+; the rest, given.* No word; the dawn, his own. *(The night asked enough.)*

options.label: Double the keeping
options.detail: *Resolve+; the guard, doubled.* Amos down; the orders, day's. *(The sleeping are the hunted.)*

scenes.synopsis: the day's watch — the lantern, handed on; the drive, grey.
scenes.prose:
> *(At half past five the night watch hands the drive to the day. The relief brings the lantern down to the lodge, and the stable lads take the daylight's rounds, yawning and exact, the way the Park's own always are. At the keeping the morning man relieves the night's guard, the fire in the lean-to banked, the path walked once and found quiet. The drive lies in the first grey, empty all the way to the village.)*
> *(Rose watches the handover from the hall window. Whatever the door, the account riding, the wall rising, the trust paying, the changing is the same: the night does not leave its dark unwatched for a minute, and the day takes it up without a gap. The lantern, handed on. The drive, grey.)*

scenes.synopsis: the witness, sleeping — the keeping, unbroken; the deed, per door.
scenes.prose:
> *(By half past five the keeping is dark and still, and Harrow sleeps at last — the schoolmaster's rest after the week's keeping, sixty-one and the scar's receipt put by for the morning. The guard's fire burns low in the lean-to. The morning man walks his round. The cloth-covered box sits under its cloth. The kettle is cold on the hob. The keeping keeps its witness the way it keeps everything: sparely, and completely.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the town will name him for a week, and the keeping is the house's answer to the naming. If she chose bury: the quiet is kept, his half under its cloth, nothing naming him, the town's talk passing him by. If she chose atone: the £150 order, three years' wages, is written and the keeping deeded to him outright — the first payment, the first keeping, sixty-one and learning to be kept by a house. Whatever the door, the sleeping is the same: the witness, kept. She turns back up the path. The keeping, dark. The keeping, unbroken.)*

scenes.synopsis: the garden, in first grey — the wall, faced; the rosemary, greening.
scenes.prose:
> *(The walled garden at half past five, and the grey finds the wall first. If she chose bury: the second course stands in the grey, stone on stone, the gap less of a wound, and the third course waits for seven, promised. If she chose expose or atone: the gap stands open, and the grey sits in it patiently, the wall down where the papers came out, the dark thinning at its edges.)*
> *(The rosemary shows green at the edges now, remembrance, by morning. The path is empty of the heir. The garden does not hurry. It has been here since before the sin and will be here after the paying, and the small hours are a small thing to it, a held breath between days, nearly let go. She watches till the grey steadies. The garden, in first grey. The breath, nearly loosed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the modiste's morning — the black silk; the posy, for whatever Monday is.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise at half past five wears the morning's own dress: the modiste's black silk, twenty years old and cut like a uniform, the white apron off now and folded over her arm, the sleeves down, the posy basket on her wrist — dried violets and rosemary, faithfulness and remembrance, and the white lilies for the morning room, purity of intent, cut at dusk from the garden's own bed. Her hair is pinned up under the cap, and she looks, for the first time all week, like a woman with nothing left to brush.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the lilies are for the house that will be read, dressed steady. If she chose bury: the lilies are for the house that keeps its secret, dressed quiet. If she chose atone: the lilies are for the house that pays, dressed to last. Whatever the door, the modiste is the same: warm, exact, unbuyable. The posy, cut. The morning, flowered.)*
