scenes.synopsis: dark again — the reload, gone to ground; the morning, loaded.
scenes.prose:
> *(At half past five the lodgings are dark again — the one lamp out, the street empty, the shutters shut. The reload woke before the house and has gone to ground before the day, the shape at the window gone with the light. Somewhere the money moves where she cannot see it, his second man's instructions in his head and on no paper, the plan set at half past one spending itself out in the dark.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the spending is the gutter's Monday special, the lie set ahead of the truth — or killed, if the truth got there first. If she chose bury: the spending is the search's first prices — the stones, the letters, the memory. If she chose atone: the spending is the smear's first line, the forty-one thousand six hundred dressed as hush money. Whatever the door, the dark is the same: the plan, waiting; the morning, loaded. The lodgings, dark. The reload, gone to ground.)*

scenes.synopsis: the bag, riding — the mail cart down the drive; the road, taken.
scenes.prose:
> *(At six the mail cart goes down the drive with the post bag, the boy up beside the driver, the London letters and the county letters riding under the canvas. The team moves out steady through the first grey, past the lodge, past the garden gate, onto the village road. She watches it go from the hall window, the way she has watched everything go this week: deliberately, and once.)*
> *(If she chose atone: the trust's first notices ride among them, sealed, the paying begun on paper before breakfast. If she chose expose: the bag holds no more of the week's truth — the account is the town's already, riding or arrived. If she chose bury: the bag holds nothing of the week's truth, and that is the truth it holds. Whatever the door, the going is the same: Monday's words, out before Monday's mouth is open. The cart, gone. The road, taken.)*

scenes.synopsis: the first labor, done — the range, banked; the house, nearly awake.
scenes.prose:
> *(At six the kitchen's first labor is done: the loaves cooling on the rack, the men's breakfast eaten or waiting on the board, the range banked for the day, the dresser wiped. Alice sits a moment with the household book closed on Monday's first page, and the sitting is the whole of her rest: the keys are moving upstairs, the shutters going up, the morning room's fire being lit. The house wakes from below, the way it always wakes.)*
> *(Rose comes down the stair and the kitchen rises — not ordered, only noticed. Whatever the door, the account riding, the wall rising, the trust paying, the kitchen is the same: the house's working heart, the first up and the last acknowledged. The range, banked. The bread, cooling. The house, nearly awake.)*

scenes.synopsis: the friend's morning dress — the precision, armed; the week, to be mapped.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia at six wears the morning's precision: the dark silk, plain and unadorned, the shawl folded over her arm, the memorandum book under it, the pencil behind her ear. The sums are done being counted. The week is to be mapped — Monday the execution, the days after the consequences, the whole of it to be drawn in pencil, with erasures. She looks like a general before a campaign, or a woman who has finished something and is choosing the next thing.)*
> *(If she chose expose: she priced the telling, and the telling rides. If she chose bury: she priced the keeping, and the keeping stands. If she chose atone: she priced the paying, and the paying waits for morning no longer. Whatever the door, the friend is the same: the courage to name the cost, and the grace to map the week. The book, under her arm. The friend, armed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the aunt, sleeping — the crack, at rest; the confession, keeping.
scenes.prose:
> *(She passes Letitia's door at six and does not knock. Behind it the quartermaster sleeps out of uniform at last — the wrapper, the grey wool, the night plait loosened, the woman out of the blacks for the small remainder. The mending basket stands empty by the chair. The drawer is shut, the folded letter inside it, the three lines crossed out. The candle is out.)*
> *(Rose stands a moment with her hand half-raised, and lets it fall. The crack is at its widest, and the silence is holding it, and the holding is the night's last mercy. Whatever the door, the account riding, the wall rising, the trust paying, the aunt's night ends the same: the mending done, the speaking not, the confession keeping till its own hour. The door, unknocked. The aunt, asleep.)*

scenes.synopsis: the vigil, totalled — six o'clock; the choosing, carried by other hands.
scenes.prose:
> *(At six she totals the night the way she totals everything: in columns that almost balance. The watch walked. The kitchen waked. The bag away. The keeping dark. The lodgings dark again. The garden grey. The choosing, carried into its sixth hour by other hands, and her hands, for once, empty.)*
> *(If she chose expose: her hands are empty because the account is the town's now, riding or arrived. If she chose bury: her hands are empty because the papers are ash and the wall is the mason's. If she chose atone: her hands are empty because the trust is the clerk's and the paying is the fortune's. Whatever the door, the emptiness is the same: the choosing, done, and the doing belonging to the morning. She stands at the window with empty hands. The grey, coming.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE VIGIL'S END: how she spends the night's last hour.
scenes.prose:
> *(Six o'clock, and the dark is nearly done, and one question remains for the night: how does she spend its last hour? Lie down: the bed turned down, the wrapper exchanged, one hour of sleep before the maid's hour, mercy to herself, because the week will ask everything and the body is the week's first instrument. Walk the garden: the path in the first grey, the rosemary greening, the wall faced per the door, resolve to the ground, because the Park is the reason and the reason should be walked before it is worked. Stand the window: the hall window, the drive, the grey coming up, the night named to the light, candor to herself, because a woman who has watched all night should watch the ending too.)*
> *(She stands in the hall with the house awake behind her and the grey changing outside it, and thinks: the choosing was the door, the night was the weighing, the small hours were the groundwork, and this — the last hour — is the vigil's end. This is the crossing, met or kept.)*
> *(She chose for the vigil's end the way she had chosen for the night: deliberately, and once. Whatever it was, the lying, the walking, the standing, the small hours took it up without a murmur, and the grey went on changing over the drive. The vigil, ended.)*

scenes.synopsis: the posy, in first grey — violets, rosemary, lilies; the house's language.
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning's flowers stand in the dressing room in the first grey: the dried violets, faithfulness, the season's flower; the rosemary, remembrance, cut long; the white lilies, purity of intent, for whatever Monday is. Élise set them at dusk, and the grey finds them now, the lilies for the morning room, where the town will look first. She touches a lily's petal. It is cool, and waxy, and exact.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the intent is the telling, whole and true. If she chose bury: the intent is the keeping, witnessed and borne. If she chose atone: the intent is the paying, ten years, named. Whatever the door, the flowers are the same: the language the house speaks when it has no words left. The posy, set. The morning, flowered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Morning's Taking ritual — the night hands the house to the day; the chapter's ritual.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: the handing — per door. Expose: the account the town's, the Gazette's Monday truth in type before the light. Bury: the second course standing, the third course promised to seven. Atone: the deed fair-copied, the trust's first notices away with the post. Whatever the door, the handing's face is the same: the night, delivered; the morning, received.)*
> *(Story morsel: the keeping — the keeping dark, the witness sleeping; the guard relieved; the lodgings dark again; the drawer shut. The small hours hold them all, and ask nothing.)*
> *(Story morsel: the wearing — the claret brushed, the pearls coiled, the gloves beside; the wrapper kept on till the maid's hour. The morning dressed before the morning wakes.)*
> *(Story morsel: the morning's last dark — per door. Expose: the road to town grey, the boy's errand done, the press at work. Bury: the yard's lantern out, the men's breakfast eaten, the stones sorted. Atone: the first notices riding, the smear's first line being written somewhere in London. Three labors, one reload, one morning.)*
> *(Story morsel: the maid's hour approaches — the shutters up, the breakfast room laid, the claret waiting. The house awake. The vigil done. The grey past the dark, punctual as ever.)*

ritual.occasionBrief: Six o'clock has struck and the house is at its handover: the night watch gives the drive to the day, the kitchen gives the range to the morning, the post bag is away, the keeping keeps its witness, the claret waits for the woman. The small hours dress the morning before the morning dresses itself. Walk the taking in the ritual's order — the handing, the keeping, the wearing. Exact. Quiet. Deliberate. The house that watched does not meet the day unready.

scenes.synopsis: the coach, readied — Henry's morning; the team, harnessed.
scenes.prose:
> *(The stable yard at six: the coach readied, the team harnessed, Henry's bag aboard, the ostlers moving in the grey with the day's first business. The post horse is home, rubbed down, steaming in the cold air. The coachman's whip is coiled. The books open at nine, and the trace rides to meet them.)*
> *(Rose watches from the yard's edge. If she chose expose: the coach carries the tracing of the gutter's money, the name Monday's, not tonight's. If she chose bury: the coach carries the tracing of the search's money, the stones and letters priced. If she chose atone: the coach carries the tracing of the smear's money, the paying defended. Whatever the door, the going is the same: the brother, dressed and riding. The coach, readied. The morning, loaded.)*

scenes.synopsis: the cart, gone — the town, waking; the counsel, holding.
scenes.prose:
> *(By half past six the mail cart is gone down the village road, past the Crown, past the forge, out toward the town and London beyond it. The Crown's shutters are up. The blacksmith's forge is going, the hammer not yet started. Mrs. Pike's counter is swept. The taproom's talk has not begun — Monday's paper is not yet read — and the village holds its counsel a while longer, the way it keeps its churchyard: completely, and without being asked.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the road carries the Gazette's Monday truth toward the town. If she chose bury: the road carries nothing of the week's truth, and the wall's third course comes at seven. If she chose atone: the road carries the trust's first letters, the paying begun on paper. Whatever the door, the road is the same: the village, waking; the counsel, kept. The cart, gone. The town, unwarned.)*

scenes.synopsis: the brother's morning dress — the coat; the cravat; the trace, going.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry at half past six wears the morning's dress: the coat brushed, the cravat tied exact, the boots blacked, the bag in his hand, the factor's direction fair in the breast pocket. The brother undressed by halves no longer — the night's chair-sleeping shed with the wrapper, the cravat's knot the day's first argument, and won. He takes his tea standing, the way men do who have a coach to catch.)*
> *(If she chose expose: the dress will walk into the town's reading, steady. If she chose bury: the dress will walk past the wall's third course, unmoved. If she chose atone: the dress will walk with the trust's first letters, defended. Whatever the door, the dressing is the same: the brother, at half past six, going. The coat, brushed. The brother, dressed.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the cravat, tied; the day, argued.

fashionChoices.label: Henry, ready
fashionChoices.detail: the bag, in hand; the coach, caught.

fashionChoices.label: Rose's eye
fashionChoices.detail: the mistress judges the brother.

scenes.synopsis: the last round — the day's first circuit; the lantern, out.
scenes.prose:
> *(At half past six the day's first round walks the drive in the grey, the stable lads with the daylight's orders, and the night's lantern is out, handed to the lodge. The drive is empty all the way to the village. Nothing has come up it all night but the mason's cart. Nothing will till the mason's men at seven, the coach, whichever Monday brings. The round is walked steady, unhurried, the grey doing the lantern's work now.)*
> *(Rose watches from the hall window. Whatever the door, the account riding, the wall rising, the trust paying, the watch is the same: the night guarded into the morning, the house awake behind it. The lantern, out. The drive, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — the papers, in type; Monday, spending at dawn.
scenes.prose: > *(The sting comes at half past six, and it is the morning's printing. If she chose expose: the Gazette's Monday truth is in type before the light, the account set whole and untrimmed in her own hand, Bell's own type, and the gutter's Monday special dies unborn — Pounce holds Saturday's issue and nothing more, the hundred pounds' purchase, the four lines starved. If she chose bury: the Lash's Monday issue is prizefights and a parson's debts, Pounce holding Saturday's issue and nothing more. If she chose atone: the trust's founding is in type beside the account, the sin and the paying printed together, and the smear's first line is killed before it is written. Whatever the door, the sting is the same: Monday has printed before the house has dressed. The light, coming. The paper, set.)*
scenes.sting: the sting — the papers, in type; Monday, spending at dawn.

scenes.synopsis: the garden, at dawn — the grey, in the gap; the breath, loosed.
scenes.prose:
> *(The walled garden at dawn, and the grey is in it fully now. If she chose bury: the second course stands in the first light, stone on stone, the gap less of a wound, and the third course comes at seven, promised. If she chose expose or atone: the gap stands open to the light, the wall down where the papers came out, the grey sitting in it patiently, the dark gone.)*
> *(The rosemary is green against the wall, remembrance, in the first light. The path is empty. The garden has held its breath all week, and now it lets the breath go — the oldest thing on the estate, older than the hunters, older than the sin, breathing in the dawn. She watches it a moment. The garden, at dawn. The breath, loosed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the waking, complete — the keys, the shutters, the table; the dowager, reading.
scenes.prose:
> *(The house is awake now, all the way: the keys at their posts, the maids with the shutters, the breakfast room laid, the morning room's fire lit, the household book's page turned. The small hours have handed the house to the day, and the day has taken it up the way it takes up everything: in order. The kitchen's second labor begins. The post is away. The coach stands ready.)*
> *(Augusta takes her place at the table in the dowager's black, the cane beside her chair, and reads her letters without comment — the longest game at the table, played the way she plays everything: quietly, and to the end. She looks up once, at Rose, and the look says what it has said all week: the branch fell, and the falling is the past's business, and the living are hers to watch. The table, laid. The house, awake.)*

scenes.synopsis: the claret, at dawn — the gown, found by the light; the woman, nearly.
scenes.prose:
> *(At dawn she stands before the claret in the dressing room, and the grey light finds it first: the deep claret archive silk, twenty-five years old, re-cut twice, the embroidery a shade darker than the stuff, the skirt's line, the bodice's statement, the sleeves full and fashionable. In the wrapper still she is the night's woman. The gown on the chaise is Monday's. The mended gloves lie beside it, the mend at the thumb catching the first light. The grandmother's pearls are coiled in their case.)*
> *(She does not put it on yet. The maid's hour is not come. If she chose expose: the claret will be read by a town that knows. If she chose bury: the claret will keep what the town doesn't. If she chose atone: the claret will attend ten years of paying. Whatever the door, the gown is the same: the archive's answer, laid out, found by the light. The silk, waiting. The woman, nearly.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the claret, faced; the morning, met.

fashionChoices.detail: the first light judges the gown.

scenes.synopsis: the grey, changing — the crossing, at the window; the night, named.
scenes.prose:
> *(She stands at the hall window in the wrapper with the grey changing over the drive — the light coming up the way it has come up every morning of the week, only this morning it comes up on Monday. The house awake behind her. The choosing done. The doing, the morning's. If she chose expose: the town will read by eleven. If she chose bury: the wall will rise at seven. If she chose atone: the trust will pay before breakfast. Three labors, one dawn.)*
> *(She thinks: the choosing was the door, the night was the weighing, the small hours were the groundwork, and this — the grey, changing — is the crossing. She stands a moment longer, listening. Below stairs a step sounds on the stair — a pause — the house's first footfall of Monday. The light changes. The window, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the cliffhanger — the grey light, changing; the stair, creaking; the maid, not yet knocking.
scenes.prose: > *(Dawn. The grey light changes over the drive, and below stairs the stair creaks — a step, a pause — the house's first footfall of Monday. She is awake before the maid knocks, which tells her everything about the state of her nerves. The wrapper, kept on. The claret, waiting. The morning, at the door — but the knock is not yet.)*

scenes.synopsis: the choice's morning — Sunday's decision becomes Monday's fact; the execution, conditional.
scenes.prose:
> *(Monday comes in grey and punctual, and Rose is awake before the maid knocks, which tells her everything about the state of her nerves. Sunday she chose. Monday she executes. If she chose expose: the true account went to Bell on Sunday night in her own hand — the sums exact, the names named, Harrow's half cited with his leave — and Monday's Gazette carries it on the front page, set in Bell's own type. If she chose bury: her half of the papers went into the morning-room fire on Sunday at dusk, sheet by sheet, and the mason's men come at seven to lay the wall's third course. If she chose atone: the trust deed bears Quill's seal since Sunday noon, the £150 order to Harrow is written and sent, his deed is copied fair, and the first payment leaves the fortune's surplus before breakfast.)*
> *(She stands at the window in her dressing gown and watches the drive. Whatever Monday brings — the town's reading, the wall's rising, the money's moving — it brings it because she chose first, before the hunters chose for her. That was the whole of Sunday's doctrine, and Monday is its proof. The maid knocks. The week begins.)*

scenes.synopsis: dressing for the aftermath — the archive's Monday face; Letitia's hands, not quite steady.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia lays out the Monday gown without being asked: archive silk, deep claret, twenty-five years old and re-cut twice, the skirt's embroidery a shade darker than the stuff — fashionable, deliberate, the archive's answer to a week of consequences. "If the town is reading about us," Letitia says, "the town can read claret." It is the grey doctrine in a new color, and Rose smiles despite the morning. The mended gloves come out of the drawer. The pearls, the grandmother's, at the throat.)*
> *(Letitia fastens the back, and her fingers — the quartermaster's fingers, steady through four lines and a stranger and an offer — fumble the third button twice. Rose feels it through the silk and says nothing. In the glass they look like what they are: the mistress dressed for the aftermath, the aunt dressing her, both of them holding very still around something neither has named. "There," Letitia says at last, too brightly. "Monday." The button, fastened. The hands, folded away.)*

fashionChoices.label: Wear the claret openly
fashionChoices.detail: the archive's color; the week, faced in full dress.

fashionChoices.label: Dress it down
fashionChoices.detail: plain morning dress; the household, unruffled.

fashionChoices.label: Letitia's eye
fashionChoices.detail: the quartermaster chooses the armor.

scenes.synopsis: Letitia's quiet — the aunt says little at breakfast; the composure, cracking.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia is quiet at breakfast, and the quiet is the kind with weight. She pours the tea, butters the toast, answers Rose's questions about the household in complete sentences that say nothing. Twice she starts to speak and doesn't. The second time, Rose looks up, and Letitia smiles — the hostess smile, deployed — and asks about the mason's hours. "Seven," Rose says. "They'll want the kitchen door." "I'll tell the cook," Letitia says, and writes it in the household book in a hand less even than usual.)*
> *(After breakfast, in the hall, Letitia stops with her hand on the newel post. "Rose." Just the name. Then: "Nothing. The week." She goes upstairs, and Rose stands in the hall listening to her footsteps, which are not the quartermaster's footsteps. They are a woman's footsteps, going somewhere she doesn't want to go. Rose does not follow. Some silences are load-bearing, and this one is holding up the whole house.)*

scenes.synopsis: the proprietor's terms — why the Gazette printed, or held; independence, stated plainly.
scenes.prose:
> *(Bell comes at nine, before the town has finished reading, and states her terms without preamble. If Rose chose expose: "I printed it," Bell says, "because it was true and it was news. Not for you. The Gazette doesn't print favors, Miss Hartwell — it prints facts, and the fact of your grandfather's ledgers was the biggest fact in the county this morning." If she chose bury: "I printed nothing," Bell says, "because I had nothing to print. No papers, no proof, no story. The Gazette doesn't print smoke, Miss Hartwell — come back with fire." If she chose atone: "I printed the trust," Bell says, "and the account with it. The sin was true and the payment was true, so both went in. The Gazette doesn't print halves, Miss Hartwell.")*
> *("The town will say it's your paper," Rose says. "The town," Bell says, "can read the leader and judge for itself. That's the arrangement. It was the arrangement when you were ruined and it's the arrangement now that you're —" she looks for the word, "— accounting." She stands. "One proprietor to another, Miss Hartwell: whatever Monday costs you, it doesn't cost you the paper. The paper was never yours to lose." She goes, leaving the terms where she always leaves them: in the open, non-negotiable, and — Rose has to admit — something like honorable.)*

scenes.synopsis: the town reads — Monday's paper in Monday's hands; the reading, conditional.
scenes.prose:
> *(By eleven the town has read. If she chose expose: the sin is in every coffeehouse, the sums repeated, the names named — and Pounce's version dies unborn, because a gutter sheet cannot sell lies about a story the Gazette has already told true. The hunters paid for a scandal and got a confession instead. If she chose bury: the town reads nothing new — Monday's Lash is prizefights and a parson's debts, and Pounce holds Saturday's issue and nothing more, the four lines starving for want of feeding. If she chose atone: the town reads sin and payment together — the account and the trust's founding side by side — and the talk is not of ruin but of restitution, which is a stranger story and travels faster.)*
> *(The Crown's boy brings the village's reading with the midday letters: the taproom, Mrs. Pike's counter, the blacksmith's forge — the verdicts, various, all of them hers to carry. She reads them standing at the morning-room window, the way she read the four lines, and sets them down. Whatever the town thinks by dinner, it thinks it about a woman who chose first. The reading, done. The week, underway.)*

scenes.synopsis: the week, mapped — Octavia lays out the days; counsel, precise.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia arrives with the memorandum book and maps the week the way a general maps a campaign, which is to say on paper, in pencil, with erasures. "Monday: the execution — done, or doing. Tuesday through Thursday: the consequences arrive — callers, letters, the agents' next move. Friday: the trust's first accounting, if that's the path, or the wall's fourth course. Sunday: the week closes." She looks up. "And through it all: Laurent, unanswered. Letitia —" she stops. "Letitia what?" "Letitia," Octavia says carefully, "is carrying something. I don't know what. I know the walk.")*
> *("The agents," Rose says. "Too quiet." "Agreed," Octavia says. "A hunter who misses doesn't go home. He reloads. Watch the spending, not the silence — Quill's instruction stands." She closes the book. "And Rose — whatever the week costs, it costs less than the alternative. The alternative was Saturday's timetable. You chose Monday's." She squeezes Rose's hand once, precise as everything she does. The map, drawn. The week, entered.)*

scenes.synopsis: Élise's report — violets, and the village's reading of Monday.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at noon with the dried violets and the village, and the village is in fine form. "The Crown's taproom has read the Gazette twice," she reports, arranging the posy. "Mrs. Pike's counter has opinions. The blacksmith says —" she grins, "— the blacksmith says whatever Monday cost, it was cheaper than Saturday." Rose laughs, surprised. "And the stranger?" "Gone," Élise says. "Left on the morning coach. The Crown's boy says he took the Derby poetry with him." They share the look: the notebook, full of ghosts, traveling to London.)*
> *(She settles the dried violets among the morning's flowers — faithfulness, the season's flower, Monday's too. "The village," Élise says, quieter, "is with you, Miss Hartwell. Whatever the paper said. The village remembers who mended gloves with them." She curtsies, warm as ever, and goes. Rose touches a dried violet. Faithfulness: not to the grandfather, who doesn't deserve it. To the people the week touches. The report, delivered. The flower, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE HOUSEHOLD'S FACE: open doors, steady routine, or quiet dignity; the week, faced.
scenes.prose:
> *(Monday afternoon, and the question of the household's face won't wait. Callers will come — the curious, the kind, the counting. Three faces offer themselves. Open doors: receive everyone, answer plainly, let the village see the household at its work — the candor of a house with nothing left to hide. Steady routine: the week's business proceeds exactly as any week's; no caller sees a difference, no servant changes a habit — the discipline of the unflinching, continued. Quiet dignity: few callers, gentle refusals, the house kind but closed — mercy to the household, and to herself.)*
> *(She stands in the hall where Letitia received Mrs. Quick, and thinks of the quartermaster's doctrine: the house that flinches at four lines will not survive forty. The face, chosen, becomes the week's manners.)*
> *(The household's face for the week: open, steady, or quiet. Letitia receives the instruction in the hall, and the house arranges itself accordingly. Whatever Monday costs, it will not cost the manners.)*

options.label: Quiet dignity
options.detail: *Mercy+; the softness, kept.* Few callers, gentle refusals; the house kind but closed. *(Kind, and kindness can read as retreat; the town will wonder.)*

scenes.synopsis: Harrow, placed — the week's consequence for the witness; conditional.
scenes.prose:
> *(She rides to the schoolhouse at two, because some consequences should be delivered in person. If she chose expose: Harrow is "the accomplice" for a week — his name stands in Bell's true account beside the sums, cited with his leave, and the village knows him now as the keeper of the other half. He takes it the way he takes everything: steadily. "A week," he says. "I've been the keeper for twenty years. A week of being known for it is —" he looks for the word, "— almost a holiday." If she chose bury: the quiet is kept — his half stays under its cloth in the keeping, nothing names him, the town's talk passes him by. "The cloth stays," he says. "It has stayed this long." If she chose atone: the £150 order is in his hand, the keeping deeded to him outright — the first payment, the first keeping. He holds the deed like a book he isn't sure he's allowed to open.)*
> *("Whatever the week makes of me," he says at the door, "the papers are the ground, and the ground held." She looks at him — the schoolmaster, the witness, sixty-one and steady — and understands that keeping him close was never the question. The question was whether the week would let her. It will. She told it to, on Sunday. The consequence, delivered. The witness, placed.)*

scenes.synopsis: midday — the dress, checked; the woman, holding at noon.
scenes.prose:
> *(Midday, and she checks the claret in the morning-room glass: the re-cut bodice sitting right, the embroidery catching the light, the mended glove smooth on her hand. The archive's Monday face, holding at noon. She thinks of Élise's fingers, of Letitia's, of the grandmother's — three generations of hands in the one gown, and the gown the least of what they handed down. The doctrine, the steadiness, the stitch-by-stitch. She straightens a pearl.)*
> *(The woman in the glass looks back at her, and Rose sees past the armor to the thing underneath — Octavia's distinction, kept — furious and frightened and doing it anyway. It will do. It has done, all morning. She turns from the glass. The afternoon has callers, or routine, or quiet — whichever face she chose at noon. The dress, checked. The woman, holding.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the claret through the afternoon; the consequence, worn.

fashionChoices.label: Change for the afternoon
fashionChoices.detail: the archive's second face; the day, redressed.

fashionChoices.label: The mend, examined
fashionChoices.detail: the glove's scar, studied; the emblem, tended.

scenes.synopsis: the longest game — Augusta receives Rose; the dowager watches, and says little.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta receives her in the blue drawing room at three, and the reception is itself a statement: tea, the good cups, no urgency. "So," the dowager says. "Monday." She pours. "The de Valcourt banking branch," she says presently, "fell in '94. I remember the letters. My mother's cousins." She looks at Rose over the cup. "A branch falls, a family bends. That is the way of it." She does not say what finished it. She does not know — or she does not say she knows — and Rose, who knows, says nothing. The kinship, kept light, as agreed.)*
> *("You play a long game, Grandmama." "I play," Augusta says, "the only game. One watches, one waits, one does not flinch at other people's Mondays." She sets down the cup. "Yours was well played, child. Whatever it costs —" she waves a hand, dismissing the cost the way she dismisses everything vulgar, "— it was well played." Rose curtsies, and going out understands: the longest game is not about winning. It is about still being at the table. The dowager, watching. The game, long.)*

scenes.synopsis: Julian's truth — the machinery that makes younger sons into instruments; understood, suddenly.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian comes at four, and he is quieter than she has ever seen him — the Brighton fury gone quiet, the blind-item anger spent, something thought in its place. "I've been thinking," he says, "about younger sons." He turns his hat in his hands. "My family's money — the genteel poverty of it, the way every pound has a purpose and the purposes are never mine. I used to think it was just — the way things are." He looks up. "Your grandfather's ledgers. The émigré money. Men like him built the machinery, Rose. And the machinery needs younger sons. For the army, the church, the —" he gestures, "— the instruments.")*
> *("You're not an instrument." "Aren't I?" He smiles, wry and unhandsome. "I've been one for years. I just never saw the machine." He sets down the hat. "I'm not asking you to — this isn't a proposal, it's an observation. I wanted you to know I see it now. Whatever Monday cost you, it bought me that." He goes, leaving the observation where he left it: plain, unadorned, and — she has to admit — the truest thing anyone has said all day. The machinery, seen. The younger son, awake.)*

scenes.synopsis: duty to the living — the sin old, the sinners dead, the victims owed; Henry's hardest case.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry walks with her in the garden at five, and puts the case the way only he can: as a question with no comfortable answer. "The sin is old," he says. "The sinners are dead. The victims are owed — some of them dead too, some living." He stops by the sundial. "What does duty require of the living, Rose? Not vengeance — there's no one to visit it on. Not justice — the courts can't try a ledger from '94. So what? Remembrance? Payment? A wall with a plaque?" He looks at her. "I'm asking properly. It's the hardest case I've ever put.")*
> *("I don't know," Rose says, honestly. "Monday I chose. Today I'm —" she gestures at the garden, the wall, the week, "— I'm living inside the choosing." Henry nods. "That's the answer, you know. Not the plaque. The living inside it." They walk on. "For what it's worth," he says, "whatever the living are required to do, you're doing it. I've watched you do it all season." The case, put. The answer, lived.)*

scenes.synopsis: the quiet, noted — Mrs. Quick and Slade make no move; the silence, too complete.
scenes.prose:
> *(By evening the quiet has a shape, and Rose doesn't like the shape. No letter from Mrs. Quick. No sign of Slade. The stranger gone on the morning coach. Pounce's Monday issue innocent as a prayer book. It is, she thinks, standing at the library window, the particular silence of people who have stopped spending — or started spending somewhere she can't see. Octavia's rule holds: watch the spending, not the silence. But there is no spending to watch. There is only the silence, complete as a held breath.)*
> *(She writes it in the memorandum book, the way her grandmother taught her: not the facts, the absence of facts. "Monday: no move. The offer lapsed unanswered. The pricing man recalled." She underlines the last line twice. A hunter who misses doesn't go home — Octavia said it, and Octavia is always right about hunters. He reloads. Somewhere she can't see, the money is finding its next purchase. The quiet, noted. The breath, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the offer's ashes — Mrs. Quick withdraws the £2,000; the ashes, read.
scenes.prose:
> *(Mrs. Quick calls at six, a short call, the reticule flatter than Thursday's. "Miss Hartwell. My principals instruct me to withdraw the offer." She folds her hands. "The two thousand pounds is no longer on the table." Rose studies her: the composure total as ever, the grey eyes direct. "Because Monday happened." "Because," Mrs. Quick says carefully, "the article of sale no longer exists in its former state." Which is a precise way of saying: you printed it, or burned it, or paid it — and we can't buy what's already spent.)*
> *("Thank you for the call," Rose says. "It was correctly done." Mrs. Quick inclines her head. "For what it's worth, Miss Hartwell — and it is worth nothing, I know — you played it well." She goes, and Rose stands in the hall with the ashes of the offer: two thousand pounds, refused on Thursday, withdrawn on Monday. The debrief writes itself. They didn't retreat. They re-priced. The ashes, read. The next purchase, coming.)*

scenes.synopsis: the paperwork — Quill's instruments for the path; the law, satisfied; conditional.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill comes at seven with the leather case, and the case contains Monday's law. If she chose expose: the true account's footing — every sum sourced to the ledgers, every name to a document, Harrow's leave in writing; libel checked line by line, the solicitor's hand steady. "They can't touch it," Quill says. "It's true, it's sourced, and it's printed. Truth is the whole defense." If she chose bury: the wall contract — the mason's terms, four courses, the price agreed, the kitchen door for the men at seven. "A wall," Quill says, "is the oldest legal instrument in England." If she chose atone: the trust deed, engrossed fair — £8,800 from the fortune's surplus paid now, £3,000 a year for ten years from the canal's revenues, the de Valcourts' £2,800 promised and entered. "The canal," Quill says, "never the stones. As instructed.")*
> *(She signs where he shows her — the account's attestation, the contract, the deed's schedule — and watches him sand the signatures. The law, satisfied. Whatever Monday was in the heart, on paper it is orderly: sums, courses, payments, each in its column. She thinks of the grandfather's ledgers, the original sin in the same hand, and feels the difference between his columns and hers. His hid. Hers show. The paperwork, done. The columns, hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: dressing for Augusta — the dowager's inspection at tea; the afternoon, faced.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta's eye is the county's most exacting instrument, and Rose dresses for it the way one dresses for weather: with respect and preparation. The claret has done its morning work; for the dowager's tea she chooses the archive's second face — a deep blue day dress, Hartwell blue darkened to evening, the grandmother's pearls kept at the throat, the mended glove. In the glass, with Augusta's imagined gaze over her shoulder, she looks — she hopes — like a woman whose Monday was well played.)*
> *(Augusta's actual gaze, over the tea things, does the full inspection: gown, pearls, glove, posture. "Blue," the dowager says. "Good. Claret in the morning was —" she considers, "— honest. Blue in the afternoon is wise." It is, from Augusta, a benediction. Rose curtsies, and the afternoon proceeds on the dowager's terms: the tea, the talk, the long game discussed over seed cake. The inspection, passed. The blue, wise.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the house's color; the dowager's wisdom, worn.

fashionChoices.detail: the siege's color; the doctrine, continued.

fashionChoices.label: Augusta's choosing
fashionChoices.detail: the dowager dresses the afternoon.

scenes.synopsis: the mend, worn — the glove's scar through the afternoon; the emblem, tended.
scenes.prose:
> *(Between callers she takes off the left glove and looks at the mend — the grandmother's tiny stitches, even as print, holding through Monday's long afternoon. It has been clasped, shaken, wrung, prayed in; it has signed a deed or a contract or an attestation, depending on the path. She runs her thumb along the scar the way she did that first Thursday morning, and thinks about what the mend has become: less a doctrine now than a habit — the thing her hand does.)*
> *(She puts the glove back on, smoothing each finger. The afternoon's work waits — the letters, the household book, the week's map — and the mend goes back to work with her, unremarked, unhidden. Some emblems are carried inside the bodice, like the dried violet. This one is worn on the hand, where the world can see it. That was always the point. The scar, tended. The hand, gloved.)*

scenes.synopsis: the card, unanswered — Laurent's note lies on the desk; he has not come.
scenes.prose:
> *(The card came with the morning post, on his heavy stock, in his hand: "Comte Laurent de Varenne presents his compliments to Miss Hartwell." Nothing more. No call, no visit, no word beyond the formula. It lies on the desk all day, and she does not answer it — partly pride, mostly the knowledge that some letters can't be written until the week has said what it has to say. His devastation sits between them, unintroduced: the woman he is learning to love is the heir of his family's ruiners, and he did not know.)*
> *(At dusk she picks it up, reads the formula again, and sets it down. He stays — she believes he stays; everything in her believes it — but staying is a thing a man does on his own feet, in his own time, and Monday is not the day. The card, unanswered. The silence, his. She leaves it on the desk where the lamp will find it. Some answers take the week. This one takes him.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — HARROW'S KEEPING: land agent, pensioner-historian, or his own choice funded; the witness, kept close.
scenes.prose:
> *(Evening, and the question of Harrow's keeping won't wait for the week to decide it. He is sixty-one, scarred, the keeper of the other half — and Monday has made him, variously, the accomplice, the quiet man, or the first paid. Three keepings offer themselves. Land agent: the Park's land agent, the papers his work, the estate his charge — the living archive employed, kept close by duty. Pensioner-historian: a pension and the library, the history written at leisure — the living archive honored, kept close by kindness. His own choice, funded: ask the man what he wants, and fund it outright, no strings — the candor of letting the kept choose his keeping.)*
> *(She thinks of him at his door: "the papers are the ground, and the ground held." The keeping, chosen, becomes the season's answer to the witness.)*
> *(Harrow's keeping, decided: employed, honored, or asked. The instruction goes to Quill in the morning, and the schoolhouse learns its future. Whatever the week made of the witness, the season will keep him.)*

scenes.synopsis: the keeping, told — Rose carries the decision to the schoolhouse.
scenes.prose:
> *(She walks to the village at dusk, the decision in her pocket like a letter. Harrow is marking copybooks, and he looks up with the mild surprise of a man whose door is rarely knocked at dusk — and today it has been knocked twice. "Miss Hartwell." She doesn't waste time. She tells him: the keeping she chose — the land agency, the pension and the library, or the funded choice, whichever the week decided — and watches him take it the way he takes everything: steadily, the pen set down, the hands folded.)*
> *("You don't have to answer tonight," she says. "I know," he says. "I'm answering anyway." And he does — plainly, gratefully, with the dryness intact: the schoolmaster accepting the strangest promotion of his sixty-one years. At the door he stops her. "Miss Hartwell. Whatever the papers made me carry —" he looks for the word, "— thank you for letting me set some of it down." She walks home in the dusk, and the lane feels, for the first time in a week, like an ordinary lane. The keeping, told. The witness, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: supper — the lengthening silence; the aunt, nearly speaking.
scenes.prose:
> *(Supper is a quiet affair, and the quiet lengthens with the candles. Letitia serves, pours, carves — the quartermaster's hands doing the quartermaster's work — but the hands shake, faintly, at the gravy boat, and Rose watches her aunt set it down with elaborate care. "Letitia." "Yes, dear?" "Nothing. The gravy." "The gravy," Letitia agrees, too quickly, "is — the gravy is fine." They eat. The clock ticks. Twice more Letitia opens her mouth, and twice the moment passes, and the soup cools.)*
> *("You know," Letitia says at last, not looking up, "your grandmother always said a house is like a glove. It can be mended." A pause. "She never said what you do when the hand inside it is the thing that's torn." She rises, abruptly. "Excuse me. The household book." She goes, and Rose sits alone with the cooling soup and the sentence, which sits in the room like a third guest. The silence, lengthened. The speaking, near.)*

scenes.synopsis: Augusta's warning — the hunter isn't done; the money, patient.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends for her after supper, and the summons has the flavor of the long game: no urgency, absolute intent. "You think it's over," the dowager says, without preamble. "The purchase, the offer, the Monday paper. It isn't." She lays down her embroidery. "Cecilia's people lost a purchase, child. They did not lose the appetite. Mrs. Vane's money is patient — it was patient for twenty years, it can be patient for a week." She looks at Rose. "The hunters will find another article. See that it isn't you.")*
> *("What would you have me do?" "What you've done," Augusta says. "Choose first. Before they choose for you. It worked on Monday; it will work again." She takes up the embroidery. "And Rose — the money will try Harrow again, or the village, or your aunt." A beat. "Especially your aunt. A woman carrying something is a woman who can be —" she looks for the word, "— approached." Rose goes out with the warning folded small, like a knife in a reticule. The hunter, not done. The money, patient.)*

scenes.synopsis: evening — the dress for the night's work; the woman, bracing.
scenes.prose:
> *(Evening, and the day's armor comes under review. The claret has served since morning; the blue served the dowager. For the night's work — the ritual, the household, the steadying — she chooses the archive's night face: a dark silk, nearly black, the pearls kept, the mended glove. In the glass, the woman looks like the evening she intends: braced, deliberate, the week's weight worn the way the gown wears its embroidery. Or so she tells the glass.)*
> *(The glass, being honest glass, shows her the truth underneath: tired, resolute, the aunt's shaking hands still in her mind's eye. She touches the dried violet at her wrist — faithfulness, Monday's too — and turns away. The night has a ritual and a household and, at its end, a bed. One thing at a time. That is the whole of the evening's doctrine. The dress, chosen. The woman, bracing.)*

scenes.synopsis: the price, restated kindly — Octavia names £41,600 gently; the cost, held in view.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes before the ritual with the figures, because someone must hold them kindly and it will not be Rose. "The price," she says, "restated, because the week will try to make you forget it." She opens the memorandum book. "Forty-one thousand, six hundred pounds. That was the sin's worth in money: eight thousand eight hundred now, from the fortune's surplus; three thousand a year for ten years, from the canal's revenues; two thousand eight hundred to the de Valcourts, promised." If she chose atone, the figures are the week's payments, begun — the surplus drawn, the schedule entered. If she chose expose or bury, they are the measure — what restitution would have cost, set against what Monday cost instead.)*
> *("It's a great deal of money." "It is," Octavia agrees. "It's also the cheapest thing you've bought all season. The alternative was Saturday's timetable, and Saturday's price wasn't in pounds." She closes the book. "Restitution isn't punishment, Rose. It's arithmetic with the guilt taken out." She squeezes Rose's hand. "Now go and steady your household. The figures will keep." The price, restated. The kindness, in the restating.)*

scenes.synopsis: the ledger — the account, kept in her own hand; conditional.
scenes.prose:
> *(Before the ritual she takes up the ledger — her own book, not the grandfather's — and enters Monday. If she chose expose: the public account — what the town knows now, set down against what she knows: the sums printed, the names named, the hunters' version dead. If she chose bury: the private account — what was burned and what remains: her half ash, Harrow's half under its cloth, her memory the only complete copy. If she chose atone: the trust's account — £8,800 entered, the ten years scheduled, the de Valcourts' £2,800 promised, the £150 to Harrow paid. Three different Mondays. One hand, entering.)*
> *(She rules a line under the entry, the way her grandmother taught her: the day's business, closed. The grandfather's ledgers hid; hers show — that was the morning's thought, and it holds by lamplight. Whatever the path, the account is kept, and the keeping is the point. She closes the book. The household is gathering. The ledger, entered. The day, ruled.)*

scenes.synopsis: the talk — Élise's counsel on the village's heart; warm, shrewd.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise stays after the dried violets are delivered, and the staying is the counsel — she has something to say, and says it the way she says everything: warmly, and without permission. "The village has decided something, Miss Hartwell. About Monday." She folds her hands. "Mrs. Pike says a woman who pays — or prints, or burns, whichever it was — a woman who does it herself is a woman the village can stand behind." She looks up. "They were frightened, you know. The wall, the papers, the stranger. They're not frightened now. They're —" she looks for the word, "— they're proud. It's an odd thing to be proud of, but there it is.")*
> *("Tell them —" Rose starts. "I'll tell them nothing," Élise says. "The village doesn't need telling. It needs —" she gestures at the hall, the lamps, the gathering household, "— it needs tonight. The steadying. Go and do it, Miss Hartwell." She curtsies, warm as ever, and goes. Rose stands a moment with the counsel, which is the best kind: given freely, asking nothing. The talk, had. The village, proud.)*

scenes.synopsis: night — Letitia's hands shake at the dressing table; the confession, near.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia comes to help her dress for the ritual, and the quartermaster is not herself. The night silk's fastenings are simple, but her fingers shake on them — visibly now, not to be ignored — and when Rose meets her eyes in the glass, Letitia looks away first. "Let me," Rose says gently, and does the last buttons herself. They stand a moment in the glass together: the mistress in dark silk and pearls, the aunt behind her, her hands folded hard to still them.)*
> *("You're carrying something," Rose says. It is not a question. Letitia's mouth opens, closes. "Not tonight," she whispers. "Please. Not tonight." Rose nods, and does not press — some silences are load-bearing, and tonight the house needs its beams. But she takes her aunt's hands, shaking and all, and holds them a moment. "When, then." "Soon," Letitia says. "Before the week does it for me." The hands, held. The confession, promised.)*

scenes.synopsis: the reckoning, foreseen — Rose understands what Letitia is carrying.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone before the ritual, Rose puts it together — not the details, the shape. The quiet at breakfast. The fumbled button. The shaking hands. The sentence about the torn hand inside the mended glove. Letitia knew the shape of the sin — not the sums, not the names, the shape — and kept the family's peace, and called it love, and her comfort was the price of her silence. That is the shape Rose can see. The details are Letitia's to tell, and she will tell them — soon, before the week does it for her.)*
> *(Rose stands at the window with the night coming on, and feels the week's second reckoning gathering: Monday was the sin, faced. The aunt is next. She does not know what the confession will cost — forgiveness, or the withholding of it, or something between — but she knows it is coming, and she knows she will hear it. That is enough, for tonight. The household waits. The reckoning, foreseen. The listening, promised.)*

scenes.synopsis: the steadying — the household steadies together after Monday; the chapter's ritual.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the lamps — "steady, miss. The house takes its tone from you.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the door — "the figures will keep. Tonight the house keeps you.")*
> *(Story morsel: Harrow, at the back — come from the village, the keeping new on him.)*
> *(Story morsel: Augusta, at the stairs — "well played, child. The house, too.")*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the door — "tomorrow's gloves get the extra stitch. For steadiness.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: Monday is executed — the account printed, the papers burned, or the trust founded — and the week stretches ahead with its callers, its quiet hunters, and its unanswered cards. Tonight the household does what it does best: it steadies. The servants' hall by lamplight, the whole house gathered, the week's face chosen and worn. Dress for the steadying: the archive's night face, deliberate and unafraid — the house does not meet its week in undress. Precise. Together. Unbowed. The house that steadies together does not flinch apart.

scenes.synopsis: after the ritual — the house, braced; the quiet, held.
scenes.prose:
> *(After the ritual the house settles the way a ship settles after the sails are set: the hall emptying, the lamps low, the household carrying Monday's steadiness upstairs like a lamp. Rose stands in the hall a moment alone, the ritual's direction still on her — blue, grey, or pearled, whichever face she chose — and feels the week's weight redistribute. Not lighter. Better carried. That is what the household does: it teaches the carrying.)*
> *(She blows out the last lamp herself, the way she did after the mending. The dried violet is still at her wrist. The card is still on the desk. The aunt's confession is still coming. But tonight the house is braced, and the bracing holds. She goes upstairs. The quiet, held. The ship, under sail.)*

scenes.synopsis: nightcap — undressing; the mend, examined; the day, unpinned.
scenes.prose:
> *(The bedroom, late. The night silk comes off and is hung with care; it has steadied a household and earned its rest. The pearls are coiled. The gloves come last. She holds the left one to the lamp: the grandmother's mend, the tiny stitches, holding through Monday entire — the choosing, the reading, the callers, the ritual. A whole day of consequence, and the scar held through all of it. It will hold through the week.)*
> *(She lays the gloves beside tomorrow's dried violet and unpins her hair. The day unpins with it: the execution, the town's reading, the agents' silence, the shaking hands, the steadied hall. Pins down. Facts kept. She is tired the way a woman is tired after being exactly herself for sixteen hours. The lamp lowered. The silk, hung. The mend, holding. The day, survived.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE LETTER: write to Laurent tonight, let the week speak, or go to him; the card, answered.
scenes.prose:
> *(Night, and the card is still on the desk where the lamp finds it: "Comte Laurent de Varenne presents his compliments." Three answers offer themselves. Write it herself tonight: pen, paper, the truth in her own hand — what Monday was, what the sin was, what she is — sent at dawn, no desk between them but the miles. Let the week speak first: no letter yet; let him read the Gazette, the trust, the wall, and come in his own time — the patience of letting events do the explaining. Go to him tomorrow: ride herself, say it face to face — the bravest and most exposed, no paper, no interval, only the woman and the man and the ruin between them.)*
> *(She stands at the desk with the pen in her hand, and thinks of his devastation: the heir of his family's ruiners, and he did not know. He stays — she believes he stays. But the believing needs the answering, and the answering is hers to make. The letter, or the week, or the ride. The card, answered her way.)*
> *(The answer to the card: written, waited, or ridden. The pen laid down or taken up, the week instructed or the mare ordered. Whatever Laurent's devastation needs, it will not need it unanswered.)*

scenes.synopsis: the house, sleeping — Rose walks the quiet house; the household, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(She walks the house at eleven, the way the mistress walks when the house is hers in the particular way of night: the hall, the morning room, the blue drawing room, the servants' passage. Everywhere the steadiness has settled — the lamps out, the doors barred, the household asleep in the braced quiet of a house that chose first. In the kitchen the cook has left the bread rising under its cloth. In the hall Amos's chair stands empty, the porter's post kept even in sleep.)*
> *(She touches the newel post where Letitia stopped that morning — "Rose. Nothing. The week." — and goes upstairs. The house sleeps around her, forty souls, the week's work ticking in the dark: the ink, the courses, the payments, whichever Monday she made. All of it hers: the choosing, and what the choosing cost. She climbs the stairs. The house, sleeping. The mistress, keeping.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Bell's Monday leader on the aftermath; the paper's independence, printed.
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting is Monday's leader, read by lamplight after the ritual — Bell's own column, set in her own type, on the paper's own terms. If she chose expose, the headline is "THE ACCOUNT — On Debts, Confessed," and the leader lays the sin out plain: the émigré money, the speculation, the covering of Hartwell first — true, sourced, and printed because it was news, not because it was hers. If she chose bury, the headline is "THE WALL — On What Isn't Printed," and the leader notes, coolly, what Monday didn't bring: no names, no sums, a wall rebuilding course by course, and a gutter sheet with nothing to sell. If she chose atone, the headline is "THE TRUST — On Payment, Begun," and the leader prints sin and payment together: the account and the restitution, side by side, because both were true.)*
> *(Rose reads it twice, the way she reads everything Bell writes, and understands the leader's real subject: not the sin, but the paper. The Gazette printed what was true — the account, the silence, the payment — and nothing else, for nobody else. That is the independence, printed. The hunters bought ink; Bell owns hers. The leader, read. The paper, its own.)*
scenes.sting: the sting — Bell's Monday leader on the aftermath; the paper's independence, printed.

scenes.synopsis: Bell's private word — the proprietor, personal; blunt, warm underneath.
scenes.prose:
> *(Bell comes herself at ten, unannounced, and the unannounced is the message — the proprietor doesn't make social calls. "One thing," Bell says, "not for the paper." She looks at Rose: the night silk, the tired eyes, the woman after Monday. "I printed what was true today. Or I held what wasn't. Either way —" she stops, which for Bell is practically a speech, "— either way, it cost you. I know what things cost. I buried a husband and kept his paper." She picks up her reticule. "That's the private word. The public one ran this morning.")*
> *(At the door she turns. "Miss Hartwell. The hunters will come again — not for the sin, that's spent, but for something. When they do —" she looks for the word, finds it, "— choose first. It's worked so far." She goes, leaving the private word where she left it: plain, unprinted, and — Rose has to admit — the kindest thing anyone said all day. The word, kept. The proprietor, human.)*

scenes.synopsis: the glass — the last look; the woman, seen truly.
scenes.prose:
> *(Midnight coming, and she stands before the glass in her nightdress for the last look of Monday: the hair unpinned, the face unpainted, the woman without the archive. The claret, the blue, the night silk — all hung, all honored, all done. What remains is the Monday underneath: the choice executed, the town read, the hunters quiet, the aunt's confession coming, the card unanswered. She looks at the woman in the glass: the day's faces put away with the gowns, and underneath, simply Rose, who chose first.)*
> *(She touches the mended glove where it lies beside the dried violet, and smiles — tired, unguarded, the smile nobody sees. "Well played," Augusta said. "Choose first," Bell said. "Soon," Letitia said. The glass keeps the smile. The woman, seen. Monday, closed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the friend's verdict — "You chose first. That's the whole of it."
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes to the bedroom at half past eleven, in her dressing gown, with two cups of chocolate — the unofficial debrief, the week's first. "So," she says. "Monday." They sit by the fire. "The town read. The hunters are quiet. Harrow is kept. Laurent —" she glances at the desk, the card, "— Laurent is Laurent. Your aunt is carrying something heavy up the stairs." She sips. "And you?" "Tired," Rose says. "Exactly as tired as I should be." Octavia nods. "Good. That's the right amount.")*
> *("Octavia." "Yes?" "Was it enough? The choosing." Octavia sets down the chocolate. "You chose first," she says. "That's the whole of it. Everything else — the paper, the wall, the trust, the week — is carpentry. The choosing was the house." She stands. "Sleep, Rose. Tuesday brings the consequences, and you'll meet them the way you met Monday." The friends' talk, done. The verdict, given.)*

scenes.synopsis: the cost, held — what Monday cost, carried; the night, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone at midnight, Rose holds the cost, and it isn't counted in pounds. The town knows, or doesn't, or knows and is counting the payments: whichever Monday she made, something was spent that isn't money. Harrow's week as the accomplice. The wall's silence. The trust's long arithmetic. Laurent's unanswered card. Letitia's shaking hands. She holds them the way she held the dried violet: quietly, close to the body. That is where costs belong.)*
> *(She stands at the window, and the park is dark beyond the glass — the wall a pale line, the garden behind it, the papers' ground. Somewhere in London a woman named Vane is deciding her next purchase. Somewhere in the house her aunt is awake, carrying the shape of the sin. Somewhere — perhaps — a man is deciding whether to stay. She lets the curtain fall. The cost, held. The night, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the door — Letitia comes at midnight with a candle; the confession, about to begin.
scenes.prose: > *(Midnight, and a knock at the bedroom door — soft, the way the household knocks when the news is private. Letitia stands there in her dressing gown with a candle, and she is not shaking anymore — she is past shaking, into the terrible stillness of a woman who has decided. "Rose," she says. "You should hear it from me before the week does it for me." She steps inside. The candle flame bends in the draught. The confession begins.)*

scenes.synopsis: Tuesday morning — the note; ten o'clock; the day, arranged around an hour.
scenes.prose:
> *(Tuesday comes in grey and clears by eight. Rose is at the breakfast table with the post, and among the bills and a seed catalogue comes the note — Letitia's hand, the loops careful: "May I call at ten? There is something I must say, and it will not keep until dinner. L." Rose reads it twice. The eggs go cold. She folds the note into the reticule's inner pocket, the one where the important things live, and tells the footman the morning room will be wanted at ten, and the tea strong.)*
> *(She sits a moment longer with the cold eggs. The household goes on around her — the clink of the urn, the housemaid with the toast rack — and she thinks, with the ledger part of her mind, that whatever it is, it will cost something. Everything this season has cost something. She finishes the toast standing up. The day arranges itself around the hour: ten o'clock, the morning room, her aunt.)*

scenes.synopsis: the morning dress — plain, honest; dressed to hear the truth.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes up with the day's dress over her arm, and stops in the doorway the way she does when the occasion is unclear. "For a confession," Rose says, "one's own aunt's, at ten o'clock in the morning room — what does one wear?" Élise considers the question with professional gravity. "Nothing that rustles," she says at last. "Nothing that apologizes. Nothing that accuses." She lays out the grey merino, the plainest of the morning gowns, and the garnet pin goes back in the box. "The truth," Élise says, pinning the fichu, "is best heard in grey.")*
> *(In the glass: a young woman in grey merino, severe and unadorned, the mended gloves on the dressing table like a question. Rose picks them up, considers, sets them down again. Not today. Today the hands go bare. "Grey," she says to the glass. "Honest." Élise, behind her, ties the sash with unusual care. "Grey," she agrees, "is the color of listening.")*

scenes.synopsis: the servants' hall knows something; the house, listening at its own doors.
scenes.prose:
> *(Downstairs, the house is performing Tuesday with unusual precision — the silver polished to a confrontational shine, the morning room dusted twice. Rose finds the housekeeper in the hall with a duster and no dust. "Is everything quite all right?" Rose asks. "Quite all right, miss," says the housekeeper, dusting the already-dusted newel post. The servants' hall has heard something. It has heard nothing specific, which is worse.)*
> *(In the kitchen passage she meets the second footman carrying the strong tea up an hour early, and the under-housemaid with rosemary for the morning room, in a jug. "Mrs. Élise said the room should have something living," the girl says, defensive. Remembrance, Rose thinks, and does not say. The house is preparing for a confession the way it prepares for a christening: thoroughly, and with green things.)*

scenes.synopsis: Octavia's counsel — the friend, precise; what to do with an aunt's confession.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia arrives at half past nine, uninvited and exactly on time, with her sketchbook and the air of a woman attending a professional engagement. "You look," she says, "like a woman about to be confessed to." "I am a woman about to be confessed to." "Then listen like an heiress and not like a niece," Octavia says, opening the sketchbook. "A niece forgives before she's heard the sentence. An heiress hears the sentence first." She begins to draw the morning room, very fast, the way she draws battlefields.)*
> *("And if it's unforgivable?" Rose asks. Octavia doesn't look up. "Then you'll know at eleven, and not at ten. That's the whole of my counsel: don't spend the forgiveness before you've heard the price." The pencil stops. "She loves you, you know. In her way. Her way is just — extremely well-upholstered." Rose laughs, once, despite everything. "Go on," Octavia says, "draw the curtains. It's ten.")*

scenes.synopsis: Augusta in the garden — the dowager deflects; the morning, held off.
scenes.prose:
> *(There are still twenty minutes, and Rose spends them in the garden with Augusta, who is inspecting the lilies Élise set in the spring with the expression of a general reviewing troops. "The white ones have taken," Augusta says. "Purity of intent, your Élise tells me. In a garden, at least, one can plant the intention and get the flower." She does not ask why Rose is in grey. Dowagers do not ask; they wait.)*
> *("You knew my grandfather," Rose says, because the hour is coming and boldness is cheaper now. "I knew everyone," Augusta says. "It was a smaller world, and I was in all of it." She snaps a dead leaf from a lily stem. "The banking branch of my family — the de Valcourts — they fell in the same years. Everyone fell in those years. The wonder is not that they fell." She looks at Rose then, properly. "The wonder is what the survivors did with the falling." She walks on, before Rose can ask what she means.)*

scenes.synopsis: the witness, at work — Harrow's papers; the morning, steadied.
scenes.prose:
> *(In the library, Harrow is at the long table with his papers spread in their careful rows, the scar pulling his cheek as he bends to the page. He looks up when she comes in, and something in her face makes him set down the pen. "Ten o'clock," he says. It is not a question. The whole house knows. "My aunt," Rose says. "She has something to tell me." Harrow nods, once. "The keeping of a thing," he says, "is a weight. The telling of it is a different weight. Neither is light.")*
> *(He turns back to his papers — the other half of the estate's oldest secrets, now the library's. "If she asks your forgiveness," he says to the page, "remember that forgiveness is not a receipt. It doesn't settle the account. It just —" he searches for the word, the schoolmaster reaching — "it just files it where you can find it." Rose stands a moment in the library's quiet, steadied by the man's plain arithmetic of the heart. "Thank you, Mr. Harrow." "Ten o'clock," he says again, and picks up the pen.)*

scenes.synopsis: ten o'clock — the morning room; the waiting, done properly.
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning room at ten minutes to ten: the strong tea steaming, the rosemary in its jug, the two chairs set at the angle Letitia prefers — adjacent, conspiratorial, the angle of allies. Rose has arranged it herself, over the housekeeper's objections, because there are some rooms one must set with one's own hands. Remembrance, in a jug. She sits in her own chair and does not fidget. She has decided not to fidget.)*
> *(At five minutes to ten she hears Letitia's step in the passage — unmistakable, the quick light tread of a woman who has never in her life been late for anything, even a confession. There is a pause outside the door. Rose understands, suddenly and completely, that her aunt is standing in the passage gathering her courage the way other women gather their skirts. "Come in, Aunt Letitia," she says, before the knock can come. The door opens.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE LISTENING: how Rose receives the confession; as daughter, heir, or judge.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia is in the doorway, and Rose has one breath — one — to decide how she will listen. The aunt's face is doing something Rose has never seen it do: it is unmade, the comic composure folded away like a fan. What comes through that door will be the truth, or her aunt's version of it, and the listening is a choice. Rose thinks of Octavia: listen like an heiress. She thinks of Harrow: the telling is a weight. She thinks of the grey dress, the color of listening. The breath ends. She chooses.)*
> *(She rises, because one rises, and takes her aunt's cold hands, and leads her to the adjacent chair, and pours the strong tea with a steady hand. "I am listening, Aunt." The listening takes its shape, daughter's, heir's, or judge's, and the room holds its breath around the choosing.)*
> *(The shape is chosen — daughter, heir, or judge — and Letitia, seeing it in Rose's face, understands that she is truly heard. The confession, given its hearing. The listening, done.)*

options.label: As a daughter
options.detail: *Mercy+; the niece's ear.* She listens for the woman, not the sin — love first, ledger after. *(The niece forgives before the sentence; Octavia warned her.)*

options.label: As an heir
options.detail: *Resolve+; the heiress's ear.* She listens for the facts — what was known, when, and what it cost. *(The heiress hears the sentence first.)*

options.label: As a judge
options.detail: *Candor+; the judge's ear.* She listens for the evasion — what is softened, what is skipped, what is spared. *(The judge hears what is not said.)*

scenes.synopsis: the door, closed gently — Letitia enters; the confession, begun.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia closes the door herself, gently, the way one closes the door of a sickroom, and stands a moment with her hand on the knob, as if the room might escape. Then she crosses to the adjacent chair and sits, and arranges her skirts with the automatic precision of fifty years, and looks at Rose. "You are in grey," she says. "How — suitable. I had not thought —" She stops. The chatter, for once, does not come to rescue her.)*
> *(Rose pours the tea. The strong tea steams between them. Letitia takes the cup in both hands, as if for warmth, though the room is warm. "I have been," she says carefully, "a comic woman for a very long time. It is a useful thing to be. People tell comic women nothing, and expect nothing, and one may — one may keep a great deal, behind it." She sets down the cup, untasted. "I kept a great deal, Rose. Behind the chatter. It is time you knew.")*

scenes.synopsis: the aunt's armor — Letitia's dress, seen truly; the comic woman's costume, and its cracks.
scenes.prose:
> *(It comes to Rose, looking at her aunt across the tea, that Letitia is dressed for a battle she has already lost. The puce silk — ten years old, remade twice, the color of dried blood and discretion. The cameo at the throat, the late Mr. Hartwell's mother's, worn like a medal. The small severe knot of warm brown ringlets, silver-threaded, with a single tortoiseshell comb. Everything about it says: a respectable woman, a comic woman, a woman with nothing to confess. The costume is perfect. That is how Rose knows it is a costume.)*
> *("You dressed carefully," Rose says. Letitia glances down at the puce silk as if surprised to find herself in it. "One dresses," she says, "for the occasion one wishes it were." A ghost of the old Letitia surfaces, then sinks. "I wished it were a Tuesday call. It is not a Tuesday call." She smooths the silk over her knee — twice, the nervous habit of decades. "Well. The dress will have to do. It has done for everything else.")*
