scenes.synopsis: "I knew the shape" — the confession's first truth; the grandfather's speculation, glimpsed.
scenes.prose:
> *("Your grandfather," Letitia says, "was the cleverest man I ever knew, and the most —" she hunts for the word — "the most certain. In the war years, when the émigrés came with their money and their manners and their terrible French, he took their funds to — to play with. That is the word he used. Play." She looks at the rosemary. "The speculation failed. You know this. What you do not know, what I knew and never said, is that when it failed, he did not fail evenly. He covered Hartwell first. The house, the land, the name. And the émigré families —" her voice thins — "were left to the fall.")*
> *(Rose sits very still. The grey dress does not rustle. "You knew this." "I knew the shape of it," Letitia says quickly. "Not the sums, not the names — never the names. I knew that money had come, and that money had gone, and that our house stood while other houses fell, and that nobody spoke of it. The shape, Rose. A clever girl could see the shape, if she did not look away. I looked away. That was my part.")*

scenes.synopsis: the shape, not the details — what Letitia actually knew, and what she never asked.
scenes.prose:
> *("I never asked," Letitia says. "That is the whole of it, and the worst of it. I never asked your grandfather for the sums. I never asked your father, who knew less than I did, poor boy, barely grown when it happened; I never asked anyone. Asking would have made it real, and I had —" she gestures at the room, the house, the whole of Hartwell Park beyond the windows — "I had all this. The peace of it. The comfort. Asking would have cost me the peace, and I was not brave.")*
> *("The de Varennes," Rose says. It is not a question. Letitia flinches, actually flinches, the comic woman's face crumpling like paper. "Among them. The de Valcourts — Augusta's banking cousins — among them." She counts them off on her fingers, the way she counts dinner guests, and the ordinariness of the gesture is terrible. "I knew the shape, Rose. Ruin, with our roof still on. I never learned the names because names would have —" She stops. "Names would have required me to do something.")*

scenes.synopsis: the comfort, priced — her silence kept the peace; the aunt's account of herself.
scenes.prose:
> *("I told myself," Letitia says, "that it was for the family. The peace. Your father was a boy, and the house needed its quiet. A scandal then would have broken us. All true." She looks at her hands, folded in the puce silk. "All true, and all — convenient. The peace I kept was very comfortable, Rose. I was comfortable in it for thirty years. That is the part I cannot —" her voice breaks, properly breaks, for the first time — "that is the part I cannot make sound noble, because it wasn't.")*
> *(The clock ticks. The tea goes cold. Rose thinks of Harrow's arithmetic: the keeping is a weight, the telling is a different weight. Her aunt has carried the keeping for thirty years, and the telling is crushing her in real time, here, in the morning room, in the puce silk. "Go on," Rose says quietly. It is the kindest thing she can say, and the cruelest. Letitia goes on.)*

scenes.synopsis: the family's peace, named — what the quiet cost, under each door Rose chose.
scenes.prose:
> *(If she chose expose, the Gazette printed it yesterday, the whole true account on Bell's terms, and the peace you kept is public now, Aunt. If she chose bury, the papers are gone and the wall is going back up, and the peace you kept is the peace I have bought again, at the same price. If she chose atone, the trust was signed yesterday — forty-one thousand six hundred pounds, the canal's three thousand a year for ten years, eight thousand eight hundred now — and the peace you kept is being paid for, properly, at last. Rose hears her own voice laying it out, Octavia-precise, and is faintly surprised at herself.)*
> *(Letitia absorbs this, the expose, the bury, the atone, whichever door the season entered, with the stillness of a woman receiving a sentence. "Then it is done," she says at last. "The shape is out of my hands. Thirty years I kept it, and now —" she looks around the morning room as if seeing it for the first time — "now I am just an old woman in puce silk who knew a thing and said nothing. That is my whole biography, Rose. Make of it what you will.")*

scenes.synopsis: comic no longer — the aunt, unmasked; the confession's end.
scenes.prose:
> *(There is a long silence. The rosemary in its jug gives off its sharp clean smell — remembrance, doing its work unasked. Letitia sits with her hands folded, the comic woman entirely gone, and what is left is a woman of sixty-odd years who made a coward's bargain in her youth and has come, at last, to pay the difference. It is, Rose thinks, the bravest thing she has ever seen her aunt do. It is also thirty years late. Both things are true. The grey dress holds them both without rustling.)*
> *("I am not asking your forgiveness," Letitia says. "I have no right to ask it. I came to tell you because you are the heir, and the heir should know what the house is built on." She rises — the puce silk, the cameo, the severe comb, all of it suddenly just clothes on a tired woman. "I will be in my room. Whenever —" she does not finish. She goes to the door, and pauses with her hand on the knob, and does not turn around. The door closes. Gently. Like a sickroom.)*

scenes.synopsis: the midday dress — the afternoon, faced; what one wears after a confession.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise finds her in the morning room at noon, still in the grey, the tea long cold. "The grey has done its work," Élise says, practical as a surgeon. "It listened. Now the afternoon must be faced, and the afternoon requires —" she holds up the mulberry merino, the color of dried violets — "faithfulness. To what was heard. The dress says: I heard it, and I am still here." Rose changes without argument. There are days when the modiste is the wisest woman in the house.)*
> *(In the glass: mulberry, severe, unadorned, and the face looking back is older than it was at ten o'clock. "It is a good color for the day," Élise says, fastening the sash. "It does not forgive. It does not accuse. It remembers." Rose touches the merino's sleeve. "Then it is exactly right.")*

scenes.synopsis: the garden walk — Rose carries the confession around the still-wild beds.
scenes.prose:
> *(She walks the garden alone, the mulberry skirts brushing the still-wild beds. The wall is down on the oldest side — the breach where the season began, the papers found, everything started. The masons' work waits on her word now. If she chose bury: the new courses are going up; the garden will be walled again by week's end. If expose or atone: the breach stands open, the garden airing like a wound left to the sun. Either way, she walks it.)*
> *(She stops where the papers were found, the hollow in the old wall's line. Thirty years her aunt kept the shape. Thirty years the wall kept the papers. The house is very good at keeping. She is the first Hartwell in a generation to open things — papers, garden, aunt. It occurs to her that opening is also a kind of keeping: you keep the truth by letting it out. Her skirt brushes the rosemary Élise planted near the wall, and it gives off its smell. Remembrance, again. The garden is full of it today.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE ANSWER: forgiveness, or not; Rose answers her aunt aloud.
scenes.prose:
> *(In the garden, with the wall's breach at her back, Rose understands that the day has been walking toward this hour since ten o'clock. Letitia is in her room, waiting — not for forgiveness, she said; she has no right to ask. But waiting, all the same. The answer is Rose's to give, and it must be given aloud: the season has taught her that silent things fester. Forgive, and say so. Withhold, and say so. Or ask for time, and say that. The mulberry dress — faithfulness — does not decide for her. It only remembers.)*
> *(She thinks of Harrow: forgiveness is not a receipt; it files the thing where you can find it. She thinks of Octavia: don't spend it before you've heard the price — and the price has been heard, in full, in puce silk. She thinks of her aunt's hand on the doorknob, not turning around. The garden waits. The house waits. The answer, when it comes, will be spoken to Letitia's face, in her room, before dinner. It will be one of three things.)*
> *(The answer is chosen — given, withheld, or held for the week — and Rose turns back toward the house with it in her mouth like a stone or a seed. The afternoon, answered. The aunt, waiting.)*

options.label: Forgive her, aloud
options.detail: *Mercy+; the daughter's answer.* "I forgive you, Aunt." Said to her face, meant — the thirty years filed where they can be found. *(A receipt settles. A door opens.)*

options.label: Withhold it, aloud
options.detail: *Candor+; the judge's answer.* "Not yet. Perhaps not ever." Said to her face, honestly — the comfort was the price, and the price is named. *(Some debts are not forgiven; they are carried, openly.)*

options.label: Ask for time, aloud
options.detail: *Resolve+; the heir's answer.* "Give me the week." Said to her face, deliberately — the heir does not spend before the audit closes. *(Time is not refusal; it is the ledger, still open.)*

scenes.synopsis: the answer, given — Rose goes to her aunt's room; it is spoken aloud.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia's room at three: the fire lit against the November chill, the mending basket by the chair — she has been mending, of course; the woman mends when she cannot think — and Letitia herself very straight in the chair, the puce silk changed for a house dress, the severe comb still in. She looks up when Rose comes in, and her face does the unmade thing again, briefly. "Rose." "Aunt." Rose sits in the other chair, adjacent, conspiratorial. And says it.)*
> *(If she chose to forgive: "I forgive you, Aunt Letitia." Said plainly, aloud. Letitia's hands stop in the mending. The silence that follows is the longest of the day. Then: "Oh," her aunt says, inadequately, wonderfully. "Oh, my dear." If she chose to withhold: "Not yet, Aunt." Said plainly, aloud. Letitia nods once, the way she nods at bad news about the weather. "No," she says. "I did not expect — no." If she chose time: "Give me the week, Aunt." Letitia nods. "The week," she agrees. "I have waited thirty years. A week is —" she almost smiles — "a week is nothing. We've mended longer.")*

scenes.synopsis: Augusta's admission, lightly — the banking branch fell; the dowager's own quiet loss.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta is in the stillroom at four, supervising the lavender water with the air of one conducting diplomacy. She does not look up when Rose comes in. "Your aunt," she says, "has had her morning." It is not a question. The house knows everything; the house always knows everything. "She has." "And you have answered her." "I have." Augusta nods, satisfied, and decants the lavender with a steady hand. "Good. Things said are things filed. Your Harrow told me that. A sensible man, for a schoolmaster.")*
> *(Then, lightly, so lightly Rose almost misses it: "The de Valcourts fell in those years, you know. The banking branch. My mother's people." She sets down the decanter. "I never inquired too closely into the falling. One doesn't, when the inquiry might lead —" she pauses, the dowager's pause, perfected over decades, "home. I know they fell. I do not know who held the door." She looks at Rose then, directly. "I find, at my age, that I prefer it so. Some shapes are better unexamined." And returns to the lavender, the subject closed like a stillroom drawer.)*

scenes.synopsis: the friend's verdict — Octavia hears the answer; precision, and affection.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia is in the morning room at five, drawing the rosemary in its jug with botanical patience. She listens to the whole of it — the shape, the comfort, the answer given aloud — without lifting the pencil. When Rose finishes, Octavia shades one leaf, considers, and says: "Well. That is the most expensive forgiveness this house has purchased, or the cheapest refusal, or the most sensible week's delay. Whichever you chose." The pencil stops. "You listened like an heiress. I am proud of you. Don't tell anyone I said so.")*
> *("She said she wasn't asking." "Nobody ever is," Octavia says, "when they come at ten o'clock in puce silk. The asking is the coming." She tears the rosemary sketch from the book and hands it to Rose. "Remembrance. For the day." Rose takes it — the quick sure lines, the sharp leaves. "You draw very fast battlefields." "This wasn't a battlefield," Octavia says. "This was a mending." She says it lightly. She means it entirely.)*

scenes.synopsis: the witness's view — Harrow hears the answer; the schoolmaster's arithmetic.
scenes.prose:
> *(Harrow is still at the library table at six, the papers in their rows, the lamp lit early against the November dark. He hears the day's account with the schoolmaster's stillness — no surprise, no judgment, the face with the scar attending like a good pupil. When she finishes he is quiet a moment, then: "She kept the shape for thirty years," he says. "That is a long keeping. Longer than mine." He looks at his own papers — twenty years of keeping, his family's ruin in a box. "I do not forgive the men who did it. There is no one to forgive; they are dead. But your aunt — she is alive, and she came to the door. That counts for something. In my arithmetic, it counts for a good deal.")*
> *(If she chose expose or atone, the account is public now, or being paid — she kept the shape of a thing that is ending. If she chose bury, the papers are gone, and she kept the shape of a thing I have helped bury again. He says it without bitterness — the witness, not the judge. "What did you answer her?" Rose tells him. He nods. "Filed where you can find it," he says. "Good. That is all forgiveness is. A good filing system." The schoolmaster's arithmetic of the heart, complete.)*

scenes.synopsis: tea, and the settling — the household absorbs the day; the servants' hall, satisfied.
scenes.prose:
> *(Tea at half past six in the morning room, and the household performs the evening with the same precision it performed the morning — but the precision is different now: relaxed, almost festive. The housekeeper brings the cake herself, a thing unheard of. The second footman pours without spilling. The under-housemaid replaces the rosemary with fresh rosemary, though the old was perfectly good. "The house," Octavia murmurs, accepting cake, "has decided the day went well. The house is never wrong about these things.")*
> *(Letitia does not come down for tea. This is understood by all, and approved: the aunt is resting, the day was large, the puce silk has earned its evening off. A tray goes up — the strong tea, the cake, a sprig of the fresh rosemary laid beside the plate like a garnish. Rose writes no note with it. Some things are better sent without words. The tray comes back empty, in time. The house notes this, too. The house notes everything, and is satisfied.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening dress — dressing for dinner after a confession; the household, faced.
scenes.prose:
> *("Dinner," Élise says at seven, "is a public occasion, and the public has had a day." She holds up the evening dress — the deep green silk, remade from the stored silks, the grandmother's emeralds waiting in their box. "Green," Rose says. "The garden's color." "The future's color," Élise corrects, fastening the emeralds with deft fingers. "Today you listened to the past. Tonight you dress as what comes after it. The household will be watching. Let them see the heir.")*
> *(In the glass: green silk, emeralds, the season's signature. Rose looks at the mended gloves on the dressing table — worn open at the choosing — takes them up, considers, and lays them down again. Bare hands. The confession was heard with bare hands; the dinner will be faced with them. "No gloves," she tells the glass. Élise nods, unsurprised. "No gloves," she agrees. "The hands, honest.")*

scenes.synopsis: dinner — the table's careful kindness; the household, performing wholeness.
scenes.prose:
> *(Dinner is a careful, kind performance, and everyone knows their part. The soup is excellent — the cook has outdone herself, sensing the occasion. Conversation stays in safe waters: the masons' progress, the lilies' taking, the seed catalogue's promises. Nobody mentions the morning. Nobody needs to. The household has absorbed the confession the way great houses absorb everything: thoroughly, silently, and with excellent soup.)*
> *(Rose sits at the head in the green silk, the emeralds catching the candlelight, and feels the table's attention like a warm weight — present, and kind, and hers. These are her people. The choosing, the confession, the mending: all of it has been witnessed by this room, and the room has not flinched. If she chose atone, the trust's signing is tomorrow's business; tonight the house simply eats. If she chose expose, Bell's printed truth sits folded in the library, and tonight no one mentions it. If she chose bury, the wall goes up again this week; tonight the talk is of other things. Tonight, the house simply eats.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE TOAST: dinner's end; Rose rises with her glass, and chooses what the evening drinks to.
scenes.prose:
> *(Dessert done, the candles low. The table has been careful and kind all evening, and now it waits — because the evenings of great days end with a toast, and the toast is the heir's to give. Rose rises in the green silk, the emeralds catching the last of the light, and lifts her glass. The room quiets. The giving of the toast is a choice: honor the people who held the week, name the absent aunt gently, or face the work still ahead. The glasses wait, raised. She chooses.)*
> *(She thinks of the day: the grey of listening, the mulberry of faithfulness, the answer given aloud in her aunt's room. She thinks of the empty chair — Letitia resting upstairs, the puce silk earned its evening off. She thinks of the mending baskets, waiting to be brought down. The toast, when it comes, will be one of three things, and the table will drink it standing.)*
> *(The toast is drunk — to the house, the absent, or the mending — and the table drinks it standing. The evening, sealed. The day, almost done.)*

options.label: To the household
options.detail: *Resolve+; the people, honored.* "To the house — which holds." The week's holders, named and thanked, the servants' hall and the family together. *(The house held the choosing; the house holds the confession.)*

options.label: To the absent
options.detail: *Mercy+; the aunt, named gently.* "To those not at the table — missed, and waited for." Letitia, named without naming the morning. *(The empty chair is honored, not explained.)*

options.label: To the mending
options.detail: *Candor+; the work, faced.* "To the mending — begun, not finished." The confession sewn into the cloth, the seams still to sew. *(Honest work, named as work.)*

scenes.synopsis: the younger son — Julian, glimpsed; the machinery, understood.
scenes.prose:
> *(After dinner, Julian finds her in the passage with the port still on him and the evening's ease loosened. "A day, then," he says. "The house has the smell of a day." He leans against the wainscot, uncharacteristically still. "I heard — the shape of it. Not the details." He smiles, crooked. "Nobody tells younger sons the details. We're the machinery, not the operators.")*
> *(Rose looks at him — the second son, the genteel poverty, the man who has made himself useful because there was nothing else to make. "The machinery that makes younger sons into instruments," she says slowly, "is the same machinery that made my grandfather into —" She stops. Julian nods. "Into a man who covered his own first. Yes. I've been thinking it all day." He straightens. "I don't want to be an instrument, Rose. Or an operator, particularly. I'd rather be the fellow who keeps the thing running. Less grand." He bows, and goes in to the port.)*

scenes.synopsis: the living's duty — Henry's hardest case; what is owed, and by whom.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry is in the library after dinner, the way he always is when the day has been large: with a book he is not reading. He closes it when Rose comes in. "Your aunt," he says. "Thirty years." He shakes his head. "The sin is old, Rose. The sinners are dead. The victims —" he gestures, the soldier's vague wave at the world's sorrow — "are owed. But by whom? By us? We didn't —" He stops, the honorable man confronting the limits of honor.)*
> *("By us," Rose says, "if we choose it. Not because we owe it — because the house stands on it." Henry looks at her a long moment. "That," he says, "is either the most moral thing you've ever said, or the most practical." "It is both," Rose says. "That is the trouble with this season. Everything is both." Henry laughs — the short surprised bark of a man whose world has tilted and settled. "Both," he agrees. "Very well. Both." He opens the book again. The hardest case, rested.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evening post — nothing from the hunters; the quiet, held.
scenes.prose:
> *(The evening post comes at nine, and Rose sorts it herself in the library — a habit from the choosing week, when every letter might have been a weapon. Bills. An invitation. The seed catalogue, again. Nothing in a woman's hand. Nothing from Pounce's sheet, nothing from Slade, nothing from the agents. The hunters are quiet. If she chose expose, Bell printed the true account; there is nothing left to hunt. If she chose bury, the papers are gone; there is nothing left to find. If she chose atone, the debt is confessed; there is nothing left to threaten with. Whatever the door, the quiet holds.)*
> *(She stands at the library window with the harmless post in her hand, looking out at the dark garden. Somewhere out there the wall is down or going up, the lilies are taking, the rosemary is remembering. The season's great question — what will you do before it's done for you — has been answered. She did it first. Whatever comes now, she chose the ground. The clock strikes nine. The house settles. The quiet, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the ritual — THE MENDING; the household mends, literally; the confession, sewn into the family's cloth.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: the confession, held. She holds the day the way she holds cloth: up to the light, the weave examined. The shape, known. The comfort, priced. The answer, given aloud. She holds it up to the light once more, then lets it down. The day, held.)*
> *(Story morsel: the mending. The household's hands: Élise's fine stitching, the servants' darning, the even rows. The torn things made whole, the worn things strengthened. The house mends the way it does everything: thoroughly, silently, and together. She watches the last of it, then turns away. The house, mending.)*
> *(Story morsel: the seam, chosen. Open, invisible, or new — the direction committed, worked into the cloth. The gold shows, or the match holds, or the fresh cut lies flat. The mending takes the shape she gave it. She sees it set, and nods. The seam, chosen.)*
> *(Story morsel: the forgiveness, sewn in. The answer, given aloud in the aunt's room — forgiven, withheld, or held for the week, whichever Rose chose. It is worked into the day's cloth now, a seam among seams. She feels it settle, and breathes. The answer, sewn.)*
> *(Story morsel: the house, mended. The lamps lit, the baskets put by, the seams holding. Thirty years of keeping, one day of telling, one evening of mending. The house stands mended. She stands in it a moment longer, then comes down. The evening, mended.)*

ritual.occasionBrief: The confession is given and answered. Tonight the household mends — literally: Letitia's table, the work-baskets brought down, the torn and worn things of a great house made whole again. Walk the mending's order. Mend, keep, remember. Exact. Patient. Unhurried. The house that mends does not hide the seam — unless it chooses to.

scenes.synopsis: the mending's aftermath — the house, quieter; the evening, settling.
scenes.prose:
> *(After the ritual, the house is quieter than Rose has ever known it — the good quiet, the mended quiet. The work-baskets are put by. The lamps are turned low. In the morning room, the rosemary jug stands among the folded linen like a small green flag. The housekeeper comes to ask if anything more is wanted, and there is nothing more wanted, and they both understand this to be a kind of benediction.)*
> *(Rose walks the hall once, and the green silk moves the way Élise cut it to move: without apology. She moves through the hall of her house — the heir of old sins, the woman who listened like an heiress and answered aloud — and the house moves around her, settled. Somewhere upstairs, Letitia sleeps. Or doesn't. Either way, the day is mended into the cloth. She goes up.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night dress — the white nightgown; the day, unmade gently.
scenes.prose:
> *(In her room, the maid has laid out the night things: the white cambric nightgown, the warm shawl, the slippers. Rose unpins the emeralds herself — they go back in the box with a small, final click — and steps out of the green silk, and stands a moment in her shift, the day's heiress unmade to the day's woman. The white cambric waits on the bed, plain as a confession.)*
> *(She puts it on — the cool cambric, the mother-of-pearl buttons, the hem that brushes the floor. In the glass: a woman in white, unadorned, the hair coming down, the face older than it was at ten o'clock. "Well," she says to the glass. "That was Tuesday." The glass, wisely, says nothing.)*

scenes.synopsis: the unsent letter — Rose writes to her grandfather, and does not send it.
scenes.prose:
> *(At the writing desk, by one lamp, Rose takes up a pen. To whom? Not Letitia; that was said aloud, as it should be. Not Octavia; she has the sketch. She finds herself writing to her grandfather, the clever certain man dead thirty years, the letter no one will ever read. "You covered Hartwell first," she writes. "I understand the arithmetic. I do not forgive the arithmetic. The house stands. The cost is being paid — in print, in pounds, or in silence, whichever door the week chose.")*
> *(She reads it over. It is a good letter — precise, unflinching, unfair in the way letters to the dead always are. She folds it, and for a moment holds it toward the lamp — then sets it down. Burning is for papers with power. This has no power; it is only words. She puts it in the desk's locked drawer, with the other unsent things. Some letters are written to be kept, not sent. The pen, laid down. The lamp, still burning.)*

scenes.synopsis: one lamp — Letitia's window; the house, asleep.
scenes.prose:
> *(She stands at her own window before putting out the lamp, and looks across the dark garden to the house's other wing. One window is lit: Letitia's. The aunt is awake — mending, probably; the woman mends when she cannot sleep, as she mends when she cannot think. Rose watches the small square of light for a long time. Thirty years of keeping, and tonight the keeper is awake with her thimble. It is not Rose's to fix. It is only hers to have heard.)*
> *(She puts out her lamp. The dark comes complete — the garden invisible, the wall's breach invisible, the whole great sin invisible under the November night. But she knows where they are now, all of them: the papers, the wall, the aunt, the answer. Known things are lighter than kept things. That is the day's whole lesson, if it has one — and it had better have one, for the price. She sleeps. Or begins to.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Bell prints a small true thing; the mending, noted.
scenes.prose: > *(THE MENDING. The Hartwell household, having had its say in these columns, spent Tuesday at the mending table. Work-baskets in the morning room; seams sewn, some in the open, by choice. This paper has reported many cures for an old sin (print, fire, and restitution among them), but it notes, with professional interest, a fourth: the needle. There is a kind of honesty, this paper finds, that takes a needle, and a kind of house that is not ashamed to use one.)*
scenes.sting: the sting — Bell prints a small true thing; the mending, noted.

scenes.synopsis: almost Wednesday — the house before dawn; the day, nearly done.
scenes.prose:
> *(She wakes before dawn — the house's hour, the hour when the letters come and the choices arrive. For a moment she doesn't know what day it is. Then: Tuesday. No — Wednesday, almost. The confession's day, done. She lies still in the white cambric and listens to the house: nothing. No step in the passage, no knock, no morning room set for ten. The quiet after mending.)*
> *(It comes to her, in the pre-dawn grey, that she is not afraid of Wednesday. Whatever it brings — the trust's signing, the wall's rebuilding, Bell's next edition, the hunters' next move — she has done the day's work. Listened like an heiress. Answered aloud. Mended the evening. The grey before dawn is the color of listening, and she has listened well. She rises. Wednesday can come.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dawn glass — Wednesday's dress, considered; the woman, and the week.
scenes.prose:
> *(The maid comes with the hot water, and Élise follows with the day's dress over her arm: Wednesday's dress, the slate-blue merino, practical, unadorned. "For whatever comes," Élise says. "The slate does not presume." Rose stands in the white cambric and considers it. After yesterday — the grey of listening, the mulberry of faithfulness, the green of the future, the white of the night — the slate-blue looks like a deep breath. Ordinary. Deliberate. Kind.)*
> *(In the glass, half-dressed: the woman who heard her aunt's confession and answered it aloud. She looks — herself. Not the heiress, not the judge, not the daughter: the woman, all three filed where she can find them. "It will do," she says of the dress. Élise, pinning: "It will do very well. Wednesdays are for doing." The slate-blue, the plain sash. The week, continued.)*

scenes.synopsis: the knock — Wednesday, arriving; the morning, ordinary.
scenes.prose:
> *(She is dressed — slate-blue, plain sash, the mended gloves on the table, today perhaps worn — when the knock comes. Not ten o'clock; half past seven. Too early for callers, too late for the post. Rose opens the door herself, because the house is still half-asleep and the knock was soft. The second footman stands there with a salver, and on the salver, a note. No seal. A gentleman's hand, French-taught.)*
> *(She knows the hand. Or thinks she does — the careful continental script from the choosing week. She takes the note but does not open it. Not yet. The morning is ordinary: the slate-blue, the hot water cooling, the house waking. Whatever the note says, it will keep until she has had her tea. She has learned, this week, that hurried things are usually the wrong things. The note waits on the salver. The tea, first.)*

scenes.synopsis: the tea, and the note — Wednesday morning; the reading, delayed properly.
scenes.prose:
> *(Tea in the morning room — the ordinary chair, the ordinary hour, the rosemary jug still standing among yesterday's folded linen. Rose drinks the first cup properly, the way Octavia taught her: no spending before the price is heard. The note lies beside the plate, unopened, the French-taught hand upward. The house goes on around her — the urn, the toast rack, Tuesday's mending put by. Everything ordinary. Everything about to change; or nothing. The note will say.)*
> *(She finishes the cup. She sets it down precisely in the saucer. And then — because there is no more morning to hide behind, and because hurried things are wrong but delayed things are merely cowardly — she picks up the note and breaks it open. Four lines. The continental script, careful. She reads it twice, the way she read her aunt's note yesterday. The toast goes cold.)*

scenes.synopsis: the cliffhanger — Laurent's note; he asks to be received; the week, turning.
scenes.prose:
> *("Mademoiselle — Forgive the hour. A matter has come to my knowledge that will not keep until the week's end, and it concerns us both. I ask to be received — at your hour, on your ground, alone if you permit it. — Laurent.")*
> *(She reads it twice. The de Varenne heir asks to be received — the asking urgent, the matter unnamed. The confession's week turns. Wednesday, arriving.)*

scenes.synopsis: the card arrives — Laurent's note, asking to call; Rose braces.
scenes.prose:
> *(The note comes with the morning post, in his hand, brief to the point of curtness: "May I call today? There are things I would rather say than write. — L." Rose reads it twice at the morning room window. Three days since the choosing. One since Letitia's confession emptied the air of the house like a storm. And now this: the French hand, the plain ask, the things rather said than written. She knows what the things are. Everyone in the house knows what the things are.)*
> *(She sends the boy back with the hour before she has quite decided to, which tells her she decided in the night. Eleven. The morning room. Then she stands a moment with the note in her hand, and does the thing she does before reckonings: checks the gloves, the cuffs, the face in the glass over the mantel. Not vanity. Inventory. Whatever walks through the door at eleven, it will find her braced — which is to say, found. She folds the note once and puts it in the drawer with the others. The card, received. The bracing, done.)*

scenes.synopsis: dressing for Laurent — nothing that pleads, nothing that hides; the day's armor, chosen.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia takes one look at the note and goes to the wardrobe with the air of a general inspecting ordnance. "Not the rose," she says. "Not white. Nothing that pleads and nothing that apologizes." She lays out the Hartwell blue: a morning gown, plain to the point of severity, cut beautifully, the color of the estate's roofs against a winter sky. With it, no pearls — the plain band at the throat, the silver rose pin at the shoulder. "Blue," Letitia says, "is a color that has never begged for anything.")*
> *(Rose dresses, and the blue does its work: steady, unadorned, the house's color worn by the house's mistress on the house's business. The mended gloves last. In the glass she looks like what the day requires: a woman meeting a reckoning she did not cause and will not evade. "If he wants pleading," she says, flexing the mended thumb, "he'll have to bring his own." Letitia nods, once, the quartermaster approving the uniform. The blue, worn. The pleading, declined in advance.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE MEETING: receive him at once, walk the grounds, or write first; the devastation, staged.
scenes.prose:
> *(Eleven o'clock, and the devastation has to happen somewhere. Three stagings offer themselves. Receive him at once: the morning room, within the hour, no preparation as preparation. Candor's staging: the door opened, the thing faced head-on, whatever falls out of his mouth landing where it lands. Ask him to walk the grounds: the park, the long way round by the lake, somewhere the walls don't listen and a man can stop walking when the words stop coming. Mercy's staging: air and movement, the reckoning taken at a walk. Write first, meet after: a letter before eleven, with the worst of it on paper, so the face-to-face is for what's left. Resolve's staging: controlled, deliberate. Paper can't be interrupted, but it can't answer either.)*
> *(She stands at the window with his note in the drawer and the blue gown doing its steady work, and thinks of Octavia: a proud man needs ground under him. Of Letitia: don't manage him, miss. Of herself: the unflinching, performed or real. The staging, chosen, becomes the morning's shape.)*
> *(The devastation, staged her way: at once, at a walk, or after the letter. The drawer closed on his note. Whatever eleven o'clock brought, it would find the ground prepared.)*

options.label: Receive him at once
options.detail: *Candor+; the door, opened.* The morning room, within the hour; no staging, no delay, the thing faced head-on. *(Immediate and bare; he comes unready, and so does she — candor cuts both ways.)*

options.label: Ask him to walk the grounds
options.detail: *Mercy+; the air, offered.* The park, the long way by the lake; walls don't listen out of doors. *(Kinder and slower; walking is easier than facing, and stopping is allowed.)*

options.label: Write first, meet after
options.detail: *Resolve+; the page, first.* A letter with the worst in it before eleven; the meeting for what's left. *(Controlled and deliberate; paper can't be interrupted — but it can't answer, either.)*

scenes.synopsis: the devastation — Laurent arrives; what it means, said aloud.
scenes.prose:
> *(He comes as she asked: to the morning room within the hour, or by the garden door for the walk, or with her letter already read and folded in his pocket. The staging hardly matters once he's in the room. He looks as though he hasn't slept, which he hasn't, and the black coat is on, and the devastation is not fury anymore. The fury burned off days ago. What remains is something hollower, the look of a man doing arithmetic he doesn't want to finish. "Your grandfather," he says, without sitting, "ruined my family. I have known the shape of it since spring. This week I have learned the sums." He stops. "I am trying to find the part of this where I am not angry at you, and I cannot find it yet.")*
> *("Then be angry," Rose says. "It's honest, and it's yours." She doesn't defend the grandfather. There is no defense, and they both know it. "Ask me what you need to ask. I won't manage you, Laurent. Not today." He looks at her: the blue gown, the mended glove, the woman who is the heir of his family's ruiners and also, inconveniently, the woman he was learning to love. "Did you know," he says slowly, "when you — in the spring, when we —" "No," she says. "I learned it the way you did. From the papers. There was no version of this where I knew first and didn't tell you." He nods, once, and sits at last, and the devastation sits with him, unhidden, unhurried. The thing, said. The anger, owned.)*

scenes.synopsis: his face, kept — after he goes; what devastation looks like on him.
scenes.prose:
> *(He stays an hour and then goes to walk, he says, alone, and Rose sits in the morning room with his face kept the way she keeps figures: exactly. The sleeplessness under the eyes. The mouth, thinner. The moment he said "I cannot find it yet," and meant it as a courtesy, and it landed as a wound. She has seen Laurent furious, amused, charming, bored. She has never seen him hollow. Hollow, it turns out, is worse than all of them, because there is nothing to answer: no accusation to meet, no blow to parry, just a man doing sums that come out wrong no matter how he does them.)*
> *(She touches the mended glove, the thumb's small scar. There is nothing to mend here. That is the whole of it, and it sits in her like a stone: some things can't be stitched, only carried. He is carrying his. She will carry hers. Whether they carry them together is the week's question, and it is his to answer, and all she can do — all she has done — is lay the ground straight and refuse to plead. She gets up, finally, and goes to find Octavia. The face, kept. The stone, carried.)*

scenes.synopsis: Octavia on pride — what staying costs a proud man; the friend's counsel.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia listens to the whole of it without interrupting, which for Octavia is practically an embrace, and then says: "He'll either stay or he won't, and you can't price it in advance." She pours the tea herself, a thing she never does. "But understand what staying would cost him, Rose. Not the money — the money is arithmetic. The pride. A Frenchman, an émigré's son, raised on the story of what was taken: to stay with the house that took it requires him to set down the best story he has about himself. That's not a small thing. That's the whole of his inheritance, set down like a coat.")*
> *("Set down, not spent," Rose says. "Pride set down can be picked up again. Spent is spent." Octavia looks at her over the cup. "Just so. And that is why you mustn't ask him to spend it — no speeches about forgiveness, no scenes. If he stays, he stays the way a man sets down a coat: deliberately, and able to take it up again. That is the only staying that lasts." She sets down the cup. "And Rose — if he goes, it won't be cruelty. It will be arithmetic he couldn't finish. Don't make it a tragedy. Make it a sum." The counsel, given. The pride, priced.)*

scenes.synopsis: the losses, acknowledged — the de Varenne name in the reckoning; told per the door she chose.
scenes.prose:
> *(At noon she does the thing the week has been building toward: she acknowledges the de Varenne losses to Laurent himself, in the terms of the door she chose. If she chose atone: Octavia's ledger, open on the morning room desk, the de Varenne page first among the creditors. The column, the years, the sums, named and dated; the trust's founding names them, and the canal's three thousand a year (£3,000) will find them. If she chose expose: the Gazette's printed account, the week's issue on the desk — his mother's name in every sheet in England, the losses told truly and publicly. And beside it, honestly: the thirty-eight thousand eight hundred (£38,800), acknowledged and unspent, because exposure is not payment, and she will not pretend otherwise. If she chose bury: no page, no printing, the papers burned Sunday night. She tells him from memory, alone, what was on the de Varenne page: the losses, the names, the sums. The proof is gone. The acknowledgment is his, private and entire.)*
> *(He listens the way he listened at eleven, completely, without moving, and when she finishes he is quiet a long time. "You told me," he says at last. "However you told it, the trust, the printing, the memory, you told me. Nobody else's family told mine anything." He touches the ledger's edge, or the Gazette's, or nothing at all. "That counts. I don't know yet what it counts for, but it counts." The losses, acknowledged. The telling, received.)*

scenes.synopsis: midday — steady dress for the afternoon; the woman, held upright.
scenes.prose:
> *(Before luncheon she goes up to change out of the morning's blue. Not because the blue failed, but because the morning is over and the afternoon is a different country. The midday dress is steadier still: a plain grey-blue, high-necked, the silver rose pin moved to the shoulder, the mended gloves. No ornament. The afternoon holds Julian, Augusta, Henry — three separate reckonings, none of them hers to manage — and she will meet them upright, unadorned, the woman the morning made.)*
> *(In the glass the change is small and total: morning's armor becomes afternoon's uniform. She thinks of Laurent's hollow face, Octavia's coat set down, the de Varenne page with its column of losses. The day is half done and the hardest of it — the staying or going — is still ahead, walking the grounds somewhere with her name in his mouth. She pins the dried violet at her wrist. Faithfulness. The flower doesn't plead either. The midday, steadied. The woman, upright.)*

scenes.synopsis: Julian's truth — genteel poverty seen new; the machinery that makes younger sons into instruments.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian comes at one, unannounced, which for Julian is practically a confession, and he has the look of a man who has been thinking all night and dislikes the conclusions. "I've been thinking about younger sons," he says, without preamble. Rose gestures to the chair. "My family's poverty," he says, "was always genteel. A good name, a mortgaged estate, a younger son with no fortune and good manners. I thought it was — weather. Something that happened." He looks at her. "This week I've understood it was machinery. Men with money and secrets need men with names and debts. That's what a younger son is for. That's what I've been for.")*
> *("Bell's informant," Rose says quietly. It isn't a question. "Among other uses," Julian says. "Blackmailed first, then — habituated. You get used to being useful." He turns the hat in his hands. "Your grandfather's generation built the machine. My generation oils it. I wanted you to know that I know." A pause. "It doesn't change anything. I only wanted it said." She looks at him: the charm, the debts, the sudden clarity, all sitting together in the afternoon light. "Said," she agrees. "And heard." He nods, and goes, lighter by exactly one truth. The machinery, named. The instrument, aware.)*

scenes.synopsis: afternoon — archive lace with Augusta; the dowager's eye on the day's dressing.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta comes at two to oversee the afternoon's lace, because Augusta oversees everything eventually. The archive lace is the grandmother's — ivory, forty years old, kept in tissue — and Augusta examines it the way she examines everything: for weakness. "It holds," she pronounces. "Lace either holds or it doesn't, like families." The fichu is pinned at Rose's throat, the lace cuffs turned back. In the glass: the grey-blue steadied, the ivory softening it, the dowager's approval like a seal.)*
> *("The de Valcourt branch," Augusta says, pinning, "lost less than the de Varennes. We were bankers. We understood speculation." A pause, the pin going in. "I knew the branch fell. I did not know your grandfather finished it." She steps back. "That is the whole of my admission, and you may have it once." Rose meets her eyes in the glass. "Kept," she says. "And lightly, as agreed." "Lightly," Augusta agrees. The lace, placed. The admission, made. The afternoon, dressed.)*

scenes.synopsis: Henry's honor — the sin old, the sinners dead, the victims owed; duty, defined.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry comes at three, and he has the air of a man delivering a report he has checked twice. "I've been thinking about duty," he says. "The sin is old. The sinners are dead. The victims are owed — some of them." He ticks them on his fingers. "Harrow: owed wages, a roof. The de Varennes: owed acknowledgment, and money if the door you chose includes money. The de Valcourts: owed the light touch your grandmother negotiated." He looks at her. "Here's the hard part, Rose. Duty to the dead is sentiment. Duty to the living is arithmetic. You can't punish your grandfather. You can only pay Harrow.")*
> *("That's what I've done," she says. "Or begun, or printed, or burned — per the door." "I know," Henry says. "That's why I'm here. To say that whatever door, the duty going forward is the same: the living, kept. Harrow's keeping. The trust's payments. The names, spoken correctly." He stands. "Honor," he says, "isn't about the old sin. It's about the next ten years of Tuesdays." He touches his hat. "The sinners are dead, Rose. Be good to the living. That's the whole of it." The honor, defined. The duty, forward.)*

scenes.synopsis: the walk — the grounds, the long way; the conversation, continued on foot.
scenes.prose:
> *(He is waiting at the garden door at four, as if the morning's devastation had an afternoon appointment, and they walk the long way round by the lake without discussing it. The park is at its plainest and best: rooks in the elms, the water flat, the path soft underfoot. For a while they don't talk. Then Laurent says: "My mother used to say the de Varennes were unlucky. Not ruined — unlucky. As if it were weather." He looks at the lake. "It wasn't weather. It was your grandfather's ledger. I keep trying to make it weather again, because weather I could forgive.")*
> *("Ledgers," Rose says, "are harder than weather. I know." They walk. "Tell me about her," she says. "Your mother." And he does — small things, concrete: her hands, her French, the way she counted linen. The émigré's son, walking an English park, remembering a Frenchwoman in the particular. Rose listens, and the walk does what Octavia said walks do: the words come easier with ground under them. "Thank you," he says at the lake's far end. "For asking." "Thank you," she says, "for telling." The conversation, walked. The mother, remembered.)*

scenes.synopsis: pride, considered — his and hers; what set down looks like from inside.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone after the walk, she considers pride the way Octavia taught her to consider sums: precisely, without flinching. His pride: French, émigré, inherited, the coat he wears even indoors. Set down, not spent. He can take it up again, which is what makes the setting-down brave rather than broken. Her pride: Hartwell, English, newer, the pride of the woman who chose the door and walked through it. Hers doesn't need setting down. Hers needs holding steady while his is on the ground, which is harder in its way. It is easy to kneel beside a man, and kneeling is not what he needs.)*
> *(What he needs, she thinks, is for her not to flinch when he picks the coat up again — because he will, pride like that always gets picked up — and not to pretend the ground was never bare. She stands at the window and watches the rooks. Pride, considered. The coat, on the ground. Her job: the steady ground beside it, neither kneeling nor stepping back. She can do that. She has been practicing all season without knowing it was practice.)*

scenes.synopsis: Élise on the village's romances — ordinary love, unruined; the flower-seller's wisdom.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at five with the evening's flowers and the village's news, and the news today is romances: Mrs. Pike's girl walking out with the carrier's boy, the blacksmith's apprentice courting the dairymaid, old Mrs. Pike herself receiving a widower's attentions with great dignity. "No ledgers in it," Élise says, arranging. "The carrier's boy has sixpence and a good heart. The girl has ribbons and opinions. It will do." She looks up. "The village manages love without paperwork, miss. It's one of its talents.")*
> *("And the Comte?" Élise asks, gently. "The village says he's been walking the lake path like a man looking for something he dropped." Rose smiles despite everything. "He dropped a story," she says. "The one about his family. He's looking for what to pick up instead." Élise considers this, the flower-seller's face serious. "Tell him," she says, "that the carrier's boy didn't have a story either. He just had sixpence and showed up." She hands Rose the dried violets. "Showing up, miss. It's underrated." The wisdom, delivered. The romances, reported.)*

scenes.synopsis: Letitia on love and ruin — the aunt, after her confession; comic no longer, funny anyway.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia finds her before dinner, and the confession of two days ago sits between them the way furniture sits in a room: present, unmoved-around. "I loved him, you know," Letitia says abruptly. "Your grandfather. Not wisely. He was charming the way a bad winter is charming. You admire it and it kills your livestock." She smooths her skirt. "I knew the shape of what he'd done. Not the sums, the shape. And I kept the family's peace and called it love, and my comfort was the price." A pause. "I've been practicing that sentence for thirty years. It didn't improve with rehearsal.")*
> *("Aunt," Rose says. "Don't," Letitia says. "No absolution before dinner; it gives me indigestion." But she takes Rose's hand, briefly, the quartermaster's hand, dry and warm. "You did what I didn't, miss. You opened the thing. Whatever door." She stops. "This door." She lets go. "Now go and dress for dinner. Two houses, one table. And Rose." The old glint, back for a second. "Don't wear anything that pleads. You never could carry it off." The love, owned. The ruin, named. The aunt, herself again, almost.)*

scenes.synopsis: dinner — two houses, one table; dressing for the de Varennes and the Hartwells at once.
scenes.prose:
> *(She dresses for dinner with the two houses in mind: the de Varennes, ruined by hers; the Hartwells, doing the reckoning. The gown is the deep blue, evening-cut, with the grandmother's archive lace at the throat — Hartwell's color, the archive's trimming, both houses in the wearing. The pearls, the plain band, the mended gloves. In the glass: a woman dressed for a table where the past is a guest. Letitia, fastening the pearls, says: "Two houses." "One table," Rose answers. "The table," Letitia says, "is the whole of civilization. Remember that if the soup is awkward.")*
> *(The soup will not be awkward; the household will see to that. But the dressing is the point: she will sit at the head of her table in the color of her house with her grandmother's lace at her throat, and across from her will sit the heir of the family her grandfather ruined, and the gown will say what she won't. Both houses, honored; neither, pleaded to. She touches the dried violet at her wrist. Faithfulness — to the people, not the secret. The dinner, dressed. The table, set.)*

fashionChoices.detail: Hartwell's color, the archive's trimming; both houses, worn.

fashionChoices.label: The rose, restrained
fashionChoices.detail: the choosing's gown, quieted; the door, inhabited softly.

fashionChoices.detail: the quartermaster sets the cloth and the gown.

scenes.synopsis: what he asks — before dinner; the request, plain.
scenes.prose:
> *(He comes early, before the household gathers, and asks the thing she has been waiting for him to ask since eleven. "Show me," he says. "The de Varenne page. The exact losses. All of it." He stands very straight. "I don't want to discover it later — in a sheet, in a conversation, in my own memory improving with age. Whatever my family lost, I want it from you, now, in figures." It is the bravest ask of the day: no more surprises, no protected places. The whole of the ruin, handed over, so there is nothing left to find.)*
> *(She takes him to the morning room and opens Octavia's ledger to the marked page, or lays the Gazette's printing before him, or speaks from the burned papers' memory, per the door, and he reads, or listens, without moving. The column. The years. The names. When he finishes he is quiet, and then he says: "Thank you." Not for the losses. For the showing. "There," he says. "Now I know the worst of it, and the worst of it is —" he stops, finds the word "— accounting. I expected a tragedy. It's bookkeeping." She almost laughs. "The worst things," she says, "usually are." The asking, answered. The worst, known.)*

scenes.synopsis: dinner, the two of them — before the household; the table, set for two houses.
scenes.prose:
> *(They go in to dinner before the others, by design — Letitia's design, which means it was Rose's design three hours earlier — and for the first minutes the table is just the two of them, the candles, the soup. "Two houses," Laurent says, looking at the blue and the lace. "One table," Rose says. He smiles, the first real one of the day, and it changes his face the way sun changes a room. "Your aunt," he says, "is a general." "My aunt," Rose agrees, "is several generals.")*
> *(The soup is excellent, the conversation careful and then less careful. He tells her about the walk: what he thought about, which was mostly his mother and partly the rooks. She tells him about Henry's ten years of Tuesdays. "Your friends," he says, "are formidable." "They're yours too," she says, "if you stay." It hangs there, the word, unpressed. He doesn't answer it, not yet, but he doesn't look away either, and the candles do their work, and the second course comes, and the household begins to gather, kindly, at the edges. The dinner, begun. The word, unpressed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the household at dinner — kindly watched; the family, holding the evening.
scenes.prose:
> *(The household gathers by the second course, and the gathering is the kindest thing in the chapter: nobody stares, nobody performs, everybody simply — eats. Letitia carves with generalship. Octavia talks about the canal's levels as if they were the most interesting thing in England. Augusta is brief and dry and, once, almost warm. Harrow, invited for the first time to the family table, is quiet and upright and visibly moved by the soup. The kindness is in the not-looking: the whole table collaborating, without a word said, to let the two at the head have an ordinary evening in the middle of an extraordinary week.)*
> *(Rose watches it happen with the full heart she never shows: Letitia refilling Laurent's glass without being asked; Octavia catching her eye over the candles, steady; Augusta, at the pudding, saying to Laurent, "The de Valcourts were bankers, young man. We understand compound interest," which gets the first laugh of the evening from him — surprised out of him like a bird. The household, holding the evening the way it holds everything: together, unflinching, kind. The watching, kindly. The evening, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE OFFERING: what she lays before him; the reckoning, offered.
scenes.prose:
> *(After dinner, the household tactfully evaporating the way households do, the offering waits to be made. Three layings-before offer themselves. The full accounting, in writing: Octavia's ledger, the de Varenne page, every figure, or the Gazette's printed account, or her own hand's reconstruction from the burned papers' memory, per the door. Nothing softened, nothing summarized. Candor's offering: the whole of it, on paper, his to keep. Time, without pressure: no offering tonight at all. The space to decide what he needs, unhurried, unobserved. Mercy's offering: the clock, refused again, this time for his sake. A place in the reckoning: the garden, the trust. Not payment but partnership. His family's name in the walled garden's founding, a share in what the reckoning builds. Resolve's offering: generous, and binding. A place can't be un-offered.)*
> *(She stands in the morning room with the ledger, or the printing, or the memory, per the door, and thinks of Élise: showing up, underrated. Of Octavia: set down, not spent. The offering is the showing-up, whatever form it takes. If she chose expose, she lays beside the account the harder truth: the thirty-eight thousand eight hundred (£38,800), acknowledged and unspent. Exposure was not payment, and she will not dress it as atonement. The offering, chosen, becomes the evening's shape.)*
> *(The reckoning, offered her way: the page, the time, or the place. The morning room quiet around the choice. Whatever eleven o'clock's devastation began, the evening would finish honestly.)*

scenes.synopsis: his answer — he stays; the word, given plainly.
scenes.prose:
> *(She makes the offering as she chose — the page, the time, or the place — and he receives it completely, without moving. Then he is quiet, and the quiet is the long one, the one with the whole week in it: the hollow morning, the ledger's column, the walk, his mother's hands counting linen, the dinner with two houses at one table. Rose doesn't fill it. Octavia's counsel holds: no speeches, no scenes. Just the morning room, the candles burned low, and the man deciding.)*
> *("I stay," he says at last. Plain. French. No speech around it. "My family was ruined by ledgers. I won't be ruined by one." He looks at her. "You told me everything. Nobody told my mother anything. That counts." A pause. "Also —" the ghost of the old charm, "— the soup was excellent, and your aunt refilled my glass without being asked. A man doesn't leave a house like that." She laughs, sudden and helpless, and the laugh breaks the week's tension like a wave. He stays. The word, given. The answer, plain.)*

scenes.synopsis: the bravest thing — staying, named; pride set down, not spent.
scenes.prose:
> *("Do you know what you've done?" Rose asks, when the laugh has passed. He raises an eyebrow. "Stayed for soup?" "Set down the best story you had about yourself," she says. "The émigré's son, the ruined house, the English ledger. You set it down like a coat." He considers this. "It was a good story," he admits. "It explained everything. Without it I'm just —" he gestures, "— a man. With a mother who counted linen." "A man," Rose says, "is harder than a story. Stories don't have to decide anything.")*
> *(He nods slowly. "In my family," he says, "pride was the furniture. You didn't sit on it, you polished it." A beat. "I would like to sit down." She takes his hand — the first time today she has touched him, and the touch is the whole conversation: the mended glove against his palm, the scar deliberate. "Then sit," she says. "The chair's yours. It was always going to be yours; you just had to stop polishing it first." He holds her hand, and the bravest thing he has ever done sits quietly in the morning room, wearing a black coat, holding a mended glove. The staying, named. The pride, set down.)*

scenes.synopsis: the center, held — alone, after; the romantic center, accounted.
scenes.prose:
> *(He goes at last, to his lodgings or to walk, unwilling to end the day by ending it, and Rose sits alone in the morning room with the center held the way she holds figures: exactly, and with relief she doesn't examine. The season's romantic center. All spring she has been the heiress, the strategist, the woman with the ledger; tonight she was something simpler and harder: the woman he stayed for. Not the house. Not the money. God knows the money is the problem. Her. The telling, the showing up, the unpleading blue.)*
> *(She touches the dried violet at her wrist. Faithfulness. It has meant the household, the witness, the village, the friends, all season. Tonight it means one more thing, private: the man who set down his best story and stayed for soup. She doesn't make a ledger of it — Octavia would, but Rose won't; some columns don't take figures. She blows out the candles one by one. The center, held. The relief, unexamined. The night, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: evening — de Valcourt colors, quietly; Augusta's branch's colors, worn without announcement.
scenes.prose:
> *(Before the evening's end she changes once more — not for company, for the gesture. The de Valcourt colors: Augusta's colors, lent for the evening without a word said, a sash and a pin in the French family's shade. She wears them quietly, under no announcement: the émigré and the English house, the evening's private heraldry. In the glass the effect is small and total — the blue gown, the foreign sash, the woman who is both houses' heir and neither house's apologist.)*
> *(It isn't pleading. Pleading was declined at eleven this morning. It is acknowledgment, worn where only she and the glass will read it properly: his mother's family, her grandmother's family, the banking branch that fell — remembered in silk. She touches the pin. Tomorrow there will be gardens to prepare and invitations to write and a house to rest. Tonight there is only this: the colors, quietly worn, for the man who stayed. The evening, colored. The gesture, unannounced.)*

scenes.synopsis: Octavia's summary — the evening, read; the season in miniature.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia finds her at the sash-pinning stage and reads the whole evening in one look. "The de Valcourt colors," she says. "Quietly. Good." She sits, uninvited, the friend's prerogative. "That," she says, "was the whole season, in one evening. The devastation at eleven. The walk at four. The dinner with two houses. The staying." She ticks them on her fingers. "Walled things, opened. Old sins, faced. A Frenchman, unruined by a ledger. If I were Bell I'd set it in type." She looks at Rose. "How does it feel, to have the season's center hold?")*
> *("Like relief," Rose says honestly. "And like the part of the ledger I can't add up." "Don't," Octavia advises. "Some things are true without being accountable. That's not a failure of arithmetic, it's —" she stops herself. "It's late, and I'm moralizing. Your rule." Rose laughs. "My rule." They sit together, the precise friend and the held center, and the evening ticks on, accounted and unaccountable both. The summary, given. The season, miniaturized.)*

scenes.synopsis: Augusta's blessing — dry; the dowager, decided.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta comes at nine, brief as always, and comes to the point the way she comes to everything: directly, and as if the point were obvious. "The young man stays," she says. "I observed him at dinner. He has his mother's eyes and his father's manners, which is the right way round." She studies Rose: the blue, the sash, the evening's quiet heraldry. "The de Valcourts were bankers, Rose. We understand compound interest, on money and on injury. What your grandfather did to that branch compounded for thirty years. What you did this week —" a pause "— was a payment on the interest. Not the principal. The principal is beyond paying. But interest payments are noticed.")*
> *("Is that a blessing?" Rose asks. "It is an observation," Augusta says. "With favorable implications." The smallest smile. "He'll do. The French are dramatic, but they endure. We Valcourts know." She turns to go, then stops. "The sash suits you. Keep it till morning." The blessing, given dry. The dowager, decided. The colors, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: Harrow, watching — the witness's view of the young comte; dry wisdom.
scenes.prose:
> *(Harrow is in the hall when she comes down, putting on his coat after the dinner — the first family dinner of his sixty-one years, and he wears the occasion carefully, the way a man carries a key newly cut for his own door. "Miss Hartwell," he says. "A word, if the evening can spare one." They stand by the stairs. "I've been watching the young Comte," he says. "All evening. Professional interest — I spent twenty years watching people carry papers they didn't want to open." A pause. "He opened his. That's rarer than you'd think.")*
> *("He stayed," Rose says. "I know," Harrow says. "I watched him decide. It took him the whole dinner — I could see it happening behind the soup." The dryness, intact. "Miss Hartwell, the same fall that made me a schoolmaster made him an émigré's son with a story. Stories are heavy. He set his down tonight." He touches his hat. "Sixty-one years old, and I'm at a dinner watching a young man do in an evening what took me twenty years. The young," he says, "are efficient." The witness, watching. The wisdom, dry.)*

scenes.synopsis: Letitia's real smile — the aunt, unguarded; the day's gift.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia is in the morning room, extinguishing candles with the care of a woman putting a day to bed, when Rose comes in. "Well," Letitia says. "He stays." "He stays," Rose agrees. And then Letitia smiles — really smiles, not the quartermaster's approving nod, not the dry glint, but the real thing, unguarded, thirty years younger. "Your mother," she says, "would have liked him. She liked the French — said they argued better." The smile stays. "She'd have liked today, too. The devastation at eleven and the soup at seven. She always said a reckoning should be followed by a good dinner.")*
> *(Rose stares. "Aunt —" "Don't make a fuss," Letitia says, but the smile doesn't go. "It's been a week of confessions and ledgers. A woman is allowed one smile." She finishes the candles. "Go to bed, miss. Tomorrow's the garden, or the invitations, or the rest — your choosing." At the door she turns, the smile still there, smaller now, kept. "Stitch by stitch," she says. "Even this." The smile, real. The day's gift, given.)*

scenes.synopsis: the day, kept — like a promise; the hours, accounted.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone at last, she keeps the day the way she keeps everything that matters: deliberately, in order. Eleven: the note, the blue, the devastation. Noon: the de Varenne page, acknowledged per the door. One: Julian and the machinery. Two: Augusta's lace. Three: Henry's Tuesdays. Four: the walk, his mother's hands. Five: Élise and sixpence. Six: Letitia and the bad winter. Seven: two houses, one table. Nine: the staying, the coat set down. Ten: the real smile. She runs the hours like beads, and every bead holds.)*
> *(Kept, as in kept safe. Kept, as in kept promised. The day asked everything of her — the bracing, the telling, the unpleading — and she gave it, and the giving held. She touches the de Valcourt sash, Augusta's lending, kept till morning. Tomorrow: the garden, the invitations, the rest. Tonight: the day, kept, bead by bead, in the order it happened. She unpins her hair. The hours, accounted. The promise, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the welcome ritual — white lilies for the rooms he will see; purity of intent, no pleading.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the baskets — "lilies, miss. Not roses. Roses plead. Lilies don't.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, with a stem — "purity of intent. The flower means what you meant today.")*
> *(Story morsel: Élise, arranging — "he'll see them in the morning, miss. Flowers first, before the talking.")*
> *(Story morsel: Harrow, at the door — come up from the village, a lily for his own mantel.)*
> *(Story morsel: Rose, at the stair — "purity of intent. That's the whole doctrine, and it's enough.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: The dinner is eaten, the answer given, the center held. Tonight the house prepares its welcome for the morrow: white lilies for every room Laurent will see — purity of intent, arranged without pleading. Dress for the arranging: the welcome's face, chosen once and worn through the placing. Precise. Honest. Unafraid. The house that welcomes honestly does not plead.

scenes.synopsis: the last lily — placed by her own hand; the welcome, finished.
scenes.prose:
> *(After the ritual she walks the rooms once more, alone, and finds one mantel the household missed — or left for her, which amounts to the same thing. She takes the last lily from the basket and places it herself: the stem in water, the bloom turned to the door Laurent will come through. White lilies. Purity of intent. Not apology, not pleading. The white of a thing meant exactly as it looks. She steps back. The room holds the flower the way the day held everything: precisely.)*
> *(She stands a moment in the flowered quiet. Every room ready. Every lily placed. The house, welcoming honestly. Tomorrow he will walk through these rooms and see them before any talking starts — Élise was right about that; flowers first. She touches the last lily's petal, briefly, the way she touches the dried violet at her wrist. Faithfulness, and purity of intent: the season's two flowers, side by side at last. The welcome, finished. The hand, her own.)*

scenes.synopsis: the quiet hour — the memorandum book; the day, entered.
scenes.prose:
> *(In the study she opens the memorandum book and enters the day the way Quill enters figures: plainly, in order. Wednesday. Laurent, eleven. The devastation, faced. The de Varenne page, acknowledged per the door. Julian, the machinery. Augusta, the lace. Henry, the Tuesdays. The walk. Élise, sixpence. Letitia, the winter. Dinner, two houses. The offering, made. The answer: he stays. The lilies, placed. She writes it all in the neat hand her grandmother taught her, and the book takes the day without comment, the way books do.)*
> *(She closes the book and sits a moment in the study's quiet. The memorandum book holds the Lash, the draft, Bell's fittings, the trust's papers — the whole season's archive, in her hand. Tomorrow's entry is unwritten: the garden, the invitations, or the rest. She doesn't write it yet. Some entries need the choosing first. She puts the pen down. The day, entered. The morrow, unchosen.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE MORROW: the garden, the invitations, or rest; tomorrow, shaped.
scenes.prose:
> *(Night. The lilies are placed, the book is entered, and tomorrow waits to be shaped. Three morrows offer themselves. Prepare the garden: the walled garden, ordered and made ready. The paths, the beds, the breach's last traces, for whatever the reckoning builds next. Resolve's morrow: work, not words. The garden won't argue, and there's a trust to found or a printing to follow or a wall to tend, per the door. Write the invitations: plain letters to the town. What happened this week, what comes next, in her own hand before the gossip's version sets. Candor's morrow: honest, and exposed. The town reads everything twice, and the second reading is never kinder. Rest the house a day: no reckoning tomorrow, no callers, no ledgers. The household breathes; the lilies are admired; Laurent's answer settles. Mercy's morrow: kind, and risky. Rest can look like retreat, and the hunters are still spending.)*
> *(She stands at the study window with the pen still warm from the day's entry, and thinks of Letitia: tomorrow's the garden, the invitations, or the rest — your choosing. Of the lilies, waiting overnight. Of Laurent, asleep or walking, with the coat set down. The morrow, chosen, becomes the week's next shape.)*
> *(Tomorrow, shaped her way: the garden, the letters, or the rest. The pen, taken up again. Whatever the hunters spent tonight, it would be spent against a house that had chosen its morrow.)*

options.label: Write the invitations

options.label: Rest the house a day
