scenes.synopsis: Quill's paper — a draft, a sum; the law, keeping pace.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill comes at ten with his leather case and the week's paper, such as the door allows. If she chose atone: the trust's enrolled draft, engrossed and ready, and the sum: eight thousand eight hundred (£8,800) moved from the surplus, Harrow's hundred and fifty (£150) ordered, the keeping deeded, the canal's three thousand a year committed in writing. If she chose expose: the draft of the family's public account as the law reads it — what the Gazette's printing means for claims, for creditors, for the town, and the sum: thirty-eight thousand eight hundred (£38,800), confessed in print, unspent, still owed. Exposure was not payment, and the law keeps the ledger open. If she chose bury: the mason's final receipt for the rebuilt wall, third course and all, the breach closed, and the week's account: what the silence cost in money, which was little, and what it left untouched, which was everything.)*
> *(She signs, or files, or pays, per the door, and Quill packs the case with the solicitor's finality. "The law," he says, "keeps pace, Miss Hartwell. Slowly, but it keeps." He touches his hat. "Whatever the door, the paper is in order." He goes into the night with the week's reckoning under his arm. The draft, handled. The sum, stated. The law, paced.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Bell's draft: "ON LOVE AND LEDGERS."
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting arrives with the evening post, in Bell's own hand, marked for Rose's eyes: the proprietor's new draft, and the headline set in type: "ON LOVE AND LEDGERS." Three paragraphs, and not a blade in them — or rather, the blade sheathed, which for Bell is the more startling. They describe, without naming, a young Frenchman who learned this week what an English ledger cost his family, and an Englishwoman who laid the ledger open rather than let him find it shut. The last line is the tenderest thing Bell has ever set in type: "The Gazette notes that some debts are paid in money, and some in the harder currency of staying. This paper honors both, and prints the names correctly.")*
> *(Rose reads it twice and understands the weapon's shape: not a fitting this time, but a keeping — Bell, uncharacteristically tender, setting the week's love beside the week's ledgers and finding them both true. No names, per the rule. But the town will read it, and know, and the knowing will be kind. She files the draft with the Lash and the trust's paper: the drawer, the archive of the reckoning, complete. The blade, sheathed. The keeping, printed.)*
scenes.sting: ON LOVE AND LEDGERS.

scenes.synopsis: Bell, in person — the proprietor on the week's printing; terms, plain.
scenes.prose:
> *(Bell comes at dusk herself, ink on her cuffs as always, and they discuss the week's printing over the good tea. If she chose expose: she printed it, the whole truthful account, whole and untrimmed, because it was true and newsworthy. "Harrow was 'the accomplice' for exactly one week," Bell says, "as priced. The town's moved on to the next outrage. That's print." If she chose atone: the trust's founding is Saturday's news; she'll print the deed, the sums, the creditors named. "A woman answering for forty-one thousand six hundred (£41,600) she doesn't owe," Bell says, "is news. I'll print it straight." If she chose bury: no story. "I've got a press, Miss Hartwell, not a shovel," Bell says. "The wall's rebuilt. My press prints what's true, and the true thing this week is that there's nothing to print. That's also news, in its way.")*
> *("My terms," Bell says, "haven't changed. I print what's true." She looks at Rose over the cup, and something in the look is the sting's tenderness, unfiled. "You laid the ledger open, one way or another. That's rarer than you'd think." She goes, leaving the week's printing settled: printed, to print, or unprintable — per the door, all of it true. The proprietor, plain. The terms, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the glass — evening's end; the woman, looked at.
scenes.prose:
> *(At dusk she stops at the glass in the morning room. Not to undress, not yet, but to look. The evening's dress: the blue, the de Valcourt sash kept till morning per Augusta's allowance, the pearls, the mended gloves. The day is on her face: the bracing, the devastation, the walk, the dinner, the staying. She looks at the woman who did all of it, the heir of the ruiners, the teller of the losses, the keeper of the lilies, and the woman looks back, steady, unpleading, tired in the way of a day fully inhabited.)*
> *(She touches the sash's pin, Augusta's lending. "Keep it till morning." She will. The glass shows her what the day made: not a tragedy, not a triumph — a woman, dressed, who told the truth in three different doors, and in every one of them he stayed. Enough. She turns from the glass. The looking, done. The woman, kept.)*

fashionChoices.label: Look long
fashionChoices.detail: the day, read in the face; every hour, owned.

fashionChoices.label: Look away
fashionChoices.detail: enough reckoning; the glass, passed by.

fashionChoices.label: Touch the pin
fashionChoices.detail: the token, confirmed; the wearing, owned till morning.

scenes.synopsis: goodnight — brief, plain; the day, closed kindly.
scenes.prose:
> *(The knock comes at dusk. Laurent himself, not a letter, come to say goodnight properly. Two minutes, he says, and means it. They stand in the hall among the lilies, and the flowers do the talking for a moment: white, everywhere, purity of intent, no pleading. "I saw them," he says. "In every room. Before the talking." "Élise's doctrine," Rose says. "Flowers first." He nods. Then, plainly, the French plainness that is his best thing: "Goodnight, Rose. Thank you. For the day. For the page. For not managing me." He takes her hand, the mended glove, briefly. "Tomorrow: the garden, or the letters, or the rest. Whatever you chose. I'll come.")*
> *(He goes, the black coat into the dusk, and she stands among the lilies with his goodnight in her like a kept bead. Two minutes, and the day is closed kindly: no speeches, no scenes, just the flowers and the plainness and the promise of the morrow. She touches the lily nearest her. Purity of intent. It meant exactly what it looked like. The goodnight, said. The day, closed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the heart, accounted — the ledger's last column; the day, balanced.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone, she accounts her heart the way Octavia accounts sums: in columns, without flinching. What was lost: his best story about himself, set down like a coat; her morning's certainty, traded for his evening's answer. What was paid: the telling — the page, the printing, the memory, per the door; the unpleading blue; the lilies, twenty rooms. What remains: the man, staying; the house, welcoming; the morrow, chosen. She runs the columns twice, the way she reads stings, and the balance holds — not even, never even, but held.)*
> *(She closes the imaginary ledger. Some columns don't take figures — she told Octavia that, and it's true — but the heart keeps accounts anyway, in its own currency: the staying, the soup, the real smile, the goodnight. The balance isn't happiness, exactly. It's something better, and rarer: the thing faced, the thing kept. She blows out the last lamp. The heart, accounted. The day, balanced.)*

scenes.synopsis: the cliffhanger — Quill at dusk; Pounce's hundred pounds, traced.
scenes.prose:
> *(Dusk, going dark. The knocker sounds — Quill, at an hour when solicitors don't call, with his leather case and the face of a man carrying a number. "Miss Hartwell." He doesn't sit. From the case he takes a single paper, which he lays on the desk but does not yet explain. "We've found," he says, "where Pounce's hundred pounds came from." The room is very still. Outside, the dusk goes on darkening, indifferent to ledgers. Rose looks at the paper on the desk, and does not yet touch it.)*
> *(Quill waits. The paper waits. The hundred pounds — the blind item's price, the advertisement, the fitting's subject — has a source now, beyond the factor's desk, beyond the fog. Rose puts out her hand toward the paper, and stops it halfway, and looks up at Quill. "Tell me," she says. And the chapter ends.)*

scenes.synopsis: the money, traced — Quill completes the walk through the fog; the account's name; the grandfather's figures, laid beside.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill comes at nine with the leather case, and the case has the particular fullness of finished work. He lays the papers out on the study table in order, like a hand of cards: Pounce's hundred pounds, entered as "advertising services" and paid by a London factor's draft, and behind the factor, a second draft drawn on a smaller house, and behind that two cutouts with names Rose has never heard and will never need again, and behind them the account itself. The name on it is Vane. "Mrs. Vane," Quill says. "The money is hers. The management is the daughter's people: Cecilia's agents, in England ahead of her, spending it." He taps the last draft with one finger. "The fog, walked through. Managed money always leaves a trail. It can't help itself.")*
> *(Then the older accounting, because Quill does nothing by halves: the grandfather's figures, copied fair from the papers. Forty-one thousand, six hundred pounds entrusted. Eight thousand, eight hundred — now. He reads them without emphasis, the way solicitors read sums that have ruined families. Rose looks at the two figures the way she looked at the fallen wall in the spring: the shape of the sin, priced to the pound. If she chose atone, the figures are a bill. If she chose expose, they are evidence. If she chose bury, they are the cost of the silence she bought. Whichever choice, they are hers now. "Thank you," she says. Quill touches his hat. "The money is traced, Miss Hartwell. What it buys next is your decision.")*

scenes.synopsis: quiet armor for the unmasking — Hartwell blue, severe; the day the hunter is named, dressed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia lays out the Hartwell blue without being asked — the severe one, high at the throat, the skirt's weight doing the talking. "If you're naming the hunter today," she says, "the house names her in its own color." With it, the silver rose pin at the shoulder, and the mended gloves, the left thumb's scar turned outward where the light finds it. "The archive's answer," Letitia says, "is the same as the siege's. We do not dress for them. We dress as ourselves, and let them do the arithmetic.")*
> *(Rose stands in the blue and understands the quartermaster's doctrine at its simplest: the gown is not armor against the hunter, it is the announcement that armor was unnecessary. In the glass she looks like the house made visible — severe, solvent, unhurried. "Mrs. Vane has never seen me," she says. "She's about to." Letitia nods once. "Then let her first sight be accurate." The unmasking, dressed. The hunter, about to be named by a woman in blue.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the house's color; nothing softened, nothing explained.

fashionChoices.label: The blue, softened
fashionChoices.detail: the same gown, the pearls added; severity, made approachable.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE TRACED MONEY: print it, hold it, or send it back; the hunter's funds, handled.
scenes.prose:
> *(Morning. The traced drafts sit in the study in Quill's fair copy, and the question of what to do with them won't wait for the afternoon. Three handlings offer themselves. Print it: give the whole chain to Bell — the factor, the cutouts, Cecilia's people, the name Vane. The Gazette prints what's true, and the hunter is named in daylight for all of London to read. The honest handling. But a named hunter is a warned hunter, and Mrs. Vane has resources beyond a gutter sheet. Hold it: keep the chain in the drawer. A card unplayed is a card that frightens; let Cecilia's people wonder what Rose knows and when she'll use it. The patient handling. But leverage unused is leverage that rots, and the operation is already underway. Send it back: return the trace to its source — let Mrs. Vane receive, by a quiet channel, the proof that her money has been walked through the fog to her name. A warning, and a courtesy. The merciful handling. But mercy to a hunter is information, and information is ammunition.)*
> *(She stands at the study window with the fair copy in her hand and thinks of Octavia: a hunter named is a hunter who changes shape. Of Bell: I print what's true. Of Letitia: the house that names its enemy had better be dressed for the answer. The handling, chosen, becomes the day's doctrine.)*
> *(The money, handled her way: printed, held, or returned. The fair copy went where she sent it — to Bell, to the drawer, or back down the chain to its source. Whatever Mrs. Vane bought next, she would buy it knowing the fog had been walked.)*

options.label: Print it in the Gazette
options.detail: *Candor+; the name, printed.* Give Bell the whole chain; let London read it. *(The hunter named in daylight; a warned hunter changes shape.)*

options.label: Hold it, for leverage
options.detail: *Resolve+; the card, kept.* Keep the chain in the drawer; let them wonder. *(Leverage frightens; leverage unused rots.)*

options.label: Send it back as warning
options.detail: *Mercy+; the warning, sent.* Return the proof by a quiet channel; courtesy, and notice. *(Mercy is information; information is ammunition.)*

scenes.synopsis: on hunters and money — Octavia on what the unmasking buys, and what it costs.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes at eleven, hears the handling, and does what she always does: prices it. "If you printed it," she says, "you've bought daylight. The town knows the name, the Lash loses its mystery, and Mrs. Vane —" she pauses, "— Mrs. Vane learns that her money is visible. If you held it, you've bought fear. They'll spend the next month wondering what you know. Fear is expensive to maintain, Rose. It costs the holder more than the held." She takes up her tea. "If you sent it back, you've bought manners. And manners, between hunters, are a language. The question is whether she speaks it.")*
> *("And what would you have done?" Rose asks. Octavia considers. "I would have done what you did," she says, "and then I would have worried about it exactly as much as you are worrying now." A beat. "The unmasking buys you one thing, whatever the handling. It buys you the knowledge that the hunter has a name and the name has an owner. Before today, it was fog. Fog can't be answered. Mrs. Vane can." She sets down the cup. "Not seen. But answerable." The counsel, taken. The purchase, priced.)*

scenes.synopsis: Mrs. Vane, surfaced — never seen; Bell on what she knows of the name, and what she'll print.
scenes.prose:
> *(Bell arrives at noon with her memorandum book and no preamble. "Mrs. Vane," she says. "Here's what the paper knows. The money behind Cecilia's people is hers. The operation's funds, walked through the fog to her name. It's managed through men who've never met her." She looks up. "She is the only person in this story I have never seen. I've seen Pounce drunk. I've seen Cecilia. I have never seen Mrs. Vane.")*
> *("What will you print?" Rose asks. "The name," Bell says. "If you give it to me. The chain, if it's true — and Quill's chain is true. What I won't print is a face I don't have. No descriptions, no guesses, no 'a woman of a certain age.' The Gazette prints what it knows." She closes the book. "One more thing. Whoever she is — she's not done. The hundred pounds was the advertisement. The story will cost more, and she can afford it." She goes, leaving the arithmetic she always leaves: the name, surfaced; the face, absent; the money, still moving. The hunter, described by her absence.)*

scenes.synopsis: her last card — Mrs. Quick, recalled; the refused £2,000, dead on the table; the agent, dismissed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Mrs. Quick comes at one, and the difference is visible before she speaks: the reticule is thinner, the composure rehearsed rather than total. "Miss Hartwell," she says. "My principals have authorized me to —" "Stop," Rose says, not unkindly. "Your principals have been traced, Mrs. Quick. The factor's draft. The cutouts. Cecilia's people." A pause. "Mrs. Vane." The name lands the way names land when they're true. Mrs. Quick's hands fold over the thin reticule. "I see," she says. "Then my instructions are —" "Your instructions," Rose says, "are to go home.")*
> *(On the table between them sits the envelope, unopened since Thursday: two thousand pounds, the price once offered for the story, refused. Mrs. Quick looks at it. "My last card," she says quietly, "was to double it." "It would still be refused," Rose says. "Take it back to them. Tell them the story is not for sale at any price, because —" she touches the envelope, "— it is already printed. Or burned. Or paid for. The choosing is done." She meets the agent's eyes. "There is nothing left to buy." Mrs. Quick curtsies, correctly, and goes, recalled or cut loose, it hardly matters. The last card, unplayed. The envelope, dead.)*

scenes.synopsis: Cecilia — the absence; Rose considers the woman who operates but never appears.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone after luncheon, Rose thinks about Cecilia — not the girl she knew, but the operator: the woman who has spent years building money, agents, and patience, and who has never once stepped into the light. It is, Rose realizes, the opposite of everything she herself has done this season. She has printed, and buried, and paid, all in daylight. Cecilia has bought, and managed, and waited, all in fog. Two doctrines. Only one of them has a face.)*
> *(She tries to picture her — the dearest friend, the brilliant match — and finds she cannot. The face won't come. What comes instead is the shape of the operation: the money moving through men who've never met its owner, the agents in England ahead of their principal, the gutter sheet bought by the pound. An operation, not a person. That is the point, and it is also the weakness. You can hate a person. You can only outwait an operation. She folds the thought away with the morning's drafts. Cecilia, absent. The absence, noted. Tomorrow, the garden.)*

scenes.synopsis: midday, steady — the dress for the middle of the day; the unmasking's afternoon, dressed.
scenes.prose:
> *(At two she changes for the afternoon's work — not the blue, which has done its morning duty, but the dove grey, the siege's old standby, with the dried violets at the wrist. Faithfulness, worn where the pulse is. The grey is the gown that has outlasted the blind item, the stranger, the offer, and the trace; it has earned its place in the week's rotation the way a good servant earns trust: by being there, unremarked, when needed.)*
> *(In the glass, the grey does what grey does: it steadies. The morning's naming sits behind her eyes, and the gown refuses to perform it. That is the point of the midday change. The unmasking was the morning's business; the afternoon's business is the archive, and the archive wants steadiness. She pins the dried violets, touches the mend, and goes down. The day, halved. The grey, holding.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the siege's standby; the steady choice.

fashionChoices.label: The blue, kept
fashionChoices.detail: the morning's armor, worn through; the naming, extended.

fashionChoices.label: The white, early
fashionChoices.detail: tomorrow's garden, tried on at noon; anticipation, dressed.

scenes.synopsis: his settlement — the £150; the keeping his, deeded outright on the atonement path; the witness, honored.
scenes.prose:
> *(Harrow comes at three, and the settlement is the simplest business of the day. One hundred and fifty pounds — the sum the estate owes its witness, counted out in Quill's fair hand, receipted in Harrow's schoolmaster's script. He looks at the money the way he looks at everything: steadily, without hunger and without refusal. "Twenty years," he says, "I carried half of it without knowing the whole. I never expected payment." "It's not payment," Rose says. "It's acknowledgment. There's a difference, and the estate knows it.")*
> *(If she chose atone, there is more: the keeping, deeded. The keeping where he lodged through the siege, made over to him outright — his, whatever his choice of place. He holds the deed a long moment. "Miss Hartwell," he says, and stops, and starts again: "I have lived in other people's houses all my life." If she chose expose, she shows him the Gazette's printed account, his name cleared in it, the receipt made public. If she chose bury, she tells him the wall is rebuilt and the cache burned — and that his half, his own, was never the estate's to burn. Whichever path, the settlement holds: the witness, honored; the scar, acknowledged; the man, kept close. He folds the receipt into his pocket like a letter from a friend.)*

scenes.synopsis: the library, dressed for — archive grey, plain; the afternoon's shelving, costumed.
scenes.prose:
> *(For the library work she changes again — the plainest grey she owns, the one with ink already in its history, sleeves that turn back without argument. Harrow, arriving for the afternoon's sorting, looks at the gown and laughs, a short surprised sound. "Miss Hartwell," he says, "you dress for archiving the way other people dress for dinner." "The papers," Rose says, "deserve the compliment. They've waited twenty years to be shelved properly.")*
> *(He is in his schoolmaster's coat, the elbows mended — she notices the mending, and does not comment, and he notices her noticing, and they understand each other. The library's north room waits with its empty shelves and its ladders and its dust, and the two of them stand a moment in the doorway like guests at a threshold. Then Rose turns back her sleeves, Harrow opens the first box, and the afternoon's work begins: the living archive, about to be shelved. The grey, ink-ready. The witness, sleeves rolled.)*

fashionChoices.detail: ink-ready; the archive, honored by plainness.

fashionChoices.label: The dove grey, kept
fashionChoices.detail: the siege's gown, worn through; continuity, dressed.

fashionChoices.detail: the morning's severity, back for the shelving; the house, present.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — HARROW'S PAPERS: shelved under his name, sealed unattributed, or kept in his hands; the living archive, placed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Late afternoon, in the library's north room, the shelves half-filled and the dust in the light. The boxes stand in their rows — Harrow's half, twenty years carried, the papers pressed with dried violets, the other half of the sin. The keeping was decided Monday, and told, and accepted; the post is his. What isn't decided is the papers themselves. They are the library's now — that much the season has settled — but a library can hold a thing three ways, and the catalogue waits to be entered. Three dispositions offer themselves. Shelve them under his name: the catalogue entered "Harrow's half, carried twenty years," the boxes open on the north room's shelves beside the estate's account, the living archive honored where the household can see it. But a named archive is a readable one, and Harrow has spent twenty years being uninteresting. Seal them unattributed: the boxes closed and corded, the catalogue marked only "the witness's half," the papers kept but not read aloud. But discretion, kept too long, curdles into the family's old habit — the silence they are trying to stop buying. Leave them in his hands: the library's papers, but the keeper keeps them — his box, his key, his twenty years' charge continued under the estate's roof. But mercy to one man is a risk to the archive: what one pair of hands can carry, one fire can take.)*
> *(Harrow listens with his hands on the nearest box, the scar catching the light. "They're the library's," he says. "I've said so. The question is only —" he looks for the word, the schoolmaster reaching — "the question is only how a library holds what a man carried." Rose thinks of the spring: the scarred gentleman at the wall's breach, carrying half the sin like a hamper. The disposition, chosen, becomes the archive's answer to the witness.)*
> *(The papers, placed her way: named on the shelves, sealed without a name, or kept in the keeper's hands. Whatever the archive held, it held it the way she chose — and Harrow nodded among the boxes, the dust in the light, and whatever the papers' place, the archive would hold.)*

scenes.synopsis: the papers, placed — whatever was chosen, the disposition is enacted; the archive, ordered.
scenes.prose:
> *(What she chose, they do. If shelved under his name: the boxes go up on the north room's shelves with the estate's account beside them, and Rose writes the catalogue entry herself — "Harrow's half, carried twenty years" — the living archive honored where the household can see it. If sealed unattributed: the boxes are closed and corded, the catalogue marked only "the witness's half," and they go up behind the estate's account, kept but not read aloud. If in his hands: the boxes stay in his charge — the library's papers, the keeper's keeping — and Rose notes it for Quill's catalogue, with the key's number beside it.)*
> *(Harrow watches his twenty years go onto shelves, or into seals, or back into his own hands — whichever the choosing, his face does the same thing: the scarred cheek pulls, the mouth steadies. "Twenty years," he says, "I carried half of it without knowing the whole." He looks at the north room — the ladders, the dust, the light. "Whatever the shelves say, Miss Hartwell —" he stops, and starts again: "I have lived in other people's houses all my life. The papers, at least, have come home." The witness, placed. The living archive, settled in the manner she picked — kept close, as the season required. She touches the dried violets at her wrist. Faithfulness: his, for twenty years; the estate's, from today.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Vane money — the shape, recognized; Letitia on managed money, and her youth's second layer.
scenes.prose:
> *(At tea, Rose lays Quill's chain before Letitia — the factor, the cutouts, Cecilia's people, the name. Letitia studies it a long moment, and something in her face changes. "I know the shape of that," she says quietly. "Not the people. The shape." She looks up. "Your grandfather's generation moved money exactly so. Not the speculation — the management. The men who never met the owner. The drafts that walked through fog." A pause. "I was twenty. I watched it done at dinner tables and called it banking.")*
> *("You recognized it in the spring," Rose says, "and didn't say." "I recognized the shape of the sin," Letitia says. "This is the shape of the money. It's different." She folds her hands. "The sin was my family's. The money is hers — Mrs. Vane's. But the shape is the same shape, and shapes are how you know a thing before you can prove it." She touches Rose's sleeve. "You proved it. That's the difference between my youth and your week." The confession's echo. The shape, recognized — and this time, spoken.)*

scenes.synopsis: the longest game, acknowledged — Augusta's admission; the £2,800, promised to the de Valcourts, made formal.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta receives Rose in the drawing room at four, and the interview has the quality of a treaty. "The de Valcourts," Augusta says, without preamble. "My mother's people. The banking branch. They fell in your grandfather's fall, and I have spent forty years playing the longest game in this family — keeping the connection warm, the name honored, the debt unspoken." She looks at her granddaughter steadily. "It is time to speak it. Two thousand, eight hundred pounds. Promised." A pause. "It was never the money. It was the acknowledgment the money carries.")*
> *(Rose thinks of the morning's figures, forty-one six and eight eight, and understands, suddenly, what Augusta's game cost her: forty years of courtesy toward a family her own husband's father ruined, never flinching, never explaining. "The promise," Rose says, "will be in Quill's hand by evening." Augusta nods. "Your grandfather covered the Hartwell losses first. I have spent my life covering the courtesy." She rises. The interview is ended. At the door she turns. "You did in a week what I did in forty years, child. Don't waste it being modest about it." The longest game, acknowledged. The promise, formal.)*

scenes.synopsis: agents watched off — Major Lord Henry Beaumont sees Mr. Slade off the estate; courtesy, and steel.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry finds Slade on the London road at five, the ordinary man in the ordinary coat, the stranger who priced the witness all spring, and the interview is brief, military, and final. "Mr. Slade," Henry says. "The estate's hospitality is concluded." Slade looks at the major's face and understands, with the particular comprehension of men who price things for a living, that the pricing is over. "My employers —" "Your employers," Henry says, "have been named. Mrs. Vane. Cecilia's people. The money's been traced, the fog's been walked. There's nothing left here to price.")*
> *(Slade bows, correctly, even gracefully, and goes, the ordinary coat disappearing down the ordinary road. Henry watches him out of sight, then rides back to the house and reports to Rose in three sentences. "He's gone," he says. "He'll write it all down, of course. Let him. There's nothing left to write that we haven't already said ourselves." He pauses at the door. "The sin is old, Rose. The sinners are dead. The victims are owed, and paid or promised. What duty requires of the living now is the future." He goes. The agents, watched off. The road, empty.)*

scenes.synopsis: the town's reading — Julian on how London will read a surfaced Mrs. Vane.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian comes at six, hears the day's accounting, and does what younger sons do: he reads the town. "London," he says, "will read Mrs. Vane the way London reads everything: as a story about money and women. If you printed her, she'll be the villainess of the season by Saturday. If you held the name, she'll be the mystery. If you sent it back —" he smiles, "— she'll be the correspondent. The town loves a correspondent.")*
> *("And what does the town read in me?" Rose asks. Julian looks at her — the grey, the dried violets, the mend — and his voice loses its lightness. "The town reads a woman who was handed her family's ruin and did the accounts in public. Do you know what my family's genteel poverty looks like in this light, Rose? It looks like the machinery you just dismantled. Younger sons, made into instruments." He takes her hand briefly. "You didn't just name your hunter. You showed the town the machine. That's rarer than courage." The town, read. The machine, shown.)*

scenes.synopsis: afternoon — the dowager's pearls, lent; dressing for the evening's accounting.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends the pearls at half past six with a note in her own hand: "For the evening. The longest game lends its ornaments to the shortest week." Letitia fastens them, and the pearls sit against the grey like a sentence Augusta has been waiting forty years to complete. "She never lends them," Letitia says quietly. "Not to anyone. Not for anything." Rose touches one pearl, cool and perfect. "Then I'd better be worth the lending.")*
> *(In the glass, the pearls change the grey — not softening it, exactly, but dating it: the gown is this week, the pearls are forty years, and the combination is the season's whole argument worn at the throat. The grandmother's doctrine, the dowager's ornaments, the granddaughter's week. "How do I look?" Rose asks. Letitia steps back, the quartermaster inspecting the uniform. "Like the acknowledgment," she says, "has been made." The pearls, lent. The evening, dressed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the mend, outward — the mended glove, worn where the light finds it; the season's answer, restated.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone before dinner, Rose looks at the mended glove — the left thumb's scar, turned outward all day — and thinks about what the mend has become this season. It started as the grandmother's doctrine: a glove could be mended, a reputation earned back stitch by stitch. It became the siege's uniform: forty pairs, forty hands. Today it became something else: the signature on the week's accounting. The scar, shown, while naming the hunter. The mend, outward, while settling the witness.)*
> *(She flexes the thumb in the glass, and the scar catches the light the way it has all week — deliberate, unhidden, earned. Tomorrow the garden opens, and the white will be simple, and the mend will still be there, because some things are not finished when the week is. The doctrine holds: the house that mends together does not flinch apart. The glove, worn. The answer, restated. The habit, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the village, sated — the network stands down; the misinformation, retired with honors.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes at seven with the evening dried violets and the last report, and the report is the kind she delivers like a curtain call. "The stranger's gone," she says. "The Crown's boy watched him take the London coach. One of the village girls cried." Rose laughs. "Cried?" "She'd grown fond of lying to him. She asked if another one could be sent." Élise arranges the dried violets. "The blacksmith wants to know if the cottage is still haunted, for the record. I told him the haunting is retired with honors.")*
> *("And the village?" "The village," Élise says, "has had the best spring of its life and is prepared to be bored again." She looks up, suddenly serious. "You know what they did, Rose. They lied for you — cheerfully, inventively, without being asked. The Derby grandmother. The haunted cottage. The French poetry." A beat. "That's not misinformation. That's love with a straight face." Rose touches the dried violets, faithfulness, and thinks of the village's enjoyment, the spring's long joke, the lies told like gifts. "Tell them," she says, "the house thanks them. Stitch by stitch." The network, stood down. The village, sated.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE ANSWER TO MRS. VANE: silence, a line, or preparation; the surfaced name, answered.
scenes.prose:
> *(Night. The name sits in Quill's case, in Bell's memorandum book, in the day's accounting: Mrs. Vane. Surfaced, never seen. The question of the answer won't wait for morning. A surfaced hunter must be answered, and the answer is the week's last doctrine. Three answers offer themselves. No answer: the silence, pointed. Say nothing, print nothing, send nothing. Let the unmasking sit in the drawer and the knowledge sit in the house. Silence is an answer, and a pointed one. It says: we know, and we are not afraid enough to speak. The disciplined handling. But silence can be read as fear, and Mrs. Vane reads. A line in the Gazette, unsigned: one line, no name attached, in Bell's leader, the paper noting coolly that certain funds have been traced to their source. The truth, printed, unattributed. The honest handling. But a line is a beginning, and beginnings invite replies. Prepare the house: no message, no print, only preparation. Warn the household, brief the village, set the watch. Treat the surfaced name as what it is: the present attack, announced. The merciful handling, and the mercy is to the house, not the hunter. But preparation is visible, and visible preparation is its own message.)*
> *(She stands at the window with the day behind her — the traced drafts, the refused two thousand, the dismissed agent, the settled witness, the lent pearls — and thinks of Octavia: an operation now, not a rumor. Of Bell: I print what's true. Of Letitia: the house that names its enemy had better be dressed for the answer. The answer, chosen, becomes the season's closing doctrine.)*
> *(The name, answered her way: with silence, with a line, or with preparation. The answer went where she sent it — nowhere, into print, or into the household's discipline. Whatever Mrs. Vane did next, she would do it against a house that had named her.)*

options.label: No answer — the silence, pointed
options.detail: *Resolve+; the silence, kept.* Nothing said, nothing printed; let her read the quiet. *(Silence says unafraid; silence can be read as fear.)*

options.label: A line in the Gazette, unsigned
options.detail: *Candor+; the line, printed.* One cool line in Bell's leader; the funds, traced, unattributed. *(The truth, printed; beginnings invite replies.)*

options.label: Prepare the house for her
options.detail: *Mercy+; the house, readied.* Warn the household, brief the village, set the watch. *(Mercy to the house; preparation is its own message.)*

scenes.synopsis: the surfaced name — Rose sits with "Mrs. Vane"; the absence, considered.
scenes.prose:
> *(After dinner, alone in the study, Rose writes the name in her memorandum book: Mrs. Vane. She looks at it a long time. The letters are ordinary. The hand is her own. Nothing about the ink suggests money, or agents, or funding a daughter's war from a distance. That is the thing about surfaced names: they disappoint. You expect the fog to have a face, and it has only a name, and the name has only letters.)*
> *(She thinks of Bell: the only person in this story I have never seen. She thinks of Cecilia, whom she has also never seen — not in years, not since the friendship ended. Two unseen women, running an operation against a house. Frightening, and clarifying. The past is settled — printed, buried, or paid for, by her choice. What remains is the present, and the present has a name now, and a name can be answered. She closes the book. Mrs. Vane, surfaced. The absence, considered. The answer, chosen.)*
> *(The answer, chosen — and then, because a doctrine unacted is only a thought, enacted. If her answer was silence: she does nothing further with the name. No letter, no instruction, no word to Bell. The house will sit in the quiet tonight, and Mrs. Vane's people — listening, as they have listened all spring — will hear nothing, and read the nothing. The strain of it is already in her shoulders: saying nothing, on purpose, is the hardest sentence she has written all week. If her answer was a line, unsigned: she takes a fresh sheet and writes one line — cool, exact, unattributed — the funds traced to their source, no name attached. She folds it without a seal and without a signature, and sets it by for Amos to carry to the Gazette's messenger at dawn. Somewhere tomorrow, over breakfast, strangers will read it and wonder whose hand held the pen. If her answer was preparation: she turns the memorandum book's page and writes the night's orders — the watch doubled, the lamps on the hour, Élise to the village at first light, the shutters checked, the gate watched. No message to the hunter. The preparation is the message, and it is written in lamplight for anyone watching to read.)*

scenes.synopsis: "an operation now, not a rumor" — Octavia names the shape of what's coming.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes after dinner, uninvited and welcome, and goes straight to the point. "It's an operation now, not a rumor," she says. "Rumor was the blind item. Operation is the money, the agents, the years of funding. Cecilia's return isn't coming, Rose. It's underway. The advance party has been here all spring." She sits. "I wanted to say it plainly, because plain is what you need now. The past was an investigation. The present is a siege. Different discipline.")*
> *("What does the siege want?" Rose asks. "You," Octavia says. "Not the house — you. Cecilia doesn't want Hartwell Park. She wants the woman who took her place in it." A pause. "That's why the money, the agents, the gutter sheet. It's all aimed at one person." She looks at her friend steadily. "The good news is that one person just spent a week proving she can be aimed at." Rose considers this. "That's the good news?" "It's the only news," Octavia says. "The rest is logistics." The operation, named. The siege, declared — by a friend, over tea, plainly.)*
> *("And the answer?" Octavia asks — for Rose has told her that too. She prices it the way she priced the handling at eleven. If silence: "Then the house sits quiet," she says, "and Mrs. Vane's people read the quiet. They will read it as fear or as contempt, and either way they will read it wrong, and wrong readings are useful. The strain is the price. Saying nothing, pointedly, costs the sayer." If a line, unsigned: "Then the town gets its puzzle," she says. "One cool line, no name. Bell will set it where the town can't miss it, and by noon tomorrow every coffeehouse will have a theory, and the wrong theories will do your work for you." If preparation: "Then the lamps tell it," she says. "Doubled watches, lit windows, a village gone suddenly discreet — Mrs. Vane's people will see the house brace, and understand they are expected. There is no braver sentence than a lit house at midnight." She pours the last of the tea. "Whatever the answer, Rose — it is an answer, and now she must answer it.")*

scenes.synopsis: warned and steady — the household is told of Mrs. Vane; Letitia's discipline, the house braced.
scenes.prose:
> *(At nine, the household gathers in the servants' hall — not summoned, exactly, but assembled by the particular gravity Letitia deploys when something must be said once, to everyone. Rose stands before them in the grey, the pearls, the mend, and tells them plainly: the money behind the spring's troubles has been traced to a name, Mrs. Vane; the name's agents are gone; the operation behind the name is not. "The past," she says, "is settled. The present is an operation already underway. I am telling you because this house does not flinch at what it has been told.")*
> *(Letitia follows with the discipline, and the discipline is the answer made visible. If her answer was silence: no change to the night's orders — the watch continued as it stands, no questions in the village, no letters to London, Élise's eyes still open. The house is told to hold its tongue, and the quiet itself is the message, and the strain of it sits on forty folded pairs of hands. If her answer was a line, unsigned: the household is told that the morning's Gazette will carry one cool line, unattributed — and that no one here wrote it, has read it, or knows anything about it. Élise's eyes still open, and sharpened: for who asks after the line, and who wonders aloud. If her answer was preparation: the full readiness — the watch doubled, the lamps lit on the hour, the shutters checked and the gate watched, Élise to brief the village at first light, the girls who lied so well all spring now briefed to say nothing at all. Preparation you can see from the London road, and meant to be seen.)*
> *(The household listens the way it has listened all season, forty pairs of hands folded, the mending baskets at their feet. If her answer was silence, the hall does not exhale when Rose finishes — it holds, the way a house holds a weight it has been asked to carry quietly, and Amos the porter says, "Very good, miss," and it sounds like an oath. If a line, someone near the back asks whether the town will know it was us, and Letitia says, "The town will wonder. That is the point of it," and the hall laughs, quietly, at the pleasure of a secret kept in company. If preparation, the hall exhales, and someone laughs, quietly, with relief — the relief of being given something to do. Warned, and steady, each in the manner of the answer. The house that mends together does not flinch apart. The bracing, done.)*

scenes.synopsis: evening — the white, considered; tomorrow's garden, tried on tonight.
scenes.prose:
> *(At ten she goes up to consider the white — the gown for tomorrow's garden, laid out on the bed like a question. It is simple, as the ceremony requires: white silk, unadorned, the garden's own colors to come from the flowers, not the cloth. She holds it against herself in the glass and thinks of the season's fashion spine: the archive, the heirlooms, the remade silks — and now this, the future, dressed as itself. No armor. No statement. The woman the house chose, in white.)*
> *(The evening's answer comes up the stairs with her, whatever its shape. If silence: the house below is quieter than usual, the servants' hall holding its tongue, and the quiet follows her into the bedroom like a guest. If a line, unsigned: she finds herself composing the sentence again in her head — shorter, cooler — and stops, and trusts the folded sheet. If preparation: the lamps are being lit below on the hour, and through the floorboards she hears the watch change, and the house sounds like a place that expects to be worth attacking. She stands a moment in the lamplight, and turns back to the gown.)*
> *(She does not put it on — tomorrow is tomorrow, and the white deserves its own morning — but she considers it the way she considers everything this week: deliberately, completely. The pearls will go with it, or not; the mend will be there, or not; the dried violets, certainly. Faithfulness, at the wrist, for the garden's opening. She lays the gown back down, touches the white silk once, and turns down the lamp. The white, considered. Tomorrow, the garden.)*

fashionChoices.label: The white, simple
fashionChoices.detail: as laid out; the future, unadorned.

fashionChoices.label: The white, with the pearls
fashionChoices.detail: the dowager's loan, extended; continuity, dressed.

fashionChoices.label: The white, with dried violets only
fashionChoices.detail: faithfulness, and nothing else; the garden's colors, enough.

scenes.synopsis: the money, the past, the future — Laurent stays; what the settled past leaves the two of them.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent comes at half past ten, and they walk the terrace in the dark, the house lit behind them. He has heard the day's accounting, the traced money, the surfaced name, the settled witness, and he is quiet a long time. "My family's ruin," he says at last, "has a price now. Forty-one thousand, six hundred. I keep thinking of it as a number. It's easier than thinking of it as my grandfather." Rose nods. If she chose atone, the restitution is the answer, and he knows it. If she chose expose, the printed truth. If she chose bury, the silence they share. Whichever path, the past is settled, and he stayed.)*
> *(Halfway down the terrace he asks about the answer — he has heard it, from Octavia or the servants' hall. If her answer was silence, he nods slowly. "Pointed quiet," he says. "Augusta's weapon. She once ended a dinner party with it — three courses, not a word." If a line, unsigned, he smiles in the dark. "The town will go mad wondering whose hand held the pen. You do like them to wonder." If preparation, he glances back at the house, the lamps lit on the hour. "She'll see them," he says. "Good. Let her see them." They walk on.)*
> *("What does the future cost?" he asks, and she laughs, surprised. "Everything," she says. "It always did." They walk to the terrace's end, where the walled garden's gate stands dark. "Tomorrow," he says, "the garden." "Tomorrow," she agrees. He takes her hand — not the lover's gesture of the spring, but something steadier. "Pride set down," he says quietly. "Not spent. There's a difference, and I'm learning it." She holds his hand a moment. "Stitch by stitch," she says. The money, accounted. The past, settled. The future — theirs, to price together.)*

scenes.synopsis: her hardest leader, drafted — Bell writes on Mrs. Vane; the paper's independence, at the root.
scenes.prose:
> *(Bell comes at eleven with the draft, and her face has the particular gravity of a proprietor about to spend capital. "Read it," she says. The leader is three paragraphs, cool and deliberate. It follows the money behind the spring — the factor, the cutouts, Cecilia's people — to its source, and it handles the source the way Rose instructed. If she chose print: the name in type, plain and spelled correctly, the chain with it. If hold: the name in type, the chain held back — traced, the paper says, and held. If return: the name in type, the return beside it, the courtesy noted.)*
> *(And the answer, laid over the draft. If her answer was silence: the leader folded and held from the morning's paper by Rose's own instruction — drafted, not set. "The paper can wait," Bell says. "The truth keeps." If her answer was a line, unsigned: the three paragraphs cooled to a single line for the editorial column — no name attached, only the funds, traced to their source. "One cool line," Bell says. "No name, no signature. The town will read it twice and ask whose hand held the pen, and I will answer none of them. That is the whole of unsigned copy." If her answer was preparation: the draft standing as drafted — the name set for the morning's Gazette, three paragraphs, cool and final. "I don't print what I can't prove," Bell says. "The money I can prove. The name I found myself — the town is good at arithmetic, and so am I. The chain itself is yours to give, to keep, or to send back. The woman behind it I have never seen.")*
> *("It's your hardest call," Rose says. "Printing what you can't see —" "Printing the truth with no face," Bell says. "The paper has printed what you gave it and respected what you asked it to respect. This is harder. A name I can't see, money I can prove, aimed at a woman who's never set foot here." She rests her hand on the draft — folded, cooled, or standing for the morning, by Rose's answer. "The paper's independence isn't proven by printing what helps you, Miss Hartwell. It's proven by printing what's true when the truth has no face." The leader, drafted. The independence, at the root.)*

scenes.synopsis: seals, deeds — the week's instruments, executed; the solicitor's hand, the week's signature.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill comes at midnight. Solicitors keep late hours when the work is finished, not when it's begun. The study table fills with the week's instruments. Harrow's settlement, sealed: the £150 receipted, the placing entered. The keeping deed, if she chose atone: made over outright, witnessed, sealed. The ten-year instrument, if she chose atone: three thousand a year, for ten years, charged on the canal's revenues, never the Park's stones. The de Valcourt promise: two thousand, eight hundred pounds, in Augusta's name, acknowledged. If she chose expose: the Gazette's printed account, filed with the estate papers as the true record. If she chose bury: the wall's rebuilding deed, the garden's new planting orders, the silence made legal.)*
> *(And the answer, given its instrument — or its deliberate lack of one. If her answer was silence: no paper for it. Quill makes no entry, at Rose's word. "Some doctrines," he says, "are better unwitnessed." If a line, unsigned: the folded sheet, unsealed and unsigned, entered into his case for the Gazette's messenger at dawn — the only anonymous paper in a case of signatures. If preparation: the night's orders, written fair in his hand — the watch, the lamps, the village briefed — and filed with the week's instruments. "A house that braces," he says, sanding the page, "should brace in writing.")*
> *(Rose signs where he indicates, the pen scratching in the lamplight, and Quill witnesses, sanding each page with the particular care of a man who has seen unsigned weeks come undone. "The money," he says, capping the pen, "is now where money should be. Owed, paid, promised, or printed — accounted for, in every case." He gathers the instruments into the case. "A solicitor's week, Miss Hartwell." "A family's week, Mr. Quill." He touches his hat, and goes into the midnight with the case full of the settled past. The seals, set. The deeds, done.)*

scenes.synopsis: the quartermaster, restored — Letitia, dressed for the evening; the confession's aftermath, worn well.
scenes.prose:
> *(At half past midnight, Letitia comes to Rose's room, not to dress her, but to be seen. She is in the deep grey, the silver embroidery, the grandmother's pearls at her own throat now, lent by Augusta for the evening. "How do I look?" she asks, and there is something almost girlish in it. "Like the quartermaster," Rose says, "restored." Letitia turns in the glass. "The confession," she says, "took forty years to say. I expected to feel smaller. I feel —" she considers, "— the right size.")*
> *("And the answer?" Letitia asks — the quartermaster cannot help herself. If silence: she nods once. "The hardest discipline. The house will hold its tongue. It has had practice." If a line, unsigned: "The town will wonder," she says, considering. "Let them. Wondering is work, and tonight it is not ours." If preparation: "The lamps are lit," she says. "The watch is doubled. I have seen this house brace before, miss. It braces well.")*
> *(Rose understands: the week's second devastation, survived. Letitia knew the shape and stayed silent, said so aloud, and was forgiven, or not, by Rose's choosing. Here she stands, in grey and silver, the right size. "You kept the family's peace and called it love," Rose says quietly. "It was love," Letitia says. "It was also silence. Both things were true. That's what took forty years." She touches Rose's cheek, briefly, the quartermaster's benediction. "Tomorrow, the garden." She smiles. "Tonight we are the right size." The restoration, worn. The aunt, herself again.)*

scenes.synopsis: the week, accounted — Rose does the ledger; the money, the past, the future, balanced.
scenes.prose:
> *(At one in the morning, Rose does the week's ledger in her memorandum book — not the estate's books, which are Quill's, but her own accounting. Money traced: Pounce's hundred, walked through fog to Mrs. Vane. Money refused: two thousand, dead in its envelope. Money paid: one hundred and fifty, to the witness. Money promised: two thousand eight hundred, to the de Valcourts; three thousand a year for ten years, if she chose atone, charged on the canal. The old sin: forty-one six entrusted, eight eight now — printed, burned, or paid for, by her choice.)*
> *(She totals the column, as her grandmother taught her, and the total is not a number. The total is: the hunter, named. The witness, placed. The household, warned. The aunt, restored. The dowager, acknowledged. The village, sated. The lover, stayed. The garden — tomorrow. The answer, she does not total — it has no column. If silence: the quiet, kept, and the house keeping it with her. If a line: the folded sheet, riding toward London in the dark. If preparation: the lamps, the watch, the braced house. She closes the book on the balanced week and sits a moment in the lamplight, the pearls cool at her throat, the mend at her thumb. The past, settled. The present, an operation. The future — the garden's gate, standing open at dawn. The ledger, closed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the accession — Harrow's papers join the library; the living archive, shelved and sealed.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: Harrow, at the boxes — "twenty years in boxes. Tonight they get shelves.")*
> *(Story morsel: Letitia, at the shelves — "the north room was empty when I was a girl. Look at it now.")*
> *(Story morsel: Octavia, at the catalogue — "an archive with a living keeper. That's the trick of it.")*
> *(Story morsel: Rose, at the lamp — "what's shelved is settled. What's sealed is kept.")*
> *(Story morsel: Harrow, at the door — "the living archive. That's me, then. Shelved and sealed, and still walking about.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: The money is traced, the witness is settled, and the hunter has a name. Tonight the household does what the house has always done with its past: it archives it. Harrow's papers, twenty years carried, the other half of the sin, join the library's north room — shelved under his name, sealed unattributed, or kept in his hands as the library's keeper, by her choosing at the papers decision. If she chose bury, the cache burned; what he kept, he gives. If expose or atone, the papers join their printed or paid account. Dress for the shelving: the archive's finest, deliberate. The living archive is not plain work, and the house does not under-dress its memory. Precise. Together. Unafraid. The house that archives together remembers together.

scenes.synopsis: the library, complete — Rose stands in the north room after the household has gone.
scenes.prose:
> *(After the household disperses, Rose stays in the north room alone, the lamp still lit, the sealed shelves in their rows. The room that was empty when Letitia was a girl is full now — Harrow's boxes, shelved, sealed, or in his keeping by her choosing, the estate's account, the catalogue in Octavia's hand, the pressed violets still in the pages. She walks the shelves slowly, touching nothing, reading the catalogue entries the way you'd read headstones: here the sin, here the accounting, here the restitution, here the silence.)*
> *(The north room keeps its own silence — shelved silence, older than the evening's. If her answer was silence, the house's quiet matches it, and she stands a moment in the doubled stillness, and lets it hold her. If a line, unsigned, she thinks of the folded sheet riding toward London in the dark, and the strangers who will read it at breakfast. If preparation, she hears the watch change outside — boots on gravel — and the archive sits within the bracing, kept and guarded both.)*
> *(If she chose bury, one shelf stands empty — the cache's place, burned, marked only by the catalogue's note. She stops before it longest. The empty shelf is the honest part of the archive: the record of what was chosen, kept as carefully as the papers themselves. What's shelved is settled. What's sealed is kept. What's burned is marked. She turns down the lamp, locks the north room, and keeps her key. The library, complete. The past, in its place.)*

scenes.synopsis: night — the day, undressed; the week's costumes, retired.
scenes.prose:
> *(At half past one she undresses the day — the accession's direction laid aside, the pins, the pearls, the mend's glove placed precisely on the dressing table. The week's costumes hang in the wardrobe in order: the blue of the naming, the greys of the siege, the white waiting for morning. She stands in her shift and looks at them, the whole week's doctrine in cloth, and feels the particular tiredness of a thing finished well.)*
> *(The dressing gown is plain, warm, unremarkable — the first unconsidered garment of the week. She ties it, lets down her hair, and sits at the glass without studying herself. Tomorrow the white. Tonight, the plain. The house sleeps. The garden waits. The woman in the glass, for once, is not being read by anyone — not the town, not the hunters, not even herself. If her answer was a line, the town will read something of her at breakfast — one cool sentence, no name — and she finds she does not mind. If silence, the unread night feels like the answer, extended an hour. If preparation, the lamps still burn below, and the house is being read by whoever watches, and that was the point. She blows out the candles. The day, undressed. The week, nearly done.)*

scenes.synopsis: his goodnight — the witness, settled, says goodnight; the living archive, walking about.
scenes.prose:
> *(Harrow knocks at two, softly, the schoolmaster's knock, and stands in the doorway of the morning room with his hat in his hands. "I wanted to say goodnight," he says. "Properly. The week —" he stops. "Twenty years I carried it. Tonight it's on shelves." He looks at her, the scar catching the lamplight. "You gave me a keeping, a post, and a key to the north room. That's more settlement than most men get in a lifetime.")*
> *("The key," Rose says, "is because the archive needs its keeper. The keeping is because a man should own his roof. The post —" she smiles, "— the post is because the estate needs someone who reads ledgers the way you do." He bows, correctly, and at the door he turns. "The answer," he says — he has heard it, the way the whole house has heard everything this week. If silence: "Quiet," he says, approving. "The schoolmaster's answer. Nothing said, and everything understood." If a line, unsigned: "The town will chew on it for a month," he says, and smiles, the scar pulling. If preparation: "The lamps," he says. "I saw them lit from the keeping. A library with a watch on it — I have waited twenty years for that sentence.")*
> *("Miss Hartwell. If the operation comes, Mrs. Vane's people, whatever's next." "You'll be in the library," Rose says. "I know," he says. "Shelved and sealed, and still walking about." "Still walking about," she agrees, and he goes. The goodnight, said. The witness, home.)*

scenes.synopsis: goodnight — the quartermaster's last round; the house, settled for the night.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia makes her last round at half past two, and finds Rose in the morning room. "The house is settled," she reports, the quartermaster's final dispatch — and the dispatch is the answer, made visible. If her answer was silence: "Amos has the gate. The lamps are trimmed to their night setting. The household holds its tongue. The village is asleep. Mrs. Vane —" she pauses, "— is in London, or Paris, or wherever unseen women are at half past two. Not here, and not answered." If her answer was a line, unsigned: "Amos has the gate. The lamps are trimmed. The household knows nothing about any line in any paper, and will go on knowing nothing. The messenger rides at dawn. Mrs. Vane is in London, or Paris, or wherever unseen women are — and tomorrow she reads it, or she doesn't." If her answer was preparation: "Amos has the gate, and a second man with him. The lamps are lit on the hour, not trimmed. The shutters are fast, the watch is doubled, the village briefed and discreet. Mrs. Vane is in London, or Paris, or wherever unseen women are at half past two — and if her people are watching, they see a house that is ready.")*
> *("Not here," Rose agrees. They stand together a moment, the aunt and the niece, the week's two devastations behind them — the confession said, the silence priced, the forgiveness given or withheld by Rose's choosing. "You were right," Letitia says quietly, "about the shapes. Knowing the shape isn't the same as proving it." "You proved the other one," Rose says. "The silence. You said it aloud." Letitia nods, once. "Goodnight, miss." "Goodnight, quartermaster." The round, completed. The house, held — asleep where it may be, awake where the answer requires — all but the two of them, and the garden, waiting.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Bell's leader on Mrs. Vane; printed, held, or cooled to a line, by Rose's choosing.
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting arrives in the small hours by special messenger, in Bell's own hand, marked for Rose's eyes alone. If her answer to Mrs. Vane was silence: the leader, drafted but not set — three paragraphs, cool and final, the name in the first line, plain and spelled correctly, held from the morning's Gazette by Rose's own instruction. "Held," Bell's note says, "as you instructed. The paper can wait. The truth keeps." The blade, undrawn; the unmasking, in the drawer. If her answer was a line, unsigned: the leader, cooled to a single line in Bell's editorial column — no name attached, the paper noting only that certain funds have been traced to their source. The truth, printed, unattributed; the name, kept. If her answer was preparation: the leader, set in type, running in the morning's Gazette. Three paragraphs, cool and final. The name is in the first line, plain and spelled correctly: Mrs. Vane. No face described, no history ventured, no guess at the woman behind the money. The paper prints what it knows, and what it knows is the name and the movement of the funds. And the treatment, by her choosing at the traced-money decision: if she chose print, the chain goes with it, every link — the factor's draft, the cutouts, Cecilia's people, the hundred pounds that bought a blind item. Daylight, complete. If she chose hold, the name goes in and the chain stops short: traced, the paper says, and held. The proof unprinted, in the Gazette's keeping. The warning inside the restraint — we know, and we are not showing all we know. If she chose return, the name goes in with the return beside it: the funds traced to their source and sent back by a quiet channel, the paper noting the courtesy and declining to print more. Mercy, made legible.)*
> *(Rose reads it twice and understands the weapon's final shape, whichever version is hers. If silence: the hunter unnamed in print, the receipts in Bell's keeping — and Mrs. Vane left to wonder whether the blade will ever fall. If a line: the truth unattributed, the name unprinted, the paper's cool eye the whole of it. If preparation: the hunter named in daylight, the treatment per the traced-money choosing — printed with receipts, held with warning, or returned with courtesy. Every version ends on the same line, Bell's blade: "The Gazette has never seen Mrs. Vane. The Gazette does not need to." Surfaced, never seen — in print, or in keeping. She files the leader with the week's drafts. The sting, run or held.)*
scenes.sting: ON MRS. VANE.

scenes.synopsis: goodnight — the answer, weighed; Octavia's last counsel of the season's penultimate week.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes at three in the morning — she does not knock, she never knocks — with the Gazette's first edition and a bottle of the good claret. The edition carries the answer, in print or in its absence. If her answer was silence: the leader is not in it — three paragraphs, cool and final, held in Bell's drawer by Rose's own instruction. Octavia sets the paper down nearly unopened. "The town will do the arithmetic on the quiet," she says, pouring, "the way you notice a missing tooth. And Mrs. Vane's people will read it all the way to London." If her answer was a line, unsigned: she finds it in the editorial column and reads it aloud — one cool sentence, no name attached, the funds traced to their source. "There it is," she says. "The town will do the arithmetic by noon, and Bell will have three letters asking whose hand held the pen, and she will answer none of them. The town loves a puzzle more than an answer." If her answer was preparation: she spreads the paper open on the leader — three paragraphs, the name in the first line, plain and spelled correctly. "Named," she says. "The town will do the arithmetic by breakfast.")*
> *(They drink — to the leader, or the line, or the blade undrawn; to Bell; to the town's skill at sums. Then Octavia turns serious, and the counsel is the answer, priced. If silence: "The strain is the price," she says. "Saying nothing, pointedly, costs the sayer. Hold it lightly, or it will hold you." If a line: "A beginning is the price," she says. "Beginnings invite replies. If she answers, you will hear it first in the town's mouth." If preparation: "Daylight is the price," she says. "The operation has lost its fog, and fog hides. Daylight aims.")*
> *("What do I do?" "What you've done," Octavia says. "The household, warned. The village, briefed. The watch, set — each in the manner of your answer. And —" she tops up the claret, "— you open the garden tomorrow, in white, in daylight, with the whole estate watching. You do the thing she can't buy, can't print, can't price." She raises her glass. "To the answer, given. And to the woman it can't touch." They drink. The counsel, given. The friend, kept: past three in the morning, past the week's end, into whatever's next.)*

scenes.synopsis: the glass — the night's last look; the woman the week made, considered.
scenes.prose:
> *(At half past three, Rose stands before the glass in the plain dressing gown, the week's last look. The woman in it has named a hunter, settled a witness, warned a household, forgiven — or not — an aunt, acknowledged a dowager, buried or printed or paid for the old sin, and dressed every day of it deliberately. The glass shows no triumph. It shows tiredness, and steadiness, and the particular clarity of a ledger balanced.)*
> *(Under the looking, the answer sits — the evening's last texture. If silence: the quiet she chose follows her up the stairs, and the house holds it with her, and the strain has its own steadiness, she finds. If a line, unsigned: she thinks of the folded sheet riding toward London in the dark, and wonders, briefly, whose breakfast table it will land on — then stops wondering, which was the point. If preparation: the lamps burn below on the hour, and the watch changes, and the house sounds awake in its bracing, and she is glad — absurdly, completely — to hear it.)*
> *(She thinks of the morning's blue, the siege's grey, the accession's direction, the white waiting for dawn. The week's doctrine in cloth, retired to the wardrobe. What remains is the woman underneath the costumes — the one Octavia named in the spring: furious and frightened and doing it anyway. The fury is quieter now. The fright is quieter. The doing — the doing continues. She touches the mend's glove on the dressing table, the thumb's scar, and turns away from the glass. The look, taken. The week, worn well.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the week, owned; no flinching, even alone.

fashionChoices.label: The glass, turned from
fashionChoices.detail: the looking, done; rest, chosen.

scenes.synopsis: the house sleeps; the garden waits — the night's last round; all quiet.
scenes.prose:
> *(At four, the house holds — asleep where the answer lets it, awake where the answer requires. If her answer was silence: Amos has the gate, the lamps are trimmed to their night setting, the north room stands locked, the village lies quiet under a clear sky, and the whole house keeps the quiet it was given, like a secret kept in company. If her answer was a line, unsigned: Amos has the gate, the lamps are trimmed, the messenger's horse stands saddled for dawn, and the house sleeps around the folded sheet the way a town sleeps around a rumor not yet born. If her answer was preparation: Amos has the gate with a second man beside him, the lamps burn on the hour, the watch walks the grounds, the shutters are fast — and anyone watching from the London road sees a house that has braced, and knows it is expected. The north room stands locked, Harrow's papers shelved and sealed within it — or in his keeping, by her choosing. Rose walks the hall once, the quartermaster's round made by the chatelaine, and finds everything as Letitia reported: settled, steady, braced, each in the manner of the answer. The forty pairs of mending hands are still. The dried violets at the wrists have been unpinned for the night. The white waits on the bed.)*
> *(She stands at the garden door. Not the walled garden's gate, not yet; tomorrow is tomorrow. She looks out at the dark grounds. Somewhere beyond the walls, the garden waits: the walls down or rising again, the papers shelved, the past settled, the ceremony prepared. Somewhere beyond that, London, and Paris, and wherever unseen women are at four in the morning, planning operations. But here: the house, asleep. The garden, waiting. The week, done. She turns the key in the garden door, locked till dawn, and goes up. The round, completed. The night, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the past, settled — Rose's last accounting before dawn; the season's weight, set down.
scenes.prose:
> *(At half past four, Rose sits at the study window and does the season's last accounting. Not the week's, which is closed, but the whole. The wall, come down in the spring. The papers, found. The sin, priced at forty-one six. The choice, made at the twentieth chapter: expose, bury, atone, hers. The hunters, surfaced. The money, traced. The witness, placed. The aunt, confessed. The dowager, acknowledged. The lover, stayed. The season of the walled garden, the season of walled things and the oldest secrets, ends with the walls down or rebuilt and the secrets shelved.)*
> *(The answer, she weighs last — it has no column in the ledger. If silence: the quiet, kept all evening, and the house keeping it with her, and Mrs. Vane's people hearing nothing, and nothing the message. If a line, unsigned: the folded sheet, riding toward London in the dark, and the town's wondering doing her work for her by breakfast. If preparation: the lamps, the watch, the braced house — the message written in lamplight for anyone watching to read. Whatever its shape, the answer was given. The present, answered.)*
> *(She thinks of her grandfather, the ledgers instead of knives, the respectable ruin. She thinks of Harrow's scar, Letitia's forty years, Augusta's longest game, Laurent's pride set down. The past is settled: put in its place, the north room, the catalogue, the sealed shelves. What remains is the present, an operation already underway, and the future, a garden gate standing open at dawn. She closes her eyes, the pearls cool at her throat, or the plain throat by her choosing, and sets the season's weight down. The past, settled. The dawn, coming.)*

scenes.synopsis: the cliffhanger — dawn; the walled garden gate stands open; tomorrow, the garden.
scenes.prose:
> *(Dawn. Rose wakes to the light coming through the shutters in bars, and for a moment she doesn't know what woke her. Then she knows: the garden door's key, cold in her hand where she fell asleep holding it. She goes to the window. The grounds lie in the grey-gold light of first morning, the mist low over the lawns, and there, beyond the walls, the walled garden's gate stands open.)*
> *(She stands at the window in the plain dressing gown, the key in her hand, the white waiting on the bed, and understands nothing except the fact of it: the gate, open. She locked the garden door at four. The walls are down or going up, the morning is here before its ceremony, and the gate stands open. She dresses for the white, quickly, her heart beating faster than it has all week. The gate stands open. Tomorrow, the garden.)*

scenes.synopsis: dawn — Rose at the garden before the household stirs; the gate, open.
scenes.prose:
> *(Friday comes up pale gold, and Rose is on the garden path before the household stirs. She walks in the white dress's wrapper, her shawl over her shoulders, and stops at the gate — which stands open, and will stand open. If she chose bury: the masons' new courses came down again in a single morning, at her order, and she watched the stones come down without flinching. The wall had kept its secret; the garden was done with walls. The gate, open, is the season's last argument: what was walled is walled no longer.)*
> *(She stands a moment in the gateway, between the house and the garden, and looks at the beds: the old roses, the weeds, the lilies Élise set in the spring, the bare square where the new rose will go. The garden, waiting. The day, beginning. She touches the gate's iron, cold from the night, and walks in.)*

scenes.synopsis: the reclamation's dress — plain white muslin, the green sash; dressed as the future.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia dresses her in the bedroom, and the dressing is quick — the day is not for fuss. The white dress: plain white muslin, cut simply, with a green sash the color of new leaves. No pearls. No pin. The mended gloves, last, worn open. "The future," Letitia says, "does not overdress." In the glass: a woman in white, severe and simple, the garden's own colors. Rose turns. "It looks like —" "It looks like you," Letitia says, "on a Friday, opening a garden.")*
> *(Down the stairs, through the hall, into the morning's honest light. The household is gathering at the garden. The white, worn. The future, dressed.)*

fashionChoices.detail: the white, plain; the day, faced.

fashionChoices.label: Rose, softened
fashionChoices.detail: the green sash, bright; the morning, met.
