fashionChoices.detail: the quartermaster judges the white.

scenes.synopsis: the gathering — servants, village men, tenants, friends; the people, come.
scenes.prose:
> *(They come up the path in the morning light: the servants' hall in its best, the village men in clean coats, the tenants from the farms, the friends from the choosing. Nobody was commanded; the word went round, and the word was enough. The garden fills the way a church fills — quietly, and all the way to the walls that are no longer walls. Rose stands at the gate in the white dress, and receives them one by one, by name.)*
> *(The names take a while. She knows them all — the house's people, the estate's people — and she says each one aloud, because the day is for saying. When the last of them is through the gate, she turns and looks at the gathering: the garden, full. The people, come. The giving, about to begin.)*

scenes.synopsis: the flowers — Élise brings white lilies and rosemary, and the unnamed rose in its pot.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes through the gate with her arms full: white lilies, tall and cool; rosemary, dark and fragrant; and between them, in a clay pot, the rose — a young plant, strong canes, no bloom yet, no name. "The lilies," Élise says, setting them down, "are purity of intent. The rosemary is remembrance." She holds out the pot. "And this — this is whatever you decide it is. It has no name until you give it one.")*
> *("No name," Rose says, taking the pot. The canes are green and certain. "The first rose of the restoration, and it doesn't know what it's called." "It will," Élise says. "When the house is ready, you said — when it all is —" She stops. "When it's ready." Rose looks at the plant, the lilies, the rosemary. "It's ready to be planted," she says. "That's enough for today.")*

scenes.synopsis: the living archive — Harrow at the fallen wall; his settlement, made.
scenes.prose:
> *(Harrow is waiting by the fallen wall, where the breach began the season, the scar pale in the morning light, the papers' weight gone from his shoulders. The settlement is signed and sealed: one hundred and fifty pounds, his wages, paid; the keeping deeded, if she chose atone; the placing entered — land agent, pensioner-historian, or his own choosing, as she decided Monday — and his papers the library's, shelved under his name, sealed unattributed, or kept in his hands, by her choosing at the papers decision.)*
> *("Mr. Harrow." "Miss Hartwell." He looks at the wall, the breach, the garden. "I came here in the spring looking for work or sanctuary," he says. "I seem to have found both, and a garden besides." A pause. "The papers are the library's now. But the remembering —" he touches his scar, lightly — "the remembering stays with me. That's the arrangement." "That's the arrangement," Rose agrees. The archive, living. The witness, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the aunt, at her side — forgiven or not, the confession's week behind them.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia stands at Rose's side at the gate, in dove grey, the quartermaster at her post. If Rose forgave her aloud in the choosing's week: the forgiveness sits between them like something mended — visible, and stronger at the join. "You look," Letitia says, "like your grandmother's doctrine, finally worn by someone who understands it." If Rose has not yet forgiven her: the unforgiven sits between them like something awaiting the needle — and Letitia stands at her post anyway, because that is what quartermasters do. "You look," she says, "like the day, and the day is enough.")*
> *("Aunt Letitia." "Miss." A beat. "Stay by me today." "I had not planned," Letitia says, "to be anywhere else." The aunt, at her side. The week, behind them. Whatever remains, remains — and the garden is opening.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's acknowledgment — Augusta, in French blue beside Hartwell colors.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta comes up the path on Henry's arm, and she is dressed for the day in the émigré and the English house together: a French blue worked into the bodice's embroidery beside the Hartwell colors. She looks at the open gate, the full garden, the granddaughter in white. "Well," the dowager says. "The wall is down.")*
> *("It is." "Your grandfather," Augusta says, "would have rebuilt it by now. Twice." A pause — and then, quietly, for Rose alone: "What the network cost my family — I have carried it a long time. Today I set some of it down." She touches Rose's sleeve, the white muslin. "You dress as the future. Good. Somebody in this family should." The acknowledgment, made. The dowager, in daylight, with the past.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE OPENING: the gate stands open; who walks through first.
scenes.prose:
> *(The garden is full, the household is waiting, and the gate stands open. Somebody must walk through it first. The opening needs a first step, and the first step is Rose's to give. She stands at the threshold in the white dress, the people behind her and before her, and considers the order of the day: alone first, the house's act, the heir's; with the household, the choosing's witnesses, the week's holders; with the village, all together, the estate's people, the giving's own.)*
> *(Letitia waits at her elbow. Augusta watches from the path. Laurent stands among the tenants, Harrow by the wall, Élise with the lilies. The gate, open. The day, hers to order. She takes a breath, and chooses who opens the garden.)*
> *(The step is taken in the open, at the season's pace. The garden, opened. The order, hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the staying, witnessed — Laurent among the tenants; the devastation, and what came after.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent stands among the tenants, not apart from them — the comte in a plain coat, his hands empty of everything but the morning. The week told him what the season told everyone: the woman he is learning to love is the heir of his family's ruiners, and he did not know. The devastation was the season's. The staying is the day's. He meets Rose's eyes across the garden, and nods — once, the way Frenchmen nod when the words are too large for the occasion.)*
> *(She crosses to him, through the gathering, and takes his hand where everyone can see it. "Comte." "Miss Hartwell." A beat. "You stayed." "I am," Laurent says, "a difficult man to dislodge." The garden hears it, and the garden — tenants, servants, friends — smiles. The staying, witnessed. The pride, set down.)*

scenes.synopsis: midday white — the dress in the morning sun; the future, in daylight.
scenes.prose:
> *(The sun climbs, and the white dress changes in it — muslin gone luminous, the green sash vivid, the mended gloves pale against the white. Rose stands in the garden's center, in full light, and the day looks at her: the heir in the future's colors, the season's last costume. She turns once, slowly, letting the skirt move. The dress is simple. The simplicity is the statement.)*
> *(A tenant's child stares, round-eyed, at the lady in white. Rose curtsies to her — a full, proper curtsy, the white pooling — and the child laughs, delighted. The garden laughs with her. The white, in sun. The future, in daylight.)*

scenes.synopsis: the canal, the future — Julian at the water; what younger sons understand now.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian is waiting by the canal, where the water runs toward the garden's new course — the revenue's water, if she chose atone: three thousand a year, for ten years, the canal paying for the past. He skims a stone, and it jumps three times. "The machinery," he says, not looking at her, "that makes younger sons into instruments. I understand it better, this week. The money moves, and the men move with it, and nobody asks the men." He looks at her. "You asked. That's the difference.")*
> *("The canal stays the Park's," Rose says. "Whatever the week cost — the stones untouched, the roofs untouched." If she chose atone: "The revenue pays. That's what revenue is for." Julian nods. "The future," he says, "with plumbing." She laughs — the first full laugh of the day. The suitor, steadied. The water, running.)*

scenes.synopsis: duty, kept — Henry's honor; the hardest case, answered.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry stands at the garden's edge with Quill — the brother and the solicitor in the morning light — and he has the look of a man whose hardest case has been heard. The sin was old, the sinners dead, the victims owed — what does duty require of the living? The week answered it, whatever door she chose: the living pay, or tell, or carry. Henry bows to Rose, precise as ever.)*
> *("Major." "Miss Hartwell." A pause. "The law," Henry says, "is a blunt instrument for old sins. You used —" he searches — "a sharper one." "I used the household," Rose says. "And the garden." "The garden," Henry agrees, "is not in the statutes." The smallest smile. "It should be." Duty, kept. The honor, intact.)*

scenes.synopsis: the cost, named kindly — Octavia's last accounting; the affection, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia finds Rose by the lily beds, the ledger nowhere in sight for the first time in a month. "No figures today," she says. "The counting is done." She looks at the garden, the people, the white dress. "The cost," she says, "named kindly, because the week is over: if she chose atone — forty-one thousand six hundred, ten years, the canal and the surplus, and the only inheritance worth having. If she chose expose — the town knows, the debts remain, and the courage is the inheritance. If she chose bury — the proof is ash, the peace is kept, and the carrying is the inheritance.")*
> *("Whichever," Octavia says, "you paid it. Or told it. Or carry it. The price was stated, and you did not flinch from saying it." She touches Rose's arm. "The affection," she says, "was the easy part. The precision took all season." They look at each other, and the laughter comes — tired, warm, the season's own. The cost, named. Kindly.)*

scenes.synopsis: the paper's verdict — Bell, in the garden; independence, proven at the root.
scenes.prose:
> *(Bell comes through the gate in her plain black, the proprietor in the garden like a rook among doves, and she looks at the gathering with a printer's eye. If she chose expose: "We printed it," Bell says, "because it was true and it was news. Not because you asked. The paper's independence is the point — you know that." If she chose bury: "We printed nothing," Bell says, "because there was nothing to print. The paper does not invent. The independence is the point." If she chose atone: "We printed the price," Bell says. "Forty-one thousand six hundred, ten years. The town reads the sin tomorrow. The independence is the point.")*
> *("Whatever the week," Bell says, "the Gazette's hardest call was made on the paper's own terms. That's the verdict." She looks at the white dress, the lilies, the people. "Nice garden," the proprietor concedes. "Print that." The paper, unbuyable. The root, proven.)*

scenes.synopsis: deeds, trust, record — Quill's papers; the week's signatures, filed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill waits by the sundial with his leather case, the solicitor in the sun, and he opens it with the care of a man handling the week's whole weight. If she chose atone: the trust's founding, signed — the eight thousand eight hundred, the canal's three thousand a year, the creditors named; Harrow's keeping, deeded; the de Valcourts' twenty-eight hundred, promised and recorded. If she chose expose: the account's copy, filed — the telling, on record, the paper's printing witnessed. If she chose bury: the masons' bill, paid — the wall's coming and going, on record, the proof's absence witnessed.)*
> *("The record," Quill says, "is complete. Whatever the door — the papers are the library's, the signatures are the file's, and the file is the house's." He closes the case. "A solicitor," he observes, "rarely gets to file a happy ending." "File it," Rose says, "before it changes its mind." The deeds, done. The record, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the garden, seen whole — Rose walks its length; the walls, down.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone, between the gatherings, Rose walks the garden's length — from the gate to the far bed, where the old wall's line runs under the grass like a scar under skin. The courses are down. The breach is a gate. The beds Élise planted are coming up. The bare square waits for the rose. She walks slowly, the white dress brushing the weeds, and sees it whole: the season's wound, become the season's gift.)*
> *(At the far bed she stops, and looks back: the house beyond the gate, the people in the garden, the morning gold on the white. The garden, seen whole. The walls, down. She bends, takes a handful of the bed's earth, and lets it run through her fingers. The earth, hers. The garden, hers. The giving, coming.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dowager's lilies — Augusta pins the flowers; the heir, adorned.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta beckons Rose to the bench by the lilies, and from her reticule she takes a small cluster of white lily buds, wired by her own dresser. "Purity of intent," the dowager says, pinning them at Rose's shoulder. "Your gardener's girl taught me the language. I am an apt pupil." The lilies sit against the white muslin, cool and exact. "There," Augusta says. "The future, with flowers.")*
> *(Rose looks down at the buds, the white on white. "Grandmama." "Yes?" "Thank you. For the setting down." Augusta pats her hand, once, the dowager's whole tenderness in the pat. "Thank you," she says, "for the garden." The lilies, pinned. The heir, adorned.)*

fashionChoices.detail: at the shoulder; the intent, declared.

fashionChoices.label: Wear them low
fashionChoices.detail: at the sash; the intent, carried.

fashionChoices.detail: the dowager judges the lilies.

scenes.synopsis: the mend, worn open — the season's motif, at the ceremony.
scenes.prose:
> *(Between the gatherings, Rose looks at her hands: the mended gloves, the left thumb's fine scar of stitching, worn open all season. The mend began as the grandmother's doctrine — a glove could be mended, a reputation earned back stitch by stitch — and became the season's answer: nothing hidden, nothing flaunted. She flexes the thumb, feeling the mend's ridge. The sin was faced. The price was stated, or told, or carried. The garden is opening.)*
> *(She holds the mended hand up to the light, the stitching fine as a vein. Whatever the week made of her — heir of old sins, the woman who chose — the mend is the record: broken, and repaired, and worn. She lowers the hand. The ceremony is waiting. The mend, worn open, goes with her.)*

scenes.synopsis: the giving — the garden, given to the estate's people as well as the house.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose climbs the two stone steps at the garden's center, and the gathering quiets. The giving needs words — few, and plain. "This garden," she says, "was walled for a generation. The wall is down. The garden is the estate's — the house's, and the people's who keep the house." She looks at the tenants, the servants, the village men. "Come when you like. Bring your children. The roses are the house's; the rest is yours.")*
> *(A silence — and then the garden answers the way gardens answer: a tenant's wife laughs, a child runs for the beds, the village men nod, the servants' hall applauds. The giving, said. The garden, given. Rose steps down, and the people come up to her — not bowing, not quite; greeting. The estate's people, in the estate's garden.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE ROSE: the first unnamed rose of the restoration; who plants it.
scenes.prose:
> *(The clay pot waits on the stone by the bare square: the young rose, strong canes, no bloom, no name. The planting is the day's heart, and the heart needs hands. Rose stands over the pot in the white dress, the trowel in the mended glove, and considers the planting's order. Herself, alone, the heir's hands, the future's. With Harrow, the witness, who carried the papers and the scar. With Letitia, the forgiven, whose silence cost and whose standing held.)*
> *(Élise kneels by the square, ready. The household rings the bed. The lilies watch, white. The rosemary breathes, dark. The rose waits, unnamed, for the hands that will put it in the earth. She chooses the planting.)*
> *(The hands are chosen in the open, without hurry. The rose, planted. The name, withheld — until the end of Book One.)*

options.label: Plant it herself
options.detail: *Resolve+; the heir's hands.* The trowel, the earth, the rose — hers alone, the future planted by the future's own hands.

options.label: With Harrow — the witness
options.detail: *Candor+; the archive's hands.* The man who carried the papers puts the rose in the earth beside her — the past, planting the future.

options.label: With Letitia — the forgiven
options.detail: *Mercy+; the family's hands.* The aunt's hands over hers on the trowel — the silence, answered with soil.

scenes.synopsis: the planting — the unnamed rose, in the earth.
scenes.prose:
> *(The trowel goes in, the earth opens, the rose goes down — canes green, roots pale, the clay pot set aside. If she plants it herself: her hands, the mended gloves dark with soil, press the earth firm. If with Harrow: his scarred hand steadies the canes while hers firms the soil — the witness, planting. If with Letitia: the aunt's hands cover hers on the trowel's haft — the family's hands, together. Whichever hands, the rose is planted: the first of the restoration, unnamed, in the estate's earth.)*
> *(She waters it from the can Élise holds, and the water darkens the soil. No name — not yet. The rose will be named at the end of Book One, when the house is ready. For now it is simply planted: the future, in the ground, taking hold. She stands, the knees of the white dress earth-marked, and does not brush them clean.)*

scenes.synopsis: the rose, the future — Laurent at the planted bed; what grows.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent comes to the bed after the planting, and looks at the young canes for a long time. "A rose with no name," he says. "In my family, everything had a name. The names were the first thing to go." He touches a cane, lightly. "Yours will earn its name. That is the better order." A pause. "The de Varennes —" he stops. "No. Today, the rose.")*
> *("Today, the rose," Rose agrees. They stand at the bed together, the planted future between them. "It will bloom next year," Élise calls from the lilies. "White, I think. Or blush." "Blush," Laurent says, firmly. "The future should blush." Rose laughs — and the bed, the canes, the earth, hold the laughter the way soil holds water. The rose, the future. What grows.)*

scenes.synopsis: her tears, allowed — Letitia at the planted rose; the week's last weeping.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia comes to the bed alone, after the gathering has moved on, and stands looking at the planted rose. If Rose forgave her aloud: the tears come quietly — the confession's week, the forgiveness's weight, the garden's opening, all at once. If Rose has not forgiven her: the tears come anyway — the confession made, the standing kept, the garden opening whether or not the mending is done. Either way, the quartermaster weeps, once, briefly, into a handkerchief.)*
> *(Rose finds her there, and does not comment on the handkerchief — some things the household does not note. "It will bloom," Rose says instead. "Next year." "Blush, Élise says." "Blush." Letitia folds the handkerchief, precisely. "Good," the aunt says. "The garden could use some color." The tears, allowed. The week, ending.)*

scenes.synopsis: the working white — changed for the ceremony; the dress, after the planting.
scenes.prose:
> *(After the planting, Rose changes for the ceremony — the morning's white is earth-marked at the knees and hem, and the afternoon asks for fresh. Letitia lays out the second white: plain muslin again, simpler still, with the rosemary at the wrist instead of the sash's green. "The working white," Letitia calls it. "For the giving's second half." In the glass: the same woman, the same future, the dress renewed.)*
> *(She keeps the earth-marked sash folded on the dresser — not discarded. The marks are the day's record. The fresh white goes on, and she turns once before the glass, the decision still hers to make. The ceremony is coming. The white, renewed.)*

scenes.synopsis: goodnight to the season — Octavia's farewell to the choosing's month.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia finds Rose in the garden's quiet hour, the ledger finally left at home, and they walk the beds together without an agenda — the first walk in a month with nowhere to be. "The season," Octavia says. "The blind item, the offer, the price, the screw, the choosing, the garden." She counts them off on her fingers. "A month's work. Done.")*
> *("Done," Rose agrees. They stop at the planted rose. "The affection," Octavia says, "was the easy part." "The precision," Rose says, "took all season." "The season," Octavia says, "is closed." They look at the canes, the earth, the white dress. "Goodnight, then," Rose says. "Goodnight," Octavia says, "to the season." The friends, at rest. The month, done.)*

scenes.synopsis: daylight concession — Augusta, before the gathering; what was built, acknowledged.
scenes.prose:
> *(In the afternoon's full light, Augusta stands at the garden's center, and the gathering turns to her — the dowager does not ask for attention; the day gives it. "I have lived," she says, "in houses with higher walls than this one had. The walls kept the weather out. They kept other things out, too." A pause. "This garden is better without its wall. The house is better for the opening. I concede it — in daylight, before witnesses.")*
> *(The gathering hears it: the establishment's acknowledgment, made in the open. Augusta looks at Rose, in the working white, the rosemary at her wrist. "You built this week," the dowager says, "the way your grandmother mended gloves. Stitch by stitch." The concession, made. The daylight, holding.)*

scenes.synopsis: the flowers, hers to tend — Élise's charge; the garden's keeping.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise comes to Rose in the afternoon with soil on her hands and the day's brightness still in her face. "The lilies are in," she says. "The rosemary's bedded. The rose —" she glances at the planted canes — "the rose is yours to name, when it's ready. But the tending —" She holds out her soil-dark hands. "The tending is mine. If you'll have me as the garden's keeper.")*
> *("The garden's keeper," Rose says. "The flowers, hers to tend." She takes Élise's hands, soil and all, in the mended gloves. "I will have you. The house will have you." She looks at the beds, the people, the day. "The garden already does." Élise curtsies, laughing, the soil on her hands. The charge, given. The keeping, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: the last walk — Rose and Laurent, the garden's length, at the day's turning.
scenes.prose:
> *(At the day's turning, Laurent offers his arm, and they walk the garden's length together — from the gate to the far bed, the long walk, the last of the season. They do not talk of the sin, or the price, or the staying. They talk of the beds: the lilies, the rosemary, the rose with no name. "Blush," Laurent says again, of the future's color. "You are certain." "I am French," he says. "We are certain about flowers.")*
> *(At the far bed they stop, where the wall's line runs under the grass. "The walk's end," Rose says. "The season's," Laurent says. He bows over her hand — the mended glove, the soil at the wrist. "Until the war," he says, lightly, and the lightness does not quite hide the knowledge. The last walk, walked. The end, at hand.)*

scenes.synopsis: the day, held — Rose alone, before the ceremony; the hours, gathered.
scenes.prose:
> *(Before the ceremony, Rose is alone in the garden for a few minutes — the gathering resting, the household preparing, the day holding its breath. She stands at the planted rose, in the working white, the rosemary at her wrist, and gathers the hours: the dawn gate, the white dress, the people, the lilies, Harrow's scar, Letitia's post, Augusta's colors, the opening, Laurent's nod, the canal, Henry's statutes, Octavia's kindness, Bell's verdict, Quill's file, the walk, the giving, the planting, the walk again.)*
> *(The hours, gathered, are the season: the sin faced, the price stated or told or carried, the garden opened, the rose planted. She touches the rosemary at her wrist — remembrance — and the lily at her shoulder — purity of intent. The day, held. The ceremony, coming.)*

scenes.synopsis: THE RECLAMATION — the planting ritual; the garden, given; the chapter's ritual.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: commit to a direction, A, B, or C, then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*
> *(Story morsel: the walls, down. She walks the garden's length in the mind: the fallen courses, the open gate, the beds given to the estate's people. The breach where the season began is the gate where the season ends. She walks it to the gate, and stops. The garden, open.)*
> *(Story morsel: the giving. She gives it in the mind: the beds, the lilies, the rosemary, the paths — the estate's people, the house's people, all. "The roses are the house's; the rest is yours." She says it once, and means it. The garden, given.)*
> *(Story morsel: the rose, planted. She plants it in the mind: the trowel, the earth, the canes — herself, or with Harrow, or with Letitia, whichever hands the day chose. The first rose of the restoration, unnamed. It will be named at the end of Book One. She plants it deep, and pats the earth. The rose, planted.)*
> *(Story morsel: the choosing, remembered. She chose before anyone chose for her — the account, the fire, or the trust, whichever door the season entered. The hunters' version died, or starved, or was outpaid. She remembers it whole, and lets it go. The season, closed.)*
> *(Story morsel: the future, dressed. She stands in the white — muslin, silk, or linen, whichever the ritual chose — the garden's own colors, the future's. The season is closed. The war is coming. She is dressed for it.)*

ritual.occasionBrief: The garden is opened. The walls are down, the gate stands open, and the walled garden is given — to the estate's people as well as the house. Tonight the reclamation is witnessed in fashion: white, simple, the garden's own colors — Rose dressed as the future, not the past. Walk the garden in the ritual's order. Plant, give, remember. Exact. Courageous. Unhurried. The house that gives does not count the cost.

scenes.synopsis: the earth, the hands — after the ritual; the soil, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(After the ritual, Rose looks at her hands: the mended gloves are dark with the day's earth — the planting, the layings, the garden's own soil worked into the stitching. She does not take them off. The earth on the hands is the reclamation's signature: the heir who digs, the future with dirty gloves.)*
> *(She rubs the thumb's mend, the soil rough against the fine stitching. The day is nearly done. The garden is given, the rose is planted, the ritual is walked. The earth, on the hands. The hands, the day's.)*

scenes.synopsis: soil at the hem — the evening's white, earth-marked; the marks, worn proudly.
scenes.prose:
> *(The evening's white has acquired the day: soil at the hem, a smudge of earth on the skirt, the rosemary at the wrist wilted to fragrance. Rose looks at the marks in the glass and does not reach for the brush. The marks are the reclamation, written on the dress. The future, it turns out, gets dirty.)*
> *(She turns once, the soiled hem moving. The dress is still white — the marks are the day's, not the dress's failure. On the dresser, the brush waits within reach. She smiles at the woman in the glass: the heir, the gardener, the future, all in one white dress with soil at the hem. The marks, worn. Proudly.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE DECLARATION: the garden given, the season closed; what Hartwell Park is for.
scenes.prose:
> *(The garden is given, the rose is planted, the ritual is walked — and one thing remains: the declaration. Hartwell Park has been ruin, restoration, battleground, archive, and garden this season. Tonight, before the household, Rose says what it is for. The words will be the season's last — and the Book's hinge. She stands in the evening's white, the soil at the hem, the people waiting, and chooses the declaration.)*
> *(Augusta watches. Letitia stands ready. Laurent is at the garden's edge, Julian by the canal path, Octavia with the friends, Harrow by the wall, Élise with the flowers, Bell with her notebook, Quill with his case. The household, the village, the estate. The declaration, hers to make.)*
> *(The words are spoken in the open, before them all. The Park, declared. The future, named — all but the rose.)*

options.detail: *Candor+; the telling.* The Gazette's creed, the season's creed — the house stands on what is true.

options.label: "It is for the future — and the future starts now."
options.detail: *Resolve+; the beginning.* The rose, unnamed; the garden, open; the war, coming — the house faces forward.

scenes.synopsis: the declaration, heard — the household receives the words.
scenes.prose:
> *(The declaration lands in the dusk garden, and the household receives it — precisely, and with loyalty. If she said the people: the servants' hall stands straighter, the tenants nod, the village men touch their hats. If she said the truth: Bell's pencil stops, just for a moment, and the proprietor inclines her head. If she said the future: the young ones — the tenants' children, Élise's girls — press forward, toward the planted rose.)*
> *(Whatever the words, the answer is the same: "Hartwell." The name, spoken by the people, in the garden, at dusk. Rose stands in the white with soil at the hem, and receives it. The declaration, heard. The house, purposed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sting — Bell's finale: "ON THE RECLAMATION."
scenes.prose:
> *(The sting comes at dusk, in Bell's own hand, delivered to the garden: the season's verdict, set in type. Three paragraphs, cool and certain. They describe, without naming, a house that opened its oldest garden and gave it to its people; a rose planted without a name; a week that began with a wall and ended with a gate. The last line is the verdict: "The Gazette has watched this house for a season. It finds the garden open, the heir dressed as the future, and the week's account settled on the house's own terms. So noted.")*
> *(Rose reads it once, and folds it into the drawer of the reckoning's archive — with the Lash, the trust's paper, the choosing's draft. Bell's rule held to the last: no names, no favors, the paper's own terms. The season's verdict, printed. The finale, filed.)*
scenes.sting: ON THE RECLAMATION.

scenes.synopsis: her last word — Bell, at the garden's edge; the proprietor's farewell.
scenes.prose:
> *(Bell lingers at the garden's edge after delivering the sting, the plain black against the dusk, and for once the proprietor is not in a hurry. "A word," she says, "not for print." Rose waits. "I have printed ruin, and restoration, and war in my time. I have never printed —" Bell searches — "a garden, given away. The town will not know what to do with it." A pause. "Good.")*
> *("Your last word?" Rose asks. "My last word for the season," Bell corrects. "The paper continues. The town continues." She looks at the white dress, the soil, the rose. "You continue." She touches her hat, the printer's farewell, and goes. The last word, given. Not for print.)*

scenes.synopsis: evening white at dusk — the dress in the last light; the glass, consulted.
scenes.prose:
> *(Dusk settles on the garden, and the white dress goes pearl in the last light — muslin turned luminous, the soil at the hem darkened to shadow, the rosemary at the wrist a dark green line. Rose stands before the bedroom glass, in the evening's full quiet, and consults it: the woman who opened a garden, planted a rose, declared a house. The glass shows a woman in white, earth-marked, lily-pinned, the future's colors.)*
> *(She looks a long moment. Then she nods — once, the quartermaster's nod, learned from Letitia — and turns from the glass. The evening white, at dusk. The woman, consulted. The day, nearly done.)*

scenes.synopsis: the walk's end — Laurent, at dusk; the season's last walk, closed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent is waiting at the garden's gate at dusk — the open gate, the season's closing evidence — and they walk the short path together without speaking, the season's last walk closed in quiet. At the gate he stops. "The rose," he says. "Blush." "Blush," Rose agrees. "The devastation," he says, "was the season's. The staying —" "The staying," Rose says, "is yours.")*
> *(He bows over her hand — the mended glove, the soil, the day. "Until the war," he says, and this time the lightness is gone, and the knowledge is plain. "Until the war," Rose says. The walk's end, reached. The gate, open, behind them.)*

scenes.synopsis: the season, closed — Rose alone, at night; the reckoning, complete.
scenes.prose:
> *(Night, and the garden is empty — the people gone home, the lilies closed, the planted rose a dark shape in the dark bed. Rose walks the length once more, alone, in the evening's white, and closes the season the way she opened it: deliberately, and in the open. The sin was faced — exposed, buried, or atoned, whichever door. The price was stated, or told, or carried. The garden is open. The rose is planted, unnamed. The house is declared.)*
> *(At the gate she stops, and looks back one last time: the beds, the wall's line under the grass, the rose. The season, closed. The reckoning, complete. She touches the gate's iron — warm now, from the day — and walks out, leaving it open.)*

scenes.synopsis: the cliffhanger — London; the evening post brings word of Cecilia's operation; the door, opened.
scenes.prose: > *(London, Friday night. The evening post is sorted by lamplight, and among the bills and invitations comes the word — not a letter, never a letter: a factor's draft, honored; a lease, signed; a house, taken, in Mayfair, for the Season. The money traces clean through two cutouts to the account name the week already knows: Vane. Cecilia's people are in London. The operation is not coming. It has begun. The past is settled. The present has already begun.)*
